cards.title: A card comment from the console needs no pasted Linear key — the side panel's comment box posts the owner's words signed by the console (as Answer does), so "Couldn't post — your Linear key is not connected" goes away
cards.description:
**Repo:** agent-bureau (console backend and web)

**CEO, 2026-09-13 ~11:40 PT:** *"I found this bug … go ahead and fix."* On a card's side panel ([DRE-3786](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3786/green-lights-answer-posts-the-ceos-words-on-the-card-signed-by-the)'s, below the PR and branch lines), he typed a comment into the comment box and pressed post. A toast refused it: **"Couldn't post — your Linear key is not connected (Settings → Integrations)"**.

**Why it happens:** the comment box ([DRE-3655](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3655/the-ceo-can-comment-on-a-card-from-the-console-a-comment-box-on-the), `console/backend/card_comment.py`) goes through `console_actor.own_identity_post`, and that returns nothing without a personal Linear grant. [DRE-3755](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3755/a-signed-in-owners-groom-decisions-and-card-comments-go-out-with-a) made groom decisions work without a key by signing them. It deliberately left free-text comments out, because a comment under the fleet's name would read as the pipeline speaking. Two changes remove that concern. [DRE-3785](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3785/agents-read-a-console-signed-answer-as-the-ceos-own-words-the) (bureau-pipeline #382, on `stable`) makes every pipeline reader accept a console-signed comment as the CEO's own words. [DRE-3786](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3786/green-lights-answer-posts-the-ceos-words-on-the-card-signed-by-the) ([dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau#2531](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/review/featdre-3786-green-lights-answer-posts-the-ceos-words-on-the-card-f82364f345de)) adds the signed answer path. The CEO wants his comments to work the same way.

## What to build

* **The owner with a personal grant:** unchanged. The comment posts on his own key, and it is also signed, as [DRE-3786](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3786/green-lights-answer-posts-the-ceos-words-on-the-card-signed-by-the) does.
* **The signed-in owner without a grant:** the comment posts on the console's Linear credential with the console-signed receipt, using [DRE-3785](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3785/agents-read-a-console-signed-answer-as-the-ceos-own-words-the)'s format (the answer or comment kind, binding the body's SHA-256, the card, the console user and the time). It carries a plain header: "Comment from <name> (signed in to the console), <PT time>:" and then his words.
* **A non-owner:** refused, as today.
* **The side panel** follows the one button standard ([DRE-3756](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3756/every-atom-follows-the-one-button-standard-menu-items-and-icon-buttons)): pressed, then busy after 0.5 s, then done or failed with the reason. The "your Linear key is not connected" message no longer appears for the owner.
* **Reuse** [DRE-3786](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3786/green-lights-answer-posts-the-ceos-words-on-the-card-signed-by-the)'s `card_answer.py` signing and [DRE-3755](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3755/a-signed-in-owners-groom-decisions-and-card-comments-go-out-with-a)'s key. Add no new crypto.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Tests:
  * the owner without a grant posts a signed comment that verifies against the published key, and the pipeline's reader test vector reads it as the CEO's
  * a grant holder's comment is unchanged and signed
  * a non-owner is refused
  * the private key never appears in a response or a log
- [ ] **PROOF in production:** the UI/UX session posts one comment from the CEO's side panel with no pasted key, and the comment appears on the card with its signed receipt. Record the card, the comment and the PT time here.

**Sequencing:** builds on [dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau#2531](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/review/featdre-3786-green-lights-answer-posts-the-ceos-words-on-the-card-f82364f345de) ([DRE-3786](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3786/green-lights-answer-posts-the-ceos-words-on-the-card-signed-by-the)), and starts off `main` once that merges.

cards.title: The rest of the card-edit path answers from memory — AlertFeed, StatRibbon, ActivityFeed and NeedsYou batch their per-card lookups the DRE-3788 way, so a Linear edit reaches the console within 3 s (3.54 s today)
cards.description:
**Repo:** agent-bureau (console backend)

**Production, 2026-09-13 11:31 PT, v1.6.63** (the full reading is on [DRE-3788](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3788/the-last-17-s-a-lone-live-update-reloads-at-once-instead-of-after-the)): a Linear edit now reaches the open One River DOM in **3.54 s** at the median. That is down from 13.3 s this morning and 4.74 s at 10:07 PT, but still over 3 s. [DRE-3788](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3788/the-last-17-s-a-lone-live-update-reloads-at-once-instead-of-after-the) removed the N+1 statements from `InFlight`, `Fleet` and `KpiTrends`, and none of those three logs slow any more. The frame-to-DOM 2.4 s is now held by the **other reads on the card path**, which all run slow and none queue:

| read | slow warnings, 11:30–11:34 PT | range |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `AlertFeed` | ~35, usually three at once per frame | 2.0–3.8 s |
| `StatRibbon` | 8 | 2.0–3.4 s |
| `ActivityFeed` | 4 | 2.5–5.1 s |
| `NeedsYou` | 1 | 2.1 s |

The console is on **HTTP/1.1**: six connections per tab, one held by the SSE stream. So these reads fill the connections, and the river's reload queues behind them.

## What to build

* Apply [DRE-3788](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3788/the-last-17-s-a-lone-live-update-reloads-at-once-instead-of-after-the)'s method to each read above. Count its statements on the production-shaped fixture (`console/backend/tests/board_shape.py`), then replace per-card, per-epic and per-event lookups with batched reads. Each batched read gets a tenant-scoped twin. Where a read is repeated within one frame, reuse `board_reads.py`'s generation-keyed memo, which is exact, per tenant and single-flight. `pipeline_alert_rows` is already memoised ([DRE-3746](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3746/a-linear-edit-reaches-an-open-console-within-3-s-in-production-the)), so look at what `AlertFeed` does around it.
* Compare the answers byte for byte, before and after, the way [DRE-3788](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3788/the-last-17-s-a-lone-live-update-reloads-at-once-instead-of-after-the) did (36 answers across tenant scopes and clocks).

## Acceptance

- [ ] Local statement counts before and after for each read. Cold each is under 300 ms at 4 ms per statement, and warm each is under 50 ms.
- [ ] Production after release: five edits at a median of ≤3 s (the [DRE-3746](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3746/a-linear-edit-reaches-an-open-console-within-3-s-in-production-the) method, **without** an extra listener stream), recorded on [DRE-3746](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3746/a-linear-edit-reaches-an-open-console-within-3-s-in-production-the) and here.
- [ ] Production slow-operation warnings: none of these four over 2 s for 15 minutes.

cards.title: portico: the design system's token swatches are drawn from the real CSS, every colour token
cards.description:
Sid, 2026-09-13, on part 1 of the design system: "The token colors still look wrong. Are you using the real CSS?" Measured: the swatches were hex values typed into `parts/01-intro.html` — all 17 matched the tokens, but they were copies, and only 17 of the 45 colour tokens in layer 0 had a swatch at all (no `--ink3`, `--ctl`, the soft and ink shades of amber, red, indigo and graphite, the inherited-access lines, the folder colours, the six `--kind-*` badges, `--desk`).

## What this card does

* `build.py` reads layer 0 of `src/styles.css` and generates the swatch grid: every colour token, grouped (surfaces, ink, lines, accent, status, Foundry and drives, folders, file kinds), each half painted with `var(--token)` — the light half inside a generated forced-light scope, the dark half inside the spec's own `.dark` scope — with the values printed from the file. No colour is typed into the page.
* The forced-light scope is generated from the `:root` block by `build.py`, never hand-copied.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] every colour token in layer 0 has a swatch, and a token added to `styles.css` appears with no edit to the parts
- [ ] no swatch colour is written as a literal in `parts/`
- [ ] the page reads right in light and dark, and `index.html` rebuilds byte for byte

cards.title: portico: molecules, people and adding — PersonLine, AccountFooter, DropZone, UploadRow
cards.description:
Four molecules from part 3 of `docs/design/system/index.html`, made only of part 1's atoms.

* `PersonLine.tsx` (Avatar and the one fact that matters where it appears).
* `AccountFooter.tsx` (Avatar, Version in its channel state, ToolbarButton opening the Account menu): everyone sees their name and the version; moderators also see the branch pill, how far behind main, and version · commit, after agent-bureau's footer (Sid, 2026-09-13). It takes the build facts as props; reading them is [DRE-3787](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3787/portico-the-portal-knows-its-branch-and-how-far-it-is-behind-main-for)'s.
* `DropZone.tsx` (Icon, Button: where files are dropped, with the same thing as a button).
* `UploadRow.tsx` (ItemGlyph, Progress, Button: uploading, being read, failed with a reason and retry). The spec's "being read" caption needs Progress to take a caption — if it does not, use the text beside it; do not change the Progress atom.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] each matches its section in part 3 of the spec, light and dark, side by side in Chrome; the footer in both its moderator and partner forms
- [ ] imports only atoms; no raw control or svg (layer test)

cards.title: portico: molecules, the library — SidebarItem, ItemRow, IconTile, EmptyPane

cards.title: portico: molecules, organisms and templates never redraw an atom — DRY, held by the layer test
cards.description:
Sid, 2026-09-13: "we are using DRY Principles: We're only creating one React object and then reusing it again and again. We're not creating different ones, so all the atoms are, by definition, singular, right? Everything's built up from these atoms."

The layer-direction test ([DRE-3768](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3768/portico-a-test-that-holds-the-layers-to-their-direction-and-stops-new)) holds which layer may import which. It does not stop a molecule from drawing its own button, field or icon instead of importing the atom, which is exactly how duplicates appear.

## What this card does

`client/app/src/components/layers.test.ts` gains one rule: a file in `components/molecules/`, `components/organisms/` or `components/templates/` contains no raw `<button`, `<input`, `<select>`, `<textarea` or `<svg` element. Those come from Button, ToolbarButton, Field, Select, Checkbox, Radio, Switch and Icon. Today's molecules, which predate the atoms, are recorded with their current counts and may only go down, the same ratchet features have; a new file starts at zero. The message names the atom to use.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] a new molecule with a raw `<button>` or `<svg>` fails, naming the atom to import (mutation-checked)
- [ ] today's tree passes; lowering a recorded count is a one-line edit

cards.title: The last controls off the one button standard — native dropdown saves, failover drag-to-reorder, busy buttons with no done/failed, and buttons that disable at 0 ms; plus the Members table overflowing at 834 px
cards.description:
**Repo:** agent-bureau (console web)

**CEO, 2026-09-13 08:15 PT:** *"we should be following the same standard for all of the atoms."* [DRE-3756](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3756/every-atom-follows-the-one-button-standard-menu-items-and-icon-buttons) ([dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau#2527](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/review/featdre-3756-every-menu-item-and-icon-button-that-saves-something-c3a03ef6b7a0)) and [DRE-3784](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3784/the-rest-of-the-console-joins-the-one-button-standard-chat-sendretry) ([dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau#2529](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/review/featdre-3784-the-rest-of-the-console-follows-the-one-button-standard-a-0a409877f44f)) converted the menus, the lane dot, the bulk bar, the groom icons, chat, dialogs, members, toggles, the danger zone, the wizard and toast Retry. [DRE-3784](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3784/the-rest-of-the-console-joins-the-one-button-standard-chat-sendretry)**'s builder listed these as still off the standard:**

* **Native** `<select>` **saves:** the Members role select, and Org security's two policy selects. The select itself can't show a busy bar, so the standard runs on the row beside it: pressed, busy after 500 ms, then done or failed.
* **The failover drag-to-reorder:** a drop that saves shows the standard on the dropped row.
* **Busy with no done or failed state yet:** Subscriptions reconnect and add-subscription, DemoReset, CreateCustomer, and Security's "sign out other sessions".
* **Disable at 0 ms instead of showing pressed:** the project MembersCard add and remove, and remove-passkey.
* **Layout bug, already on** `main`**:** at 834 px the Members table squeezes the name column, and its row menu overflows the card.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Every control listed follows the five states. Each has a test holding the write for 2 s and a refusal test.
- [ ] The Members table fits at 834 px with no overflow, measured and shown in a screenshot.
- [ ] The [DRE-3756](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3756/every-atom-follows-the-one-button-standard-menu-items-and-icon-buttons) guard's documented blind spots list shrinks by the patterns this card closes.
- [ ] Screenshots at 1280 and 834, light and dark, attached to the PR.

**Sequencing:** starts after [dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau#2529](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/review/featdre-3784-the-rest-of-the-console-follows-the-one-button-standard-a-0a409877f44f) merges, off fresh `main`.

cards.title: The last 1.7 s — a lone live update reloads at once instead of after the 750 ms quiet window, and the river's InFlight read drops from ~2.5 s to under 1 s, so a Linear edit reaches the console within 3 s
cards.description:
**Repo:** agent-bureau (console web + backend)

**Measured in production, 2026-09-13 10:07–10:09 PT, v1.6.61** (full reading on [DRE-3746](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3746/a-linear-edit-reaches-an-open-console-within-3-s-in-production-the)): a Linear edit reaches the open One River DOM in **4.74 s** at the median, against a 3 s target (13.3 s before today's work). The sixth edit's breakdown:

| step | time |
| -- | -- |
| Linear to SSE frame | 1.02 s |
| frame to refetch start (coalescer quiet window + timer alignment) | 1.00 s |
| slowest refetch, `InFlight` (the river) | 2.56 s |
| render | 9 ms |

## What to build

1. **Fire the leading edge.** When a frame arrives after a quiet stretch, with no delivery in the last 2 s and nothing in flight for the entry, reload at once instead of waiting 750 ms. Keep all of [DRE-3728](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3728/the-live-push-makes-every-open-console-tab-reload-every-panel-on-every)'s guarantees:
   * ≤1 load in flight per query entry
   * ≥2 s between deliveries
   * `cancelRefetch:false`
   * one owed follow-up per entry
   * a burst still coalesces, so only the first frame of a burst fires early

   Tests should use real frame rates, as the v1.6.55 storm lesson requires: a burst of 20 frames in 2 s must produce ≤2 loads per entry.
2. `InFlight` **answers in under 1 s.** The production slow-operation warnings show it ran 2.4–2.85 s with 0 s queued, so the time goes into the store work building the river tree per request. Profile it locally against a copy of the production store's shape, then memoise it on the read-model generation (exact, per tenant, single-flight), the way [DRE-3746](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3746/a-linear-edit-reaches-an-open-console-within-3-s-in-production-the) keyed `pipeline_alert_rows`. Also check `Fleet` (2.2–3.1 s) and `KpiTrends` (2.2–2.8 s), which sit on the same card-edit path, and apply the same treatment where it holds.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Local: a lone frame reloads within 50 ms; a 20-frame burst gives ≤2 loads per entry; `InFlight`, `Fleet` and `KpiTrends` answer in under 100 ms when warm.
- [ ] Production, after release: five edits at a median of ≤3 s (method as on [DRE-3746](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3746/a-linear-edit-reaches-an-open-console-within-3-s-in-production-the)). Record them on [DRE-3746](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3746/a-linear-edit-reaches-an-open-console-within-3-s-in-production-the) and here.
- [ ] Production slow-operation warnings: no `InFlight`, `Fleet` or `KpiTrends` line over 2 s for 15 minutes.

cards.title: portico: the portal knows its branch and how far it is behind main, for the moderator footer
cards.description:
Sid, 2026-09-13, pointing at agent-bureau's sidebar footer (a branch pill reading "main", "22 behind", "v1.6.60 · 60799d0"): "you need to show the version number and for moderators you need to show how this approach for agent bureau". The Source list spec ([DRE-3760](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3760/portico-the-source-list-design-system-and-the-gate-that-holds-every), Account footer) draws it. The bundle already knows its version, build count, commit and build time (`client/app/src/lib/config/buildInfo.ts`, [DRE-2292](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2292/version-stamp-for-the-spa-build-identity-visible-in-the-ui-prod-vs-dev) and [DRE-2301](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2301/human-readable-version-above-the-build-hash-xyz-build-n-in-the)). Two facts are missing.

## What this card does

* **The branch.** `vite.config.ts` stamps the branch it built from into `__PORTICO_BUILD__` beside `sha`, `"unknown"` outside a checkout, the same honest fallback; `vitest.config.ts`'s shim and `buildInfo.test.ts` move with it.
* **How far behind main.** The portal cannot know main's head from the browser, and CI holds no cloud credentials. The release engine already computes "N commits behind" per account (`ship.sh --verify`). This card makes that number reachable by the app with no new credential: the engine records main's build count for each account where the API can read it (an SSM parameter beside the one the edge already reads, or a stamped meta), and a moderator-only read returns `{ servedBuild, mainBuild, behind }`. The card's first commit is a short decision in its PR on which of the two, weighed against the ADR-0003 throughput note.
* Readers never see it: the read is moderator-only, like the usage log.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `buildInfo` carries `branch`, pinned by `buildInfo.test.ts`
- [ ] a moderator's read returns how far the served build is behind main; a reader's is refused with today's refusal shape
- [ ] after `ship.sh --verify` for an account, the number the app shows equals the number the engine printed

cards.title: portico: Branding — a company's logo and colour, stored, checked and served to its portal
cards.description:
Today a portal can carry its name (`portalNames`, [DRE-2277](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2277/the-library-never-says-which-portal-youre-in-root-and-wordmark-both)) and the sign-in email's sender name, and nothing else. The Source list spec's Branding pane (part 6) adds a logo and a brand colour. Test commit first, in `infra/test/branding.test.ts`.

## What this card does

* A pure `infra/lambda/branding_lib.ts`: validates a brand colour (a hex value that keeps 4.5:1 text contrast on white for the main button, with a derived dark-mode value) and a logo (SVG or PNG under a size limit; SVG passed through the same sanitiser rules documents get, no scripts and no external references).
* Storage per project, with a builder; the logo in the project's content store as uploads are, never fetched by link.
* `GET /branding?project=…` for anyone signed in to that portal; `PUT` for whoever Tool access allows (Foundry only by default), writing a change-log event.
* The SPA reads it at boot and sets `--acc` (and only `--acc`) for that portal; status colours, Foundry ink, drive graphite and ↳ never change. A test holds that list.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] a colour that fails the contrast check is refused with a sentence saying why
- [ ] an SVG logo with a script or an external reference is refused
- [ ] GridCorr's brand reaches GridCorr's portal and no other project's
- [ ] the SPA changes only `--acc`, and a test fails if it touches another token

cards.title: portico: Tool access — the per-company setting, and the routes that honour it
cards.description:
Builds what ADR-0007 ([DRE-3779](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3779/portico-adr-0007-per-company-tool-access-and-what-foundry-only-means)) decides. Test commit first, then the code, in `infra/test/tool_access.test.ts`.

## What this card does

* The decision lives in a pure `infra/lambda/tool_access_lib.ts`: given verified claims, a project, a tool and the stored setting, may this caller use it. No AWS SDK in it.
* The setting is stored and read where the ADR says, with a builder in the house style so the key shape cannot drift.
* `GET` and `PUT /tool-access?project=…`: readable by any moderator of that project, writable only by Foundry staff; every change writes a change-log event, so it shows in Activity.
* `POST /people`, the trusted-domain routes, Branding writes ([DRE-3781](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3781/portico-branding-a-companys-logo-and-colour-stored-checked-and-served)) and form placement call the lib and refuse a company moderator where the setting says `foundry`, with today's refusal shape.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] with invites set to `foundry`, a GridCorr moderator's `POST /people` is refused and a Foundry staff member's succeeds (unit tests over the lib and the route table)
- [ ] a company moderator cannot change the setting, even for their own company
- [ ] each guarded route is covered by a route-table-driven test, so a new route that forgets the check fails (the conformance-suite pattern)
- [ ] mutation-checked: removing the check from any one route turns the suite red

cards.title: portico: ADR-0007 — per-company Tool access, and what "Foundry only" means
cards.description:
A decision record, written before any code, because it changes who may do what in every company's portal. Today `moderators` is one account-wide Cognito group (`access_lib.ts`), so a GridCorr moderator can invite into GridCorr, and into VeriCorr if they are in its group too.

## What this card does

`docs/folder-access/ADR-0007-tool-access.md` (Proposed; Sid accepts), in the shape of ADR-0004 and ADR-0005:

* **Who is Foundry staff:** a moderator who is also in the `foundry` project's group ([DRE-3720](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3720/portico-the-foundry-project-in-the-dreadnought-account)), read from verified JWT claims, never the request.
* **The setting:** for each project, each tool (invite people and allow domains, see People, Activity, Branding, place Foundry forms) is `foundry` or `moderators`; the default is today's behaviour except invites, which start as `foundry` as Sid asked. Where it is stored (a `tools#<project>` item beside the library partition, or deploy config), with the ADR-0003 throughput trigger weighed.
* **Which routes check it**, and that a refused request gets the same answer shape as today's moderator refusals.
* **Alternatives rejected**, including per-company moderator groups in Cognito.
* A test pinning the file and this card's pointer, in the `adr_shared_answers.test.ts` style.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] the ADR names the identity rule, the storage, every route that checks the setting, and the default for each tool
- [ ] a test fails if the ADR file or its pointer from CLAUDE.md is removed

cards.title: [EPIC] portico: Branding and Tool access — the server work under the Manage tools
cards.description:

Sid, 2026-09-13: "we can control who can do it. The people one, eventually, we'll give it to the actual company to invite, but not right now because we want to control it more." **Branding** lets a company's portal carry its logo and colour; today only the portal's name ([DRE-2277](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2277/the-library-never-says-which-portal-youre-in-root-and-wordmark-both)) and the sign-in email's sender name exist. This epic is the server half: the settings, where they live, and the routes that honour them. The panes are drawn in part 4 of the rebuild ([DRE-3777](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3777/epic-portico-source-list-rebuild-part-4-every-screen-moves-over-and)).

## Cards

1. ADR: what "Foundry only" means (a moderator who is also in the `foundry` group), where the per-company setting lives, and which routes check it, written before any code because it changes who may do what.
2. Tool access: the per-company setting, stored and read, and `POST /people`, `/trusted-domains`, Branding writes and form placement refusing a company moderator where the setting says Foundry only. TDD in `infra/test/`.
3. Branding: a company's logo (SVG or PNG, size-limited, sanitised the way documents are) and brand colour, stored per project and served to the portal, with a contrast check so the colour stays readable on white and in dark mode.
4. PROOF and DEMO, last.

## Acceptance criteria for the set

- [ ] with People set to Foundry only, a GridCorr moderator's `POST /people` is refused and a Foundry staff member's succeeds, observed on a local backend
- [ ] a logo and colour set for GridCorr reach its portal and no other

cards.title: [EPIC] portico: Source list rebuild, part 4 — every screen moves over, and the old parts go
cards.description:
The wave where Portico actually changes in front of people. Each screen moves from today's components to the templates and organisms of part 3, as drawn in part 6 of `docs/design/system/index.html`, with nothing the app does today dropped. As each old atom loses its last importer it is deleted and leaves `APPROVED` in the same change; when the last screen moves, today's tokens and the Fraunces face go, and the layer ratchet reaches zero. This is the first part that needs a frontend deploy to reach anyone, and the release is Sid's to run. Planned in detail when part 3's DEMO is accepted; it will likely be two epics, library first and then viewer, forms and Manage.

## Outline

* The app shell: Sidebar with Manage, Toolbar, Account menu (theme, Sign out), Search.
* The library: list, icons and columns with the Inspector; Share, Move, Add document and Details sheets; the archive shelf; the Foundry's company drives in the sidebar.
* The viewer: full window with handles; Comments rail with suggestions and agreed wording; the spreadsheet, file, kept-elsewhere and not-available panes.
* Forms: answering with the Answer panel; progress for moderators; the task card for partners; the place sheet.
* Manage: People (with last seen from the usage log, [DRE-3682](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3682/epic-usage-log-who-came-in-when-and-what-they-opened-shown-to)) and Activity, moved; Branding and Tool access panes over the server work of the Branding and Tool access epic.
* Deletions: `StatusChip` (and `STATUS_LABEL`, which query code reads), `Chip`, `Badge`, `DocKindIcon`, `FolderExposureIcon`, `Toggle`, `Empty`, today's molecules, `layout/Sheet.tsx`, the retired handoff bundle, today's tokens, Fraunces.
* The moderator Account footer: branch, how far behind main, version ([DRE-3787](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3787/portico-the-portal-knows-its-branch-and-how-far-it-is-behind-main-for) supplies the data).
* Then PROOF and DEMO. The PROOF checks everything, not a sample (Sid, 2026-09-13: "at the end you should check everything as part of your proof card"): every screen and function in the spec, light, dark and 390px, as moderator and as partner, and the full suites.

## Acceptance criteria for the set

- [ ] every screen in part 6 of the spec exists in the app and matches it, light, dark and at 390px
- [ ] every function listed in part 8 of the spec still works, through its e2e test
- [ ] `components/atoms/` holds exactly the approved set, and the layer ratchet stands at zero

The first wave of rebuilding Portico's UI in the Source list look that Sid chose on 2026-09-12, bottom up, as specified in `docs/design/system/` ([DRE-3760](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3760/portico-the-source-list-design-system-and-the-gate-that-holds-every)). This epic lays the ground every later layer stands on: the new tokens, alongside today's so nothing breaks; per-component visual baselines so builders can work in parallel; a test that holds the layers to their direction; and the 19 atoms in part 2 of the spec. Old and new atoms live side by side until the pages move to the new ones in part 4; nothing on a live screen changes in this epic except through Avatar and ExternalMark, which keep their names.

Sid, 2026-09-13: "Once you've got this all done, then I want you to go build it. You should use sub-agents and build it locally so I can see everything as you go." And: "only atoms can change if I agree that they should change or be added." Every atom's approval record quotes his words and the date.

## The wave

1. **This epic**: tokens and atoms.
2. Molecules (filed, blocked on this).
3. Organisms and templates (filed, blocked on 2).
4. Pages: every screen moves to the new parts and the old atoms and tokens are deleted (filed, blocked on 3, planned when 3 is Done).
5. Server work for Branding and Tool access (its own epic, runs beside 2 and 3).

## How it is built

Each card is hand-built by a sub-agent in its own worktree, on its own `agent/DRE-<n>-…` branch. Finished branches merge into a local integration branch, `ui/rebuild-integration`, which the dev server serves so Sid can watch `/specimen` fill up. Nothing is pushed until Sid says ship. Before any branch joins the integration branch, the component is put beside its section of the spec in Chrome; if it does not match, it does not merge.

cards.title: The groomer writes each batch card's reasons in full and in labelled form (why now, value, effort, if skipped, depends on), so the console's chevron can show them
cards.description:
**Repo:** bureau-pipeline

## Why

CEO, 2026-09-13 08:10–08:25 PT, on the Green Light design page: *"I can open up a row and see all the reasons why this card is the right one to add."*

[DRE-3757](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3757/a-groom-batchs-cards-carry-visible-icon-actions-with-tooltips-not-this) builds that chevron on each groom batch card in the console. The chevron can only show what the proposal carries, and today that is very little. For each batch card, the proposal comment `render_proposal` writes (bureau-pipeline `scripts/groomer.py` on `stable`) carries:

* the position, the priority band, the repo, the epic and the title (cut at 60 characters);
* **one "Why" line, cut at 90 characters** (`_cell(row.get('reason'), 90)`).

`_mark` fills `trigger` only for a not-now row and `evidence` only for a likely-dead row. A batch card has its one `reason` and nothing else. There is no value, effort, if-skipped or depends-on for any card, so the console shows the one line and the position, and says nothing it cannot read.

## What to build

* The ranked read returns labelled reasons for each card it puts in the batch: **why now, value, effort, if skipped, depends on**. Each one goes through `_showable`, as `reason` does. A reason the guard refuses is dropped and counted in `withheld`. Nothing is ever put in its place.
* The proposal comment carries them per card, **in full and uncut**, in their own section after the batch table, so the table the console already reads (`console/backend/groom_proposal.py`, `_BATCH_ROW`) does not change. Example shape: `## Why each card is in the batch`, then `### DRE-N` per card, then `- **Why now:** …` lines. The full "Why" line goes there too.
* The JSON artifact carries the same fields from the same source.
* A rules-only run (`--no-judgement`) writes no labelled reasons, and its comment is byte-identical to today's.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A judged proposal renders the section: every batch card, with its labelled reasons, uncut.
- [ ] A reason the plain-English guard refuses is dropped and listed in `withheld`. No placeholder text is written.
- [ ] A rules-only proposal renders exactly what it renders today (a byte-for-byte test).
- [ ] A test pins the section's grammar (the heading, the per-card heading and the label lines), so the console's reader has a fixed format to parse.

## Out of scope

Reading and showing these in the console. That is a small agent-bureau follow-up once this format lands: `groom_proposal.py` parses the section, and [DRE-3757](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3757/a-groom-batchs-cards-carry-visible-icon-actions-with-tooltips-not-this)'s chevron already renders labelled lines.

cards.title: Every new company gets its Portico share when its first project is set up — created by portico's own deploy, not by a script outside the repo
cards.description:
When a project is set up for a company that has no share yet, setup declares one, and portico's own deploy creates it: `share.<company domain>`, its sign-in group, its trusted sign-up domain and its sign-in pages. When the company already has a share, the project gets its own shelf there instead. Our own internal projects get a shelf on the Foundry drive.

Today a share takes an 11-step operator card ([DRE-3721](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3721/operator-provision-sharedreadnoughtfoundrycom-and-put-ai-readiness-on) is the current one). Most of those steps run `~/Docs/_tool/aws/setup.sh`, which lives outside every repo, followed by hand removal of the passphrase shim, the CDN scripts, `provision-project-grants.ts` and a hand-written `_publish.json`.

This is outcome 2 of epic [DRE-2284](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2284/epic-a-new-project-is-set-up-once-in-the-console-and-is-born-on-the). Read the epic's decision record first. Decisions 3 and 4 govern this card.

## What changes (planner: split on file footprint)

**portico**

* Portico's deploy creates a declared project's bucket, distribution, certificate and alias, attaches the sign-in gate with no passphrase shim (see [DRE-3725](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3725/attach-gatesh-removes-the-legacy-passphrase-cloudfront-function-when)), and applies the CDN behaviours and the report-only CSP. The stack then knows the distribution's own host, so the second "add the cloudfront host" commit ([DRE-3727](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3727/portico-the-foundry-distributions-cloudfront-host-and-its-three)'s shape) is no longer needed.
* The same deploy provisions a new project's grants (the `provision-project-grants.ts` logic, which already refuses to touch existing projects) and publishes its sign-in pages and 404 page without a `~/Docs/<project>/_publish.json`.
* A share whose domain's DNS zone is not in the account stops and says so plainly. It never serves an unmapped host.

**agent-bureau**

* `onboard-customer.py` opens the portico pull request that declares the share (projects, portalNames, trustedSignupDomains, orgDomains and the portals map in `infra/config/<account>.json`), or the shelf on an existing share. It does this through the GitHub API, the same way it already opens the bureau-pipeline pull request. This waits for [DRE-3608](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3608/onboard-customerpy-fails-closed-on-an-unreadable-ssm-routing-map-and) and for outcome 1's change to the same file.

## Order

* [DRE-3717](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3717/epic-the-dreadnought-foundry-drive-sharedreadnoughtfoundrycom-one-step) (the Foundry drive) finishes by hand first, and its run record is the recipe.
* [DRE-3216](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3216/operator-portico-grant-the-portals-release-identity-run-one-supervised) must put portico's own train live and on. Until then, a merged declaration creates nothing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] In portico, `npm run synth` for a config that declares a new project shows its bucket, distribution, certificate and gate association. Every existing share's resources are byte-identical.
- [ ] The first deploy after a declaration merges leaves `verify-portal.sh <project>` passing, with a signed-out request redirected to `auth-gate.html`. Recorded in the repo.
- [ ] `onboard-customer.py --share new --share-domain <d>` opens one portico pull request that passes portico's `portal_naming`, `org_domains` and `account_roster_in_docs` tests. `--share shelf:<existing>` declares a shelf and creates no new distribution.
- [ ] `~/Docs/_tool/aws/setup.sh` is no longer on the path for a new share, and the new-project section of `infra/config/README.md` says so.

cards.title: Every new project is born on the release train — its first lane is added from a template when there's something to release, switched off, with the one card that turns it on
cards.description:
When a project is set up, it leaves setup on the release train with its first surface declared. Today it leaves with the train workflow and an empty `release.json` ([DRE-3211](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3211/agent-bureau-the-scaffold-ships-the-ninth-stub-release-trainyml-plus)), which means nothing ever releases until someone writes a script, a rollback, an AWS role and a card by hand. That happened three times in September for the website, the relay and portico's shares, and each took its own card.

This is outcome 1 of epic [DRE-2284](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2284/epic-a-new-project-is-set-up-once-in-the-console-and-is-born-on-the). Read the epic's decision record first. Decisions 1 and 2 govern this card.

## What happens after this card

* Setup asks nothing about releasing (epic decision 1). The project is on the train from its first minute, with no lane, and the fleet sweep reports "nothing to release yet" rather than calling it missing.
* The card that builds the project's first releasable thing (a website, a web service or a function) adds its lane from a scaffold template: one `release.json` entry at `auto: false`, the template's release script and its rollback. The engineer brief says so. A lane can also be added from the project's Settings tab, which opens the same change as a pull request.
* Declaring a lane files one Needs-you card carrying the exact commands: deploy the release role in the account from Settings → New projects (or the project's override), set `RELEASE_ROLE_ARN`, run the first supervised release, and run one rollback. Turning `auto` on stays the CEO's decision.

## Where it lands (planner: split on file footprint)

* `scaffold/`: three surface templates generalised from `infra/release-website.sh`, `infra/release-console.sh` and `cloud/relay/release-relay.sh`, plus a release-role template that imports the account's existing GitHub OIDC provider. A second provider for the same URL fails CloudFormation, which is what portico found in [DRE-3212](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3212/portico-the-portals-join-the-train-through-porticos-own-stub-and-data).
* `bureau-pipeline/briefs/engineer.md` (operator-routed): when a card builds the first releasable thing, it declares that thing's lane from the template. The Needs-you card is filed when a lane is first declared; the planner picks the seam. Anything that touches `scripts/onboard-customer.py` waits for [DRE-3608](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3608/onboard-customerpy-fails-closed-on-an-unreadable-ssm-routing-map-and), which edits the same file.
* `scripts/check_pipeline_channel.py`: the train column reads `release.json` and reports releasing, declared but off, nothing to ship yet, no train, or UNKNOWN. Today it only checks that the stub file exists.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each of the three templates, applied to a fictitious repo, yields a `release.json` entry at `auto: false` with a release script and a rollback, all passing bureau-pipeline's `release.json` check.
- [ ] A freshly onboarded repo has an empty `surfaces` block, and the fleet sweep reports it as "nothing to release yet", not as failing.
- [ ] The Needs-you card filed when a lane is declared names the role template, the secret, and the two dispatch commands with the project's slug filled in.
- [ ] `make check-channel-fleet` prints the new train reading for every roster repo. For today's fleet that is agent-bureau releasing, bureau-pipeline and portico declared but off, and atlas, deltasolv and agent-bureau-demo with no train.

cards.title: The groom batch discards the model's picks — a collision rule pulls older cards forward, so 14 of batch 1's 18 and 13 of batch 2's 20 were cards the model said should wait
cards.description:
**Repo:** bureau-pipeline

**Found by the** [DRE-3151](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3151/operator-audit-the-groomers-first-two-judged-batches-by-hand-every) **audit, 2026-09-12 21:39 PT; filed on the CEO's instruction to go through** [DRE-3151](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3151/operator-audit-the-groomers-first-two-judged-batches-by-hand-every) **and bring him the outcome.**

## What happened

The groomer's judgement run picks which cards should be worked now. The batch it then proposes does not follow those picks:

* **Batch 1** (`f673bfefa340`, 2026-09-08): the model called 27 cards "now"; only **4** made the 18-card batch. **14 of the 18** were cards the model said should wait (13) or declined to rank (1). Its own picks were pushed out to cycles 22–23.
* **Batch 2** (`42ed15f7527d`, approved and drained 2026-09-12 21:30 PT): **13 of its 20** cards are ones the model said should wait.

The mechanism, traced for four cards: the collision ordering places an older card ahead of a newer one that touches the same file, and that ordering runs AFTER the model's ranking and overrides it, pulling older "not now" cards into the batch. [DRE-2506](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2506/every-pr-pushes-partner-names-to-the-gh-pages-branch-one-settings) and the four [DRE-3004](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3004/dre-2810s-stub-fix-never-reached-portico-or-deltasolv-the-fix-loop) cards could not be traced from the saved run.

Consequence on the audit (full table on [DRE-3151](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3151/operator-audit-the-groomers-first-two-judged-batches-by-hand-every)): the model's own calls agreed with the CEO's 15 of 25; the rules-only run agreed 17 of 26; **the batch as placed agreed 7 of 26.** The judgement is being paid for and then thrown away by the ordering step.

## What to build

The collision rule orders cards WITHIN the set the model picked (so two picks touching one file still land in a safe order); it never admits a card the model did not pick. If a pick must wait on an older colliding card, the older card is named in the proposal as a blocker, not silently promoted into the batch.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] RED first: a replay of batch 1's saved model answer (`run1/` artifact of the 2026-09-08 run) produces a batch whose cards are all ones the model called "now" (or explicitly named blockers), and the current code fails it.
- [ ] A test with two model picks touching one file orders them oldest first without admitting a third, unpicked card.
- [ ] The proposal comment shows, per batch card, whether it is a model pick or a named blocker.
- [ ] PROOF: the next judged proposal's batch, compared to its own model answer, contains no unpicked, unnamed card — recorded here with the proposal id and PT time.

**Related:** [DRE-3544](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3544/a-card-the-groomer-could-not-rank-must-never-appear-in-the-proposed) (a declined card under 14 days old still enters the batch — the same "the batch ignores the model" family).

cards.title: Console releases v1.6.50–v1.6.55 carry cards whose pull requests never changed the console — take them off by hand; the filter that stops it landed in DRE-3707 after these six were cut
cards.description:
**CEO, 2026-09-12 ~21:15 PT**, looking at Linear's Releases view (`agent-bureau-console-v1.6.50` … `v1.6.55`, 12 / 2 / 5 / 4 / 7 / 3 cards): *"you need to move these other releases to their own release and not the console."*

## Why

* The six releases were cut by `scripts/linear_release.py` **as it stood before PR** [dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau#2499](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/review/dre-3707-the-website-and-relay-release-into-their-own-linear-pipelines-1d6ae2663d03) **(**[DRE-3707](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3707/every-train-surface-gets-its-own-linear-release-pipeline-website-and)**)**. The train runs the script from the commit it releases, and v1.6.55's commit (`296d95fc7`) is the merge just before [dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau#2499](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/review/dre-3707-the-website-and-relay-release-into-their-own-linear-pipelines-1d6ae2663d03) (`765315548`, 16:48 PT). So all six ran the old card picker.
* The old picker is `commits_since` at `scripts/linear_release.py:533-572` (pre-#2499), called from `sync` at `:843-846`. It went wrong in two ways:
  1. `--full-history` **with a path filter (**`:559-564`**)** keeps any merge that differs from *any* parent. A branch cut before main's later console commits always differs from its own tip under `console/`. That is how the merges for [DRE-3663](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3663/the-light-runner-tier-built-from-the-2026-09-11-measurement-a-second) (runner tier), [DRE-3675](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3675/adr-the-runner-fleet-on-owned-hardware-the-2026-09-12-mac-mini-shape) and [DRE-3677](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3677/adr-amendment-the-consoles-live-channel-has-never-connected-in) (ADRs), [DRE-3691](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3691/the-nightly-standards-regenerate-bumps-the-dreadnought-standards) (plugin) and [DRE-3692](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3692/every-repos-claudemd-points-a-session-at-the-one-card-standard-the) (scaffold) got onto console releases without touching a console file.
  2. **It read the whole commit body (**`%B`**,** `:560`**)** and attached every `DRE-n` in it. Cards mentioned *as history* inside another card's commit got attached: [DRE-3665](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3665/a-dependabot-pull-request-gets-a-linear-card-of-its-own-the-consoles), [DRE-2027](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2027/restrict-linear-syncs-done-transition-to-gate-merged-agent-branches-a), [DRE-3493](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3493/proactive-actions-spend-warning-on-the-live-org-usage-endpoint-as-a), [DRE-3268](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3268/the-release-role-cannot-read-migrationtaskstacks-outputs-the-first) (v1.6.50), [DRE-3182](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3182/auto-switch-executor-on-a-429-or-three-limit-deaths-in-fifteen-minutes) (v1.6.52), [DRE-3678](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3678/the-strips-slow-facts-follow-the-release-deploy-lag-and-abandoned-work), [DRE-3679](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3679/the-capacity-strip-says-how-old-each-slow-fact-is-one-age-vocabulary), [DRE-2840](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2840/operator-prove-phase-7-grooming-scoring-and-the-cutover) (v1.6.54), [DRE-2840](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2840/operator-prove-phase-7-grooming-scoring-and-the-cutover) (v1.6.55).
* [DRE-3707](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3707/every-train-surface-gets-its-own-linear-release-pipeline-website-and) already fixed the picker on `main`: it walks main's first-parent line, judges each pull request by what its merge changed, filters by `.github/bureau/release.json` paths, and reads only the merge's own card id. Relay-v12 (17:03 PT) is the first release cut with it, and it carries one card, [DRE-3707](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3707/every-train-surface-gets-its-own-linear-release-pipeline-website-and). **The next console release will be the first console release cut with it.** No code change is needed. This card fixes the Linear data those six releases left behind.

## What lands

* For each card on v1.6.50–v1.6.55, work out which surface or surfaces it really changed. Use main's own oracle: [DRE-3707](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3707/every-train-surface-gets-its-own-linear-release-pipeline-website-and)'s `commits_since` + `issue_references`, run over each release's range (previous release sha..this release sha) against `release.json` paths, for console, website and relay.
* Take every card the oracle does not put on the console off that release. If a card belongs on a website or relay release that exists in Linear for the same period, add it there. If none exists, it goes on no release. No release is deleted and no note text is edited.
* Post the table (release → card → was → should be → evidence) as a comment here.
* Dry-run the same check over v1.6.40–v1.6.49 and report the count. Do not apply it there without saying so.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] v1.6.50 carries 7 cards, v1.6.51 2, v1.6.52 2, v1.6.53 4, v1.6.54 2, v1.6.55 2, each re-read from Linear after the writes
- [ ] Every card taken off is listed in a comment with the commit that wrongly attached it, and where it went (another surface's release, or none)
- [ ] No release is deleted and no release note is edited
- [ ] Cases where the path rule and the CEO's intent part ways are named for his call, not decided here

cards.title: attach-gate.sh removes the legacy passphrase CloudFront Function when it attaches the edge gate
cards.description:
`~/Docs/_tool/aws/setup.sh` still attaches a `docs-auth-<company>` CloudFront Function, the old passphrase gate, to every new distribution's default behaviour. `infra/scripts/attach-gate.sh` sets only `LambdaFunctionAssociations`, so the shim stays attached unless someone removes it by hand. gridcorr's run record ([DRE-2263](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2263/operator-provision-the-gridcorr-portal-sharegridcorrcom-born-on-the)) lists it as outstanding, and the Foundry portal ([DRE-3721](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3721/operator-provision-sharedreadnoughtfoundrycom-and-put-ai-readiness-on), step 4) will need the same hand edit.

The only tool that zeroes `FunctionAssociations` today is the retired `_tool/aws/signin-gate.sh`, which reads the other clone's config and must not be used ([DRE-2427](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2427/signin-gatesh-silently-re-attaches-the-old-edge-version-when-the)).

## What this card does

* `attach-gate.sh` sets `DefaultCacheBehavior.FunctionAssociations` to `{ "Quantity": 0 }` in the same distribution update that attaches the gate, but only when every existing association is a `docs-auth-*` function. Any other CloudFront Function makes it stop, naming the function.
* Its read-back asserts `FunctionAssociations.Quantity == 0` along with the Lambda version.
* A test of the jq transform in the style of the existing attach tests: a distribution carrying the shim comes out with none, and one carrying a foreign function is refused.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] a distribution with a `docs-auth-*` association comes out of the transform with none, and the attach still sets the gate
- [ ] a distribution with any other CloudFront Function is refused, with the function named
- [ ] the read-back fails if a function association survives
- [ ] test commit first; `cd infra && npm test` green

cards.title: [EPIC] The Foundry originates every form — upload a template on the Foundry shelf, send it to a company, place it into that company's folder
cards.description:
Every form starts at Dreadnought Foundry. A Foundry moderator uploads a template onto the Foundry shelf. From that shelf, one dialog sends it to GridCorr, VeriCorr or DeltaSolv and, in the same step, places it into a chosen folder in each company's library. Companies never write forms; they receive and place them. EveryBite is a separate account, so it keeps receiving from the build catalogue and is never a Send target.

This is stage two of the plan Sid approved on 2026-09-12 (package 2, "control room"): [https://claude.ai/code/artifact/bfb929ea-1f7c-4a90-b018-22b8d7bc20fe](<https://claude.ai/code/artifact/bfb929ea-1f7c-4a90-b018-22b8d7bc20fe>). It waits for stage one ([DRE-3717](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3717/epic-the-dreadnought-foundry-drive-sharedreadnoughtfoundrycom-one-step)), because the Send dialog's list of companies is the Company drives list that stage one stamps into the Foundry page, and the Foundry project has to exist. Its cards are written here as the plan. They are filed as child cards when stage one is Done, so they describe the portal as it actually came out.

## The planned cards

1. **ADR-0006, the Foundry is the form origin.** The account's `formOrigin` project is where templates are written. Its moderators may send a template to a sibling project in the same account and place it there. The Foundry page may read a sibling project's library for that dialog, gated by the caller's own membership of that project. The companies' existing script path onto their own shelves stays open.
2. **The send route.** `POST /library/forms/send { project, templateId, target, parentId }`. It gates on both projects, loads the Foundry definition on the server (nothing returns a definition to the browser), and upserts it into the target shelf through the same `upsertTemplate` the script uses. It then optionally places it through the placement logic extracted from `POST /library/docs/form`, so the two can never disagree. It records `sentTo` on the Foundry row. `GET /library/forms` says whether this project is the origin. Config key `formOrigin`, env `FORM_ORIGIN`.
3. **New template, on the Foundry shelf.** Drop or choose a `definition.json`. A shallow preview shows title, version and counts. The server's parser is the check, and its refusal shows inline.
4. **Send to a company.** From a Foundry template's menu: tick companies, pick a folder in each or leave it shelf-only, and read one line per company saying who will be able to answer. Outcomes are reported per company.
5. **PROOF**, then **DEMO**. Upload a template, send v1 into Oncor's folder on GridCorr and shelf-only to DeltaSolv, see an Oncor reader find it, then send v2 and see the Oncor instance keep v1.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A template uploaded on the Foundry shelf can be sent to each dreadnought-account company and placed into a folder there, from the Foundry screen alone
- [ ] No company portal offers New template or Send
- [ ] EveryBite still receives forms from the build catalogue, and is not offered as a Send target

On [share.everybite.com](<http://share.everybite.com>) he sees the **From the Foundry** group ([DRE-3104](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3104/the-shelf-lists-the-templates-this-build-carries-and-one-button-puts-a)) and puts AI Readiness on EveryBite's shelf with one click. That is how EveryBite receives forms.

A walkthrough artifact with screenshots of each step is published before the demo, so he can look first.

cards.title: OPERATOR: provision share.dreadnoughtfoundry.com and put AI Readiness on the Foundry shelf
cards.description:
The live steps that turn the `foundry` config into a working portal. Every step is Sid's, in his own terminal, in this order. It is the order `infra/config/README.md` gives for a new project, and gridcorr's run record ([DRE-2263](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2263/operator-provision-the-gridcorr-portal-sharegridcorrcom-born-on-the)) followed it. Record each step's output in `docs/runbooks/foundry-provisioning.md`.

 1. **The zone.** `dreadnoughtfoundry.com` is a hosted zone in the dreadnought account (read on 2026-09-12). Confirm the registrar's name servers match it before anything points at it.
 2. **First deploy.** After [DRE-3726](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3726/the-ses-reputation-alarm-reads-one-account-wide-total-a-fourth-project) (the SES alarm fix) and [DRE-3720](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3720/portico-the-foundry-project-in-the-dreadnought-account) (the foundry project config) both merge, in that order: `bash infra/scripts/ship.sh --only dreadnought`. This creates the `foundry` Cognito group and a new edge version, and the lap attaches it to vericorr, deltasolv and gridcorr.
 3. **The roster and the distribution.** Add to `~/Docs/_tool/aws/companies.sh`: `foundry` to `ALL_COMPANIES`, `foundry) echo "dreadnought" ;;` in `profile_for`, and `foundry) echo "share.dreadnoughtfoundry.com" ;;` in `domain_for`. Then run `~/Docs/_tool/aws/setup.sh foundry`. It creates the bucket, the distribution, the certificate and the alias, and prints the `*.cloudfront.net` host. Hand that host to the session, which builds [DRE-3727](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3727/portico-the-foundry-distributions-cloudfront-host-and-its-three) with it.
 4. **Remove the passphrase shim.** `setup.sh` still attaches a `docs-auth-foundry` CloudFront Function, and `attach-gate.sh` only sets the Lambda association. Remove the function association from the default behaviour. After step 5, check that `FunctionAssociations.Quantity` is 0.
 5. **Second deploy.** After [DRE-3727](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3727/portico-the-foundry-distributions-cloudfront-host-and-its-three) (the cloudfront host and the three company drives in config) merges: `bash infra/scripts/ship.sh --only dreadnought`. The edge bundle changes again, so all four portals are re-attached.
 6. **CDN behaviours** via the `infra/cdn/` scripts: assets, content, fonts, 403→404, and the report-only CSP.
 7. **Grants.** `cd infra && npx tsx scripts/provision-project-grants.ts --account dreadnought --project foundry --profile dreadnought`, read the plan, then run the same command with `--apply`. Then, signed in as a moderator, raise `dreadnoughtfoundry.com` to **editor** at the root in the share panel, so staff can work and not only read.
 8. **People.** Put `<redacted-email>` in the `foundry` group. One more [dreadnoughtfoundry.com](<http://dreadnoughtfoundry.com>) mailbox self-signs up, to prove the trusted domain.
 9. **Publish.** Create `~/Docs/foundry/_publish.json` with auth pages, widget and 404, and no content. Then run `bash infra/scripts/ship.sh --only dreadnought --project foundry`. The page shell is stamped `foundry` with the three company drives.
10. **Verify.** `infra/scripts/verify-portal.sh foundry --profile dreadnought`. A signed-out request to the root must be redirected to sign-in.
11. **AI Readiness.** Signed in at the portal, run `copy(localStorage.eb_id_token)` in the console, then hand the token to the session. The session runs `cd infra && PORTICO_ID_TOKEN=… npx tsx scripts/shelf-template.ts foundry ai-readiness` once and prints the shelf back.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] the run record holds each step's output
- [ ] a signed-out request to [share.dreadnoughtfoundry.com](<http://share.dreadnoughtfoundry.com>) is redirected to `auth-gate.html`
- [ ] `FunctionAssociations` is empty on the default behaviour
- [ ] `lib#foundry` holds the two bridge grants, the domain grant at editor, and the AI Readiness shelf row

cards.title: [EPIC] The Dreadnought Foundry drive — share.dreadnoughtfoundry.com, one step from every company's drive, AI Readiness on its shelf
cards.description:
Dreadnought Foundry gets its own Portico drive at [share.dreadnoughtfoundry.com](<http://share.dreadnoughtfoundry.com>), for Foundry staff only. Its home page shows the GridCorr, VeriCorr and DeltaSolv drives as three tiles, one click each, on the login Sid already has. The AI Readiness form sits on its shelf from day one. This is stage one of two. Stage two, which makes the Foundry the place every form is written and sent from, is its own epic, blocked on this one.

Decided by Sid on 2026-09-12, from the walkthrough at [https://claude.ai/code/artifact/bfb929ea-1f7c-4a90-b018-22b8d7bc20fe](<https://claude.ai/code/artifact/bfb929ea-1f7c-4a90-b018-22b8d7bc20fe>) ("package 2, in two stages"):

* It is a Portico portal, not a Google Shared Drive. Staff only.
* The project is called `foundry`. The AWS account stays `dreadnought`. One word for two things is the mistake the `vericorr` account and project made, and it cost a whole section of CLAUDE.md.
* Tiles for the three portals in the dreadnought account only. EveryBite is a separate account and a separate login, so it has no tile. It receives forms from the build catalogue instead ([DRE-3104](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3104/the-shelf-lists-the-templates-this-build-carries-and-one-button-puts-a)).
* AI Readiness is the one template on the Foundry shelf on day one.

## Why

The Foundry runs three companies' portals and has no drive of its own. Its staff work inside GridCorr's library today, on a root editor grant written by hand on 2026-09-04 ([DRE-3105](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3105/gridcorrs-library-lost-its-internalexternal-regions)).

## Cards, in order

1. The publisher stamps the company-drive list into the page shell. Infra only.
2. The Company drives tiles on the library home. Page only. Independent of card 1, because both sides write the same meta name `portico-company-portals` and the page shows nothing until a stamp exists.
3. The `foundry` project in `infra/config/dreadnought.json`. Blocked by card 1, because its `companyPortals` entry has to pass card 1's config test.
4. OPERATOR: provision the portal and shelve AI Readiness. Blocked by cards 2 and 3.
5. PROOF, then DEMO. Both blocked by every card above, and the DEMO also by [DRE-3104](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3104/the-shelf-lists-the-templates-this-build-carries-and-one-button-puts-a).

The full plan, with every file: `/Users/fsconklin/.claude/plans/bubbly-jumping-lovelace.md` (local). The walkthrough artifact above is the readable version.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A signed-out request to [share.dreadnoughtfoundry.com](<http://share.dreadnoughtfoundry.com>) is sent to sign-in, and a Foundry address signs in
- [ ] The library home shows three Company drives tiles. Each opens its portal in a new tab, and a Foundry person arrives already signed in
- [ ] AI Readiness is on the Foundry shelf
- [ ] No other portal's library home changed
- [ ] Every card closed itself on merge, on an `agent/DRE-<n>-*` branch

cards.title: The groomer posts a proposal marker for an empty batch, and a blank cycle name breaks the proposal's title line — a dry run on 2026-09-04 left a 0-card "decision" in the CEO's queue for eight days
cards.description:
**Repo:** bureau-pipeline

The producer half of [DRE-3708](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3708/green-light-asks-the-ceo-to-decide-a-groom-proposal-of-0-cards-on-a) (the console half, PR agent-bureau [dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau#2497](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/review/fixdre-3708-an-empty-groom-proposal-or-one-on-a-closed-card-is-not-a-76f6e7c9a07a), stops SHOWING such proposals as decisions).

## What happened

On **2026-09-04 10:21 PT** the groomer posted `🧺 groom-proposal: 2b10ecfb36f6` on [DRE-2840](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2840/operator-prove-phase-7-grooming-scoring-and-the-cutover): 0 of 0 cards, blank cycle name — a dry-run demonstration while Intake was empty (the next comment says so). The console read it as an open proposal; on 2026-09-12 at ~15:20 PT the CEO found it in Green Light "waiting 196.9 h" and asked *"is there something else going on here I should know?"* The alert title read "0 cards for cycle 0 cards of 0 in Intake…" because, with a blank cycle, the title pattern (the console's copy mirrors the groomer's) captures the next line.

## What to build

* The groomer posts **no** proposal marker when the batch is empty, and a dry run posts no marker at all (it can print its would-be proposal to the run log).
* A proposal with no cycle name either names the cycle it would use or omits the "for cycle …" clause; the title line is well-formed for every input. Change the pattern in lockstep with the console's copy (the two-copies rule — note the console file in the PR so the parent session can mirror it).
* Tests: empty batch → no marker; dry run → no marker; blank cycle → a title the console's reader parses as intended.

## Acceptance

- [ ] RED first on all three tests
- [ ] No `🧺 groom-proposal:` comment is ever written for 0 cards
- [ ] The title line parses identically in the groomer and the console reader for a blank and a named cycle

cards.title: The Red-Main Repair loop names its branch repair/<sha>, so its own card never sees its PR — the card promises to close "through the card id in the branch name" and the branch carries none
cards.description:
**Repo:** bureau-pipeline

**Filed on the CEO's explicit instruction, 2026-09-12 ~16:00 PT, overriding INTAKE_HOLD:** "Everything should have a card associated with it."

## What happened

The Red-Main Repair loop files a card for every red main (e.g. [DRE-3570](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3570/red-main-repaired-integration-harness-failed-at-657651b56a86) "Red main repaired — Integration Harness failed at 657651b56a86") whose acceptance criteria say it is **"Closed by the merge, through the card id in the branch name."** It then pushes the repair on `repair/<full sha>` — a branch with **no card id in it**. Six repairs have merged this way (bureau-pipeline #208, #266, #267, #312, #340, #355, 2026-08-29 → 2026-09-10).

Consequences, observed:

* `linear-sync` cannot close the card on merge, so it sits In Progress; the unlanded-work watchdog then reports "nothing to point at: no branch, no pull request" ([DRE-3570](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3570/red-main-repaired-integration-harness-failed-at-657651b56a86) at 187 min).
* On 2026-09-12 09:53 PT an operator session read that and **cancelled** [DRE-3570](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3570/red-main-repaired-integration-harness-failed-at-657651b56a86) **as never repaired** — the repair had merged on 2026-09-10 12:45 PT as #355. Corrected to Done at 16:00 PT.
* The console's Pull Requests and Activity rows show the repair PR with no card.

## What to build

The repair branch carries the card: `agent/DRE-<n>-red-main-<short sha>` (the prefix every gate already reads, so the merge gate, fix loop and linear-sync all apply), and the PR body links the card. If a separate `repair/` prefix must survive for the merge gate's repair-specific handling, it becomes `repair/DRE-<n>-<short sha>` and every reader of the branch (merge-gate, linear-sync, the watchdog, the console's card extraction) matches the card id in it — one parser, not six.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] RED first: a test over the repair loop asserts the branch it creates carries `DRE-<n>` of the card it filed, and linear-sync's card extraction resolves that branch to that card.
- [ ] The repair card's acceptance line and the branch the loop creates agree (no card promising a closer that cannot fire).
- [ ] PROOF: the next red-main repair's card closes on its own merge — card id, PR number, PT time recorded here.

**Files:** the Red-Main Repair workflow and script in bureau-pipeline (grep `repair/` under `scripts/` and `.github/workflows/`), linear-sync's branch parser, their tests.

cards.title: The wave commit stamps every child epic with the WAVE's repo label — a child the wave plan places in another repo gets its planner dispatched to the wrong one (DRE-3694, 2026-09-12); the commit reads each epic's repo from the plan, or asks
cards.description:
**Repo:** bureau-pipeline

## What happened

The wave [DRE-3681](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3681/epic-the-claude-subscription-chain-is-seamless-the-console-stops) was approved at 2026-09-12 14:57 PT and `wave_commitment.py commit` created its eight epics at 15:13 PT. The wave plan says of epic 2, "A run death carries its error body … This one is built in the pipeline repo", and the wave card's own body flags it `(bureau-pipeline)`. The commit gave all eight children the wave's label, `repo:agent-bureau`. When [DRE-3694](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3694/a-run-death-carries-its-error-body-so-throttled-revoked-and-capped-are) entered Planning the relay dispatched its planner to **agent-bureau** (run 34722161017), where none of its files exist. The operator caught it within two minutes, relabelled the card, cancelled the run and bounced the card Backlog → Planning so the relay would dispatch to bureau-pipeline.

## What to build

1. `wave_commitment.py commit` reads each epic's repo from the wave plan (the plan artifact names it; the commitment record should carry a `repo` field per epic, defaulting to the wave's when the plan is silent) and labels the child with that repo.
2. When the plan names a repo that is not in `config/repo-map.json` (or the wave's org), the commit refuses that epic with a plain-English line on the wave card rather than guessing.
3. RED first: `tests/test_wave_commitment*.py` — a wave plan with one epic marked for another repo commits a child carrying that repo's label; a plan naming an unknown repo refuses with the epic named.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The RED test fails on `origin/main` and passes after; existing wave-commitment tests unchanged and green.
- [ ] The commitment record on the wave card shows the repo per epic.
- [ ] PROOF: the next wave with a cross-repo epic dispatches that epic's planner to the right repo, run URL and PT time recorded here.

## Not in this card

Re-parenting or relabelling epics already committed ([DRE-3694](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3694/a-run-death-carries-its-error-body-so-throttled-revoked-and-capped-are) was fixed by hand).

**Files:** `bureau-pipeline/scripts/wave_commitment.py`, `bureau-pipeline/tests/test_wave_commitment*.py`, the wave plan standard if it must name the field.

cards.title: The mini runner containers are not ephemeral — `restart: always` brings the SAME container back with its writable layer, so /tmp and the work dir survive from job to job; a stale critic verdict was re-posted from one 30 minutes later
cards.description:
**Observed 2026-09-12 15:10 PT.** Two `call / review` jobs on agent-bureau PR [dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau#2488](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/review/featdre-2625-a-hold-open-sse-probe-endpoint-so-app-runners-stream-c3fd85d709db) — run 34720547204 at 21:38Z and run 34721696440 at 22:09Z — report **different runner names** (`bureau-mini-light-NQGOL3UpobHRC`, then `bureau-mini-light-iwiu5Ms2fo6W2`) and the **same** `Machine name: '20c99a9b84ff'`: one container, two registrations. The second job's Resolve PR step died on a transient TLS timeout, the critic was skipped, and the workflow found the FIRST job's `/tmp/qa-verdict.md` still on disk and posted it as a verdict with no sha ([DRE-3701](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3701/qa-review-posts-a-stale-verdict-with-no-sha-when-resolve-pr-dies-on-a) is the workflow half).

**Repo:** agent-bureau

## Why

`scripts/runners/docker-compose.yml` sets `EPHEMERAL: "1"` and `restart: always`, and its own comment says the container "takes ONE job, exits, and `restart: always` brings a fresh one … required, not a preference: agent jobs branch on `/tmp/agent-blocker.txt` and `/tmp/agent-escalation.txt` existing, and on a persistent runner a leftover file from card A parks card B in Backlog." But a Docker **restart is not a fresh container**: the writable layer — `/tmp`, `/_work`, anything a job wrote outside `/cache` — is exactly as the last job left it. Only the runner registration is new. So the hazard the comment was written to prevent is live: a blocker file, an escalation file, a verdict file, or a token file from job A is present for job B. `scripts/runners/Dockerfile` adds no cleanup and the base entrypoint does not wipe `/tmp`.

## What to build

* A thin entrypoint wrapper in the image (`scripts/runners/Dockerfile`) that removes `/tmp/*`, `/_work/*` (everything but the mounted `/cache`) BEFORE handing off to the base entrypoint, so a restart is as clean as a first start. Prefer this over `tmpfs: /tmp` (a tmpfs counts against the 4 GB cap and some jobs write tarballs there).
* `scripts/runners/tests/` gains a test that builds the wrapper's cleanup list from the compose file's declared volumes (only `/cache` survives) and pins it; `check-runners.sh` gains a row that reads a marker file written by the previous job and reports `STALE FS` if it is ever present at job start (a canary the drill can exercise).
* README: the ephemeral rule re-stated with the mechanism ("restart keeps the layer; the entrypoint wipes it").
* Operator note: the image is rebuilt and the pool drained/started (`drain-runners.sh` → build → `start-runners.sh`), per the compose rules; the CEO runs it as a script that carries its own ssh.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A file written to `/tmp` by one job is absent at the start of the next job on the same container (drill: write a marker in a throwaway workflow run, read it in the next; the check-runners row shows clean)
- [ ] `/cache` still survives (npm/pip cache hit rate unchanged in the drill)
- [ ] The pinned test on the cleanup list is green; `make check-runners` (or the existing runner tests) green
- [ ] Applied on the mini and recorded with the drill's two run ids and PT times

cards.title: qa-review posts a STALE verdict with no @sha when Resolve PR dies on a transient GitHub error — the critic never ran, the old verdict file was still on the runner's /tmp, and the fix agent was dispatched at a phantom
cards.description:
**Observed 2026-09-12 15:10 PT on agent-bureau PR** [dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau#2488](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/review/featdre-2625-a-hold-open-sse-probe-endpoint-so-app-runners-stream-c3fd85d709db) (`agent/DRE-2625-sse-hold-probe`, head `3a3faf6b9`, the fix agent's push after a REQUEST_CHANGES). Run 34721696440, job `call / review` (qa-review.yml @ `stable` = `edcacd997`).

**Repo:** bureau-pipeline

## What happened, from the job log

1. `Decide review` → review=true. `Resolve PR` (step 6) died at 22:09:22Z: `Post "https://api.github.com/graphql": net/http: TLS handshake timeout` under `bash -e`. A transient blip.
2. Every critic step was skipped (7–19, 21–24) — **no critic ran on this head**.
3. `Gate critic result (attempt 1)` (step 20) still printed `critic result gate: ok — real verdict`, because `/tmp/qa-verdict.md` and the exec file EXISTED: they were the **first review's** files (21:49 PT, head `23c777b86`), still on the runner. That review ran on `bureau-mini-light-NQGOL3UpobHRC`; this job ran on `bureau-mini-light-iwiu5Ms2fo6W2` — a DIFFERENT container, so `/tmp` is shared across the pool's containers (host mount) or survives the restart. Verify on the mini; either way the workflow must not trust a pre-existing verdict file.
4. `Post verdict or neutral status` (`if: always() && … review == 'true'`) posted the stale body as `🔎 QA Critic — VERDICT: REQUEST_CHANGES cause:defect @` — **empty** `REVIEWED_SHA`**, no content id** — at 22:10:23Z. Its text demands a cap that head `3a3faf6b9` already has.
5. `Publish review check on the reviewed head` failed three times: `No commit found for SHA:  (HTTP 422)`; the `QA critic review` check on the head reads FAILURE.
6. That comment dispatched `Agent Fix` run 34722000359 (attempt 2) against code the critic never saw. The UI session cancelled it at 15:13 PT and re-ran the failed review job with `gh run rerun 34721696440 --failed`.

Cost: a wasted fix run, a red check on a clean head, and a PR that would have sat until a person read the log — the "nothing repairs the gates" shape.

## What to build

* **The post step requires the resolve step:** `Post verdict or neutral status` and the check publisher run only when `steps.pr.outcome == 'success'` AND a critic step actually produced the verdict this run (gate on `steps.critic.outcome`/`steps.critic_retry.outcome`, not on the file's presence). A run whose Resolve PR failed posts a neutral "review did not run — transient <error>, re-run" line, never a verdict, and exits non-zero so the medic's one retry fires.
* **No stale verdict can be read:** the job's first step removes `/tmp/qa-verdict.md`, `/tmp/qa-evidence-hold.md`, the exec file and `/tmp/qa-*.json`, and `check_critic_result.py` refuses a verdict file older than the job's start. Pin both with tests (a fixture verdict file pre-seeded on disk must NOT be posted).
* **Resolve PR survives one blip:** the three `gh` reads in that step retry once on a transport error (the [DRE-3087](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3087/the-reconcile-sweep-survives-one-transient-network-fault-a-connection) shape), so a single TLS timeout is not a dead review.
* Record the runner finding: if the mini pool's `/tmp` is shared, that is a separate agent-bureau card (per-job `/tmp` in the container spec); this card is the workflow half and is safe either way.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A test run (or the workflow's own unit tests) with Resolve PR failing posts no verdict and no `@` with an empty sha; the check on the head is neutral/skipped, not FAILURE
- [ ] A pre-seeded `/tmp/qa-verdict.md` is never posted; the gate reports "critic did not run"
- [ ] One transient error inside Resolve PR is retried once and the review proceeds
- [ ] The fix agent is not dispatched by a verdict that names no sha (the fix workflow's trigger filter, or the post step never producing one — either, pinned)
- [ ] Parity test against agent-bureau's stub unchanged; `stable` promotion unaffected
