cards.title: DEMO: the CEO watches a person sign in and open two documents, then sees both in the People panel within a minute, and signs off
cards.description:
The CEO sees [DRE-3682](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3682/epic-usage-log-who-came-in-when-and-what-they-opened-shown-to) work, and his yes is the sign-off for the epic. A merged PR and a passing suite are invisible to the person who green-lit this; the demo is the evidence he can see. Executed, not described: the app is run, the flow is driven, the panel is shown. Last-two child of the epic with the PROOF.

Blocked by: [DRE-3683](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3683/usage-libts-the-two-usage-events-their-key-shapes-the-gap-and-window), [DRE-3684](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3684/docs-the-usage-partitions-retention-row-the-deletion-step-and-two), [DRE-3685](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3685/visit-capture-in-the-dispatcher-a-persons-first-successful-request-on), [DRE-3686](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3686/open-capture-in-the-render-route-a-served-document-writes-one-usage), [DRE-3687](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3687/get-activity-moderators-read-last-seen-and-recent-opens-per-person), [DRE-3688](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3688/the-people-panel-says-when-each-person-was-last-seen-and-lists-what)

## What is shown

1. Two browser sessions side by side: a reader (not the operator's own account) and a moderator, on a local run or a deployed portal, whichever the operator prefers. A deployed portal is better; it is the same thing the PROOF card reads.
2. The reader signs in, opens one document, moves to a second one inside the app without a page reload, and follows a shared link to a document they cannot see, which shows the not-available screen.
3. The moderator opens the People panel. Within a minute: the reader's row reads "Last seen" with the right time, Recent activity lists the two documents opened and not the third, and the reader's own screen has nothing about activity anywhere.
4. One sentence on what is not captured: opens on a portal still serving legacy HTML, downloads and exports, anything before the deploy. The epic lists them.

## The two things he is asked

* Does this tell him what he wanted to know about how people use the portals?
* Should the reader-facing confidentiality copy now say sign-ins and opens are recorded? That decision was left to him on the epic.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The demo was run in front of the CEO, with a recording or screenshots attached to this card.
- [ ] Both documents appeared under the reader's Recent activity within a minute and the hidden one did not.
- [ ] The CEO's answer to both questions is recorded as a comment on this card, and the epic is closed on his yes.

cards.title: PROOF: on a deployed portal, one real visit and one real open appear as rows, a hidden document leaves none, and the library epoch never moved — recorded in docs/evidence
cards.description:
The mechanism of [DRE-3682](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3682/epic-usage-log-who-came-in-when-and-what-they-opened-shown-to) observed running against real state, not a green suite. Every child's tests drive an in-memory double; this card is the one that reads the live table after a real person did a real thing, and writes down what it found so the record merges. Operator work: it needs a deploy and a signed-in partner session, both of which agents do not have. Last-two child of the epic with the DEMO.

Blocked by: [DRE-3683](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3683/usage-libts-the-two-usage-events-their-key-shapes-the-gap-and-window), [DRE-3684](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3684/docs-the-usage-partitions-retention-row-the-deletion-step-and-two), [DRE-3685](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3685/visit-capture-in-the-dispatcher-a-persons-first-successful-request-on), [DRE-3686](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3686/open-capture-in-the-render-route-a-served-document-writes-one-usage), [DRE-3687](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3687/get-activity-moderators-read-last-seen-and-recent-opens-per-person), [DRE-3688](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3688/the-people-panel-says-when-each-person-was-last-seen-and-lists-what)

## Steps, after the six build cards are on main and a release lap has deployed them

1. Read the library epoch first: `get-item` on `pk = lib#<project>, sk = meta#epoch` with the account's profile. Note `n`.
2. One person who is not the operator (a partner, or a second test mailbox in the project) signs in on the portal, opens one document they can see, and tries a shared link to one they cannot (a document in a folder they have no grant on). Note the times in Pacific.
3. Query `pk = use#<project>#people`: one row for that person's sub with `lastVisitAt` and `lastOpenAt` within the noted minutes, `visitCount` 1.
4. Query `pk = use#<project>`: exactly two rows for that sub, one `kind: visit`, one `kind: open` naming the document they could see. No row for the document they could not.
5. Read the epoch again. `n` is unchanged.
6. Open the People panel as a moderator: the person shows "Last seen" with the right time and the one document under Recent activity.
7. Paste the four reads and a screenshot of the panel into `docs/evidence/usage-log-<account>-<date>.md`, with the release-run line from `~/.portico/release-runs.jsonl` that deployed it, and open a PR for the file.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `docs/evidence/usage-log-<account>-<date>.md` is on main with the raw command output for steps 1, 3, 4 and 5, the account, the commit deployed, and the times in Pacific.
- [ ] The hidden-document attempt produced no `use#` row and the person's `recentOpens` does not name it.
- [ ] The epoch read before and after is the same number.
- [ ] The panel screenshot shows the person with the right last-seen time.

cards.title: The People panel says when each person was last seen and lists what they opened, and says "not seen" rather than nothing
cards.description:
The only thing a moderator sees from [DRE-3682](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3682/epic-usage-log-who-came-in-when-and-what-they-opened-shown-to). The panel already lists every person in the project with whether they can sign in; this adds when they last came in and which documents they opened, per person, in the viewer's timezone. Readers never see any of it: the route is moderator-only server-side and the panel already is. Card 5 of [DRE-3682](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3682/epic-usage-log-who-came-in-when-and-what-they-opened-shown-to).

Blocked by: [DRE-3687](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3687/get-activity-moderators-read-last-seen-and-recent-opens-per-person)

## What to build — `client/app/src/features/people/PeoplePanel.tsx`

1. The `load` callback's `Promise.all` gains a fourth read, `fetchActivity(project)` from `./queries` ([DRE-3687](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3687/get-activity-moderators-read-last-seen-and-recent-opens-per-person)'s export, 30-day default). A 403 or failed read sets activity to `null`, which the panel renders as **unknown**, never as "nobody has been here" — the same rule `signInStatus` applies to the directory, and for the same reason.
2. Every person row (both the stranded list and "People with accounts") gains one line on the right: **Last seen today, 9:14 AM** / **Last seen Tue 4:02 PM** / **Last seen 12 Aug**, formatted in the viewer's timezone by the helper the answer strip already uses for "edited by … at …"; a person with no activity in the window reads **Not seen in the last 30 days**; when activity is `null` the line is **Activity unavailable**. Never a blank.
3. A row with opens gets a disclosure control, **Recent activity (3)**, collapsed by default, that lists `recentOpens` newest first as "Opened *Title*" with the time, plus one "Signed in" line at `lastVisitAt`. Keyboard-operable, `aria-expanded`, the same pattern the Details rail's history list uses.
4. Matching is by email, lower-cased, the way the panel already matches the directory (`norm` in `signInStatus.ts`), since the panel's people come from grants and the activity comes keyed by sub with an email alongside.
5. The pure parts (matching a person to their activity, choosing the last-seen sentence, formatting relative days) go in `features/people/activityLine.ts` with their own Vitest file, per the house rule that panels fetch and render and the answers live in a pure module.

Files: `client/app/src/features/people/PeoplePanel.tsx`, `client/app/src/features/people/PeoplePanel.test.tsx`, `client/app/src/features/people/activityLine.ts`, `client/app/src/features/people/activityLine.test.ts`.

## Contract (with [DRE-3687](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3687/get-activity-moderators-read-last-seen-and-recent-opens-per-person))

* Reads `fetchActivity(project)` and the `PersonActivity` type exactly as `features/people/queries.ts` exports them. No second fetch path.

## Do not

* Do not add a per-document "opened by" anywhere; the epic declines the Details-rail option.
* Do not show activity to a non-moderator, and do not render an empty list as "no activity" when the read failed.
* Do not touch `queries.ts`, `signInStatus.ts` or `projectPeople.ts`; [DRE-3687](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3687/get-activity-moderators-read-last-seen-and-recent-opens-per-person) and earlier cards own them.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `PeoplePanel.test.tsx` gains, red first: with a mocked activity payload, a person with a visit today shows "Last seen today, …"; a person absent from the payload shows "Not seen in the last 30 days"; a failed activity read shows "Activity unavailable" on every row and the rest of the panel renders as before; the disclosure lists opens newest first and is toggled by keyboard.
- [ ] `activityLine.test.ts` pins the sentence choice at the today / this-week / older boundaries against an injected `now` and timezone.
- [ ] The dev mock (`npm run dev` in `client/app`) renders the panel with the mock's two people and their opens; a screenshot of that state is attached to the PR.
- [ ] `cd client/app && npm run typecheck && npm test` green; TDD commit order holds.

cards.title: GET /activity — moderators read last seen and recent opens per person, opens filtered to what the caller can open; manifest, conformance exclusion, dev mock, client query
cards.description:
The read side of [DRE-3682](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3682/epic-usage-log-who-came-in-when-and-what-they-opened-shown-to): one moderator-only route that turns the two usage partitions into what the People panel shows. A new route means four touch points or the route-table agreement test goes red, and all four are in this card so the route exists nowhere half-registered. Card 4 of [DRE-3682](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3682/epic-usage-log-who-came-in-when-and-what-they-opened-shown-to).

Blocked by: [DRE-3683](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3683/usage-libts-the-two-usage-events-their-key-shapes-the-gap-and-window)

## What to build

**Route** `GET /activity`, authorizer `jwt`, in a new `infra/lambda/routes/activity.ts` (I/O only) with its manifest `infra/lambda/routes/manifests/activity.routes.ts`, registered in the dispatch table in `routes/index.ts` by one spread like every other module.

1. `assertModerator(groups, MODERATOR_GROUP)` then `assertKnownProject(project, PROJECTS)`, in that order, the escalation-guard pair `routes/people.ts` uses. A non-moderator gets the same 403 `GET /people` gives.
2. Query string: `project` (required), `days` (optional integer, default `30`, capped at `90`; anything else is a 400).
3. One Query on `use#<project>#people` for the summaries, one Query on `use#<project>` with `sk >= <now - days>` for the timeline, both `KeyConditionExpression: pk = :pk` (plus the sort-key range on the timeline), no Scan, no index, no FilterExpression. Pin the command inputs the way `log_route.test.ts` does.
4. Fold the timeline into per-person `recentOpens`, newest first, at most 20 per person, and drop opens whose `docId` fails `openableBy(subjectOf(claims, groups), libRows, isModerator).narrates(docId)`, the same walk `routes/log.ts` runs for `GET /changelog`. A moderator who cannot open a document must not learn its title from someone else's visit.
5. Response: `{ project, days, people: [{ sub, email, name, lastVisitAt, visitCount, lastOpenAt, recentOpens: [{ docId, title, at }] }] }`, people sorted by most recent activity, absent fields absent rather than null. A project with no usage rows answers `{ project, days, people: [] }`.
6. The pure folding and filtering live in `infra/lambda/activity_lib.ts` (no AWS SDK import); the route calls them.

**Conformance.** `test/section_7_conformance.test.ts` §1 goes red the moment the manifest grows. Add one `EXCLUSIONS` entry for `GET /activity` with the reason in the file's own grammar: carries `project` and `days` only, no item id enters the request, and the opens list is narrowed by `narrates()` after the read. Touch nothing else in that file.

**Fixture.** `test/api_shapes.test.ts` emits `fixtures/api-shapes/activity.json` from a run of the real handler, the [DRE-2879](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2879/a12-the-four-new-form-routes-join-the-shared-api-shape-fixture-seam) protocol, so the client validates against captured bytes, never a hand-written shape.

**Dev mock.** `client/app/dev/mockDevServer.ts` serves `GET /activity` with two people and three opens, so the panel renders locally ([DRE-2979](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2979/the-dev-mock-is-missing-changelog-and-attachments-the-details-rail) is what happens when a route is missing here).

**Client query.** `client/app/src/features/people/queries.ts` gains `fetchActivity(project, days?)` returning `PersonActivity[]` typed from the fixture, through `readJson(await authedFetch(...))` like its neighbours, with a 403 raised as `ApiError` so the panel can render "unknown" rather than "nobody". No panel change here; [DRE-3688](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3688/the-people-panel-says-when-each-person-was-last-seen-and-lists-what) owns `PeoplePanel.tsx`.

Files: `infra/lambda/routes/activity.ts`, `infra/lambda/activity_lib.ts`, `infra/lambda/routes/manifests/activity.routes.ts`, `infra/lambda/routes/index.ts` (the dispatch spread only), `infra/test/activity_route.test.ts`, `infra/test/activity_lib.test.ts`, `infra/test/section_7_conformance.test.ts` (one EXCLUSIONS entry), `infra/test/api_shapes.test.ts`, `infra/test/fixtures/api-shapes/activity.json`, `client/app/dev/mockDevServer.ts`, `client/app/src/features/people/queries.ts`.

## Contract (with [DRE-3683](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3683/usage-libts-the-two-usage-events-their-key-shapes-the-gap-and-window) and the People panel card)

* Route key: `GET /activity`, authorizer `jwt`. Query: `project`, `days`.
* Response shape exactly as in item 5; timestamps ISO-8601 UTC; `recentOpens` newest first, at most 20.
* Client: `fetchActivity(project: string, days?: number): Promise<PersonActivity[]>` returns the `people` array; type `PersonActivity` exported from `features/people/queries.ts`.
* Fixture: `infra/test/fixtures/api-shapes/activity.json`.

## Do not

* Do not read `use#` partitions from any existing route, and do not add a per-document rail; the epic declines the Details-rail option.
* Do not return anything to a non-moderator, and do not skip the `narrates()` filter for moderators.
* Do not touch `PeoplePanel.tsx`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `activity_route.test.ts` lands first, black-box through `handler(event)`: a non-moderator gets 403; a moderator with `days=7` gets exactly two Query commands with the pks and sort-key range above and no FilterExpression; `days=500` is a 400; the response shape matches item 5 with two seeded people and their opens newest first.
- [ ] An open on a document the moderator cannot open (seeded on the `folder-only` shape from `write_gates_section_7.test.ts`) is absent from `recentOpens` while the person's `lastOpenAt` still reflects it.
- [ ] `section_7_conformance.test.ts` §1 green with the new exclusion; `route_table_agreement.test.ts` green.
- [ ] `api_shapes.test.ts` emits the fixture and the client type is derived from it; `cd client/app && npm run typecheck` green.
- [ ] `cd infra && npm test && npm run typecheck` green; TDD commit order holds.

cards.title: Open capture in the render route: a served document writes one usage row after the §7 gate, and the content suite's "never writes" contract is restated as "writes only the usage partition"
cards.description:
The "what they opened" half of [DRE-3682](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3682/epic-usage-log-who-came-in-when-and-what-they-opened-shown-to). Recorded server-side in the route that serves a document, so a client that forgets to report cannot make a gap in the record, and recorded after the document has resolved, so a hidden document and a nonexistent one leave the same nothing. Card 3 of [DRE-3682](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3682/epic-usage-log-who-came-in-when-and-what-they-opened-shown-to).

Blocked by: [DRE-3683](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3683/usage-libts-the-two-usage-events-their-key-shapes-the-gap-and-window)

## What to build — in `infra/lambda/routes/content.ts`

In `'GET /d/{docId}/render'`, immediately after `if (!doc) return notFoundOrForbidden();` and before any payload is built:

1. Decide with `isNewOpen(summary, doc.id, now)` against a per-container cache `Map<'<project>#<sub>', { docId, atMs }>`; a hit inside `OPEN_WINDOW_MS` for the same document does no I/O. The viewer refetches the render payload on a stale epoch and on retry, and without this every refetch would be an open.
2. On a miss: build `ev = buildOpenEvent({ project, claims, docId: doc.id, title: doc.title, now })`, send one `UpdateCommand` of `{ TableName, ...summaryUpdateFor(ev, now) }`, and on success one `PutCommand` of `usageEventItem(ev)`. Build no key or expression in the route. On a conditional-check failure, update the cache and write nothing else.
3. Both writes swallowed the `notifySafe` way. The render response is built and returned exactly as today whether the writes succeeded, failed or were skipped.
4. The three early returns above the hook (`notFoundOrForbidden`, `notReadyPayload`) are untouched. A document that is not ready is not an open.

**The contract this restates.** `infra/test/content_route.test.ts`'s `ReadOnlyDdb` throws on any command that is not a Query or Get, with the message "the serve routes read, never write". That was true and is now false for exactly one partition. Restate the double: it accepts `UpdateCommand` and `PutCommand` **only** when the key's `pk` begins with `use#`, records them, and still throws on any other write. The zero-I/O assertions in that file then keep their meaning (the library is read, never written) and gain a new one (the only writes are usage writes). The throw on a non-`use#` write is the assertion; do not weaken it to a warning.

Files: `infra/lambda/routes/content.ts`, `infra/test/content_route.test.ts`.

## Contract (with [DRE-3683](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3683/usage-libts-the-two-usage-events-their-key-shapes-the-gap-and-window), [DRE-3687](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3687/get-activity-moderators-read-last-seen-and-recent-opens-per-person))

* The timeline row is the `UsageEvent` shape with `kind: 'open'`, `docId` and `title` set to the row's `id` and `title` at the time.
* The summary row after an open carries `lastOpenAt` (ISO) and `lastOpenDocId`.
* Constants as `usage_lib.ts` exports them; `OPEN_WINDOW_MS` is not restated here.

## Do not

* Do not write before `notFoundOrForbidden()` has had its say. The hidden and ghost arms must produce zero usage commands, and `section_7_conformance.test.ts` drives this route on all four partition shapes and asserts byte-identical output and identical command lists; that suite is the proof and must stay green untouched.
* Do not record `/download`, `/source` or `/revisions`; downloads are a follow-on card.
* Do not touch `routes/index.ts`; the visit event is [DRE-3685](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3685/visit-capture-in-the-dispatcher-a-persons-first-successful-request-on).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `content_route.test.ts` gains, red first: a member with a grant fetching render for a ready document produces one `UpdateCommand` on `use#<project>#people` keyed by their sub and one `PutCommand` on `use#<project>` whose item has `kind: 'open'`, the doc id and the title; a second fetch inside ten minutes produces neither; a fetch of a different document produces both; a fetch of a document the caller cannot open produces no usage command and the `NOT_FOUND_BODY` unchanged.
- [ ] With the double's usage writes made to throw, the render payload is byte-identical to the no-throw case.
- [ ] The restated double still throws on any write whose `pk` does not begin with `use#`, and a test proves it by attempting one.
- [ ] `section_7_conformance.test.ts` passes without edits.
- [ ] `cd infra && npm test && npm run typecheck` green; TDD commit order holds; the PR body names the test that reddens if the hook is moved above the `!doc` return.

cards.title: [EPIC] The Claude subscription chain is seamless — the console stops throttling its own accounts, never distributes a token that answers 429, Reconnect owns the chain, one owner by lease, the switch goes both ways and says what it did, and a seven-step production test proves it
cards.description:
**Repo:** agent-bureau (one child is bureau-pipeline; the planner labels it so)

**Filed on the CEO's instruction, 2026-09-12 ~14:50 PT: "do it and promote them from intake, let's get them going" — an explicit override of** `INTAKE_HOLD` **for this epic.** Decision record: `~/Desktop/agent-bureau-notes-2026-09-12/claude-credential-plan.md` on the operator's machine (the forensics file beside it); its substance is below so the planner needs nothing outside this card.

## Why (what the 30-day production log, the code map and 60 cards say)

The fleet's Claude Max accounts are OAuth chains; each repo holds a frozen copy of one access token; every mint revokes the copy issued beside the link it spent. The console watches, renews, fans out, switches and reports on that. Assessed 2026-09-12 from the full App Runner log (08-13 → 09-12), a map of every code path, and every card since June. Fourteen cases are broken. The ones that take the fleet down:

* **A. The watching throttles the account.** The usage probe is a real `POST /v1/messages` every 240 s per account; the health monitor adds a `max_tokens:1` inference per account per 5 min; the page probes on load; every deploy runs two instances probing at once (~700 probes/account/day). Anthropic rate-limits the ACCOUNT: Dreadnought 429 clusters on 08-19, 08-20, 08-21, 08-26, 08-31, 09-01, 09-05, and continuous since 09-11 18:00 PT (body: "would exceed your account's rate limit", `retry-after` to a fixed reset ≈07:00 PT 09-13). CI jobs on a throttled account die `is_error / 1 turn / $0` with no message — indistinguishable from a dead credential (09-12 09:48–10:03 and 10:27–10:36, both inside 429 windows, interleaved with successes on the same token).
* **E. The fan-out proof accepts a 429.** `fleet_credential_sync._default_prove` treats `out-of-quota` as authenticated, so the console distributes a token the account cannot use (09-12 07:31:57 to all six repos; 08-19 16:52 a dead token to seven).
* **B. Reconnect never repairs the chain.** No `refresh seed changed` line in 30 days. Prod has no `CLAUDE_OAUTH_REFRESH_*` seed (`infra/cdk.json` ARNs empty) → the stored record has `grown_from: null` → `claude_oauth_token._restore` (:509-515) never adopts the pasted chain; the new refresh token lives only in `os.environ`. The 09-11 18:07 Reconnect's token was overwritten by the warmer at 23:35 on the OLD chain; 09-10 07:33–07:38 four Reconnects → "refresh exchange was refused" for all three accounts.
* **D. Every deploy runs two fleet owners for 10–12 min** (`BUREAU_FLEET_OWNER` is an env var): both probe, both run the auto-switch executor (09-11 18:10–18:13 refusals from two instance ids); before [DRE-2943](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2943/every-console-restart-renews-the-claude-token-and-revokes-the-one-the) both minted (08-22, 08-23, 08-25, 08-27 ×5, 08-28 ×5, 09-01). The 09-05 08:36 "foreign write" [DRE-3180](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3180/switch-log-every-change-of-the-fleets-claude-account-manual-reconnect)/3181 were built on was the console's own new instance 20 s after a deploy. [DRE-2704](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2704/a-new-console-instance-mints-a-claude-token-twelve-seconds-after-boot).

The ones that cost the CEO time: **G** a console-driven switch stamps every repo `operator`, so the pool never brings repos home and the health monitor tells the operator to revert by hand (`claude_reconnect._rotate` :907, `claude_pool.plan_failover` :427, `_swapped_away` :752; no recovery test among 34); **H** `record_stand_down` has zero callers and "auto-switch is off" stands down silently; **I** Reconnect/"Use this" fan-out and the 80% label advance are not owner-gated (09-10 11:15:34 three identical switches in 130 ms); **C** no token fingerprint on the probe's non-200 lines ([DRE-3652](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3652/the-consoles-usage-probe-token-for-an-account-is-a-second-copy-of-the)'s "second copy" premise was wrong — the probe already sends the fleet's token — but the CEO's ruling stands: one token, fingerprint every line); **L** the page keeps a stale red refusal row and the hero refuses to name an errored account ([DRE-3607](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3607/a-reconnect-or-use-this-that-rewrites-six-repos-shows-no-progress-and)); **F** 429 → switch → target's stored credential rejected → a 60-s refusal loop (4–6k lines/day 08-25→09-01; [DRE-2660](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2660/a-chain-rotation-kills-the-consoles-own-stored-pool-credential-and) live since 09-11 should end it; VeriCorr's 09-11 rejection after a 15:39 rotation unexplained). Words and record: **K** revoked reads as expired, `invalid_grant` as a blip; **M** alerts leave no log line; **N** monitors README documents 1 of 6 Claude monitors, "seven repos" (six), runbook says the refresh token is memory-only, `autoSwitch` says default off; **J** the warmer rewrites six secrets every 7 h 55 min and nothing surfaces that as scheduled.

Already built: [DRE-3614](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3614/the-usage-probe-tells-a-rate-limited-429-from-a-capped-account-only-a) (rate-limited vs capped, **live v1.6.51 14:14 PT**), [DRE-3616](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3616/subscriptions-page-a-stood-down-switch-log-line-and-a-rate-limited) (page rows, merged), [DRE-3613](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3613/the-switch-log-can-carry-a-non-switch-line-trigger-stood-down-the)/3615 (live), [DRE-3617](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3617/auto-switch-stands-down-on-every-evidence-path-when-the-fleets-account) ([dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau#2486](<https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/review/featdre-3617-an-unknown-fleet-identity-stands-auto-switch-down-on-927e64301902>) open), [DRE-3618](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3618/one-usage-probe-per-account-per-minute-whatever-the-page-does-a-per) ([dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau#2485](<https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/review/featdre-3618-one-usage-probe-per-account-per-minute-whatever-the-page-e204f2fde92a>) open), [DRE-2660](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2660/a-chain-rotation-kills-the-consoles-own-stored-pool-credential-and), [DRE-2943](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2943/every-console-restart-renews-the-claude-token-and-revokes-the-one-the), [DRE-2662](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2662/the-credential-fan-out-silently-reversed-a-failover-and-left-the-pools), [DRE-3181](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3181/fleet-identity-which-account-each-repo-is-on-is-read-from-githubs) (live). Auto-switch is OFF since 09-11 18:13 PT; the fleet bills VeriCorr since the CEO's "Use this" at 10:38 PT.

## What to build — three waves, each item test-first (RED replays the logged event), then a live proof

**Wave 1 — stop hurting the account, stop lying to the fleet**

1. Probe budget: ≤ 100 requests per account per day. One probe per account per minute at most ([DRE-3618](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3618/one-usage-probe-per-account-per-minute-whatever-the-page-does-a-per) lands or is folded in); the health monitor's inference rides the same floor; the page never probes on load; a non-owner instance never probes; the fleet's own run receipts carry the window headers so the usage read needs no inference when the account is the fleet's. Proof: Dreadnought's `retry-after` stops climbing; the row reads a percentage after the 07:00 reset with no click.
2. The fan-out proof never distributes a 429: for the DISTRIBUTION decision `out-of-quota` is a refusal; the proof reads the 429 body and names it; a refused distribution raises CRITICAL naming the account and reason. RED: replay 09-12 07:31:57. Proof: the next renewal logs `proved: works` + fingerprint, or refuses and says why.
3. **(bureau-pipeline)** A run death carries the error body: `dead_run.py` reads the Claude result's error text into the receipt so `is_error/1 turn/$0` splits into throttled / revoked / capped; the console's receipt exhaustion stops counting throttled deaths as exhaustion. RED: the three receipt shapes from 09-12's runs.
4. Reconnect owns the chain from then on: on `complete` the provider is rebuilt from the pasted refresh token and the stored record is REPLACED, seed or no seed; origin = the new link's fingerprint; provision the refresh ARNs in the backend stack. RED: boot seedless → warmer mints → Reconnect → the next warmer mint comes from the NEW chain and logs `refresh seed changed`. Proof: one Reconnect on Dreadnought, the next renewal's fingerprint differs from the pre-Reconnect chain.
5. One owner by lease ([DRE-2704](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2704/a-new-console-instance-mints-a-claude-token-twelve-seconds-after-boot)): a DB lease with heartbeat; the instance without it neither probes, switches nor mints; a deploy hands over explicitly. RED: two instances for 12 min → one mint, one probe stream, one executor. Proof: a deploy with nobody at the keyboard logs one owner throughout.

**Wave 2 — the switch goes both ways and says what it did**
6. Recovery home: a console-driven switch stamps `failover`, the pool brings repos home when the home account is healthy and under 80%, the loaner WARN fires only on a real hand swap. RED: cap → switch → cap clears → repos return, no human step.
7. Every stand-down is a switch-log line (executor and pool; "auto-switch is off" once per hour, not per tick) so [DRE-3616](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3616/subscriptions-page-a-stood-down-switch-log-line-and-a-rate-limited)'s rows render.
8. `is_fleet_owner` gates Reconnect, "Use this" and the label advance; the non-owner shows a named refusal; a multi-submit within 10 s is one switch.
9. Fingerprints on every line: probe non-200, fan-out, switch log; the page shows the fleet's fingerprint beside the probe's. Closes [DRE-3652](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3652/the-consoles-usage-probe-token-for-an-account-is-a-second-copy-of-the) as the CEO ruled.
10. The page tells the truth: a refusal row clears when superseded or when auto-switch is turned off; the hero names the errored account and its error. Closes [DRE-3607](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3607/a-reconnect-or-use-this-that-rewrites-six-repos-shows-no-progress-and).

**Wave 3 — words and record**
11. Name the cause: `401 … revoked` → "revoked (this console minted at HH:MM)" when the switch log has a matching mint; `invalid_grant` → "chain dead — Reconnect"; transport blip → unread, nothing raised.
12. Alerts in the log (kind, account, raise/resolve) so an incident reconstructs without SMTP.
13. The record: monitors README rows for all six Claude monitors; six repos; the durable refresh token; the `autoSwitch` default; [DRE-3180](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3180/switch-log-every-change-of-the-fleets-claude-account-manual-reconnect)/3181's premise corrected.
14. The page shows "next scheduled renewal HH:MM PT" so a rotation stops reading as an event.

## Acceptance — the equilibrium test, on production, the CEO watching, auto-switch ON

Expected log line and page state written down before each step:

1. A scheduled renewal: no job dies, one `fleet-sync` line, fingerprints match on page and log.
2. A Reconnect on the running account: the next renewal mints from the new chain (`refresh seed changed`), no job dies.
3. "Use this" to another account: six repos re-pointed, the switch log shows it within a minute, the page names account and fingerprint.
4. A real cap: auto-switch moves the fleet with one switch-log line; when the window resets the fleet comes home by itself with a second.
5. A probe rate-limit (ten page loads): nothing moves, the row says "rate-limited, retrying", one `stood-down` line.
6. A backend deploy: one owner throughout, no mint, no rotation, the persisted token reused.
7. A break-glass `gh` swap: the page reads `rotated outside the console` within five minutes and names the repo.
   All seven in one sitting → [DRE-3255](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3255/proof-auto-switch-observed-firing-on-the-live-console-a-429-switches), [DRE-3606](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3606/auto-switch-fired-on-a-usage-probe-429-while-the-fleets-account-was) and [DRE-3170](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3170/claude-auto-switch-never-fires-it-watches-the-account-the-console-last) close on the same record.

## Not in this epic

[DRE-2400](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2400/a-manual-or-soft-threshold-active-account-change-doesnt-re-point-ci) (does a manual switch re-point CI — the CEO's A/B/C); [DRE-2674](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2674/move-the-vericorr-claude-account-under-dreadnought-do-it-while-it) (fewer accounts). Wave 1 items 1, 2 and 4 are the fleet-down causes and go first; item 3 is bureau-pipeline (`repo:bureau-pipeline`); item 5 is the largest (a lease + a deploy handover). cards.title: The One River design record catches up to two CEO decisions — Green Light is green letters with no outline, and the Overview opens on List with a Tree switch
cards.description:
**Repo:** agent-bureau

**Filed on the CEO's ruling of 2026-09-12 13:22 PT on** [DRE-3067](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3067/operator-prove-phase-3-the-three-tabs-in-parallel) (and on his override of INTAKE_HOLD for One River's sign-off): his 2026-09-07 instruction "just put the letters in green" stands as the amendment for the Green Light tab, and the Overview's List-first opening with a Tree switch ([DRE-3393](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3393/one-river-tree-list-on-the-overview-tab-every-moving-card-as-one-flat), [DRE-3463](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3463/one-river-the-overview-opens-on-the-list-view-tree-is-one-press-away)) is amended. The code already does both. The design record does not.

## What happened

The Phase 3 proof ([DRE-3067](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3067/operator-prove-phase-3-the-three-tabs-in-parallel)) found two tabs that differ from the `**Design:**` PNG they were signed off against, with the design contract still saying the opposite:

* `console/design/atomic/templates.html:943` still reads "Green Light keeps its outline and never a fill"; the code (`shell.decisions.test.tsx:451`, `GreenLightTab.decisions.test.tsx:314`) asserts green letters and NO outline since commit `8d2b09ee4` (PR [dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau#2353](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/review/featdre-3306-one-river-tier-4-the-templates-and-the-showroom-b82cfb04fc44), 2026-09-07).
* `console/design/screens/dashboard-one-river-overview.png` (and the One River design HTML) shows the tree opening; the code opens on List with a Tree | List switch since PRs [dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau#2366](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/review/featdre-3393-one-river-tree-list-every-moving-card-as-one-flat-row-03d58a13ee06) and [dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau#2386](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/review/featdre-3463-the-overview-opens-on-the-list-view-tree-is-one-press-cd8bacb109a4).

## What to build

1. `console/design/atomic/templates.html`: the Green Light line says green letters, no outline, never a fill, citing the CEO's 2026-09-07 decision and the 2026-09-12 ruling.
2. The One River design source (`console/design/screens/web-dashboard-one-river-2026-09-03.html` or wherever the Overview and Green Light frames are authored) and the exported PNGs `dashboard-one-river-green-light.png` and `dashboard-one-river-overview.png` are re-exported to show green letters without an outline and the Overview on List with the Tree | List switch. Read `feedback_pen_files_read_only` before touching any `.pen` file: if the source is a `.pen`, STOP and hand the export to the operator; edit only the HTML/PNG.

cards.title: [OPERATOR] Put the website and relay surfaces live on the release train: deploy ReleaseStack, simulate the role, one dispatch and one rollback per surface
cards.description:
**This card is the timer for the second and third train surfaces**, the [DRE-3324](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3324/operator-exercise-a-console-rollback-against-production-then-flip-the) shape. [DRE-3397](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3397/the-marketing-website-joins-the-release-train-as-its-second-surface) (website) and [DRE-3670](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3670/the-linear-relays-code-rollout-joins-the-release-train-as-a-surface) (relay) go Done the moment their PRs merge ([dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau#2480](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/review/featdre-3397-the-marketing-website-joins-the-release-train-as-its-4d152db01125), [dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau#2481](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/review/featdre-3670-the-linear-relays-code-rollout-joins-the-release-train-949196ec4c90)) — merge is what Done means — but nothing is released by the train until the operator does the steps below. Without this card those steps live only in two PR bodies and are lost at Done.

**Where things stand at filing (2026-09-12 11:25 PT):** both surfaces are declared in `.github/bureau/release.json` (`auto: false`, 30-minute spacing, 07:00–21:00 PT window), each has ONE rollout script the hand path and the train share, the release role's grants are written in `infra/lib/release-stack.ts` and pinned by tests, and `make check-release-role` reads every new website/relay row as **implicitDeny** — expected, because the stack has not been deployed. The website was hand-deployed at 10:39 PT (`agent-bureau-website-v1.0.4`, tip of `main`), so its first dispatch is a no-op by design.

## The steps, in order (all OPERATOR — needs the dreadnought AWS profile and your own `gh` login)

- [ ] **1. Apply the grants.** `cd infra && AWS_PROFILE=dreadnought npx cdk deploy ReleaseStack`. This only widens `bureau-console-release-role`; no service is touched.
- [ ] **2. Prove them.** `make check-release-role` — every row must read `allowed`, including the six website rows (CloudFormation describe, S3 list/put/delete, CloudFront create/get invalidation) and the five relay rows (Lambda get/get-config/update-code/update-config/publish-version). A `denied` row is a card for an agent, not something to work around.
- [ ] **3. Website, first dispatch.** `gh workflow run release-train.yml -f surface=website`. Expected: `deferred:` and no tag, because v1.0.4 already sits at the tip of `main` ([DRE-3397](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3397/the-marketing-website-joins-the-release-train-as-its-second-surface) acceptance criterion 2). The first real website release is the next `website/` commit — hand dispatch again then, or set `auto: true` (step 6).
- [ ] **4. Relay, first dispatch.** `gh workflow run release-train.yml -f surface=relay` once [dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau#2481](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/review/featdre-3670-the-linear-relays-code-rollout-joins-the-release-train-949196ec4c90) is on `main`. Expected: build → update-code → `DEPLOYED_SHA`/`DEPLOYED_AT` stamped → publish-version → `agent-bureau-relay-v<N>` cut; `make deploy-lag` reads the relay `ok 0`. The `live` alias is NOT moved (that stays [DRE-2790](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2790/the-relay-can-be-deployed-but-not-rolled-back-publish-versions-alias)).
- [ ] **5. One rollback each, at a quiet hour, recorded on** [DRE-3397](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3397/the-marketing-website-joins-the-release-train-as-its-second-surface) **/** [DRE-3670](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3670/the-linear-relays-code-rollout-joins-the-release-train-as-a-surface)**.** Website: `make rollback-website VERSION=agent-bureau-website-v1.0.3`, then forward again. Relay: from a checkout at the previous `agent-bureau-relay-v<N-1>` commit, `RELEASE_SHA=<that sha> make release-relay`, then forward again. A green harness is not one real run.
- [ ] **6. Decide** `auto: true` **for each surface.** CEO's call, made here, not by drift. The website has no migration and no service to repoint, so the console's reason for waiting (an unattended migration) does not apply to it. The relay is a code-only rollout with the same property.

The helper script for steps 1–4 with a stop after each is handed over in the session that filed this card; the steps above are the durable copy.

**This is an operator/CEO card, not agent work.** No agent should deploy the stack, dispatch a surface, or flip `auto: true` on its own.

**Repo:** agent-bureau

cards.title: The planner files a PROOF child and no DEMO child — an epic closes on its proof record, which the CEO reads himself
cards.description:
**Repo:** bureau-pipeline

**Filed on the CEO's explicit override of INTAKE_HOLD, 2026-09-12 ~10:25 PT** ("Make sure we change that across all of our cards we're doing. Just having the proof card is the key.").

## What happened

Every epic the planner has shaped since Wave 1.5 carries two closing children: a PROOF card (a record merged as a `no-code` PR, then hand-closed on the `🔬 proof-observed` line) and a DEMO card (a CEO walkthrough sitting). On 2026-09-12 the In Progress column held 29 items; in fourteen of the epics the proof was merged or nearly so and the DEMO card was the last open child — a sitting nobody had time to hold, with a script nobody had written. The CEO's decision, 2026-09-12: **no demo sittings. He reads the proof record and closes the proof card himself.** All 25 open DEMO cards were cancelled that morning with that reason.

## What to build

1. `scripts/proof_and_demo.py` (and whatever the wave planner and `wave_commitment.py` call to shape an epic's closing children) files **one** closing child, the PROOF card, and no DEMO card. The PROOF card's body gains one line: *"The CEO reads this record and closes this card; there is no demo sitting."*
2. `standards/card-quality.md` — the epic-shape section says PROOF only, with the 2026-09-12 decision and its reason in one sentence, so the pre-approval critic stops asking where the demo is.
3. Any validator or critic rule that requires a DEMO child (grep `validate_card.py`, `plan_critic*`, `config/planner-audit.json`, `config/routing-verdicts.json` for `DEMO`) is relaxed to PROOF-only; a plan that still files a DEMO child is not rejected, but the planner no longer produces one.
4. The PROOF card's acceptance criteria template drops any "the CEO has said so at a sitting" line and keeps "the CEO closes this card after reading the record".

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] RED first: a test over the epic-shaping code asserts a planned epic's closing children are exactly `[PROOF]` — no DEMO card is created; the existing test that expected two children is inverted, not deleted.
- [ ] `standards/card-quality.md` names the 2026-09-12 decision and the PROOF-only shape; the pre-approval critic's checklist (wherever it reads the shape from) no longer lists a demo.
- [ ] Every grep for `DEMO` under `scripts/`, `config/` and `standards/` is either removed or is a reader of historical cards, with a comment saying so.
- [ ] PROOF: the next epic the planner shapes after this merges carries a PROOF child and no DEMO child — its id and PT time recorded on this card.

## Not in this card

* Cancelling existing DEMO cards (done by hand 2026-09-12 10:21 PT, 25 cards).
* Changing how a PROOF card is closed (still a human, never the pipeline).

**Files:** `scripts/proof_and_demo.py`, `standards/card-quality.md`, the tests that pin the epic shape, and any `config/*.json` that lists the DEMO child.

## Lane

Fleet — ordinary engineer card through the critic and the gate.

cards.title: OPERATOR: deploy DRE-3667, rewrite the sign-up projection, and have a Summit address sign in on share.vericorr.com
cards.description:
> **HOLD the deploy — found 2026-09-12 while publishing the Summit ledger.** [share.vericorr.com](<http://share.vericorr.com>) is not cut over: its flat document keys (sallyport-*.html, chapman-ai-survey-data-assessment.html, trophy-coupon-data-review.html, harris-connector-cis.html, compliance-*.html, and more) still hold full documents, not redirect stubs (verified by reading the objects in vericorr-docs-442004016891). The edge gate authorizes those paths on Cognito group membership alone (`edge_gate_lib.ts` gateDecision: `groups.includes(project)`), with no per-document check. So every member of the `vericorr` group can open every flat document by URL — today that already includes the Chapman and Trophy users. [DRE-3667](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3667/portico-let-summitmidstreamcom-self-sign-up-into-the-vericorr-project) makes every [summitmidstream.com](<http://summitmidstream.com>) sign-up a `vericorr` group member, which would extend that to all Summit staff.
>
> **State at 22:45 UTC:** step 1 is DONE — the deploy ran at 21:22 UTC and both sign-up Lambdas carry `{"vericorr":["summitmidstream.com"]}`. Step 2 is NOT done: `signup#/domains` still lists only `vericorr.com`, so Summit sign-up is still refused and no Summit user exists. Reopened from Done: the acceptance criteria are unmet.
>
> **Do not do step 2 yet, and do not add, change or revoke ANY domain grant on ANY portal in the dreadnought account** (vericorr, gridcorr, deltasolv): every domain-grant write rewrites the account-wide projection from the new config and would switch Summit sign-up on as a side effect.
>
> First: cut [share.vericorr.com](<http://share.vericorr.com>) over with `infra/scripts/migrate-legacy-docs.ts --account dreadnought --project vericorr` (dry run first; see docs/runbooks/legacy-cutover.md), so the flat keys become stubs and reads go through the per-document check. New documents for Summit go in by the library upload into External / Summit Midstream, never by the flat publish.

The build card [DRE-3667](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3667/portico-let-summitmidstreamcom-self-sign-up-into-the-vericorr-project) adds [summitmidstream.com](<http://summitmidstream.com>) as a trusted sign-up domain for vericorr. Three live steps make it real, and none of them can be checked against the diff, so they live here.

## Steps

1. Deploy and attach: `infra/scripts/deploy-and-attach.sh dreadnought --apply` (the account is `dreadnought`, not `vericorr`).
2. Rewrite the sign-up projection. The PreSignUp and PostConfirmation triggers read `pk=signup#, sk=domains` and fail closed; a deploy does not rewrite it. Any domain-grant write does (`routes/access.ts` includes `signupProjectionPut` on create, role change and revoke of a domain grant). So on [share.vericorr.com](<http://share.vericorr.com>), open the External / Summit Midstream folder's access list and re-save the existing [summitmidstream.com](<http://summitmidstream.com>) viewer grant once. Do not use the trusted-domains button: it also writes a root grant for the domain.
3. Read-only check: `get-item` on `signup#/domains` with `--profile dreadnought` shows `summitmidstream.com` under `vericorr`.
4. A Summit person (Reagan, or a Summit test mailbox) signs in at [share.vericorr.com](<http://share.vericorr.com>) with an email code or Google, lands on External / Summit Midstream, and sees nothing else.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Projection lists [summitmidstream.com](<http://summitmidstream.com>) under vericorr.
- [ ] No `grant#root#d:summitmidstream.com` row exists in `lib#vericorr`.
- [ ] One Summit address has signed in and reports seeing only the Summit Midstream folder.

Blocked by: [DRE-3667](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3667/portico-let-summitmidstreamcom-self-sign-up-into-the-vericorr-project)

Documentation gaps found on the way, for a separate card if wanted: `docs/runbooks/summit-fold.md` says the trusted-domains UI route grants no access (wrong: it writes a root grant), and no runbook covers the post-deploy projection rewrite.

cards.title: The console's usage-probe token for an account is a second copy of the credential — a Reconnect revokes it and the probe answers 429 until someone repairs the chain by hand
cards.description:
**Observed 2026-09-11 18:00 PT → still failing at 20:51 PT on production (console v1.6.45).** The console's cost-usage probe for Dreadnought has answered `HTTP 429 — token may be expired or unauthorized` every 240 s since 18:00:19 PT: past the account's 5-hour window reset (19:30 PT), while the other three accounts' probes answered normally, and while the FLEET ran fine on Dreadnought the whole time (the [DRE-2660](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2660/a-chain-rotation-kills-the-consoles-own-stored-pool-credential-and) and [DRE-3606](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3606/auto-switch-fired-on-a-usage-probe-429-while-the-fleets-account-was) planner and build runs from 18:17 PT on all succeeded on it; PR [dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau#2468](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/review/featdre-2660-the-chain-rotation-keeps-the-consoles-own-stored-5122bb26899c) merged 19:28 PT). So the account is neither capped nor throttled — the probe's own token is dead.

**Why there are two tokens.** The fleet's token and the probe's token are meant to come from one refresh chain per account. A Reconnect (the CEO's, at 18:07:24 PT, after "Use this" refused the dead stored credential — [DRE-2660](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2660/a-chain-rotation-kills-the-consoles-own-stored-pool-credential-and)) mints a NEW token from the operator's click and fans it out to the six repos, but since [DRE-2532](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2532/the-token-self-refresher-burns-its-own-seed-the-rotated-refresh-token) the chain does not adopt a Reconnect's seed (that adoption is what looped the token burn in August). So after a Reconnect the fleet holds the fresh token and the probe still holds the previous chain's, which the mint revoked. Two copies of one credential, kept current separately — the same family as [DRE-2660](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2660/a-chain-rotation-kills-the-consoles-own-stored-pool-credential-and), in the other direction.

**What it costs.** The Subscriptions hero reads "No active account" and the Dreadnought row reads `Unavailable · usage unavailable (HTTP 429)` even though the identity verdict says Dreadnought, known, no foreign repos (the hero keys off the probe, folded into [DRE-3607](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3607/a-reconnect-or-use-this-that-rewrites-six-repos-shows-no-progress-and)); the 84%-budget warning for that account is blind; and, until [DRE-3606](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3606/auto-switch-fired-on-a-usage-probe-429-while-the-fleets-account-was) lands, auto-switch reads the 429 as exhaustion and tries to move the fleet (it is switched OFF for that reason). `cost_usage._probe` logs only the status code — never the body or `retry-after`/cap headers — so a revoked token, a throttled probe and a capped account are indistinguishable in the log ([DRE-3606](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3606/auto-switch-fired-on-a-usage-probe-429-while-the-fleets-account-was) adds the logging).

## What to build

One credential per account, one owner. After a Reconnect the chain provider re-seeds from the freshly minted refresh token (the [DRE-2532](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2532/the-token-self-refresher-burns-its-own-seed-the-rotated-refresh-token) loop was the chain re-adopting the SAME seed every tick; adopting a NEW seed exactly once, keyed by the mint's fingerprint, is the fix, not the bug), so the probe, the pool and the fleet all draw from the one chain. Alternatively the probe asks the same provider the fleet-sync uses, and the separate probe copy is deleted. Either way: after a Reconnect, the next probe tick answers 200 with no human step, and a genuinely capped account still reads as capped.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] After a Reconnect of account X, the next cost-usage probe for X answers 200 (test: replay tonight's ordering — chain token T1, Reconnect mints T2 revoking T1 — the probe uses T2)
- [ ] The chain adopts a Reconnect's seed exactly once per mint (keyed by fingerprint); the [DRE-2532](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2532/the-token-self-refresher-burns-its-own-seed-the-rotated-refresh-token) regression test (no re-adoption loop) stays green
- [ ] `claude_pool.default_token_for` (post-[DRE-2660](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2660/a-chain-rotation-kills-the-consoles-own-stored-pool-credential-and)) and the probe read the same credential object; a test asserts they are equal after a rotation and after a Reconnect
- [ ] A genuinely capped account still probes as capped, never as "unavailable"
- [ ] The production probe for Dreadnought reads 200 after the first deploy of this change, recorded on this card with the PT time

**Related:** [DRE-2660](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2660/a-chain-rotation-kills-the-consoles-own-stored-pool-credential-and) (the stored pool credential half — merged [dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau#2468](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/review/featdre-2660-the-chain-rotation-keeps-the-consoles-own-stored-5122bb26899c)), [DRE-2532](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2532/the-token-self-refresher-burns-its-own-seed-the-rotated-refresh-token) (why the chain stopped adopting seeds), [DRE-3606](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3606/auto-switch-fired-on-a-usage-probe-429-while-the-fleets-account-was) (auto-switch on a false 429), [DRE-3607](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3607/a-reconnect-or-use-this-that-rewrites-six-repos-shows-no-progress-and) (the hero should read the identity verdict), [DRE-3255](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3255/proof-auto-switch-observed-firing-on-the-live-console-a-429-switches) (the drive that exposed it).

cards.title: harness.yml runs the driver's one Linear read on the sandbox seat — secrets.LINEAR_API_KEY_SANDBOX, declared LINEAR_IDENTITY: sandbox
cards.description:
Re-created from DRE-3635, which was canceled under DRE-3622 when the first critic found the seam: this card waits on a person having created the sandbox seat and watched it work (DRE-3634), so it belongs to the second epic, blocked on the first epic's PROOF card.

This repo's `harness.yml` is the harness DRIVER: it runs every rehearsal against `bureau-harness`, and its `lane_contract` rehearsal makes one read-only Linear query per run. Today that query is made with `secrets.LINEAR_API_KEY` — the fleet's key — so every proving run on `main` and every boundary pull request spends the production bucket, and the job declares no identity at all (`budget: undeclared` on its budget line). Move the driver onto the sandbox seat.

In `.github/workflows/harness.yml`, on the `Run harness scenarios` step, set `LINEAR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.LINEAR_API_KEY_SANDBOX }}` (the env var name inside the driver stays `LINEAR_API_KEY` — `linear_ops` reads that name and nothing in `scripts/harness/` changes), and add a job-level `env: LINEAR_IDENTITY: sandbox` on the `harness` job, beside the job that reads the secret, the DRE-3321 shape. Update the comment on the step: the one read is now on the sandbox's own hour. Pin both in `tests/test_harness_wiring.py`: the scenarios step reads `secrets.LINEAR_API_KEY_SANDBOX` and never `secrets.LINEAR_API_KEY`, and the job declares `sandbox`. Add one line to `scripts/harness/README.md`'s "The Linear side" saying the read is made as `bureau-sandbox`, not as the fleet.

By the time this card is released, the secret exists and has been observed working: DRE-3636 (the PROOF of DRE-3622) records the identity check passing on the sandbox key and a real `bureau-harness` sweep ending `budget: sandbox`, and this card is blocked on it. That is what makes the change safe to merge — with `LINEAR_API_KEY_SANDBOX` absent the expression would resolve to an empty string, the `lane_contract` read would fail, the harness would go red on every push to `main`, and `stable` would stop advancing. `tests/test_agent_linear_key.py` sweeps only `claude-code-action` steps and does not constrain this `run:` step.

**What this card does not claim.** Whether the first `Integration Harness` run on `main` after the merge ends its budget line with `budget: sandbox` is an observation made after the merge, so it cannot gate the merge and is not a criterion here. It belongs to this epic's own PROOF card, written when the epic is planned. The PR body may note it as the observation the proof will make; nothing in this card is owed until it is seen.

**Files:** .github/workflows/harness.yml, tests/test_harness_wiring.py, scripts/harness/README.md

## Contract (shared with siblings)

* Secret read: `secrets.LINEAR_API_KEY_SANDBOX` in `dreadnought-foundry/bureau-pipeline` — the name DRE-3634 (the operator card in DRE-3622) created.
* Declared identity: `LINEAR_IDENTITY: sandbox`, job level on `harness`, the `name` DRE-3628 added to `config/linear-identities.json`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `harness.yml`'s `Run harness scenarios` step sets `LINEAR_API_KEY` to exactly `${{ secrets.LINEAR_API_KEY_SANDBOX }}`; no step in the workflow reads `secrets.LINEAR_API_KEY`; the `harness` job's `env` carries `LINEAR_IDENTITY: sandbox` and no step carries one (tests in `tests/test_harness_wiring.py`, reading the YAML).
- [ ] `python3 -m pytest tests/test_harness_wiring.py tests/test_agent_linear_key.py tests/test_linear_identity_declared.py` is green.
- [ ] `scripts/harness/README.md` says the `lane_contract` read is made as the `bureau-sandbox` seat.
- [ ] The `Integration Harness` check on the pull request itself is green — the run that reviews this change already reads with the sandbox secret, which exists by the time this card is released, and a red harness on the PR means the secret is not where DRE-3634 said it was.

**Blocked by:** DRE-3636

cards.title: [EPIC] The harness driver rides the sandbox seat — bureau-pipeline's one Linear read on bureau-sandbox, after the seat is proven (part 2 of DRE-3622)
cards.description:
**Split from DRE-3622 on 2026-09-12 at the first critic's send-back.** The fence epic had a seam the seam reader named: this repo's harness driver cannot be pointed at the sandbox's Linear seat until a person has created that seat, minted its key, fanned it out and watched a sandbox sweep run on it — the operator card DRE-3634 — and a build card on the far side of a human act is a second epic, not a later step (`standards/card-quality.md`, *When a plan is two epics — the observation-gated seam*, DRE-3244). Left in one epic, the driver card would have merged against a secret nobody could yet prove existed, and its own acceptance criterion could only be checked after the merge it was meant to gate.

**This epic is blocked on DRE-3622 and is planned in detail only when DRE-3622 is Done** — against a seat that exists, a secret that is in place, and an identity check that has printed four `[OK]` lines. Its one build card already exists, carried over from DRE-3622 with the post-merge criterion taken out of it; the planner re-plans around it when this epic enters Planning, and adds this half's own PROOF (the first Integration Harness run on `main` ending `budget: sandbox`, and the fleet key's remaining-requests header read before and after one harness run, unchanged) and DEMO. Nothing under here builds until the CEO approves that plan.

**What rides here:** the harness driver — `harness.yml` makes its one Linear read with `secrets.LINEAR_API_KEY_SANDBOX` and declares `LINEAR_IDENTITY: sandbox`. That card is DRE-3651, re-created from DRE-3635, which is canceled under DRE-3622 with a comment naming its replacement. It is blocked on DRE-3636, DRE-3622's PROOF card — the observation that the seat is real is what releases it.

**What stays in DRE-3622:** the declared identity (DRE-3628), the age-out fence (DRE-3629), the `reconcile.yml` input (DRE-3630), the three other sweep writers (DRE-3632), the operator sign-off (DRE-3634), and its proof and demo, both narrowed to the seat, the sandbox's own sweeps and the production board.

**Where it sits in the wave.** A sibling of DRE-3622 under the wave DRE-3530, with its own number, the shape DRE-3164 and DRE-3245 took. The wave's committed sequence records reorders and drops only, so this epic is not a row in that ledger: it waits on the relation below, and it is moved to Planning when DRE-3622 is Done. It shares no file with the wave's third epic (the sweep) or its fourth (headroom).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The plan for this epic is written when its turn comes — after DRE-3622 is Done — and the CEO green-lights it on that plan.

**Blocked by:** DRE-3622

cards.title: PROOF: a full day of the medic's door on both @main repos, read off the live run list — no job on a run that did not fail, no failure missed
cards.description:
Did it work? Not a green suite: the medic's door observed on the live run lists of the two repos that ride `@main`, over one full day after DRE-3625, DRE-3626 and DRE-3627 are all on `main`, with the reading recorded in the repo so the record merges.

What the operator reads, by hand, from GitHub Actions for `dreadnought-foundry/bureau-pipeline` and `dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau`, for one calendar day (PT):

1. Each `Pipeline Medic` run record of the day, split into: declined at the door (conclusion `skipped`, the `call` job skipped, zero nested jobs) and woke (at least one nested job ran).
2. Each run of a watched workflow that day whose conclusion was `failure` or `timed_out`.
3. The pairing: each run in (2) has a medic run in (1) that woke — none missed — and no medic run woke for a run whose conclusion was `success`, `skipped` or `cancelled`.
4. Three sampled run ids per repo — one declined, one woken by a failure, and the failed run that woke it — with PT times and the nested-job count on each.
5. The day's numbers for the wave's open decision (8): medic run records per repo, medic runs that ran a job, and the day's failure count — the reading the CEO decides the daily bar against.

Record it in `docs/medic-wake-proof-2026-09.md` in the shape of `docs/review-rerun-proof-2026-09.md`: each time in PT, each claim with its run id, read-only. A day on which something was missed is still recorded — the document says so rather than waiting for a clean day.

The baseline this is read against, measured 2026-09-11 02:10 → 2026-09-12 02:10 UTC on bureau-pipeline: 216 medic run records, 213 empty, 8 skipped nested jobs on each empty one, 3 that ran a job, 2 watched-workflow failures.

DRE-3584 is named below because it is a child of this epic; it was cancelled as superseded by the three build cards and clears at once.

**Files:** `docs/medic-wake-proof-2026-09.md` (new)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `docs/medic-wake-proof-2026-09.md` is on `main`, covering one full PT day observed on the live run lists of bureau-pipeline and agent-bureau after all three build cards merged.
- [ ] Observed by hand: zero medic runs of that day ran any job on a completion whose conclusion was `success`, `skipped` or `cancelled`, with the day's declined count per repo and the nested-job count on a sampled declined run (expected 0, against 8 before).
- [ ] Observed by hand: each `failure` or `timed_out` completion of a watched workflow that day is paired with a medic run that ran a job — the run ids listed, none missing.
- [ ] The reading for decision (8) is in the document: medic run records, medic runs that ran a job, and failures, per repo, for the day.

**Blocked by:** DRE-3625, DRE-3626, DRE-3627, DRE-3584

cards.title: PROOF: three live sweeps at or under thirty, one card-done dispatch scoped to one card, and one owner of the age-out for a day, recorded with run ids
cards.description:
Proof is the mechanism observed against the live board, recorded in the repo, not a green suite. Every sibling changes what a live sweep spends or does; this card watches the live sweeps after all of them are on `main` and writes down what they said, with run ids and PT times.

Note on the fleet: bureau-pipeline rides `@main`, so its sweeps carry the change the moment the last sibling merges. agent-bureau rides a release tag and gets it only when the operator promotes the next release, and its stub needs the two `sweep_reason` / `sweep_card` lines added when it does. The agent-bureau section of the record is written when that has happened, or says plainly that it has not yet.

**Files:** docs/sweep-spend-proof-2026-09.md

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Three consecutive `schedule` sweeps on bureau-pipeline, read from `gh run view <id> --log` against the live board, each show `sweep-spend: total` at or under 30 requests; the run ids, PT start times, per-phase lines and totals are recorded in the document.
- [ ] One `repository_dispatch` sweep on bureau-pipeline fired by a card going Done shows the `sweep-scope: card-done …` line and a total at or under 15, recorded with its run id and the card.
- [ ] One 24-hour window in which the only sweep logs carrying an `intake: … aged out` line are bureau-pipeline's, and every other sweeping repo's logs carry the `intake-age-out-owner:` line — read off the runs of every repo in `config/repo-map.json` plus bureau-harness, recorded with counts per repo.
- [ ] The run summary page of one bureau-pipeline sweep shows the `linear-budget:` line; the run id is recorded.
- [ ] `python3 scripts/check_linear_budget.py --hours 1` is run by hand during a busy hour and its table is pasted into the document; every reconcile row shows `max/run` at or under 30 for bureau-pipeline.
- [ ] The agent-bureau section records three consecutive sweeps at or under 30 after the release is promoted, or states that the release has not been promoted yet and what the last three sweeps spent.

**Blocked by:** DRE-3638, DRE-3639, DRE-3640, DRE-3641, DRE-3642, DRE-3643, DRE-3644, DRE-3645
