cards.title: A card-done dispatch reads one card: the sweep scopes a pass whose reason is card-done to the named card's dependents and parent
cards.description:
The relay fires a `repository_dispatch` of type `reconcile` at a repo's stub when a card changes lane — a card going Done, an epic activating — and the stub calls the reusable, which runs a full board pass. Twenty such dispatched sweeps ran on this repo on 2026-09-10 and nine ran on agent-bureau in 54 minutes on 2026-09-09, each a full pass at 92 requests. A card going Done can change exactly two things: the cards it blocks may now be promotable, and its parent epic may now be finished. That is the scoped pass `linear-sync.yml` already runs in-process on a merge, through `merge_sweep_gate.decide` and `reconcile.merged_card_scope` (DRE-2930, DRE-3236). A dispatch for a card-done cannot be dropped — a `no-code` card the operator closes by hand reaches the board only through the relay, never through a merge — so it runs the SAME scoped pass instead of the whole board.

Read two optional environment variables in `reconcile.py`: `SWEEP_REASON` and `SWEEP_CARD`. Add `sweep_scope()` returning the decision and printing one line for it. When `SWEEP_REASON` is `card-done` and `SWEEP_CARD` names a card, `run()` does what linear-sync's merge step does: `merge_sweep_gate.decide(card)`, then for each flag it returns, one scoped pass with `MERGED_CARD` set to the card (`main(promote_only=True)` / `main(close_only=True)`), and nothing else — no backstops, no watchdogs, no age-out, no nudge loop; those are the cron's. When the reason is `epic-activated`, empty, or anything the sweep does not recognise, it runs the full pass it runs today and the line says why. An unreadable card at the gate falls open exactly as the gate already does. `REQUIRED_ENV` does not change: both variables are optional.

**Files:** scripts/reconcile.py, tests/test_sweep_dispatch_scope.py

## Contract (with the workflow sibling that sets the env)

`SWEEP_REASON`: `card-done` scopes; `epic-activated` and every other value, including empty, is a full pass. `SWEEP_CARD`: a card identifier such as `DRE-1234`; case-insensitive, stripped. Printed line: `sweep-scope: card-done <CARD> — scoped to its dependents and parent (<n> pass(es))` or `sweep-scope: full pass (<reason>)` where `<reason>` is the value given or `schedule`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With `SWEEP_REASON=card-done` and `SWEEP_CARD=DRE-1998` over the merge fixture in `tests/test_sweep_request_cuts.py`, `run([])` makes at most 15 Linear reads, reads no whole-Backlog page, evaluates the unblocked dependent and closes the finished epic — the same assertions `test_merge_sync_*` make, reached through `run()`.
- [ ] With `SWEEP_REASON=card-done` and no `SWEEP_CARD`, or with `SWEEP_REASON=epic-activated`, or with both unset, `run([])` runs the full pass (the full-pass backstops are called) and prints the full-pass line naming the reason.
- [ ] A card-done pass never calls `escalate_aged_intake`, `flag_stranded` or any backstop — asserted with mocks.
- [ ] The existing merge-path tests and `scripts/check_reconcile_env.py` pass unchanged.

**Blocked by:** DRE-3644

cards.title: One sweep owns the age-out: the owner is declared in config, and every other repo's sweep leaves Intake alone and says so
cards.description:
Every repo's sweep runs `escalate_aged_intake` over the same board, by design and with no repo filter (an Intake card has no `repo:` label yet). So the fleet-wide age-out rate is the per-sweep cap times the number of sweeping repos, and on the night of 2026-09-09/10 two of those repos were sandboxes: 130+ cards aged out of Intake into the CEO's queue. DRE-3579 was the same-day stop (a dated hold and no schedule on the two sandbox stubs). This card is the durable one: one declared owner of the age-out, and every other sweep leaves Intake alone and says so.

Declare the owner as data: `config/intake-age-out.json` with `{"owner": "bureau-pipeline", "why": "…"}`. The owner is bureau-pipeline because its sweep rides `@main` and so always runs the newest age-out code, while every product repo rides a release tag; neither sandbox slug can ever match it. Add `intake_controls.age_out_owner() -> str` (reads the file), `intake_controls.may_escalate(slug, rail) -> bool` (true only when `slug == owner` and `slug in rail`), and `intake_controls.owner_notice(slug, owner) -> str`, one line opening with the tag `intake-age-out-owner:` saying this sweep is not the owner and which repo is. In `reconcile.escalate_aged_intake`, before the operator's hold is read, consult `may_escalate(REPO_SLUG, validate_card.VALID_SLUGS)`: a non-owner prints the notice once per pass and returns having moved nothing; the owner proceeds exactly as today. A CI test pins that the declared owner is a key of `config/repo-map.json`, so a typo or a retired repo cannot leave the board with no age-out at all. The runbook section "What drains Intake afterwards" in `docs/backlog-cutover.md` says which sweep does it.

The fence epic (DRE-3622) planned the sandbox's own Linear seat; this card delivers the `may_escalate(slug, rail)` seam DRE-3579 named, so the fence epic should not file it again.

**Files:** config/intake-age-out.json, scripts/intake_controls.py, scripts/reconcile.py, tests/test_intake_age_out_owner.py, docs/backlog-cutover.md

## Contract

`config/intake-age-out.json`: `{"owner": "<repo slug>", "why": "<one line>"}`. `intake_controls.age_out_owner() -> str`; `intake_controls.may_escalate(slug: str, rail) -> bool`; `intake_controls.owner_notice(slug: str, owner: str) -> str`. Log tag: `intake-age-out-owner`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With `REPO_SLUG` set to a slug other than the owner, `escalate_aged_intake()` moves nothing, posts nothing, prints exactly one `intake-age-out-owner:` line naming the owner, and returns an empty set — asserted over a board with three cards past the window.
- [ ] With `REPO_SLUG` equal to the owner, behaviour is byte-for-byte what `tests/test_intake_escalation.py` and `tests/test_intake_pen.py` already pin (both suites pass unchanged); the hold still wins when set.
- [ ] A test fails the build if the declared owner is not a key in `config/repo-map.json`.
- [ ] `may_escalate` returns False for `agent-bureau-demo` and for any slug not on the rail.
- [ ] `docs/backlog-cutover.md` names the owning sweep and the config file in the age-out section.

**Blocked by:** DRE-3643

cards.title: The growth record converges and the green light is read off the pass: zero reads and zero rewrites per epic when nothing changed
cards.description:
Two facts, both measured on 2026-09-12 against this repo's live board.

**The growth record never converges.** `report_epic_growth` runs on every full sweep and rewrote all nine active epics' descriptions in one pass with nothing changed (`DRE-2964 description updated`, nine times, every 15 minutes). The cause is verified: `mid_epic.render_artifact` writes `- (none)` under the additions and amendments headings, Linear stores it back as `* (none)` with a blank line before it, so `merge_artifact(description, block) != description` on every read, forever. Each rewrite costs a `get_issue` read inside `set_description` plus the mutation, and bumps the epic's `updatedAt` every pass — nine reads and nine writes per sweep for a record that did not move.

**The green light and the growth are read one request per epic.** `mid_epic.read_epic` (`_EPIC_QUERY`: description, children with `createdAt`, history) is called once per epic by `refresh_epic_growth` and again by `last_green_light` for every wave-committed card the gate looks at — 9 plus 5 reads in the measured pass.

Fix both. Make the convergence check compare what the record MEANS, not its bytes: write the description only when `parse_artifact(merged)` differs from `parse_artifact(description)` or when the description has no managed region yet. Then let both readers take a pre-read record: `mid_epic.refresh_epic_growth(linear_ops, epic, *, add=None, amend=None, issue=None)` and `mid_epic.last_green_light(linear_ops, epic, *, issue=None)` use `issue` when given and read as today when it is `None` (the CLI and `discovery` are unchanged). In `reconcile.report_epic_growth` and in `promote_ready`'s wave-commitment check, pass the record from `reconcile.epic_records(...)` — the seam the epic-close sibling added — so a full sweep makes zero per-epic reads for growth or green light.

Lower `REAL_BOARD_SWEEP_BUDGET` in the replay test to what it measures after this cut, at most 30 — the wave's ceiling, on a real board.

**Files:** scripts/mid_epic.py, scripts/reconcile.py, tests/test_mid_epic_growth_converges.py, tests/test_sweep_real_board.py

## Contract (with the epic-close sibling)

Reads `reconcile.epic_records(identifiers) -> dict[str, dict]` exactly as that sibling defines it (each record: `identifier`, `description`, `state {name}`, `children {nodes [{identifier, createdAt, state {name}}]}`, `history {nodes [{createdAt, toState {name}}]}`, `inverseRelations {…}`). The `issue=` kwarg on the two `mid_epic` readers accepts that record; a record's superset fields are ignored.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A description whose managed region Linear has re-rendered (`* (none)` with a blank line before it) is NOT rewritten: `refresh_epic_growth` makes no `set_description` call when the parsed record is unchanged — a test feeds the exact live shape captured on DRE-2964 and asserts zero writes.
- [ ] A genuine change (a new child after the green light, an addition, an amendment) still rewrites the record and posts the existing notices — the existing `mid_epic` tests pass unchanged.
- [ ] Over the real-board replay, a full sweep makes zero Linear reads attributable to `report_epic_growth` and zero to the green-light lookup, and zero description writes when nothing changed; the recorded decisions are unchanged.
- [ ] `REAL_BOARD_SWEEP_BUDGET` is lowered to the measured value, at most 30, with the date and number in its comment.

**Blocked by:** DRE-3642

cards.title: One read per pass for every active epic: the epic close and the epic gate read a batched record instead of one request each
cards.description:
Measured read-only on 2026-09-12 on this repo's board: `close_finished_epics` costs one children read per active epic (9), and the epic-level gate inside `promote_ready` costs one relations read per epic that has Backlog children (9, via `_fetch_epic_relations`). Both scale with the number of active epics, and the number of active epics is what grew between DRE-3236's measurement (~20 per pass) and today's 65 and 92. The board read already carries every epic; what it does not carry is the epic's children states, its relations and its history, so each consumer buys its own read per epic.

Replace the per-epic reads with ONE paged read per pass. Add `reconcile.epic_records(identifiers)`: one `gql_paged` read of the named epics (`filter: {team: DRE, number: {in: […]}}`, the shape `backlog_children(only=…)` already uses) selecting the union of what every per-epic reader needs, cached in a module-level dict for the pass and cleared by `reset_sweep_cards()`. Then make `_close_epic_if_finished` read its children states off the record and `_fetch_epic_relations` read `identifier`, `description` and `inverseRelations` off it. The per-epic isolation that DRE-3148 and DRE-1772 built stays: an epic missing from the record (unreadable, or its identifier not answered) is treated exactly as an unreadable read is today — skipped for the close, fail-safe blocked for the gate, both out loud. A batched read that fails as a whole is retried once per epic the old way, so a Linear hiccup on the batch never silently blocks every epic.

Lower `REAL_BOARD_SWEEP_BUDGET` in the replay test to what it measures after this cut, at most 50.

**Files:** scripts/reconcile.py, tests/test_epic_records.py, tests/test_sweep_real_board.py

## Contract (read by the growth sibling)

`reconcile.epic_records(identifiers: Iterable[str]) -> dict[str, dict]` — keyed by identifier; one paged read for every identifier not already in the pass's cache; cleared by `reset_sweep_cards()`. Each record carries exactly: `identifier`, `description`, `state {name}`, `children {nodes [{identifier, createdAt, state {name}}]}` (`first: 250`), `history {nodes [{createdAt, toState {name}}]}` (`last: 50`), `inverseRelations {nodes [{type, issue {identifier, state {name}}}]}` (`first: 20`). An identifier Linear did not answer is absent from the dict, never present as an empty record.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Over the real-board replay, a full sweep makes at most ONE Linear read attributable to `close_finished_epics` and at most ONE attributable to the epic gate's relations, however many epics are active; the replay's recorded decisions are unchanged.
- [ ] An epic absent from the batched answer is skipped by the close with a printed line and treated as blocked by the gate with a printed line — the existing fail-safe tests for both still pass.
- [ ] A batched read that raises falls back to the per-epic reads, once, and the sweep still completes.
- [ ] `REAL_BOARD_SWEEP_BUDGET` is lowered to the measured value, at most 50, with the date and number in its comment.

**Blocked by:** DRE-3639, DRE-3641

cards.title: The request ceiling is measured on the real board: a replay test runs every phase of the sweep over the snapshot and pins the spend
cards.description:
The existing ceiling test measures a sweep with 18 of its phases mocked out, over a board that has no wave-committed cards, no aged Intake cards and five epics. That is why it says 30 while a live pass costs 65 here and 92 on agent-bureau. This card measures the real thing in CI: every phase of the sweep, live, over the committed real-board snapshot, with only GitHub stubbed.

Add `tests/test_sweep_real_board.py`. It loads the fixture the snapshot sibling committed, serves it through a subclass of `test_sweep_request_cuts.FakeLinear` (import it, do not copy it) that answers every query shape the sweep makes on this board — the epic history read, the label-filtered break-glass count, the scoped Backlog read, the children read, the relations read — and runs `reconcile.main()` with `REPO_SLUG` pinned to `bureau-pipeline`, every GitHub seam stubbed (`gh_read`, `gh`, `gh_dispatch`, `gh_actions_read`, `_nudge`) and every Linear write stubbed the way the existing suite stubs them. NO phase is mocked. It then asserts three things: the total reads are at most `REAL_BOARD_SWEEP_BUDGET`; a per-phase table (reads attributed to the function `main()` called, the way the read-only measurement on 2026-09-12 attributed them) is printed on failure so the next reader sees where the spend went; and the sweep's decisions over the fixture — which cards it would promote, hold, escalate and close — equal a recorded list committed beside the test, so a later cut that meets the ceiling by doing less work fails by name.

Set `REAL_BOARD_SWEEP_BUDGET` to what the replay measures on the day it lands (expected about 65), not to 30: the ceiling is honest from this card on, and each cut sibling lowers it to what it measures, ending at 30. A ceiling that passes on a fake board is the defect; a ceiling that fails on the real one before the cuts exist is just a red build.

**Files:** tests/test_sweep_real_board.py, tests/fixtures/board-snapshot-2026-09-12.decisions.json

## Contract (shared with the cut siblings, which lower the number)

`REAL_BOARD_SWEEP_BUDGET` — a module-level int in `tests/test_sweep_real_board.py`, the only place the real-board ceiling lives. The per-phase attribution names phases by the `reconcile.py` function name, the same names the `sweep-spend:` lines use.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The test runs every backstop and every phase of a full sweep over the committed snapshot with no `reconcile` function mocked; only the GitHub seams and the Linear writes are stubbed.
- [ ] It fails when the total exceeds `REAL_BOARD_SWEEP_BUDGET`, printing a per-phase table; the constant is set to the measured value with a comment naming the date and the number.
- [ ] It fails when the sweep's decisions over the fixture differ from the recorded decisions file (promotions, holds, escalations, closes).
- [ ] It runs in under 30 seconds and does not touch the network (a test asserts `urllib.request.urlopen` is never called).

**Blocked by:** DRE-3638

cards.title: The reconcile workflow shows the sweep's spend in its run summary and threads the dispatch's reason and card into the sweep
cards.description:
Two things the wave asks of the reconcile workflow, both YAML only, both in the files this repo owns.

**The summary.** The sweep prints `linear-budget: <first> → <last> (spent N this run; …)` on stderr as it exits and nothing shows it: reading a pass's spend today means opening the run log. In the `Sweep` step of the reusable, capture the step's output, let it flow to the log as it does now, and append the `linear-budget:` line (and every `sweep-spend:` line, if present) to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, so the run's summary page carries the spend. A pass that printed no budget line writes one summary line saying so rather than nothing.

**The dispatch's reason and card.** The pipeline's own stub takes `repository_dispatch: types: [reconcile]` from the relay and calls the reusable with fixed inputs, so a relay dispatch fired for one card going Done runs a full board pass — 20 of them on 2026-09-10 on this repo alone, each the full price. Add two optional `workflow_call` inputs to the reusable, `sweep_reason` and `sweep_card` (type string, default empty), threaded into the `Sweep` step's env as `SWEEP_REASON` and `SWEEP_CARD` verbatim (never a literal), and have `self-reconcile.yml` pass `${{ github.event.client_payload.reason }}` and `${{ github.event.client_payload.identifier }}`. On `schedule` and `workflow_dispatch` both interpolate to the empty string, which the sweep reads as a full pass. The stub is the adapter: read the relay's actual payload keys off the relay source in agent-bureau before wiring, and if the relay names them differently, map them in the stub — the reusable's input names are the contract and do not move.

**Files:** .github/workflows/reconcile.yml, .github/workflows/self-reconcile.yml, tests/test_reconcile_workflow_spend_and_scope.py

## Contract (shared with the sweep sibling that reads the env)

Reusable inputs: `sweep_reason` (string, optional, default `""`; values the sweep recognises: `card-done`, `epic-activated`; anything else, including empty, means a full pass) and `sweep_card` (string, optional, default `""`; a card identifier such as `DRE-1234`). Env in the Sweep step: `SWEEP_REASON: ${{ inputs.sweep_reason }}` and `SWEEP_CARD: ${{ inputs.sweep_card }}`. Stub `with:` lines: `sweep_reason: ${{ github.event.client_payload.reason }}`, `sweep_card: ${{ github.event.client_payload.identifier }}`. Summary lines are the sweep's own `linear-budget:` and `sweep-spend:` lines, verbatim.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A live-extraction test loads `reconcile.yml` and asserts the two inputs exist with type string and empty default, and that the Sweep step's env threads each as `${{ inputs.<name> }}` and never a literal.
- [ ] The same test loads `self-reconcile.yml` and asserts both `with:` lines are present with the `client_payload` expressions above.
- [ ] The Sweep step's shell writes the `linear-budget:` line (and any `sweep-spend:` lines) to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, and a test executes that shell over a fake log containing both line kinds and a fake log containing neither, and checks the summary file each time.
- [ ] `scripts/check_reconcile_env.py`, `scripts/check_wip_cap.py`, `scripts/check_pipeline_ref.py` and `tests/test_intake_pen.py` still pass over the edited workflows.

cards.title: Every full sweep prints its Linear spend per phase and in total, one greppable line each
cards.description:
A live sweep prints one `linear-budget:` line as it exits, and that is the whole of what it says about its spend. Measured read-only on 2026-09-12 against this repo's board, one full pass cost 65 Linear reads: 18 in `promote_ready` (one relations read per epic with Backlog children, one green-light read per wave-committed card), 18 in `report_epic_growth` (one read plus one description rewrite per active epic, every pass), 15 in `escalate_aged_intake` (five reads per escalated card), 9 in `close_finished_epics` (one children read per epic), 4 for the board itself and 1 for the break-glass count. None of that is readable from the run log today, so the sibling cuts cannot show their effect live and a regression cannot be placed.

Make the sweep say it. Add `linear_ops.requests_made() -> int` (the count `gql` already keeps in its budget state, read out, never reset here). In `reconcile.main()`, wrap every phase a full pass runs — each backstop in the loop, `flag_stranded`, `escalate_aged_intake`, the board read, `close_finished_epics`, `promote_ready`, the nudge loop, and each of the four report steps — so that after each one the sweep prints one line naming the phase and the reads it cost, and at the end one total line. Print the line only when the phase cost at least one request, so a quiet phase does not add noise; always print the total. The event-driven modes (`--promote-only`, `--close-epics`, `--conflicts-only`) print the same lines for the phases they run.

**Files:** scripts/reconcile.py, scripts/linear_ops.py, tests/test_sweep_spend_lines.py

## Contract (read by the PROOF card and the workflow-summary sibling)

Per phase: `sweep-spend: <phase> <n> request(s)` where `<phase>` is the function's name as it appears in `reconcile.py` (`promote_ready`, `report_epic_growth`, `escalate_aged_intake`, `close_finished_epics`, `board_read`, `nudge_loop`, …). Last line of every pass: `sweep-spend: total <n> request(s) over <k> phase(s)`. Both go to stdout. The `linear-budget:` line is unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A full sweep over a fake board prints one `sweep-spend:` line per phase that made a request, with the count equal to the fake's own count of requests made during that phase, and a final `sweep-spend: total …` line whose number equals the fake's total.
- [ ] A phase that made zero requests prints no line; the total line is printed even when it is zero.
- [ ] `--promote-only` prints lines for the gate and the total only.
- [ ] No sweep decision changes: the existing suites `tests/test_sweep_request_cuts.py` and `tests/test_sweep_request_budget.py` pass unchanged.

cards.title: The board snapshot: a script takes the real board in the shape the sweep reads, and the fixture is committed
cards.description:
The CI ceiling on the sweep's Linear spend passes at 30 while a live pass costs 65 on bureau-pipeline and 92 on agent-bureau, because the fixture it runs over is not a real board: `tests/test_sweep_request_cuts.py` hand-builds 5 epics and 260 Backlog cards and mocks 18 of the sweep's phases out entirely (its `_sweep_mocks()` list). The wave's Plan A names this: the fixture is part of the defect.

This card takes the real board and commits it as a fixture, in the shape the sweep's own reads return, so the replay test (a sibling) can run every phase over it. Add `scripts/board_snapshot.py take --out <path>` — stdlib plus `linear_ops`, read-only, one paged read of every DRE card in the lanes the sweep reads (`reconcile.SWEPT_LANES` plus `Backlog`, `Intake` and `Planning`), selecting per card exactly what the sweep's queries select. It pages through `linear_ops.gql_paged` and prints its own `linear-budget:` line; taking the snapshot must cost under 20 requests. Commit the snapshot it takes today as the fixture.

Scrub on the way out, and test the scrub as a pure function: comment bodies are truncated to their first 200 characters (every marker this pipeline reads is anchored at the start of a body), descriptions are kept whole (the sweep reads growth records, wave-commitment blocks and blocker lines anywhere in them), user ids are kept (opaque, the authorship credential), and no display names or emails are written. The file must be under 4 MB. Comments are stored newest first, exactly as Linear answers a `first: 50` window, with the window's `pageInfo`.

**Files:** scripts/board_snapshot.py, tests/test_board_snapshot.py, tests/fixtures/board-snapshot-2026-09-12.json

## Contract (shared with the replay-test sibling)

Fixture path: `tests/fixtures/board-snapshot-2026-09-12.json`. Top level: `{"taken_at": <ISO-8601 UTC>, "team": "DRE", "lanes": [<lane names read>], "cards": [<card>, …]}`. Each card carries exactly these keys, in the shape the sweep's board reads return them: `id`, `identifier`, `title`, `description`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `state {name}`, `labels {nodes [{name}]}`, `parent {identifier, state {name}} | null`, `children {nodes [{id, identifier, createdAt, state {name}}]}`, `comments {pageInfo {hasNextPage, endCursor}, nodes [{body, createdAt, user {id} | null}]}` (newest first), `relations {pageInfo {hasNextPage}, nodes [{type, issue {identifier}, relatedIssue {identifier}}]}`, `inverseRelations {nodes [{type, issue {identifier, state {name}}}]}`, `history {nodes [{createdAt, toState {name}}]}`. A key the sweep never reads is not in the file.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `python3 scripts/board_snapshot.py take --out /tmp/x.json` against the live board writes a file in the contract shape and its `linear-budget:` line shows fewer than 20 requests spent.
- [ ] `tests/fixtures/board-snapshot-2026-09-12.json` is committed, under 4 MB, and every card in it validates against the contract keys (a test loads it and checks).
- [ ] The scrub is a pure function with tests: bodies over 200 characters are cut to 200, descriptions are untouched, `user` keeps only `id`, and a card with a partial comment window keeps `hasNextPage: true`.
- [ ] The script never sends a mutation (a test patches `linear_ops.gql` and asserts no query starts with `mutation`).

cards.title: PROOF: three Linear seats held apart, the sandbox spending its own hour, and three consecutive sandbox sweeps refusing every board move — observed live and recorded in docs/sandbox-seat-proof-2026-09.md
cards.description:
The mechanism, observed against the live workspace and the live sandbox, with the observation recorded in the repo beside `docs/linear-identities-proof-2026-09.md` — the same shape, one document, every time in PT, every number read off a run log or an API header, never remembered.

This proof covers what DRE-3622 ships: the seat, the sandbox's own sweeps and gates on it, and the sweep fence. This repo's Integration Harness driver still reads on the fleet key until the sibling epic DRE-3650 moves it; its one read per run is that epic's proof to make, not this one's, and this document says so in its closing table rather than leaving it out.

Write `docs/sandbox-seat-proof-2026-09.md` recording, in this order:

1. **Three seats, held apart.** `python3 scripts/check_linear_identities.py check` with all four key homes exported: four `[OK]` lines, three distinct user ids, none an admin, exit 0. Pasted verbatim with the PT time.
2. **The sandbox spends its own hour.** The `linear-budget:` line from three `bureau-harness` workflow runs on the day — one reconcile sweep, one merge gate, one probe PR's CI — each ending `budget: sandbox`, with run ids. Then the fleet key's `x-ratelimit-requests-remaining` read twice — immediately before and immediately after one `bureau-harness` reconcile run dispatched by hand — showing the sandbox run did not lower it (the reading's own drift from other traffic stated honestly).
3. **The sandbox sweep holds its hands off.** From three consecutive `bureau-harness` reconcile runs on the day: the `off-rail:` line present on every pass, four times per pass (age-out, retiring-lane drain, limit-death re-entry, fleet reviewer-outage), and no `intake: … aged out` line, no `drain:` line, no `fleet-reviewer-outage:` card filed. Then the production side: one `agent-bureau` or `bureau-pipeline` sweep on the same day with NO `off-rail:` line and its age-out running (or its `intake-hold` line, if the pen is held).
4. **The board.** Every card that left Intake in the 24 hours ending at the observation, with the receipt's `intake-overdue` comment on each, and the answer to one question: did any of them leave by a sandbox sweep? The expected answer is zero, and it is read off the receipts, not assumed.
5. **Did the claim hold** — criterion by criterion, in the table shape the earlier proof uses, including anything that did not, and one row naming the harness driver's read as deferred to DRE-3650.

This card is confirmed by a person reading live state and is not fleet-buildable: every line above is an observation of production or of the live sandbox, by hand.

**Files:** docs/sandbox-seat-proof-2026-09.md

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `docs/sandbox-seat-proof-2026-09.md` is on `main` with the five sections above, every time in PT, and every run id resolving.
- [ ] The identity check's four `[OK]` lines were observed by hand against the live workspace and are quoted in the document.
- [ ] The `off-rail:` lines were observed in the live `bureau-harness` sweep logs on three consecutive passes, and the absence of any Intake move by a sandbox sweep over 24 hours was read off the live board's receipts, by hand.
- [ ] The document's closing table names every criterion of this epic's plan and says held or did not, with the evidence line for each, and names the harness driver's read as the observation DRE-3650 owes.

**Blocked by:** DRE-3628, DRE-3629, DRE-3630, DRE-3632, DRE-3634, DRE-3635, DRE-3579, DRE-3581, DRE-3583

cards.title: The sweep's other three fleet-wide writers ask the same question — retiring-lane drain, limit-death re-entry, fleet reviewer-outage card — and off the rail none of them writes
cards.description:
The age-out is the sweep writer that moved 130+ cards, and the sibling card fences it. It is not the only writer in `reconcile.py` that moves or files a card this repo does not own. Read at plan time, there are exactly three more, and this card fences those three with the same predicate so the epic's claim — a sandbox sweep moves, escalates or ages out nothing on the production board — is true of the whole pass, not of one function:

1. `drain_retiring_lanes()` — moves every card out of a retiring lane, whoever owns it (nothing is retiring today; it returns before reading, and the fence goes before that read so the next retirement is fenced too).
2. `recover_limit_deaths()` — re-enters limit-dead runs for cards with no `repo:` label as well as this repo's, moving lanes and dispatching; a sandbox owns no card and must re-enter nothing.
3. `report_fleet_reviewer_outage()` — reads every active card's comments and files ONE fleet-wide card when the reviewer is down everywhere; a sandbox's probe PRs are the harness's evidence, not the fleet's, and it must file nothing.

At the top of each, ask `intake_controls.may_escalate(REPO_SLUG, validate_card.VALID_SLUGS)`; when refused, print `intake_controls.off_rail_notice(REPO_SLUG, "<what this writer declined>")` and return — before any board read, never as a write failure, never red. Three sites, one predicate, one notice; no new module, no new tag. Everything else in the pass — the per-card nudge loop, `promote_ready`, `close_finished_epics`, `flag_stranded`, `flag_stalled_planning`, `report_epic_growth` — is already filtered to `REPO_SLUG` or to cards whose slug is on the rail, and is not touched. The GitHub-side backstops the harness depends on (`review_dependabot_prs`, `unstick_conflicts`, `retrigger_dead_heads`, `recover_crashed_reviews`) are not touched either: the sandbox's `dependabot_flow` rehearsal needs them.

Collision rule with the wave's sweep work: DRE-3580 (the sweep-spend card) claims `reconcile.py` for the wave and asks every other card to add a call site of three lines or fewer with its logic elsewhere. This card adds three such guards and no logic; the predicate and the notice are the sibling's, in `intake_controls.py`.

**Files:** scripts/reconcile.py, tests/test_off_rail_writers.py

## Contract (shared with siblings)

Reads, never redefines, the sibling's seam: `intake_controls.may_escalate(slug, rail)`, `intake_controls.off_rail_notice(slug, detail)`, `intake_controls.TAG_OFF_RAIL == "off-rail"`, with `validate_card.VALID_SLUGS` as the rail.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With `REPO_SLUG=bureau-harness`, each of the three functions returns without calling `active_cards`, `cmd_advance`, `cmd_state`, `cmd_comment`, `find_open_prefix` or `gh_dispatch`, and prints exactly one line opening `off-rail:` (one test per function, counting the tag).

cards.title: The sweep's age-out asks intake_controls.may_escalate(slug, rail) — a sweep off the routing rail moves no Intake card, and says so once per pass
cards.description:
`reconcile.escalate_aged_intake()` has no repo filter by design — Intake cards carry no `repo:` label yet, so every repo's sweep reads the whole lane and moves the oldest three past the window into Green Light. That design assumed every sweep was a production sweep. The sandbox repos run the same reusable `reconcile.yml`, and on the night of 2026-09-09/10 sandbox sweeps helped age 130+ cards out of Intake into the CEO's queue. The operator set a dated `INTAKE_HOLD` on both sandbox stubs the same day; this card is the durable fence the wave asked for.

Add `intake_controls.may_escalate(slug, rail)` — the fourth reading of the pen, beside `hold`, `max_age_minutes` and `escalation_cap` — answering one question: may a sweep running as repo `slug` move a board card it does not own? The answer is `slug in rail`, where `rail` is the routing snapshot's slug set (`validate_card.VALID_SLUGS`, the bundled `config/repo-map.json` keys — deterministic, no network; `bureau-harness` is not on it, every product repo is). Add `intake_controls.off_rail_notice(slug, detail)`, the one line a refused pass prints, opening with the tag `off-rail`. In `escalate_aged_intake()`, ask `may_escalate(REPO_SLUG, validate_card.VALID_SLUGS)` BEFORE the Intake walk (a refused sweep spends no read on the lane), print the notice and return the empty set. The refusal is a normal pass — never a write failure, never red: the harness reads a red sandbox sweep as a dead sandbox and blocks `main`'s proving run.

Do NOT filter by repo inside the walk — an on-rail sweep still reads and moves unlabelled cards exactly as today; the docstring's "NO REPO FILTER, deliberately" stays true for production sweeps and gains one sentence saying a sandbox is refused at the door. Update `docs/backlog-cutover.md`'s controls table with the fourth control. `agent-bureau-demo` IS on the rail (cards route to it), so this card does not fence it; the wave's third epic makes one production sweep the age-out owner by narrowing this same predicate, and the operator's dated hold on the demo stub stands until then — say so in the docstring.

Collision rule with the wave's sweep work: DRE-3580 (the sweep-spend card) claims `reconcile.py` for the wave and asks every other card to land its logic in its own module and add a call site of three lines or fewer. This card honours that — the predicate and the notice live in `intake_controls.py`; the edit to `escalate_aged_intake` is one guard of three lines plus one sentence in its docstring.

**Files:** scripts/intake_controls.py, scripts/reconcile.py, tests/test_intake_off_rail.py, docs/backlog-cutover.md

## Contract (shared with siblings)

* `intake_controls.may_escalate(slug: str, rail) -> bool` — `True` iff `slug` (lower-cased) is in `rail` (any container of lower-case slugs). Pure; reads no environment. An empty or `None` rail returns `False` and is a caller defect, not a sweep decision — the caller passes the bundled snapshot, which is never empty.
* `intake_controls.off_rail_notice(slug: str, detail: str) -> str` — one line, opening `off-rail: `, naming `slug`, saying this sweep runs off the routing rail so it moves no board card it does not own, and carrying `detail` (the caller's own words for what it declined).
* `intake_controls.TAG_OFF_RAIL = "off-rail"` — the tag the notice opens with; the sibling card that fences the sweep's other three writers prints the SAME notice and nothing else.
* The rail the sweep passes is `validate_card.VALID_SLUGS` (already imported by `reconcile.py`). Not `live_rail_slugs()` — that is a network read with a `None` answer, and a sweep must not spend a request to decide whether it may spend requests.
* The wave's third epic narrows `may_escalate` to "the declared age-out owner" by adding a clause to THIS function — it does not add a second function.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `intake_controls.may_escalate("bureau-harness", validate_card.VALID_SLUGS)` is `False`; for every key of `config/repo-map.json` it is `True` (a test iterates the real file, never a restated list).
- [ ] With `REPO_SLUG=bureau-harness`, `reconcile.escalate_aged_intake()` returns an empty set, calls neither `cmd_advance` nor `cmd_comment`, does not call `active_cards`/the Intake read at all, and prints exactly one line opening `off-rail:` (a test counts the tag).
- [ ] With `REPO_SLUG=agent-bureau` and the same aged fixture, the existing `tests/test_intake_escalation.py` and `tests/test_intake_pen.py` behaviour is unchanged (both suites green, untouched).
- [ ] The refusal never lands on `_write_failures` or `_read_failures`: a full `reconcile.main()` run with `REPO_SLUG=bureau-harness` and the age-out reached exits 0 on that path (test through the existing intake test harness pattern).
- [ ] `docs/backlog-cutover.md` names the off-rail refusal beside the three existing Intake controls, and `scripts/intake_controls.py`'s docstring says four readings, not three.

cards.description:
The fleet has two declared non-human Linear identities — `fleet` (`Agent-Bureau`) and `operator-tools` (`bureau-tools`) — and the sandbox has none: `bureau-harness`'s stubs and this repo's `harness.yml` driver both spend the fleet's 2,500/hour bucket, which is how probe traffic on `main` sat in the same bucket as every planner and review on 2026-09-09 (wave DRE-3530). This card declares the third seat as data, so that the check that already holds the other two apart holds this one apart too, and so `linear_ops.declared_identity()` accepts the word `sandbox` on a run's `linear-budget:` line.

Add a third row to `config/linear-identities.json` exactly as the contract below states, add `"sandbox"` to the `must_differ_from` list of BOTH existing rows (the check judges each pair once, but the declaration should read symmetrically), and update the file's `_readme` so it no longer says "WHY TWO". `scripts/check_linear_identities.py` is config-driven and needs no logic change — its module docstring says "two non-human identities" and must say three (docstring-only change). Pin it in `tests/test_linear_identities.py`: the shipped declaration carries three identities, `sandbox` reads its key from `LINEAR_API_KEY_SANDBOX`, it must differ from both others, `config_problems()` is empty on the shipped file, and a fake viewer that resolves the sandbox key to the same user as the fleet key FAILS naming `must_differ_from`.

Nothing here touches a workflow, a secret or the sweep. The key itself is minted by the operator card in this epic; until then the check reports `[UNKNOWN] sandbox` and exits non-zero, which is its designed behaviour for an absent key and is run on the operator's machine, not in CI.

**Files:** config/linear-identities.json, scripts/check_linear_identities.py, tests/test_linear_identities.py

## Contract (shared with siblings)

The identity row, verbatim in the JSON (`purpose` and `lives_in` may be reworded; the four quoted values may not):

* `"name": "sandbox"`
* `"display_name": "bureau-sandbox"`
* `"env": "LINEAR_API_KEY_SANDBOX"` — the variable the check reads on the operator's machine
* `"lives_in"`: the GitHub Actions secret `LINEAR_API_KEY` in `dreadnought-foundry/bureau-harness` (read by every sandbox stub as `secrets.LINEAR_API_KEY`), the GitHub Actions secret `LINEAR_API_KEY_SANDBOX` in `dreadnought-foundry/bureau-pipeline` (read only by `harness.yml`), and the operator's `.env` as `LINEAR_API_KEY_SANDBOX`
* `"must_not_be_admin": true`
* `"must_differ_from": ["fleet", "operator-tools"]`

The word a run declares in `LINEAR_IDENTITY` for this seat is `sandbox` — the `name`, never the display name.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `config/linear-identities.json` declares exactly three identities: `fleet`, `operator-tools`, `sandbox`, and `python3 scripts/check_linear_identities.py check` with no keys exported prints an `[UNKNOWN]` line for each of the four key homes (fleet, fleet/relay, operator-tools, sandbox) and exits non-zero — no `[FAIL] config:` line.

- [ ] A test drives `check_linear_identities.run` with a fake viewer in which the sandbox key resolves to the fleet's user and asserts a `[FAIL] sandbox` line naming `must_differ_from`; the same test with three distinct non-admin users asserts four `[OK]` lines and exit 0.

cards.description:

1. `agent-bureau/.github/workflows/medic.yml` (the stub) — its `call` job gains an `if:` carrying the contract expression below. The watch list, the `uses:` ref and `secrets: inherit` do not change.
2. `agent-bureau/tests/test_medic_stub_wake_set.py` — RED first: load the stub with `yaml.safe_load` and assert its `call` job's `if:` is byte-identical to the contract expression. agent-bureau's test run has no bureau-pipeline checkout to import the module from, so the test pins the literal — that literal IS the contract with DRE-3625, and the test's docstring says so. If agent-bureau already has a test module that pins this stub's shape, put the assertion there instead and name that file in the PR body.

After this card a medic run in agent-bureau for a `success`, `skipped` or `cancelled` completion shows one skipped job and no nested jobs; a `failure` or `timed_out` completion runs exactly as it does today.

— the string bureau-pipeline's `scripts/medic_wake.py` `expression()` returns (DRE-3625). The set is `failure` and `timed_out`, nothing else.

cards.title: bureau-pipeline: the medic's wake set is declared once — failure and timed_out — and the reusable medic reads it
cards.description:
The reusable Pipeline Medic (`.github/workflows/medic.yml`) already refuses to start any job unless the run it was woken for concluded `failure`: the `classify` job carries that condition and the seven jobs downstream of it repeat it — eight `if:` sites in total, at lines 99, 275, 305, 356, 425, 453, 489 and 534 on today's `main`. Two things are wrong with the way that rule is held. It is written as a literal in eight places and pinned by nothing, so nothing says which conclusions CAN need a medic and why the others cannot. And the set is one short: a run that concluded `timed_out` never wakes the medic at all. The operator's decision on the wave (DRE-3530, 2026-09-10 21:59 PT) is: wake on `failure` and `timed_out`; stay silent on `cancelled` (a sweep superseded by its own concurrency group), as well as on `success` and `skipped`.

This card declares that set ONCE, in a new stdlib-only module `scripts/medic_wake.py`, and makes the reusable medic read it — in the only way a workflow can read a Python declaration: the module renders the GitHub Actions expression, the workflow carries the rendered text, and a test holds the two to each other.

What to build:

1. `scripts/medic_wake.py` — `WAKE_ON = ("failure", "timed_out")`; `SILENT_ON`, a dict of conclusion → the one-line reason it stays silent, covering at least `success`, `skipped` and `cancelled`; and `expression()` returning exactly the contract expression below. The docstring carries the operator's `cancelled` decision and its date. `python3 scripts/medic_wake.py` prints the expression.
2. `.github/workflows/medic.yml` — each of the eight `github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'failure'` clauses becomes the rendered expression, byte-identical. Nothing else in the file changes, except the header comment's "when any pipeline workflow fails" gains "or times out".
3. `tests/test_medic_wake_set.py` — RED first: (a) `medic_wake.WAKE_ON` is exactly `failure` and `timed_out`, and `SILENT_ON` names `success`, `skipped` and `cancelled` each with a non-empty reason; (b) live-extracts `medic.yml` with `yaml.safe_load`, finds every job `if:` that mentions `workflow_run.conclusion`, and asserts each contains `expression()` and none contains the old `== 'failure'` form; (c) the `classify` job's `if:` is exactly the expression.

The change is mechanical — eight one-line replacements in a 690-line workflow, a ~40-line module and one test file. The turn budget is raised one rung (`turns:250`) because the spend here is reading `medic.yml` and its six wiring tests, not writing: the DRE-3088 shape.

Not in this card: the calling stubs (this repo's `self-medic.yml`, agent-bureau's stub) — sibling cards blocked on this one; the Linear reads a real failure costs once the medic is awake; the four tag-riding repos' stubs (deferred in the plan).

**Files:** `scripts/medic_wake.py` (new), `.github/workflows/medic.yml`, `tests/test_medic_wake_set.py` (new)

## Contract (shared with siblings)

The rendered expression — written identically in this card and in both stub cards, and produced by `medic_wake.expression()`:

```
contains(fromJSON('["failure","timed_out"]'), github.event.workflow_run.conclusion)
```

The module path is `scripts/medic_wake.py`; the two public names are `WAKE_ON` and `expression`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `python3 scripts/medic_wake.py` prints exactly the contract expression, and `medic_wake.WAKE_ON == ("failure", "timed_out")`.
- [ ] Every job `if:` in `.github/workflows/medic.yml` that reads `workflow_run.conclusion` contains the contract expression and none contains `conclusion == 'failure'`; pinned by `tests/test_medic_wake_set.py`, which fails against today's `main`.
- [ ] The six existing medic wiring tests (`tests/test_medic_*.py`) are unchanged and green — the DRE-2954, DRE-3171 and DRE-3430 cases still classify on a `failure` payload.
- [ ] `SILENT_ON` names `cancelled` with the operator's reason and `success` and `skipped` with theirs; the test asserts all three are absent from `WAKE_ON`.
- [ ] The TDD commit order holds: `python3 scripts/check_tdd_commits.py origin/main HEAD` exits 0.

cards.title: PROOF: the production console stands down with the fleet's account unknown, classifies a real usage-probe 429, and survives ten page reloads without one — observed live and recorded in the repo
cards.description:
The mechanism observed running against real state, with the observation recorded in the repo — not a green suite. Every build card of this epic ships behind tests; this card answers whether the production console actually stands down, classifies a real 429 correctly, and stops asking Anthropic on every page load. It is run by a person at an interactive session against `https://app.agent-bureau.com` and the live App Runner service, in the shape of `architecture/audits/2026-09-DRE-3170-auto-switch-proof.md` (DRE-3255), and it says plainly what was and was not observed.

Pre-condition: the release carrying all six build cards is live. Record the `CONSOLE_VERSION` / `CONSOLE_BUILD_SHA` read from `aws apprunner describe-service` and the PT time, and `git tag --contains` for each card's merge commit, as DRE-3255 §1 does.

Three observations, each with PT times, verbatim copy, and the log lines quoted (no token value ever):

1. **The stand-down.** Repeat DRE-3255 §5(c) on the demo repo only — `gh secret set CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN -R dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau-demo` with a value the console did not write, never while that repo is building a card. Within one identity tick record: the per-repo WARN naming `agent-bureau-demo`, the Subscriptions hero reading the fleet-account-unknown line, and the backend log's auto-switch line for the next ticks. Then, for the duration of the episode, watch for exhaustion evidence arriving on its own (a 429 row on the active account, or limit receipts). If any arrives: record the `Stood down (stood-down): …` line appearing in the switch log on the page (PT time, amber chip, the reason naming `agent-bureau-demo`), that NO switch line followed it, that `claude_auto_switch_last` did not move, and that the same evidence on later ticks wrote no second line. If none arrives inside the episode, say so — the stand-down with evidence is then recorded from the replay test's run, named as such, and the epic's demo carries that caveat. End the episode by rotating from the console (Reconnect or "Use this") and record the repo returning to `console` and the WARN resolving.
2. **The 429, classified.** Do NOT arrange a 429 — never drive Anthropic's rate limit on purpose. Record the FIRST usage-probe 429 the backend log carries after the release (the new WARNING with status, retry-after and the message excerpt), quote its body, state which string the row carried on the page (`usage unavailable (rate-limited, retrying)` or `usage limit reached (HTTP 429)`), and what followed: for a rate-limited reading, no cap alert, no pool move, no switch, and the row recovering on the next probe; for a genuine cap (DeltaSolv sat at 85% of its week on 2026-09-10, so one is plausible), the cap alert, and the switch — or the stand-down, if the identity was unknown at that moment. If no 429 arrives within the observation window, say so and give the window.
3. **The probe budget.** Reload `/settings/subscriptions` ten times inside one minute while tailing the backend log. Record that no usage-probe 429 followed and that the page's rows kept their readings across the reloads; state plainly that the count of Anthropic calls is not directly observable from the console (successful probes are not logged) and that the floor's one-per-account-per-minute guarantee rests on `test_subscriptions_probe_budget.py`, quoted by name and run id.

Write the record to `architecture/audits/2026-09-DRE-3606-stand-down-proof.md`, sources section last, and open the PR carrying it. The record is the deliverable; a green suite is not.

**Files:** architecture/audits/2026-09-DRE-3606-stand-down-proof.md

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `architecture/audits/2026-09-DRE-3606-stand-down-proof.md` exists on `main`, names the console version observed, and carries PT-stamped observations for all three items above, each marked observed live or explicitly not observed with the reason.
- [ ] Observation 1 was taken by hand against the production console: the identity episode is recorded with the alert, the hero line, and the switch log's `stood-down` line or the plain statement that no evidence arrived during the episode.
- [ ] Observation 2 quotes a real 429 body from the production backend log (token-free) and the classification the console gave it, or states the window in which none arrived.
- [ ] Observation 3 records ten reloads inside one minute on the live page with no 429 following, and names the test that carries the count guarantee.
- [ ] No token value, code or fingerprint of a live credential appears in the file.

**Blocked by:** DRE-3613, DRE-3614, DRE-3615, DRE-3616, DRE-3617, DRE-3618

cards.title: PROOF: the live routing map survives a broken AWS session and the completion tools reach EveryBite/atlas and DeltaSolv/deltasolv — observed by hand, recorded in architecture/audits
cards.description:
The three build cards change two operator tools and a test suite proves their logic. This card proves the MECHANISM against real state — the live relay routing map and the live GitHub repos of the two non-dreadnought orgs — and records what was observed, by hand, in the repo, in the shape `architecture/audits/2026-09-*-proof.md` already uses. A green test suite is not this card.

The operator runs three observations from a checkout of `main` that contains all three merged cards, and writes the transcript, the time of each reading in Pacific Time, and what it said into a new `architecture/audits/2026-09-onboarding-fail-closed-proof.md`:

1. **The routing map survives a broken AWS session.** Read the live map first: `AWS_PROFILE=dreadnought aws ssm get-parameter --name /bureau/relay/repo-map --region us-west-2 --query Parameter.Value --output text` — record the slug list and count. Then run `onboard-customer.py` for an ALREADY-ONBOARDED slug (idempotent; nothing new is created) with AWS credentials that cannot read SSM — e.g. `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=invalid AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=invalid AWS_PROFILE=` — and `--no-pipeline-pr`, so the only live surface the run can reach is SSM. Record that the run aborts at step 5 with the refusal quoting the AWS error, and re-read the map: identical slug list, identical count. Before DRE-3608 this exact run wrote a one-entry map over the live one.
2. **The shrink guard refuses by hand.** In a Python session against the merged module, call the write path with a map that drops one live key and the map just read as the current one; record the refusal text naming the dropped key. Do NOT pass `--force` against the live parameter.
3. **The completion tools reach both foreign orgs.** Pick one Done atlas card and one Done deltasolv card whose PR is merged (the board shows them; `gh pr list --repo EveryBite/atlas --state merged --limit 3` and the same for `DeltaSolv/deltasolv` name candidates). Run `bash scripts/complete-card.sh <card> --pr <n> --dry-run` for each with NO `--repo` and record that it resolves `EveryBite/atlas` / `DeltaSolv/deltasolv` and reports the real `mergedAt`. Run `python3 scripts/linear-api.py set-state <the same atlas card> Done --pr <n>` on a card that is ALREADY Done (a no-op transition) and record that the gate passes rather than refusing on a non-existent `dreadnought-foundry/atlas` PR. Before DRE-3609/DRE-3610 both commands refused.

The record also notes, in one line each, the two audit findings this epic found already closed on `main` and where: the printed secrets list carries `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` (DRE-2131; observed in the same dry-run output), and the GitHub-events relay resolves repos from the SSM map at cold start (`cloud/relay-gh/lambda_function.py`, DRE-1668). Neither is re-proven here beyond that reading.

**Files:** architecture/audits/2026-09-onboarding-fail-closed-proof.md

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Observation 1 was run by hand against the live `/bureau/relay/repo-map` parameter, and the record shows the slug list and count read before and after, identical, with both readings timestamped in PT.
- [ ] The record quotes the abort message from observation 1 and shows the run never reached a `put-parameter` call.
- [ ] Observation 2's refusal text, naming the key that would have been dropped, is in the record; no `--force` write was made against the live parameter.
- [ ] Observation 3 shows one atlas card and one deltasolv card resolving to `EveryBite/atlas` and `DeltaSolv/deltasolv` with a real `mergedAt`, from both `complete-card.sh --dry-run` and `linear-api.py set-state … --pr`, with no `--repo` passed.
- [ ] The record is merged to `main` at the named path, and names the three card ids it proves.

cards.title: complete-card.py finishes atlas and deltasolv cards — the repo comes from config/repo-map.json, not a hardcoded org, and the runbook example is corrected
cards.description:
`scripts/complete-card.py` (the one-command finish for a by-hand PR merge) resolves a card's repo as `DEFAULT_ORG + "/" + <repo:label slug>` in `_split_repo` — `DEFAULT_ORG = "dreadnought-foundry"` at the top of the file. For `atlas` (`EveryBite/atlas`) and `deltasolv` (`DeltaSolv/deltasolv`) that means the merge proof (`gh pr view --repo dreadnought-foundry/atlas`) queries a repo that does not exist and the tool refuses a genuinely merged PR unless the operator remembers `--repo`. The operator runbook's own example (`docs/operator-runbook.md`, the `DRE-920 --pr 42 --repo dreadnought-foundry/atlas` line) shows the wrong org for atlas.

Consume the resolver the sibling card declared in `scripts/linear-api.py` (this module already loads that file by path as `linear`):

1. `_split_repo` resolves a label-derived slug through `linear.repo_full_for_slug(slug)`. A resolved `owner/repo` is split and returned. A slug the map does not know exits 1 with a message naming the slug, `config/repo-map.json`, and the `--repo <owner/slug>` override — it never guesses `dreadnought-foundry/<slug>`. An explicit `--repo owner/slug` still wins outright, and a bare `--repo slug` (no slash) is also resolved through the map (so `--repo atlas` means `EveryBite/atlas`), refusing when unknown.
2. Delete `DEFAULT_ORG` and the "if not dreadnought-foundry/<repo-label>" hint in the `resolve_pr` error text; word the hint in terms of the routing map.
3. The PR-URL attachment path (owner and repo taken from the URL itself) and the branch-name path are unchanged apart from using the resolved repo.
4. Fix the runbook example to `--repo EveryBite/atlas` and add one line saying the org now comes from the routing map, so `--repo` is only needed for a repo the map does not carry.

Existing tests in `scripts/tests/test_complete_card.py` assert `("dreadnought-foundry", "agent-bureau", 42)` for a card labelled `repo:agent-bureau` — that stays true because the map carries `agent-bureau` → `dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau`; the test that infers a PR from an attachment URL `github.com/dreadnought-foundry/atlas/pull/77` is about URL parsing and its expectation is also unchanged (the URL is the source there). Add tests for the atlas/deltasolv resolutions and the unknown-slug refusal, pointing `linear.REPO_MAP_PATH` at a fixture where needed.

**Files:** scripts/complete-card.py, scripts/tests/test_complete_card.py, docs/operator-runbook.md

## Contract (declared by the sibling card in scripts/linear-api.py)

* `linear.repo_full_for_slug(slug: str) -> str | None`, exact-key lookup in `config/repo-map.json`, `None` for an unknown slug; `linear.REPO_MAP_PATH` is the module constant tests redirect.
* This card only CALLS it; it defines no second copy of the lookup.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `resolve_pr` for a card labelled `repo:atlas` with `--pr 7` and no `--repo` returns `("EveryBite", "atlas", 7)`; the same for `repo:deltasolv` returns `("DeltaSolv", "deltasolv", 7)`.
- [ ] `_split_repo` for a label slug absent from the map exits 1 before any `gh` call, and the message names the slug, the map path and the `--repo` override; `--repo Some/thing` bypasses the lookup.
- [ ] `--repo atlas` (no slash) resolves to `("EveryBite", "atlas")`; `--repo unknown` exits 1.
- [ ] `grep -n "DEFAULT_ORG\|dreadnought-foundry" scripts/complete-card.py` returns nothing.
- [ ] `docs/operator-runbook.md` shows `--repo EveryBite/atlas` in its example and states the org is read from the routing map.
- [ ] The existing suites `scripts/tests/test_complete_card.py` and `scripts/tests/test_operator_runner.py` still pass; the new tests fail against the current `_split_repo` (RED commit first).

The runbook line this card fixes sits in the `complete-card` section; the auto-switch epic DRE-3606 (DRE-3614, then DRE-3617) rewrites two bullets under "What fires auto-switch, and what it writes" in the same file, so this card waits on DRE-3617 to keep two open pull requests off one file.

**Blocked by:** DRE-3609, DRE-3617

cards.title: linear-api.py resolves a card's repo through config/repo-map.json — the merge gate stops hardcoding dreadnought-foundry and the dead msg.sh hint goes
cards.description:
`scripts/linear-api.py`'s merge gate (`_verify_pr_merged_for_done`, the `set-state Done --pr N` path) hardcodes the GitHub org: it takes the card's `repo:<slug>` label and runs `gh pr view N --repo dreadnought-foundry/<slug>`. But `config/repo-map.json` says `atlas` lives at `EveryBite/atlas` and `deltasolv` at `DeltaSolv/deltasolv`, so for those two roster repos the gate looks up a PR that does not exist and refuses a valid merged PR. The same file still tells the operator to "Use '[msg.sh](<http://msg.sh>) complete-card --pr N'" in two places (the gate's error text and the `--pr` argument help) — `msg.sh` was the retired v1 platform's entry point and no longer exists; the live command is `bash scripts/complete-card.sh`.

Declare the slug→repo resolution ONCE here, so the sibling card that fixes `complete-card.py` (which already loads this module by path as `linear`) reuses it instead of inventing its own:

1. Add `repo_full_for_slug(slug)` to `scripts/linear-api.py`. It reads `config/repo-map.json` from the repo root (`Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "config" / "repo-map.json"`, the same path `scripts/operator_runner.py` uses) and returns the `owner/repo` string for an exact key match, or `None` when the slug is not a key. It does not strip an `owner/` prefix — callers already reduce a legacy `repo:owner/slug` label to its last segment before asking. A missing or unreadable map file raises rather than returning a guess.
2. The merge gate calls it. With a `repo:` label whose slug resolves, `gh pr view` runs with `--repo <owner/repo>` from the map. With a slug the map does not know, the gate exits 2 with a message naming the slug, the map path and the valid slugs — it never falls back to guessing `dreadnought-foundry/<slug>`, because a guessed org is exactly the defect being removed. With no `repo:` label the pre-existing behaviour (no `--repo`, local checkout) is unchanged. The four error strings in that function that interpolate `dreadnought-foundry/{repo_slug}` use the resolved `owner/repo` instead.
3. Delete both `msg.sh complete-card` references; point the operator at `bash scripts/complete-card.sh <card> --pr N` instead.

Tests go in a new file under `scripts/tests/` (the toolkit CI job collects `scripts` with pytest; `scripts/tests/test_complete_card.py` shows how to load a hyphenated module by path and stub `subprocess.run`).

**Files:** scripts/linear-api.py, scripts/tests/test_linear_api_repo_for_slug.py

## Contract (shared with the sibling that fixes [complete-card.py](<http://complete-card.py>))

* Function: `repo_full_for_slug(slug: str) -> str | None`, defined in `scripts/linear-api.py`, module-level.
* Source of truth: `config/repo-map.json` at the repo root, read on each call (no import-time cache that a test cannot redirect); the map path is exposed as the module constant `REPO_MAP_PATH` so tests can point it at a fixture.
* `repo_full_for_slug("atlas") == "EveryBite/atlas"`; `repo_full_for_slug("nope") is None`; the input is used as an exact key.
* An unknown slug is a refusal at the CALL SITE (exit 2 in this file's gate), never a fallback to `dreadnought-foundry/<slug>`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `repo_full_for_slug("atlas")` returns `EveryBite/atlas` and `repo_full_for_slug("deltasolv")` returns `DeltaSolv/deltasolv` against the committed `config/repo-map.json`; `repo_full_for_slug("not-a-repo")` returns `None`.
- [ ] With `REPO_MAP_PATH` pointed at a fixture and `subprocess.run` stubbed, the merge gate for a card labelled `repo:atlas` invokes `gh pr view N --repo EveryBite/atlas` (asserted on the argv), and a merged PR on `main` passes the gate.
- [ ] The merge gate for a card labelled `repo:unknown-slug` exits 2 before calling `gh`, and the message names the slug, the map path and the valid slugs.
- [ ] A card with no `repo:` label still runs `gh pr view N` with no `--repo` (pre-existing behaviour pinned).
- [ ] `grep -n "msg.sh" scripts/linear-api.py` returns nothing; the replacement text names `scripts/complete-card.sh`.
- [ ] No test file, and no other script, is left referring to `msg.sh` in `scripts/` (verify with grep; only `archive/platform/` may).
- [ ] The RED commit (the new test file) precedes the first change to `scripts/linear-api.py` in the branch history; `ruff check scripts/ --ignore E501` is clean.

cards.title: onboard-customer.py fails closed on an unreadable SSM routing map and refuses to shrink a live one without --force
cards.description:
`scripts/onboard-customer.py` step 5 reads the relay's live routing map from SSM (`read_ssm_map`, the `aws ssm get-parameter` call), merges the new customer in (`merge_routing_entry`) and writes the result back with `--overwrite` (`write_ssm_map`). Today `read_ssm_map` returns `{}` on ANY non-zero exit — a throttle, an expired session, the wrong `AWS_PROFILE`, a network blip — and on malformed JSON. The caller cannot tell "the parameter does not exist yet" from "I could not read it", so on a transient failure it writes a map containing only the new customer over `/bureau/relay/repo-map`, un-routing the cards of all six routed repos (the map carries six slugs today) until a human notices Todo cards not moving. The same function serves step 5b for `/bureau/relay/org-tenant-map`, so the org→tenant map has the identical trap.

Make the read fail closed and the write refuse to shrink:

1. `read_ssm_map` distinguishes the one legitimate empty case from the failure modes. Only a `ParameterNotFound` error (the `aws` CLI reports it in stderr) means "not seeded yet" and returns `{}`. Any other non-zero exit aborts the run with `SystemExit` quoting the CLI's stderr and the parameter name — no write happens. A value that is not valid JSON, or parses to something other than a dict, also aborts (it is a corrupt live map, not an empty one). Structure it so the classification is a pure function over `(returncode, stderr, stdout)` that the tests drive directly without `aws` installed.
2. The write path refuses to shrink a non-empty live map. Before `write_ssm_map` puts a value, compare the keys of the map that was read with the keys of the map about to be written: if any key would disappear, abort with a message listing the dropped keys by name and the parameter, unless the new `--force` flag was passed. `--force` prints what it is overriding. `merge_routing_entry` never removes keys today, so this is the second lock on the same door — it protects against the next code path that builds a map some other way.
3. Both SSM parameters get the same two protections through the same functions (step 5 and step 5b both call them). Keep the `read_ssm_map(region, param=...)` / `write_ssm_map(new_map, region, param=...)` call shapes compatible with how `FailureSummaryExitTest` stubs them, adding keyword-only parameters if the write needs the read result.
4. `--dry-run` is unchanged: it still makes no network calls.
5. Update the step 4 row and the "re-run after a partial failure is safe" sentence in `docs/customer-onboarding-runbook.md` so the runbook says what the tool now does: an unreadable map aborts the run before any write, and a write that would drop a live entry is refused without `--force`.

**Files:** scripts/onboard-customer.py, scripts/test_onboard_customer.py, docs/customer-onboarding-runbook.md

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A stubbed `aws ssm get-parameter` exiting non-zero with `ParameterNotFound` in stderr returns `{}` from `read_ssm_map` and the run proceeds to seed the map (existing behaviour for a fresh parameter is preserved).
- [ ] A stubbed `aws ssm get-parameter` exiting non-zero with any other stderr (a throttle message, an expired-token message, an empty stderr) raises `SystemExit`, the message names the parameter and quotes the stderr, and `write_ssm_map` is never called — asserted for BOTH `/bureau/relay/repo-map` and `/bureau/relay/org-tenant-map`.
- [ ] A stubbed read returning a value that is not a JSON object (invalid JSON, a JSON list, a JSON string) raises `SystemExit` rather than returning `{}`.
- [ ] Writing a map whose keys are a strict subset of the keys just read raises `SystemExit` listing the dropped keys by name, and the `put-parameter` call is never made; the same write with `--force` proceeds and prints the keys it is dropping.
- [ ] Writing a map that only adds or changes keys proceeds exactly as before (the idempotent re-add path and `already present — skipping` output are unchanged).
- [ ] `--force` appears in `--help`, and `--dry-run` still makes no network calls (the existing dry-run tests stay green).
- [ ] The existing suites `scripts/test_onboard_customer.py` and `scripts/test_onboarding_runbook.py` still pass; the new tests fail against the current `read_ssm_map` / `write_ssm_map` (the RED commit is first in the branch history).
- [ ] `docs/customer-onboarding-runbook.md` §2 states the abort-before-write and the `--force` refusal in the step 4 row.

cards.title: A Reconnect or "Use this" that rewrites six repos shows no progress and locks nothing — the page must show the fan-out step by step and refuse every other action until it lands
cards.description:
**The CEO's words, 2026-09-11 18:12 PT, after reconnecting Dreadnought on the production console:** "if it takes this long there needs to be some progress indication and not to do anything while the swap out is happening."

**What he saw.** He pressed Reconnect, approved on [claude.ai](<http://claude.ai>), pasted the code, and the page gave no sign of what was happening for the tens of seconds the console spent minting the token and writing six repo secrets (18:07:24–18:07:28 PT per GitHub, plus the vault write and the identity re-read). Nothing on the page said "writing agent-bureau… atlas… portico…", nothing said it had finished, and every other control stayed live — "Use this" on another account could have been pressed mid-fan-out, which is the split-fleet shape [DRE-2614](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2614/the-console-revokes-the-credential-it-just-gave-the-fleet-the-rotation)'s harness exists to prevent. When the writes were done the hero still read "No active account" for minutes (its own defect, filed separately), so he could not tell success from failure.

## What to build

1. **A progress surface for any fleet rewrite** (Reconnect, "Use this", and the pool's own failover when a person is watching): a step list on the Subscriptions page — mint · vault · then one row per repo in `config/repo-map.json` order, each going pending → written (with the PT time and the fingerprint) or refused (with the console's own refusal sentence, e.g. "stored credential was rejected") — driven by the same receipts the switch log is written from, so the page shows what the log will say.
2. **A lock while it runs.** From the first write to the last, every other mutation on the page is disabled with the reason on the control ("a switch is in progress — 4 of 6 repos written"); a second Reconnect or "Use this" is refused server-side too, not only greyed out (the fan-out is not idempotent across accounts).
3. **A terminal state that says so**: "Switched to Dreadnought · 6 of 6 repos · 18:07:28 PT" (or "2 of 6 — could not rotate agent-bureau, …", the [DRE-2662](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2662/the-credential-fan-out-silently-reversed-a-failover-and-left-the-pools) morning's shape) stays on screen until dismissed, and the hero re-reads the identity verdict at that moment rather than waiting for the next monitor tick.

Design: the existing switch-log row grammar, extended with a live pending state; the tokens in console/design/. This is a UI change and goes through the design critic (DRE-3xxx product/designer rule).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] During a Reconnect or "Use this", the page shows per-repo progress in repo-map order with PT times and fingerprints, driven by the fan-out's receipts (vitest on the component with a replayed receipt stream; backend test that the receipts carry per-repo timing)
- [ ] While a fan-out is in flight, every other account mutation is disabled on the page AND refused by the backend with a plain-English reason (backend test: a second switch during a fan-out returns the refusal, writes nothing)
- [ ] The terminal state names the account, N of 6 repos, and the PT time, and the hero reflects the identity verdict immediately after the last write (test: hero text after a completed fan-out, with the usage probe stubbed to 429, still names the account)
- [ ] The [DRE-2614](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2614/the-console-revokes-the-credential-it-just-gave-the-fleet-the-rotation) harness case (never a split fleet) stays green

**Related:** [DRE-2662](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2662/the-credential-fan-out-silently-reversed-a-failover-and-left-the-pools) (the fan-out records what each repo holds), [DRE-2614](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2614/the-console-revokes-the-credential-it-just-gave-the-fleet-the-rotation) (split-fleet guard), [DRE-2660](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2660/a-chain-rotation-kills-the-consoles-own-stored-pool-credential-and) (dead stored credentials, seen the same evening), [DRE-3255](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3255/proof-auto-switch-observed-firing-on-the-live-console-a-429-switches) (the drive this came from).

cards.title: Auto-switch fired on a usage-probe 429 while the fleet's account was UNKNOWN, instead of standing down — and the 429 was the probe being rate-limited, not a cap
cards.description:
**Observed 2026-09-11 18:00–18:04 PT on production (console v1.6.43), during the** [DRE-3255](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3255/proof-auto-switch-observed-firing-on-the-live-console-a-429-switches) **identity drive, from the backend log:**

```
01:00:19Z WARNING console.cost_usage cost-usage probe for Dreadnought returned HTTP 429 — token may be expired or unauthorized
01:01:21Z (alert) system:claude_fleet_identity:agent-bureau-demo raised — token rotated outside the console; activeKnown=false, foreign=[agent-bureau-demo]
01:01:43Z WARNING console.claude_auto_switch auto-switch: StoredCredentialRejected refused the switch to VeriCorr
01:01:43Z WARNING console.claude_reconnect account switch refused for VeriCorr — VeriCorr's stored credential was rejected. Reconnect to mint a new one.
01:01:45Z WARNING console.claude_pool claude-pool: refusing to re-point <five repos> at VeriCorr — invalid credential; refusing to re-point atlas at EveryBite — invalid credential
01:03:54Z (the same pool refusals again)
01:04:21Z WARNING console.cost_usage cost-usage probe for Dreadnought returned HTTP 429
```

Two things are wrong here.

1. **It did not stand down.** [DRE-3182](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3182/auto-switch-executor-on-a-429-or-three-limit-deaths-in-fifteen-minutes) made auto-switch stand down on a 429 when the fleet's account is unknown (a repo rotated outside the console), with a result saying so; `claude_auto_switch.py:31` still says "the usage path is DISABLED and only the …" when a repo is foreign. Twenty-two seconds after the identity alert, with `activeKnown=false` persisted, it fired anyway and attempted a fleet-wide move to VeriCorr. Either the auto-switch reads a stale identity verdict, or the check is on a different key than the monitor writes (`fleet_identity.FLEET_IDENTITY_KEY`).
2. **The trigger was not a cap.** Dreadnought was at 1% of its 5-hour window and 32% of its week on the last good probe (~17:56 PT), and the fleet kept running on Dreadnought throughout — the [DRE-3606](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3606/auto-switch-fired-on-a-usage-probe-429-while-the-fleets-account-was)/[DRE-2660](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2660/a-chain-rotation-kills-the-consoles-own-stored-pool-credential-and) planner runs at 18:17–18:25 PT succeeded on that account. The 429 is specific to the PROBE's token for Dreadnought: it began at 18:00:19 PT and repeated every 240 s for at least 30 minutes while the other three accounts' probes answered normally. (Correction, 18:33 PT: this was first blamed on the operator's page reloads; it is not — `cost_usage` caches each probe for 300 s and the warmer runs every 240 s, so page loads never reach Anthropic.) The console rendered Dreadnought `Unavailable · usage unavailable (HTTP 429)` and auto-switch treated that as exhaustion. A probe token that cannot authenticate, a throttled probe, and a capped account are three different facts; only the last should move the fleet, and the probe logs neither body nor headers, so today they are indistinguishable.

Nothing moved tonight only because every stored fallback credential was dead ([DRE-2660](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2660/a-chain-rotation-kills-the-consoles-own-stored-pool-credential-and)), which is not a safety mechanism.

## What to build

* Auto-switch reads the persisted fleet-identity verdict at decision time and stands down when `activeKnown` is false, writing the stand-down result the [DRE-3182](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3182/auto-switch-executor-on-a-429-or-three-limit-deaths-in-fifteen-minutes) contract describes (visible on the Subscriptions page and in the switch log as a non-switch line), pinned by a test that replays tonight's ordering (identity alert at T, 429 at T+22s).
* The usage probe distinguishes "rate-limited" (HTTP 429 with a retry-after / on the usage endpoint) from "capped" (Anthropic's cap marker); only the cap marker, or a run receipt, is a switch trigger. A rate-limited probe reads `usage unavailable (rate-limited, retrying)` and moves nothing. Test with tonight's 429 body.
* The Subscriptions page's own polling backs off so an operator reading the page cannot rate-limit the probe (one probe per account per N minutes regardless of page loads).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With `activeKnown=false` persisted and a 429 arriving, auto-switch writes a stand-down result and attempts no switch (test on the replayed ordering; fails on main today)
- [ ] A usage-probe 429 that is a rate limit is classified as unavailable-transient and is not a switch trigger; a genuine cap still is (tests for both bodies)
- [ ] Reloading the Subscriptions page ten times in a minute produces at most one usage probe per account (test on the page's data loader or the backend cache)
- [ ] The stand-down result is visible on the page as the [DRE-3182](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3182/auto-switch-executor-on-a-429-or-three-limit-deaths-in-fifteen-minutes) contract specifies

**Related:** [DRE-3182](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3182/auto-switch-executor-on-a-429-or-three-limit-deaths-in-fifteen-minutes) (stand-down design), [DRE-3255](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3255/proof-auto-switch-observed-firing-on-the-live-console-a-429-switches) (the proof that saw this), [DRE-2660](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2660/a-chain-rotation-kills-the-consoles-own-stored-pool-credential-and) (the dead stored credentials that happened to catch it), [DRE-3170](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3170/claude-auto-switch-never-fires-it-watches-the-account-the-console-last) (the epic).
