cards.title: The Alerts feed keeps no history — a resolved alert cannot be read back, so a CRITICAL that clears itself minutes later (a failed release, a refused run) is unprovable after the fact
cards.description:
**Observed 2026-09-11 17:38 PT, in the CEO's signed-in production session (console v1.6.43), while closing** [DRE-3239](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3239/proof-the-release-train-observed-live-on-the-console-the-unattended)**.** The proof asked one question: did the real failed release of 2026-09-08 18:59 PT (run 34301370471) raise the CRITICAL `release_train:agent-bureau` alert on the Alerts feed? Nothing in the system can answer it now:

* The Alerts tab's **Resolved** view renders the sentence: *"Resolved alerts are not on this read — marking one done clears it from the queue for good."* Zero rows.
* `alertFeed(offset:0, limit:1000)` returns the 32 open alerts (oldest raised 2026-09-08 14:30 PT) and nothing else; no `release_train` row among them, though the train also refused at 07:11 PT today (run 34608674797 concluded failure, "a red commit is never released") and released green twenty minutes later.
* The production backend log group (`/aws/apprunner/bureau-console-backend/…/application`) for 2026-09-08 18:30–23:00 PT holds no line matching `release_train`, `alert` and `release`, `raised`, or `CRITICAL` — alert raises are not logged.

So an alert designed to fire on a failure and clear on the next success is exactly the alert nobody can prove ever fired: its whole life is shorter than the interval at which a person looks. The CEO reads the feed to decide whether something happened overnight; "it was there at 19:09 and gone by 19:32" is the reading he needs and cannot get.

## What to build

1. Resolved alerts are kept, with `raisedAt` and `resolvedAt`, and the Resolved view lists them (newest first, 30 days), with the same row shape as Open plus the resolution reason ("cleared by run 34301370471's successor", "marked done by Sid").
2. `alertFeed` grows a `state: OPEN | SNOOZED | RESOLVED | ALL` argument (default OPEN, so nothing today changes), and `resolvedAt` on `UnifiedAlert`.
3. Every alert raise and resolve writes one structured log line (`alert raised kind=… id=… urgency=…` / `alert resolved …`) so the backend log is a second reader when the table is not.
4. The [DRE-3239](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3239/proof-the-release-train-observed-live-on-the-console-the-unattended) record's rule 7 gets its answer from the first failed release after this ships, read from the Resolved view; until then the record says "unobservable by design, DRE-<this card>".

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A resolved alert is readable on the Resolved view and through `alertFeed(state: RESOLVED)` with `raisedAt` and `resolvedAt` (backend test on the feed; vitest on the view)
- [ ] Marking an alert done no longer deletes it; the "clears it from the queue for good" sentence is gone
- [ ] Raise and resolve each write one log line, pinned by a test that captures the logger
- [ ] Open-state behaviour, counts and the Needs You tile are unchanged (existing tests stay green)
- [ ] The next failed release's CRITICAL alert is read from the Resolved view and posted on [DRE-3239](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3239/proof-the-release-train-observed-live-on-the-console-the-unattended) with PT times

**Related:** [DRE-3239](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3239/proof-the-release-train-observed-live-on-the-console-the-unattended) (the proof that hit this), [DRE-3164](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3164/epic-the-release-train-one-reusable-train-in-bureau-pipeline-a-thin) (the release-train epic), [DRE-3392](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3392/one-river-the-needs-you-tile-says-what-waits-on-you-an-honest-number-a) (the Needs You tile), [DRE-3061](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3061/cut-over-to-one-river-swap-the-route-delete-the-old-dashboard-delete) (One River cutover).

cards.title: The console release row follows the NEWEST train run, so a hold run three minutes behind a release hides the release's verify/live stages and its version
cards.description:
**Observed live 2026-09-11 08:17–08:24 PT, during the** [DRE-3527](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3527/proof-a-hand-dispatched-console-release-read-end-to-end-off-the) **walk.** `release_rows()` (`console/backend/release_row.py`, read through `LiveGitHubReader` every 30 s from the operator's checkout at `e8aa0d2`) followed the hand-dispatched release run 34615231805 through `ci_green` (15:17:43Z), `cut` and `build` (15:18:05Z) and `roll_out` (15:19:21Z), version `agent-bureau-console-v1.6.41`, detail "the release train is cutting console". At 08:20:48 PT a second train run (34615560824, `workflow_run` for the CI of the next merge) was created; from that tick the row switched to it — `stage: cut · mark: unk · "the release job for console has not started"` — while run 34615231805 went on to roll out, verify and land (`released … as agent-bureau-console-v1.6.41 at f041b10`, 15:23:07Z; tag `deployed: 15:23:03Z`). The row never showed `verify` or `live` for the release, and after landing it read `ci_green · hold · held_by: spacing · version: null` (the second run's no-op). The same masking happened at 07:41–07:47 PT: two runs fired three seconds apart for v1.6.40, and the row settled on the second run's "console reads current" with no version.

So the two things a person most wants from the row — "did it land?" and "what version is live?" — are exactly what a following run erases. [DRE-3527](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3527/proof-a-hand-dispatched-console-release-read-end-to-end-off-the)'s acceptance criterion 1 (an answer at each of CI_GREEN, CUT, BUILD, ROLL_OUT, VERIFY, LIVE) is unreachable whenever any CI completes within the ~6 minutes a release takes, which is most of the time.

## What to build

The row should follow the newest run **that is releasing or has released**, not the newest run of any kind. A run whose decision is `no-op`/`hold` (current, spacing, window, held, ci-pending) must not displace a release run that is still in flight or that landed more recently than the hold was decided; the hold's own sentence can ride as a secondary line ("next release may be cut at 08:53 PT") beneath the landed release's `live · v1.6.41`. `version` on a hold row that follows a release carries the landed tag, never null.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With a release run in flight and a later no-op run created, `release_rows()` keeps serving the release run's stages through `verify` and `live` (a test drives the two-run fixture from this morning's run ids and times)
- [ ] After the release lands, the row reads `live` with `version` equal to the tag cut, and the later hold's sentence is served beside it, not instead of it
- [ ] A hold run with no release in flight still renders as today (`held_by` + the train's sentence)
- [ ] The bogus `${{ matrix.surface }}` row (already named in [DRE-3527](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3527/proof-a-hand-dispatched-console-release-read-end-to-end-off-the)'s record) is dropped from the served rows, or a separate card is filed for it and referenced here
- [ ] The parity test against bureau-pipeline@stable stays green

**Related:** [DRE-3527](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3527/proof-a-hand-dispatched-console-release-read-end-to-end-off-the) (the proof this blocked), [DRE-3336](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3336/epic-the-release-run-is-a-fact-the-console-can-read-release-acts-with) (the epic), [DRE-3524](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3524/console-release-rowpy-walks-the-inner-stages-off-the-deployment-record) (the record half of the row source).

cards.title: One River reads a PR with no card as "Stuck — needs you"; a bot/standards-sync or probe/ branch is automation or a probe, and its row must say so with the PR's own age
cards.description:
**Observed 2026-09-11 07:30 PT on the Pull Requests tab.** Two rows read `Stuck — needs you · blocked · age not served` with a dash where the card goes:

* agent-bureau [dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau#2460](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/review/chorestandards-re-sync-dreadnought-standards-plugin-from-bureau-f6a154df8103), branch `bot/standards-sync`, opened by `standards-sync.yml` ([DRE-1731](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-1731/auto-sync-the-dreadnought-standards-plugin-when-the-standards-source)) — the nightly plugin re-sync. By design it has no card: it is the machine keeping the generated `dreadnought-standards` plugin in step with canon. `merge-gate.yml` accepts `bot/standards-sync` explicitly. It was APPROVED by the critic and merges on its own.
* agent-bureau-demo #12, branch `probe/draft-held-3276` — a throwaway probe [DRE-3276](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3276/proof-a-live-draft-pr-with-a-red-check-reads-draft-held-a-proof) asked for; its disposal card is [DRE-3555](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3555/dispose-of-the-dre-3276-proof-probe-close-agent-bureau-demo-pr-12-and). Closed by the operator this morning.

The CEO's reading: "Why do we have PRs without cards associated with them? This can't happen." The row gave him no way to tell a legitimate machine PR from an orphan. The console derives the card from the branch name (`agent/DRE-<n>-…`, `repair/DRE-<n>-…`); anything else gets no card, no age, and the stuck rail.

## What to build

Classify the cardless PR by its branch prefix, from the same prefix list the gates use (`merge-gate.yml`: `agent/*|repair/*|dependabot/*|bot/standards-sync`), never a copied enumeration:

* `bot/*` and `dependabot/*` → kind **automation**: the row says which workflow opened it (from the PR body's first line or the branch), the age column carries the PR's own opened-at, the rail is the ordinary green/amber/red from its checks and verdict — never `Stuck — needs you` unless the critic has parked it.
* `probe/*` → kind **probe**: the row names the card in the PR title if one is there (`probe(DRE-3276)`), age from opened-at, and a quiet "throwaway — close after the proof" caption.
* any other prefix with no card → the existing **unowned** reading, which IS the "this can't happen" case: `unowned-branch-watchdog` already posts the notice; the row should carry that notice's text, so a human PR on a `fix/*` branch reads as the defect it is.

Design: the existing row grammar; no new component. The chip text and the age source are the change.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A PR on `bot/standards-sync` renders kind `automation`, names `standards-sync.yml`, shows its opened-at age, and never `Stuck — needs you` while its checks are green or pending (backend test on the row model + vitest on the row)
- [ ] A PR on `probe/…` renders kind `probe` with the card id from its title if present and the throwaway caption
- [ ] A PR on any other cardless prefix renders the unowned reading with the watchdog's own sentence
- [ ] The prefix list is read from the merge-gate stub's `case` line (or a shared config the stub also reads), pinned by a test that fails if the two ever differ
- [ ] The Needs You count excludes `automation` and `probe` rows

**Related:** [DRE-3411](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3411/a-card-parked-for-a-person-keeps-its-place-on-its-prs-row-an-orphan) (orphan cards keep their row), [DRE-1731](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-1731/auto-sync-the-dreadnought-standards-plugin-when-the-standards-source) (standards sync), [DRE-3555](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3555/dispose-of-the-dre-3276-proof-probe-close-agent-bureau-demo-pr-12-and) (the probe's disposal).

cards.title: apply_branch_protection.py's full PUT answers HTTP 500 from GitHub; write the required-check list through the PATCH endpoint, and drop the expired TDD grace window from the config
cards.description:
**Observed 2026-09-10 21:15 PT and again 2026-09-11 07:18 PT.** `python3 scripts/apply_branch_protection.py --repo dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau --apply` printed `FAILED — unexpected end of JSON input` both times. With `GH_DEBUG=api` the cause is GitHub's: `PUT /repos/dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau/branches/main/protection` answered `HTTP/2.0 500 Internal Server Error`**,** `Content-Length: 0`**, after 8.4 s** (request id `D1EA:7B5D4:1F2A7F:24CF5A:6AA40DAE`), with an org-admin token carrying `repo` + `admin:org`. The payload was the script's own read-modify-write body (all live settings carried across, only the checks list changed). The same change through the narrower endpoint succeeded at once:

```
PATCH /repos/dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau/branches/main/protection/required_status_checks
{"strict": false, "checks": [{"context": "Lint · Guards"}, {"context": "TDD commit discipline"}]}
→ HTTP/2.0 200 OK  (request id D262:1E9EB5:217601:27294C:6AA40DE7, 07:19 PT)
```

`check_branch_protection.py --strict` then read OK on both repos. Cost of the gap: the TDD check's grace window (`awaiting_operator_apply_until: 2026-09-10`) had expired at 17:00 PT on 09-10, the guard turned `Lint · Guards` red on every agent-bureau CI run, and because that is the one required check **nothing merged in agent-bureau for 14 hours** (PRs [dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau#2455](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/review/featdre-3404-the-console-reads-the-held-repos-and-writes-the-repo-7993bafccc53)–[dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau#2460](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/review/chorestandards-re-sync-dreadnought-standards-plugin-from-bureau-f6a154df8103) all critic-APPROVED and blocked; the red-main repair [dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau#2459](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/review/fixdre-3573-read-the-four-channel-codes-the-release-train-now-emits-4667a29ebf62) among them).

## What to build

1. In `apply_branch_protection.py`, write the required-check list with `PATCH …/protection/required_status_checks` (`strict` + `checks`) and `enforce_admins` with `POST/DELETE …/protection/enforce_admins`, instead of one full `PUT` — the script only ever changes those two things, and the narrow endpoints leave everything else untouched by construction rather than by carrying it across. Keep the plan output the same.
2. On any non-2xx, print the HTTP status and the `X-GitHub-Request-Id` header (send with `-i` or read `gh api --include`), never only gh's parse error.
3. `config/branch-protection.json`: drop `awaiting_operator_apply_until` from the `TDD commit discipline` entry (the guard asks for this now that it is live), keeping `declared`.
4. The guard, when a window expires unapplied, prints the apply command it already prints — and also names in one line that this failure blocks every PR in the repo because the job carrying it is the required check (so the next reader knows the blast radius from the log line).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `apply_branch_protection.py --apply` issues no full `PUT`; a test with a fake runner asserts the PATCH body `{"strict": …, "checks": […]}` and the enforce_admins call, and that a 500 reply prints the status and request id
- [ ] `config/branch-protection.json` has no `awaiting_operator_apply_until` on the TDD entry; `make check-protection` (and the CI guard) stays green
- [ ] The guard's expired-window message names the blast radius in one sentence
- [ ] `scripts/test_*branch_protection*` cover the new shape and pass; the existing expectation tests are unchanged

**Related:** [DRE-2554](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2554/step-5-bind-the-branch-protection-that-is-currently-advisory-and-make) (the guard), [DRE-3008](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3008/agent-bureau-does-not-run-the-tdd-commit-check-in-ci-the-only-enforcer) (the TDD check's declaration and window).

cards.title: PROOF: a hand-dispatched console release watched on the Activity tab end to end — the row appears, the bar walks every stage, the dot pulses during roll out, it reads live with the tag — recorded in the repo
cards.description:
The epic's own acceptance test, run by a person against real state and written down: one hand-dispatched console release watched on the Activity tab from dispatch to landing — the row appears within one refresh named `console · v1.6.NN`, the bar walks `CI green → cut → build → roll out → verify → live`, the dot pulses and the current segment sweeps during roll out and goes quiet between steps, and the row ends reading `live · v1.6.NN` with the same version the capacity strip and Shipped today show — with the observation recorded in the repo. A green suite is the tab proving itself off a fixture; this is the mechanism watched against a real release by someone other than the agents that built it (the DRE-3142 precedent, `architecture/audits/2026-09-browser-unknown-direction-guard-proof.md`, and the sibling epic's own proof, DRE-3527).

The tab has to be running the merged code while the release it watches is the one deploying that code, so the production console cannot be the watcher on the first pass. Two observations, both recorded: **(A)** during the first release after the last sibling merges, a frontend and backend started from `main` at the merged sha on the operator's machine (`make back` with `GH_TOKEN` from `scripts/github-bot-token.sh`, `make front`), reading the same live GitHub state production reads; dispatch by hand with `gh workflow run release-train.yml -f surface=console` on a `main` with an unreleased console change, or take the train's own run for that merge, and screenshot the Activity tab at each stage as the row moves (a screenshot per stage, PT-stamped, with the `data-liveness` / `data-journey-stage` / `data-journey-mark` attributes read off the row in the browser's inspector beside it). **(B)** once that release has landed, the production console's Activity tab at [app.agent-bureau.com](<http://app.agent-bureau.com>) carries the landed row (`live · v1.6.NN`) — screenshot it beside the capacity strip's running version and Shipped today; then watch ONE further console release end to end ON PRODUCTION, the same way as (A), when the next console change ships. Then read one no-op train (the next 07:00 PT scheduled run, or a hand dispatch inside the 30-minute spacing) and record the `hold` row and the rule it names. Do NOT provoke a failure or a rollback in production for this proof: the `fail` and `rolled back` rows are covered by the DEV fixture and the tests in the siblings, and the record says so. The four inner stages read `unk` until DRE-3520's grant is in place — that card is a blocker here for that reason, and if a stage still reads `unk` the record says which and why.

Write the record as one dated file: verbatim commands, PT times, the run id, the head sha, the tag cut, one screenshot per stage (committed under the same audits directory), the `deployLag` running version and the Shipped today version at the moment of the `live` reading, and the DRE-3527 record beside it where the two proofs watched the same run. Open it on a `proof/<this card's id>-release-row-on-the-tab` branch, not `agent/*`, so a person merges it and no gate auto-closes this card (the unowned-branch watchdog will post its notice; that is expected and the record says so). Close this card by hand with `linear_ops.py proof-observed` naming the file and the PT time.

**Files:** architecture/audits/2026-09-release-row-on-the-tab-proof.md, architecture/audits/2026-09-release-row-on-the-tab/ (the stage screenshots)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A real console release was watched by hand on the Activity tab from dispatch to landing (observation A on a `main` build, then observation B on the production console at [app.agent-bureau.com](<http://app.agent-bureau.com>)), and the record carries a PT-stamped screenshot of the row at each of `CI green`, `cut`, `build`, `roll out`, `verify` and `live`, with the row's `data-liveness`, `data-journey-stage` and `data-journey-mark` read off the live DOM beside each; the row appeared within one refresh of the dispatch.
- [ ] During roll out the dot was pulsing and exactly one segment was sweeping (`data-live` present), and between steps the row was quiet — both stated in the record with the times; no stage read `unk` once DRE-3520's grant was in place, and if one did the record names it and why.
- [ ] The final row read `live · v1.6.NN` with the version equal to the tag the run cut, and the record shows the same version on the capacity strip's running version and under Shipped today at that moment, in one screenshot.
- [ ] One no-op train was observed live on the tab and its row read `CI green · held by <rule>` with the rule the train printed (`current`, `spacing`, `window`, `held` or `ci-pending`) and the train's own sentence beneath, and the row did not move.
- [ ] The record is merged to `main` at `architecture/audits/2026-09-release-row-on-the-tab-proof.md` from a `proof/` branch by a person, and this card was closed by hand with a `proof-observed` line naming the file and the PT time.

**Blocked by:** DRE-3593, DRE-3594, DRE-3595, DRE-3596, DRE-3597, DRE-3520

cards.title: console: the release row on the Activity tab — releaseRuns read beside the feed, the row's dot and sweep off deriveLiveness over the current stage, the release JourneyBar, hold/fail/live/rolled back rendered as the backend marked them
cards.description:
**Design:** console/design/images/screens/desktop/dashboard-one-river-activity.png

A release is the most consequential thing the pipeline does and it is invisible on the console while it happens. The read exists (`query ReleaseRuns`, DRE-3593), the derivations exist (`releaseJourneyOf` / `releaseJourneyLabel` / `releaseHalfFrom` in `journey.ts` and `releaseWorkStateOf` / `releaseToneOf` in `workState.ts`, DRE-3594), the model holds the union and the pill (`activityModel.ts`, DRE-3596) and the design draws the row (DRE-3595). This card mounts it: `ActivityTab.tsx` reads `releaseRuns` beside `activityFeed`, merges the two through the model, and renders a release row in the Activity table's eight cells — the liveness dot and the `Release` chip in the Event cell, the project name, `—` for Card and PR, the title `console · v1.6.35` over a six-segment `JourneyBar` whose hue changes where the backend said and whose label is `releaseJourneyLabel`, the train's own sentence beneath, `release train` in By, the run's duration in Cycle once landed, and the current stage's timestamp in When. Composed from the shared pieces only — `ToneDot`, `JourneyBar`, the existing chip markup — NO new atom, NO new molecule, and nothing decided here that the two derivation modules did not return (`RiverRow.decisions.test.tsx` and `atomic.guard.test.ts` scan this file).

The dot and the sweep are ONE verdict, exactly as on `RiverRow`: `deriveLiveness({ state: releaseWorkStateOf(run), at: current.lastActAt, cadenceMs: current.cadenceMs }, now)` where `current` is the stage whose `name === run.stage`; the pair travels together off that one stage and is never assembled from two. The verdict rides the dot as `pulse={liveness.pulse}` (tone from `releaseToneOf`) and reaches the bar whole as `liveness={liveness}` so only the `now` segment sweeps, and only inside its cadence (`liveness.guard.test.ts` accepts nothing else). A stage with no act renders `unknown` — no pulse, no overdue, the same amber `unknown` a card row shows — because the backend served null and the frontend does not default it. A row with an `outcome` is finished: no pulse whatever its newest act says, tone green for `LIVE`, red for `ROLLED_BACK` / `FAILED`, bar complete for `LIVE`, marked `fail` at `live` for a rollback and marked `fail` at the stage it died on for `FAILED` (label `stopped at <stage>`), exactly as the backend marked it. A `HOLD` row is quiet and amber, and the rule that held it is in the label (`CI green · held by current`) and the sentence beneath.

The epic's own acceptance criterion — *a* `fail` *row stays on the tab* — is proven HERE, mounted, and not only in the pure-function tests of DRE-3594 (the second plan critic, 2026-09-11). Two `fail` rows exist and both are exercised: the rollback (`fail` at `live`, `outcome: ROLLED_BACK`) and the stopped run (`fail` at `build`, `outcome: FAILED`, the DEV fixture's sixth row). Nothing in this file, and nothing in the model it calls, drops a row because it failed: a stopped release is filtered by window and by pill exactly like every other row, counts in the `Releases` pill and the tab badge, and renders red and quiet with its stage and sentence — the CEO sees where it died, on the same tab, with the same filters.

The read follows the feed's: `useLiveQuery(ReleaseRunsDocument, { variables: { repo: null } })`, project filter applied client-side over rows already in hand. Honesty for the second read (`standards/console-honesty.md` rule 2): while `releaseRuns` has not answered, the feed renders as today with NO release rows and the coverage line gains `Releases could not be read — the release rows are missing, not absent.` only once that read has failed (`connectionState` provisional), never during the first load; a `releaseRuns` answer that is empty adds no line — an empty list is a fact. The `total` handed to the strip badge counts both kinds of row in the window. Row ids for the release rows are `release:<repo>:<surface ?? 'unread'>:<runId ?? ''>` through the existing `rowIds` uniqueness rule. The row is a `<tr>` with `data-kind="RELEASE"`, `data-testid="activity-row-<id>"`, `data-journey-stage`, `data-journey-mark`, and the dot carries `data-testid="activity-release-dot"`, `data-liveness`, `data-pulse`; the bar keeps `JourneyBar`'s own test ids. Extend `ActivityTab.test.tsx` in its own style (the mocked `request` answering both documents in turn) and add `ActivityTab.release.decisions.test.tsx` beside `ActivityTab.decisions.test.tsx` — later cards add their own decisions file, never edit the first.

**Files:** console/web/src/components/oneriver/ActivityTab.tsx, console/web/src/components/oneriver/ActivityTab.test.tsx, console/web/src/components/oneriver/ActivityTab.release.decisions.test.tsx

## Contract (imported, not declared here)

* From DRE-3593: `ReleaseRunsDocument`, `ReleaseRunsQuery`. From DRE-3596: `ActivityRow`, `ReleaseRow`, `isRelease`, `RELEASE_KIND`, `releaseRows`, `rowAt`, `rowKind`, `rowChip`, `releaseTitle`, `releaseCycleMinutes`, the generic `filterEvents` / `kindCounts` / `projectCounts` / `projectPalette` / `activityTotal` / `sortEvents` / `dayGroups` over `ActivityRow`, `SOURCE_LABELS.releases`. From DRE-3594: `releaseJourneyOf`, `releaseHalfFrom`, `releaseStageLabels`, `releaseJourneyLabel`, `RELEASE_HALF_NAMES`, `releaseWorkStateOf`, `releaseToneOf`. From the atoms: `ToneDot`, `deriveLiveness`; from the molecules: `JourneyBar` (`halfNames={RELEASE_HALF_NAMES}`).
* The words on screen are DRE-3595's: chip `Release`, pill `Releases`, By `release train` (`—` on the unreadable row), title and bar labels as the model and the journey return them.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With the mocked `releaseRuns` answering the six DEV-fixture rows and the feed its usual events, the table renders six `data-kind="RELEASE"` rows interleaved by time with the events, the six rows carrying the dot, the `Release` chip, the project name, `—` in Card and PR, the title from `releaseTitle`, a `JourneyBar` of six segments and the label from `releaseJourneyLabel`; the `Releases` pill shows 6 and clicking it leaves exactly those rows; the tab badge total counts them.
- [ ] The in-flight row (ROLL_OUT / NOW, `lastActAt` two minutes ago, `cadenceMs` 600000) renders `data-liveness="moving"`, a pulsing dot and exactly one `journey-segment` with `data-live`, and that segment carries `data-half="live"`; the same row with `lastActAt` twelve minutes ago renders `data-liveness="overdue"`, a red dot and no sweep; with `cadenceMs: null` it renders `data-liveness="unknown"` and no motion — the three from one fixture row and `now`, nothing else changed.
- [ ] The held row renders an amber, non-pulsing dot, `data-journey-mark="hold"`, the label `CI green · held by current` and the train's sentence beneath; the landed row renders a green dot, six `done` segments and `live · v1.6.34`; the rolled-back row renders a red dot, `data-journey-mark="fail"` at stage 5 and `rolled back · v1.6.32`; the unreadable row renders a neutral dot, `stage unknown`, `release · not read` and `—` in By — and none of these four moves.
- [ ] The stopped row (BUILD / FAIL, `outcome: FAILED`) renders a red, non-pulsing dot with no sweep whatever its `lastActAt` says (a finished run is never `moving` or `overdue`), `data-journey-stage="2"`, `data-journey-mark="fail"`, the label `stopped at build`, the sentence `the release of console failed at build` beneath, `console · v1.6.31` as its title and its run's duration in Cycle (the run concluded, so both instants are served and `releaseCycleMinutes` returns them); it is present under the default window, present and counted when the `Releases` pill is clicked, and absent under `24h` only because of its age — a test asserts that the same row dated one hour ago is present under `24h` too, so the row is filtered by time and never by its mark.
- [ ] The segments before the hue-change index carry `data-half="machine"` and the ones from it `data-half="live"`, read from the row's `hueChangesAt` (a fixture row with `hueChangesAt: CUT` moves the boundary) — no constant in this file names the stage.
- [ ] With `releaseRuns` failing after a first answer, the coverage line names Releases and the last release rows stay; with `releaseRuns` never answering, the feed renders as before with no release rows and no notice; an empty `releaseRuns` answer renders no rows and no notice.
- [ ] `ActivityTab.release.decisions.test.tsx` scans this file's code (comments stripped) and fails on any literal of `animate-pulse`, any numeric cadence, any of the six stage words, any of the five work-state words, and any literal of the three `ReleaseOutcome` names or the four `ReleaseMark` names (the file renders what `releaseJourneyOf`, `releaseWorkStateOf` and `releaseToneOf` returned and decides nothing off a mark or an outcome itself); `RiverRow.decisions.test.tsx`, `atomic.guard.test.ts`, `liveness.guard.test.ts`, `tableRoles.decisions.test.tsx` and the existing `ActivityTab` tests pass; `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` green; the RED test commit lands first and the TDD commit-order check exits 0.
- [ ] The critic's visual check of the Activity route against the re-exported `dashboard-one-river-activity.png` ran (no `Visual check did not run` line on the verdict) and the verdict is APPROVE.

**Blocked by:** DRE-3594, DRE-3596, DRE-3595

cards.title: console: activityModel.ts learns the release row — one ActivityRow union, the Releases pill, and a release filtered, counted, sorted and day-grouped by the same rules as a card row
cards.description:
`activityModel.ts` is the pure model behind the Activity tab — which rows a pill yields, how a header sorts, where a day breaks and what a chip says are decided there over `ActivityEvent[]`, and the tab renders what it returns. A release run is not an `ActivityEvent` (the feed's four kinds are the backend's `ActivityFeedKind`, and a release is served by `releaseRuns`, DRE-3525), so no function in the model can hold one. This card teaches the model a second row type and generalises its rules over the union, so a release row is filtered, counted, sorted and day-grouped by exactly the code a card row is — one grammar, no second list under the table. No React: the tab (a sibling card) mounts what this returns.

Two constraints shape the change. First, `ActivityTab.tsx` is a sibling's file and is NOT edited here, so it must keep compiling and behaving as it does today: `ActivityRow` is the union `ActivityEvent | ReleaseRow`, a bare event IS a row, and the list functions become generic over `R extends ActivityRow` (`filterEvents<R>(rows: readonly R[], …): R[]`, `sortEvents<R>`, `dayGroups<R>` returning `ActivityDayGroup<R>`, `kindCounts`, `projectCounts`, `projectPalette`, `activityTotal` over `readonly ActivityRow[]`) — the tab's `ActivityEvent[]` calls typecheck unchanged and return `ActivityEvent[]`, and the existing test file keeps passing without an edit to any existing case. Keep `eventChip`, `cardCell`, `formatCycle`, `formatWhen`, `unreadNotice`, `projectLabel` as they are. Second, nothing is re-derived: the release row's `at` is a served timestamp (the current stage's `lastActAt`, else the run's `completedAt`, else `startedAt`), never the poll's `readAt` and never now; its cycle is the run's own two instants; its version label is the tag's trailing version and nothing more. And nothing here reads a row's `mark` or `outcome` to decide whether it is shown: a failed release is kept, dropped and grouped by its time exactly as a landed one is.

**Files:** console/web/src/components/oneriver/activityModel.ts, console/web/src/components/oneriver/activityModel.test.ts

## Contract (imported by the row card; the pill and chip words are the design card's)

```ts
export type ReleaseRunRow = ReleaseRunsQuery['releaseRuns'][number]
export interface ReleaseRow { row: 'release'; run: ReleaseRunRow }
export type ActivityRow = ActivityEvent | ReleaseRow
export function isRelease(row: ActivityRow): row is ReleaseRow   // 'row' in it
export const RELEASE_KIND = 'RELEASE' as const
export type KindFilter = 'ALL' | ActivityFeedKind | typeof RELEASE_KIND
/** All · Shipped · Releases · Escalations · Plans · Runs */
export const KIND_PILLS: readonly KindPill[]            // gains { key: RELEASE_KIND, label: 'Releases' } after Shipped
export function releaseRows(runs: readonly ReleaseRunRow[], window: ActivityWindow, now?: number): ReleaseRow[]
export function rowAt(row: ActivityRow): string | null   // event.at; release: releaseRowAt(run)
export function releaseRowAt(run: ReleaseRunRow): string | null
export function rowRepo(row: ActivityRow): string
export function rowKind(row: ActivityRow): KindFilter    // event.kind, or RELEASE_KIND
export function releaseTitle(run: ReleaseRunRow): string
export function releaseVersionLabel(version: string | null | undefined): string | null
export function releaseCycleMinutes(run: ReleaseRunRow): number | null
export const RELEASE_CHIP: EventChip                     // { key: 'release', label: 'Release', glyph: '⇧', className: GREEN }
export function rowChip(row: ActivityRow): EventChip     // eventChip(event) or RELEASE_CHIP
export const SOURCE_LABELS                               // gains releases: 'Releases'
```

* `releaseRows`: keeps a run whose `releaseRowAt` falls inside `window` (24h · 7d · 30d back from `now`) AND a run whose `releaseRowAt` is null (an unreadable row is shown, grouped under the unknown-time header — a repo we could not read is never an absent row). It never reads `mark` or `outcome`.
* `releaseRowAt`: the stage whose `name === run.stage` → its `lastActAt`; else `run.completedAt`; else `run.startedAt`; else null. Never `readAt`.
* `releaseVersionLabel`: the tag's trailing `v<digits>[.<digits>]*` (`agent-bureau-console-v1.6.35` → `v1.6.35`); a tag with no such suffix → the tag verbatim; null → null.
* `releaseTitle`: `surface` null → `release · not read`; version label null → `<surface>`; else `<surface> · <vN.N.N>`.
* `releaseCycleMinutes`: whole minutes from `startedAt` to `completedAt` when both parse, else null.
* `kindCounts` counts `RELEASE_KIND`; `sortEvents` keys a release row as: event → `RELEASE_CHIP.label`, project → `projectLabel(run.repo)`, card → null, pr → null, cycle → `releaseCycleMinutes`, when → `releaseRowAt`; the tiebreak stays newest-first and a null key still sorts last both ways; `dayGroups` reads `rowAt`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `releaseRows` over the DEV fixture's six rows and a 7d window keeps the in-flight, held, landed, rolled-back and stopped rows, drops the two-day-old rolled-back row and the five-day-old stopped row under `24h` and keeps both under `7d`, and ALWAYS keeps the `UNK` row with `rowAt` null; a test asserts `readAt` is never read as a time (a row whose only timestamp is `readAt` has `rowAt` null); a test asserts the stopped row (`mark: FAIL`, `outcome: FAILED`) dated one hour ago is kept under `24h`, so a failed release is kept or dropped by its time and never by its mark.
- [ ] `releaseRowAt` prefers the current stage's `lastActAt`, then `completedAt`, then `startedAt`, and a test proves the order with three rows.
- [ ] `releaseTitle` reads `console · v1.6.35`, `console` (version null) and `release · not read` (surface null); `releaseVersionLabel('agent-bureau-console-v1.6.35') === 'v1.6.35'` and a tag with no version suffix comes back verbatim.
- [ ] `kindCounts` over mixed rows counts `RELEASE` and `ALL` correctly and the `Releases` pill sits after `Shipped` in `KIND_PILLS`; `filterEvents` with `kind: RELEASE_KIND` yields only release rows and the project filter applies to them by `run.repo`.
- [ ] `sortEvents` under `when` interleaves release and event rows by their instants newest-first, and under `cycle` a release row's `releaseCycleMinutes` sorts against events' `cycleMinutes` with nulls last; `dayGroups` places a release row in the PT day of its `rowAt` and the `UNK` row under the unknown-time group.
- [ ] The existing `activityModel.test.ts` cases pass without an edit; `ActivityTab.tsx` and its tests are untouched and `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` are green in `console/web`; the RED test commit lands first and the TDD commit-order check exits 0.

**Blocked by:** DRE-3593
