cards.title: [EPIC] Role routing — 14 agent:* labels route nowhere, there is no agent:database label, and two of the three roles the CEO named cannot be addressed
cards.description:
**Repo:** agent-bureau

**Blocked by:** DRE-3586

The CEO asked for **role-specific daily plans** — one for UI, one for front-end, one for database — as part of the 06:30 review cycle. We cannot build them, because a role label does not route to anything. This epic decides whether to make roles real. **It is a placeholder: the CEO green-lights it or declines it; nothing here is costed or scheduled yet.**

## What is actually true today

* `config/linear-workspace.json` records **14** `agent:*` **labels as "NOT READ BY ANYTHING"**. Three route: `agent:planner`, `agent:devops`, `agent:frontend`. The rest are decoration.
* **There is no** `agent:database` **label at all** — one of the three roles the CEO named cannot be expressed, let alone routed.
* `docs/product/roles.md` (2026-09-07) records the **DESIGNER and DESIGN-CRITIC roles as "Not built"**. Today's visual QA is a stage inside the one QA-critic pass, not a role.

So "a daily plan per role" is not a rendering problem. Two of the three named roles have nowhere to be routed to.

## What this epic would cover, if green-lit

1. Decide which roles are real — the list, and what each one owns.
2. Make the label set match that list: retire the labels nothing reads, add the ones that are missing, and say in `linear-workspace.json` what each routes to.
3. Route them: `agent-task.yml` and `agents.yaml` pick the brief from the label.
4. Then, and only then, a per-role daily plan is a filter over a list that already exists.

## Acceptance criteria (for the decision, not the build)

- [ ] The CEO answers: build role routing, or drop role-specific daily plans from the 06:30 ask.
- [ ] If built, the epic is planned properly and this placeholder is replaced by its children — it is **not** built from this text.

## Not in this epic

* The 06:30 cron and the daily plan email — both ship without roles; the plan is one list for everyone until this lands.

## Size

XL, uncosted. No `size:` label: the planning-shape check refuses an epic that wears one.

**Files:** `config/linear-workspace.json`, `bureau-pipeline/.github/workflows/agent-task.yml`, `bureau-pipeline/agents.yaml`, `docs/product/roles.md`

cards.title: The Intake age-out has ONE owning sweep — one key in lane-contract.json, and every other sweep prints the owner and returns
cards.description:
**Repo:** bureau-pipeline

## What happened

**130+ cards aged out of Intake into Green Light overnight on 2026-09-09/10**, and the CEO's queue was unreadable in the morning. `escalate_aged_intake` has **no repo filter, by design** — so every repo that runs a reconcile stub ages out the same production board, and each one is separately allowed its cap of 3 per pass. N repos × 3 every 15 minutes is not a cap, it is a multiplier.

Editing the sandbox stubs stops it today. This is the narrowest true version of the durable fix — and a better one than a stub input someone has to remember to pass, because a new repo gets it for free.

## What to build

The board declares **one owning sweep** for its age-out: a single key in `config/lane-contract.json`. `escalate_aged_intake` runs only when the sweep's `REPO` matches that owner. Every other sweep **prints the owner and returns** — a stated refusal, not a silent skip, so the next person reading a log knows why nothing was escalated.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `config/lane-contract.json` declares the age-out owner for the board, with a comment saying why one owner exists.
- [ ] A sweep whose `REPO` is not the owner performs no escalation and prints one line naming the owner.
- [ ] The owning sweep's escalation behaviour and its cap are unchanged — pinned by the existing tests.
- [ ] The cap is now the board's cap, not per repo: a pass across every repo escalates at most 3 cards in total.
- [ ] PROOF: one overnight with at most 3 cards per 15 minutes entering Green Light, from the sweep logs, posted here with PT times.

## Not in this card

* The same-day stub edit (dated `intake_hold`, schedule removed) and the key-level guard `may_escalate` — the three are deliberate layers. **Sequence: stub edit, then this, then** `may_escalate`**.**

## Collision rule

`reconcile.py` belongs to the sweep-cost card this wave. Land the owner check in `intake_controls` / `lane-contract` and keep the call site in `reconcile.py` to three lines or fewer.

**Files:** `bureau-pipeline/config/lane-contract.json`, `bureau-pipeline/scripts/reconcile.py` (call site only), `bureau-pipeline/scripts/intake_controls.py`, `bureau-pipeline/tests/test_intake_escalation.py`

cards.title: The pen switch says the act and its consequence — "Open the pen — releases 41 cards", never a bare Open or Close
cards.description:
**Repo:** agent-bureau

**Design:** console/design/images/screens/desktop/dashboard-one-river-green-light.png

## What happened

The Intake pen's switch is labelled with a bare verb, and **the verb is the opposite of the state** — a closed pen shows "Open". Twice the pen has been opened by accident, and an accidental opening releases every card behind it into the CEO's queue at once. The switch says what it will do to itself; it says nothing about what happens to the board.

## What to build

The switch says the act **and its consequence**, with the number in it:

* `Open the pen — releases 41 cards`
* `Close the pen — holds 41; the drain and the age-out both stop`

The count is the live one. No bare **Open** / **Close** anywhere on the control.

The footprint is five files, and one of them is a pin: `scripts/test_one_river_design.py:1104–1114` asserts `penVerb` equals `'Open'` / `'Close'` against the design HTML. **Amend the design HTML and the pin together** — the test exists so the console and the design cannot drift, and changing only one of them is the failure it was written to catch.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both labels read as the act plus its consequence, with the live card count in the sentence.
- [ ] No bare `Open` or `Close` remains on the control — asserted by a test.
- [ ] The design HTML and `test_one_river_design.py`'s `penVerb` pin are amended in the same commit and the design test is green.
- [ ] With zero cards behind the pen the sentence still reads correctly (no "releases 0 cards" awkwardness) — pinned by a test.
- [ ] PROOF: a screenshot of both states posted here with the PT time it was taken.

## Not in this card

* The pen's behaviour — it is already a readable, switchable fact (DRE-3369, DRE-3372).

## Collision rule

`CapacityStrip.tsx` is shared with the operator-rail card and with DRE-3549. **Sequence, never concurrent.**

**Files:** `console/web/src/lib/capacityModel.ts`, `console/web/src/components/oneriver/CapacityStrip.tsx`, `console/design/…` (the One River design HTML), `scripts/test_one_river_design.py`, `console/web/src/components/oneriver/CapacityStrip.test.tsx`

cards.title: The 06:30 plan reaches the CEO as an email he can act on — the groom proposal rendered in full, with links that focus the row and never mutate
cards.description:
**Repo:** agent-bureau

**Blocked by:** DRE-3586, DRE-3380, DRE-2535

**Design:** console/design/images/screens/desktop/dashboard-one-river-green-light.png

## What happened

The CEO's ask, from the 2026-09-10 walk: at **06:30 PT an email lists the day's proposed tasks**; he approves, strikes or modifies; the finalised plan goes to the fleet. The proposal itself exists and is green-lit. What does not exist is the email that carries it.

**What is already built, and must be amended rather than duplicated:** DRE-3375 (Done) raises the `groom_proposal` alert — CRITICAL, category `NEEDS_APPROVAL`, de-duplicated per proposal id — and calls `delivery.deliver`. What it sends is an alert title. What is missing is the plan itself in the body, links that work, the pen state, and a transport that leaves the box: `delivery.py:111` returns below CRITICAL and `ALERT_SMTP_HOST` has never been set in production (DRE-2535). Every CRITICAL the console has ever raised has been panel-only.

## What to build

Render and deliver the existing `groom_proposal` alert kind (`alerts_v2.py:480/578/595`) on DRE-2535's transport:

* **A header** — the proposal id, the cycle, how many cards, and what it is asking for.
* **The batch in order, each card with the groomer's reason.**
* **The left-outs**, and why each was left out.
* **The collisions** the groomer found.
* **The pen state.** An `INTAKE_HOLD` makes the proposal undrainable — an email that does not say so is asking for an approval that cannot land.
* **Every link is** `/green-light?proposal=<id>` — the tab's deep-linkable child route, behind `RequireAuth` with `?redirect` — which **focuses the row and never fires a mutation**. No signed one-time URL, ever: the drain refuses any marker not authored in the CEO's own identity (DRE-2721), and a signed link would be a way to approve as the CEO without the CEO. Pin that with a test.
* **One email per proposal id**, not one per send.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The email body carries the header, the ordered batch with reasons, the left-outs, the collisions and the pen state, from one render of the proposal — asserted against a fixture proposal.
- [ ] Every link in the email is `/green-light?proposal=<id>`; a test fails the build on any URL carrying a signature, token or mutation.
- [ ] Opening a link focuses the proposal row and fires no mutation.
- [ ] A held pen renders as a stated line in the email, naming the date it closed and the cards behind it.
- [ ] One proposal id yields exactly one email however many times the monitor runs.
- [ ] PROOF: the 06:30 PT proposal arrives by email **two mornings running** with working links, recorded here with PT times and the message ids.

## Not in this card

* The transport itself — DRE-2535 owns `delivery.py`'s sending; this card renders only.
* The four buttons the links point at — DRE-3380.
* The cron that makes 06:30 happen — the groomer-cron card.

## Collision rule

`delivery.py`: DRE-2535 owns transport, this card owns render. `GreenLightTab.tsx`: this card lands **after** DRE-3380.

**Files:** `console/backend/alerts_v2.py`, `console/backend/delivery.py` (render only), `console/backend/tests/test_groom_proposal_email.py`, `console/web/src/components/oneriver/GreenLightTab.tsx`

cards.title: "Needs the operator" is not "needs you" — WhoNext gains operator, needsYou() is false for it, and operator work gets its own amber rail
cards.description:
**Repo:** agent-bureau

## What happened

The console has one "needs you", and the CEO is the only "you" it knows. Every operator park lights his red rail. On 2026-09-10 the board read Green Light 6, Triage 3, Intake 250+, and the rail was showing a two-hour operator park as **"32.1h in Triage — Stuck, needs you"**. Three operator cards had been closed Done from the console with nothing done. None of that is a decision the CEO can make, and all of it is in the queue that is supposed to hold only decisions.

The console already knows the difference elsewhere: `alerts_v2.AlertAudience.OPERATOR` reads the very signals this needs — the `no-code` label, an `[OPERATOR]` title, `hand-built`, a park with no give-up receipt. The in-flight tree just does not use them.

**This replaces the lane half of DRE-3412.** That half is declined — the lane it proposes is the one DRE-2723 and DRE-3411 already settled — and its second half (an "answered blocker" read against the verdict it answers, not a bot receipt posted six seconds later) is re-scoped into area 2. DRE-3412 itself is the CEO's to close; nothing here touches it.

## What to build

`WhoNext` gains a third value, `operator`. `inflight.who_next()` derives it from the signals `AlertAudience.OPERATOR` already uses — `no-code`, an `[OPERATOR]` title, `hand-built`, and a park carrying no give-up receipt. `needsYou()` is **false** for `operator`. The operator's work gets an **amber rail** of its own and its own bucket on the ribbon, so it is visible and counted without being in the CEO's queue.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `who_next()` returns `operator` for each of the four signals, individually, pinned by a test per signal.
- [ ] `needsYou()` is false for `operator`; the red rail and the Needs-you count exclude it.
- [ ] The amber operator rail renders the same rows the red rail used to show for operator work, with its own count; nothing is dropped from the board.
- [ ] A card that is genuinely the CEO's decision (a plan awaiting go, a park with a question) still reads `you` and still lights red.
- [ ] PROOF: one morning where Green Light holds only CEO decisions and every operator item is on the amber rail, with the counts from both rails posted here with PT times.

## Not in this card

* Operator cards closing Done from the console with no record — DRE-3545, same family, separate card.
* The draft-PR misread — DRE-3554.

## Collision rule

`CapacityStrip.tsx`, `Ribbon.tsx` and `workState.ts` are shared with the pen-switch card and with DRE-3549's error boundary. **Sequence these three, never run them concurrently.**

**Files:** `console/backend/inflight.py`, `console/backend/schema.py`, `console/web/src/lib/workState.ts`, `console/web/src/components/oneriver/Ribbon.tsx`, `console/web/src/components/oneriver/CapacityStrip.tsx`, and their tests

cards.title: The 06:30 daily plan runs itself — a third job on self-groomer.yml on a schedule, with the PT-hour guard and the wiring test in the same commit
cards.description:
**Repo:** bureau-pipeline

## What happened

There are **more than 250 cards in Intake**, and the groomer that would sequence them into a batch the CEO can approve runs only when somebody opens Actions and presses a button. Nobody presses it. The whole loop is built and green-lit (DRE-3337): `propose` writes one Linear comment, the console renders it as a row with four buttons, Approve fires the drain. The missing piece is a clock.

**Decision D5 (2026-08-23) forbids the clock.** `groomer.yml` is declared "on demand, never on a schedule", and `tests/test_groomer_wiring.py` fails the build the moment a cron appears. So this card is gated on the CEO reopening D5 — the operator drafts the comment on DRE-2683, the CEO answers it. **Do not build this until that answer is on the record.** (Recorded as a body note rather than a Linear relation, because the gate is a decision, not a card.)

The honest framing of the reopen, for the record: D5's precondition (DRE-3151's audit) is **not** met. The argument is substitution — the cron reaches `propose` only, which writes one comment and moves nothing, and the drain still refuses any marker not authored in the CEO's own identity (DRE-2721).

## What to build

A **third job** on `self-groomer.yml`, gated `if: github.event_name == 'schedule'` — the existing job renders `inputs.*` empty on a non-dispatch event, so it cannot be reused — passing literals:

* `mode: propose`
* `judgement: on`
* `card: ${{ vars.GROOM_PROPOSAL_CARD }}`
* `intake_hold: ${{ vars.INTAKE_HOLD }}`

The schedule is the cron **pair** `30 13` and `30 14` (UTC) with a **PT-hour guard step** that exits unless the local hour is 06 — the release train's precedent — so it fires once at **06:30 PT** on either side of a DST change.

`tests/test_groomer_wiring.py` is updated **in the same commit** as the workflow; the two move together or the build is red for the wrong reason. Both file headers are rewritten to cite the reopened decision and its date.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The CEO's answer reopening D5 is on DRE-2683 and linked here, before any file is edited.
- [ ] A third job exists, runs only on `schedule`, and passes the four literals above; the manual dispatch job is unchanged.
- [ ] The PT-hour guard makes exactly one of the two cron runs do work, on both sides of a DST change — pinned by a test over both hours.
- [ ] `test_groomer_wiring.py` is updated in the same commit and states which decision permits the cron.
- [ ] PROOF: two consecutive mornings where a proposal comment is written at 06:30 PT with no person involved, recorded here with both run ids and PT times.

## Not in this card

* The email that carries the proposal to the CEO — a separate card, blocked by this one.
* The console's four buttons (DRE-3380).

## Lane

WORKBENCH — one workflow file, its wiring test and two headers. No fleet run spent.

**Files:** `bureau-pipeline/.github/workflows/self-groomer.yml`, `bureau-pipeline/tests/test_groomer_wiring.py`, `bureau-pipeline/.github/workflows/groomer.yml` (header only)

cards.title: A burst reserves its headroom before it starts — linear-budget.json and linear_ops.reserve(kind), so a planner waits instead of dying one write in
cards.description:
**Repo:** bureau-pipeline

**Blocked by:** DRE-3580

## What happened

On 2026-09-09 the fleet's Linear bucket sat between **0 and 100 for about six hours**. What died in it: two planner runs before the planner had started, a post-approval review one write after it had posted its PASS, four integration-harness legs (each critic-approved, each red only for this), two classifiers, and the sweep itself — **nine dead runs**, some with half their writes done. The operator re-entered every one by hand, one at a time, over about **five hours**.

The failure is not "too many requests". It is **no headroom**: background traffic runs the bucket near its floor, and a run that needs a burst — a planner filing ten cards, a review reading a whole plan — arrives to find nothing left and dies mid-flight.

## What to build

A burst reserves its headroom before it starts.

1. `config/linear-budget.json` — the reserve per kind, as data: a plan needs ~300, a review ~150, a classify ~50. The numbers are readable and tunable without a code change.
2. `linear_ops.reserve(kind)` — read the bucket before the planner, the post-approval review, the classifier and a harness scenario start. If it is under the kind's reserve, **wait and re-check on a short cadence inside the run** rather than dying one write in, and print a `linear-budget:` line saying so.
3. **The sweep yields, the plan does not.** The sweep's age-out and promotions are the ones that stand down when the bucket is low — they run next pass, and a plan cannot re-run itself. That yield call lands in the sweep-cost card's PR, not this one.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A planner started against a fake budget under its reserve waits and re-checks instead of dying; the `linear-budget:` line names the kind, the reserve and the wait.
- [ ] A run that has its reserve starts immediately and costs one extra request to find out.
- [ ] The reserves are read from `config/linear-budget.json`; changing a number changes the behaviour with no code edit, pinned by a test.
- [ ] A run that waits past its own ceiling exits with a receipt naming the budget, not a generic death.
- [ ] PROOF: one busy hour — at least four builds, two reviews, one harness run on `main` and one planner — read from `check_linear_budget.py --hours 1`, with the bucket **never under ~1,000** and zero `linear_ratelimited` classifications, posted here with PT times.

## Not in this card

* The sweep's own cost cut and its yield call — the sweep-cost card owns `reconcile.py` this wave.
* Re-dispatching the runs a limit already killed — DRE-3195, which lands last.

**Files:** `bureau-pipeline/config/linear-budget.json`, `bureau-pipeline/scripts/linear_ops.py`, `bureau-pipeline/.github/workflows/plan.yml`, `bureau-pipeline/tests/test_linear_budget*.py`

cards.title: The machine splits after ONE turn-cap death when the run's own receipt says the card is too big — 6 dead runs on 3 PRs, ~$87, zero pushes
cards.description:
**Repo:** bureau-pipeline

## What happened

On 2026-09-09/10 three pull requests each cost **two** dead fix runs: #2428 twice, #2414 twice, #344 twice. **Six runs, ~$87 imputed, about three hours of wall time, and zero pushes.** Every one of them died at the turn cap, and in every case the FIRST run's own receipt already said the card was too big before the second was dispatched.

The house rule already says it: two turn-cap deaths on one card means split, never a third try. `docs/split-ledger.md` counts **$1,223 imputed in dead runs across 40 cards**, and cards that declared more than one file died at the turn cap **9 times in 11**. The machine should not need the second death to learn what the first receipt told it.

## What to build

A new `scripts/too_big.py` with one predicate, `too_big(receipt, card)`: read the dead run's own receipt — the turn-cap subtype, turns spent against the ceiling, and the file footprint the card declares — and answer whether the card is too big for one run.

`fix_dead_run.py` calls it on the **first** turn-cap death. When it answers yes, the card is split there and then — `mid_epic.py discovery --kind addition` with reason `split-turns` — and **no second run is dispatched**. When it answers no, today's behaviour is unchanged.

Update the house rule in the standards from "after two deaths" to "after one, when the receipt says so".

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A first turn-cap death whose receipt says too big files a `split-turns` addition and dispatches no second run — pinned by a fixture built from one of yesterday's real receipts.
- [ ] A death that is not a turn cap (a model error, a limit death, a rate-limited kill) is unchanged and still re-dispatches under the existing rules.
- [ ] A first turn-cap death whose receipt does **not** say too big still gets its second run.
- [ ] The split ledger records the split with the dead run's id, so the turn-cap column can be read as a number.
- [ ] The house rule reads "one death" in `standards/`, and this card records the change.
- [ ] PROOF: one full day with **zero** second turn-cap deaths — the split ledger's turn-cap column stops growing — posted here with PT times.

## Not in this card

* The turn budgets themselves and the planner's sizing (DRE-3022).
* The post-review ceiling (DRE-3282).

## Collision rule

The predicate lives in its own module; the call site in `fix_dead_run.py` is three lines or fewer. `reconcile.py` belongs to the sweep-cost card this wave — do not edit it here.

**Files:** `bureau-pipeline/scripts/too_big.py` (new), `bureau-pipeline/scripts/fix_dead_run.py`, `bureau-pipeline/.github/workflows/agent-fix.yml`, `bureau-pipeline/tests/test_too_big.py`, `bureau-pipeline/standards/card-quality.md`

cards.title: The refutation receipt says "state: dispatched · next: qa-review.yml" when the dispatch 403'd and the run parked for a human
cards.description:
**Observed 2026-09-10 20:38 PT, agent-bureau PR** [dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau#2433](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/review/featdre-3427-the-console-learns-the-reviewer-environment-hold-act-f16d68b35e1d)**, fix run 34558728382 → 34558688339.** The fix agent wrote a refutation; the reusable `agent-fix.yml` posted the 🛑 "Fix attempt 1 refuted the finding" comment ending:

> The pipeline is having the reviewer look at this same commit once more with the evidence above attached…
> 📎 pipeline-act: fix-finding-refuted · kind: recovery · state: dispatched · next: qa-review.yml · discharges: nothing · subscriber: qa-review.yml · tag: refuted-finding

Seconds earlier the same run had logged `HTTP 403` on the `qa-review.yml` dispatch and `##[warning]could not dispatch qa-review.yml … parking for a human instead of promising a re-review that will not run`. The comment promised exactly the re-review the log had just given up on. The console read the receipt as a recovery in flight; nothing said a person was needed; the operator found it by reading the run log ten minutes later.

## What to build

The receipt must be written from the dispatch's outcome, not before it. On a failed dispatch the comment's closing paragraph says the re-review could not be started, names the missing permission and the stub file, and the trailer reads `kind: hold · state: escalated · next: operator` with a tag that the console and reconcile classify as needs-you — the `fix-attempt-blocked` shape — so the card parks where a person will find it. On a successful dispatch the receipt stays as it is. The scenario harness gets one case: refutation + dispatch 403 → escalated receipt, card in the needs-you queue.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A refutation whose `qa-review.yml` dispatch fails posts a receipt whose trailer is `kind: hold · state: escalated · next: operator`, and whose body names the permission and stub file, never "the pipeline is having the reviewer look at this same commit once more"
- [ ] A refutation whose dispatch succeeds posts the current `state: dispatched` receipt unchanged
- [ ] The act registry / receipts contract that agent-bureau's `receipts.py` mirrors is unchanged, or the console card lands first (docs/pipeline-acts.md: console first, pipeline second)
- [ ] A harness scenario drives the 403 branch and fails on main today

**Related:** [DRE-3084](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3084/a-refuted-verdict-re-reviews-itself-when-the-fix-agent-answers-the), [DRE-3427](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3427/agent-bureau-console-teach-acts-the-reviewer-environment-hold-act-and); the stub-permission fix is its own card on repo:agent-bureau.

cards.title: Every agent-fix stub lacks `actions: write`, so the refutation re-review (DRE-3084) 403s in every repo and the PR parks on a human instead
cards.description:
**Observed 2026-09-10 20:38 PT on agent-bureau PR** [dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau#2433](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/review/featdre-3427-the-console-learns-the-reviewer-environment-hold-act-f16d68b35e1d) **(**[DRE-3427](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3427/agent-bureau-console-teach-acts-the-reviewer-environment-hold-act-and)**).** The operator answered the fix agent's blocker with an Operator decision; the fix agent took the refutation path ([DRE-3084](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3084/a-refuted-verdict-re-reviews-itself-when-the-fix-agent-answers-the)) and wrote a refutation; the reusable `agent-fix.yml` then tried to dispatch `qa-review.yml` for the same commit and got:

```
HTTP 403: Resource not accessible by integration (https://api.github.com/repos/dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau/actions/workflows/qa-review.yml)
##[warning]could not dispatch qa-review.yml for PR #2433 — this repo's agent-fix stub needs `actions: write`; parking for a human instead of promising a re-review that will not run
```

(run 34558688339, job `call / fix PR #2433`). The stub in agent-bureau (`.github/workflows/agent-fix.yml:48-50`) grants only `contents: write` and `pull-requests: write`. **The scaffold ships the same block** (`scaffold/customer-repo/.github/workflows/agent-fix.yml:63-65`), so every repo onboarded from it has the same gap, and the refutation path has never once completed on its own in a consumer repo. The operator re-ran the original `pull_request` review by hand at 20:49 PT to move the PR.

## What to build

1. Add `actions: write` to the `permissions:` block of the scaffold's agent-fix stub, with a comment naming this card and [DRE-3084](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3084/a-refuted-verdict-re-reviews-itself-when-the-fix-agent-answers-the) as the reason (the refutation re-review dispatches `qa-review.yml` from inside the fix run).
2. Add the same line to agent-bureau's own installed stub in the same PR.
3. `make check-channel-fleet` (or the pins column's sibling) reports, per repo, whether the installed agent-fix stub carries `actions: write`, so the remaining consumer repos are computed, never remembered ([DRE-2605](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2605/which-repos-still-ride-main-is-computed-from-the-roster-not-remembered)'s rule). The fan-out to those repos is a follow-up per repo via the API route, not this PR.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `scaffold/customer-repo/.github/workflows/agent-fix.yml` and `.github/workflows/agent-fix.yml` both grant `actions: write`, each with a one-line comment citing [DRE-3084](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3084/a-refuted-verdict-re-reviews-itself-when-the-fix-agent-answers-the) and this card
- [ ] A test pins that the scaffold stub's permissions include `actions: write` (fails on main today)
- [ ] `make check-channel-fleet` prints a per-repo column for the installed agent-fix stub's `actions: write`, with UNKNOWN for a repo the token cannot read, and the fleet's outstanding repos are listed by that output in the PR description
- [ ] `make check-channel` and `make check-pins` stay green (the stub still rides `@stable` with `pipeline_ref: stable`)

**Related:** [DRE-3084](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3084/a-refuted-verdict-re-reviews-itself-when-the-fix-agent-answers-the) (the refutation path), [DRE-3427](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3427/agent-bureau-console-teach-acts-the-reviewer-environment-hold-act-and) (the PR it stranded), [DRE-3006](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3006/the-scaffold-ships-the-pre-dre-2810-fix-loop-concurrency-group-every) (the last time the scaffold shipped a stale fix-loop stub).

cards.title: Console: show the reviewer-environment-hold reason on the row — which part of the runner broke, what it means, and the check that proves it
cards.description:
**Follow-up cut by the operator decision on** [DRE-3427](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3427/agent-bureau-console-teach-acts-the-reviewer-environment-hold-act-and)**'s PR** [dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau#2433](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/review/featdre-3427-the-console-learns-the-reviewer-environment-hold-act-f16d68b35e1d) **(2026-09-10 20:30 PT, option A).** [DRE-3427](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3427/agent-bureau-console-teach-acts-the-reviewer-environment-hold-act-and) ships the registry half: the console classifies the `reviewer-environment-hold` act as a held reviewer and never as a fix agent working. Its criterion 2 — the hold's reason text visible on screen — moves here, because no pipeline act's own words reach any screen today and the two times a receipt's words were put on screen ([DRE-2821](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2821/every-automatic-recovery-is-invisible-to-the-console-it-shows-the-last)'s held-card reason, [DRE-3273](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3273/the-proof-waiting-receipt-is-read-by-receiptspy-as-a-hold-and-served)'s waiting-for-proof caption) each needed a served field plus the piece of screen that draws it.

**Build after the receipt exists.** The receipt is written by the bureau-pipeline sibling [DRE-3428](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3428/reviewer-environmentpy-the-environment-crash-signatures-the-medic) (`reviewer_environment.py`, the one `runner-environment-hold` receipt writer) and posted by [DRE-3430](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3430/medicyml-on-an-environment-crash-name-the-cause-on-the-card-skip-the)/[DRE-3431](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3431/reconcilepy-hold-a-crashed-review-after-one-retry-when-the-cause-is). Where it is posted — the Linear card, the PR, or both — decides which row reads it; do not guess. Read the merged writer and its receipt shape first:

`🛑 runner-environment-hold @<full sha>: reviewer cannot run on this runner — <signature>: <meaning> — twice on <sha8>; holding, nothing re-dispatched. Check: <command>.`

Signature slugs: `native-binary-missing`, `executable-not-found`, `credential-refused`, `authentication-error`.

**What to build.** Extract the three parts (signature, meaning, the check command) from the receipt in the console's receipt reader, serve them as one field on the row that already renders the held/recovering family ([DRE-2821](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2821/every-automatic-recovery-is-invisible-to-the-console-it-shows-the-last)'s shape), and draw them on that row on One River — the Pull Requests tab row and the card's river row — so a person reading the row knows what to go fix and the command that proves it is fixed. Keep the family and the chip [DRE-3427](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3427/agent-bureau-console-teach-acts-the-reviewer-environment-hold-act-and) chose; this card adds the reason text beneath it, nothing else. Design: reuse the [DRE-2821](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2821/every-automatic-recovery-is-invisible-to-the-console-it-shows-the-last) held-reason treatment; no new component.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A receipt of the shape above, fed through the console's receipt reader, yields the signature, the meaning and the check command as a served field on the PR row and the card row (unit test on the reader, and a GraphQL test on the served field)
- [ ] One River renders that text on the held row, on the Pull Requests tab and on Overview, in the [DRE-2821](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2821/every-automatic-recovery-is-invisible-to-the-console-it-shows-the-last) held-reason treatment (a vitest on the row component)
- [ ] The row still classifies in the held/recovering family and never as a fix agent working — [DRE-3427](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3427/agent-bureau-console-teach-acts-the-reviewer-environment-hold-act-and)'s tests stay green
- [ ] A receipt with no recognised signature still renders the family with the generic sentence, never a blank
- [ ] The screen is verified by a real run of the console against a fixture receipt, with a screenshot in the PR

**Blocked by:** [DRE-3427](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3427/agent-bureau-console-teach-acts-the-reviewer-environment-hold-act-and), [DRE-3428](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3428/reviewer-environmentpy-the-environment-crash-signatures-the-medic)

cards.title: The runner-pool monitor logs a full HTTP 403 traceback every tick for atlas and deltasolv — repos the bot App is not installed on read as an error, not as UNKNOWN
cards.description:
## What is wrong

Every tick of `console/backend/monitors/runner_pool.py` in prod writes, for atlas (EveryBite org) and deltasolv (DeltaSolv org):

```
WARNING console.monitors.runner_pool runner-pool: could not read BUREAU_RUNS_ON on atlas
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.14/urllib/request.py", line 611, in http_error_default
    raise HTTPError(req.full_url, code, msg, hdrs, fp)
urllib.error.HTTPError: HTTP Error 403: Forbidden
```

Seen 2026-09-10 11:15:38 and 11:15:39 PT in the App Runner application log, and on every tick before and after. The 403 is expected: the bot App's `actions_variables` permission was granted on the dreadnought-foundry installation ([DRE-3351](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3351/operator-stand-up-the-ephemeral-linux-runner-pool-on-the-mac-mini-and), 2026-09-08 18:25 PT), and those two repos live in other orgs. The monitor is right to skip them; it is wrong to print a traceback for a known, permanent condition, because a stack trace every tick buries the errors that matter and reads as an outage to anyone tailing the log.

## What to build

* A 403 on the variable read is "this repo is outside the pool's reach" — one INFO line per tick at most, or better, once per process with the repo named, and the repo reported as UNKNOWN in the monitor's roster (never 0, never healthy). No traceback: `log.warning(..., exc_info=False)` or a caught `HTTPError` with `code == 403`.
* A 5xx / network failure stays a WARNING with the reason, still without the trace for a single tick.
* The console-honesty rule holds: an unreadable repo never counts as "on the pool" or "off the pool".

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test with a fake GitHub returning 403 for one repo asserts: no traceback logged, one line naming the repo, the repo's fail-back verdict is UNKNOWN
- [ ] The prod log shows no `runner_pool` traceback for atlas/deltasolv across one hour after deploy
- [ ] The two-tick sample at 2026-09-10 11:15 PT is quoted on this card as the before state

**Files:** `console/backend/monitors/runner_pool.py`, its tests

cards.title: check_runner_load.py --full has no upper window bound — assess_repo fires live requests up to "now" and cannot replay a closed window from the cache
cards.description:
## What is wrong

`assess_repo(repo, *, gh, since)` takes a lower bound only. The CLI's `--full` and `--servers` paths call it, so every full assessment runs `since..now`. Two consequences seen on 2026-09-09/10:

* A replay of a closed window (2026-09-02..09-08) from the 14,856-response cache could not use `assess_repo` at all — the analysis for [DRE-3541](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3541/the-runner-capacity-adrs-conclusion-was-priced-at-on-demand-only)/[DRE-3548](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3548/the-runner-capacity-adr-covers-one-repo-of-five-extend-it-to-the-whole) had to rebuild rows from `gh.runs(..., until=)` and `gh.jobs()` directly.
* An analysis script that did call `assess_repo` defaulted to today and fired live API calls that competed with the fetch already in flight (killed by hand).

`gh.runs()` already accepts `until`; the gap is only in `assess_repo` and the CLI.

## What to build

* `assess_repo(..., since, until=None)` passed through to `gh.runs`; `--until` on the CLI for `--full`, `--servers` and `--bill-only`, defaulting to now.
* A test that a window with `until` in the past reads only from the cache and makes zero live calls (the fake GitHub asserts no request outside the window).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `check_runner_load.py --full --since 2026-09-02 --until 2026-09-09 --cache <dir>` reproduces the ADR's agent-bureau tables with no network
- [ ] A RED test fails on `main` (no `until` accepted) and passes after
- [ ] The ADR's line "The CLI also lacks `--until`" is removed in the same PR

**Files:** `scripts/check_runner_load.py`, `scripts/test_check_runner_load.py`, `architecture/decisions/adr-runner-pool-capacity.md`

cards.title: check_runner_load.py's class table does not know bureau-pipeline's own workflows or portico's specimen/red-main-repair — 3,969 of 4,270 pipeline jobs classify as unknown
cards.description:
## What is wrong

The tool keys a job's class (ci / release / agent / housekeeping) on the workflow file name. Its table covers the scaffold's stub workflows. bureau-pipeline's own workflows — `self-*.yml`, `tests.yml`, `pr-review.yml`, `release-gate.yml` — and portico's `specimen.yml` and `red-main-repair.yml` are not in it, so [DRE-3548](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3548/the-runner-capacity-adr-covers-one-repo-of-five-extend-it-to-the-whole)'s fleet analysis had to show bureau-pipeline as whole load (8,584 runner-minutes) and never split by class: 3,969 of its 4,270 jobs read `unknown`.

bureau-pipeline nets $0.00 and is never a saving, so this does not move a price. It does leave a slot-sizing gap: its jobs are real load on any pool that carried it.

## What to build

* Add the missing workflow files to the class table with the class each really is (the `self-*` stubs are the same classes as the scaffold stubs they mirror; `tests.yml` is ci; `pr-review.yml` is agent; `release-gate.yml` is release; portico's `specimen.yml` is ci and `red-main-repair.yml` is housekeeping — confirm each by reading the file, not the name).
* Report `unknown` per repo as a percentage in the tool's summary so a future new workflow shows up as a gap instead of silently vanishing from the class tables.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Replaying the cached window, bureau-pipeline's `unknown` share is under 5% and portico's is 0%
- [ ] The summary prints each repo's unknown share; a test pins that a job from an unlisted workflow file is counted as unknown, not dropped
- [ ] The ADR's paragraph explaining why bureau-pipeline is shown as whole load is updated in the same PR

**Files:** `scripts/check_runner_load.py`, `scripts/test_check_runner_load.py`, `architecture/decisions/adr-runner-pool-capacity.md`

cards.title: A draft PR whose check is red but whose critic verdict is APPROVE reads "Stuck — needs you" — `_rank_draft` rewrites FIX_STALLED, MERGE_GATE and AWAITING_OK on a draft but not APPROVED_BLOCKED
cards.description:
**Repo:** agent-bureau

## What happened

The [DRE-3276](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3276/proof-a-live-draft-pr-with-a-red-check-reads-draft-held-a-proof) proof probe (agent-bureau-demo PR #12, a deliberate draft with a failing check, 2026-09-10 07:46 PT) read `Draft — held` for 7m46s — then the critic reviewed it (the critic reviews every PR since [DRE-2250](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2250/critic-silently-skips-every-hand-named-branch-a-substantive-pr-can)), approved it as a deliberate diagnostic, and from 07:54 PT the row read `Stuck — needs you`. An APPROVE over a failing check derives `APPROVED_BLOCKED`, and `console/backend`'s `_rank_draft` ([DRE-3272](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3272/a-draft-pr-is-read-from-githubs-isdraft-and-derives-draft-held-never)) rewrites `FIX_STALLED`, `MERGE_GATE` and `AWAITING_OK` on a draft but not `APPROVED_BLOCKED` — though [DRE-3272](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3272/a-draft-pr-is-read-from-githubs-isdraft-and-derives-draft-held-never)'s own argument for `MERGE_GATE` ("promises a merge GitHub will not perform") applies to it word for word, and `APPROVED_BLOCKED` is the one of the four that shows red in the CEO's needs-you queue. So `Draft — held` on a failing draft is a window, not a resting state, and a draft nobody should act on pages the CEO.

## What to build

`_rank_draft` treats `APPROVED_BLOCKED` like the other three: on a draft, the row reads `Draft — held` with the hover explaining GitHub will not merge a draft, and the row is not counted in needs-you. Test-first with the probe's facts (draft, red check, APPROVE verdict, no fix run) as the fixture; a non-draft with the same facts keeps `Stuck — needs you`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The fixture derives `DRAFT_HELD`, not `APPROVED_BLOCKED`, and is excluded from the needs-you count.
- [ ] A ready (non-draft) PR with the same facts still derives `APPROVED_BLOCKED`.
- [ ] PROOF: agent-bureau-demo PR #12 (or its successor) observed reading `Draft — held` with a red check and an APPROVE standing, recorded on [DRE-3276](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3276/proof-a-live-draft-pr-with-a-red-check-reads-draft-held-a-proof)'s record.

## Not in this card

* The critic reviewing drafts at all — by design since [DRE-2250](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2250/critic-silently-skips-every-hand-named-branch-a-substantive-pr-can).

cards.title: The 80% soft auto-switch did not fire in 24 h with every input satisfied — find which silent return it takes
cards.description:
## What was observed (2026-09-10 06:20–07:30 PT, prod)

`auto_advance_active_account` (`console/backend/subscriptions.py:252-311`) is the soft-threshold switch: when the active account is at or over `NEAR_CAP_THRESHOLD` on either window, advance the console's active account to the next one in failover order with headroom. It runs on every `claude_token_budget` tick (`monitors/claude_token_budget.py:199`).

Every input it needs was satisfied for at least 24 hours, and it did not fire:

* auto-switch toggle **ON**; failover order Dreadnought → VeriCorr → EveryBite → DeltaSolv
* all four `CLAUDE_OAUTH_*` present in prod's App Runner env
* active account = **DeltaSolv at 0.85** seven-day (fractions, from `anthropic-ratelimit-unified-7d-utilization`); Dreadnought at 0.46 = headroom
* prod logs at INFO (1,157 INFO lines in 2 h)
* **zero** `auto-switch:` **lines in 24 h, zero** `token_budget` **lines, no** `monitor check failed` **for it**

So either the monitor never reaches line 199, or the engine returned `None` at one of its silent exits (lines 274, 285, 292, 311 — none of them logs why).

## Not the same as the cards already open

* [DRE-3170](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3170/claude-auto-switch-never-fires-it-watches-the-account-the-console-last) / [DRE-3182](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3182/auto-switch-executor-on-a-429-or-three-limit-deaths-in-fifteen-minutes) / [DRE-3178](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3178/exhaustion-evidence-a-usage-endpoint-429-and-the-fleets-own-limit) are the **hard** executor (usage 429 or three limit deaths → real fleet switch). This card is the **soft** 80% label move, a different function on a different monitor.
* [DRE-2400](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2400/a-manual-or-soft-threshold-active-account-change-doesnt-re-point-ci) (parked, CEO decision) is *whether* the soft switch should re-point CI at all. This card is not that: by design today the soft switch moves only the console's billing label, so it would not have protected the fleet on 09-10. It is still a switch that silently declines with every input satisfied, the same failure shape as everything else this week.
* [DRE-2598](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2598/split-which-account-is-active-into-two-facts-the-exhaustion-alarm-must) is the exhaustion alarm clearing on a label move; related, not this.

## First check

Is a `DeltaSolv — Claude token budget low` WARN open on the Alerts page?

* **Present** ⇒ the monitor runs to the engine; diagnose inside it — `store.subscription_accounts()` rows, `is_account_configured`, the label mapping in `_failover_order_with_headroom`, and whether `active_used` is read as a fraction or a percent against `NEAR_CAP_THRESHOLD`.
* **Absent** ⇒ the monitor is not reaching that line; find out why the tick is not running or is raising before it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each silent `return None` in `auto_advance_active_account` logs one line at INFO naming which condition stopped it (toggle off / no headroom candidate / active below threshold / unknown account), so the next 24 h of silence is explainable from the log alone
- [ ] A test feeds the 09-10 state (active at 0.85 seven-day, another account at 0.46, toggle on, four configured accounts) through the real monitor tick and asserts the active account advances — it must fail on `main` if the cause is in the engine, or the card records with evidence that it was the monitor not running
- [ ] The root cause is named on this card with PT times and the log lines that prove it
- [ ] No new Anthropic probe; everything reads the existing `cost_usage` signal (same constraint as [DRE-2399](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2399/the-budget-alert-cancels-itself-by-failing-over-and-nothing-watches))

cards.title: One River's Pull Requests tab carries no read age — the only tab whose freshness the CEO cannot tell from the screen
cards.description:
**Repo:** agent-bureau

## What happened

`console/web/src/components/oneriver/PullRequestsTab.tsx` renders its rows with no read-age line, while the ribbon, the Overview tab, the capacity strip and the Alerts tab all carry one (the `read-age` rule `scripts/prove_phase.py` pins on four surfaces). Found on 2026-09-10 while moving those pins for the cutover (PR [dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau#2414](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/review/featdre-3061-one-river-is-the-home-page-the-old-dashboard-alerts-and-f183f3e80d97)): the tab shipped on main before the cutover branch forked, so the cutover is neither the cause nor the place to fix it. A stale PR list looks identical to a fresh one, which is exactly the "vouching for data on a schedule it no longer keeps" the read-age rule exists to prevent.

## What to build

The Pull Requests tab shows the same read-age line, derived the same way (`schema.stale_after_seconds` off the GitHub poll cadence), and `prove_phase.py`'s read-age pin covers five surfaces, not four. Test-first.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The tab renders the read age and the stale state like its siblings (mount test).
- [ ] `prove_phase.py 6` counts the Pull Requests tab among the read-age surfaces.
- [ ] Design critic passes the addition.

## Not in this card

* The read-age rule itself or its threshold.

cards.title: The One River home page has no error boundary — one unexpected payload in any of its ~10 reads blanks the whole console instead of one panel
cards.description:
**Repo:** agent-bureau

## What happened

While rescuing PR [dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau#2414](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/review/featdre-3061-one-river-is-the-home-page-the-old-dashboard-alerts-and-f183f3e80d97) (the One River cutover, 2026-09-10 06:40–07:20 PT), the card deep-link dialog "not opening" turned out not to be a routing defect at all: One River was **throwing during render** on a payload shape the old Dashboard tolerated (a `{}` where the SDL promises non-null fields), and the throw took down `CardFlyoutHost` and everything else in `AppShell` with it. In production the same class of failure — one read returning something a panel does not expect — blanks the entire home page rather than the one panel. With the cutover, One River is the console's front door, so a single bad read anywhere on it is a console outage the CEO sees as a white screen.

## What to build

* An error boundary per One River panel (ribbon, capacity strip, each tab, the flyout host): a panel whose render throws renders its own "could not draw <panel> — <reason>" tile in the design's grammar, in place, and the rest of the page stays up. Never a global blank.
* The boundary reports the throw once through the console's existing alert path so it is not silent.
* Test-first: a mount of `AppRoutes` with one panel's read stubbed to throw shows the other panels and the tile; the deep-link dialog still opens.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A throwing panel renders its tile; the page, the ribbon and the flyout host survive (pinned by a mount test).
- [ ] The throw is reported once on the alerts path.
- [ ] Design amended per the DESIGNER role decision (2026-09-07) and the design critic passes it.

## Not in this card

* Fixing individual reads' shapes — each is its own defect when found.

cards.title: The release row source yields a bogus second row for a train run with nothing to release — GitHub reports the skipped matrix job as `call / Release ${{ matrix.surface }}`, and the row reads `surface: "${{ matrix.surface }}" · unk`
cards.description:
**Repo:** agent-bureau

## What happened

Running the merged `console/backend/release_row.py` (`release_rows` with `LiveGitHubReader`) against the live train runs on 2026-09-10 06:50 PT (the [DRE-3527](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3527/proof-a-hand-dispatched-console-release-read-end-to-end-off-the) proof, PR [dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau#2437](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/review/docsdre-3527-the-release-row-read-off-live-github-the-held-train-2b855d02ad90)) produced, beside the real `console · hold · window` row, a second row with `surface: "${{ matrix.surface }}"` and `mark: unk`. When a train run has nothing to release, GitHub never expands the matrix, and the skipped job is reported with its name literally as `call / Release ${{ matrix.surface }}`. The row source treats that job name as a surface. A CEO reading the Activity tab would see a release row for a surface called `${{ matrix.surface }}`.

## What to build

* `release_row.py` recognises an unexpanded matrix job (`${{` in the job name, or the job's `conclusion == "skipped"` with no steps) as "no surface released on this run" and yields no row for it — the real row for the run (the `hold` at `ci_green` with the rule that held it) already says what happened.
* Test-first: a fixture from the live run's jobs payload (the skipped `call / Release ${{ matrix.surface }}` job beside the plan job) yields exactly one row; a fixture with an expanded `call / Release console` job yields the console row.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No row ever carries a surface containing `${{`; pinned by the fixture.
- [ ] A held/no-op train run yields exactly one row, the hold at `ci_green`.
- [ ] PROOF: the next held train run read through the deployed console shows one row (recorded on [DRE-3527](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3527/proof-a-hand-dispatched-console-release-read-end-to-end-off-the)'s proof record).

## Not in this card

* The train's matrix itself — [DRE-3164](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3164/epic-the-release-train-one-reusable-train-in-bureau-pipeline-a-thin); reading the skipped job is the console's job.

cards.title: Three operator cards were closed Done from the console with nothing done (DRE-3497 09-09 13:35 PT, DRE-3494 09-09 13:35 PT, DRE-3155 no code on main) — a `no-code` / OPERATOR card must not close from the queue without its record
cards.description:
**Repo:** agent-bureau

## What happened

Three cards found closed Done with none of their work done, all in the 2026-09-09/10 cleanup:

* [DRE-3497](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3497/operator-apply-the-ceos-bureau-only-decision-every-repo-outside-agent) — the Bureau-only groomer operator card: "Completed by Sid Conklin via the console" 2026-09-09 13:35 PT; nothing performed; re-issued as [DRE-3505](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3505/operator-apply-the-ceos-bureau-only-decision-every-repo-outside-agent).
* [DRE-3494](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3494/operator-grant-the-app-org-billing-read-and-deploy-the-console-so-the) — grant the console's App billing read: "Completed via the console" 2026-09-09 13:35 PT; the App still carries `actions:read` only, the console's spend read answers HTTP 403, and the deploy its own step 5 asks for ran at 20:18 PT — 6h43m after the close (found by the [DRE-3495](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3495/proof-the-rebuilt-actions-budget-alarm-observed-reading-the-2026-08-18) proof, PR [dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau#2432](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/review/docsdre-3495-the-2026-08-18-actions-budget-forensics-report-with-the-4315af33dd1b)). Reopened 2026-09-10 07:10 PT.
* [DRE-3155](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3155/score-the-groomers-judgement-against-the-hand-audit-it-never-saw) — the groomer scorer: Done, but `scripts/groomer_score.py` is not on `main` and no PR ever carried it (found by the [DRE-3260](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3260/proof-the-judged-groomer-observed-reading-the-live-intake-population) proof, PR #348). Reopened 07:04 PT.

Two of the three closed in the same minute from the console's queue. A `no-code` / `OPERATOR:` card's whole content is a record of a hand act; the console let a single click mark it Done with no record, and the lane guard's "Done without evidence" report (which fired on [DRE-3171](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3171/work-the-claude-limit-killed-comes-back-on-its-own-after-the-account) on 09-06) either did not fire or was not read. The effect downstream: PROOF cards that depend on these ([DRE-3260](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3260/proof-the-judged-groomer-observed-reading-the-live-intake-population), [DRE-3495](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3495/proof-the-rebuilt-actions-budget-alarm-observed-reading-the-2026-08-18)) cannot close, and an epic reads "nearly done" when its operator step never happened.

## What to build

* In the console's Green Light / Needs-you actions: a card carrying `no-code` or whose title opens `OPERATOR:` / `[OPERATOR]` is not offered "Done"; it is offered "Record the outcome" — a required sentence that is posted as the card's comment (the record the card asks for) before the state moves, attributed the way an approval is ([DRE-3089](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3089/the-consoles-approve-plan-button-approves-as-the-ceo-not-as-the-fleet)).
* The sweep's lane guard (`lane-guard-report`, [DRE-2746](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2746/every-epic-carries-a-proof-card-and-a-demo-card-and-neither-can-be)'s rule) moves a `no-code` card back to Backlog when it lands in Done with no comment from a human in the preceding hour, and says so on the card — today it reports and leaves it.
* Test-first on both.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A `no-code` card cannot reach Done from the console without a recorded outcome comment (pinned by a test on the resolver).
- [ ] A `no-code` card set Done by any path with no human comment in the last hour is returned to Backlog by the next sweep with a receipt (pinned by a test).
- [ ] PROOF: the three cards above listed in the record with what closed them; one live no-record close returned by the sweep.

## Not in this card

* The three cards' own work — reopened and owned by their epics.

cards.title: A card the groomer could not rank must never appear in the proposed batch — batch f673bfefa340 carried DRE-3020 at position 32 with "could not rank — needs a person" as its reason
cards.description:
**Repo:** bureau-pipeline

## What happened

In the groomer's judged proposal `f673bfefa340` (2026-09-08 09:17 PT, population 260, 18 proposed), [DRE-3020](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3020/proof-fd-6-a-card-that-is-a-business-decision-not-work-expect-the) sits inside the proposed batch at position 32 with its printed reason "could not rank — needs a person", while the same proposal comment lists it among the unranked cards that "stayed exactly where the rules had them". A drain of that batch would have moved a card the model explicitly declined to place. Batch `42ed15f7527d` (2026-09-09 12:11 PT) did not repeat it. Found by the operator's audit of the first two judged batches ([DRE-3151](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3151/operator-audit-the-groomers-first-two-judged-batches-by-hand-every) worksheet, [DRE-3260](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3260/proof-the-judged-groomer-observed-reading-the-live-intake-population) proof record, PR #348 `docs/groomer-judged-batch.md`).

## What to build

In `scripts/groomer.py` `propose`: a card the judgement returns as unranked is removed from the batch before the proposal is written and before the drain reads it — the two lists (proposed; unranked) are disjoint by construction, asserted at write time. Test-first: a fixture where the rules rank a card and the judgement declines it must produce a batch without that card and an "unranked" line that names it; a mutation that lets it through fails the test.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `proposed ∩ unranked = ∅` is asserted in `propose` and pinned by a test.
- [ ] The next live judged proposal shows no card in both lists (checked and recorded here with the proposal id).

## Not in this card

* What the judgement ranks or why — [DRE-3149](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3149/epic-the-groomer-gets-judgement-it-reads-what-we-are-doing-before-it), done.

cards.title: A re-review dispatch must not be deduped against the run that sent it — DRE-3282's round 2 was dropped as a duplicate of its own parent, alive three seconds longer
cards.description:
**Repo:** bureau-pipeline

## What happened

On 2026-09-10 the post-approval review of [DRE-3282](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3282/the-post-critics-ceiling-cut-a-7-card-review-at-48-of-51-turns-the) sent the plan back (round 1, 06:40 PT); the re-plan changed no card, took the `changed=false` branch correctly at 06:46:52 PT and dispatched its own re-review at 06:46:53 PT. That dispatch — run 34484792305 — was discarded at 06:47:09 PT: `Duplicate dispatch skipped: a planner run for DRE-3282 was already in flight (run 34483751603)`. It was deduped **against the very run that dispatched it**, which outlived it by three seconds. Round 2 did not run unaided; a person re-posted `▶️ re-run the review` at 06:47:59 PT and round 2 landed at 06:52 PT. The same thing killed [DRE-3022](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3022/the-planner-sizes-against-the-ledger-every-turn-cap-death-split-and)'s round 2 on 2026-09-09 (recorded on [DRE-3284](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3284/the-ceo-has-approved-dre-3257-three-times-and-dre-3164-five-every-re)). [DRE-3284](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3284/the-ceo-has-approved-dre-3257-three-times-and-dre-3164-five-every-re)'s acceptance criterion 2 ("a re-plan re-reviews itself") is therefore not met as written; its proof record (PR #347, `docs/review-rerun-proof-2026-09.md`) says so.

## What to build

`dedupe_dispatch.py` already exempts a run's own id; it does not exempt its parent's. Carry the dispatching run id on the `repository_dispatch` payload (`parent_run_id`), and treat a run whose id equals the payload's parent as "the run that sent me", never as a duplicate. Test-first: a fixture with an in-flight run whose id is the payload's parent is NOT deduped; an in-flight run with a different id still is.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A re-review dispatched by a still-alive parent run starts; the fixture pins it.
- [ ] An unrelated in-flight planner run for the same epic still dedupes.
- [ ] PROOF: one live re-plan whose round 2 runs with no person posting the act, recorded on this card with both run ids and PT times.

## Not in this card

* The re-run act itself or the console's Approve — [DRE-3284](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3284/the-ceo-has-approved-dre-3257-three-times-and-dre-3164-five-every-re), done.

## Scope added 2026-09-10 (Plan A)

Before building, confirm which path the re-review dispatch actually takes. If it goes through the relay rather than `plan.yml` alone, `parent_run_id` is a **two-repo pair** — the payload written in bureau-pipeline and read in `agent-bureau/cloud/relay/` — and this stops being an XS one-file change. Record the answer on this card first; it decides the shape.

cards.title: The split-ledger daily job (#343 / DRE-3357) pushes straight to `main` and branch protection refuses it — it has failed every run since it landed and will spend 233 fleet Linear calls a night to throw the result away
cards.description:
**Repo:** bureau-pipeline

## What happened

[DRE-3357](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3357/the-split-ledger-regenerates-itself-daily-and-commits-the-result-never) (PR #343, merged 2026-09-09 19:56 PT) added a daily job that regenerates `config/split-ledger.json` and `docs/split-ledger.md`. Its first scheduled run — 34438436573, 21:46 PT on 09-09 — failed: the job ends with `git push origin HEAD:main`, and `main` is protected (all writes via PR). It fires again every night at 21:41 PT and fails the same way. After PR #344 ([DRE-3356](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3356/the-split-ledger-discovers-its-own-population-dates-every-row-and)) lands, the derive step reads the whole board through discovery — about 233 Linear requests on the fleet key — and the result is discarded at the push. Found by the operator's sub-agent while rescuing #344 on 2026-09-10 06:50 PT.

## What to build

The job lands its regeneration the way every other bot write lands: a commit on `bot/split-ledger` off fresh `origin/main`, pushed, and ONE PR opened or updated (the `standards-sync` / `mulch-sync` shape), for the critic and the gate — never a push to `main`. If nothing changed, it opens nothing and says so. The Linear reads stay on the fleet key but are counted in the run's `linear-budget:` line so the cost is visible.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A scheduled run with changes opens/updates exactly one PR on `bot/split-ledger`; with no changes it exits green with "nothing to do".
- [ ] No step in the workflow pushes to `main`; a test pins that (`grep`-level is enough) the way the other sync workflows are pinned.
- [ ] PROOF: one nightly run observed landing its PR, recorded here with the run id and PT time.

## Not in this card

* The ledger's content or the 13-vs-6 August discrepancy noted on #344 — [DRE-3356](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3356/the-split-ledger-discovers-its-own-population-dates-every-row-and)'s critic weighs that.

cards.title: Nothing detects a dependency cycle between an epic-level gate and the card-level gates beneath it — DRE-3420/3421 held ten cards for 38 hours while both sweeps printed a correct "held by" line every pass
cards.description:
**Repo:** bureau-pipeline

## What happened

From 2026-09-08 ~17:40 PT to 2026-09-10 06:41 PT, epics [DRE-3420](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3420/when-the-reviewer-is-down-fleet-wide-the-fleet-says-so-once-the-sweep) and [DRE-3421](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3421/the-medic-holds-after-one-retry-on-an-environment-crash-that-will) (both In Progress, ten open children between them) released nothing. Epic [DRE-3421](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3421/the-medic-holds-after-one-retry-on-an-environment-crash-that-will) carried a formal `blockedBy` relation on epic [DRE-3420](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3420/when-the-reviewer-is-down-fleet-wide-the-fleet-says-so-once-the-sweep); `promote_ready`'s epic-level gate (`epic_blockers_unmet`, [DRE-1772](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-1772/enforce-epic-level-dependencies-gate-a-blocked-epics-cards-auto)) held every [DRE-3421](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3421/the-medic-holds-after-one-retry-on-an-environment-crash-that-will) child because [DRE-3420](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3420/when-the-reviewer-is-down-fleet-wide-the-fleet-says-so-once-the-sweep) was not Done. [DRE-3420](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3420/when-the-reviewer-is-down-fleet-wide-the-fleet-says-so-once-the-sweep) could not reach Done because its lead child [DRE-3433](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3433/reviewer-downpy-the-pure-fleet-outage-decision-the-reviewer-outage) was `blockedBy` [DRE-3428](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3428/reviewer-environmentpy-the-environment-crash-signatures-the-medic) — a [DRE-3421](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3421/the-medic-holds-after-one-retry-on-an-environment-crash-that-will) child. A closed loop across the two levels. Every sweep on both repos printed a correct line — `epic-gate: DRE-3421 is held by a formal blockedBy relation on DRE-3420 (In Progress)` and `promotion: DRE-3433 is held by DRE-3428 (Backlog)` — and would have printed it forever. WIP was 1/12 and 3/8; the cap masked nothing. The operator's audit found it by hand; the fix was deleting the epic-to-epic edge (relation `b0fb56cd-390d-4240-b96c-9cf4e9d4f826`, recorded on both epics); the 06:44 PT sweep released [DRE-3427](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3427/agent-bureau-console-teach-acts-the-reviewer-environment-hold-act-and) immediately.

## What to build

* In `scripts/reconcile.py`, after the epic gate and the card gate have each computed their holds for a pass, walk the combined graph (epic→epic `blocks`, epic→child membership, card→card `blocks`) and detect any cycle that includes at least one non-terminal node. `epic_blockers_unmet` and the card gate already fetch every edge the walk needs — no new Linear reads.
* A detected cycle is named ONCE per pass on the sweep's log and, once per day, as a comment on each epic in the cycle: the nodes in order, and the edge whose removal breaks it with the fewest side effects (prefer the epic-level edge — two epics are never truly serially dependent when their cards cross both ways). Never delete the edge itself: naming is the sweep's act; the operator or the planner removes it.
* The planner's critic (`plan_critic.py`) refuses a plan that would add an epic-level `blockedBy` onto an epic whose children already have a card-level edge back — the cheap check at the moment the edge is written.
* Test-first: a fixture with the [DRE-3420](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3420/when-the-reviewer-is-down-fleet-wide-the-fleet-says-so-once-the-sweep)/3421 shape (two epics, one epic edge, one crossing card edge) makes the current sweep print two "held by" lines and no cycle; after the fix it names the cycle and the edge. A second fixture with a legitimate serial epic dependency (no crossing card edge) stays silent.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The fixture cycle is named on the sweep log and on both epics, once per day, with the edge to remove.
- [ ] A legitimate serial dependency produces no cycle line.
- [ ] The planner's critic refuses a plan that would create a crossing epic edge, with the two cards named.
- [ ] PROOF: the 2026-09-08/09 hold reproduced from the fixture, and one live sweep after landing reading `cycles: 0` in its summary.

## Not in this card

* Auto-deleting relations — the sweep names, people decide.

cards.title: bureau-harness's dependabot.yml is not the house shape — weekly, no `version-update:semver-major` ignore, no minor/patch group — so the sandbox files majors the merge gate holds forever (PR #1, pytest 7→9, 51 days)
cards.description:
**Repo:** bureau-pipeline (the file lives in `bureau-harness`, which has no `repo:` label because it is not a dispatch target — like its stubs, the operator installs the file there from the pipeline's reference copy)

## What happened

The sandbox repo's `.github/dependabot.yml` diverges from the fleet's house pattern ([DRE-2064](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2064/agent-bureau-dependabotyml-ignore-all-semver-major-updates-globally)): weekly, no `ignore: version-update:semver-major` for `"*"`, no minor/patch group. So Dependabot filed a semver-major bump (pytest 7.0.0 → 9.1.1, bureau-harness PR #1, 2026-07-20), the merge gate correctly held it "waiting for human merge — semver-major", and it sat 51 days until the operator closed it on 2026-09-10 06:45 PT. Every other repo on the platform ignores majors for `"*"` because replying "@dependabot ignore this major version" suppresses only that one major and the next is re-filed the following round — a CI run and a review each time.

## What to build

Bring `bureau-harness/.github/dependabot.yml` to the house shape — bureau-pipeline's own file is the reference: monthly interval, one `minor`/`patch` group per ecosystem+directory, `ignore: [{dependency-name: "*", update-types: ["version-update:semver-major"]}]` on every `updates:` entry, with the [DRE-2064](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2064/agent-bureau-dependabotyml-ignore-all-semver-major-updates-globally) rationale in a comment. Stable-only is Dependabot's default — add nothing for it. If the scaffold carries a dependabot template, this is that template applied; if it does not, note it.

**[OPERATOR]** install the file on bureau-harness `main` via the Contents API (the sandbox has no branch protection; its stubs were installed the same way).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] bureau-harness's file matches the house shape wherever the shape is shared (interval, groups, ignore); per-repo facts (ecosystems, directories) are the only difference.
- [ ] No open Dependabot major PR in bureau-harness after the next Dependabot round.

## Not in this card

* The majors themselves — pytest 9 lands only through a deliberate upgrade card.
