cards.title: [EPIC] The fleet's Linear traffic fits one user's 2,500 an hour — the sandbox gets its own identity, the sweep's spend is pinned at its DRE-3236 level, the medic stops waking 50 times an hour, and a planner, a review or a harness run reserves its headroom before it starts
cards.description:
**Repo:** bureau-pipeline

## What happened

On 2026-09-09 the fleet's Linear key (`Agent-Bureau`) hit 0 of 2,500 three times — ~13:08, 15:47 and ~18:00 PT — and stayed under 100 for most of the afternoon and evening. [DRE-3168](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3168) had already done what it set out to do: the operator reads on a second seat (`bureau-tools`), and a sweep that cost 143 requests was cut to about 20 ([DRE-3236](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3236/the-first-measured-hour-sweeps-and-merge-sync-spend-1070-of-the-fleets)). Today's exhaustion was the **fleet key alone**, with no operator involved. What died on it, each time: two planner runs before the planner started ([DRE-3336](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3336/epic-the-release-run-is-a-fact-the-console-can-read-release-acts-with), [DRE-3507](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3507/epic-the-release-run-is-a-row-on-the-activity-tab-the-release-journey), 15:47 PT), a post-approval review one write after it had posted its PASS ([DRE-3337](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3337/epic-the-groomers-proposal-is-in-the-ceos-needs-you-queue-one-row-per) round 5, 15:48 PT), four integration-harness runs (PR #333, #335, #340 and #332 attempt 4 — each critic-approved, each red only for this), the sweep itself (`Reconcile` failures on agent-bureau and bureau-pipeline), [DRE-3412](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3412/a-fix-loop-escalation-parks-the-card-in-plan-review-never-triage-and)'s classifier (18:57 PT), and every rescue push's `deliver-rescue` receipt. The medic classified each `linear_ratelimited` and correctly retried none — and nothing re-entered any of them; the operator did it by hand, one at a time, over five hours.

Measured that evening (operator, from run logs and the `x-ratelimit-requests-remaining` header):

* The three agent-bureau sweeps between 15:45 and 16:45 PT spent **90, 89 and 144** requests each — the [DRE-3236](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3236/the-first-measured-hour-sweeps-and-merge-sync-spend-1070-of-the-fleets) level of ~20 did not hold. Nothing pins it.
* Between 18:15 and 19:15 PT the org ran **50 Pipeline Medic wake-ups** (28 bureau-pipeline, 22 agent-bureau, nearly all `skipped`), **55 runs in bureau-harness** (CI, merge gate, QA review for the harness's own probe PRs), and 3 sweeps on `agent-bureau-demo` — all on the fleet key. The sandbox's own sweeps and gates read the same board with the same identity as production.
* With one build and two reviews in that hour the bucket still sat at 24; it refilled at ~30/min only once the harness runs on `main` stopped (19:17 PT).
* The console polls on the same key (4×/hour, small) and the relay's escalation reads do too (small). Neither is the problem; both count.

The shape of the failure is not "too many requests" but "no headroom": background traffic (sweeps × repos, sandbox, medic) runs the bucket near its floor, and anything that needs a burst — a planner filing ten cards, a review reading a whole plan, a harness leg — arrives to find nothing left and dies mid-flight, sometimes with half its writes done.

## What the CEO sees when it is done

* A busy afternoon no longer kills planners or reviews: a run that needs a burst either has it or says, before it starts, that it is waiting — and re-enters on its own.
* One line on the epic each day: the hour's spend per consumer, against the budget, from `check_linear_budget.py`.

## What to build (the planner counts before filing)

1. **The sandbox on its own identity.** `bureau-harness`'s `LINEAR_API_KEY` (and the harness driver's) becomes a third non-human seat, `bureau-sandbox`, declared in `linear-identities.json` and checked by `check_linear_identities.py` like the other two. Production's board reads never share a bucket with probe traffic again. (Operator half: create the seat, mint the key, fan it out — one `[OPERATOR]` card.)
2. **The sweep's spend is pinned.** `check_linear_budget.py` runs in CI on a fixture of a full board and fails on a sweep above the [DRE-3236](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3236/the-first-measured-hour-sweeps-and-merge-sync-spend-1070-of-the-fleets) ceiling (30 per pass); the live sweep prints its spend and the reconcile workflow's summary shows it. Find and fix what took a pass from ~20 back to 144.
3. **The medic wakes only when there is something to do.** `medic.yml` triggers on `workflow_run` conclusions that can need a medic (failure, cancelled — not success, not skipped), and its first step decides from the run record alone ([DRE-3201](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3201/the-medic-decides-it-has-nothing-to-do-before-it-reads-linear-a)'s intent, cancelled then, re-issued here) before any Linear read.
4. **A burst reserves its headroom.** Before the planner, the post-approval review, the classifier and a harness scenario start, they read the bucket (`linear_ops.budget()`), and if it is under a declared reserve (data in `config/linear-budget.json`, per kind — a plan needs ~300, a review ~150) they wait and re-check on a short cadence inside their own run instead of dying one write in; a `linear-budget:` line says so. The sweep's age-out and promotions are the ones that yield (they can run next pass; a plan cannot re-run itself).
5. **Limit-dead runs re-enter on their own** — [DRE-3195](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3195/the-sweep-re-dispatches-limit-killed-work-when-the-account-changes-or)'s content, pulled in here: the sweep re-dispatches a plan, review or classify run that a `linear_ratelimited` receipt names, once the window has rolled, bounded by the WIP cap.

## Acceptance criteria (for the set)

- [ ] `check_linear_identities.py check` prints three `[OK]` identities — fleet, operator-tools, sandbox — none an admin; bureau-harness's workflows resolve to the sandbox seat.
- [ ] A full-board sweep fixture stays under 30 requests in CI; the live sweep's `linear-budget:` line is on every pass and in the workflow summary.
- [ ] The medic runs only on conclusions that can need it; a day's medic count is under 10 per repo with no loss of coverage (the [DRE-2954](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2954/the-medics-one-retry-re-dispatches-a-card-the-pipeline-has-just-parked) cases still classified).
- [ ] A planner started against a bucket under its reserve waits and re-checks rather than dying; asserted with a fake budget, and observed once on the live board with PT times on this epic.
- [ ] A run killed `linear_ratelimited` is re-dispatched by the sweep after the roll, once, and the receipt names the re-entry — observed live.
- [ ] PROOF: one busy hour (≥4 builds, ≥2 reviews, one harness run on main, one planner) recorded from `check_linear_budget.py --hours 1` with the bucket never under 300 and no `linear_ratelimited` classification; the reading posted here in PT.
- [ ] DEMO: the CEO watches a planner start during a busy hour and finish.

## Not in this epic

* The operator's second seat, the frugal reads and the RATELIMITED client — [DRE-3168](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3168/the-fleets-linear-budget-is-one-users-2500-requests-an-hour-shared-by), done.
* The console's poll cadence or the relay's reads — small and correct today.

## Planner notes

Five deliverables across bureau-pipeline (sweep, medic, budget reserve, re-entry), bureau-harness (the seat's fan-out, operator) and agent-bureau (identities config, the check). Split on file footprint; the reserve (4) and the re-entry (5) touch `reconcile.py` and `plan.yml` and are wired `blockedBy` the budget-reading helper. The sandbox seat (1) shares no file with the rest and can run first. Every child needs `initiative:bureau` and a `repo:` label.

## Scope added 2026-09-10 (Plan A)

The CEO approved Plan A at 2026-09-10 12:40 PT after reading the measured numbers. Six additions. Nothing above is withdrawn.

**Deliverable 6 — a card-done dispatches a SCOPED sweep, not a full board pass.** `linear-sync` already carries the merged card down the `MERGED_CARD` road through `merge_sweep_gate.py`, and then dispatches a sweep that reads the whole board anyway. Measured 2026-09-09: **9 card-done sweeps in 54 minutes**, each a full pass at ~92 requests. Scope the card-done pass to the merged card and its epic; `epic-activated` stays a full sweep (a handful a day). Worth **~690 requests an hour** back.

**The live numbers for deliverable 2 are 92 and 61, not 20 — and the CI fixture is part of the defect.** A live pass costs **92** requests on agent-bureau and **61** on bureau-pipeline today, while `tests/test_sweep_request_cuts.py` passes at 30 — because its fixture is not a real board. The fixture is rebuilt from a real board snapshot in the same card as the cut, or the ceiling goes on passing while the sweep spends three times it.

**New criterion — the sandbox must not touch production.** No sweep running in a sandbox repo (`bureau-harness`, `agent-bureau-demo`) moves, escalates or ages out a card on the production board. **130+ cards aged out of Intake into Green Light overnight on 2026-09-09/10.** Same-day: a dated `intake_hold` and no `schedule:` on both sandbox stubs. Durably: one declared age-out owner per board, and `intake_controls.may_escalate(slug, rail)` — `escalate_aged_intake` has no repo filter by design.

**Deliverable 3 gains its number and its mechanism.** The Pipeline Medic ran **5,610 times in 15 days** (2026-08-27 → 2026-09-10), ~97% of them skipped *after* starting a paid `ubuntu-latest` runner; medic + merge gate together are **61% of every run in the fleet**. The mechanism is a **job-level** `if:` in the calling stubs, so the job never starts on a conclusion that cannot need a medic — not a first step that exits early.

**Correction —** `limit_wait.py` **does not exist on** `main`**.** Deliverable 5's contract is re-pointed at the live module, `limit_recovery.py`. DRE-3195 carries the same correction.

**The PROOF bar is the CEO's target: above ~1,000 all day.** The busy-hour reading in the acceptance criteria stands, but the bucket floor it must clear is **~1,000**, not 300.

cards.title: A deferred release leaves the Actions list green — the train annotates the run it did not ship from
cards.description:
When a surface defers, the release train prints the surface script's receipt verbatim and concludes `success`. Nothing in GitHub's own UI marks the run as having shipped nothing: no `::warning::` annotation, no step summary. A reader scanning the Actions list sees an unbroken column of green.

On 2026-09-09 the console train deferred every run from 12:53 PT onward. Run 34427367183 at 18:55 PT logged `deferred: infra changed since agent-bureau-console-v1.6.32 — run make deploy-console` and then `release-train: no-op … — deferred: …`, and concluded `success` with both jobs green, including a step named `Run the surface`. Six hours and 46 commits later — including migration `0038_intake_pen_act.py` — the CEO found it by asking why no release had happened.

The console side of this is already covered and shipped: [DRE-3483](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3483/the-release-train-says-when-it-is-standing-on-a-deferral-a-deferred-no)'s `release_train_health.py` (live in v1.6.32) parses that receipt and raises `release_train_deferred:<slug>` at WARN. **This card is the GitHub side only** — the run itself should say what it did not do, for whoever is looking at Actions rather than at the console.

The deferral is correct behaviour and does not change. A deferral is a no-op, not a failure: the run must keep concluding `success` and must not go red. This is annotation, not enforcement.

## Scope

In `release_train.py`, on the path that renders a `deferred` no-op:

1. Emit a `::warning::` annotation naming the surface, the commit it would have released, the tag it would have cut, and the operator action that clears it. GitHub shows it on the run, in the Actions list, and in the checks API.
2. Write the same facts as a `## Deferred` block to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, so opening the run shows it without scrolling a job log.
3. Keep the existing verbatim receipt line exactly as it is — `release_train_health.py` parses it with `release-train: no-op \S+ (?P<surface>\S+) — deferred:` and must not break.

Surface-agnostic: every surface in a caller's `release.json` gets this, not console only.

**Files:** `scripts/release_train.py` and its tests. Do not edit `release-train.yml` unless the summary write needs it, and do not touch any caller's `release-console.sh`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A deferred surface raises one `::warning::` naming surface, commit, would-be tag and the clearing action
- [ ] The same facts appear as a `## Deferred` block in the job's step summary
- [ ] The run still concludes `success` — a deferral is a no-op and must never turn a run red
- [ ] The existing `release-train: no-op … — deferred: …` line is byte-identical, and a test asserts `release_train_health.py`'s regex still matches it
- [ ] A test drives the 2026-09-09 shape — a surface script exiting 0 with a `deferred:` line — and fails if either the annotation or the summary is missing
- [ ] Nothing about when a surface defers changes

## Evidence

* Run 34427367183 (18:55 PT, 2026-09-09): `deferred:` receipt in the log, run concluded `success`, no annotation, no tag
* Trains at 17:33, 17:40, 18:03, 18:21, 18:55 PT — all green, none shipped
* `RELEASE_HOLD` unset; window 07:00-21:00 PT, spacing 30 min, paths matched, green-at-SHA satisfied — the planner chose `f8d98b3` and the surface script declined it
* The deferral is emitted by the caller at `agent-bureau/infra/release-console.sh:848-851` (`release_can_apply_cdk` false + `release_cdk_app_changed` true → echo, `return 0`)

cards.title: Product repos have no `deliver-rescue.yml`, so the rescue's delivery follow-up is refused with 403 in every repo but bureau-pipeline — the scaffold ships the stub and the operator installs it fleet-wide
cards.description:
**Repo:** bureau-pipeline

## What happened

When a rescue push is refused, agent-task.yml's fallback ([DRE-3262](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3262/the-rescue-push-failed-with-400-on-its-own-fresh-mints-and-the-card)) dispatches a delivery workflow that downloads the rescue artifact with its own fresh token, applies it on a branch and opens the PR — "Nobody needs to do this by hand". On 2026-09-09 that worked exactly once, in bureau-pipeline ([DRE-3358](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3358/ledger-contextpy-renders-the-split-ledger-and-the-mulch-planning), `self-deliver-rescue.yml`, 15:55 PT). In agent-bureau every one of the three refusals that afternoon ended instead with:

```
⚠️ the delivery follow-up could NOT be dispatched (`deliver-rescue.yml` on `dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau`: HTTP 403: Resource not accessible by integration …/actions/workflows/deliver-rescue.yml), so this card needs a human
```

`deliver-rescue.yml` exists in no product repo — not agent-bureau, not portico, not atlas, not bureau-harness (checked 17:00 PT). bureau-pipeline has only its own `self-deliver-rescue.yml`. The scaffold (`scaffold/`) ships no such stub, `config/pipeline-channel.json` and `make check-channel-fleet` know nothing of it, so the fallback can never fire where the fleet builds. The 403 is GitHub's answer to "dispatch a workflow file that does not exist" for an App token; it reads as a permissions problem and is not one.

## What to build

* A `deliver-rescue.yml` stub in `scaffold/` in the house shape (a thin `workflow_call` consumer riding `@stable` with `pipeline_ref: stable`, secrets mapped the way the other eight stubs map them), calling a reusable `deliver-rescue.yml` in bureau-pipeline that does what `self-deliver-rescue.yml` does for a product repo: download the named artifact from the named run with a fresh mint, apply it on `agent/<card>-…` off the default branch, push, open the PR, comment on the card.
* The stub is counted: `make check-channel-fleet` reports it per repo like the other stubs, and the scaffold's stub roster (and the retirement runbook's count of nine) becomes ten.
* The dispatching side in agent-task.yml distinguishes "workflow not present" from a real permission refusal in the comment it writes — the operator half below is the fix for the first, a secrets change is the fix for the second.
* **[OPERATOR]** install the stub on `main` of every repo in `config/repo-map.json` that builds (the same route used for bureau-harness's stubs), then re-run `make check-channel-fleet` and record the rows on this card.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `scaffold/` carries `deliver-rescue.yml`; the scaffold tests count it; `check-channel-fleet` lists it per repo with `present`/`absent`.
- [ ] A rescue refusal in a product repo with the stub installed ends with `🚚 rescue-delivery-dispatched` and a PR, not "needs a human" — PROOF on one real run, recorded here with run id and PT time.
- [ ] The "could NOT be dispatched" comment says whether the workflow is missing or the token was refused.
- [ ] Every building repo in the roster shows the stub present after the operator install.

## Not in this card

* The two-header 400 itself (sibling card) — once that is fixed the fallback fires rarely, but it must exist for the day it fires.

cards.title: [EPIC] The release run is a row on the Activity tab — the release journey in journey.ts, the row with its dot and sweep off the backend's release-row type, the design amendment, and the CEO watching one release land
cards.description:
A release is the most consequential thing the pipeline does and today it is invisible on the console while it happens. The CEO started the train by hand on 2026-09-08 and asked where to watch it; the honest answer was "GitHub". Putting a release on the river is two epics, split on 2026-09-09 at the CEO's instruction: [DRE-3336](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3336) makes the release run a fact the backend can answer with — the six stages, their marks, the acts, the version and the outcome, as a GraphQL type; **this epic draws that answer on the Activity tab** as a row of its own, with a journey bar whose stages are the train's real stages, so the bar advances, the dot pulses, and the sweep runs from the same derivation every card row already uses. This epic invents nothing: it reads what [DRE-3336](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3336/epic-the-release-run-is-a-fact-the-console-can-read-release-acts-with) derives.

## What the CEO sees when it is done

* Dispatching the train (by hand today, by itself once `auto: true`) makes a row appear on the Activity tab within one refresh, named for the surface and the version it is cutting (`console · v1.6.24`).
* The row's journey bar walks the train's own stages — `CI green · cut · build · roll out · verify · live` — one hue for the machine's half and one for the live half, exactly the way a card row's bar changes hue where the card becomes a pull request. The words and the hue-change stage are [DRE-3336](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3336/epic-the-release-run-is-a-fact-the-console-can-read-release-acts-with)'s; this epic keeps them.
* The dot pulses and the current stage sweeps while a step is actually happening, go quiet between steps, and turn red when a step is past its cadence with nothing discharging it. A row for a run that stopped shows `fail` at the stage it stopped on; a row waiting on a person shows `hold`, saying which rule held it.
* When the release lands, the row reads `live` with the version, and the same version appears under Shipped today on the right rail. A release that rolled back reads `rolled back`, still on the row, never silently gone.
* Yesterday's releases are readable in the same place the CEO reads yesterday's cards, on the same tab and with the same filters.

## Where the facts come from — derive, never infer

* **The row.** Everything on the row is the release-row GraphQL type [DRE-3336](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3336/epic-the-release-run-is-a-fact-the-console-can-read-release-acts-with) exposes: surface, version, six stages with marks, the hue-change stage, `last_act_at` and the act name per stage, the outcome. The frontend derives nothing from Actions itself and never reads a run.
* **The pulse and the sweep.** `deriveLiveness` (`console/web/src/components/atoms/liveness.ts`) over the stage's `last_act_at` and the cadence looked up by act name from the act registry the card rows already read. A stage with no act renders `unknown`: no pulse, no overdue. No number typed into a component.
* **The journey.** `journey.ts` already carries two six-stage journeys off one pair of functions; the release journey is the third, not a fourth renderer.

## Not in this epic

* Deriving anything from a run — the stages, marks, acts, version and outcome are [DRE-3336](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3336/epic-the-release-run-is-a-fact-the-console-can-read-release-acts-with)'s, and a gap in them is a card on [DRE-3336](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3336/epic-the-release-run-is-a-fact-the-console-can-read-release-acts-with), not a workaround here.
* Changing the train itself, its rules, or `auto` ([DRE-3164](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3164/epic-the-release-train-one-reusable-train-in-bureau-pipeline-a-thin), [DRE-3324](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3324/operator-exercise-a-console-rollback-against-production-then-flip-the)).
* Portico, the relay or the website joining the river ([DRE-3245](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3245/epic-the-fleet-joins-the-release-train-portico-the-relay-the-website)); once they join the train, their runs are rows by the same code with no change here.
* A new alert. The CRITICAL failure alert ([DRE-3210](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3210/agent-bureau-a-failed-train-release-raises-a-critical-alert-on-the)) stands; the row is where the CEO watches, the alert is what reaches him off-console.

## Acceptance criteria (for the set — the planner writes each child's own)

- [ ] A release row from the backend is a row on the Activity tab while the run runs and after it lands, named for its surface and version, sorted and filtered like a card row.
- [ ] The row's journey bar carries exactly the six stages and the four marks `now / fail / hold / unk` as the backend returned them, with the hue change at the stage the backend named — rendered through `journey.ts`'s existing pair of functions as the third journey.
- [ ] The dot and the sweep on a release row come from `deriveLiveness` over the stage's `last_act_at` and the registry cadence for its act; a stage with no act renders `unknown`.
- [ ] A `hold` row shows which rule held it; a `fail` row stays on the tab; a landed release reads `live` with the version and a rolled-back one reads `rolled back`.
- [ ] The design is amended for the release row (the One River design contract, PR [dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau#2280](<https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/review/designdre-3106-the-one-river-design-contract-lands-and-the-planning-55fb5cca1487>) lineage) and the design critic passes it, per the DESIGNER role decision of 2026-09-07.
- [ ] PROOF: a hand-dispatched console release observed on the tab end to end — row appears, bar walks every stage, dot pulses during roll out, reads `live` with the tag — recorded in the repo.
- [ ] DEMO: the CEO watches one release land on the Activity tab.

## Planner notes

Count before filing: this is one tier — `console/web` — in three pieces with one outside contract: the release journey in `journey.ts`, the row (its data hook off the GraphQL type, its dot and sweep), and the design amendment with its critic pass; then the PROOF and the DEMO. Split on file footprint. cards.title: OPERATOR: apply the CEO's Bureau-only decision — every repo outside agent-bureau and bureau-pipeline is switched off on the standing proposal card, and the first proposal after the switch ships is seen honouring it (re-issue of DRE-3497)
cards.description:
OPERATOR: the CEO's decision of 2026-09-08 — Bureau only, until it is solid — is applied through the switch this epic builds, so it is in force from the first proposal after the switch ships rather than from the first time someone remembers it. The epic quotes the CEO saying it three times and gives the cost of not having it: atlas cards were proposed, approved as part of a batch, drained, and one was mid-planning before it was pulled back by hand. The pipeline card builds the switch (`🧺 groom-hold-repo: <slug>`, honoured by `propose` and by the drain) and the console cards show and operate it; none of them throws it. This card throws it.

**Why this card exists a second time.** It re-issues DRE-3497, which was moved to Done through the console on 2026-09-09 while DRE-3403 — the card that builds the switch — was still in Backlog, and with no `🧺 groom-hold-repo:` marker on the standing proposal card (0 of its 22 comments carry one). None of the five steps below had happened, and steps 4 and 5 could not have: the `## Held repos — switched off by you` section, the `held_repos` JSON and the Bureau-only Repo column only exist once DRE-3403 has merged. The pipeline never reopens a finished card, so the work moves here, blocked by DRE-3403 as a real relation, and DRE-3497's own record says so.

Steps, all by hand, in order. (1) Compute the set: every key of bureau-pipeline's `config/repo-map.json` other than `agent-bureau` and `bureau-pipeline`, read from the file on the day and never from memory — on 2026-09-09 the map holds 6 repos and the set is the 4 outside Bureau: `atlas`, `deltasolv`, `agent-bureau-demo` and `portico`; if the map has changed, the file wins and this card records the count and the slugs it found. (2) Name the standing proposal card: the card `propose --post` is run against and the self-groomer stub's `card` input names. Today that is DRE-3327, the card the 2026-09-08 proposals were posted to. A hold lives on the card it is written on, so it goes on THIS card, and every later `propose --post` — the proof card's included — runs against the same card; if the operator ever moves proposals to another card, the CEO rewrites the holds there before the first proposal is posted to it. (3) The CEO writes one comment per repo on that card, opening with the marker, in his own Linear identity — by hand in Linear, or from the row's `not this repo` once the console control is live; never the operator's `bureau-tools` key and never the fleet's, which the groomer ignores and the epic forbids for decisions. One slug per comment: `🧺 groom-hold-repo: atlas`, `🧺 groom-hold-repo: deltasolv`, and so on through the set. (4) The operator runs the groomer in `propose` mode against that card (the self-groomer stub with `card` = the standing card, or `python3 scripts/groomer.py propose --lane Intake --post DRE-3327` from a bureau-pipeline checkout on the fleet key) and reads the result: the `## Held repos — switched off by you` section lists every repo from step 1 with its card count, the JSON's `held_repos` names the same set, and the batch table's Repo column holds only `agent-bureau` and `bureau-pipeline`. (5) Record on this card, as a comment: the date and PT time, the slugs held, the CEO's Linear actor name as shown on the markers, the proposal id from step 4, and its `offered` and population counts.

Nothing in this card releases a repo, and the decision has no end date. It is lifted one repo at a time by the CEO's `🧺 groom-release-repo: <slug>` — the row's `bring back`, or by hand — when he judges Bureau solid, and by nobody else. This is the switch on what is proposed; the per-repo work-in-progress cap on builds is a different control and is not touched.

**Files:** none — nothing is committed by this card; the record is the markers on the proposal card and the comment on this one.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each of the repos in `config/repo-map.json` other than `agent-bureau` and `bureau-pipeline` (4 on 2026-09-09) carries a `🧺 groom-hold-repo: <slug>` comment on the standing proposal card, authored by the CEO's Linear user — the actor name is recorded on this card and is neither `Agent-Bureau` nor `bureau-tools`.
- [ ] The first `propose --post` on that card after the markers lists all of those repos under `Held repos — switched off by you` with their card counts, its JSON `held_repos` names the same set, and its batch table's Repo column contains only `agent-bureau` and `bureau-pipeline`; the proposal id and PT time are recorded on this card.
- [ ] This card's record names the standing proposal card by id and states that every later `propose --post` runs against it.
- [ ] No `🧺 groom-release-repo:` marker is written by this card, and the held set recorded at close equals the computed set.
- [ ] This card is not moved to Done until every line above is recorded on it as a comment — a Done with no record is what DRE-3497 became, and it is the defect this card replaces.

**Blocked by:** DRE-3403

cards.title: PROOF: a ≥7-card post-approval review finishes with a verdict, its turns receipt lands, and the medic stamps no limit death
cards.description:
Observe the three fixes running against real state, and record what was seen in the repo.

A green test suite is not the proof. The proof is the next post-approval review on an epic with seven or more children — run on the merged `main` of bureau-pipeline, through the live `plan.yml` — finishing and leaving a verdict, with the new receipt on the epic and no false limit-death stamp anywhere in its wake. This card waits for that review to happen and writes down what it said.

What to watch for, on the first post-approval review of a ≥ 7-card epic after DRE-3498, DRE-3501 and DRE-3499 have all merged:

1. The epic's thread carries a pipeline-authored comment that is exactly one line of the form `🧮 review-turns: spent=<N> ceiling=<M> children=<K> model=<model>`, alone in its comment, with `<M>` equal to `40 + 4 × <K>` — or 60 when that is smaller, or 140 when larger (the cap is the QA critic's retry ceiling and this epic does not move it) — and with `<N>` at most `<M>`. Seven cards read `ceiling=68`.
2. The round is recorded as a decision — a `plan-critic: stage=post … result=PASS` or `result=SEND_BACK` record — not as a `🪦 plan-critic-died:` tombstone. If the review does die, the tombstone's note must not contain `(success)`, and a death whose turns reached the ceiling must have been followed by the pipeline's own retry comment.
3. The medic run for any red plan run in that window posts no `🪦 limit-death: kind=claude` marker on the epic unless the run's log genuinely carries the account-limit text; read the medic run's `Is this a limit death?` step output by hand and note which branch it took.
4. Also record, as the first data point of the series the constant is to be tuned from, what epic DRE-3282's own post-approval review spent. That review ran BEFORE DRE-3498 merged — it is the review that released these cards — so it left no receipt; read its ceiling off the run's `Second critic — turn ceiling` step output (five children under the formula in force at the time: `30 + 4 × 5 = 50`, floored to 60) and its turn count off the run's execution result, and write both down with the run id, stating that the receipt did not yet exist.

Write the observation as a dated section in a new file `docs/review-turns-proof-2026-09.md`: the epic identifier, the run id, the receipt line verbatim, the round record verbatim, the medic's branch, the date and who read it. That file is the deliverable — an observation that is not written down is a claim.

**Files:** docs/review-turns-proof-2026-09.md

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Observed against the live pipeline, by hand: a post-approval review on an epic with ≥ 7 children, run after all three build cards merged, finished and left a `plan-critic:` round record rather than a tombstone; the run id and the epic are named in the observation file.
- [ ] The `🧮 review-turns:` receipt for that review was observed in production on the epic's thread, alone in its comment, and its `ceiling` value matches the new formula for that child count (`40 + 4 × K`, floor 60, cap 140); the line is quoted verbatim in the observation file.
- [ ] The medic's `Is this a limit death?` step for any failed plan run in the same window was read by hand and took the not-a-limit branch for the turn-cap or over-ceiling deaths in that window (expected: zero or one); the run ids read are listed.
- [ ] `docs/review-turns-proof-2026-09.md` is merged to `main` with the observations above and a dated entry for this epic's own review — run id, the ceiling it ran with, the turns it spent, and a note that it predates the receipt — as the first data point in the series.

**Blocked by:** DRE-3498, DRE-3501, DRE-3499

cards.title: The scenario harnesses stop hand-copying a workflow step's environment, and the suite stops depending on a GitHub runner to pass
cards.description:
Two faults in the pipeline's test harness, both found while fixing the 2026-09-09 outage ([DRE-3484](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3484/agent-taskyml-is-unparseable-the-report-steps-run-block-crossed)), both of which made a small correct change look dangerous.

## Fault 1 — the step's environment is hand-copied into at least four files

`test_platform_fault_scenario.py`, `test_turn_budget_scenario.py` (twice), `test_act_emission_scenario.py`, `test_refuted_verdict_rereview.py` and `test_critic_no_verdict_cause.py` each carry their **own** literal table of the Report step's `${{ }}` values and their **own** hand-built `env` dict. Nothing derives either from the workflow.

Moving five values out of that step's script and into its `env:` — a change that touched one workflow file — **broke 27 tests across files that never mention it.** Each one had to be found and corrected by hand. The producer changed and six consumers had no idea.

The fix is the house rule for exactly this (`feedback_producer_consumer_drift_extract_or_update_all`): one helper, in one place, that reads the step's own `env:` block out of the workflow and resolves it against a single table of test values. A caller asks for "the Report step's environment" and gets it. A value added to the workflow reaches every scenario at once, and a value the table cannot resolve is an error naming the expression — never a silent empty string, which is what an unresolved value degrades to today.

## Fault 2 — twelve tests fail on any machine that is not a GitHub runner

`tests/test_qa_review_model_note.py`, `test_crashed_critic_holds_merge.py` and `test_critic_size_strategy.py` execute a rendered `qa-review.yml` block that reads `$GITHUB_REPOSITORY`. On a runner it is always set. On a laptop it is not, and the block dies with `GITHUB_REPOSITORY: unbound variable` — twelve failures, on a clean checkout of `main`, with nothing wrong.

That is worse than noise. **A suite that is red for environmental reasons cannot be used as a baseline**, and a baseline is the only way to tell "my change broke 27 tests" from "these were already failing" — which was the single most important measurement taken during this outage. Anyone running the suite locally learns to discount failures, which is how a real one gets discounted too.

The harness declares the runner variables the blocks under test depend on, the way it already declares `RUNNER_TEMP`. A block that reads a variable the harness does not supply fails naming it, rather than dying on `set -u`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One helper resolves a named step's `env:` from the workflow itself; every scenario file uses it and no file carries its own copy of the table
- [ ] An expression the value table cannot resolve raises, naming the expression and the step — proven by a test that asks for an unknown one
- [ ] Adversarial: adding a new `env:` entry to the Report step requires no edit in any scenario file for the suite to keep passing
- [ ] `python3 -m pytest tests/` is green on a developer machine with no `GITHUB_*` variables set, on a clean checkout
- [ ] A block reading a runner variable the harness does not supply fails with a message naming the variable
- [ ] Test count does not fall: a scenario that no longer applies is replaced, not deleted

**Files:** tests/test_platform_fault_scenario.py, tests/test_turn_budget_scenario.py, tests/test_act_emission_scenario.py, tests/test_refuted_verdict_rereview.py, tests/test_critic_no_verdict_cause.py, tests/test_qa_review_model_note.py, tests/test_crashed_critic_holds_merge.py, tests/test_critic_size_strategy.py, plus the new shared helper

cards.title: The pipeline's embedded shell moves into script files — a workflow step calls a script instead of carrying 23,000 characters of it
cards.description:
`agent-task.yml` is 1,111 lines and one of its steps is a 23,000-character shell script. `qa-review.yml` is over 1,600. `agent-fix.yml` carries two blocks at 17,550 and 16,694 characters. On 2026-09-09 the first of those crossed GitHub's 21,000-character expression ceiling and took the fleet's build lane down for 3h20m ([DRE-3484](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3484/agent-taskyml-is-unparseable-the-report-steps-run-block-crossed)).

[DRE-3484](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3484/agent-taskyml-is-unparseable-the-report-steps-run-block-crossed) made that file **safe** — its script carries no `${{ }}`, so no ceiling applies — and added a guard at 18,000 for the blocks that still interpolate. This card makes them **small**, which is the thing that actually stops the class.

## Why they grew, and why nobody saw it

Every incident adds a few lines and a comment saying why those lines exist. Each addition is small and each is justified. Nothing ever reported the total, so no one was ever asked whether 20,000 characters of shell belongs in a YAML file. The comments are the most valuable thing in there — they carry the history of every failure this fleet has paid for — and they were also, until now, inside the budget.

The pattern is already established in this repo: the same step calls `check_agent_result.py` and `deliver_rescue.py`, real files with real tests. What never got extracted is the glue between those calls, and the glue is what reached 23,000 characters.

## What lands

* The three oversized steps — `agent-task.yml`'s `Report result to Linear`, and `agent-fix.yml`'s `Report` and `Resolve PR, mode, and attempt budget` — each become a script under `scripts/`, invoked by a one-line `run:` with its inputs passed through `env:`. Behaviour is preserved exactly; this is a move, not a rewrite.
* **The knowledge moves with the code, and is re-ordered as it moves.** Those comments are a chronological sediment of incident notes, several of which amend or supersede an earlier one in place. In the script file they become a docstring at the top stating what the script does today, with the incident history below it, each note keeping its card reference. A note that a later note has overtaken is resolved into one statement rather than left as two.
* Each extracted script gets direct tests that call it, replacing the harnesses that today render the YAML and execute the block. See the test-harness card for that half.
* The expression-budget guard from [DRE-3484](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3484/agent-taskyml-is-unparseable-the-report-steps-run-block-crossed) stays as the backstop, and should end up with nothing left to measure.

## Deliberately not in scope

Rewriting the logic, changing behaviour, or touching `merge-gate.yml` (13,794, comfortable). This card is a move plus a documentation pass, and its correctness claim is that nothing changed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each of the three steps is a single `run:` line calling a script, with every input passed via `env:`
- [ ] No `run:` block in any pipeline workflow exceeds 8,000 characters
- [ ] Each script carries a docstring stating current behaviour, and the incident notes below it, each keeping its card reference; no note contradicts another
- [ ] The scenario suites pass unchanged in count — a test that no longer applies is replaced, never deleted to go green
- [ ] The harness passes on the resulting commit before the channel advances

**Files:** .github/workflows/agent-task.yml, .github/workflows/agent-fix.yml, new scripts under scripts/, their tests

cards.title: PROOF: the deploy seam, the client claim and the relay-gh record observed against the live estate
cards.description:
Tests cover the five build cards. This card is the mechanism watched running against the real estate, with what was read, when (PT), and what it said, recorded in the repo so the record merges. The three observations below are also posted to this card with `linear_ops.py proof-observed`.

1. **The deploy seam, both arms, against the real tree and the real ECR.** On `main` after DRE-3474 and DRE-3480 have merged, run `DRY=1 NONINTERACTIVE=1 make deploy-console` by hand: the plan carries the `IngestWsStack: unchanged since <tag>` line and no `cdk deploy IngestWsStack` runs. Then on a throwaway local branch with one whitespace-only commit under `infra/lambda/ingest-ws/`, run the same dry run: the plan names IngestWsStack, the tag it is being compared against and the changed path, and — still DRY — touches nothing. Record both outputs verbatim, with the PT time and the last-deploy tag they were read against, and delete the branch.
2. **The client on the live push channel, after the first real deploy carrying DRE-3475.** Read the backend's App Runner log after that deploy: `starting ws ingest consumer … consumer=__platform__`, a successful connect, and NO fallback warning naming IngestWsStack. Read the `bureau-ingest-ws-connections` table by hand: the console's row carries `tenant=__platform__`. Open the Alerts page: no "Live updates have stopped arriving" row. Record the log lines, the table read and the Alerts state with PT times. This is the platform-claim path still working with the fallback code present in production.
3. **The relay-gh record, live.** On the next `cloud/relay-gh/deploy.sh` run (after DRE-3476 merged), the deploy reads `DEPLOYED_SHA` back off `bureau-github-relay` and cuts `agent-bureau-relay-gh-v1`; `make deploy-lag` then prints a `relay-gh` row carrying that version where previously there was no row at all (DRE-3477). Record the deploy tail and the panel line, PT.

**What is deliberately not observed live, and why.** The degraded arm of the client (a 403 to the platform claim followed by a tenant-claim connect) is not forced against production: watching it would mean un-deploying the live authorizer, which recreates the 2026-09-05 incident on purpose. Its evidence is DRE-3475's fake-server test, and the record says so in those words rather than leaving the arm unmentioned.

The record lives in a new `architecture/forensics/push-channel-seam-2026-09.md` beside the incident forensics that already sit there, with the three observations above as sections and the not-observed arm as a fourth, and merges through an ordinary PR.

**Files:** architecture/forensics/push-channel-seam-2026-09.md

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both arms of the deploy seam observed by hand against the real checkout and live ECR with `DRY=1`, outputs recorded verbatim with PT times and the tag compared against
- [ ] After the first production deploy carrying the fallback, the live backend log, the live connections table and the Alerts page observed and recorded with PT times: platform claim in use, no fallback warning, no live-feed alert
- [ ] The first `agent-bureau-relay-gh-v1` tag observed cut by a real relay-gh deploy and the `relay-gh` row observed in `make deploy-lag` output, recorded with PT times
- [ ] The record states in plain words that the 403-fallback arm was not observed in production and names the test that is its evidence
- [ ] The record is merged to `main` at the path above and the three observations are posted to this card with `proof-observed`

**Blocked by:** DRE-3474, DRE-3475, DRE-3476, DRE-3477, DRE-3480

cards.title: The console deploy ships IngestWsStack in the same run when its seam moved
cards.description:
`infra/deploy-console.sh` runs `cdk deploy` for five stacks (Dns, Release, MigrationTask, Backend, Frontend) and never for `IngestWsStack`, whose Lambdas are the server half of the push channel the backend it rolls out connects to. On 2026-09-05 at 15:41 PT v1.6.17 shipped DRE-3162's client half against an authorizer that had not been deployed, and the console had no live feed for anyone until an operator deployed the stack by hand at 16:13 PT. Nothing in the deploy said so. This card makes the operator deploy read the seam the sibling card declared (`INGEST_WS_PATHS` in `infra/release-console.sh`, which this script sources), ship the stack in the same run, and say what it did with it if the run is killed.

1. Decide beside the image plan, before the `DRY=1` exit so a dry run reports it: the seam moved when `git -C "$ROOT" diff --quiet "$LAST_DEPLOY_TAG" HEAD -- "${INGEST_WS_PATHS[@]}"` exits 1 — the same shape and the same `-C "$ROOT"` rule as `needs_build`; no prior tag counts as moved. Keep the answer in one variable, `INGEST_WS_MOVED` (`1` or `0`), because the trace in step 3 needs it. Print one plan line either way: `IngestWsStack: changed since <tag> (<paths>) — deploying it before the backend rolls` or `IngestWsStack: unchanged since <tag> — not deployed`. Read the array; never restate the two paths in this file.
2. When it moved, deploy it in the same run, AFTER `[4/5] MigrationTaskStack` and BEFORE `release_main` (which is the backend rollout): `node_run infra npx cdk deploy IngestWsStack --exclusively --require-approval never --context allowPlaceholderImage=true`. `--exclusively` is load-bearing: `bin/agent-bureau.ts` gives IngestWsStack `addDependency(backendStack)` for the shared WsIngestToken secret, and without the flag CDK would deploy BackendStack from a placeholder-image template, which is what DRE-2773's tests forbid. No digest exists at this point, so the placeholder context is the one steps [1/5], [2/5] and [4/5] pass. Give the step its own `==> IngestWsStack …` banner and do not renumber the five step banners `test_deploy_console_steps.py` pins. Bracket the call with TWO step markers, the way `release_cdk_apply` brackets its own apply: `release_mark ingest-ws-started` on the line before it and `release_mark ingest-ws-applied` on the line after. Two, not one: a run killed inside the apply and a run that never reached it are different states — CloudFormation goes on finishing the first one server-side (DRE-3269) — and a single marker cannot tell them apart.
3. `deploy_trace` READS the pair. Today its if/elif chain reports on exactly three named markers (`migrated`, `cdk-started`/`cdk-applied`, `rolled-out`) and nothing else, so a marker nobody reads is a marker that does nothing: a run killed mid-IngestWsStack would print the same `BackendStack + FrontendStack NOT started` line as a run that never reached the step. Add one segment to the `DEPLOY INTERRUPTED` line, after `images pushed` and before the migration segment (that is the run order: the stack ships between [4/5] and `release_main`, and the migration runs inside `release_main`), with four states: `INGEST_WS_MOVED=0` → `IngestWsStack unchanged, not needed`; moved and `ingest-ws-started` not reached → `IngestWsStack NOT started`; `ingest-ws-started` reached and `ingest-ws-applied` not → `IngestWsStack update STARTED and NOT confirmed (CloudFormation finishes it server-side; it cannot be cancelled from here)`; `ingest-ws-applied` reached → `IngestWsStack updated`. Same claim discipline as the Backend + Frontend branch beside it: the trace says what its markers know and nothing more. One wording rule: `deploy_trace` sits ABOVE the pre-flights, and `deploy-console-activity-preflight.test.ts` reads the first `cdk deploy` / `docker build` / `docker push` in the file as the first mutating step, so neither the new segment nor a comment on it may spell those tokens — the function's existing comment says why, in the same words.
4. Add `IngestWsStack` to `CONSOLE_STACKS`, the stacks a deploy writes, so the mid-update pre-flight refuses on it too. In the stub world a stack absent from `stacks` answers "does not exist", which the pre-flight treats as not created yet, so the existing tests keep passing.
5. `infra/DEPLOY.md`: one paragraph saying the console deploy now deploys IngestWsStack when its seam moved, the DRY line to read it off, the by-hand recovery command (`cdk deploy IngestWsStack --exclusively` with the placeholder context) for a 2026-09-05-shaped incident, and that a killed run's `DEPLOY INTERRUPTED` line now says whether the stack update was started. Nothing documents that command today.

Tests, in two files, both driven in the existing stub world (`conftest.World`; `diff_files[f"{LAST_DEPLOY_TAG}..HEAD"]` drives the diff with the pathspec prefix matching already in `stubs._git`, and the volta stub records the `cdk deploy` calls):

* New `infra/test/rollback/test_deploy_ingest_ws_seam.py`: (a) a world where `infra/lambda/ingest-ws/authorize.js` changed makes `cdk deploy IngestWsStack --exclusively`, and that call sits after `MigrationTaskStack` and before the first `BackendStack` or `apprunner` call; (b) a world with nothing under the seam changed makes no such call and prints the unchanged line; (c) `DRY=1` prints the seam line and makes no cdk call; (d) `infra/lib/ingest-ws-stack.ts` alone triggers it; (e) a second literal of either seam path in `deploy-console.sh` fails the test. `test_every_cdk_deploy_the_run_makes_can_synth_the_app` and `deploy-console-synth-context.test.ts` will see the new invocation and require the placeholder context; both stay green.
* In `infra/test/rollback/test_deploy_console_steps.py`, beside `test_the_trace_names_the_stack_update_it_left_running` and using that file's `dying_script` fixture (a copy of the script with `kill -TERM $$` after a chosen anchor — the fixture replaces the FIRST occurrence, and each marker occurs once), on `_deployable(world)` plus `diff_files[...] = ["infra/lambda/ingest-ws/authorize.js"]` for the moved worlds: (f) seam moved, killed after `release_mark ingest-ws-started`: the output carries `DEPLOY INTERRUPTED`, `IngestWsStack update STARTED and NOT confirmed`, `migration NOT run`, `BackendStack + FrontendStack NOT started` and `NO tag cut`, and no `apprunner` or `git tag -a` call was made; (g) seam moved, killed after `release_mark cdk-started`: `IngestWsStack updated` and, for Backend + Frontend, `NOT confirmed`; (h) killed after `release_mark images-pushed`, parametrized over the seam moved and unchanged: `IngestWsStack NOT started` for the moved world, `IngestWsStack unchanged, not needed` for the other, and neither prints `STARTED`. The four existing trace tests in that file pass unmodified — they assert substrings, and the anchors they kill at are unchanged.

**Files:** infra/deploy-console.sh, infra/DEPLOY.md, infra/test/rollback/test_deploy_ingest_ws_seam.py, infra/test/rollback/test_deploy_console_steps.py

## Contract

Reads `INGEST_WS_PATHS` from `infra/release-console.sh` (the sibling card's declaration: the two literals `infra/lambda/ingest-ws` and `infra/lib/ingest-ws-stack.ts`). The step markers are `ingest-ws-started` and `ingest-ws-applied`, written with `release_mark` and read with `release_reached` (both defined in `infra/release-console.sh`), and only `infra/deploy-console.sh` writes or reads them. The plan line begins `IngestWsStack:`. The trace segment's four literals are the ones in step 3.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A deploy from a tree where `infra/lambda/ingest-ws/**` or `infra/lib/ingest-ws-stack.ts` changed since the last console tag runs `cdk deploy IngestWsStack --exclusively` after MigrationTaskStack and before the backend rollout — driven in the stub world and asserted on the recorded call order, not on the script text
- [ ] A deploy where neither changed makes no IngestWsStack call and the plan says `IngestWsStack: unchanged since <tag>`
- [ ] `DRY=1` prints the IngestWsStack plan line and makes no `cdk deploy` call
- [ ] A run killed inside the IngestWsStack apply prints a `DEPLOY INTERRUPTED` line saying `IngestWsStack update STARTED and NOT confirmed`; killed before the step with the seam moved it says `IngestWsStack NOT started`; with the seam unchanged it says `IngestWsStack unchanged, not needed`; killed after the apply it says `IngestWsStack updated` — driven with the killed-script fixture and asserted on the trace output
- [ ] The seam paths are read from `INGEST_WS_PATHS`; a test fails on a second literal in `infra/deploy-console.sh`
- [ ] `IngestWsStack` is in `CONSOLE_STACKS`; the two suites `infra/test/rollback/` and `infra/test/*.test.ts` stay green with no step banner renumbered, the four existing trace tests and `deploy-console-activity-preflight.test.ts` unmodified
- [ ] `infra/DEPLOY.md` documents the seam, the by-hand recovery command and the trace line

**Blocked by:** DRE-3474

cards.title: relay-gh is a deployable surface: deploy-lag, the console panel and the proof runner can name it
cards.description:
`scripts/check_deploy_lag.py` declares four deployable surfaces (console, website, relay, pipeline-channel) and `console/backend/deploy_lag.py` restates them for the console's Pending-release panel (the backend image cannot import the toolkit; `console/backend/tests/test_deploy_lag.py` drives both copies off one fake and fails if they disagree). `cloud/relay-gh/` is in neither. So the three readers — `make deploy-lag`, the console's deploy rows, and the proof runner's DRE-3000 criterion ("which deployable surfaces this phase's merged work touches", which `prove_phase.surface_paths` reads straight off `SURFACES`) — report a pull request that changes the GitHub relay as touching no deployable surface at all. The epic's third item — a change spanning the relays names the deploys it needs, and the check can hold it to that — is impossible while the list cannot name one of the two relays.

Add `Surface("relay-gh", ("cloud/relay-gh/",), ("agent-bureau-relay-gh-v*",))` to BOTH copies, after `relay`. The glob is the prefix the sibling card's deploy writes, verbatim. Prefix matching already keeps `cloud/relay/` and `cloud/relay-gh/` apart because the prefixes carry their trailing slash (`prove_phase.surfaces_touched` documents why). Until the first relay-gh tag is cut the row reads UNKNOWN, "no deployment record exists", which is the honest answer and the one the relay row gave until its own first tag.

Deliberately NOT changed: `infra/lambda/ingest-ws/` stays inside the `console` surface's `infra/` prefix. Once the sibling deploy cards land, the console deploy ships IngestWsStack whenever that seam moved and the train defers when it cannot, so the console tag IS that stack's record; a separate `ingest-ws` surface would have no record of its own and would fail `test_no_surface_carries_an_excuse_for_having_no_record`.

Tests, in `scripts/test_check_deploy_lag.py`: `test_every_deployable_surface_is_declared` names five surfaces; `test_each_surface_names_the_paths_that_affect_it` and the no-excuse test pass for the new row; a test that `prove_phase.surfaces_touched(["cloud/relay-gh/lambda_function.py"])` is `["relay-gh"]` and `["cloud/relay/lambda_function.py"]` is still `["relay"]`; and a test that reads the single `TAG_PREFIX` declaration out of `cloud/relay-gh/deploy.sh` and asserts the `relay-gh` surface's glob is that prefix plus `*` (the same check `scripts/test_relay_deploy_record.py` makes for the Linear relay, written here so this card and the sibling own disjoint files — which is also why this card is blocked on the sibling: the prefix it reads has to exist). `console/backend/tests/test_deploy_lag.py`'s agreement test covers the new row in both copies.

**Files:** scripts/check_deploy_lag.py, console/backend/deploy_lag.py, scripts/test_check_deploy_lag.py, console/backend/tests/test_deploy_lag.py

## Contract

The surface is named `relay-gh`, its path prefix is `cloud/relay-gh/` (trailing slash), and its tag glob is `agent-bureau-relay-gh-v*` — the glob form of the `TAG_PREFIX="agent-bureau-relay-gh-v"` the sibling card declares in `cloud/relay-gh/deploy.sh`. Both copies of `SURFACES` carry the identical record.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `make deploy-lag` prints a `relay-gh` row (UNKNOWN before the first tag, a version after), and the console's Pending-release rows carry the same row — pinned by the agreement test that drives both copies off one fake
- [ ] `prove_phase.surfaces_touched` returns `["relay-gh"]` for a file under `cloud/relay-gh/` and still `["relay"]` for a file under `cloud/relay/` — pinned
- [ ] `test_every_deployable_surface_is_declared` names exactly console, website, relay, relay-gh, pipeline-channel
- [ ] The `relay-gh` glob is pinned against the `TAG_PREFIX` read out of `cloud/relay-gh/deploy.sh`
- [ ] `infra/lambda/ingest-ws/` is not declared as a separate surface, and the reason is stated in a comment beside `SURFACES` in both copies

**Blocked by:** DRE-3476

cards.title: The GitHub relay's deploy records which commit is live, and its default PEM secret name is one that exists
cards.description:
`cloud/relay-gh/deploy.sh` deploys the GitHub relay Lambda (`bureau-github-relay`) and records nothing: no `DEPLOYED_SHA` on the function, no git tag. `cloud/relay/deploy.sh` closed exactly this gap for the Linear relay in DRE-2789 — it stamps `DEPLOYED_SHA`/`DEPLOYED_AT` into the function's environment, reads them back off the live function after the update, refuses to tag on a disagreeing read-back, and cuts and pushes an annotated `agent-bureau-relay-v<N>` tag LAST, after the whole deploy succeeded. So a merged relay-gh change sits undeployed with nothing able to say so; `make deploy-lag` cannot even ask. That is the "merged is not deployed" shape one Lambda over, and the GitHub relay was the second of the three deploys the 2026-09-05 recovery had to do by hand. Copy the mechanism from `cloud/relay/deploy.sh`, do not rebuild it: exactly one `TAG_PREFIX="agent-bureau-relay-gh-v"` declaration, the same dirty-input guard, the same read-back, the same ordering (update, read back, tag last).

Second defect, same file, found in the same recovery: the script's default `PEM_SECRET_NAME` (`bureau/relay-gh/github-app-pem`) names a secret that has never existed. The live function has always used the Linear relay's shared `bureau/relay/github-app-pem`, and the 2026-09-05 redeploy only worked because the operator passed `PEM_SECRET_NAME=bureau/relay/github-app-pem` by hand. Default to the secret that exists — the one `cloud/relay/deploy.sh` upserts — and say so in the header. The env override stays.

Tests, credential-less source-shape assertions in `scripts/test_relay_deploy_record.py`: parametrize `DEPLOY` and the `script` fixture over the two relay deploy scripts (`cloud/relay/deploy.sh`, `cloud/relay-gh/deploy.sh`) so the 12 existing assertions — the stamp, the read-back after the update and before the tag, the annotated tag cut last, the refusal on a disagreeing read-back, the series continuation, and the rest — hold for both. The one exception is `test_the_panel_reads_exactly_the_prefix_this_script_writes`: leave it relay-only here, because it reads `check_deploy_lag.SURFACES` and the `relay-gh` surface is the sibling card's, which pins the relay-gh prefix against the surface in its own test file. Add one test that the relay-gh default PEM secret name equals the name `cloud/relay/deploy.sh` upserts.

**Files:** cloud/relay-gh/deploy.sh, scripts/test_relay_deploy_record.py

## Contract

`TAG_PREFIX="agent-bureau-relay-gh-v"`, declared exactly once in `cloud/relay-gh/deploy.sh`; the tags it cuts match the glob `agent-bureau-relay-gh-v*`, which the sibling surface card declares in `check_deploy_lag.SURFACES` and `console/backend/deploy_lag.py` verbatim. The environment keys are `DEPLOYED_SHA` and `DEPLOYED_AT`, the same names the Linear relay uses.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `cloud/relay-gh/deploy.sh` stamps `DEPLOYED_SHA`/`DEPLOYED_AT` into the function environment, reads them back off the live function after the update, refuses to cut a tag on a mismatch, and cuts and pushes an annotated `agent-bureau-relay-gh-v<N>` tag last — pinned by the 12 source-shape tests, now running over both relay deploy scripts
- [ ] Exactly one `TAG_PREFIX` declaration in the script, and it is `agent-bureau-relay-gh-v`
- [ ] The default `PEM_SECRET_NAME` is `bureau/relay/github-app-pem`, pinned by a test against the name `cloud/relay/deploy.sh` upserts
- [ ] The existing relay tests stay green: the 12 in `scripts/test_relay_deploy_record.py` and `console/backend/tests/test_relay_deploy_runtime.py`

cards.title: The push-channel client falls back to the tenant claim on a 403 and names the deploy that is missing
cards.description:
`console/backend/ws_ingest.py` dials the ingest WebSocket with `?consumer=__platform__` (DRE-3162). A server whose `IngestWsStack` predates that claim answers the handshake with HTTP 403 (`websockets.exceptions.InvalidStatus`, `response.status_code == 403`), and today `consume_forever` treats that like any dial failure: log an exception, back off to the 60-second cap, retry the same claim forever. From 15:52 PT on 2026-09-05 that loop was the console's entire live feed. The client should degrade to what it did before DRE-3162, say once which deploy is missing, and go back to the platform claim by itself the moment the server accepts it.

Build, in `ws_ingest.py`:

1. A second dial URL, `_tenant_fallback_url(url)`, which appends `tenant=<tenancy.OPERATOR_TENANT_ID>` to the base URL (respecting an existing `?`, as `_connect_url` does). That is the claim this client used before DRE-3162; the authorizer mints a `?tenant=` value verbatim for a token-bearing client, so it works against both the old and the new server. `_connect_url` is unchanged and still never carries `tenant=` — the tests pinning that stay exactly as they are.
2. Classification: `_platform_claim_rejected(exc) -> bool`, True for an exception carrying a `response` whose `status_code` is 403 (check by attribute, so the unit suite still imports no `websockets`); anything else is an ordinary dial failure.
3. The connect seam gains a keyword-only `claim` argument with the two literal values `"platform"` and `"tenant"`, default `"platform"`. `_default_connect` composes the dial URL from it (`_connect_url` or `_tenant_fallback_url`); `url=` stays the raw base URL, so `test_start_ws_ingest_ignores_a_leftover_tenant_env_var` still reads it. The `_fake_connect` seam in the tests already takes `**kwargs`.
4. The loop rule in `consume_forever`: an iteration's first dial is on the platform claim. If that dial is rejected with a 403 to the platform claim, dial again IMMEDIATELY on the tenant claim, in the same iteration, with no backoff sleep between the two. Because a reconnect starts from the platform claim again, the next attempt after the operator deploys IngestWsStack lands on the platform claim with no restart — the shape observed live at 16:13 PT on 2026-09-05. A 403 to the tenant claim, or any other failure, is the ordinary backoff path; there is no third claim.
5. ONE warning per process, on the first fallback, and it names the missing deploy: `ws ingest: server rejected the platform claim (HTTP 403) — IngestWsStack is not deployed at a commit that accepts consumer=__platform__; falling back to the tenant claim (tenant=<id>), which carries only this tenant's repos. Deploy IngestWsStack: make deploy-console, or cdk deploy IngestWsStack --exclusively.` Later fallbacks in the same process log at debug, so the log does not carry one warning a minute the way it carried one error a minute. One `log.info` when a later dial succeeds on the platform claim again. State the fallback's retirement in the docstring where it lives: it goes when the tenant claim itself is retired, which is a later card, not this epic.

Tests, two levels:

* `console/backend/tests/test_ws_ingest.py` (seam level, no network): a `_fake_connect` whose first session raises a 403-shaped exception for `claim="platform"` and yields a heartbeat and a Linear envelope for `claim="tenant"`. Assert the tenant dial happens in the same iteration with no `sleep` call between the two dials (the injected `sleep` records calls), the two frames are ingested, exactly one WARNING record naming `IngestWsStack` (caplog), and the next iteration dials `claim="platform"` first again. A `ConnectionError` on the platform claim does not fall back. A 403 on the tenant claim does not loop.
* A new `console/backend/tests/test_ws_ingest_claim_fallback.py`, the fake server this epic asks for: `pytest.importorskip("websockets")` (the backend's `requirements.txt` carries it, so CI runs it), an in-process `websockets.asyncio.server.serve` on 127.0.0.1 whose `process_request` answers 403 when the query carries `consumer=__platform__` and accepts `tenant=<OPERATOR_TENANT_ID>`, then sends one heartbeat and one Linear envelope. Run `consume_forever` with the REAL `_default_connect`, bounded `iterations`, backoff 0.01, an injected `fetch_updated_since` and `fetch_linear`. Assert the server saw the platform handshake first and the tenant handshake second, the two frames landed (`store.ingest_health()` frame stamps), and one warning. A second server that accepts the platform claim: first handshake succeeds, no warning, no tenant handshake.

**Files:** console/backend/ws_ingest.py, console/backend/tests/test_ws_ingest.py, console/backend/tests/test_ws_ingest_claim_fallback.py

## Contract

The connect seam's keyword is `claim`, with the literal values `"platform"` and `"tenant"`. The fallback query parameter is `tenant=<tenancy.OPERATOR_TENANT_ID>`. cards.title: The push-channel seam is declared once, and the release train defers on it
cards.description:
The push channel's server half is `IngestWsStack`: the Lambdas under `infra/lambda/ingest-ws/` and the stack in `infra/lib/ingest-ws-stack.ts`. No console release path can see that seam today. The release train (`infra/release-console.sh`) defers when the CDK app moved — `CDK_APP_PATHS` is infra/bin, infra/lib, infra/cdk.json — so a change to the stack file already defers it, but a change confined to the Lambda source under `infra/lambda/ingest-ws/` is invisible to it. On 2026-09-05 the authorizer under that directory was the half that had not been deployed when v1.6.17 shipped the client, and the console had no live feed from 15:41 PT to 16:13 PT.

This card is the seam's ONE declaration, and the train's half of reading it. The sibling card teaches the operator deploy (`infra/deploy-console.sh`, which sources this file) to read the same array and deploy the stack, which is why that card is blocked on this one.

1. In `infra/release-console.sh`, beside `CDK_APP_PATHS`, declare `INGEST_WS_PATHS=("infra/lambda/ingest-ws" "infra/lib/ingest-ws-stack.ts")` with a comment naming the incident and the sibling reader.
2. The deferral in `release_main` reads `CDK_APP_PATHS` plus `INGEST_WS_PATHS`. A change confined to `infra/lambda/ingest-ws/` since the newest console tag defers the train the way an `infra/lib` change does: exit 0, no tag, one `deferred:` line — and that line names `IngestWsStack` when the seam is the reason (`deferred: IngestWsStack changed since <tag> — run make deploy-console`). The existing `CDK_APP_NOT_A_DEFERRAL` rule (`infra/lib/release-stack.ts`) is untouched.

Tests, in `infra/test/rollback/test_release_console.py`, driven in the existing stub world (`diff_files[f"{LAST_DEPLOY_TAG}..HEAD"]` drives the diff): a world whose only change is `infra/lambda/ingest-ws/authorize.js` defers with a `deferred:` line naming IngestWsStack, exit 0, no tag; a world whose only change is `console/backend/app.py` still releases; the three existing deferral tests stay green. A source-shape test that `INGEST_WS_PATHS` is declared exactly once in `infra/release-console.sh` and holds the two literals.

**Files:** infra/release-console.sh, infra/test/rollback/test_release_console.py

## Contract

`INGEST_WS_PATHS` is a bash array declared exactly once, in `infra/release-console.sh`, holding the two literals `infra/lambda/ingest-ws` and `infra/lib/ingest-ws-stack.ts`. The sibling deploy card reads it and never restates it. The deferral line for this reason begins `deferred: IngestWsStack changed since`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The release train defers, exit 0 with one `deferred:` line naming IngestWsStack and no tag cut, on a change confined to `infra/lambda/ingest-ws/` — driven in the stub world
- [ ] A change confined to `console/backend/` still releases with no `deferred:` line
- [ ] `INGEST_WS_PATHS` is declared exactly once in `infra/release-console.sh` with the two literals above, pinned by a test
- [ ] The three existing deferral tests in `test_release_console.py` pass unmodified

The deferral this card adds mirrors the `CDK_APP_PATHS` one exactly: exit 0, no tag, one `deferred:` line, which the reusable train records as a `no-op` and the run concludes `success`. That is the right behaviour for the train (it cannot run `cdk deploy`, so deferring to the hand deploy is the only honest act), and the sibling card DRE-3480 is what makes the hand deploy ship the stack. cards.title: The merge gate says "this pull request is a draft" instead of dying on GitHub's raw error — and an agent PR handed to the critic is not left in draft
cards.description:
The merge gate names a draft pull request as the reason it cannot merge, instead of failing the run with GitHub's raw `Pull Request is still a draft (mergePullRequest)` — and an agent PR that is ready for the gate is not left in draft.

## Why

2026-09-08 21:26–21:43 PT, bureau-pipeline #323 (DRE-3389): every check green, the critic APPROVEd the head, `mergeStateStatus` CLEAN, and the gate decided correctly — `decision=merge`, `reason=CI green + critic APPROVE bound to 09b52e93` — then died on `GraphQL: Pull Request is still a draft (mergePullRequest)` and exited 1. Nothing on the PR, the card or the console said "draft": the console read it as waiting at the merge gate, the card sat in Triage, and the CEO asked twice why it was stuck. It had been opened as a draft by `agent-bureau-bot-4` and nobody marked it ready. The operator ran `gh pr ready 323` at 21:41 PT and it merged two minutes later on the next gate dispatch.

Two halves, both small:

1. **The gate's report.** `scripts/merge_gate.py` should read `isDraft` with the other merge conditions and, when true, print a held reason in its own vocabulary — `held=draft — this pull request is a draft; mark it ready and the gate merges it` — and exit 0 (a hold, not a failure), the way it holds for a missing verdict. A red run for a state the author controls reads as a broken pipeline.
2. **The author.** A build agent that opens its PR as a draft (`agent-task.yml`'s `gh pr create --draft`, or the draft-held path DRE-3271/3272 introduced) must mark it ready when it hands the PR to the critic — or never open it as a draft in the first place. Read which of the two shapes applies before changing anything: DRE-3272 deliberately renders a draft as "Draft — held", so a draft that is genuinely held must keep that reading; this card is only about the one that is finished and waiting.

## What lands

* `scripts/merge_gate.py`: `isDraft` in the PR read; a `draft` held-reason ahead of the merge attempt; exit 0. A test with a draft-but-otherwise-mergeable fixture asserts the reason string and the exit code, and a second asserts a non-draft PR is unaffected.
* `.github/workflows/agent-task.yml` (or wherever the PR is opened): the PR is opened ready, or marked ready at the same step that posts `🤖 PR opened`. If the draft is deliberate for the DRE-3271 held case, leave that path alone and say so in the PR body.
* The console (agent-bureau `console/backend/enrich.py`): a draft PR whose checks are green and whose critic APPROVEd already reads `DRAFT_HELD` (DRE-3272) — confirm it does and that the row says "Draft — held", not "waiting at the merge gate". If it does not, that is the third piece and belongs here.

**Files:** bureau-pipeline scripts/merge_gate.py, tests/test_merge_gate*.py, .github/workflows/agent-task.yml; agent-bureau console/backend/enrich.py (confirm only)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A draft PR that is otherwise mergeable produces a gate run that exits 0 and prints the draft held-reason; a test pins the string and the code
- [ ] An agent-opened PR handed to the critic is not in draft (or, if deliberately held, the console reads it as "Draft — held")
- [ ] Replaying #323's state through the gate's decision function yields the draft hold, not `decision=merge`

cards.title: The Mac mini runner pool runs under a dedicated standard account, not the CEO's admin login — bootstrap moves cleanly between users, and the runbook says how
cards.description:
**Why.** The pool went live on 2026-09-08 ([DRE-3351](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3351/operator-stand-up-the-ephemeral-linux-runner-pool-on-the-mac-mini-and)) inside the CEO's own admin account on the mini: Colima, the LaunchAgents, the runner image and `~/.config/bureau-runners.env` all live in that login. * `bootstrap-mini.sh`: nothing user-specific is hard-coded today (verify and pin with a test that no path under `/Users/<name>` appears in the scripts).

cards.title: PROOF: the pin gate refuses a float on a real PR, every roster repo's pins are read live from two tokens, and the SHAs re-resolve to their tags — recorded in the repo
cards.description:
Proof that the pins hold against real state, not a green suite. All seven siblings ship a mechanism — a checker, a gate, a fleet column, five pinned repos; this card watches the seven run against the live repos and writes what it saw into this repo, so the record merges. An operator runs it at an interactive session with a token that can read all six roster repos (a build agent's token reads four of them as 404, which is itself one of the observations).

**Observe, by hand, and record each with the command, the PT timestamp and the exact line read:**

1. **The gate on** `main`**.** `make check-pins` on a fresh checkout of `main` after DRE-3441 merged: exit 0 and the `OK: <n> third-party action sites …` line verbatim, with the `main` sha it was read at. `make check-channel` exit 0 beside it — the channel refs were not touched.
2. **A float put back is refused, locally and in CI.** On a scratch branch, change ONE line back to `actions/checkout@v5`: `make check-pins` exits 1 naming `<file>:<line>` (verbatim). Push it and open a throwaway pull request titled `PROOF DRE-3419 — do not merge`: the `Lint · Guards` check goes red on the `Third-party action pin gate` step (run link, the failing line from the log). Close the PR unmerged and delete the branch; record the PR number. This is the same PR the DEMO card shows the CEO, so keep it open until the demo has happened if the two are run together.
3. **The SHAs are the tags' commits, re-resolved live.** For each of the seven actions in DRE-3441's PR-body table, `git ls-remote --tags https://github.com/<owner>/<repo> 'refs/tags/<tag>' 'refs/tags/<tag>^{}'` on the day of proof: the pinned SHA equals the dereferenced commit (or the tag has since moved, which is recorded as a fact, not a failure — the pin is doing its job).
4. **The fleet reads every repo.** `make check-channel-fleet` with the operator's token: the six `pins:` readings verbatim, plus the outstanding heading and any MIXED problem lines. Then the same command from a token shaped like a build agent's (this repo plus public bureau-pipeline only — the planner's token on 2026-09-09 is the reference): four rows read `pins: UNKNOWN`, never `none` or `pinned`. Record both outputs and which token produced each.
5. **The mirrors landed.** For each of DRE-3443, DRE-3444, DRE-3445 and DRE-3446: the merged PR (`gh pr view <n> -R <repo> --json mergedAt,url`), and the fleet row for that repo reading `pins: pinned` — or the recorded reason it does not (agent-bureau-demo handed back with no third-party site is a valid reason, and reads `pins: none`).
6. **The parity tether's state.** `python3 -m pytest scripts/test_check_action_pins.py -q -rs`: either `SKIPPED … DRE-3418 has not landed bureau-pipeline's copy yet`, or the byte-equality test passing because it has. Record which, and bureau-pipeline's fleet row (`MIXED` until DRE-3418 merges, `pinned` after).
7. **Dependabot still proposes.** The first monthly `github-actions` Dependabot run in this repo after DRE-3441 merged: the Dependabot log line (`Insights → Dependency graph → Dependabot`) saying a grouped PR was opened or nothing was to bump; if a PR opened, the diff shows a new SHA AND an updated `# vX.Y.Z` comment on the same line. If the monthly window has not come by the day of proof, say so with the next scheduled date rather than leaving it out.

Write all seven into `architecture/audits/third-party-action-pins-proof-2026-09.md` in the shape of `architecture/audits/2026-09-browser-unknown-direction-guard-proof.md` — what was read, when, what it said — and open a PR carrying only that file.
