cards.title: Pin every third-party GitHub action in dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau-demo to a commit SHA with its version in a comment — the DRE-3419 mirror
cards.description:
Every third-party GitHub action in `dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau-demo`'s workflows is pinned to the full commit SHA of the release its floating tag resolves to today, with the version in a trailing comment — the DRE-3419 mirror for this repo, the same route DRE-2692 used to reach the six consumer repos once instead of six times. Why: on 2026-09-08 a vendor's floating `v1` tag moved and the fleet's Claude jobs died for 72 minutes (DRE-3416); the engine's own copies are pinned by DRE-3418 and agent-bureau's by DRE-3441, and this repo's `.github/workflows/` is what remains for `agent-bureau-demo`.

This repo is the fleet's throwaway canary (8 stubs, no guard yet) — if the scan finds no third-party site at all, that is a real result: post the scan output on the card and hand it back as a blocker, because an empty diff is not a pull request (standards/engineering.md).

**Scan first — the inventory was not readable from the planner's token on 2026-09-09.** Run over every file in `.github/workflows/`:

```
grep -nE '^\s*(-\s*)?uses:' .github/workflows/*.yml .github/workflows/*.yaml 2>/dev/null
```

A site is THIRD-PARTY unless its value starts with `./` (a local action), `docker://`, or `dreadnought-foundry/` — those `@stable` references are the release channel, symbolic by design, guarded by this repo's canonical pipeline-channel guard, and they must not change (nor must any `pipeline_ref: stable`). Post the inventory on the card as the first heartbeat. **Bound:** a consumer repo is expected to hold well under 40 third-party sites; if the scan finds more than 40 third-party sites, stop, post the count, and hand the card back to be split by workflow file rather than building it.

**Resolve each tag to a COMMIT, not a tag object.** For every third-party site still on a symbolic ref:

```
git ls-remote --tags https://github.com/<owner>/<repo> 'refs/tags/<tag>' 'refs/tags/<tag>^{}'
```

If a `^{}` line appears the tag is annotated: the `^{}` sha is the commit to pin and the bare sha is a tag object Actions will not resolve (`aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4` was that case on 2026-09-09). Then find the full `v<MAJOR>.<MINOR>.<PATCH>` tag at the same commit (`git ls-remote --tags … | grep <sha>`) for the comment. Do not change majors: `@v4` pins to v4's current commit, never to v5's. A site that is already a 40-hex SHA but has no version comment gains the comment only.

**The pinned line, exactly** (the grammar DRE-3440's checker enforces in agent-bureau; there is no checker in this repo, so the critic checks the diff against it):

```
uses: <owner>/<repo>[/<path>]@<40 lowercase hex chars>   # v<MAJOR>.<MINOR>.<PATCH>
```

**Record, do not change, this repo's Dependabot posture.** In the PR body say whether `.github/dependabot.yml` exists and whether it has a `github-actions` entry. With one, Dependabot reads the `# vX.Y.Z` comment and proposes minor/patch bumps as new SHA plus comment; without one the pins stay where they are until a human moves them — either is acceptable for this card, and enabling Dependabot in a repo is its own boundary card (DRE-2047: a dependabot-actor run gets an empty secrets store). Answer vendor-boundary questions 1–5 for a Dependabot bump PR in the PR body if the entry exists.

**Files:** dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau-demo/.github/workflows/ci.yml, and every other file under dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau-demo/.github/workflows/ that carries a third-party `uses:` (named in the PR body from the scan; nothing else in the repo)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] After the change, `grep -nE '^\s*(-\s*)?uses:' .github/workflows/*` shows every third-party site as `@<40 lowercase hex>` followed by a `# v<MAJOR>.<MINOR>.<PATCH>` comment, and the PR body quotes that output
- [ ] Every `dreadnought-foundry/…@stable` line and every `pipeline_ref: stable` is byte-identical to before, and this repo's pipeline-channel guard is green on the PR
- [ ] The PR body carries a tag → commit → version table, one row per action, with the resolution date, and the SHAs are the dereferenced commits of annotated tags where those apply
- [ ] The PR body records this repo's Dependabot posture for `github-actions` (entry present / absent / no config) without changing it
- [ ] CI is green on the PR — a mistyped SHA fails at checkout, which is the proof the pins resolve
- [ ] The PR is named in DRE-3419's close-out comment (the operator's step, not this card's — but the branch is `agent/DRE-<this card>-<slug>` and the PR title carries the card id, so it can be)

**Blocked by:** DRE-3441

cards.title: Pin every third-party GitHub action in EveryBite/atlas to a commit SHA with its version in a comment — the DRE-3419 mirror
cards.description:
Every third-party GitHub action in `EveryBite/atlas`'s workflows is pinned to the full commit SHA of the release its floating tag resolves to today, with the version in a trailing comment — the DRE-3419 mirror for this repo, the same route DRE-2692 used to reach the six consumer repos once instead of six times. Why: on 2026-09-08 a vendor's floating `v1` tag moved and the fleet's Claude jobs died for 72 minutes (DRE-3416); the engine's own copies are pinned by DRE-3418 and agent-bureau's by DRE-3441, and this repo's `.github/workflows/` is what remains for `atlas`.

This repo is outside the dreadnought-foundry org — its Actions run cross-org, and it carries the canonical Python channel guard (DRE-2693), which must stay green.

**Scan first — the inventory was not readable from the planner's token on 2026-09-09.** Run over every file in `.github/workflows/`:

```
grep -nE '^\s*(-\s*)?uses:' .github/workflows/*.yml .github/workflows/*.yaml 2>/dev/null
```

A site is THIRD-PARTY unless its value starts with `./` (a local action), `docker://`, or `dreadnought-foundry/` — those `@stable` references are the release channel, symbolic by design, guarded by this repo's canonical pipeline-channel guard, and they must not change (nor must any `pipeline_ref: stable`). Post the inventory on the card as the first heartbeat. **Bound:** a consumer repo is expected to hold well under 40 third-party sites; if the scan finds more than 40 third-party sites, stop, post the count, and hand the card back to be split by workflow file rather than building it.

**Resolve each tag to a COMMIT, not a tag object.** For every third-party site still on a symbolic ref:

```
git ls-remote --tags https://github.com/<owner>/<repo> 'refs/tags/<tag>' 'refs/tags/<tag>^{}'
```

If a `^{}` line appears the tag is annotated: the `^{}` sha is the commit to pin and the bare sha is a tag object Actions will not resolve (`aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4` was that case on 2026-09-09). Then find the full `v<MAJOR>.<MINOR>.<PATCH>` tag at the same commit (`git ls-remote --tags … | grep <sha>`) for the comment. Do not change majors: `@v4` pins to v4's current commit, never to v5's. A site that is already a 40-hex SHA but has no version comment gains the comment only.

**The pinned line, exactly** (the grammar DRE-3440's checker enforces in agent-bureau; there is no checker in this repo, so the critic checks the diff against it):

```
uses: <owner>/<repo>[/<path>]@<40 lowercase hex chars>   # v<MAJOR>.<MINOR>.<PATCH>
```

**Record, do not change, this repo's Dependabot posture.** In the PR body say whether `.github/dependabot.yml` exists and whether it has a `github-actions` entry. With one, Dependabot reads the `# vX.Y.Z` comment and proposes minor/patch bumps as new SHA plus comment; without one the pins stay where they are until a human moves them — either is acceptable for this card, and enabling Dependabot in a repo is its own boundary card (DRE-2047: a dependabot-actor run gets an empty secrets store). Answer vendor-boundary questions 1–5 for a Dependabot bump PR in the PR body if the entry exists.

**Files:** EveryBite/atlas/.github/workflows/ci.yml, and every other file under EveryBite/atlas/.github/workflows/ that carries a third-party `uses:` (named in the PR body from the scan; nothing else in the repo)

cards.title: The medic holds after one retry on an environment crash that will recur (no Claude binary, dead credential) instead of re-dispatching into the same wall every sweep
cards.description:
The medic and the crashed-review re-dispatch recognise an environment crash that will recur — the runner never got a working Claude ("native binary not found", the installer signature) — and HOLD after one retry with the reason named, instead of re-dispatching into the same wall every sweep.

## Why

2026-09-08 (DRE-3416): the critic died in 13 s on every run. `medic_classify.py` correctly called it an infra crash ("NOT a code rejection") and `crashed-review-redispatch` re-ran it — into the identical crash, on every PR, every sweep, for 72 minutes: #2367, #2369, #2370 each collected two or three "could not run" receipts and an Agent Fix run that skipped. Each re-dispatch cost a runner-minute and a review round's worth of noise and told nobody anything new. A crash whose cause is the runner's environment (no Claude binary, a dead credential, an Anthropic 5xx storm) is not cured by trying again in the same environment — the second identical failure is the proof. The retry that IS right (a transient 429, a sandbox blip) stays: one retry, then hold.

**CEO's decision 2026-09-08 16:40 PT: do it, fast-tracked.**

## What lands

* `scripts/medic_classify.py`: a class `environment-crash` with the signatures that mean "the runner cannot run Claude": `Claude Code native binary not found`, `executable_not_found`, the `is_error`/1-turn/$0 credential shape, `authentication_error` — each with a one-line plain-English meaning and the check that confirms it (the vendor action's tag SHA; `make cred-doctor`).
* Re-dispatch budget for that class: **one** retry per head; on the second identical crash, `review_rerun.py` / the medic posts ONE receipt — `🛑 reviewer cannot run on this runner — <signature> — twice on <sha>; holding, nothing re-dispatched. Check: <the confirming command>` — carries `📎 pipeline-act: reviewer-environment-hold` (new act in `config/pipeline-acts.json`; console ACTS mirrored, DRE-3081 rule), and stops. The `reviewer-down` fleet alarm (sibling card) reads these.
* Release: the first successful critic verdict anywhere in the fleet (or an operator "re-review" act) clears the hold — the sweep re-dispatches held heads once, oldest first, capped per sweep.
* Tests: two identical `native binary not found` crashes → one hold receipt, no third dispatch; a 429 then a success → no hold; a hold then a fleet success → exactly one re-dispatch.

**Files:** bureau-pipeline scripts/medic_classify.py, scripts/review_rerun.py, scripts/reconcile.py (release), config/pipeline-acts.json, tests/test_medic_environment_hold.py; agent-bureau console/backend/receipts.py ACTS mirror

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Replaying #2370's run history (3 identical crashes 15:36–16:11 PT) yields one hold receipt after the second and no third dispatch
- [ ] A transient (one crash, then success) never holds
- [ ] `pipeline-acts.json` and the console's ACTS agree; the hold renders in the console as "recovering — held, reason named", never as "fix agent working"

cards.title: No token ever enters a runner container — the host mints a just-in-time runner config per container from the org API, so a job with sudo finds nothing in /proc/1/environ worth taking
cards.description:
**Why.** Today each runner container starts with `ACCESS_TOKEN` (the fine-grained PAT, org permission "Self-hosted runners: Read and write") in its environment; the base image trades it for a registration token and `export -n`s it before the job starts. That keeps it out of the job's inherited environment, but jobs run with passwordless sudo, and root can read the entrypoint's original environment from `/proc/1/environ`. Found while building [DRE-3396](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3396/a-job-on-the-mac-mini-pool-cannot-reach-the-ceos-home-folder-his). The blast radius is bounded (that permission can register and remove runners, nothing else), but a secret that never enters the container cannot be read from it.

**The change.** `start-runners.sh` (host side, where the PAT already lives in `~/.config/bureau-runners.env`) mints one just-in-time runner configuration per container with `POST /orgs/dreadnought-foundry/actions/runners/generate-jitconfig` (`name`, `runner_group_id` 3, `labels ["bureau-mini"]`, `work_folder`), and passes only the returned `encoded_jit_config` to the container; the runner starts with `run.sh --jitconfig <value>` and is single-use by construction, which also removes the base image's SIGTERM-deregistration dance and the stale-Offline-row problem. The PAT never leaves the host. Compose `restart: always` no longer fits (each container needs a fresh config), so the supervisor becomes a small host loop or a per-container systemd-style unit under launchd: keep N running, mint on each start. Check first whether `myoung34/github-runner` supports a jitconfig path or whether the image switches to `ghcr.io/actions/actions-runner` plus our tool layer.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `docker inspect` of a running runner shows no `ACCESS_TOKEN` and no registration token in `Config.Env`; a test drives the supervisor against a stub `gh` and asserts the container run command carries only the JIT config
- [ ] A drained pool leaves no Offline rows on the org runner list
- [ ] The README's security section states the new bound: nothing in the container can register or remove runners

**Files:** `scripts/runners/start-runners.sh`, `scripts/runners/docker-compose.yml` (or its replacement), `scripts/runners/Dockerfile`, `scripts/runners/README.md`, `scripts/test_runners_bootstrap.py`

cards.description:
The console shows a `hand-built` card in Todo as **the operator's turn** — on the board, the One River rows, the who-acts-next banner and the actor key — instead of "queued", so the Todo column becomes the person's queue once the sweep starts putting operator cards there.

## Why

Once DRE-3341 (relay honours `hand-built`) and the sweep card (operator cards promote to Todo) land, Todo holds the cards a person builds. Today nothing under `console/web/src` reads `hand-built` except the timeline block: `components/composed/actorKey.ts:23` and `flyout/WhoActsNextBanner.tsx:71-76` derive the actor from the lane alone, so a hand-built Todo card renders as "queued — the pipeline picks this up", which is exactly the false claim `standards/console-honesty.md` forbids: nothing is going to pick it up. The CEO's stated expectation (2026-09-08) is a board where Backlog means "waiting on something real" and the cards that are his or the operator's are visible as such.

**Blocked by** DRE-3341 and the sweep card — without the move, there is nothing to render.

cards.title: PROOF: the ledger loop observed live — the daily commit, a planner run given the ledger, a critic citing a row, and the split-rate number posted on the epic
cards.description:
Proof that the ledger loop works against the live board, not a green suite. Every sibling ships a mechanism; this card watches each one run on real state and writes what it saw into the repo, so the record merges. An operator runs it at an interactive session with Linear and GitHub in view.

**Observe, by hand, and record each with the run link, the timestamp and the exact line read:**

1. **The schedule ran.** `.github/workflows/split-ledger.yml` (DRE-3357) observed on a scheduled trigger — not `workflow_dispatch` — committing a regenerated `config/split-ledger.json` to `main` as `agent-bureau-bot`, with `generated_at` inside the file later than the previous commit's. Record the commit sha and the row count before and after.
2. **The planner was given the ledger.** A real epic's plan run (DRE-3359 live) whose step log shows the `LEDGER STATUS: fresh — …` line and the `MULCH STATUS:` line, and whose published plan artifact carries the `ledger-check` table with one row per child (DRE-3362 live). Record the epic id, the run link, the status lines verbatim and the table.
3. **The critic cited a row.** The plan critic's ledger check shipped before this epic was approved (DRE-3079, PR #311, on `main` since 2026-09-08) and is already visible on DRE-3022's own thread: the mechanical-findings comment of 2026-09-09 names the rows it matched (DRE-2719, DRE-3016, DRE-3022) and the tell rates it quoted. Record that comment, or a later one on a real epic, verbatim — the finding sentence, the row it names, its deaths. Only if no real epic carries one, file a throwaway `PROOF-PL-` epic in `agent-bureau-demo` with one deliberately over-wide child (the replay harness's rule: nothing ships from there) and record its finding instead.
4. **UNKNOWN is not silent.** With the ledger deliberately renamed on a local checkout, `ledger_context.py render` prints `LEDGER STATUS: UNKNOWN — …` and `plan_artifact.py check` on an artifact whose records say UNKNOWN passes. Record both outputs.
5. **The number.** The scorer's split-rate row is on `main` (DRE-3079, PR #311) and reads the date the ledger reached the planner from `config/planner-audit.json` — the `ledger_injected_at` field of the `split-rate` dimension, `null` today with a stated reason. Set it to the merge time of DRE-3359's PR (`gh pr view <PR> --json mergedAt`), rewrite `ledger_injected_why` beside it to name that PR, and confirm `python3 scripts/planner_score.py check` passes. Then run `python3 scripts/planner_score.py split-rate --month <YYYY-MM>` for each month from 2026-07 to the current one against the live board and post the rendered tables on DRE-3022 as a comment — the epic says the number goes on the card before it is called done — and record them here with the date used. The "after" side will read UNKNOWN or an empty population until a whole month has passed after the merge; say so rather than filling it.

Write all five into `docs/split-ledger-audit.md` in the shape of `docs/planner-audit.md` (what was read, when, what it said), and open ONE PR carrying that file and the `config/planner-audit.json` date from observation 5.

**Files:** docs/split-ledger-audit.md, config/planner-audit.json

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `docs/split-ledger-audit.md` is merged and records observations 1–5 above, each with a run or commit link, a timestamp and the line read verbatim, observed against the live board by hand
- [ ] Observation 1 is a scheduled run, observed in production on `main`, not a manual dispatch
- [ ] `config/planner-audit.json` carries `ledger_injected_at` set to DRE-3359's PR merge time with `ledger_injected_why` naming that PR, merged in the same PR as the audit doc, and `python3 scripts/planner_score.py check` exits 0
- [ ] The split-rate tables are posted on DRE-3022 as a comment with the injection date used, and the "after" side is reported as UNKNOWN if no complete month has passed
- [ ] Any observation that could not be made says so in the record, with the reason, rather than being left out

cards.description:
**Operator-only. The fleet cannot close this card, by construction.** `needs-human` stops the sweep promoting it; `no-code` stops a merged PR closing it.

**Why now.** 52,584 hosted Linux minutes Sep 1–8 2026, $233 billed, about $900 a month at this rate. The Mac mini (M4, 32 GB, dedicated, on 24/7) becomes the runner pool for the private repos. Self-hosted minutes bill nothing.

**Shape.** Ephemeral Linux runner containers on the mini — one container per job, destroyed after it — registered at the ORG level with labels `self-hosted, linux, arm64, bureau-mini`, in the Default runner group (which already refuses public repos). Ephemeral is not optional: agent jobs branch on `/tmp/agent-blocker.txt` and `/tmp/agent-escalation.txt` existing, and a leftover file from card A would park card B in Backlog; ephemeral also means no Claude, Linear or GitHub App token outlives its job. Docker Desktop is not the runtime: its file-descriptor leak already needs a weekly restart on the operator's machine, and on a 24/7 runner host that restart is a pipeline outage. The bootstrap script, runner image and settings are committed under `scripts/runners/` by the companion card so the host is rebuildable from `main`.

## What must be done, by hand, in this order

- [ ] On the mini: run the bootstrap script from `scripts/runners/` (installs the container runtime, sets `pmset` so the box never sleeps, registers the runtime to start at login, builds the runner image, starts N runners as a launchd service). Record the PT time and N here.
- [ ] Confirm on [github.com](<http://github.com>) → Organization settings → Actions → Runners that N runners show **Idle** with the four labels.
- [ ] Set the repository variable `BUREAU_RUNS_ON` = `["self-hosted","linux","arm64","bureau-mini"]` on **bureau-harness** only. Watch its next Reconcile and one Merge Gate run land on the mini (job log: `Runner name: bureau-mini-…`) and finish green. Record run URLs and PT times.
- [ ] Let the harness prove one bureau-pipeline commit end to end on the mini (a `stable` advance after this point). Record it.
- [ ] Set the same variable on **agent-bureau**; watch one agent-task run (the long one, claude-code-action) and one qa-review complete on the mini. Record.
- [ ] Set it on **agent-bureau-demo**. Record. (**portico waits** — CEO call 2026-09-08: not out of the gate; [DRE-3355](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3355/porticos-ciyml-and-specimenyml-read-bureau-runs-on-the-playwright) is parked in Backlog until the pool has carried the platform repos for a while.)
- [ ] Rollback drill: delete the variable on one repo, confirm its next run lands on `ubuntu-latest`, set it again. Record.
- [ ] Next day: read Settings → Billing → Usage; record the day's hosted minutes here against the Sep 1–8 average of ~6,500.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every step above observed against the live system and recorded here with PT timestamps and run URLs
- [ ] Hosted Linux minutes for a full day after the last cutover step are under 500
- [ ] The rollback drill was performed, not reasoned about
- [ ] Nothing in this card was closed by a merge event; the operator closes it after the billing read

**The switch back.** Rollback is deleting the repo variable `BUREAU_RUNS_ON` — the next job of that repo runs on GitHub-hosted, no PR, no deploy. [DRE-3353](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3353/the-pool-has-an-automatic-fail-back-when-no-mac-mini-runner-is-online) makes that automatic when the pool is offline for 10 minutes. cards.title: A Green Light row aged out of Intake says WHY it is in front of the CEO — the 🚨 intake-aged receipt on the card reaches the tab instead of "no reason recorded"
cards.description:
Sibling of [DRE-3348](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3348/the-one-river-green-light-tab-shows-1-card-while-the-lane-holds-7-the), which makes non-epic Green Light cards appear on the tab at all. Once they do, each reads `Question · no reason recorded`: `greenLightModel.ts` has an `aged` matcher (`/^\s*🚨\s*intake-aged\b/m`) and `console/backend/receipts.py:193` recognises the receipt, but `receiptsFor()` is fed only by `needsYou` (ACTIVE_STATES + hold), needs-human alerts and the alert feed — none of which carries the Linear comment the sweep wrote when it moved the card.

Carry the card's `🚨 intake-aged` receipt (the sweep's own comment: since when it sat in Intake, and the reason already stated on it) into what the tab reads for a Green Light row, through the receipts path that already knows the marker — never a second summary. The row then files under the tab's `Aged` filter with that sentence, and `Questions` stays for planner escalations.

cards.title: [EPIC] The groomer's proposal is in the CEO's Needs-you queue — one row per proposal, approve / decline-with-reason / per-card comments that the drain honours, the drain fired by the approval, and the Intake pen as a switch on the console
cards.description:
The groomer is the only gate between Intake and the fleet, and on 2026-09-08 the CEO could not see its work at all. Its proposal is a comment on a Linear card ([DRE-3327](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3327/operator-first-real-groomer-proposal-read-every-verdict-before-any)); the console's home page never reads it; the proposal card the console does have ([DRE-2753](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2753/the-console-needs-a-batch-approval-surface-the-groomer-proposes-and)) sits on the old Plan Review page with an Approve button that writes a database row the drain never reads ([DRE-3325](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3325/the-consoles-batch-approval-writes-a-db-row-and-moves-nothing-the-live)). The fleet was idle all morning with 261 cards in Intake because no proposal had reached the one person who can approve one. This epic puts the proposal where the CEO already looks for things that need him, gives him the three moves the groomer can act on, and makes the approval itself move the batch.

## What the CEO sees when it is done

* A new groom proposal appears in the Needs-you queue on the One River home page within one refresh, as one row: `Groom proposal · 20 cards for cycle 13 · ranked by claude-fable-5-1 · 257 of 261 ranked`. It counts in the ribbon's "need you" number, the same way a plan awaiting a go does.
* Because this is the CEO's only gate on the fleet, a new proposal also reaches him off-console by push and email, the way a CRITICAL alert does today. A proposal nobody saw is a fleet that does nothing.
* Expanding the row shows the batch in order, each card with the model's one-line reason; below it, what was left out and why; below that, the collisions the rules fixed. The same words as the Linear comment, never a second summary.
* Three actions on the row, and one on each card:
  * **Approve** — the console posts `🧺 groom-approved: <id>` on the proposal card **in the CEO's own identity** (the same identity path Green Light uses to approve a plan), then the drain is dispatched by that approval. No hand dispatch, no operator script.
  * **Decline, with a reason** — a required sentence. The console posts `🧺 groom-declined: <id> — <reason>` on the proposal card; the next proposal opens by answering it. A decline without a reason is not offered.
  * **Per card: "not this one" / "add this one" / "why?"** — the first two are recorded on the proposal card as exclusions and additions the drain honours, so nineteen of twenty can be approved without declining the batch; "why?" asks the model about that one card and the answer lands as a reply on the row.
* The Intake pen (`INTAKE_HOLD`) is a switch on the console with the date it was closed and how many cards are behind it. Opening it from the console is the operator's act and is recorded like any other; the drain refuses while it is closed, as today.
* After the drain, the proposal row reads `drained · 20 cards to Planning · 2 held back by you` and stays readable for the day.

## Added 2026-09-08 10:00 PT — per-REPO exclusion, by CEO decision

The CEO said it three times today: Bureau (agent-bureau, bureau-pipeline) only, until it is solid. The groomer has no way to say that. Atlas cards were proposed, approved as part of a batch, drained, and one was mid-planning before it was pulled back by hand. So the proposal row carries one more control beside the per-card ones: **"not this repo"** — a repo the CEO switches off is left out of every proposal (not ranked, not counted against capacity, listed once at the bottom as `held: atlas · 12 cards`) until it is switched back on. The switch is a comment marker on the proposal card like the others (`🧺 groom-hold-repo: atlas` / `🧺 groom-release-repo: atlas`), read by `propose` and honoured by the drain, and it is shown on the row so a held repo is never a silent absence. It is distinct from the per-repo work-in-progress cap, which stops BUILDS after classification; this stops the cards being proposed at all.

## The rule that holds the whole thing

**The Linear comment is the single approval record.** The console writes it as the CEO, never as the pipeline (the drain refuses the pipeline's own identity as an approver, and must go on refusing it). The drain reads the comment and nothing else. The database-row gate from [DRE-2753](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2753/the-console-needs-a-batch-approval-surface-the-groomer-proposes-and) is retired, not kept beside it — two gates is how the current button became a lie ([DRE-3325](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3325/the-consoles-batch-approval-writes-a-db-row-and-moves-nothing-the-live)).

## Where the facts come from — derive, never infer

* **The proposal.** `proposal.json` is already written per run and uploaded as the `groom-proposal` artifact; the proposal comment on the card carries the proposal id and the receipt line. The console reads the proposal off the card comment the way it reads a routing verdict, or off the artifact through the Actions read the console already holds — the planner picks one and says why.
* **The decisions.** Approve, decline and per-card moves are comments on the proposal card with fixed markers, so `groomer.py drain` reads them the way it reads `🧺 groom-approved:` today. Per-card exclusions and additions are the per-card record [DRE-3326](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3326/the-groomers-drain-records-no-per-card-reason-so-undoing-a-bad-batch) asks for; an undo is then the list the drain itself recorded.
* **The identity.** The console's per-user Linear identity — the one that approves a plan from Green Light — writes every one of these comments. The operator's and the fleet's identities never do.
* **The pen.** `INTAKE_HOLD` is a repo variable read by `intake_controls.py` on both movers out of Intake (the drain and the sweep's age-out). The console reads it through the same Actions/variables read and writes it only through the operator's recorded act.

## Not in this epic

* Changing what the groomer ranks or how (the brief, the rules, the budget — [DRE-3331](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3331/the-groomers-judgement-answers-but-ranks-almost-nothing-258-of-260) closed that).
* Auto-approval of any kind. The CEO approves every batch; that is the design.
* The One River release row ([DRE-3336](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3336/epic-the-release-train-is-on-the-river-a-release-run-is-a-row-on-the)) — a sibling epic, no shared files.

## Acceptance criteria (for the set — the planner writes each child's own)

- [ ] A `propose` run posted to a card produces a row in the Needs-you queue on the home page within one refresh, counted in the ribbon, with push and email delivery through `delivery.py`.
- [ ] The row renders the batch in order with each card's reason, the cards left out with theirs, and the collisions — read from the run's own proposal, never restated.
- [ ] Approve posts `🧺 groom-approved: <id>` on the proposal card in the CEO's own identity and dispatches the drain; the drain's existing approval check passes on that comment and still refuses the pipeline's identity.
- [ ] Decline requires a reason, posts `🧺 groom-declined: <id> — <reason>`, and the next proposal's first line answers it.
- [ ] "Not this one" and "add this one" are recorded per card on the proposal card and the drain moves exactly the batch minus exclusions plus additions; "why?" returns the model's answer on the row.
- [ ] The [DRE-2753](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2753/the-console-needs-a-batch-approval-surface-the-groomer-proposes-and) database-row approval path is removed; `test_batch_proposal.py` asserts the console has exactly one approval writer and it is the comment.
- [ ] The Intake pen is visible on the console with its date and the count behind it; opening it is an operator act recorded on the console; the drain refuses while closed.
- [ ] The row reads the drain's outcome (moved, held back, refused) after the drain.
- [ ] The design for the proposal row and the pen switch is amended into the One River design contract and passes the design critic (DESIGNER role decision, 2026-09-07).
- [ ] PROOF: one real proposal observed on the home page, approved from it in the CEO's identity, drained by that approval, with the comments and the moved cards recorded in the repo.
- [ ] DEMO: the CEO approves one batch from the home page and watches the cards enter Planning.

## Planner notes

Count before filing: this is at least four deliverables across three trees with contracts between them — the decision markers the drain reads (bureau-pipeline, `groomer.py`), the console's read of the proposal and the pen (agent-bureau backend), the Needs-you row and its actions (agent-bureau frontend), and the retirement of the row gate (backend + tests). The markers are the contract everything else reads: split them out first in bureau-pipeline and wire `blockedBy` from every console piece to that card. Split on file footprint; the frontend row and the backend reader share nothing but the GraphQL type, which is written identically in both.

cards.title: Virtual company — phase 1: the organisation on paper, the design-critic lens, and a real org seed
cards.description:
**Design:** console/design/images/screens/desktop/fleet-landing-page.png

The first phase of the new-world organisation, decided with the CEO on 2026-09-07 (plan: the CEO's session file "moonlit-toasting-prism"; the org on one page: `docs/product/roles.md`). The company runs with an agent in every seat and the CEO in every key decision. This phase puts the organisation on paper, makes the design critic a rule every UI change passes, and replaces the engine's demo seed with the real org — so that phase 2 (the product field watch) and phase 4 (the engine on real data) build on something true.

## Why

The June company-engine designs are partly built (`console/web/src/pages/engine/*`, epics [DRE-1735](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-1735/company-engine-org-and-strategy-data-model-first-slice-foundation)–1741 Done) but sit behind a flag over a DEMO seed: four fictional companies including VeriCorr, which left the fleet on 2026-08-23; the whole Agent Bureau board attributed to one Atlas initiative; zero objectives. Turning the flag on today would show the CEO a fictional company. Meanwhile every UI change still depends on habit to reuse the atomic design system built this week ([DRE-3299](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3299/one-river-atomic-rebuild-tier-1-the-atoms-ten-pieces-built-once-at-the)/3303/3305/3306): atoms are closed (CEO sign-off), molecules critic-gated, and every UI change must pass the design critic — but no standard says so where the agents read.

## What lands

1. **The organisation, on paper, in the repo** — `docs/product/roles.md` (the org chart: CEO, operator, product in two modes, chief of staff, designer + design critic, the build department), `docs/product/product-role.md`, `docs/product/personas.md` (the product role's first deliverable: five personas with evidence, a market read, and the decisions they force). Already drafted in the agent-bureau-ui worktree; land them, and amend `architecture/company-engine-architecture.md` and `company-engine-roadmap.md` for what dated: VeriCorr as first host (gone), Department = Linear Team (superseded 2026-08-25, no Teams), Phase 0 (the console IS deployed).
2. **The design-critic lens as a standard** (bureau-pipeline, `repo:bureau-pipeline` child): extend `standards/design-parity.md` (or a sibling `console-atomic-design.md`) with the compose-and-reuse rule — screens mount atoms/molecules/organisms and draw none; reuse first; a proposed atom is the CEO's decision with a reason nothing existing fits; molecules critic-gated; every UI card and PR passes this lens. Injected via `scripts/assemble_context.py` ROLE_STANDARDS for frontend, critic and verifier; README table row; `tests/test_brief_and_standard_contract.py` assertions. Precedent: `standards/design-parity.md`.
3. **The real org seed** (`console/backend/tenancy.py:133-267`): Portfolio → Dreadnought Foundry (holding) → Agent Bureau, DeltaSolv; EveryBite and Atlas independent operating companies; no VeriCorr; stop attributing the whole board to one Atlas initiative (line 261 `INITIATIVE_AGENT_BUREAU_ID = INITIATIVE_ATLAS_ID`). The engine flag (`console/web/src/lib/featureFlags.ts:20`) STAYS OFF in this phase.

## Out of scope (later phases)

Web access for agents ([DRE-2712](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2712/give-every-agent-web-search-and-fetch-the-fleet-reasons-about-the) shape), the product field-watch workflow, the chief of staff, merging DECIDE items into One River's needs-you queue, retiring the second drill-down tree, any revenue reporting.

**Files:** docs/product/{roles,product-role,personas}.md, architecture/company-engine-architecture.md, architecture/company-engine-roadmap.md, console/backend/tenancy.py and its tests; bureau-pipeline: standards/design-parity.md (or console-atomic-design.md), standards/README.md, scripts/assemble_context.py, tests/test_brief_and_standard_contract.py

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The three product docs and the architecture amendments are on main; the CEO has read the personas and signed off the org chart
- [ ] A frontend build agent's assembled context contains the compose-and-reuse lens; the critic's and verifier's too; `check_design_widths.py` and `atomic.guard.test.ts` still pass
- [ ] Backend tests pass with the real seed; with the flag on locally, `/portfolio` shows Dreadnought Foundry → Agent Bureau and DeltaSolv, EveryBite and Atlas beside, and no VeriCorr; no initiative claims the whole board
- [ ] The flag is still off on the deployed console

cards.title: The groomer's drain records no per-card reason, so undoing a bad batch is fifty manual moves
cards.description:
`groomer.py drain` **moves a card Intake → Planning and stamps a cycle. It writes nothing on the card about WHY that card was in the batch.**

The proposal — the ranking, the verdict, the reasoning — exists as **one comment on the batch card**. The individual cards carry none of it. So after a drain:

* No card can answer "why was I picked?" from its own history.
* Reversing a batch of 50 is 50 manual state moves, performed by a human reading a comment on a different card.
* By the time anyone starts, entering Planning has **already fired the relay per card, uncapped**, and up to 50 planner runs may have produced plans and pull requests.

**The undo cost is what should bound the batch size, and right now the undo cost is unbounded.** Capacity defaults to 20 and the population is 256.

## What would fix it

Write the reason onto the card as the drain moves it — the verdict, the rank, and the proposal id that produced it — so the card carries its own provenance and a reversal is mechanical rather than archaeological.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Each drained card carries its verdict, its rank and the proposal id
- [ ] A reversal can be driven from the cards themselves, without reading the batch comment
- [ ] The record names the proposal, so a card drained by a batch later judged wrong is findable

**Repo:** agent-bureau

cards.title: The console's batch approval writes a DB row and moves nothing — the live approval path is a Linear comment
cards.description:
**A CEO who approves a groomer batch in the console will see nothing happen, and nothing will tell him why.**

There are two approval gates for the same batch and they are not connected:

* **The live one.** `groomer.py drain` looks for a Linear comment `🧺 groom-approved: <id>` posted by a non-pipeline identity. That is what actually releases a batch.
* **The console one.** `console/web/.../BatchProposalCard.tsx` → `approveBatch` → `schema.py:10016` writes a **database row**. Nothing in bureau-pipeline calls `proposeBatch` or reads that row. It moves nothing.

So the console offers an approve button for a decision it cannot carry out. The failure is silent in the worst way: the click succeeds, the UI presumably updates, and the batch stays exactly where it was.

This matters more now than when it was written. Phase 7's proof card records that "one real groomer batch is approved through the console" — and the one exercise that has ever run was approved by **comment**, not by the console.

## Decide, then fix

Either the console's approve must post the Linear comment the drain reads, or the console must stop offering the button. **What it must not do is keep offering an approval that does nothing.**

## Acceptance

- [ ] Approving in the console either releases the batch or is removed
- [ ] A test pins whichever contract is chosen, so the two cannot drift apart again
- [ ] If the console keeps the button, an approval it cannot deliver fails loudly rather than silently

**Repo:** agent-bureau

cards.title: After the cutover, the board's shape needs one deliberate review — Backlog cannot be moved by position, Todo reads empty by design, and two epics are sitting in a lane that cannot activate them
cards.description:
**For the review a week after the cutover (which ran 2026-09-07 19:08–19:17 PT: Backlog 289 → 39, Intake 12 → 262).** Three questions about the board's shape that are only answerable once the new flow has been watched for a few days. Filed now so they are not lost, deliberately NOT actioned tonight — the board changed by 250 cards an hour ago and the right time to judge which columns you want is after the groomer has run a few batches.

## 1. Backlog sits first on the board and cannot be moved by position

Linear orders board columns by state TYPE first (backlog → unstarted → started → completed), and only then by position. `Backlog` is the one lane whose type is literally `backlog`, so it is always drawn ahead of Intake, Planning, Green Light and Triage however its position is set. **Linear's API cannot change a state's type after creation** — `WorkflowStateUpdateInput` has no `type` field (confirmed against the live API 2026-09-07 19:26 PT).

Moving it therefore means creating a NEW `unstarted` lane, migrating the cards, and retiring the old one — a lane replacement of the DRE-2779 shape, touching every script that queries the lane by name (`reconcile.py` alone matches `"Backlog"` in several places). Nothing keys off the TYPE, checked; everything keys off the NAME.

**And if the lane is being recreated anyway, the name is the real question.** Before the cutover, Backlog was the holding pen. It is not any more — Intake is. What Backlog holds now is classified work carrying a routing verdict, waiting for its blockers and the WIP cap. "Backlog" now means the opposite of what it means everywhere else in the industry, which is a bigger cost than the column's position.

## 2. Todo reads as an empty column, and that is by design

The CEO asked (19:24 PT) whether Backlog and Todo could collapse into one lane. **They cannot, and the reason is not visible on the board:**

* Backlog is the QUEUE — approved, verdict-carrying, waiting.
* Todo is the TRIGGER — a card ENTERING Todo is what makes the relay dispatch an agent. Nothing else starts work.
* The promotion between them (`reconcile.promote_ready`) is the only throttle in the system: `budget = MAX_WIP - active_count`. Collapse the lanes and every approved card dispatches on approval, with nothing left to hold the cap.

So the streamlining worth considering is display, not flow: hide Todo from the default view (a card resting there for more than a minute is already an alert), or rename the pair so the board says what each one is (e.g. the queue and "Starting").

## 3. Two epics are sitting in Todo, and epics do not belong there

At 19:25 PT: **DRE-3168** and **DRE-2926**, both carrying `agent:planner`. An epic in Todo does nothing — the relay activates an epic only on a transition INTO `In Progress` (`_is_epic_activation`), so an epic parked in Todo is silently inert. DRE-3168 was approved and activated by the CEO on 09-05 18:26 PT; DRE-2926 was moved Green Light → Backlog on 09-05 and never approved.

**I could not determine what moved them or when.** The relay's log shows only `linear_published` (it observed the change, it did not cause it); the sweeps at 02:05–02:25Z name neither card; and the history API returned oldest-first, so I could not cheaply page to the recent entries. Rather than guess, this is recorded as unknown.

**What to check in the review:** whether anything in the fleet moves an epic to Todo (the sweep is documented never to promote an epic — `promote_ready` skips them by design), and whether an epic in Todo should be an alert in its own right, since today it is simply invisible.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A decision, recorded, on whether the Backlog lane is recreated as `unstarted` and under what name — with the script/name migration scoped if yes
- [ ] A decision on Todo's visibility on the default board
- [ ] The cause of DRE-3168 and DRE-2926 sitting in Todo is identified, and an epic in a lane that cannot activate it is made loud rather than silent

## Not in scope

Anything before the review. The cutover itself (done).

cards.title: The offline rollback harness takes 8m25s for 210 tests and its CI cap had to go to 20 minutes — find where the seconds go before the number grows again
cards.description:
Measured 2026-09-07: `python3 -m pytest infra/test/rollback -q` takes **8m25s for 210 tests** on the operator's Mac, and longer on a hosted runner. Every other suite in CI is milliseconds a test; this one runs `release-console.sh` or `deploy-console.sh` END TO END against process-level stubs, so a test costs seconds. DRE-3295 raised the job's cap from the house 10 minutes to 20 because the suite legitimately needed it — a cap should fail a hang, not a suite doing its job — but 8 minutes of wall clock on every `infra/` change is a real tax on the loop, and the number only grows as the harness earns more coverage.

## What to build

Find where the time actually goes before changing anything — instrument one run (`pytest --durations=25`) and put the table on this card. The likely candidates, in the order worth checking:

1. **The poll sleeps.** `release-console.sh` polls the rollout with `sleep "$ROLLOUT_POLL"`. If the harness does not already drive that to ~0, each test pays real seconds waiting for a stub that answered instantly. A harness-only override (the script keeps its production default) is the cheapest win available.
2. **Process spawn.** Each stub call is a fresh Python interpreter through a shim. Hundreds of invocations per test × a Python start each is measurable; a persistent stub or a lighter shim would cut it.
3. **The** `_state_lock` **serialisation** (DRE-3295): the two service rollouts are backgrounded subshells whose stub calls now serialise. Correct — it exists because they were losing each other's writes — but measure what it costs before deciding it is free.
4. **Per-test world setup**: if each test writes and re-reads a large JSON world, the file I/O adds up.

Then take the cheapest fix that does not weaken what the suite proves, and put the job's cap back to something honest for the new number.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A `--durations` table on this card says where the time went, before and after
- [ ] The suite's wall time is materially lower (target: under 4 minutes for the current test count) with no test removed, skipped or made less strict
- [ ] `timeout-minutes` on the rollback job is set from the measured number with the reasoning in the comment, as it is today
- [ ] A test pins whatever knob makes it fast (e.g. the poll override) so a later change cannot silently restore the slow path

## Not in scope

Removing or thinning tests. The stubs' correctness (DRE-3295 fixed a real lost-write defect there; do not undo it).

cards.title: The post critic's ceiling cut a 7-card review at 48 of 51 turns, the finished review was recorded as dead, and the medic stamped it a Claude limit death — three misreads of one run
cards.description:
**Seen 2026-09-07 09:39–09:50 PT, agent-bureau run 34144302622 — the post-approval review of DRE-3257 (7 cards) after the CEO's re-approval.** Three things on one run:

1. **The ceiling is still too low.** DRE-3241 sized it `20 + 4 × children` (7 cards → 48). The review needed 51 turns on claude-sonnet-5 and was cut off. The formula was calibrated on one data point (round 2 of DRE-3164: 41 turns on 15 cards, on the previous model); a Sonnet review that also has to verify a live-system premise and one collision spends more per card. Raise the base and the floor (e.g. `40 + 4 × children`, floor 60) and record the turns actually spent per review as a receipt so the number is tuned from data, not guessed.
2. **A review that FINISHES over the ceiling is recorded as dead.** The action's result was `"subtype": "success"` at turn 51 with `maxTurns: 48` — the step was marked failure and DRE-3241's tombstone posted *"died (success) after 51 turns of its 48-turn ceiling"*. Whether the critic wrote a verdict before the cut is not read: if the result file exists and parses, the round should count as decided (PASS/SEND_BACK) — a verdict that exists is not a death. If it does not exist, the tombstone's wording should not say `(success)`.
3. **The medic stamped it a Claude limit death.** A `🪦 limit-death: kind=claude stage=plan reset=unknown` receipt landed on the epic for the same run (16:50Z). Nothing in the run hit an account limit — it hit the turn cap. `medic_retry.py`'s limit classifier is reading the wrong signal (a turn-cap `error_max_turns`/over-ceiling result is not a 429), and the limit-recovery sweep (DRE-3171) will now try to "re-enter" this card when a window resets, which is noise at best and a phantom re-dispatch at worst.

## What to build

1. `plan_critic.post_review_turns`: new base/floor; a `🧮 review-turns: spent=N ceiling=M children=K model=…` receipt on the epic per round (trusted-author, sole-record shape, ignored by `parse_markers`) so the constant can be re-tuned from the last 30 reviews.
2. `plan.yml` post review → decision: when the review step ends over the ceiling but a parseable result file exists, treat it as the round's verdict; only a missing/unparseable result is a death. Tombstone wording drops `(success)`.
3. `medic_retry.py` (or `limit_recovery`) classifier: a turn-cap result (`error_max_turns`, or `num_turns >= maxTurns`) is never `kind=claude`; test with this run's execution JSON as the fixture.

**Files:** `scripts/plan_critic.py`, `.github/workflows/plan.yml`, `scripts/medic_retry.py` / `scripts/limit_recovery.py`, `tests/test_plan_critic*.py`, `tests/test_medic_retry*.py`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A 7-card review at the new ceiling has ≥ 20% headroom over 51 turns (pinned by test), and the receipt line is posted per round
- [ ] A fixture with `subtype=success`, `num_turns > maxTurns` and a parseable result file yields the result's verdict, not a tombstone
- [ ] The same fixture through the medic classifier yields NOT a limit death
- [ ] The next post-approval review on a ≥ 7-card epic finishes and leaves a verdict, recorded here

## Not in scope

The bound. The pre-approval critic's ceiling (same formula — apply the same change if it shares the function).

cards.description:
The mechanism observed running against real state, by a person, and the observation recorded in the repo — not a green suite. Every reading is stamped in Pacific Time.

**What is observed, on the production console ([app.agent-bureau.com](<http://app.agent-bureau.com>)), after the operator deploy.**

**The surface this proof reads survives One River's cutover (second-critic send-back, round 4, 2026-09-07).** DRE-3060's cutover card DRE-3061 deletes the old home page at `/` and its Open pull requests panel. It is ordered after DRE-3274 (the chip lands first) but NOT after this card, so the cutover may land before or during this proof. Every reading below is therefore taken on the One River row — the Pull Requests tab and the river's Overview — which exists at `/dashboard/next` today and at `/` after the cutover; the old panel is an EXTRA reading while it is live, never the only one. The note records, for each reading, the URL it was taken at and whether the old home page was still live.

1. The operator ships the merged console siblings (`/ship-it`) and redeploys the GitHub relay so the push path carries `isDraft` (`AWS_PROFILE=dreadnought bash cloud/relay-gh/deploy.sh`), and records the deployed console version and relay deploy time.
2. **A draft PR with a red check reads** `Draft — held`**.** Take one real open `agent/*` PR in a console repo (or open a throwaway one on an `agent/DRE-<this card>-…` branch with a deliberately failing check), convert it to a draft (`gh pr ready --undo <n>`) — choose one with NO critic rejection standing on its head and a non-conflicted branch, because the fix agent runs on a draft the critic has rejected (it ran on draft PR #2317 at 2026-09-06 09:19 PT), and such a row honestly reads the fix loop, not `Draft — held`; if the critic rejects the throwaway PR, wait for the fix attempt to end and record what the row read while it ran as an extra reading — wait one poll or provoke a webhook, and read its row on One River's Pull Requests tab (`/dashboard/next/pull-requests` until DRE-3061 cuts over, `/pull-requests` after — record which) and, while the old home page is still live at `/`, on its Open pull requests panel too. Record the row's chips verbatim with the PT time. It must read `Draft — held` and must NOT read `Stuck — needs you` or `Stalled — no fix agent engaged`. Record the Merge button's hover reason too.
3. **The proof-waiting receipt reads on both rows.** On that PR's card post the receipt with the helper from the bureau-pipeline sibling (`python3 scripts/linear_ops.py proof-waiting <CARD> "a failing agent PR in a console repo" "one open agent/* PR with a red check"`), wait for the card's events to be re-read, and record the PR's row on the Pull Requests tab and the card's river row on Overview (and the old panel's row, if that page is still live) reading `Waiting for proof — a failing agent PR in a console repo — needs one open agent/* PR with a red check`, PT-stamped.
4. `proof-observed` **clears it.** Post `linear_ops.py proof-observed <CARD> "…"`, re-read both rows, record that the chip is gone and the draft reads `Draft — held` alone.
5. **The regression reading.** Find one non-draft failing `agent/*` PR in a console repo whose Agent Fix runs all concluded `skipped` and record that it still reads `Stalled — no fix agent engaged` (DRE-3001's reading; PR #2316 read it at 2026-09-06 09:31:58 PT). If none exists that day, record the nearest live shape and say so plainly — never argue a missed reading into a met one (the DRE-3135 critic's finding).
6. Mark the throwaway PR ready or close it, and record what was cleaned up.

The record is a forensics note under `architecture/forensics/` linked from its README (the DRE-3135 note is the shape), opened as a PR that merges; this card is operator-closed on that evidence, not by the merge (`no-code`).

cards.title: Every console rollout logs four monitor ERROR tracebacks that mean nothing — the old instance's shutdown closes the pool under a running tick; log it once at INFO and keep ERROR for the real case
cards.description:
Seen on the v1.6.20 rollout, 2026-09-06 17:09:20–21 PT, in the console backend's application log: `shutdown: 2 background task(s) did not reach a tick boundary within 10.0s and were interrupted mid-tick: run-monitors, ws-ingest`, followed one second later by three `ERROR console.monitors monitor check failed — skipping, others still run` tracebacks (`run_signal_health.py:207`, `wip_health.py:88`, `ws_ingest_health.py:110`, each `psycopg.OperationalError: the connection is closed`) and one `monitors: could not read the open alerts (no live signal)`. Zero recurrence after the first tick of the new instance; not present on the v1.6.19 boot. It is the OLD instance being told to stop while a monitor tick is mid-query: the pool closes, the in-flight checks fail, and each is logged as an ERROR with a traceback.

Every rollout of the console will print four ERROR lines that mean nothing, and anyone reading the log after a deploy has to know that. Under the release train, that is every console merge.

## What to build

On shutdown, the monitor runner stops scheduling new ticks and lets an in-flight tick finish OR cancels it and logs ONE INFO line (`shutdown: monitor tick cancelled mid-query — expected on rollout`) — never an ERROR with a traceback for a connection the app itself closed. `_open_alert_state` the same. A test in `console/backend/tests/test_monitors_runner*.py` pins that a `psycopg.OperationalError` raised during shutdown is logged at INFO without a traceback, and that the same error OUTSIDE shutdown is still an ERROR (that one is real).

**Files:** `console/backend/monitors/runner.py`, `console/backend/app.py` (the shutdown sequence), their tests.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test pins the shutdown-time connection error as one INFO line, no traceback
- [ ] A test pins the same error outside shutdown as ERROR (unchanged)
- [ ] The next console rollout's log carries no `monitor check failed` ERROR, recorded here with the deploy tag

## Not in scope

The monitors' own logic. The 10-second shutdown budget.

cards.title: A draft PR held for a reason reads as "Stuck — needs you" — a draft is its own state, and a proof waiting on an observation says what it waits for: "Waiting for proof — <reason>"
cards.description:
**What the CEO saw (2026-09-06 ~09:57 PT).** The Open pull requests panel showed PR #2317 — the DRE-3135 proof note, converted to a DRAFT on purpose because two of its observations could not be taken yet — as `Stuck — needs you` and `Stalled — no fix agent engaged`. Both chips are the console's generic reading of "an agent PR with a red check and no fix agent". Neither was true in the sense a reader takes them: nothing was stuck, nobody was needed, and the fix agent skipping a draft is the fix agent behaving. The reason the PR was waiting was written on the Linear card by hand and nowhere on the console. The CEO's ask: *"we need a better message as to why it is waiting — what's waiting for proof and what it's waiting for, so that I can quickly see why."*

## What to build

1. **A draft is its own state, read from GitHub.** A PR with `isDraft: true` never renders `Stuck — needs you` or `Stalled — no fix agent engaged`. It renders `Draft — held`, and the merge gate / fix-agent readings that assume a ready PR are suppressed for it (they already skip drafts in the pipeline; the console should read the same fact instead of inferring from the checks). Leverage GitHub's own signal — do not invent a label.
2. **The reason rides on the card as a receipt, one line.** A PROOF card (or any card) held on a missing observation carries a `🔬 proof-waiting: <what is still to be observed> — needs <what would let it be observed>` comment, written by whoever holds it (the operator's session or a proof runner) in the same trusted-author, sole-record shape as the lane-guard receipts, and cleared by a `🔬 proof-observed:` line. `console/backend/receipts.py` files it as a HOLD kind with the reason as its caption; the card row and the PR row render the chip `Waiting for proof — <reason>` (e.g. *Waiting for proof — a failing agent PR in a console repo*). A draft PR with no such receipt on its card renders `Draft — held` alone.
3. Tests pin: a draft PR with a red check renders neither stuck nor stalled; a card with a proof-waiting receipt renders the chip with the reason verbatim; `proof-observed` clears it; a non-draft PR with a red check and no fix agent still reads `Stalled — no fix agent engaged` (that reading is correct and DRE-3001 proved it).

**Files:** `console/backend/receipts.py` (the receipt kinds), `console/backend/pr_status.py` or wherever `FIX_STALLED` / "needs you" is derived (grep `FIX_STALLED`), the PR row and card row components under `console/web/src`, their tests. Pipeline side (bureau-pipeline): the `🔬 proof-waiting` line added to `config/pipeline-acts.json` and a `linear_ops.py proof-waiting <card> "<reason>"` helper — a separate small card if the footprint splits.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A draft agent PR with a failing check renders `Draft — held` and neither `Stuck — needs you` nor `Stalled — no fix agent engaged` (test + a live reading on the console with PT time)
- [ ] A card carrying a `🔬 proof-waiting:` receipt renders `Waiting for proof — <reason>` on its card row and its PR row, and `🔬 proof-observed:` clears it (tests)
- [ ] The receipt line is declared in the acts registry and posted by a one-line helper, so a proof runner or the operator can write it without hand-formatting
- [ ] A non-draft failing agent PR with all fix-agent runs skipped still reads `Stalled — no fix agent engaged` (regression test)

## Not in scope

Changing what the fix agent does with drafts (it already skips them). The proof cards themselves.

cards.title: PROOF: auto-switch observed firing on the live console — a 429 switches the fleet within one poll cycle, a repo rotated by hand flips the hero to UNKNOWN and stands it down, and every switch left its log line
cards.description:
Proof that auto-switch now fires on the fleet's own evidence, observed on the LIVE console against real state — not the test suite. The epic's first acceptance criterion says it outright: "observed once on the live console and recorded here with PT times". That observation cannot gate any sibling's merge (the mechanism has to be deployed to be watched), so it lives here, run by the operator at an interactive session after every build card has merged and the console has been deployed.

Three observations, recorded in one audit file in the repo with PT times, the switch-log lines copied verbatim, and the backend log excerpts that back them:

1. **The 429 path.** With auto-switch on and the fleet on a known account, drive that account's usage endpoint to answer 429 (or wait for a real cap — 2026-09-05 supplied one unprompted) and watch the console switch to the next account in failover order within one poll cycle (at most five minutes). Record: the PT time of the 429 row, the PT time of the switch-log line, its trigger (`usage-429`), the repos it rotated, and a fresh planner or build run succeeding on the new account.
2. **The receipts path.** With the usage endpoint healthy, feed three limit receipts through the real ingest path — three cards carrying the pipeline's own `agent died with API/model error (is_error)` comment inside fifteen minutes, on a throwaway project — and watch the console switch with trigger `run-receipts` naming the three cards. If a live limit cannot be arranged, record the receipts-path test run instead and say so plainly; the 429 observation is the one that must be live.
3. **The identity path.** Rotate one repo's `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` by hand (`gh secret set` on the demo repo), and within one identity tick see: the Alerts page entry naming the repo and the time, the Subscriptions hero reading `FLEET ACCOUNT UNKNOWN`, and auto-switch standing down on a 429 (its result says the fleet's account was unknown). Then switch by hand from the console and see the repo return to `console` and the alert resolve.

The audit file follows the `architecture/audits/2026-09-browser-unknown-direction-guard-proof.md` shape: what was read, when (PT), what it said, and the exact commands.

**Files:** architecture/audits/2026-09-DRE-3170-auto-switch-proof.md (new — the recorded observation, nothing else)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Observed on the live console, by hand: one automatic switch with trigger `usage-429` completing within five minutes of the 429 row, recorded with PT times and the switch-log line verbatim
- [ ] Observed on the live console, by hand: one repo rotated outside the console raises the Alert, flips the hero to `FLEET ACCOUNT UNKNOWN`, and stands auto-switch down; a manual switch from the console clears all three
- [ ] The receipts path is either observed live (trigger `run-receipts`, three card ids in the reason) or explicitly recorded as test-only with the reason
- [ ] The audit file is merged on `main` and the epic carries a comment linking it, with the PT time of each observation
- [ ] The manual "Use this" switch was used during the proof and worked exactly as before, and the file says so

Planning that second half before the train existed cost two send-backs (a collision with One River's capacity strip over the deploy-lag data, and a plan that drifted out of date against its own children). The rule is now [DRE-3244](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3244): two epics at the gate.

Nothing under here builds until the CEO approves that plan.

cards.description:
Split out of [DRE-3236](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3236) on 2026-09-06 because it lives in a different repo from the two spend cuts (agent-bureau's toolkit, not bureau-pipeline), and a card whose work spans two PRs goes Done on the first merge.

**What is wrong.** `scripts/check_linear_budget.py --hours 1` skips every run whose log GitHub has not yet made retrievable — at 17:20 PT on 2026-09-05 that was 136 of 222 runs, and at 22:50 PT a `--hours 1` read returned nothing at all. An hour's table read at the top of the next hour is therefore incomplete exactly when it is read, and the "skipped: log not available" count is the only sign.

## What to build

`check_linear_budget.py` retries a run whose log is not yet available (bounded: a few attempts with a short back-off inside the one invocation), and when a run still has no log after the retries it is counted and NAMED in the footer, never silently dropped. An hour's table read after the hour closes is complete.

**Files:** `scripts/check_linear_budget.py`, `scripts/test_check_linear_budget.py`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test with a fake `gh` that returns "log not available" twice then the log pins that the run is counted, not skipped
- [ ] A test pins that a run with no log after the retries is named in the footer with its run id
- [ ] One live `--hours 1` read after the hour closes shows `0 skipped`, recorded here with the PT time

## Not in scope

The spend cuts themselves (DRE-3236). Any change to what the sweeps do.

cards.title: agent-bureau: the terminal deploy-lag report reads its surfaces from release.json across the fleet — the CLI literal goes, after One River's capacity strip is built and observed against today's rows
cards.description:
Split out of DRE-3213 at the 2026-09-05 20:10 PT re-plan, after the second critic found that rewriting the deploy-lag readers collides with One River ([DRE-3060](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3060)): its capacity strip (DRE-3116) is built against the rows `make deploy-lag` and the console's `deployLag` print today, and its Phase 4 observation (DRE-3068) checks that strip against `make deploy-lag` by hand. This card waits for both, as real relations, so the rows One River builds and proves are rows this epic has not yet changed. DRE-3117 then records what DRE-3068 saw; the train's own proof (DRE-3220) makes the same side-by-side observation again after the rewrite.

The terminal deploy-lag report stops carrying its own surface table and reads the fleet's release data instead (`adr-one-writer-per-fact`). Today `scripts/check_deploy_lag.py` holds a literal `SURFACES` tuple (console, website, relay, pipeline-channel) that `.github/bureau/release.json` restates since DRE-3213; after this card the tuple is gone and the rows come from the data.

## What to build

* `scripts/release_surfaces.py` (DRE-3213's loader) gains the fleet read: `load_fleet(repos, fetch) -> FleetRead` — this repo's file from the checkout, every other repo in `config/repo-map.json` through `gh api repos/<owner>/<name>/contents/.github/bureau/release.json` behind an injectable `fetch`. A 404 means that repo declares no surfaces and is not an error; any other failure makes that repo's surfaces UNKNOWN and is carried as coverage. `Surface.repo` is the full `owner/name` for every surface.
* `scripts/check_deploy_lag.py`: `SURFACES` goes; `collect()` takes its surfaces from the loader. **Row order:** this repo's surfaces in file order, then each other repo in `config/repo-map.json` order, each in its file order — DRE-3214's console copy uses the same order. A row from another repo names its repo in the summary. A `record: channel` surface keeps the `compare` read (`channel_lag()`) against the repo that declares it — bureau-pipeline's `pipeline-channel`, once DRE-3167's file is on its `main`; until then that row reads UNKNOWN with the reason named, never from a literal. `render()` prints one coverage line, `surfaces read from N of M repos`, above the rows. The relay row now counts the paths the data names (the three deploy inputs), so it may read a larger number than the literal did; that is the data being right, pinned by a fixture rather than left to be noticed.
* `console/backend/tests/test_deploy_lag.py`: its one assertion `test_the_surfaces_table_is_the_cli_s_table` compared the backend literal to `cli.SURFACES`, which no longer exists; it now compares the backend literal to the loader's reading of THIS repo's file, so CLI/backend parity survives until DRE-3214 removes the backend literal too. No other line of that file changes, and `console/backend/deploy_lag.py` is not touched.

**Files:** scripts/check_deploy_lag.py, scripts/test_check_deploy_lag.py, scripts/release_surfaces.py, scripts/test_release_surfaces.py, console/backend/tests/test_deploy_lag.py

## Contract

Reads `.github/bureau/release.json` in the shape fixed in DRE-3213 and DRE-3167; this reader consumes `surfaces.<name>.{tag_series, paths, record}` and nothing else. The fetch path per repo is `repos/<owner>/<name>/contents/.github/bureau/release.json` (base64 `content`). `Surface(repo, name, paths, tag_globs, record)` is the record DRE-3214's backend twin mirrors field for field, and the row order above is the order both readers print. The GraphQL `deployLag` field is not changed by this card.

## Aware of One River (DRE-3060)

* DRE-3116 builds the capacity strip from the `deployLag` GraphQL field. This card changes no GraphQL field.
* DRE-3068 observes that strip against `make deploy-lag` by hand. This card lands only after that card is Done, so the observation was of a reader this epic had not touched.
* DRE-3117 records what DRE-3068 saw; DRE-3220 records the same comparison after this card and DRE-3214, so both epics have a record of the mechanism as they proved it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `scripts/check_deploy_lag.py` holds no `SURFACES` literal; on `main`, `make deploy-lag` prints the same console, website, relay and pipeline-channel rows it printed before this card, read from data, plus one coverage line naming how many repos' declarations were read
- [ ] A repo whose `release.json` cannot be fetched (not a 404) renders its surfaces UNKNOWN with the reason and lowers the coverage count — never 0, never omitted silently — pinned by a test with a failing fake fetcher
- [ ] A 404 is "declares no surfaces": no row, no failure, coverage counts the repo as read — pinned
- [ ] A fixture declaring a surface under another repo's name renders that row after this repo's rows, naming its repo — pinned
- [ ] `console/backend/tests/test_deploy_lag.py` still passes; its parity assertion reads this repo's file through the loader; `console/backend/deploy_lag.py` is unchanged in the PR diff
- [ ] `python3 .bureau-pipeline/scripts/check_tdd_commits.py origin/main HEAD` exits 0 before the push

**Blocked by:** DRE-3213, DRE-3116, DRE-3068

cards.description:
## Seen 2026-09-05

[DRE-3161](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3161/the-prose-blocker-detector-reads-a-card-id-out-of-a-linear-links-url) (the prose-blocker detector reads ids from link slugs) has been through Planning three times today — 09:06, 13:0x and 16:42 PT. Each time the classifier stamped it one-off in seconds and the pre-approval critic then died: the Claude Code result carried `is_error: true` after 21 turns (run 33999238213 at 16:42 PT is the third), the route wrote `plan-critic: stage=one-off round=3 result=NO_RESULT`, and the card was parked in Green Light with *"the critic produced no result, and on this route that is not a pass"*. The CEO answered this card's question at 11:30 PT; nothing about the card has needed him since. Other one-offs re-entered at the same minute ([DRE-2924](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2924/ci-the-pr-size-router-calls-a-pr-one-pass-that-the-critic-cannot)) passed the critic normally, so this is specific to this card.

Two defects:

1. **A critic death is being escalated as a decision.** Three `NO_RESULT`s in a row is a failure of the critic, not a question for a person, and Green Light is the decision queue. This case belongs in Triage (the broken-card lane, [DRE-2723](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2723/triage-becomes-the-broken-card-lane)) with the run linked, or — since the death is the pipeline's — to the medic as a `crash`, never to the CEO.
2. **Something in this card kills the critic.** The card body quotes regexes and Linear link markup (`<issue …>` mentions, `DRE-\d+` patterns, the `**Blocked by:**` line under test). The likeliest cause: the critic's brief tells it to run the card's own examples, and the mention markup or a regex in the body drives a tool call that fails 21 turns in a row. Reproduce by running the critic locally on this card's body (the repo has a critic harness) and read the transcript.

## What to build

* Diagnose from the run's transcript (the failed step's log carries the model's turns); fix the cause in the critic brief or the body rendering, with a test that feeds this card's body through the critic's prompt assembly and asserts it renders without the failing construct.
* After a third `NO_RESULT` the route parks the card in **Triage** with a comment naming the three runs, not Green Light; a test pins the destination.

**Files:** scripts/plan_critic.py (or the sibling that owns the one-off critic route), standards/plan-critic.md, tests.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] [DRE-3161](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3161/the-prose-blocker-detector-reads-a-card-id-out-of-a-linear-links-url)'s body, fed as a fixture through the pre-approval critic's prompt assembly, renders without the construct the failed transcript blames (the test asserts on the rendered prompt, and fails on today's rendering)
- [ ] `deferred: live pass of DRE-3161 through the critic in one round — observed AFTER this merges, on the follow-up observation card blocked by this one (needs-human, no-code); it cannot gate this merge (DRE-3075)`
- [ ] Three consecutive `NO_RESULT`s route to Triage with the runs named, pinned by a test

cards.title: PROOF: the three export defects observed closed on a deployed portal, recorded in the repo
cards.description:
The mechanism observed running against real state, with the observation recorded in the repo — not the test suite. Each of the three findings of DRE-2895 is watched closing on a deployed portal, by hand, and the record merges.

Where: a form instance in the `drafts` project (the private review space on the `everybite` account; gated to `lambdaworks.io`, no library) or, if the operator prefers, a two-company test folder on a live portal after the release train has shipped `main` with all six sibling cards. No production partition held a form answer on 2026-08-31, so this is the first real observation of these paths.

What is observed and recorded, in `docs/demos/export-integrity.md` (a new file, in the house style of `docs/demos/shared-answers.md`: what was read, when, by whom, what it said — with the exact JSON and screen text pasted in):

1. **Files are per company.** Two people from two email domains open one form; one uploads a file on a file question. The submit export (a moderator's, so it carries every group) is downloaded: the uploader's row lists the file, the other company's row lists `files: []`, the other company's `answers` does not count that question, and the uploader's reading view ticks it while the other's does not.
2. **An overwrite clears the status.** Two browsers, one field, one company. Browser A types and marks *Answered*. Browser B, holding a stale version, types different text. Observed: B's strip note names A and says the label was cleared; the "changed elsewhere" row shows A's text marked *Answered*; the export row for that field shows B's name, B's text and `status: null`; the answer history rail shows A's entry beneath B's.
3. **An unasked answer is kept and flagged.** With a moderator token, `PUT /d/{docId}/responses/q99` (an id the frozen definition does not contain) — the exact call is in DRE-2898's probe. Observed: 200; the shelf row reads `v1 · N/N · 1 outside the form`; the export row for `q99` carries `outOfForm: true` and the group summary `outOfForm: 1`; the row is still in `answers`.
4. **The backfill ran.** The release run log shows `migrate-form-definitions.ts --apply` reporting the question-id step, and a pointer row read back carries `form.questionIds`.

Anything that cannot be established from the live portal is recorded as UNPROVABLE in those words (`docs/demos/prove.sh`'s rule), never as "probably fine".

**Files:** docs/demos/export-integrity.md

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All four observations made by hand against a deployed portal after the release train shipped every sibling, and recorded in `docs/demos/export-integrity.md` with the date, the account, the project, and the pasted evidence
- [ ] Observation 1's export JSON in the record shows one file on exactly one company's row
- [ ] Observation 2's record shows the strip note text, the replaced row's status label, and the export row with `status: null`
- [ ] Observation 3's record shows the 200, the shelf label, and the flagged export row
- [ ] Any observation that could not be made is written as UNPROVABLE with the reason, and the card is not closed on it
- [ ] The record is merged to `main` through the normal PR path (author ≠ merger)
