cards.title: The critic's own experiments can delete the pipeline's nested checkout it is running from — check_critic_result.py was gone when the post-review step ran, and the review crashed
cards.description:
Seen 2026-09-05 15:46 PT on bureau-pipeline PR #279 (head `b78e519`): the QA critic's review run crashed at the post-review step because `.bureau-pipeline/scripts/check_critic_result.py` no longer existed on the runner. The critic had been doing what its brief asks — reverting files to `main` to prove the PR's tests actually bite — and that experiment (a `git stash -u`, a `git clean`, or a checkout of a path that contains the nested clone) took the pipeline's untracked nested checkout with it. The verdict comment read `QA Critic could not run (infra error) — re-review needed, this is NOT a code rejection`; the sweep's `recover_crashed_reviews` re-dispatched once and the second run approved, so nothing was lost this time. The class will recur on any PR the critic experiments on.

## What to build

* The nested pipeline checkout the review workflow uses lives OUTSIDE the PR's working tree (e.g. `$RUNNER_TEMP/bureau-pipeline`, or a sibling directory), so no git operation inside the PR repo can touch it. The workflow references it by an absolute path exported once.
* The critic's brief says explicitly that experiments run inside the PR repo only, and names the two commands that are off-limits in the repo root (`git stash -u`, `git clean -x`); the post-review step asserts the checkout is still present before it runs and, if not, says so in the verdict instead of crashing.

**Files:** `.github/workflows/qa-review.yml` (checkout location + the assertion), `standards/critic.md` (or the brief the critic reads), tests over the workflow shell.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test renders the review workflow's steps and asserts the nested checkout path is outside `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE`
- [ ] A test runs the post-review step with the checkout removed and asserts the verdict says the checkout was missing rather than the step crashing
- [ ] The critic brief carries the two forbidden commands and the reason, in one sentence each

cards.title: The console deploy ships a push-channel client whose server lives in a stack the deploy never touches — DRE-3162 left the console with no live feed at all from 15:41 PT
cards.description:
## Seen 2026-09-05

`make deploy-console` at 15:41 PT shipped v1.6.17, carrying [DRE-3162](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3162/the-consoles-push-channel-only-carries-dreadnoughts-repos-an-atlas-or)'s client half: `console/backend/ws_ingest.py` now connects to the ingest WebSocket with `?consumer=__platform__`. [DRE-3162](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3162/the-consoles-push-channel-only-carries-dreadnoughts-repos-an-atlas-or)'s server half — `infra/lambda/ingest-ws/authorize.js` and `connect.js`, which accept that claim, and `fan_out` in `cloud/relay` and `cloud/relay-gh` — lives in `IngestWsStack` and the two relay Lambdas, none of which `infra/deploy-console.sh` deploys (it deploys Dns, Release, MigrationTask, Backend, Frontend). The undeployed authorizer answers the unknown claim with **HTTP 403**; the backend backs off 60 s and retries forever (`console.ws_ingest … connection failed — backing off 60.0s … InvalidStatus: server rejected WebSocket connection: HTTP 403`, every minute from 15:52 PT). The Alerts page raised `Live updates have stopped arriving (15 min)` at 15:57 PT — correctly.

Net effect: BEFORE the deploy the console had a live feed for Dreadnought's repos and a poll for the rest; AFTER it has no live feed for anyone until the operator deploys `IngestWsStack` by hand. A deploy made the board less honest, and nothing in the deploy said so.

## What to build

1. **The deploy knows its seams.** `infra/deploy-console.sh`'s "Detect changed surfaces" step gains `IngestWsStack`: when `infra/lambda/ingest-ws/**` or `infra/lib/ingest-ws-stack.ts` changed since the running release, the deploy either deploys that stack in the same run (it already runs `cdk deploy` for five stacks) or REFUSES with one line naming the stack and the commit, before rolling the backend. Shipping a client whose server is not deployed is the [DRE-2789](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2789/nothing-records-which-relay-commit-is-live-merged-but-never-deployed) shape ("merged" ≠ "deployed") one layer down.
2. **The client degrades, not dies.** `ws_ingest.py`: on a 403 to the platform claim, fall back to the tenant claim it used before (`?tenant=<operator tenant>`) so the pre-3162 behaviour survives a half-deployed server, and log ONE warning naming the missing deploy. Remove the fallback in the card that retires the tenant claim.
3. The relay halves (`cloud/relay`, `cloud/relay-gh`) stay on their own deploys (`make relay-deploy`, `cloud/relay-gh/deploy.sh`); the PR body for any change spanning them names every deploy it needs, checked by the critic's "which deployable surfaces" list ([DRE-3000](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3000/the-proof-runner-can-report-a-phase-proven-while-its-work-is-not)'s shape).

**Files:** infra/deploy-console.sh, console/backend/ws_ingest.py, their tests.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A console deploy from a tree where `infra/lambda/ingest-ws/**` changed either deploys `IngestWsStack` in the same run or stops before the backend rollout with a one-line reason — pinned by the deploy script's tests
- [ ] With the server rejecting the platform claim (403), the backend connects on the tenant claim within one backoff, logs one warning, and the live feed resumes; pinned by a test with a fake server
- [ ] Observed live: after the operator deploys `IngestWsStack`, the backend connects on the platform claim on its next attempt and the Alerts page clears the "live updates have stopped" alert without a restart; recorded here with PT times

## Until this lands (operator)

`IngestWsStack` needs a CDK deploy by hand (see the comment below for the exact command), and the two relays their own deploys — the Linear relay only as `LANE_GUARD_MODE=report make relay-deploy`.

cards.description:
**Operator-only. The fleet cannot close this card, by construction.** `needs-human` stops the sweep promoting it; `no-code` stops a merged PR closing it.

Portico's portals roll out by themselves only after portico's operator grants the identity, watches one supervised release, and flips `auto` — the same three steps the console took in DRE-3166, done in portico and by the person who holds its AWS accounts. Not before the console (DRE-3166) and the relay (the agent-bureau operator card) have each shown a week of clean train releases: portico is customer-facing and joins last among the dreadnought surfaces.

## What must be done, by hand, in this order

- [ ] Set the repo secret `BUREAU_RELEASE_ROLE_ARN` in portico to the release role the portico train card defined, once that role exists in each account the procedure publishes to; apply the grant from your clone with the command the PR body names. Nothing broader than the grant the card's test pins.
- [ ] With `auto` still `false`, fire `release-train.yml` by hand — `gh workflow run release-train.yml -f surface=portals`, which runs that one surface with `auto` still `false` — and watch: the script publishes only the live portals, every cut-over portal still redirects afterwards (check each one in a browser and record the URLs), the `portico-portals-v*` tag is cut, `make deploy-lag` in agent-bureau reads the portico surface current afterwards
- [ ] Run the hand procedure while a train release is in flight and confirm it refuses and names the run
- [ ] Open the one-line PR that flips `auto` to `true` in portico's `.github/bureau/release.json`, let portico's gates merge it, record the merge time here in PT
- [ ] Watch the next natural merge roll out by itself inside the window; record merge time, rollout time and the tag cut

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every item above observed by hand against portico's live accounts and recorded here with PT timestamps and run URLs
- [ ] Every cut-over portal's redirect was checked after the supervised release and the list is recorded here
- [ ] Nothing in this card was closed by a merge event: the operator closes it after the last observation

cards.title: agent-bureau: the console's deployLag reads the same release data — the backend twin drops its surface literal and fetches each repo's release.json over GraphQL, coverage travelling with the number
cards.description:
**Rewritten 2026-09-05 20:10 PT (re-plan after the second critic).** This is the card that touches the GraphQL type One River's capacity strip (DRE-3116, under [DRE-3060](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3060)) is built against, and regenerates the file that strip reads its documents from. So it waits, as real relations, for the strip to be built and for its Phase 4 observation (DRE-3068) to be made against the rows as they are today — and for DRE-3238, which moves the terminal report onto the data first. Everything the strip reads is preserved verbatim: this card is additive to the type and changes no field the `DeployLag` operation selects.

The console's own copy of the deploy-lag rules reads the same data the terminal report reads after DRE-3238. `console/backend/deploy_lag.py` restates the surface table as a literal because the backend image cannot import the toolkit (its build context is `console/backend/` alone). After this card the literal is gone.

## What to build

* `console/backend/deploy_lag.py`: the live reader fetches each repo's `.github/bureau/release.json` over the GitHub GraphQL the module already uses (`object(expression: "HEAD:.github/bureau/release.json")` on every repo in `sources.REPOS`), parses the surfaces with the contract below, and judges them by the unchanged `assess`. A repo whose file is absent declares no surfaces; a repo whose file could not be read makes its surfaces UNKNOWN and lowers `surfaces_read` — the coverage already travels with the number, and now it covers the declarations as well as the reads. `record: channel` rows keep the compare read against the repo that declares them. **Row order is DRE-3238's:** this repo's surfaces in file order, then each other repo in `sources.REPOS` order.
* `console/backend/tests/test_deploy_lag.py`: `test_the_surfaces_table_is_the_cli_s_table` becomes "both loaders produce the same surfaces from the same fixture file" — one fixture drives `scripts/release_surfaces.py` and this module; the parity-on-`assess` tests are untouched.
* `console/backend/schema.py`: `DeployLagRow` gains ONE nullable field, `repo`, so a row from another repo can say where it came from. `console/web/schema.graphql` is re-exported (`npm run schema:export`) and `console/web/src/generated/graphql.ts` regenerated in the same PR. `console/web/src/graphql/operations.graphql` is NOT touched: the `DeployLag` query keeps selecting exactly the fields it selects today, so `DeployLagDocument`'s result type is unchanged and the strip compiles and renders as built. Selecting `repo` on the strip is a later One River addition through `mid_epic.py`, not this card's.

**Files:** console/backend/deploy_lag.py, console/backend/tests/test_deploy_lag.py, console/backend/schema.py, console/web/schema.graphql, console/web/src/generated/graphql.ts

## Contract

Reads `.github/bureau/release.json` in the shape fixed in DRE-3213 and DRE-3167 — `surfaces.<name>.{tag_series, paths, record}` are the three fields this module consumes; the rest are the train's. Surface names, the `record` vocabulary (`tag` | `channel`) and the row order are shared with DRE-3238 verbatim.

The GraphQL after this card — everything in DRE-3107's contract unchanged, plus one field:

```graphql

With the browser's network panel open, rename (PATCH) a real document id in another organisation's folder — a `d-…` slug the operator picks from the live library — and then a slug that names nothing. cards.description:
The mechanical proof of "every surface that can refuse on an item id", so the next leak fails CI instead of waiting to be found by accident. `infra/test/section_7_conformance.test.ts` already holds PROBES/EXCLUSIONS in set-equality with the route table and drives every probed route with a shelf template versus a ghost. That oracle cannot see the defect this epic closes: it drives the SHELF, "where the caller was shown nothing", and its own header says the ordinary-document question is DRE-2926's. This card adds the second oracle to the same mechanism, so the gate card's rule (DRE-3200) and the parent-slot reorder are proven over EVERY id-bearing route, not only the ones those cards enumerated.

Add §2b: for every PROBES entry, the same request driven with **another customer's real item** and with `NO_SUCH_ID`, asserted byte-identical with the probed id scrubbed, for a subject that holds NO effective role on it. That subject exists on exactly two shapes and the other two are excluded with the reason written down: `folder-only` (the respondent, granted only on `f-oncor`, probing `f-acme`'s document and folder) and `root-domain` with a **stranger** — a project member at a third domain the root grant does not name, so nothing is visible to them. Under `zero-grant` the pre-cutover fallback shows every member every item and under `root-group` the bridge grant does, so in both the caller was already shown the item and a refusal that names it discloses nothing — the same reasoning `write_gates_section_7.test.ts` §2 records. Each PROBES entry declares which hidden id it is driven with, `hidden: 'doc' | 'folder'`, because the create routes and the two move slots carry a `parentId` and the hidden thing there is a folder; `seedWorld` returns `otherFolderId` beside `otherDocId` for it.

Then the records catch up. The PROBES comment saying `assertParentFolder` runs on the raw tree before the write gate is rewritten to the order the parent-slot card established; the header's "WHAT THIS FILE IS NOT" paragraph is replaced by one saying the ordinary-document oracle is now §2b and what decided it (the operator, 2026-09-01, on the epic); `test/disclosure.test.ts`'s governed list gains `POST /access/request` (existence-blind by never reading the partition) and the create/move parent slot (gate before parent check), beside the item-write entry the gate card wrote there. `ORACLE_GAPS` grows a `subject` dimension only if §2b finds a split the siblings left — and then it names a real card, filed as a mid-epic addition, never this epic's id. The expected result is that it finds none; the file reports whichever is true.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] §2b runs every PROBES route × {folder-only respondent, root-domain stranger} with the declared hidden doc or folder against `NO_SUCH_ID` and asserts status, headers and scrubbed body byte-identical, and that neither the other customer's document title nor folder name rides out.
- [ ] `zero-grant` and `root-group` are excluded from §2b in code with the written reason (the caller was shown the item), and a test asserts the excluded-shape list is exactly those two.

cards.title: The parent slot on the create and move routes: the write gate runs before the parent-folder check, so a hidden folder and a ghost parent answer the same bytes
cards.description:
The one item-id slot the gate card DRE-3200 cannot reach from inside the gate, found while planning this epic. Every create route and both move slots in `infra/lambda/routes/library.ts` run `assertParentFolder(parentId, tree)` on the RAW tree **before** `assertWrite` — seven sites, read off the file on 2026-09-05: `POST /library/folders` (line ~742), `PATCH /library/folders/{id}` move slot (~802), `POST /library/docs` (~889), `POST /library/docs/link` (~993), `POST /library/docs/external` (~1142), `POST /library/docs/form` (~1519), `PATCH /library/docs/{id}` move slot (~1687). Read the handlers rather than trusting the line numbers, and check `POST /library/docs/upload-url` for the same pair.

A `parentId` naming a folder the caller cannot open passes the parent check (it IS a folder) and is then refused by the gate — 403 today, the §7 404 once DRE-3200 lands — while a `parentId` that never existed is refused **400** `parent folder "<id>" not found` by the check itself. Two different answers for "a folder you cannot see" and "no such folder". It is the ordering defect DRE-2906 fixed for `findLibItem` ("a finder that ran one line too early"), in the one slot DRE-2906's template probe could not see: a template is not a folder, so it got the 400 on both arms and the probe passed.

The fix is the order at every site and nothing else: `assertWrite({ …, itemId: parentId ?? ROOT_ITEM_ID })` **first**, then `assertParentFolder`, then the cycle and depth checks as today. For a non-moderator the gate answers a hidden folder and a ghost with one `hiddenItem()` (`chainOf` throws on the ghost, the gate turns that into the §7 body); a visible non-folder still gets the 400, which discloses nothing to a caller who can already see it. For a moderator nothing changes: the gate resolves against the raw tree, a ghost leaves it with no role and falls through to `assertModerator ∧ assertKnownProject`, and the parent check still says `parent folder "<id>" not found`, as it does today. Every moderator write that succeeded before still succeeds.

Pins that say "a non-moderator posting to an unknown parent gets 400" are rewritten to the new order with the reason kept, never deleted — `grep -n 'parent folder' infra/test/*.test.ts` is the list. `write_gates_section_7.test.ts` §4 (the move-target slot) stays green if it asserts byte-identity and is rewritten if it pinned the 400. The new test drives all seven sites with another customer's folder and a ghost as `parentId`, as a folder-only respondent, and asserts status, headers and body byte-identical with nothing written, plus positive controls.

**Files:** infra/lambda/routes/library.ts, infra/test/parent_slot_gate_order.test.ts, infra/test/write_gates_section_7.test.ts

## Do not

* Do not change what `assertParentFolder` itself answers — the 400 stays for a visible non-folder and for every moderator.
* Do not touch `access_lib.ts`; the gate's rule is DRE-3200's.
* Do not edit `test/section_7_conformance.test.ts` — its PROBES comment on this ordering is corrected by the sibling that owns that file.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] At every create and move site in `routes/library.ts`, `assertWrite` on the parent runs before `assertParentFolder`; `test/parent_slot_gate_order.test.ts` enumerates the sites by route key and goes red if one is missed.
- [ ] Folder-only partition, respondent with a viewer grant on their own folder: each site driven with another customer's folder id as `parentId` and with `d-no-such-document-at-all` answers byte-identical (status, headers, body) with no write recorded on the double.
- [ ] A moderator posting to a ghost parent still receives `400 parent folder "<id>" not found`; an editor on a visible folder still creates inside it; a respondent moving their own document into a visible non-folder still gets the 400 (positive controls, all three).
- [ ] Every pre-existing pin of the 400 for a non-moderator is rewritten to the new order with a header saying why the 400 was there and what replaced it; none deleted.
- [ ] `cd infra && npm run verify` green; TDD commit order holds; the PR body carries the mutation table (revert one site's reorder, name the test that reddens).

**Blocked by:** DRE-3200

cards.title: Request access, existence-blind: POST /access/request answers one 202 for a hidden item and a ghost, and mails the project's moderators
cards.description:
The half of the operator's decision (recorded on the epic, 2026-09-01) that gives the reader a way forward. Once the gate card DRE-3200 lands, a project member with no grant meets 404 on a real document exactly as on a broken link; this card gives every such 404 an action — **request access** — that confirms nothing. It is a new route and it exists in no form today (no route, no storage, no notification, no UI). DRE-2951 described it as a standalone card and never went through planning; this card supersedes it inside the epic.

**The rule it must hold:** the route accepts identically for an id that names a real item the caller cannot open and for an id that never existed — same status, same headers, same body, same DynamoDB command sequence, same notification behaviour. It achieves that **by never reading the library partition at all**: nothing in the handler looks the id up. The id is carried, as the caller typed it, into an email to the project's moderators, who open the library themselves and decide. Existence-blind by construction, not by care.

What to build, in `infra/lambda/routes/access.ts` (the handler, I/O only) with a new pure module `infra/lambda/access_request_lib.ts` (every decision: body validation, the recipient rule, the email text — no AWS SDK import, the house rule):

1. `POST /access/request`, registered in `manifests/access.routes.ts`. Body `{ project, itemId, note? }`. `assertProjectAccess(groups, project)` first — a non-member gets the project-level 403 every route gives, which is the edge gate's own line and item-blind (TWO DOORS, `test/disclosure.test.ts`). Then validate: `itemId` a non-empty string of at most 200 characters; `note` optional, trimmed, at most 500 characters, control characters stripped (it lands in an email body). Then answer `202 {"ok":true}` — always.
2. Recipients = the project's moderators: members of `MODERATOR_GROUP` ∩ members of the `<project>` group, both walked with `cognito_lib.collectAllUsers` over `ListUsersInGroupCommand` (the IAM the API Lambda already holds — `lib/comment-stack.ts` grants `cognito-idp:ListUsersInGroup` for `GET /people`), matched on the email attribute, lower-cased. The intersection rule is pure and lives in the lib. The Cognito calls do not depend on the item, so the work is equal by construction.
3. Sender = `notify_lib.resolveSender(project, NOTIFY_FROM)`; null means no mail is sent and the caller still gets the same 202 (the shipped state of `gridcorr`, which has no `notifyFrom` in `config/dreadnought.json` — the plan names that as an operator follow-up, not this card's problem). Send through `notify.sendToAll` wrapped by `db_lib.makeNotifySafe` exactly as `routes/comments.ts` and `routes/responses.ts` do, and expose it the way responses.ts exposes `submitNotifier` — `export const accessRequestNotifier: { send: typeof sendToAll }` — so the test counts sends without SES.
4. The email is a pure function of (requester email + name from the verified claims, project, `itemId` as typed, note, `notify_lib.portalBaseFor(project, PORTAL_BASE_URL)`): subject `Access request from <email> — <project>`, text naming who asked, the id they asked about, the note, and the portal's library link. **No title, no kind, no "this item exists" or "does not exist"** — the route does not know and must not find out. The requester's email is in the text so the moderator can reply; no Reply-To header is added (`mime_lib` has none and this card does not add one).
5. Rate-limit with its OWN bucket through the `RateOverride` mechanism `routes/index.ts` already exposes in `IDEMPOTENCY_EXEMPT_ROUTES` (exemption from replay recording is right here: a replayed request is one duplicate email, not a second thing created — `test/idempotency_lib.test.ts` already handles exempt routes generically): `ACCESS_REQUEST_RATE_CAPACITY = 3`, `ACCESS_REQUEST_REFILL_PER_SEC = 1 / 300` (a burst of three, then one every five minutes), exported from `routes/access.ts` beside the route key `ACCESS_REQUEST_ROUTE_KEY = 'POST /access/request'`, the way responses.ts exports `PRESENCE_*`. The 429 is the guard's existing `too many changes — wait a moment and retry`, which names nothing about the item.
6. `test/section_7_conformance.test.ts` §1 goes red the moment the manifest grows, by design. Add ONE PROBES entry for `POST /access/request` driving `itemId` — the template-vs-ghost oracle then holds for free, which is the proof the route is blind. Touch nothing else in that file; the sibling that adds the hidden-document oracle owns the rest of it.
7. The response shape joins the fixture protocol: `test/api_shapes.test.ts` emits `fixtures/api-shapes/access-request-accepted.json` = `{"ok":true}` so the client card validates against the same bytes.

**Files:** infra/lambda/access_request_lib.ts, infra/lambda/routes/access.ts, infra/lambda/routes/manifests/access.routes.ts, infra/lambda/routes/index.ts, infra/test/access_request_lib.test.ts, infra/test/access_request_route.test.ts, infra/test/section_7_conformance.test.ts, infra/test/api_shapes.test.ts, infra/test/fixtures/api-shapes/access-request-accepted.json

## Contract (shared with the request-access client card)

* Route key: `POST /access/request`, authorizer `jwt`.
* Request body: `{"project":"<slug>","itemId":"<id>","note":"<optional, ≤500 chars>"}`.
* Accepted response: status `202`, `content-type: application/json`, body exactly `{"ok":true}` — for every project member, whether or not `itemId` names anything.
* Refusals: `403` from `assertProjectAccess` (non-member), `400` for a malformed body (never echoing an over-long id), `429` from the shared guard — none of them varies with the item.
* Fixture: `infra/test/fixtures/api-shapes/access-request-accepted.json`.
* Nothing is stored. No `req#` row, no change-log event — a log event keyed on a real id and dropped for a ghost is a leak by work, and a moderator inbox is a later feature if the emails prove insufficient.

## Do not

* Do not read the library partition `lib#<project>` anywhere in the handler — not to find a title, not to pick a per-kind link, not to check the kind.
* Do not vary the notification on existence — sending only for real ids leaks by absence, one step removed.
* Do not touch `access_lib.ts`, `routes/library.ts` or `test/disclosure.test.ts` — siblings own them.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `test/access_request_route.test.ts` (black-box through `handler(event)`, `InMemoryDdb` recording commands, the Cognito prototype double from `test/handler_contract.test.ts`, `accessRequestNotifier.send` swapped): for a project member with no grant, the request on a REAL hidden document and on `d-no-such-document-at-all` produce byte-identical status/headers/body, an identical recorded DynamoDB command list, and identical send calls with only the id differing — on the `folder-only` and `root-domain` shapes `write_gates_section_7.test.ts` seeds.
- [ ] The email reaches exactly the moderators who are also members of the project (a moderator of another project and a plain member receive nothing), names the requester's email and the id as typed, and contains no title.
- [ ] With `NOTIFY_FROM` unset, or set but not resolving for the project, the caller still receives `202 {"ok":true}` and zero sends occur.
- [ ] The rate-limit refusal after the bucket empties is byte-identical for a real id and a ghost id; a non-member gets the same 403 for both.
- [ ] `note` is capped at 500 characters and stripped of control characters before it is placed in the email; an `itemId` over 200 characters is a 400 that does not echo it.
- [ ] `section_7_conformance.test.ts` §1 is green with the new PROBES entry and §2 holds for the route on all four shapes.
- [ ] `api_shapes.test.ts` emits the fixture; `cd infra && npm run verify` green; TDD commit order holds (the route test lands before the handler).
- [ ] Mutation-proven: the PR body names the test that reddens when (a) the handler reads the partition to add a title, (b) the send is skipped for a ghost.

cards.title: PROOF: limit-killed runs observed coming back on a real account switch, recorded with PT times
cards.description:
The proof is the mechanism observed running against real state on a real account switch, with the observation written into the repo — not a green suite. An operator, at an interactive session with the console open, records one live cycle end to end and commits the record.

What the operator does, by hand: wait for (or reproduce, by pointing `CLAUDE_ACCOUNT`/the active token at an account that is at its five-hour limit) a run that dies with the `You've hit your limit` receipt in at least three stages — one plan or classify death (a card in Planning), one build death (a card In Progress) and one review death (a PR in review). Read each card's thread and confirm exactly ONE `🪦 claude-limit-death` receipt naming `stage=`, `account=`, `resets=` and `run=`, no `dead-run-requeue`, no `model-error:` marker, and that the medic's `retry-declined` receipt names `usage-limit` where the medic saw the run. Then switch the active account (or let the window reset), note the PT time, and watch the next reconcile sweep: each card gets one `🔁 claude-limit-redispatch` receipt naming the trigger (`account switched Dreadnought → DeltaSolv` or `window reset at HH:MM PT`), the plan/classify card's ORIGINAL run shows attempt 2 on GitHub, the build card moves to Todo and dispatches, the review PR's ORIGINAL `pull_request` run shows attempt 2 (no new `workflow_dispatch` run in the review stub's list), and the console's Alerts row reads `N runs waiting on the account switch` before the sweep and disappears after it.

**Files:** architecture/audits/limit-wait-proof-2026-09.md (new — the record, committed by the operator: card ids, run ids with attempt numbers, PT times of death, switch and re-dispatch, the exact receipt lines, the Alerts row before and after)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Observed live, by hand, on a real account switch or window reset in production: at least three stages (one of classify/plan, build, review) each got exactly one `claude-limit-death` receipt and exactly one `claude-limit-redispatch` receipt naming the trigger, with PT times recorded
- [ ] Observed live: none of the cards spent a `dead-run-requeue` strike and none carried a `model-error:` marker from the limit death; the medic posted `retry-declined` with rule `usage-limit` and no attempt-2 rerun of its own
- [ ] Observed live: the review re-dispatch is attempt 2 of the original `pull_request` run in GitHub's run list, and no `workflow_dispatch` review run was created for that head
- [ ] Observed live: the console's Alerts page showed `N runs waiting on the account switch` while the cards waited and showed no row after the sweep, without anyone touching it
- [ ] The record above is merged to `main` in `architecture/audits/`, and the epic's description is updated by hand with the PT times (the epic's own acceptance criterion asks for them there)

**Blocked by:** DRE-3185, DRE-3179, DRE-3186, DRE-3187, DRE-3188, DRE-3189, DRE-3194, DRE-3195, DRE-3196, DRE-3197

cards.title: Console Alerts row: N runs waiting on the account switch (agent-bureau)
cards.description:
The console's Alerts page shows `N runs waiting on the account switch` while any limit-killed run is outstanding, and the count goes to zero on its own. This is the agent-bureau half of the epic (the console's alert row), split out because it is a different repo and a different tier. The pipeline side posts a `claude-limit-death` receipt on every card whose run died on the Claude account's five-hour limit and a `claude-limit-redispatch` receipt when the sweep brings the work back; the console already reads card receipts by act tag (`console/backend/receipts.py:ACTS`, which the console-first card taught the two tags). This card adds one alert row computed from those receipts and nothing else — no button, no switch control (the switch itself is DRE-3170's).

The row appears on the Alerts page only while the count is above zero, reads exactly `N runs waiting on the account switch` (singular `1 run`), and lists the waiting cards beneath it as links with their stage and the account recorded on the death. The count is derived, never stored: for every open card (not Done, not Canceled), take the newest `claude-limit-death` receipt; the card is waiting unless a LATER comment carries `claude-limit-redispatch` or starts with `🧠 model-attempt:` — the same predicate `limit_wait.waiting()` implements in bureau-pipeline, restated here because the two repos share no module. When nothing is waiting the row is absent, not "0 runs".

**Files:** console/backend/alerts.py, console/backend/tests/test_alerts_limit_wait.py (new), and the Alerts page component in the console frontend that renders alert rows (one row added; locate the existing alerts list component rather than creating a page)

## Contract (shared with siblings — identical in every card)

* **Death receipt.** Tag `claude-limit-death`; first line `🪦 claude-limit-death: stage=<classify|plan|build|fix|review> account=<identity> resets=<ISO|unknown> run=<run URL>` followed by `—` and a sentence. Parse `stage=`, `account=`, `resets=` off the first line by key, never by position.
* **Re-dispatch receipt.** Tag `claude-limit-redispatch`; first line `🔁 claude-limit-redispatch: <trigger> — <what>`.
* **Waiting predicate.** newest `claude-limit-death` on the card, unless a later comment contains `claude-limit-redispatch` or starts with `🧠 model-attempt:`.
* **Row text.** `N runs waiting on the account switch` (`1 run waiting on the account switch`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With three open cards whose newest receipt is a `claude-limit-death`, one of which has a later `claude-limit-redispatch` and one a later `🧠 model-attempt:` comment, the alerts backend reports a count of 1 and lists that card with its stage and account; a Done card with a bare death receipt is not counted
- [ ] The Alerts page renders the row `1 run waiting on the account switch` from that data and renders no row at all when the count is 0 (rendered-output test, the console's existing alerts test pattern)
- [ ] The row uses the console's design tokens (`console/design/tokens.css` custom properties) and the existing alert-row component; no new styles are hard-coded
- [ ] The console's act-registry test and every existing console test still pass

**Blocked by:** DRE-3185

cards.title: The sweep re-runs a merged PR's original linear-sync run before closing the card directly (reconcile.py)
cards.description:
The merge sync has the same gap, and the same remedy: re-run the ORIGINAL run, never a hand-named dispatch. On 2026-09-05 PR #2295 (DRE-3110) merged at 10:14 PT; the `linear-sync` run that closes the card fired once at 10:14:51 PT, died on the Linear rate limit, and nothing re-fired it — a merge event happens exactly once. The card sat In Review for 42 minutes with its code on `main`, DRE-3062 (blocked by it) could not promote, until an assistant ran `gh run rerun 33980354743` by hand; DRE-3140's sync run died and was re-run by hand the same day. The sweep's existing merged-PR backstop (the `PR was already merged — moved to Done` branch of the nudge loop) closes such a card directly — but it runs on a cron that lands 78–100 minutes apart in practice, and closing directly skips what the sync run also does: the merge-sweep gate that promotes the dependents.

This card teaches the merged-PR branch to try the original run first. When a card in the review lane has a MERGED PR, the sweep looks up the `linear-sync` stub's most recent run for that PR's head sha with `event == pull_request` (`gh run list --workflow <stub> --event pull_request --json databaseId,headSha,conclusion,status`, resolved through a `sync_workflow()` helper beside `review_workflow()`); if that run concluded `failure` and the card carries no `merge-sync-rerun` receipt naming its id, the sweep calls the sibling card's `gh_rerun(run_id)` and posts ONE `merge-sync-rerun` receipt naming the run (through `pipeline_act.receipt("merge-sync-rerun", …)` composed at the site, the reconcile shape) — and leaves the card for that run to close. If no such failed run exists, or the receipt is already there and the card is still not Done on a later sweep, the direct close runs exactly as today. One re-run per run id, ever: the receipt is the counter. The act is declared in `config/pipeline-acts.json` (kind `recovery`, state `dispatched`, `next_actor`/`subscriber` `linear-sync.yml`, `emits` at the reconcile site); the console already carries the tag (the console-first card).

**Files:** scripts/reconcile.py, config/pipeline-acts.json, tests/test_reconcile_merge_sync_rerun.py (new)

## Contract (shared with siblings — identical in every card)

* **Act.** `merge-sync-rerun`, tag `merge-sync-rerun`, kind `recovery`, state `dispatched`. Receipt: one line starting `🔁 merge-sync-rerun: run <run id> re-run — the merge sync for <PR URL> died before it closed this card`, followed by one plain-English sentence. Neither the tag nor the name may be a substring of any other act's tag or name (`pipeline_act.problems()` must stay empty).
* **Re-run helper.** `reconcile.gh_rerun(run_id) -> bool` — `gh run rerun <id> --failed` under `GH_DISPATCH_TOKEN`, True only on rc=0. Owned by the sweep limit-pass card; this card calls it.
* **Order.** Original-run re-run first, direct close second, never both in one sweep.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With the seams stubbed, a review-lane card whose PR is merged and whose sync run for that head concluded `failure` gets exactly one `gh run rerun <id> --failed` call and one `merge-sync-rerun` receipt naming that id, and is NOT moved to Done in that sweep; the next sweep, with the receipt present and the card still open, moves it to Done through the existing branch
- [ ] A merged PR whose sync run succeeded, or has no `pull_request` run at all, takes the existing direct-close path unchanged; a `gh run rerun` stub returning rc=1 posts no receipt and records one `_write_failures` entry
- [ ] A test pins that the re-run is `gh run rerun` of the listed run id and that no `gh workflow run` of the sync stub is ever issued for this path
- [ ] `config/pipeline-acts.json` declares `merge-sync-rerun` with `emits` at the reconcile site; `pipeline_act.py check`, `check_act_receipts.py` and `tests/test_pipeline_acts_consumers.py` pass (the console-first card has already landed the tag)
- [ ] Every existing test under `tests/` still passes

**Blocked by:** DRE-3179, DRE-3195, DRE-3185

cards.title: The sweep re-dispatches limit-killed work when the account changes or the window resets, bounded by the WIP cap (reconcile.py)
cards.description:
The sweep re-dispatches limit-killed work when the world changes. Today nothing reads the receipts back: after the CEO switched the account to DeltaSolv at 10:44 PT on 2026-09-05 every dead card stayed where its death left it until an assistant bounced each by hand. `reconcile.py` has no notion of a Claude account at all (its only quotas are GitHub's and Linear's) and no `gh run rerun` machinery — every review restart in it is a fresh `workflow_dispatch` of the review stub, which is the DRE-2853 mistake this card must not repeat.

This card adds one pass, `redispatch_limit_killed()`, to the backstop tuple in `main()` (after `recover_crashed_reviews`, so it gets the per-pass `ReconcileWriteError` isolation), and one helper beside `gh_dispatch()`: `gh_rerun(run_id) -> bool` (`gh run rerun <id> --failed` under `GH_DISPATCH_TOKEN`, which the stubs grant `actions: write`; True only on rc=0). The pass reads `limit_wait.waiting(card_comment_bodies(card))` over the active cards in `Planning`, `In Progress` and `In Review` (never Green Light, Backlog, Done or Canceled — a card that moved on is not a candidate), skips `held()`/`needs-human`, `hand_built()` and `card_parked_for_human()` cards, computes `limit_wait.trigger(death, limit_wait.account_identity(os.environ), now)`, and for each card with a trigger — oldest receipt first, at most `MAX_WIP` per sweep, the rest left marked for the next pass — re-enters the stage that died:

* `classify` / `plan` (card in Planning): `gh_rerun(death.run_id)` — the original plan run, guarded on the run's `status == completed`.
* `build` (In Progress): `linear_ops.cmd_state(ident, "Todo")` — the relay dispatches; NO `dead-run-requeue` receipt.
* `fix` (In Review, PR open): the same `_nudge(fix_workflow(), pr_number)` dispatch `retry_dead_fix_runs` performs, honouring `FixLane` and `fix_dispatch_blocked`.
* `review` (In Review, PR open): `gh_rerun(death.run_id)` of the ORIGINAL run named on the receipt — never `_nudge(review_workflow(), …)`; guarded on the PR still being open and `gh run view <id> --json headSha` equalling the PR's current head; if the head moved, a fresh review already ran, so the pass posts the re-dispatch receipt saying no re-run was needed and does nothing else.

Every action posts exactly ONE `claude-limit-redispatch` receipt through `limit_wait.post_redispatch(ident, trigger, what)` and only after the dispatch reported success (DRE-1254's false-receipt class: a rerun that 403'd must not tell the card it restarted; failures go to `_write_failures`). The pass prints `limit-wait: N run(s) waiting on the account switch` every sweep (N counts every waiting card, dispatched or not, and is 0 when none). Four existing passes learn to leave a waiting card alone, each pinned: the In-Progress dead-run requeue and the review-lane no-PR requeue (a limit death must not become a `dead-run-requeue` strike after `STALE_MINUTES`), `flag_stranded`/`flag_stalled_planning` (a waiting Planning card is not stranded), and `recover_crashed_reviews` (a PR whose card is waiting is not re-dispatched into the limit and spends none of `CRASHED_REVIEW_RETRY_CAP`). `reconcile.yml`'s Sweep step gains `CLAUDE_ACCOUNT: ${{ vars.CLAUDE_ACCOUNT }}` and the Claude credential under the same `vars.CLAUDE_AUTH_MODE` switch every Select-model step uses (the secrets are already declared in the reusable's `secrets:` block and never passed today), so `account_identity` resolves inside the sweep; nothing else in that file changes.

**Files:** scripts/reconcile.py, .github/workflows/reconcile.yml, tests/test_reconcile_limit_redispatch.py (new), tests/test_reconcile_limit_wait_guards.py (new)

## Contract (shared with siblings — identical in every card)

* **Waiting predicate.** `limit_wait.waiting(bodies_oldest_to_newest) -> LimitDeath | None` — the newest `claude-limit-death` receipt unless a LATER comment carries `claude-limit-redispatch` or starts with `🧠 model-attempt:`. `LimitDeath` carries `stage, account, resets, run_url, run_id, posted_at`.
* **Trigger.** `limit_wait.trigger(death, account, now) -> str | None` — exactly one of `account switched <old> → <new>` or `window reset at <HH:MM> PT (<ISO>)`; `resets=unknown` reads as the receipt's posting time + 5 hours.
* **Re-dispatch receipt.** Act `limit-redispatch`, tag `claude-limit-redispatch`, one line starting `🔁 claude-limit-redispatch: <trigger> — <what was re-dispatched>`, posted ONLY through `limit_wait.post_redispatch(identifier, trigger, what)` (composes and writes in one function, the `medic_retry.post_declined` shape the receipt guard recognises).
* **Account identity.** `limit_wait.account_identity(env)`: `CLAUDE_ACCOUNT` when set, else `fp:` + 12 hex of SHA-256 of the credential, else `unknown`. An `unknown` sweep identity never fires the account trigger (unknown ≠ recorded is not a switch); the reset trigger still works.
* **Bound.** `MAX_WIP` (the sweep's existing cap, `resolve_max_wip`) re-dispatches per sweep, oldest receipt first.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With the Linear and `gh` seams stubbed (the `tests/test_reconcile_retries_dead_fix_runs.py` pattern), a board of five waiting cards — one per stage — and `CLAUDE_ACCOUNT=DeltaSolv` against receipts recording `Dreadnought` re-dispatches all five in one sweep: the Planning ones through `gh run rerun <receipt run id> --failed`, the build one through `cmd_state(…, "Todo")` with no `dead-run-requeue` text posted, the fix one through `_nudge(fix_workflow(), pr)`, the review one through `gh run rerun` of the receipt's run id — and asserts NO `gh workflow run` of the review stub was issued (this is the DRE-2853 pin)
- [ ] The same board with the account unchanged and `now` before every reset re-dispatches nothing and prints `limit-wait: 5 run(s) waiting on the account switch`; with `now` past one card's reset it re-dispatches that one with the `window reset at HH:MM PT` trigger and prints 4 waiting afterwards
- [ ] With `MAX_WIP=2` and five triggered cards, exactly two are re-dispatched, three stay marked, and the next sweep (their receipts still the newest) takes the next two
- [ ] A card whose thread has a `🧠 model-attempt:` newer than its death, a card already carrying a `claude-limit-redispatch` after its death, a card in Done/Canceled/Green Light, and a card labelled `needs-human` are each left untouched; a review PR whose head moved since the run gets a re-dispatch receipt reading "no re-run needed" and no `gh` call
- [ ] A receipt is posted only after the dispatch succeeded: a `gh run rerun` stub returning rc=1 yields no `claude-limit-redispatch` comment and one `_write_failures` entry
- [ ] Guard tests: a waiting In-Progress card older than `STALE_MINUTES` is not requeued and gets no `dead-run-requeue`; a waiting Planning card older than `PLANNING_MINUTES` gets no `stranded-watchdog`; a PR whose card is waiting is skipped by `recover_crashed_reviews` with no `crashed-review-redispatch`
- [ ] `check_reconcile_env.py`, `check_wip_cap.py`, `check_act_receipts.py` and `pipeline_act.py check` all pass; the sweep env in `reconcile.yml` carries `CLAUDE_ACCOUNT` and the credential under the `vars.CLAUDE_AUTH_MODE` switch (pinned by a wiring test)

**Blocked by:** DRE-3179

cards.title: The medic declines its retry on a limit death and never diagnoses one (medic_retry.py, medic.yml)
cards.description:
The medic stops retrying into a known limit. `medic.yml` re-runs a failed run once (`gh run rerun --failed`) unless `medic_retry.py decide` says no; today it says no for two rules only — the card is parked for a human, or the run died of turn exhaustion (DRE-2954). A limit death is the same kind of thing as turn exhaustion: deterministic on something a rerun does not change (the ACCOUNT's five-hour window, not the model, not the card), so the rerun sixty seconds later dies identically — DRE-3168's medic rerun on 2026-09-05, one minute after the original. And on a run's second attempt (which the sweep's re-run will now create) the medic's `diagnose` job would dispatch a diagnosis agent at a limit death, burning inference to report "the account is at its limit".

This card adds the third rule, `usage-limit`, read from two witnesses exactly as the turn-exhaustion rule is: the failed run's own execution record reconstructed from its log (`execution_from_log` → `check_agent_result.classify_death` == `DEATH_LIMIT`), and the card's own `claude-limit-death` receipt posted after the run started (`_newest_after(receipts, "claude-limit-death", run_started_at)`, the second witness that survives an unreadable log). The decline posts the existing `retry-declined` receipt with `Rule applied: usage-limit` and a detail sentence naming the account and reset time off the receipt when it has one. `medic.yml`'s `diagnose` job additionally requires `needs.classify.outputs.rule != 'usage-limit'`, so a limit death is never diagnosed on any attempt — there is no defect to find, the same reasoning as the Linear rate-limit class. No new act, no new tag: the refusal is the one the registry already declares. There is no medic brief file (`assemble_context.py` gives the medic standards only), so the one-line brief change the epic mentions has nowhere to go; the rule lives in the module and the workflow comment.

**Files:** scripts/medic_retry.py, .github/workflows/medic.yml, tests/test_medic_retry_usage_limit.py (new)

## Contract (shared with siblings — identical in every card)

* **Death class.** `check_agent_result.DEATH_LIMIT = "usage_limit"`. Owned by DRE-3179; this card reads it through `classify_death`, never a local regex.
* **Death receipt tag.** `claude-limit-death` — the second witness; parsed with `limit_wait.parse_death(body)` for the account and reset time named in the decline detail.
* **Rule name.** `medic_retry.RULE_USAGE_LIMIT = "usage-limit"`, printed as `rule=usage-limit` in `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` and as `Rule applied: usage-limit.` on the `retry-declined` receipt.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `medic_retry.decide(execution={"is_error": True, "result": "You've hit your limit · resets 8:30pm (UTC)"})` returns `Decision(DECLINE, "usage-limit", …)`; `decide(limit_receipt="🪦 claude-limit-death: stage=plan account=Dreadnought resets=2026-09-05T20:30:00Z run=…")` with no execution also declines under `usage-limit` and the detail names `Dreadnought` and the reset time; the park rule still wins when both apply
- [ ] `execution_from_log` over a real `gh run view --log-failed` shape carrying the agent-result gate's failure block with `result: You've hit your limit …` yields a record `classify_death` reads as `usage_limit` (fixture built the way `tests/test_medic_retry_honours_the_park.py` builds its log)
- [ ] The `decide` CLI prints `retry=false` and `rule=usage-limit` for such a run, and `post` composes the receipt through `pipeline_act.receipt("retry-declined", …)` unchanged
- [ ] A wiring test reads `medic.yml` and pins that the `diagnose` job's `if` contains `needs.classify.outputs.rule != 'usage-limit'` and that the `retry` job's gate is unchanged (`retry != 'false'`)
- [ ] A turn-exhaustion death, an infra flake, a pre-agent death and a run with no record all keep their retry (every existing test under `tests/` still passes)

cards.title: The fix stage records a limit death without spending the outage budget or parking the card (agent-fix.yml, fix_dead_run.py)
cards.description:
The FIX stage learns to record a limit death. Today `agent-fix.yml`'s Report step, on "no new commit", asks `fix_dead_run.py decide`, which classifies every `api_death` as an outage: it posts the `⚡ fix-run-model-death` marker on the PR and the sweep's `retry_dead_fix_runs` re-dispatches the fix agent on its very next pass — into the same limit — spending one of `RETRY_CAP` consecutive deaths each time, until the hold parks the card as "the AI service failed several fix runs in a row… an outage or account problem".

With this card `fix_dead_run.decide()` returns a new action `wait` when `check_agent_result.classify_death(execution) == DEATH_LIMIT`: an EMPTY body (the PR gets no marker at all — a `fix-run-model-death` marker is exactly the thing that would make the sweep re-dispatch immediately), no fix-attempt budget spent, no park. The workflow's `wait` branch posts ONE `claude-limit-death` receipt on the CARD through `limit_wait.py post-death --card "$CARD" --stage fix --run-url "$RUN_URL" --execution-file "$EXEC_FILE"`, and one plain PR note composed through the same act (`pipeline_act.py receipt limit-death --body "$BODY" --out <file>` then `gh pr comment --body-file`, the shape the `fix-attempt-landed` site already uses) so a reader on the PR sees why nothing is happening. The card is neither parked nor labelled; the sweep's limit pass (a sibling card) re-dispatches the fix agent through the same dispatch `retry_dead_fix_runs` uses once the account changes or the window resets. `usage_limit` is checked before the outage and turn-exhaustion branches, and the `escalate` (model ran, pushed nothing) path is unchanged. The Report step's env carries `CLAUDE_ACCOUNT: ${{ vars.CLAUDE_ACCOUNT }}` and the credential under the `vars.CLAUDE_AUTH_MODE` switch the Select-model step uses.

**Files:** .github/workflows/agent-fix.yml, scripts/fix_dead_run.py, tests/test_fix_dead_run_usage_limit.py (new), tests/test_agent_fix_usage_limit_wiring.py (new)

## Contract (shared with siblings — identical in every card)

* **Death class.** `check_agent_result.DEATH_LIMIT = "usage_limit"`; `classify_death()` returns it for a record whose `result`/`errors` text contains `hit your limit` (case-insensitive). Owned by DRE-3179.
* **Death receipt.** Act `limit-death`, tag `claude-limit-death`, one line starting exactly `🪦 claude-limit-death: stage=<classify|plan|build|fix|review> account=<identity> resets=<ISO|unknown> run=<run URL>` followed by `—` and one plain-English sentence. Posted ONLY through `python3 .bureau-pipeline/scripts/limit_wait.py post-death --card <CARD> --stage <S> --run-url <U> [--result-text <T> | --execution-file <F>]`. On a fix-stage receipt the sweep re-dispatches the FIX agent (never a review) for the PR the card owns.
* `fix_dead_run.decide(execution, …)` → `Decision("wait", "")` on a limit death. The action word `wait` is printed on line 1 exactly as `retry`/`hold`/`escalate` are. `fix_dead_run.RETRY_MARKERS` is unchanged — no limit marker is ever a retry marker.
* **Account identity.** `CLAUDE_ACCOUNT` (`vars.CLAUDE_ACCOUNT`) when set; else `fp:` + 12 hex of SHA-256 of the credential; else `unknown` — `limit_wait.account_identity(env)`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `fix_dead_run.decide({"is_error": true, "num_turns": 1, "total_cost_usd": 0, "duration_ms": 400, "result": "You've hit your limit · resets 8:30pm (UTC)"}, prior_deaths=2)` returns action `wait` with an empty body — even at the cap, a limit death never holds; the same record with the phrase removed still returns `retry` with the `fix-run-model-death` marker (unchanged)
- [ ] `consecutive_prior_deaths()` over a PR thread that carries only the plain limit note (no marker) counts 0 — a limit wait pre-exhausts no outage budget
- [ ] A wiring test reads `agent-fix.yml` and pins: the `wait` branch calls `limit_wait.py post-death --stage fix`, composes its PR note through `pipeline_act.py receipt limit-death`, and calls neither `park_for_human` nor `add-label`; the `retry`, `retry-turns`, `hold-turns`, `hold` and escalate branches are textually unchanged
- [ ] The Report step's env carries `CLAUDE_ACCOUNT` and the Claude credential under the `vars.CLAUDE_AUTH_MODE` switch (pinned)
- [ ] `reconcile.retry_dead_fix_runs` (read, not modified here) does not dispatch for a PR whose newest worker-bot comment is the limit note — pinned by a test that feeds it such a thread and asserts no `_nudge`
- [ ] Every existing test under `tests/` still passes and `check_act_receipts.py` reports no new unconverted site

cards.title: The review stage records a limit death on the card so the sweep can re-run the original pull_request run (qa-review.yml)
cards.description:
The REVIEW stage learns to record a limit death. Today when both critic attempts in `qa-review.yml` crash (`is_error`, no verdict) the "Post verdict or neutral status" step posts the neutral `QA Critic could not run (infra error)` comment on the PR and the card, and fails the job for medic visibility; the medic classifies it `critic_infra_crash` and backs off (DRE-1921, correct), but the reconcile sweep's `recover_crashed_reviews` then re-dispatches a fresh `workflow_dispatch` of the review within the sweep — straight into the same limit — and spends one of the `CRASHED_REVIEW_RETRY_CAP` re-dispatches for that head sha. Two Portico PRs did exactly this on 2026-09-05 and were bounced by hand.

With this card, `check_critic_result.py` reports the death class of the attempt it gated (a new `--github-output` key `death=<class>`, read through `check_agent_result.classify_death` — the one `is_error` reader — never a second regex), and the neutral-status step, on `death == usage_limit` for the FINAL attempt, additionally posts ONE `claude-limit-death` receipt on the card with `--stage review --run-url <this run's URL> --execution-file "$EXEC_FILE"` through `limit_wait.py post-death`. The PR-side neutral comment is unchanged (merge-gate still reads it as "hold"), the job still fails for medic visibility (the medic already backs off), and nothing here re-dispatches: the sweep's limit pass (a sibling card) re-runs THIS run — the original `pull_request` run named on the receipt — once the account changes or the window resets. Only the posting step gains a Claude credential in its env, under the same `vars.CLAUDE_AUTH_MODE` switch the Select-model step uses, plus `CLAUDE_ACCOUNT: ${{ vars.CLAUDE_ACCOUNT }}`; the critic steps' env is untouched (DRE-2696 — the critic must not gain a credential attempt 1 never had).

* **Death class.** `check_agent_result.DEATH_LIMIT = "usage_limit"`; `classify_death()` returns it for a record whose `result`/`errors` text contains `hit your limit` (case-insensitive). Owned by DRE-3179.

The `run=` URL on a review-stage receipt is the review run that died — the ORIGINAL `pull_request` run (or whatever event started it), never a hand-named branch; it is the run the sweep re-runs.
* **Gate output.** `check_critic_result.py … --github-output F` writes `death=<none|turn_exhaustion|credential_expiry|api_death|usage_limit>` beside its existing `outcome`/`turns`/`cost` keys.
* **Account identity.** `CLAUDE_ACCOUNT` (`vars.CLAUDE_ACCOUNT`) when set; else `fp:` + 12 hex of SHA-256 of the credential; else `unknown` — `limit_wait.account_identity(env)`.

## Acceptance criteria

cards.title: The plan and classify stages record a limit death instead of swinging the model or escalating (plan.yml, planning_classify.py)
cards.description:
The two stages that run inside `plan.yml` learn to record a limit death. Today the planner path posts `🪦 planner died with API/model error (is_error) on <model> — the medic rerun will switch to the alternate model` plus a `model-error:` marker (the "Record is_error death" step), and the medic's rerun sixty seconds later dies identically because the limit is on the ACCOUNT, not the model — DRE-3168 twice on 2026-09-05. The classifier path (`planning_classify.py`, DRE-3074's Claude Code transport) raises `TransportError` on any `is_error` envelope, which posts the `planning-classify-transport` receipt, fails the run for the medic's retry, and — because the second failure spends `TRANSPORT_CAP` — parks the card in Green Light as a transport escalation (DRE-3169 ended there). A limit is neither a model fault nor plumbing: nothing needs to change except the account or the clock.

With this card: (1) the "Record is_error death" step branches on `usage_limit` FIRST and posts one `claude-limit-death` receipt with `--stage plan --execution-file "$EXEC_FILE"` through `limit_wait.py post-death`, writing NO `model-error:` marker; the `api_death` and `turn_exhaustion` branches are untouched. (2) `planning_classify._call_claude_code` recognises `hit your limit` in the envelope's `result` before raising a generic `TransportError` and reports it as a distinct outcome — `Decision.limit = True`, github-output `limit=true`, the result text written to a `--limit-file` — so `plan.yml` gains a step "Classification hit the account limit — record and wait" that posts the receipt with `--stage classify --result-text "$(cat limit-file)"` and exits 1 (the run is honestly red; the medic sibling card declines to rerun it). That step posts NO `planning-classify-transport` receipt and NO escalation, so `TRANSPORT_CAP` is not spent and the card stays in Planning, unstamped, for the sweep to re-run. Both steps' env carry `CLAUDE_ACCOUNT: ${{ vars.CLAUDE_ACCOUNT }}` and the credential under the `vars.CLAUDE_AUTH_MODE` switch already used by the classify step.

**Files:** .github/workflows/plan.yml, scripts/planning_classify.py, tests/test_plan_usage_limit_wiring.py (new), tests/test_planning_classify_usage_limit.py (new)

## Contract (shared with siblings — identical in every card)

* **Death class.** `check_agent_result.DEATH_LIMIT = "usage_limit"`; `check_agent_result.py classify <file>` prints `usage_limit` for a record whose `result`/`errors` text contains `hit your limit` (case-insensitive). Owned by DRE-3179.
* **Death receipt.** Act `limit-death`, tag `claude-limit-death`, one line starting exactly `🪦 claude-limit-death: stage=<classify|plan|build|fix|review> account=<identity> resets=<ISO|unknown> run=<run URL>` followed by `—` and one plain-English sentence. Posted ONLY through `python3 .bureau-pipeline/scripts/limit_wait.py post-death --card <CARD> --stage <S> --run-url <U> [--result-text <T> | --execution-file <F>]`. * **Account identity.** `CLAUDE_ACCOUNT` (`vars.CLAUDE_ACCOUNT`) when set; else `fp:` + 12 hex of SHA-256 of the credential; else `unknown` — `limit_wait.account_identity(env)`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With the transport stubbed to return an envelope `{"is_error": true, "subtype": "success", "result": "You've hit your limit · resets 8:30pm (UTC)"}`, `planning_classify.classify` yields a Decision with `limit=True`, `requeue=False`, `escalates=False`, and the CLI writes `limit=true` to the github-output file and the result text to the limit file; a 429 body without the phrase still yields the DRE-3074 transport requeue (unchanged)

cards.title: The build stage records a limit death: no strike, no model swing, no requeue (agent-task.yml, dead_run.py)
cards.description:
The BUILD stage learns to record a limit death instead of spending a strike on it. Today `agent-task.yml`'s Report step classifies every `is_error` death through `check_agent_result.py classify` and, for `api_death`, calls `dead_run.py decide --is-error --error-model <model>`: that posts a `🪦 dead-run-requeue` receipt (one of the card's three strikes), writes a `model-error:` marker (which swings the model ladder for a fault the model never had), and moves the card to Todo — where the relay dispatches a fresh run straight into the same limit. On 2026-09-05 this is what happened to DRE-3162, DRE-3130 and DRE-3072 (the limit is on the ACCOUNT, not the model).

With this card, when the classifier answers `usage_limit` the Report step posts ONE `claude-limit-death` receipt through the vocabulary card's own poster — `python3 .bureau-pipeline/scripts/limit_wait.py post-death --card "$CARD" --stage build --run-url "$RUN_URL" --execution-file "$EXEC_FILE"` — and changes nothing else: no `dead-run-requeue` tag, no `turn-exhaustion-requeue` tag, no `model-error:` marker, no state move (the card stays In Progress; the sweep's limit pass, a sibling card, moves it to Todo when the account changes or the window resets), no `needs-human` label. `dead_run.decide()` gains a `usage_limit=True` input that returns a new action `wait` with an EMPTY comment list (the receipt is posted by `limit_wait`, so the budget module composes nothing for this class); `usage_limit` is checked after `cancelled` and `pre_agent` and before every death class, because a limit death is the same shape as a pre-agent fault for the card's budget — not the card's fault. The account identity and reset time come from the environment and the execution record; the step's env must carry `CLAUDE_ACCOUNT: ${{ vars.CLAUDE_ACCOUNT }}` and the credential under the same `vars.CLAUDE_AUTH_MODE` switch the Select-model step uses, so `account=` on the receipt is never `unknown`.

**Files:** .github/workflows/agent-task.yml, scripts/dead_run.py, tests/test_dead_run_usage_limit.py (new), tests/test_agent_task_usage_limit_wiring.py (new)

## Contract (shared with siblings — identical in every card)

* **Death class.** `check_agent_result.DEATH_LIMIT = "usage_limit"`; the CLI `check_agent_result.py classify <file>` prints `usage_limit` for a record whose `result`/`errors` text contains `hit your limit` (case-insensitive). Owned by DRE-3179; this card only reads it.
* **Death receipt.** Act `limit-death`, tag `claude-limit-death`, one line starting exactly `🪦 claude-limit-death: stage=<classify|plan|build|fix|review> account=<identity> resets=<ISO|unknown> run=<run URL>` followed by `—` and one plain-English sentence. Posted ONLY through `python3 .bureau-pipeline/scripts/limit_wait.py post-death --card <CARD> --stage <S> --run-url <U> [--result-text <T> | --execution-file <F>]` (DRE-3179 owns the composer; workflows never assemble the line). It carries neither `dead-run-requeue` nor `turn-exhaustion-requeue`, so it spends no budget.
* `dead_run.decide(..., usage_limit=True)` → `Decision("wait", [])`. The CLI form is `dead_run.py decide <prior> --usage-limit …`, printing `wait` on line 1. `usage_limit` outranks every death class below `cancelled` and `pre_agent`.
* **Account identity.** `CLAUDE_ACCOUNT` (a repo variable, `vars.CLAUDE_ACCOUNT`) when set; else `fp:` + the first 12 hex characters of SHA-256 of the credential; else `unknown` — computed by `limit_wait.account_identity(env)`, never in YAML.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `dead_run.decide(0, usage_limit=True)` returns action `wait` with no comments; `dead_run.decide(2, usage_limit=True, is_error=True, error_model="claude-x")` (a card at the cap) still returns `wait` — a limit death never holds a card; `decide(0, cancelled=True, usage_limit=True)` still returns `defer` and `decide(0, pre_agent=True, usage_limit=True)` still returns `infra` (the two classes above it keep their precedence)

- [ ] A scenario test drives the real `dead_run.decide` over the thread of a card that has died three times on the limit and asserts `dead_run.count_of(bodies, DEAD_TAG) == 0` and `count_of(bodies, TURN_TAG) == 0` — three limit deaths and zero real failures is still dispatchable

cards.title: Console learns the three limit-wait act tags before the pipeline declares them (agent-bureau, console-first)
cards.description:
The console is the act registry's reader, and the sequencing rule in bureau-pipeline's `docs/pipeline-acts.md` is console-first: a new act must be known to `console/backend/receipts.py:ACTS` BEFORE bureau-pipeline declares it in `config/pipeline-acts.json`, or the pipeline's `act registry consumers` CI job fails and every open agent-bureau PR goes red on the console's own guard (DRE-3081 and DRE-3090, twice in twelve hours). This epic declares three new acts, so this card lands them in the console first. It is three lines and nothing else: no alert row, no new page (the Alerts row is a sibling card).

**Files:** console/backend/receipts.py, console/backend/tests/test_receipts.py (or the test that already pins `ACTS`)

## Contract (shared with siblings — identical in every card)

Three tags, each added to `ACTS` with its kind, spelled exactly:

* `claude-limit-death` — kind `refusal`. A run died on the Claude account's five-hour usage limit; the pipeline recorded it and did not retry.
* `claude-limit-redispatch` — kind `recovery`. The sweep re-dispatched a limit-killed run after the active account changed or the limit window reset.
* `merge-sync-rerun` — kind `recovery`. The sweep re-ran a merged pull request's original `linear-sync` run that had died before closing the card.

No tag may be a substring of another act's tag or name (that is the rule bureau-pipeline's `pipeline_act.problems()` enforces on its side; the console's own guard compares by tag or name).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `ACTS` in `console/backend/receipts.py` carries `claude-limit-death` (refusal), `claude-limit-redispatch` (recovery) and `merge-sync-rerun` (recovery), spelled exactly as above
- [ ] The console's existing act-registry test (`test_every_act_the_pipeline_declares_is_known_to_the_console`) still passes against bureau-pipeline's current `config/pipeline-acts.json` — the console knowing a tag the pipeline has not declared yet is the designed, cost-free direction
- [ ] A unit test pins the three tags and their kinds, so a later console refactor cannot drop one silently
- [ ] Nothing else changes: no alert, no page, no receipt parsing

cards.title: Limit death is its own class: the receipt grammar, the reset parse and the account identity (limit_wait.py)
cards.description:
A death on the Claude account's five-hour usage limit (`You've hit your limit · resets 8:30pm (UTC)`) is today classified as `api_death`: the build path spends a dead-run strike and arms the model swing, the planner path posts "the medic rerun will switch to the alternate model", and every retry dies identically because the limit is on the ACCOUNT, not the model (2026-09-05, 10:15–10:48 PT: eight runs across DRE-3168 ×2, DRE-3162, DRE-3130, DRE-3072, DRE-3169 and two Portico reviews, all bounced by hand). This card lands the shared vocabulary every sibling reads, and nothing else: the new death class in the one `is_error` classifier, a new stdlib module that composes, POSTS and parses the two receipts, parses the reset time, fingerprints the active account, and answers "is this card still waiting", and the two acts in the receipt registry. No workflow changes here — the writers (build, plan, fix, review) and the reader (the sweep) are sibling cards that cite this one.

`limit_wait.py` is pure stdlib and no-I/O apart from the two `post-*` seams and the `identity` CLI reading its environment (`zoneinfo` for the zone names; `hashlib` for the fingerprint). `check_agent_result.classify_death()` gains `DEATH_LIMIT` ahead of every existing branch (a limit death returns in under a second on one turn, so it would otherwise read as the outage signature). Register `limit-death` (kind `refusal`, state `unchanged`, `next_actor`/`subscriber` `reconcile.yml`) and `limit-redispatch` (kind `recovery`, state `dispatched`, `next_actor`/`subscriber` `reconcile.yml`) in `config/pipeline-acts.json`, both `adopted: false`, with `emits` pointing at the composers in `limit_wait.py` (the literal `pipeline_act.receipt("limit-death", …)` / `pipeline_act.receipt("limit-redispatch", …)` calls). `docs/pipeline-acts.md` is prose about the sequencing rule, not a rendered list, so it needs no change; `config/README.md` carries the registry shape. `pipeline_act.problems()` must stay empty: neither new tag may be a substring of another act's tag or name. The console (agent-bureau) learns both tags FIRST — the console-first card this one is blocked on — or the `act registry consumers` CI job fails this repo's PR.

**Files:** scripts/limit_wait.py (new), scripts/check_agent_result.py, config/pipeline-acts.json, tests/test_limit_wait.py (new), tests/test_check_agent_result_usage_limit.py (new)

## Contract (shared with siblings — identical in every card)

* **Death class.** `check_agent_result.DEATH_LIMIT = "usage_limit"`. `classify_death()` returns it when the execution record's `result` or `errors` text contains `hit your limit` (case-insensitive), checked FIRST — before the outage signature, the turn-cap evidence and the credential refusal. The CLI `check_agent_result.py classify <file>` prints `usage_limit`. Only the record's own fields are read, never the transcript, so a card body quoting the phrase cannot classify.
* **Account identity.** `limit_wait.account_identity(env) -> str` — `CLAUDE_ACCOUNT` when set (a repo variable, `vars.CLAUDE_ACCOUNT`, e.g. `DeltaSolv`); else `fp:` + the first 12 hex characters of SHA-256 of `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` (or of `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` when that is the one set); else `unknown`. CLI: `python3 .bureau-pipeline/scripts/limit_wait.py identity`. The token itself is never printed or posted.
* **Reset parse.** `limit_wait.reset_at(text, died_at) -> str | None` — the ISO-8601 UTC instant (`2026-09-05T20:30:00Z`) of the first `resets <h[:mm]><am|pm> (<zone>)` wall-clock time at or after `died_at`; `None` when unparseable. `UTC` and IANA zone names are accepted.
* **Death receipt** — act `limit-death`, tag `claude-limit-death`, ONE line starting exactly
  `🪦 claude-limit-death: stage=<classify|plan|build|fix|review> account=<identity> resets=<ISO|unknown> run=<run URL>`
  followed by `—` and one plain-English sentence. Composed by `limit_wait.death_receipt(stage, account, resets, run_url)` (which calls `pipeline_act.receipt("limit-death", …)` literally); parsed by `limit_wait.parse_death(body)` into a `LimitDeath` with `stage, account, resets, run_url, run_id, posted_at`. POSTED by `limit_wait.post_death(identifier, stage, run_url, *, result_text=None, execution=None, died_at=None)` — composes and calls `linear_ops.cmd_comment(identifier, body)` in the same function (the `medic_retry.post_declined` shape `check_act_receipts.py` recognises as composed). Workflows call the CLI `limit_wait.py post-death --card <CARD> --stage <S> --run-url <U> [--result-text <T> | --execution-file <F>] [--died-at ISO]`; the account is read from the environment, the reset parsed from the text. It carries NEITHER `dead-run-requeue` NOR `turn-exhaustion-requeue`, so it spends no budget.
* **Re-dispatch receipt** — act `limit-redispatch`, tag `claude-limit-redispatch`, ONE line starting `🔁 claude-limit-redispatch: <trigger> — <what was re-dispatched>`, where `<trigger>` is exactly one of `account switched <old> → <new>` or `window reset at <HH:MM> PT (<ISO>)`. Composed by `limit_wait.redispatch_receipt(trigger, what)` (calls `pipeline_act.receipt("limit-redispatch", …)` literally); POSTED by `limit_wait.post_redispatch(identifier, trigger, what)` in the same composed-and-written shape. CLI: `limit_wait.py redispatch-receipt --trigger T --what W` (prints) and `post-redispatch --card C --trigger T --what W`.
* **Waiting predicate.** `limit_wait.waiting(bodies_oldest_to_newest) -> LimitDeath | None` — the newest `claude-limit-death` receipt, unless a LATER comment carries `claude-limit-redispatch` or starts with `🧠 model-attempt:` (a newer run began). `limit_wait.trigger(death, account, now) -> str | None` — the trigger sentence when `account != death.account` and neither is `unknown`, or when `now >= death.resets` (`resets=unknown` is read as the receipt's own posting time + 5 hours, the window's length); else `None`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `classify_death()` on a record `{"is_error": true, "num_turns": 1, "total_cost_usd": 0, "duration_ms": 400, "result": "You've hit your limit · resets 8:30pm (UTC)"}` returns `usage_limit`, and the same record with the phrase removed still returns `api_death` (the outage branch is untouched)
- [ ] A record whose `result` is a clean closing message containing the phrase but `is_error` false classifies `none` — the phrase is only read on a death
- [ ] `reset_at("… resets 8:30pm (UTC)", "2026-09-05T17:23:00Z")` → `2026-09-05T20:30:00Z`; the same text with `died_at` `2026-09-05T21:00:00Z` → `2026-09-06T20:30:00Z` (the NEXT occurrence); `resets 3pm (America/Los_Angeles)` resolves through the zone; garbage → `None`
- [ ] `account_identity()` prefers `CLAUDE_ACCOUNT`, else yields `fp:` + 12 hex of the token's SHA-256, else `unknown`; the raw token value never appears in any output, pinned by a test that greps the CLI's stdout
- [ ] `death_receipt()` output round-trips through `parse_death()` (stage, account, resets, run_url and the numeric run id off `/actions/runs/<id>`), starts with the exact first-line grammar above, and contains neither `dead-run-requeue` nor `turn-exhaustion-requeue`; `post_death()` and `post_redispatch()` write through `linear_ops.cmd_comment` with a body composed in the same function (pinned by driving them with a stub `linear_ops`)
- [ ] `waiting()` returns the death for `[death]`, `None` for `[death, redispatch]`, `None` for `[death, "🧠 model-attempt: …"]`, and the NEWER death for `[death1, redispatch, death2]`; `trigger()` fires on an account mismatch (never when either side is `unknown`), on a passed reset, on `resets=unknown` once 5 hours have passed since the receipt's posting time, and not otherwise — the reset trigger sentence renders the PT clock time
- [ ] `config/pipeline-acts.json` carries both acts, `pipeline_act.problems()` is empty, `check_act_receipts.py` passes, `tests/test_pipeline_acts_consumers.py` passes against the console (the console-first card has landed the tags)
- [ ] Every existing test under `tests/` still passes (the classifier's other three classes and `agent_started()` are unchanged)

**Blocked by:** DRE-3185
