cards.title: Claude auto-switch never fires — it watches the account the console last rotated to, reads a 429 usage answer as "unavailable", and ignores the runs that are already failing with "you've hit your limit"
cards.description:
## What happened, 2026-09-05

Auto-switch was ON (`subscriptionConfig.autoSwitch = true`, four Max 20× accounts in failover order). From about 10:15 PT every model call in the fleet failed: planner runs 33980524576 and 33980676980, the classifier on [DRE-3169](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3169/the-relay-deploy-copies-whatever-linear-api-key-is-in-the-operators) (`You've hit your limit · resets 8:30pm (UTC)`), Portico critic reviews 33980841736 and 33981307403. The fleet stayed down for half an hour until the CEO switched the active account to DeltaSolv by hand at 10:44 PT, which fanned the token out to all six repos in three seconds and fixed it at once.

Auto-switch did nothing, for three independent reasons, each of which alone would have stopped it:

1. **It believed the fleet was on EveryBite.** `claudeRotationStatus.rotatedAt` said 2026-09-04 15:01Z, account EveryBite, and `costUsage` marked EveryBite `active` at 1% five-hour use. But every repo's `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` had been rewritten at 08:36 PT that morning (`updated_at` 15:36Z on five repos, 14:51Z on atlas) by something that was not the console — no rotation line in the backend log, no change to the console's record. The fleet was on Dreadnought. The console's "active" is a memory of its own last write, not an observation of what the repos hold.
2. **It read the exhausted account as unknown.** Dreadnought's row was `status: available`, utilisation `null`, `error: usage unavailable (HTTP 429)`. A 429 from the usage endpoint IS the limit; the console rendered it as "no data" and moved on.
3. **It never reads the runs.** Four runs in twenty minutes carried the literal receipt `You've hit your limit`. The failover logic consumes only the usage endpoint; the fleet's own failures — the one signal that is always true — never reach it.

## What to build

Auto-switch fires on evidence the fleet actually produces, and the console's picture of "active" is verified rather than remembered:

* **A run's limit receipt is a trigger.** The planner, build, fix and critic workflows already surface `is_error` with the limit text; the console ingests those (the run-signal path [DRE-3001](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3001/the-console-has-been-blind-to-every-actions-run-for-a-month-the-bot) is restoring) and treats N such receipts within M minutes on the active account as exhaustion, independent of the usage endpoint.
* **A 429 from the usage endpoint counts as exhausted**, not unavailable, for failover purposes. The row still says "usage unavailable" for display, but the failover logic sees `exhausted: true` with the reason.
* **The active account is checked against the repos, not assumed.** The console keeps a fingerprint (not the value) of the token it last fanned out and each repo's `updated_at`; a repo whose secret is newer than the console's last write is flagged `rotated outside the console` on the Subscriptions page and in Alerts, and auto-switch treats the active account as UNKNOWN until the next rotation it performs — because switching "away from EveryBite" when the fleet is on Dreadnought is a switch to nowhere.
* **Every switch, automatic or by hand, writes one line to the card-visible log**: from which account, to which, why (which trigger), and which repos were rotated. The 08:36 PT rotation this morning has no such line anywhere, and finding out what did it is still open.

**Files:** console/backend (the failover module beside `claude_oauth_token.py`, `costUsage`/`subscriptionConfig` resolvers, the run-signal ingest), the Subscriptions and Alerts pages, and tests. One repo.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With auto-switch on and the active account's usage endpoint answering 429, the console switches to the next account in failover order within one poll cycle, observed once on the live console and recorded here with PT times
- [ ] With auto-switch on and the usage endpoint healthy but three runs reporting `hit your limit` within fifteen minutes, the console switches — pinned by a test that feeds the receipts through the ingest path
- [ ] A repo whose `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` is newer than the console's last fan-out shows `rotated outside the console` on the Subscriptions page and raises an Alert naming the repo and the time; auto-switch reports the active account as UNKNOWN until the console rotates again
- [ ] Every switch writes one plain-English line naming from, to, trigger and repos, readable on the Subscriptions page
- [ ] The manual switch the CEO used at 10:44 PT still works exactly as it does today

## Related, not in scope

One of the four accounts has a broken refresh chain: the backend has logged `the Claude refresh chain could not be renewed — the refresh exchange was refused. This account is running on its static access token` every four minutes since 08:27 PT today, without naming the account. Separate card; the log line should at least say which account.

cards.title: [EPIC] The groomer gets judgement — it reads what we are doing before it says what comes next, and says which cards are already done or no longer wanted
cards.description:
**The CEO, 2026-09-04 evening:** *"I want the groomer to be pretty intelligent so that it understands what we're currently doing. When it looks at what cards it should promote to the planner, it should understand what we're currently doing, what's urgently involved and what isn't, what sort of things we should come back to later. It also should look at all the cards that are in there, whether it should promote them or not, because we could have moved on, and things could have changed, or they could have already been done."*

## What the groomer is today (read from `scripts/groomer.py`, 2026-09-04)

A deterministic sorter with an approval gate. It never calls a model. It reads the whole Intake lane, treats an epic and its children as one unit, finds file collisions by regex over the file names cards cite, sequences by fixed bands (Urgent, then High, then created in the last 14 days newest first), treats anything older as "not now" by default, assigns cycles by a capacity of 20, and proposes a batch the CEO approves before `drain` moves it to Planning ([DRE-2683](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2683/the-groomer-sequences-the-whole-backlog-into-cycles-portico-first-and), [DRE-3096](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3096/the-groomer-batches-newest-first-inside-a-14-day-window-urgent-always), [DRE-2753](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2753/the-console-needs-a-batch-approval-surface-the-groomer-proposes-and)). It calls a card "dead" only when the card's own text says it was superseded by a named card or PR. Its cadence is on demand, by decision D5, *"until the groomer's judgement has been audited"* — and it has no judgement to audit.

The parts that were paid for stay: the whole-lane read ([DRE-2681](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2681/pagination-and-parents-first-repair-the-promoter-never-sees-past-row)), epics as the unit, collisions as an order, the approval gate the proposer cannot pass ([DRE-3033](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3033/the-fleet-gets-its-own-linear-identity-the-pipelines-key-stops-being)), "dead" as a recommendation with evidence and never an action, and the `INTAKE_HOLD` pen ([DRE-3035](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3035/intake-is-a-pen-the-operator-controls-an-intake-hold-switch-an-age-out)).

## What it cannot do, and what this epic adds

| the CEO wants | today | this epic |
| -- | -- | -- |
| know what we are doing now | nothing — never reads In Progress epics, plans, initiatives or recent merges | a **context pack**: the epics In Progress and their plan summaries, the initiatives and their objectives, what merged in the last 14 days, the Done and Canceled cards of the last 30 |
| what is urgent and what is not | Linear priority 1 and 2, else creation date | one bounded **model read over the whole population at once**, ranking against the context pack, with a one-line reason per card |
| what to come back to later | "older than 14 days" is "not now", unspoken | **"not now, revisit when X"** as a first-class outcome with the trigger named — an epic finishing, a decision landing, a date |
| already done, or we moved on | only if the card's body says "superseded by" | **"likely done or obsolete, because Y"**, pointing at the card, merged PR or decision that makes it so — still a recommendation the CEO confirms, never an action |

The rules become the **constraints** the judgement runs inside: collisions still order, blockers still hold, an epic is still the unit, capacity still caps, and the batch still goes to the CEO. What changes is what fills the batch and why.

## Constraints that are not negotiable

* **One prompt over a census, never one call per card.** A 226-card lane against Linear's workspace quota is how the sweeps starved on 2026-08-31 (per-workspace 2500/hr). The census is titles, ids, labels, ages and the first lines; the model ranks the census, and the rules do the rest.
* **The transport is the Claude Code path, on the planner's ladder** ([DRE-3074](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3074/the-classifier-calls-the-messages-api-raw-with-the-subscription-token)): a subscription token cannot call the raw Messages API. Reuse `planning_classify.py`'s call seam; do not write a second one.
* **Every call is written into the proposal the CEO approves**, one line per card, so a wrong call is visible before it moves anything. Reasons pass the same plain-English guard escalations do (`planning_escalation.refusal`): no diffs, no paths, no commands.
* **Refusal is not a default.** A card the model cannot place stays where it is with "could not rank — needs a person", never silently ranked last.
* **The approval gate, the proposal id bound to the batch's contents, and the identity rule are untouched.** Nothing here lets the proposer approve.
* **Cadence stays on demand until the audit card below passes.** Two real batches, every call checked by hand against what the CEO would have chosen. Then the cadence is a decision, made with the audit's numbers, on [DRE-2840](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2840/operator-prove-phase-7-grooming-scoring-and-the-cutover).

## Two children are pre-filed — wire to them, do not re-file

1. **The context pack and the ranked read** — the pipeline half, in `bureau-pipeline`.
2. **[OPERATOR] Audit the first two batches by hand** — needs-human, no-code; it blocks any cadence change and feeds [DRE-2840](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2840/operator-prove-phase-7-grooming-scoring-and-the-cutover).

The planner adds what is left: the proposal's presentation (the reason column in the comment and in the console's batch panel, `console/backend/batch_proposal.py` — that half is `repo:agent-bureau`), the "revisit when" outcome and its trigger, "likely done" with its evidence line, and the scorer for the groomer's calls in the shape of `planner_score.py`. Split on **file footprint**: the console half and the pipeline half never share a file.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A `propose` run reads the context pack and ranks the whole Intake population in ONE model call, and the proposal names a reason per card
- [ ] "Not now" carries a trigger; "likely done or obsolete" carries the card, PR or decision it points at; both are recommendations the CEO confirms
- [ ] The rules still constrain: a collision still orders, a blocker still holds, an epic is still one unit, the approval gate still refuses the proposer
- [ ] Two real batches audited by hand and recorded on the operator card, with the agreement rate, before any cadence change
- [ ] No second model transport; no per-card calls

**Not green-lit.** The planner reads this in Planning; the CEO approves the plan from Green Light by moving the epic to In Progress.

cards.title: PROOF: a live red-on-main-fault PR was refreshed once by the sweep, its own-failure sibling was not, recorded in the repo
cards.description:
PROOF that the new sweep rule works against real state — not a green suite. An operator, at an interactive session, watches the reconcile sweep refresh a live pull request that is red only on a fault `main` has since fixed, watches it leave a PR with its own failure alone, and records what was read, when, and what it said, in a file that merges. The record is the deliverable; the mechanism is DRE-3138 + DRE-3144 (pipeline) and DRE-3137 (console).

**What to observe, by hand, on a live repository (agent-bureau or bureau-pipeline, whichever next produces the shape — or stage it on a throwaway branch pair):**

1. A PR whose CI is red only on a check that is also red on its merge base, where `main` then gains a commit that makes that check green. Watch the next full reconcile sweep: exactly one `update-branch` on that PR, one receipt on the PR and one on its card, both carrying `stale-merge-ref-refresh @<main sha>` and the `📎 pipeline-act: merge-ref-refreshed` trailer. Record the PR number, the head sha before and after, the `main` sha the receipt names, the sweep run id and its timestamp, and the CI outcome on the new head.
2. The same PR on the following sweep: no second refresh (read the sweep log line and the comment count).
3. A PR red on its own failure (green on the merge base) during the same window: untouched by the rule — record its PR number and the sweep log line saying why.
4. Whether the standing critic verdict CARRIED across the refresh (content binding, DRE-2340): record what `should_review_pr` decided on the new head and whether the merge gate merged on the carried verdict or a fresh review ran. If a fresh review ran on an unchanged diff, record that as a finding against the carry and file it as a sibling card — do not fix it here.
5. The console: open the card in the console and confirm the receipt is shown as a known act (kind `recovery`), not as an unknown comment. Record a screenshot path or a one-line description of what the console showed.

Write the observation to `docs/stale-merge-ref-proof.md` (dates in absolute form, shas in full, run URLs), and open the PR for it from the operator session. Nothing else is committed by this card.

**Files:** docs/stale-merge-ref-proof.md

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Observed by hand on a live repository: one refresh, on one PR, on one `main` commit, with the PR receipt and the card receipt both present — recorded with PR number, shas, sweep run URL and timestamps in `docs/stale-merge-ref-proof.md`
- [ ] Observed on the next live sweep: the same PR was not refreshed again
- [ ] Observed on a live PR with its own failure in the same window: not refreshed, and the sweep log line saying why is quoted in the record
- [ ] The record states whether the critic verdict carried across the refresh on the live PR, and names the sibling card filed if it did not
- [ ] The record states what the live console showed for the receipt on the card
- [ ] `docs/stale-merge-ref-proof.md` is merged to `main`

**Blocked by:** DRE-3137, DRE-3138, DRE-3144

cards.title: The shelf lists the templates this build carries, and one button puts a template on the shelf — no file, no terminal, no token
cards.description:
Operator, 2026-09-04, after putting the first template on Oncor's shelf through `shelf-template.ts` and a token copied off the clipboard: "why are we doing it this way? We must have a better way going forward." Offered three ways, he chose this one: **the shelf lists the templates the deployed build carries, and a moderator puts one on it with a click.** No file picker, no terminal, no token handling — the shelf is a moderator surface and the moderator is already signed in on it.

Two server cards come first. [DRE-3102](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3102/post-libraryforms-is-an-upsert-by-definition-id-the-same-template) makes `POST /library/forms` an upsert; [DRE-3103](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3103/the-api-carries-every-committed-template-get-libraryforms-lists-the) gives the API its own copy of `forms/` and answers `GET /library/forms` with `{ templates, builtin }` plus `POST /library/forms/builtin { project, templateId }`. This card is the last hop: the shelf draws `builtin` and one button posts the short form.

**Blocked by:** [DRE-3103](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3103/the-api-carries-every-committed-template-get-libraryforms-lists-the)

## What this card does

**1. A "Built in" group under the existing shelf** (`TemplateShelf.tsx`, `FormShelfRegion.tsx`): one row per `builtin` entry, matched to `templates` by `definitionId` + `version` — never by title, which a moderator can rename.

| state | row reads | control |
| -- | -- | -- |
| not on the shelf | `AI Readiness · v1 · 132 questions` | **Put on shelf** |
| on the shelf at this version | `On the shelf · v1` | none — it is the shelf row above |
| on the shelf at an older version | `Shelf has v1 · this build has v2` | **Update to v2** |
| shelf newer than the build | `Shelf has v3 · this build has v2` | none, and says so |

The button calls `shelfBuiltinTemplate(project, templateId)` — the wrapper `formTransport.ts`'s header says to write only "in the PR that adds the authoring UI, with a caller and a test"; this is that PR, and the header is updated to say so — then re-reads the shelf, and the row moves to the state the server now reports. A refusal (409, 403, 404) shows the server's sentence inline on the row, and the row keeps its button. While the post is in flight the button is disabled and reads `Putting on shelf…`.

**2. Placement is untouched.** Putting a template on the shelf grants nobody anything; the drag onto a customer's folder stays the act that does (TemplateShelf's header: placement is permission). This adds the step BEFORE the drag, not a shortcut past it.

**3. The button is a decision, and the row says so once.** [DRE-3037](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3037/a-placed-form-freezes-a-full-copy-of-its-definition-into-the-library) (Backlog) records that a placed form freezes a full copy of its definition into the library partition, which is read as ONE page, and that five copies of the readiness questionnaire truncate the library silently. A shelf row is one such copy (`ai-readiness` is 283 KB) and every placement is another. The group's one line of help text says a template on the shelf is a large row — a sentence, not a modal.

**4. The shelf is the index.** `forms/README.md`'s "on which shelf / since" table goes: the shelf now says what it holds, per project, and a hand-kept table beside it would be the stale one. The README keeps the directory rule and how to add a template, and says to look at the shelf.

**5. The dev mock** answers `builtin` from the repo's `forms/` (it already imports the prototype's template) and accepts `POST /library/forms/builtin` with the same outcomes, so the whole flow runs on `npm run dev:mock` and in e2e.

## Design

The row is a molecule beside the existing shelf card: same edges, same eyebrow treatment, the state in words not colour, the button the library's secondary button. No new tokens. Specimen entry, light and dark, like every molecule under `src/components/`; one entry showing all four states.

## Not this card

* Authoring or editing a template in the browser. A template is a file in the repo, changed by a PR; the button ships what the build carries.
* Removing a template from the shelf (no route).
* Uploading a file from the browser. The build carries the templates; a template not in the build is not shelved from a laptop.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] the shelf renders one "Built in" row per `builtin` entry in the four states above, decided by `definitionId` + `version` against `templates`, never by title — unit-tested with all four
- [ ] **Put on shelf** posts `{ project, templateId }` and the row reads `On the shelf · v1` after the shelf re-reads; **Update to v2** does the same and the shelf row's version changes; a 409 shows the server's sentence on the row and the button stays
- [ ] a non-moderator never sees the group — the shelf's existing 403 → "no shelf" handling, no new gate
- [ ] `shelfBuiltinTemplate` exists in `formTransport.ts` with this caller and a test; the header's "NO createFormTemplate HERE" paragraph is rewritten to say what now exists and why
- [ ] the dev mock answers `builtin` from `forms/` and accepts the POST; one e2e spec drives put-on-shelf → row state change → the template appears in the shelf above and can be placed
- [ ] the [DRE-3037](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3037/a-placed-form-freezes-a-full-copy-of-its-definition-into-the-library) sentence is on the group, once
- [ ] specimen entry for the row, light and dark; visual baselines regrown with `npm run e2e:visual:update`
- [ ] `forms/README.md` no longer carries the "on which shelf" table and says where to look instead

cards.title: [OPERATOR] Observe the main harness slot working in production — the two proofs DRE-3075 could not give before merge
cards.description:
`deferred: production — unobservable pre-merge`

The two acceptance criteria [DRE-3075](<https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3075>) could not satisfy before merge, moved here so they are **owed by someone** rather than assumed.

## Why they could not be met on the PR

Both ask for an observation of two genuinely concurrent Actions runs against real `push` and `pull_request` events. That cannot happen until the new `harness.yml` config is the one live on `main` — **the card asked to watch the fix working in production before it was in production.** The critic on PR #252 caught it; the PR body had already flagged both as *"not provable before merge"*.

## Why this card exists at all rather than a note on the PR

Merging [DRE-3075](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3075/main-gets-its-own-harness-slot-a-pull-requests-proving-run-never) auto-closes it via `linear-sync` on the merge event. Without this card, shipping against an admittedly-unmet criterion leaves **nothing obliging anyone to ever capture the observation** — the propose-gate shape ([DRE-1980](<https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-1980>)), which ran dead for six weeks because it was everyone's assumption and nobody's card.

`needs-human` and `no-code` are deliberate: the deliverable is a live observation, which no merge event can attest and no sweep should be able to close.

## What must be observed, not asserted

- [ ] **The slot actually separates.** With a PR harness run in progress, a push to `main` starts its own harness run **within a minute**. Record BOTH run ids here. The cheapest way to force it: open a throwaway PR that touches a harness-relevant path, wait for its run to start, then push a trivial commit to `main`.
- [ ] **The channel keeps up.** With `main` taking three merges inside one harness duration, `stable` advances **at least once**. Record the tag moves — `gh api repos/dreadnought-foundry/bureau-pipeline/commits/stable --jq .sha` before and after, not the committed date of the tagged commit.
- [ ] Neither run deleted the other's sandbox branches — check `bureau-harness` for leftovers from the pair.

## One trap, learned the hard way today

**Do not read the tag's commit date and call it the tag-move time.** I made exactly that error twice on 2026-09-04 and reported a 14-hour stall that was really 3h07m. `stable` had moved five times inside a window I described as static. The tag move is in `promote-channel.yml`'s run history — the `Move the channel` step, which shows `skipped` when a run correctly declines to promote.

cards.title: The planner reads the split ledger and the mulch planning records before it sizes a card (piece 2 of 3 of DRE-3022)
cards.description:
**Split from** [DRE-3022](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3022/the-planner-sizes-against-the-ledger-every-turn-cap-death-split-and) **by its author, 2026-09-03 21:57 PT (two turn-cap deaths). Piece 2: the planner reads what piece 1 derives.** Blocked by piece 1, [DRE-3077](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3077/the-split-ledger-derived-split-ledgerpy-reads-every-turn-cap-death), because this injects the file it produces.

## What to build

* `plan.yml` injects a summary of `config/split-ledger.json` into the planner's context the way standards are injected from the pipeline checkout: the last N ledger rows with their tells, and the measured rates. A missing or stale ledger (older than the configured age) is injected as *"ledger UNKNOWN — <reason>"*, never silently omitted, and the plan artifact records that.
* `briefs/planner.md` gains one section: *before you size a card, read the ledger and name which of the four tells you checked it against.* The plan artifact records that check per child.
* The `planning` domain of agent-bureau's `.mulch/expertise/` records is rendered into the same injected block (read from the agent-bureau checkout the workflow already has, or fetched at `@main`), so an interactive lesson reaches the headless planner. One source, no copy.
* A test with a fixture ledger proves the planner's context contains the rows and the rates, and that a missing ledger yields the UNKNOWN line.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A planner run's prompt (visible in the run's sanitized context) contains the ledger summary and the mulch planning records
- [ ] A plan artifact from a real epic names, per child, the tell it was checked against
- [ ] Fixture test: missing ledger → UNKNOWN line in the artifact, run does not fail

## File footprint

`.github/workflows/plan.yml` (the injection step), `briefs/planner.md` (one section), `scripts/plan_artifact.py` (the per-child tell field), `tests/`.

cards.title: CI · the approved-but-red sweep treats a cancelled check as a red a fixing agent can clear — it dispatched one at an approved PR
cards.description:
Filed from portico, from the build of [DRE-3071](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3071/ci-the-infra-jobs-10-minute-cap-cancelled-three-approved-prs-in-one), whose last acceptance criterion asks for this half to be reported here rather than fixed in a product repo.

On the evening of 2026-09-03 portico's `infra — typecheck & test` job was cancelled by its own 10-minute cap on three critic-APPROVED PRs. Portico has raised that budget. What is left is what the pipeline did with the cancellation.

## What happened

PR [#415](<https://github.com/dreadnought-foundry/portico/pull/415>) got `VERDICT: APPROVE` at 03:09 UTC. At 03:50 the reconcile sweep dispatched a fixing agent at it ([run 33834644194](<https://github.com/dreadnought-foundry/portico/actions/runs/33834644194>)). No code change could have cleared what it was sent at — the check was not red, it was cancelled by a clock. The run died on a model error before it could edit anything, so this cost inference and a Linear comment rather than a bad commit.

## Where it is

`scripts/reconcile.py`, `fix_approved_but_red()`. The check-runs read counts a PR as needing a fixer when any non-review check has a conclusion in:

```
IN("failure","timed_out","cancelled")
```

`failure` and `timed_out` are states a fixing agent can plausibly act on. `cancelled` is not, and it has at least two causes that are nothing to do with the branch's code:

1. **A job that exceeds its job-level** `timeout-minutes` **is cancelled, not failed.** That is the whole incident above, and `qa-review.yml` already carries the same note about its own 65-minute wall ("a cancelled job skips even its `always()` steps").
2. `concurrency: cancel-in-progress`**.** Portico's `ci.yml` cancels a PR's in-flight run when a newer push supersedes it, which is the normal shape across the fleet. A superseded run leaves cancelled check runs on the older head — and this sweep reads the head sha, so it is only the >20-minute age guard standing between that and a dispatch.

The busy-guard, the human-park gate and the 20-minute age guard all held. None of them is the right instrument: this is a misclassification, not a pacing problem.

## What is worth deciding here

Whether `cancelled` should be dropped from that set outright, or split — a cancelled check is *unknown*, not red, and the honest answer for an approved PR sitting on one may be to re-run the check rather than to write code at it. This card names the defect and the two causes; the choice of remedy is the pipeline's.

Portico's own change is a separate matter and is already in flight — it raises the job budget and gives the Test step its own clock so a hung test fails the step rather than cancelling the job.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A check run whose conclusion is `cancelled` no longer, on its own, causes `fix_approved_but_red` to dispatch a fixing agent
- [ ] A test in `tests/` covers the cancelled case and fails if the behaviour is reverted
- [ ] `failure` and `timed_out` still dispatch, and the existing busy-guard / human-park / age guards are unchanged
- [ ] The decision about what a cancelled check SHOULD mean (ignore, re-run, or wait) is recorded on this card

## CEO decision, 2026-09-05

A cancelled CI check is UNKNOWN, not red. The approved-but-red sweep re-runs a cancelled check once; only a check that then FAILS is red and gets a fix agent. A cancellation never dispatches a fix agent, because a fix agent cannot fix a cancellation.

## Scope added 2026-09-10 (Plan A)

**Blocked by:** DRE-3580

The CEO's 2026-09-05 decision above stands and is widened. `cancelled` is not the only red no code can clear. **Re-run, don't fix** — three more classes join it:

* **Rate-limited.** A harness or CI leg killed by a Linear or Claude rate limit is red for a reason that has nothing to do with the branch. On 2026-09-09 four integration-harness runs went red this way, each on a critic-APPROVED PR.
* **No verdict.** A critic run that finished and wrote no verdict (PR #340 ran the review twice and left nothing) leaves the PR red with no statement a fixing agent could act on.
* **Inherited from a main that is now green.** A PR that went red on a main-side fault stays red after main is fixed. Re-running the check is the whole remedy.

**The evidence.** PRs **#335 and #340 waited 16 hours** for a re-run that a person finally had to make by hand. Both were critic-approved. No code change was needed, or made, in either case.

**The shape of the fix.** A **classifier in** `unfixable_checks.py` answers, for a red check, whether it is fixable-by-code or re-runnable; `reconcile.fix_approved_but_red` gains **one predicate line** calling it. A re-runnable red is re-run once; only a check that then **fails** is red and gets a fix agent.

**Files:** `bureau-pipeline/scripts/unfixable_checks.py`, `bureau-pipeline/scripts/reconcile.py` (one predicate line), `bureau-pipeline/config/pipeline-acts.json`, `bureau-pipeline/tests/test_unfixable_checks.py`

**Collision rule.** `reconcile.py` is owned this wave by DRE-3580 (the sweep-cost cut). The classifier lands in its own module; the call site here is one line.

**Added acceptance criteria**

- [ ] A rate-limited, a no-verdict and an inherited-from-a-green-main red are each classified re-runnable and re-run once, never dispatched a fix agent — one fixture per class.
- [ ] A genuine `failure` is still classified fixable and still dispatches.
- [ ] PROOF: one approved PR whose red is in one of these classes re-runs and merges **within the hour**, with no human act, recorded here with PT times and the run ids.

cards.title: [OPERATOR] Prove Phase 5 — the cutover happened and the old surface is gone
cards.description:
**Operator-only. The fleet cannot close this card, by construction.**

The whole argument for a route over a feature flag was that **the second surface actually goes away**. This card is where that claim is checked. If it closes with `/dashboard/next` still serving, the route was just a flag with extra steps.

## What must be observed, not asserted

- [ ] `/` serves One River **in production**, not only locally — checked against the deployed build, not `main`
- [ ] `/dashboard/next` is **gone**, returning 404, not redirecting
- [ ] `pages/Dashboard.tsx` is deleted and nothing imports it
- [ ] The temporary sidebar entry is gone
- [ ] `make deploy-lag` reports the console **ok 0** — the cutover is live, not merged-and-waiting
- [ ] The decision suite now asserts against the page serving `/`
- [ ] **You used it for a week of real work first.** A cutover proved by a smoke test is a cutover proved by nobody.

## The date

This phase carries the cutover date. Without one, "migrated" and "skipped" look identical — the argument [`adr-intake-cutover.md`](<https://github.com/dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau/blob/main/architecture/decisions/adr-intake-cutover.md>) already makes. Set it when the epic is green-lit, and put it here.

## The check that would have caught the propose gate

Before closing: `grep -r "dashboard/next" console/web/src`. Nothing should match. Three temporary mechanisms in this estate outlived their purpose because nobody ran the equivalent grep — the propose gate for six weeks, `fast-track` indefinitely, and four `/portfolio/*` routes still built and shipped today with nothing linking to them.

## Planner notes (2026-09-04, re-plan)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every item under "What must be observed, not asserted" above is observed by hand, against the live system, and recorded on this card as a comment with a PT timestamp
- [ ] Nothing in this phase was closed by a merge event: this card is closed by the operator after the observation, never by the pipeline

**Files:** none — nothing is committed by this card.

cards.title: [OPERATOR] Prove Phase 4 — the capacity strip, read against the live accounts
cards.description:
**Operator-only. The fleet cannot close this card, by construction.**

This strip exists because the CEO could not tell whether he was nearly out of subscription. A number that is merely *present* does not answer that — it has to be **right**, and right in the case that matters.

## What must be observed, not asserted

- [ ] Every account's percentage and reset time **matches the provider**, checked against the account itself, not against our cache
- [ ] The dispatch figure matches `github_quota` read at the same moment
- [ ] The deploy-lag figure matches `make deploy-lag`, and says **UNKNOWN, not 0**, for a repo the token cannot read
- [ ] **The alarm names the right resource.** With dispatch nearly out and every account quiet, the strip names *dispatch* — not the highest account. This was a real bug in the prototype, caught by testing it rather than looking at it.
- [ ] Quiet state still names the highest account and its reset. "All clear" answers whether anything is wrong, never whether you are nearly out.
- [ ] The amber and red thresholds were seen at least once — drive an account past 70 and 90, or prove it against a real one.

## The standing hazard this sits on

A clean read is not the same as a live one. See [[reference_green_cred_doctor_is_not_a_live_token]]: a green check that skipped its own live step is how a broken credential chain looked healthy for a month.

## Planner notes (2026-09-04, re-plan)

The capacity strip is DRE-3116.

cards.title: [EPIC] One River — the home page rebuilt at /dashboard/next, cut over on a date
cards.description:
Build the One River home page, decided with the CEO over two design sessions on 2026-09-03 ([DRE-3010](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3010), [DRE-3049](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3049)).

**Sibling of** [DRE-2520](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2520), not part of it. That epic is token cleanup, the signed-out screens, component-vocabulary duplication and dead routes. This is a home-page rebuild. Separate file footprints, separate epics.

## THE DESIGN IS THE CONTRACT — read this before decomposing

**Do not design.** Every choice below was made by the CEO and is pinned by `scripts/test_one_river_design.py` (the file is the count; it grows with each decision). The reference is:

* the decision list on [DRE-3049](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3049) — **this is the planner's input**
* `console/design/screens/web-dashboard-one-river-2026-09-03.html` — the working prototype
* `console/design/images/screens/desktop/dashboard-one-river-{overview,activity,pull-requests}.png` — every UI card carries the matching one as `**Design:**`
* **the planning stage, added 2026-09-04** — the decision record on [DRE-3106](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3106) (drawn in the design and its re-exported PNGs, PR #2280): an epic being planned is a row on the river, in the five states, with its own six-stage journey and the go on the row. It touches four cards, not a fifth: the Overview tab, the shell's ribbon, the row component and the decision suite each carry the addition in their own body
* **the Alerts tab, added 2026-09-04 15:53 PT** — the decision record on [DRE-3121](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3121): a fourth tab, last in the strip, the Alerts page's feed on the one grammar, row actions plus bulk select, and the Alerts page retires into it. Its build card is a Phase 3 child added through the mid-epic route; the route, registry, shell, suite and cutover cards each carry their one-line share. Zero new backend fields.
* **the Green Light tab, added 2026-09-05 08:45 PT** — the decision record on [DRE-3157](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3157): a fifth tab, SECOND in the strip, the CEO's decision queue — every card in the Green Light lane with the reason it is there and Approve / Answer / Send back on the row, longest-waiting first, a green outline on the tab. Read in context, work in a queue, one action: the river keeps its planning row and its Approve. The Plan Review page retires into it, and the two decision alert types leave Alerts for it. One new read that joins the lane to the pipeline's own receipts (reason per row); zero new mutations.

**If the design cannot be built as drawn, that is an amendment, not a decision.** Run `scripts/mid_epic.py discovery <this epic> --kind amendment` and it comes back to the CEO. Never a quiet redesign in a PR. See [adr-design-discovery-precedes-planning.md](<https://github.com/dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau/blob/main/architecture/decisions/adr-design-discovery-precedes-planning.md>).

## The cutover approach — a route, not a feature flag

`/` keeps today's `Dashboard.tsx`. The new page is built at `/dashboard/next`, reachable from a temporary sidebar entry. Both are live from the first PR, so supporting both interfaces costs nothing and needs no configuration.

Cutover is a one-line router change. A flag was rejected deliberately: it needs a source of truth, two code paths, both tested, and a removal card — and this estate has been burned three times by temporary mechanisms nobody deleted (the propose gate ran dead for six weeks, `fast-track` became a convention nobody meant, and `.env` drift means a flag can read differently local vs prod). **A flag is a thing you must remember to delete; a route is a thing you can see.**

The audience is the CEO and the operator. Rollback is reverting one line and redeploying.

## The data audit — run 2026-09-03, before planning

Eight of ten already exist. **Only two are new backend work.**

| the design needs | verdict |
| -- | -- |
| epic children | **exists** — `epicChildren`, tested, cold-serve tripwire ([DRE-2045](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2045/epic-children-popover-cold-cache-first-fetch-2s-resolver-first)) |
| `blockedBy` per child | **exists** — `inFlightMapping.planReviewProps` reads it today |
| cards that run in parallel | **exists, one level** — "children with no blocker" is wave 1 |
| full wave ranking | **new, frontend only** — a pure function of data already served |
| "N cards wait on it" | **new, frontend only** — the reverse edge of the same array |
| capacity per account | **exists** — `claude_accounts`, `SubscriptionsPanel` |
| GitHub dispatch quota | **exists** — `github_quota` |
| shipped / merged feed | **exists** — `shippedToday` |
| deploy lag / pending release | **NEW BACKEND** — CLI only (`make deploy-lag`), no GraphQL field |
| unified activity feed | **NEW BACKEND** — escalations, plans and runs are separate today |

Card the two backend items **first**; everything else is frontend over data that already ships.

## How to split it — the waves are project MILESTONES

This epic lives in its own project, [Bureau: One River](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/project/bureau-one-river-a7401df3c9d3), whose five milestones are the waves. **Set every child's milestone**; a card with no milestone is invisible to the project view.

| milestone | what |
| -- | -- |
| Wave 1 | the two fields that do not exist yet |
| Wave 2 | the shell — route, sidebar entry, ribbon, tab strip |
| Wave 3 | the three tabs, in parallel |
| Wave 4 | the capacity strip |
| Wave 5 | cutover, and the deletions |

Split on **file footprint**, not concern — three cards touching one file is three dirty merges.

**The milestone is for reading; **`blockedBy` **is what governs.** Reconcile promotes a Backlog child when its blockers are Done and has no awareness of milestones at all. So wire the dependency graph first and let the milestone follow it — a milestone that disagreed with the graph would be a second copy of an order the machinery already holds, and the machinery reads the graph.

## Four children are ALREADY FILED — do not create duplicates

These exist because the CEO asked what actually enforces fidelity, and the honest answer was "one gate, and it is off by default". Wire to them; do not re-file them.

| card | wave | why it is pre-filed |
| -- | -- | -- |
| [DRE-3062](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3062) | 2 | URL-addressable tabs. The visual harness addresses a **route** and cannot click a tab, so without this only Overview is ever compared. |
| [DRE-3063](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3063) | 2 | Register the three screens in `screens.mjs`. An unregistered screen is a **silent skip**, never a failure — the whole visual gate is off until this lands. |
| [DRE-3064](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3064) | 2 | The console's own decision suite. A screenshot diff cannot catch a removed control coming back; a structural assertion can. |
| [DRE-3061](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3061) | 5 | The cutover and its three deletions, filed before the build so they are written down while anyone cares. |

**All three Wave 2 cards BLOCK every Wave 3 card.** No tab may merge before the machinery that checks it exists. Wire `blockedBy` accordingly — that ordering is the enforcement, not the prose above it.

**Every Wave 3 card must, in its own body:** carry the matching `**Design:**` PNG, and extend [DRE-3064](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3064/the-consoles-own-suite-asserts-the-one-river-decisions-a-screenshot) with the decisions that belong to its tab.

## Constraints that are not negotiable

* `console/design/tokens.css` **is the palette.** The design's copy was reconciled to it on 2026-09-03; six values had drifted, two of them identity colours. Use the tokens, never the design's local names.
* **Five states, and only five.** Done and not-started are lifecycle — a dot and a quiet word, never a pill.
* **Nothing derives twice.** The read layer's one derivation shipped in Phase 6; every row reads it.
* **Port the decision assertions into the console's own test suite.** Nothing today would catch a React build that puts the removed sort control back, and a structural assertion beats a pixel diff — it survives a font change and still catches a re-decided layout.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `/dashboard/next` renders the design; `/` is untouched until the cutover card
- [ ] Every UI card carried a `**Design:**` PNG and the critic compared render to design
- [ ] The console's own suite asserts the decisions, not only the mockup
- [ ] Two new backend fields; no other schema change
- [ ] The cutover card is blocked by every other child

**Not green-lit.** Move this epic to `Planning` to start the planner — Planning dispatches it ([DRE-3030](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3030/the-relay-dispatches-the-planner-for-every-card-that-enters-planning)). Wave 7 sequencing is the CEO's call.

## Epic growth

**Green-lit at:** 21 cards · **Now running:** 44 cards

Added since green light:

* (none)

Amendments:

* (none)

cards.title: The converter carries the document's introduction, diagrams, zone strips, primers, locators and terms into `ai-readiness.json` — nothing the reader saw is left in the UNMAPPED report but answer metadata
cards.description:
Part 2 of replicating the readiness document (operator, 2026-09-03: "we lost all the graphics and other introduction text, we have to have that"). [DRE-3045](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3045/the-definition-format-gains-an-introduction-and-a-section-gains-its) adds the fields; this card fills them from the document and regenerates the template.

Blocked by: [DRE-3045](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3045/the-definition-format-gains-an-introduction-and-a-section-gains-its) — this card writes `intro`, `zone`, `primer` and `figure`, which that card's parser must accept before the regenerated definition can pass `readiness_questionnaire.test.ts`.

Hand-built: the converter runs against the source document, which is in S3 and not in the repo. Branch: `agent/DRE-<n>-<slug>`.

## The contract (declared by [DRE-3045](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3045/the-definition-format-gains-an-introduction-and-a-section-gains-its); written identically there)

```
intro: Array<{ title: string; rich: string }>
zone:   { name: string; gloss: string; tone: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 } | null
primer: string | null
figure: { svg: string; caption: string } | null
```

## What is carried, decided by the operator on 2026-09-03

**Introduction — two of the document's five front-matter sections, verbatim, plus one Portico-true block.**

1. "What this is, and how it works" — as one intro block, its prose as `rich`.
2. "What we are trying to work out" — as one intro block, prose and all six `<figure>`s (the six-layer run, the systems inside the network, hosting variants A and B, the five decisions, the review loop) inline in `rich` with their captions.
3. "How to use this form" — NOT the document's "How to use this document", which says to put a name in an owner field and press Share for a JSON file, nor "What this page does with what you type", which says answers stay in the browser with no autosave. Both are false in Portico. One short block replaces them, drafted here for the operator's approval before it is committed:

   > Nothing here has to be done in one sitting, in order, or by one person. Answers save as you type, and everyone on the form sees them. When you cannot answer fully, set the question's status — Partial, Need internal input, Cannot share and N/A all count as answers. The thirty questions flagged as gating are the ones we cannot scope without; if only those are answered, that is still worth sending. Use Comment to ask about a question and Suggest an edit to propose wording on someone else's answer. Press Submit when you are done; until then the form stays in draft.

"Document details" (prepared-by, the owner field, the customer's name) is per-instance and is not carried.

**Per section — the zone strip, the primer, the locator diagram. **`zone.name` from the strip's `.zn`, `gloss` from `.zg`, `tone` from the section's zone class in document order of first appearance (systems 1, boundary 2, runtime 3, people 4, across 5). `primer` from `p.sec-primer`. `figure.svg` from the locator's `<svg>`, `figure.caption` from its `aria-label`. The suggested-owner line names Oncor's people and is NOT carried; it stays in the UNMAPPED report as per-instance.

**After the questions — the terms as an agreement.** The "Terms, ownership and handling" view (WNK-3.4.0) becomes one entry in `agreements` with `required: true`, `gate` per the operator's choice at review (default `false`: shown and acknowledged, not blocking). The seven thousand characters of handling commitments are about an exported file and are Dreadnought's own words to reword — NOT carried, reported, and named on this card for the operator.

## Colours: resolve the variables, do not depend on the host

The document's SVGs and prose use 33 CSS custom properties from its own stylesheet (`fill="var(--z1)"`, `var(--bg2)`, …). Carried as-is they render black in Portico. The converter reads `:root { … }` from the source and rewrites every `var(--x)` in carried markup to its literal light-scheme value, so a stored definition renders the same anywhere and depends on no host CSS. A `var()` it cannot resolve is reported, not left in.

## Files (disjoint from parts 1, 3 and 4)

* `infra/scripts/convert-readiness-html.ts` — the front-matter reader, the section-head reader, the terms reader, the variable resolver.
* `infra/test/convert_readiness_sections.test.ts` — the synthetic document gains a zone strip, a primer, a locator and an intro section; each lands in the right field; a `var()` is resolved; an unresolvable one is reported.
* `docs/design/forms/templates/ai-readiness.json` — regenerated in one run. Still version 1: nothing has been placed from it.
* `infra/test/readiness_questionnaire.test.ts` — gains: three intro blocks with the two verbatim titles; six `<svg>` in the second; every section carries zone, primer and figure; five distinct tones; no `var(` anywhere in the definition; one agreement titled from WNK-3.4.0; the 132-question pins unchanged.
* `docs/design/forms/README.md` — the UNMAPPED table shrinks to answer metadata, cross-references, the blank option, "What we heard", the owner line, the handling text, and the two placeholders; say so.

## Not in this card

* Drawing any of it (parts 3 and 4).
* The handling commitments' rewrite — the operator's words.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `ai-readiness.json` carries three intro blocks, six inline diagrams, and zone + primer + locator on all thirteen sections, with no `var(` left in it
- [ ] The terms are one required agreement
- [ ] The Portico-true "How to use" block was approved by the operator before commit (link the approval)
- [ ] Section 1's fourteen questions still deep-equal `ai-readiness-data.json`
- [ ] Test commit first; mutation-proven

cards.title: The planner sizes against the ledger — every turn-cap death, split and hand-back as data it reads before it cuts a card
cards.description:
**CEO, 2026-09-03 17:31 PT: ***"We need the planner to look back over the mulch and look at our history. We're seeing a lot of cards now that are too big to get done in one cycle, and so we're having to split them. We need to make sure we take that into account."*

## What exists, and why it is not enough

[DRE-2893](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2893/the-card-quality-standard-learns-when-a-card-is-too-big-four-tells) put the **four tells** of a too-big card into `standards/card-quality.md` (contracts between pieces; two languages or tiers; a criterion counting something never enumerated; an unbounded quantifier), with the rule *two turn-cap deaths means split*. That is a static rule the planner reads as prose. It does not know how often it has been wrong, on what kind of card, or what the last split looked like — and the operator's memory says the count is going up, not down. The `.mulch/expertise/planning.jsonl` records carry the same lessons for interactive sessions, and the headless planner never sees them.

**A rule the planner cannot check itself against is a rule it will drift from.** The evidence that it drifts is measured: six dead runs and ~$65 across three cards in the week of 2026-08-29, every split shipping within hours.

## What to build

1. `scripts/split_ledger.py` — derives, from Linear and the run receipts, every card that: died at the turn cap (the `🛑` / dead-run markers, `error_max_turns`), was split (a Canceled card whose children or successors cite it; titles carrying "split from"), or was handed back by a build run as an epic. For each row: the card, its declared size, its role label, the file footprint it declared, the footprint the split pieces actually touched, the number of pieces, and which of the four tells applied in hindsight. Output `config/split-ledger.json` — regenerated by a scheduled job, never hand-edited, with the generation time inside it.
2. The planner reads it. `plan.yml` injects the ledger's summary into the planner's context the way standards are injected: the last N splits with their tells, and the measured rates (*"cards declaring more than 4 files died 7 of 9 times"* — whatever the data says). The planner brief gains one section: *before you size a card, read the ledger and say which tell you checked it against.* The plan artifact records that check per child.
3. **The mulch records reach the planner too.** The `planning` domain of `.mulch/expertise/` in agent-bureau (landed through `make mulch-sync`) is rendered into the same injected context, so a lesson recorded interactively is read by the fleet. One source, no copy.
4. **The plan critic checks it** ([DRE-2721](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2721/two-critics-one-before-you-read-it-one-after-you-approve-it)'s pre-approval critic): a child whose declared footprint matches a ledger pattern that has died before is flagged in the critic's reading, with the ledger row cited.
5. **A test with a fixture ledger** proves the planner's context contains the rows and the rates, and that a missing or stale ledger is reported as UNKNOWN in the plan artifact — never silently omitted.

## What this is measured by

[DRE-3016](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3016/score-the-planner-against-plans-it-has-never-seen-replay-past-epics)'s scorer gains a row: *split rate of planner-created children per month, before and after the ledger is read.* The number goes on this card before it is called done.

## File footprint

`scripts/split_ledger.py`, `config/split-ledger.json` (generated), `briefs/planner.md` (one section), `.github/workflows/plan.yml` (the injection), the ledger schedule (a small workflow or a step in `reconcile.yml`), `tests/test_split_ledger.py`.

**A deliberate probe, not real work.** Created 2026-09-03 18:00 PT for [DRE-3013](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3013/operator-proof-the-front-door-every-path-a-card-can-take-from-intake)'s test FD-6.

## The decision it carries, and there is nothing to build

Should the demo repo be **public**, so a prospect can read a real pipeline run before signing, or stay **private**, because its run logs show the model names, the token cadence and the internal card vocabulary?

Both are defensible. Public sells; private protects. The trade is commercial, not technical, and no acceptance criterion an agent could satisfy decides it. A planner that decomposes this into cards has misread it.

## Contract ([DRE-2848](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2848/hand-planning-is-an-escalation-and-nothing-else-no-label-flag-or-lane))

Hand-planning is an escalation and nothing else. The one exit from Planning that is not a plan: the run states the question in business terms — no diff, no code — posts it here, and parks this card in **Green Light** for the CEO.

**If a child card is created, a shape of one-off or epic is stamped and routed, or the card sits here unplanned, FD-6 FAILS** as written. Record on [DRE-3013](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3013/operator-proof-the-front-door-every-path-a-card-can-take-from-intake) the run id, the escalation text, the lane and the time. Cancel once recorded.

cards.title: Every behaviour-changing commit needs a preceding RED test — tighten the TDD floor from once-per-branch to once-per-change
cards.description:
**Operator decision, 2026-09-03: "we should always be doing TDD."** The enforced floor today is weaker than that, and the gap produced a 22-hour dispute.

## The two floors, and which one is enforced

|  |  |
| -- | -- |
| `check_tdd_commits.py` (enforced) | *"At least one commit touching files under* `tests/` *must appear STRICTLY BEFORE the first commit that changes non-test code."* One RED commit at the head of the branch satisfies it. |
| `standards/engineering.md:7-9` (prose) | *"Git history must show the test existed before the fix"* — which a strict reader applies per fix. |

They are different rules, and only the first is checked. PR #2247 is where that gap lived: the critic applied the stricter reading to `d3285ef` (a build-context fix with no paired test), the script exits 0, and both were arguably right about their own rule.

## The rule this card ships

> **Every commit that adds or changes behaviour must be preceded by a RED test commit for that behaviour. Every other commit must classify as an exemption.**

## The exemptions, and why a bare "one before each" is wrong

The critic's literal reading — a RED test immediately before *every* implementation commit — **fails honest work**, and an impossible gate teaches agents to manufacture fake pairings. That is worse than the gap it closes. These have no test that can be written first:

* **Deletions.** Removing dead code asserts nothing new; the existing suite passing IS the test.
* **Pure refactors.** Extract a module, rename a symbol, collapse duplication — the point is that behaviour does not change.
* **Docs, comments, and most config. **`d3285ef` is the live example: a `.dockerignore`-shaped exclusion. That branch did test it, twice — but many config lines have no assertable failure.
* **Generated files. **`graphql.ts`, the slug mirrors, anything a script emits. Testing them first means testing the generator, which is a different commit.
* **The RED commit itself.** Otherwise the rule recurses.
* **A fix to a broken test.** The rule would demand a test for the test.

**Note what this does to #2247:** under this rule `d3285ef` classifies as config and is exempt, so the tightened floor *vindicates* that branch rather than condemning it. The dispute was never about TDD discipline — it was about two floors and no arbiter.

## Why this is blocked on [DRE-3008](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3008/agent-bureau-does-not-run-the-tdd-commit-check-in-ci-the-only-enforcer)

agent-bureau does not run the TDD check in CI at all. Tightening the rule while nothing mechanical enforces it moves the argument from *"did you run it"* to *"does this commit qualify"* — with an LLM still adjudicating, in a `fetch-depth: 1` checkout, exactly as in #2247. **A stricter standard enforced by nothing is how this happened.** Install the gate, then raise the floor against something that runs.

## What to build

- [ ] `check_tdd_commits.py` implements the per-change rule: each `[code]` commit is either preceded by a `[test]` commit for the same behaviour, or classifies as an exemption
- [ ] **The exemption list is data, not a branch in the code** — a config file naming each exemption with its reason, so adding one is a reviewable decision rather than an edit to a conditional
- [ ] The classifier reuses the existing `[test]`/`[code]`/`[docs]`/`[ops]` machinery ([DRE-2741](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2741/the-tdd-gate-only-recognises-a-top-level-tests-so-in-every-repo-that)) — this is a stricter predicate over what already exists, not a second implementation
- [ ] **Its failure message names which commit failed and which exemption it could have claimed.** A gate that says "no" without saying "or one of these" is the thing that produces disputes
- [ ] `standards/engineering.md` states this rule ONCE, in the same words the script implements. The two-floor problem is the defect; a prose rule that differs from the enforced one recreates it
- [ ] The critic's brief points at the check's result and stops re-deriving the rule from prose
- [ ] Fixtures for every exemption — a deletion-only branch, a pure refactor, a generated-file update — each passing for the stated reason, not incidentally

## What must not break

* **A branch that satisfies the old rule and every exemption must still pass.** Run the new predicate over recent merged branches before shipping and name any that would newly fail — retroactively blocking in-flight work is not acceptable.
* The check must stay runnable offline and against the real merge base.
* Nothing here weakens the existing floor; it only raises it.

## Related

[DRE-3008](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3008/agent-bureau-does-not-run-the-tdd-commit-check-in-ci-the-only-enforcer) (installs the enforcement — blocks this), [DRE-3005](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3005/a-critic-verdict-can-assert-a-commands-output-without-running-it-two) (the critic dispute this gap produced), [DRE-2741](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2741/the-tdd-gate-only-recognises-a-top-level-tests-so-in-every-repo-that) (the test classifier), [DRE-2694](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2694/a-required-check-that-only-a-history-rewrite-can-satisfy-the-fix-loop) (the build agent's own commit-order check).

cards.title: The prototype's \"Data\" section is not the live Oncor section, and form_def_lib says it is
cards.description:
Found by [DRE-2648](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2648/operator-author-the-first-real-template-and-issue-it-to-oncor) while converting the **real** questionnaire, and independently verified against the source document before filing.

## The false claim

`infra/lambda/form_def_lib.ts:16`:

> …the section its own acceptance names — **the live Oncor "Data" section** — is one of the two it could not parse. `test/form_def_lib.test.ts` **carries that section verbatim**.

It does not. It carries the **prototype's six-question abridgement**. The live section in `~/Docs/gridcorr/readiness.html` has **14 questions**.

## Verified against the source, not inferred

Grepped the real 857 KB document:

| probe | occurrences in the live document |
| -- | -- |
| `attach a diagram` | **0** |
| `Attach a diagram` | **0** |
| `repeatLabel` | **0** |
| `system"` (D5's repeat label) | **0** |

So two constructs the format was **designed around** have no source:

* the prototype's **D6** (`type: "file"`, "attach a diagram") **is not a question in the document at all**
* **D5's **`repeats` / `repeatLabel` describes a repeating-row construct that **exists nowhere in it**

The `help` text was copied across; the `example` text was **rewritten**.

## Why this is worth its own card

`form_def_lib`**'s shape was written against the prototype rather than the card's prose** — deliberately, and the header says so, citing [DRE-2649](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2649/critic-review-the-whole-forms-card-set-before-any-of-it-starts) finding 5: *"the card's declared question shape could not express the prototype's own data."* That was a sound decision **given a prototype believed to be the live section**.

It was not the live section. So the format carries at least one field (`repeatLabel`) and one question type usage (`file`) justified by a document that does not contain them, and the test that pins the format's fidelity pins an abridgement while claiming to pin the original.

This is the [[capture-fixtures-never-invent-them]] failure in its most expensive position: **the artefact the whole epic treats as the binding spec. **[DRE-2628](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2628/epic-forms-a-form-is-its-own-object-in-portico) states the rule as *"where a card and the prototype disagree about behaviour, the card is wrong"* — that rule assumes the prototype is faithful to the source, and here it is not.

## Do

1. **Correct the comment at** `form_def_lib.ts:16` so it says what the fixture actually is — the prototype's abridgement — and stop calling it the live section. **Do not delete the fixture**: it correctly pins what the prototype requires, which is still a real constraint.
2. **Add the live section as a second fixture**, captured from `~/Docs/gridcorr/readiness.html` rather than retyped. [DRE-2648](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2648/operator-author-the-first-real-template-and-issue-it-to-oncor)'s PR #406 already produced `docs/design/forms/templates/ai-readiness-data.json` and a conversion script — **use those rather than starting again**.
3. **Decide what happens to** `repeats`**/**`repeatLabel` **and the** `file` **question type.** They may still be right — a future section or another customer may need them — but they must be justified by something real. **Either point each at a construct that exists, or record that it is speculative and why it was kept.** Removing them is also a legitimate answer.
4. **Check whether anything else in the format traces to the abridgement rather than the document.** The header names `rich`, `demo`, `figure`-as-object and a template `version` as prototype-driven. Same question applies to each.

## Do not

* **Do not "fix" the prototype to match the document.** It is a design artefact and its own thing; the error is the *claim* that it is a faithful copy, not its existence.
* **Do not weaken** `form_def_lib.test.ts`**.** It pins the prototype and should keep doing so under an honest name.

## Watch for

* [DRE-2648](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2648/operator-author-the-first-real-template-and-issue-it-to-oncor)'s PR #406 is open and touches `docs/design/forms/README.md` and adds the template JSON. **Coordinate or land after it.**
* [DRE-2957](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2957/the-measured-input-inventory-mis-adds-519-printed-as-619-in-six-places) (the 619-vs-519 input count) is the same class of defect in the same area — a number nobody re-derived from the source. The real count is **517**. Worth fixing together.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `form_def_lib.ts`'s header describes the fixture accurately and no longer claims the live section
- [ ] The live section exists as a captured fixture, sourced from the document rather than retyped
- [ ] Every format feature justified by the prototype is traced to a real construct, or recorded as speculative with a reason
- [ ] The existing prototype fixture still passes, under a name that says what it is
- [ ] Anything else in the format resting on the abridgement is identified and reported

cards.title: A comment on the form's construction cannot be anchored to a question — only answers have anchors
cards.description:
> **OPERATOR, 2026-09-02, using the build: ***"Comment anchors aren't working anymore on forms. Maybe they were never working on forms… There are comment anchors on the left-hand side. That's when you're building out the form and you're saying, 'I don't like this. I don't like that. Change this construct of the form.' Then there are comments inside the form once they've been created. Those have been done by the users."*

**They were never working on forms.** Not a regression — a gap.

## The two kinds, and which one exists

|  | who | about | today |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| **on an answer** | respondents, once the form is live | *"is Restricted the right tier here?"* | **built** — B3 ([DRE-2642](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2642/b3-a-comment-thread-on-an-answer-resolved-means-settled)), inline under each answer |
| **on the form's construction** | whoever is authoring or reviewing the template | *"question 3 is badly worded, change it"* | **missing** — document-level only |

The rail is behaving correctly for what it knows. `CommentsRail.tsx:186` reads `type AbsentReason = "external" | "form"` — B3 added `"form"` — so on a form the rail knows there is no locatable artifact and honestly offers only *"Comments here apply to the whole document."*

**What nobody built is the second anchor kind: a comment pinned to a QUESTION.** On a published document you select a passage and the anchor is a text hash. A form has no artifact to select in — its units are sections and questions, and `form_def_lib.ts` gives every question a stable `id`.

## Why this matters more than it looks

**The question id is already the universal join key** — the answer sort key `f#<questionId>`, the attachment key, and, importantly, **the comment anchor**: `response_export_lib.ts:141-152` already files unresolved thread roots by `anchorOf(row)` read as a question id, and `routes/responses.ts` joins the comment partition to answers on it.

So **the storage already supports this.** A comment whose anchor is `"D3"` is already meaningful to the server. What is missing is the surface: no way to *create* one against the question rather than the answer, and no way to see it in the rail grouped by question.

That also means this is mostly client work, and the backend should need little or nothing. **Confirm that before assuming it.**

## Do

**1. Anchor a comment to a question from the rail.** A reader reviewing the form's construction picks a question and comments on it. Decide the gesture — clicking a question while the rail is open is the obvious one, and it is what the "left-hand side" in the operator's description implies — and say why.

**2. Group the rail by question.** A thread anchored to `D3` shows as *"on question 3"* and is distinguishable from a document-level thread. The rail already renders `↳ On the answer to q1` for answer threads (B3), so there is an idiom to extend rather than invent.

**3. Keep the two kinds legibly different.** A comment about *the wording of the question* and a comment about *somebody's answer to it* are different acts by different people at different times. They may share a partition; they must not read as the same thing.

**4. Decide what happens to a construction comment when the template is instantiated.** A template snapshots into an instance at drag time (`items_lib.ts` `freeze`). Does a comment on the template's question 3 follow into every customer's copy? **Almost certainly not — that would leak our internal review notes to the customer.** Work out where those comments live and say so explicitly; this is the question most likely to be got wrong silently.

## Watch for

* `AnchorState` **has five members** (`Thread.tsx:35`) and `"answer"` means "no document position, ever". A question anchor is a sixth kind of subject or a reuse of an existing one — decide which, and do not overload `"answer"`, which B3 defined precisely.
* **Anchoring is paragraph-level and deliberately not character-precise** — a question id is stabler than a text hash, so this is the easy case. Do not build character offsets.
* **The dev mock has no** `POST /comments` **problem any more** ([DRE-2958](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2958/the-dev-mock-has-no-post-comments-the-local-loop-cannot-close-a) merged), but `/changelog` **is still missing** and another agent is live in `handlers.ts` right now. Coordinate before editing the mock.

## FILE OWNERSHIP — check before starting, several cards are live

Likely yours: `client/app/src/features/viewer/rails/CommentsRail/**` and `client/app/src/features/forms/FormReadingView.tsx`. [DRE-2993](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2993/column-view-is-two-fixed-panes-not-finder-columns-make-it-unbounded) **is live in** `features/library/**`**,** [DRE-2979](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2979/the-dev-mock-is-missing-changelog-and-attachments-the-details-rail) **in** `e2e/mocks/handlers.ts`**, and PR #402 is open against** `infra/lambda/**` **and** `AnswerHistory.tsx`**.** Read every file as it stands rather than as any card describes it.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A comment can be anchored to a specific question, and says which question it is on
- [ ] Question-anchored and document-level threads are visibly different in the rail
- [ ] A comment about the question's wording does not read as a comment about somebody's answer
- [ ] What happens to construction comments at instantiation is decided **and written down** — with the leak case named explicitly
- [ ] Existing answer threads (B3) and document-level threads are unchanged — asserted
- [ ] Driven in a browser, both themes, keyboard-reachable, screenshots in the PR

cards.description:
**Observed 2026-09-01 15:46 PT, confirmed on screen 2026-09-02** (Phase 6 reading 1 on [DRE-2950](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2950/proof-dre-2839-reading-1-take-2-lane-guard-in-report-mode-expect-a)). With `LANE_GUARD_MODE=report`, the relay wrote:

> 🚧 lane-guard-returned: [DRE-2950](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2950/proof-dre-2839-reading-1-take-2-lane-guard-in-report-mode-expect-a) was in `Todo` without the evidence that lane requires, so it has been returned to `Intake`.

The card stayed in Todo (and is in Backlog now). Report mode writes the receipt and takes the card off the dispatch path, but does not move it — the sentence describes what `enforce` would have done. The console renders the receipt's own words on the card panel ([DRE-2821](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2821/every-automatic-recovery-is-invisible-to-the-console-it-shows-the-last)), so the CEO reads a move that did not happen.

Wording only; the guard's behaviour is correct and pinned by [DRE-2725](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2725/the-guard-a-lane-must-be-justified-by-evidence-or-the-card-goes-back)'s matrix tests.

## What to change

In `cloud/relay/lane_guard.py`, the returned/parked receipt text carries the mode: in `report` it says what WOULD happen and that the card was left where it is; in `enforce` it says what did. One sentence each; the missing-evidence bullets are unchanged. The console needs no change — it renders `reason` verbatim.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Unit: the report-mode receipt for a returned card says the card was left in its lane and names the lane it would have gone to; the enforce-mode receipt is unchanged — red first
- [ ] The matrix test ([DRE-2725](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2725/the-guard-a-lane-must-be-justified-by-evidence-or-the-card-goes-back)) still passes cell for cell
- [ ] `scripts/test_receipts.py` (console side) still parses both wordings — `lane-guard-returned` is the tag either way

## File footprint

`cloud/relay/lane_guard.py`, `cloud/relay/test_lane_guard.py`. Deploy is the operator's (`cloud/relay/deploy.sh`), and the guard ships `off`, so nothing is live until Phase 7's cutover turns it on.

cards.title: CI · The client suite fails the RUN while passing every TEST — unhandled rejections after teardown
cards.description:
Observed three times in one session (2026-09-02) on unrelated PRs. Filed because each occurrence has been diagnosed from scratch, twice wrongly, and each costs a review cycle.

Branch: `agent/DRE-<n>-<slug>`, not the `sid/…` name Linear suggests.

## The signature

CI job `client — syntax & no external hosts`, always at **step 8,** `Install, typecheck, test and build the SPA`:

```
Test Files  155 passed (155)
⎯⎯ Unhandled Errors ⎯⎯
⎯⎯ Unhandled Rejection ⎯⎯   × 5
##[error]Process completed with exit code 1
```

**Every test passes and the run still fails.** An unhandled rejection does not fail a test; it fails the process. So a green "155 passed" sits directly above `exit code 1`, which is why this reads as infrastructure noise and is not.

## Occurrences

| PR | card | outcome |
| -- | -- | -- |
| #383 | [DRE-2645](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2645/b6-answer-writes-must-not-trip-the-write-budget-measure-it-before-a) | passed on a plain job re-run; branch touched **zero** client files |
| #391 | [DRE-2641](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2641/b2-suggestions-and-history-on-an-answer-in-the-ui) | real race — `mountForm()` returned before the response-poll effect committed. The critic reproduced it **once in 8 tries** running a specific **5-file combination**. Fixed with `await screen.findByText(...)` |
| #396 | [DRE-2980](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2980/the-docker-dev-stack-has-not-started-since-2026-08-16-compose-does-not) | this signature, 155/155 passing, exit 1 |

`FormPane.test.tsx` was named as the origin on #391 and is the common suspect, but do not assume it is the only one.

## Why it must be measured, not reasoned about

**A local full-suite run does not reproduce it.** On #391 I ran the whole client suite twice on the exact branch head: `exit 0`, **zero** unhandled errors, 2,229 passing — while CI failed reliably on the same sha. Vitest shards files across workers, and the race only appears in particular groupings. The critic reproduced it only by pinning a 5-file combination.

So: `npx vitest run` **passing locally is not evidence.** Reproduce by controlling the file grouping (`--shard`, or naming the files explicitly), and repeat — 8 attempts was the observed order of magnitude.

## What this has already cost

Three PRs blocked; two wrong diagnoses from me before the third was measured — first "CI infrastructure flake", then "an unguarded async effect in `FormPane.tsx`". Both were plausible from reading and both were wrong. The step's NAME is part of the trap: `client — syntax & no external hosts` says nothing about installing, typechecking, testing or building, which is what step 8 actually does.

## Scope

1. **Find what leaks.** A promise still in flight when jsdom tears down — a poll, a presence heartbeat, a fetch with no cancellation guard. `FormPane.tsx` has at least two fire-and-forget effects (`loadComments`, `loadSuggestions`) where a sibling effect in the same file uses a `cancelled` flag; that asymmetry is a lead, not a conclusion.
2. **Make the failure legible.** Whatever the cause, a run that fails while every test passes should say which file left the promise. Consider `dangerouslyIgnoreUnhandledErrors: false` with a reporter that names the origin, or a teardown assertion.
3. **Consider renaming the CI job or splitting step 8.** A step called "syntax & no external hosts" that installs, typechecks, tests and builds will keep being misdiagnosed by whoever reads the failure next.

## Do not

* Do not "fix" it by re-running the job. That worked once (#383) and hid a real race twice.
* Do not treat a green local `vitest run` as proof the branch is clean.

## Acceptance

- [ ] The leak is reproduced deliberately — a named file grouping that fails repeatably, not "it happened in CI"
- [ ] The source of the unhandled rejection is named, and cancelled at its source
- [ ] A run that fails with all tests passing prints which test file originated it
- [ ] Mutation-proven: reinstating the leak reddens a named check
