cards.title: Two popovers now sit two rows apart in the specimen — converge Tip and AccessPeek, or say why not
cards.description:
Surfaced by [DRE-2975](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2975/the-gating-badge-is-jargon-in-a-grey-pill-make-it-a-marked-icon-with-a) (PR #397), which added `Tip` and then declined to do this merge — correctly, since `AccessPeek` is moderator-gated by construction and owned by three library surfaces.

## What changed

`client/app/src/components/molecules/Tip.tsx` auto-registered in the specimen gallery (the registry globs `components/**/*.tsx`), so **two popovers now sit two rows apart on a page whose whole purpose is to show one of everything. **`Tip`'s own header already conceded the duplication and argued for it; the specimen page has now made that argument visible to everyone, which is the page doing exactly its job.

## The two, and why they were not one

* `AccessPeek` — moderator-gated by construction, carries an `AccessPeekModel`, used by three library surfaces. It cannot hold a plain sentence for a customer.
* `Tip` — a sentence and a glyph, no domain knowledge, reachable by any reader. Built for [DRE-2975](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2975/the-gating-badge-is-jargon-in-a-grey-pill-make-it-a-marked-icon-with-a) because `AccessPeek` structurally could not do the job.

`Tip` copied **every placement and dismissal rule** from `AccessPeek` deliberately, so that a later convergence would be a merge rather than a reconciliation. That was the plan; this is the card that either executes it or closes it.

## Do

**Decide, and write the decision down where the next reader meets it.** Two defensible outcomes:

1. **Converge.** Extract the shared popover mechanics — placement, flip-near-fold, edge clamping, `Escape` on a capture-phase listener, focus retention, portal to `document.body` — into one primitive, and let both compose it. `AccessPeek` keeps its model and its gate; `Tip` keeps its sentence. **One row in the specimen, two consumers.**
2. **Keep both, and say why in both headers.** If the gate and the model make a shared primitive more indirection than it removes, that is a real answer — but it has to be argued in the files, not left implied by the fact that nobody merged them.

**Do not** unify by giving `Tip` an `AccessPeekModel` or a moderator gate. That would put a customer-facing sentence behind a moderator check, which is the reason `Tip` exists.

## Watch for

* **The specimen page is a pixel gate.** Removing or restructuring a row regenerates baselines — through the pinned container (`npm run e2e:visual:update`), never on the host, and never committing `*-darwin.png` ([DRE-2372](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2372/running-playwright-on-macos-turns-the-infra-suite-red-the-platform)).
* `AccessPeek` has three consumers in `features/library/`. A change to its mechanics is a change to three screens; assert they are unaffected rather than assuming it.
* Keyboard behaviour is the load-bearing part of both. Whatever ships must keep: opens on focus as well as hover, `Escape` closes without throwing focus to the top of the page, nothing trapped.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Either one popover primitive with two consumers, or two components each carrying a written reason for staying separate
- [ ] `AccessPeek`'s three library surfaces behave identically — asserted, not assumed
- [ ] Keyboard behaviour unchanged for both: focus-open, `Escape`, no trap
- [ ] The specimen page shows the outcome honestly, and any baseline change is regenerated in the pinned container
- [ ] Both themes, screenshots in the PR

cards.title: A PR whose CI went red on a main-side fault stays red after main is fixed — nothing re-runs CI against the new merge ref
cards.description:
**Observed 2026-09-02 00:00–00:23 PT on agent-bureau PRs #2240 and #2241.** Both went red on `Console backend (pytest)` because of a fault on `main` ([DRE-2962](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2962/the-console-cannot-read-the-pipelines-new-medic-retry-declined-act-the): the console did not know a newly declared pipeline act). [DRE-2962](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2962/the-console-cannot-read-the-pipelines-new-medic-retry-declined-act-the)'s fix merged to `main` at 00:02. Both PRs stayed red: their CI had run at 00:00 against a merge ref computed before the fix, and nothing in the pipeline re-computes or re-runs it when `main` moves. #2240 had a critic APPROVE and a green fix-loop attempt sitting behind a failure that no longer existed on `main`.

The operator's session unstuck them by hand with `gh pr update-branch`, which makes a new head and re-runs everything — including a fresh critic review that the previous APPROVE already covered.

## Why a re-run is not the fix

GitHub re-runs a `pull_request` workflow against the **same **`GITHUB_SHA` — the original merge commit — so `gh run rerun` reproduces the stale failure. The only ways to get a fresh merge ref are a new head (push, `update-branch`) or close/reopen. Each has a cost: a new head discharges the verdict and re-reviews; close/reopen fires every `pull_request`-triggered workflow again and may confuse `linear-sync`.

## What to build

The reconcile sweep already knows which open PRs are red and which `main` commits landed since. Add one rule: **when** `main` **has moved since a PR's last CI run and that run failed only in jobs whose failure is also present on the pre-move** `main` (i.e. the fault was main-side, not the PR's), refresh the PR's merge ref via `update-branch` **once**, and say so in a receipt. The verdict-discharge cost is real; the receipt should name it, and the critic should recognise an `update-branch`-only head change as a re-review of the same content (the diff against `main` is unchanged).

Cheaper first step if the above is too much: detect the state and **report** it on the PR — *"CI is red on a fault that is already fixed on main; this PR needs a branch update"* — so an operator is not left diagnosing two green-looking PRs that will not merge.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A fixture: PR red only on a test that also fails on `main` at the PR's merge-base; `main` then gains a commit fixing it → the sweep updates the branch once and posts a receipt naming the main-side fix
- [ ] A PR whose failure is its own (fails on its diff, passes on `main`) is NOT updated — the fix loop owns that
- [ ] The update happens at most once per `main` commit, so a flapping `main` cannot churn a PR's head
- [ ] The receipt goes through `pipeline_act.py` and the console recognises it ([DRE-2821](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2821/every-automatic-recovery-is-invisible-to-the-console-it-shows-the-last)'s drift test stays green)

## File footprint

bureau-pipeline `scripts/reconcile.py` (a new sweep rule beside the conflict sweep) and its tests; `config/pipeline-acts.json` for the new act — **and** the console's `receipts.py:ACTS` in agent-bureau in the same window, or [DRE-2962](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2962/the-console-cannot-read-the-pipelines-new-medic-retry-declined-act-the)'s drift test fires again. Land them as a pair, pipeline first.

cards.title: SECURITY (detector gap) · The §7 conformance suite does not catch a route with NO read gate at all
cards.description:
Found by [DRE-2644](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2644/b5-mentions-in-a-form-thread-ask-somebody-never-invite-them) (PR #387) while mutation-testing its own new route. **This is a gap in the detector, not in a route** — which makes it worth more than the finding that exposed it.

## What happened

[DRE-2644](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2644/b5-mentions-in-a-form-thread-ask-somebody-never-invite-them) added `GET /comments/mentionable`. To prove its gate was load-bearing, the agent removed `assertMayOpenDoc` from the route entirely — **a route with no read gate at all** — and re-ran the suites.

Its own hand-written refusal test went red, correctly.

`infra/test/section_7_conformance.test.ts` **stayed green.**

## Why it missed

The suite tests **oracle equality**: that a hidden id and a ghost (nonexistent) id leave by the same refusal, so a caller cannot tell "exists but not yours" from "no such thing". That is the right property and it is the one §7 is about.

But it is a *relative* property. With the gate removed, the shelf gate still gave a hidden id and a ghost id **the same 404** — so the two bodies still matched and the suite passed, while the route was in fact answering to callers who should never have reached it. **Equality of refusals says nothing about whether a refusal happens.**

This is the same class as the four surfaces [DRE-2906](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2906/security-7-stops-at-four-surfaces-every-write-gate-is-a-403-vs-404) found and [DRE-2904](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2904/security-the-three-access-preview-routes-have-no-read-gate-at-all) closed (*"the three /access/* preview routes have no read gate at all"*), arriving from the other direction: those were found by reading routes, and the suite that was supposed to make that unnecessary would not have found them either.

## Why it matters now

Epic A closed roughly fifteen disclosure cards, and the conclusion recorded at the time was that a route-table-driven conformance suite beats a hand-governed list — it found leak #7 on a surface the list already claimed. That conclusion stands for *disclosure shape*. **It does not extend to gate presence, and it has been read as though it does.** Every new route since has been checked against a suite that cannot see the failure mode that matters most.

Epic B alone adds four routes on these partitions (`GET`/`POST /d/{docId}/suggestions`, `PATCH …/{suggestionId}`, `GET /comments/mentionable`).

## Do

Add a second, orthogonal check to the conformance suite: **for every route in the table, assert that an unauthorised caller is refused at all** — not merely that two refusals match. Drive it off `lib/route-table.ts` the way the existing suite does, so a new route is covered the moment it is registered rather than when somebody remembers.

The oracle-equality check stays; this sits beside it. Together they say "a refusal happens, **and** it discloses nothing".

Suggested shape, to be confirmed against the existing harness: for each `jwt` route, invoke it with a caller holding no grant on the subject and assert a refusal status; then invoke with a ghost id and assert the bodies are byte-identical. The second half exists today.

**Mind the zero-grant partitions.** Five pre-cutover portals hold no grant rows and rely on the zero-grant fallback in `assertReadableItem` ([DRE-2883](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2883/security-template-titles-and-definitions-leak-via-changelog-render)) — a naive "no grant ⇒ must refuse" assertion would go red on every one of them and get weakened rather than fixed. The check has to distinguish "no grant row exists anywhere in this partition" from "this caller has no grant".

## Acceptance

- [ ] A route registered in `lib/route-table.ts` with its read gate removed makes the conformance suite **fail**, mutation-proven on at least two different routes
- [ ] The check is table-driven, so a newly registered route is covered without editing the test
- [ ] The existing oracle-equality assertions still pass unchanged
- [ ] The zero-grant fallback partitions do not produce false failures, and the reason is written down
- [ ] The suite's header says plainly which of the two properties each half proves, so the next reader does not repeat this inference

cards.title: The cheap-poll short-circuit fires only 13% of the time — "almost entirely such polls" is not what the traffic does
cards.description:
Measured by [DRE-2645](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2645/b6-answer-writes-must-not-trip-the-write-budget-measure-it-before-a) (PR #383, `docs/evidence/DRE-2645/`). **Not urgent** — the partition sits at 0.34% of its read ceiling — but the code's own claim about its traffic is wrong, and the obvious fix is a bug.

## What the code claims

`routes/responses.ts:128-134`:

> A poll carrying `?since=<seq>` reads ONE item — the response's `meta#state` row — and, when nothing has moved, answers with an empty change list. It must never Query the whole response partition to discover that nothing happened; **the read-side of a shared editor is almost entirely such polls.**

The optimisation is real and correct. The claim about how often it *fires* is not.

## What the traffic actually does

In a sustained two-respondent session at `RESPONSE_POLL_MS = 3_000`, the cheap path took **13%** of polls — 20 `GetItem`/min against 17.3 `Query`/min. The other 87% found the cursor had moved and paid a full partition Query.

The reason is structural rather than incidental: **two people writing means the cursor is almost always moving.** The short-circuit was designed for a reader who is idle while someone else works; a shared editor with two active writers is the case where it least often applies — which is exactly the case Epic B exists to create.

## Why the obvious fix is wrong

The tempting move is to let the client advance its own cursor from the `seq` its own PUT returned, so its next poll short-circuits. **That loses writes.** Another respondent's write can hold a `seq` between the cursor the client last read and the one its own write was assigned — advancing past it means the client never learns that answer changed. This is the same class of error the version rule refuses at `responses_lib.ts:436-445`: do not infer a position in a total order from your own half of it.

So a real fix has to either make the Query cheaper (a projection, or a bounded read of only what moved) or accept the Query and say so. **Whichever it is, write down which.**

## Do

1. Correct the "almost entirely" sentence at `routes/responses.ts:128-134` to say what the measurement found, and cite it.
2. Decide whether 87% Query-per-poll is worth reducing at all. At 0.34% of ceiling on the measured load, "no" is a defensible answer and shipping the evidence is the deliverable.
3. If it is worth reducing, do **not** advance the cursor client-side. Say in the code why that option is refused, so the next reader does not rediscover it as an optimisation.
4. Re-check the numbers against whatever [DRE-2640](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2640/b1-suggested-edits-the-store-a-proposal-never-changes-the-answer) (B1) does to the poll — a cross-group read multiplies both halves by the number of respondent groups.

## Blocked by file ownership

`routes/responses.ts` is owned by [DRE-2640](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2640/b1-suggested-edits-the-store-a-proposal-never-changes-the-answer) **(B1)** this wave, and B1 changes the poll. **Land after B1**, and re-measure rather than assuming the 13% survives.

## Acceptance

- [ ] The code's claim about poll traffic matches a measurement, and names it
- [ ] The client-side cursor advance is refused in writing, with the reason
- [ ] Either a reduction ships with before/after numbers, or the decision not to reduce is recorded with the figure that justifies it
- [ ] The numbers are re-taken against B1's cross-group poll, not inherited from the single-group measurement

cards.title: The measured input inventory mis-adds — 519, printed as 619, in six places
cards.description:
Found by [DRE-2645](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2645/b6-answer-writes-must-not-trip-the-write-budget-measure-it-before-a)'s measurement (PR #383), which had to run every result at **both** totals so that no conclusion depended on which one is real. Somebody has to say which one is.

## The arithmetic

`responses_lib.ts:43-45` states the inventory measured on the real questionnaire:

> 222 textareas · 200 selects · 79 checkboxes · 18 text inputs
> = 619 inputs, over 132 questions, across 13 sections

**222 + 200 + 79 + 18 = 519.**

## Where the wrong total is repeated

| file | line |
| -- | -- |
| `infra/lambda/responses_lib.ts` | `:45` (the sum itself), `:47`, `:59` |
| `infra/lambda/routes/responses.ts` | `:30`, `:77` |
| `infra/lambda/form_attachments_lib.ts` | `:127` |

## Why it is not merely cosmetic

`MAX_FIELDS_PER_RESPONSE = 1000` is justified at `responses_lib.ts:47` as *"the 619 measured inputs plus ~60% headroom"*. That derivation only works at 619 — at 519 the headroom is ~93%. **The cap is safe either way**, so this is not a bug in behaviour; what is broken is the *provenance* of a constant that a future card will be asked to raise or lower.

`form_attachments_lib.ts:127` compounds it by citing the figure as the example of a **measurement** as against a bound: *"A BOUND, NOT A MEASUREMENT. Unlike MAX_FIELDS_PER_RESPONSE (619 measured…)"*. A measurement that does not add up is the weaker half of that contrast.

## Which number is real is not knowable from the repo

Either the four counts are right and the sum was mis-added, or one count was mistyped (322 textareas would give 619). **Re-measure the real document** — do not pick the number that makes the headroom sentence work.

## Do

1. Re-count the inputs on the source questionnaire. Record how you counted.
2. Correct the total, the four counts if any is wrong, and the headroom sentence at `:47` so the derivation matches the number.
3. Fix all six sites. They are comments only — **no behaviour change, and** `MAX_FIELDS_PER_RESPONSE` **stays 1000** unless the re-count says otherwise, in which case say so explicitly rather than folding it in.
4. Add the arithmetic as a test if it is cheap to do so — a sum stated in prose beside its own addends is checkable, and this one survived two cards' worth of close reading.

## Blocked by file ownership

`responses_lib.ts` and `routes/responses.ts` are owned by [DRE-2640](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2640/b1-suggested-edits-the-store-a-proposal-never-changes-the-answer) **(B1)** this wave. **Land this after B1 merges**, or it conflicts.

## Acceptance

- [ ] The real input count is re-measured, and how it was counted is written down
- [ ] All six sites agree with each other and with the four addends
- [ ] The `MAX_FIELDS_PER_RESPONSE` headroom sentence matches its own arithmetic
- [ ] No behaviour change, and the diff is comments only unless the re-count forces otherwise

cards.title: Request access — an existence-blind way to ask, so §7 can close without stranding the reader
cards.description:
Split out of [DRE-2926](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2926/security-the-403-vs-404-oracle-is-wider-than-the-shelf-it-covers-every) on 2026-09-01, after the operator's decision recorded there. **This lands BEFORE or WITH 2926**, never after: 2926 alone collapses every refusal to 404 and, without this, a reader holding a valid link has no way forward at all.

Branch: `agent/DRE-<n>-<slug>`, not the `sid/…` name Linear suggests.

## The problem this exists to solve

Today a project member with no grant gets **403** on a document that exists and **404** on one that does not. That pair is an existence oracle across customers — the `vericorr` group holds four unrelated organisations — and [DRE-2926](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2926/security-the-403-vs-404-oracle-is-wider-than-the-shelf-it-covers-every) closes it by making both 404.

But the 403 was doing real work. It is what makes "ask for access" a sensible next step rather than "that link must be broken". [DRE-2294](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2294/upload-never-completes-client-registers-the-doc-under-a-minted-id) chose it knowingly. Removing it without a replacement strictly worsens the reader's day, which is why this is a card and not a footnote.

## What to build

A **request access** action offered on any 404 for an item id.

**The whole point is that it must be existence-blind.** It has to behave identically for:

* an item that exists and the caller has no grant on
* an item that has never existed

Same status, same body, same latency shape, same UI. If a caller can tell those apart by ANY means — the response, an error, a timing difference, whether a later email arrives — the oracle has simply moved, and this card has failed.

## The shape to think about

* A real id produces a request a moderator can see and act on.
* A ghost id produces the same answer to the caller and nothing behind it.
* The caller is told "your request has been sent" in both cases. That sentence is true in one case and harmless in the other, and it is the price of the property.
* Rate-limit it, because an unauthenticated-feeling endpoint that writes a row per call is a write-amplification surface — see ADR-0003's throughput trigger.

Do not design the moderator side by reflex. Ask whether it belongs in the existing `/people` or share panel rather than a new inbox nobody checks.

## Do not

* Do not make the response vary on existence in any way, including the error text on a rate-limit refusal.
* Do not send a notification only when the item is real — that leaks by absence, one step removed.
* Do not tighten the grant walk or the zero-grant fallback; load-bearing for five pre-cutover portals.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A real-but-ungranted id and a never-existed id produce **byte-identical** responses to the caller
- [ ] A moderator can see and act on a request for a real item
- [ ] Nothing observable to the caller distinguishes the two cases — asserted, not assumed, including the notification path
- [ ] Rate-limited, with the limit's refusal also existence-blind
- [ ] Mutation-proven: reverting the blindness reddens a named test

cards.title: A console release attaches every card a commit message mentions — DRE-2911 and DRE-2912 read as released with nothing shipped
cards.description:
**The release step in** `infra/deploy-console.sh` **attaches to the Linear release every card whose identifier appears in a commit message since the last release — not only the cards whose work actually merged. On 2026-09-01 release** `agent-bureau-console-v1.6.11` **attached 18 cards; at least three of them shipped nothing.**

## Observed

From the deploy output, 13:11 PT:

```
cards named by those commits: DRE-2830, DRE-2731, DRE-2870, DRE-2872, DRE-2771,
  DRE-2821, DRE-2811, DRE-2890, DRE-2892, DRE-2839, DRE-2852, DRE-2891, DRE-2678,
  DRE-2308, DRE-2910, DRE-2911, DRE-2912, DRE-2943
Linear attached: DRE-2943, DRE-2912, DRE-2911, ... 
[release] completing the Linear release agent-bureau-console-v1.6.11 — it is live
    ... its cards read as live
```

* [DRE-2911](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2911/four-backend-surfaces-stop-asserting-what-they-never-read) **and** [DRE-2912](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2912/four-frontend-surfaces-stop-asserting-what-they-never-read) are open in Backlog by operator decision, each with no branch and no PR. They appear because [DRE-2914](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2914/declare-dre-2871s-three-replacements-into-phase-6-and-drop-the-two)'s roster commit and [DRE-2931](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2931/a-platform-fault-is-charged-to-the-card-as-a-model-death-two-of-dre)'s commit name them in prose. Their Linear release stage now reads as live.
* [DRE-2839](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2839/operator-prove-phase-6-the-board-can-be-read-during-the-cutover) is a `no-code` operator proof card. Nothing about it is deployable.
* Several others ([DRE-2731](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2731/the-alerts-list-renders-utc-as-if-it-were-local-an-alert-reads-7-hours), [DRE-2771](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2771/phase-1s-two-lane-changes-were-never-declared-the-board-still-has-no), [DRE-2308](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2308/unlayered-handoff-reset-beats-every-tailwind-text-utility-dark-ink-on)) are referenced by commits that cite them as context, not as the card being shipped.

## Why it matters

The whole point of the release record ([DRE-2733](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2733/the-version-annotation-records-a-mutable-tag-so-a-rollback-resolves)'s "its cards read as live") is that a card's release stage is **ground truth** for "is this on the screen yet." A card marked released because a commit *mentioned* it is the same defect as a card marked Done because an agent *said* so — the thing `linear-sync` exists to prevent. During the cutover week, when the operator is reading release state to tell shipped from not-shipped, a false "released" is worse than none.

## What to build

Attach a card to a release only when a **merged PR** for it is in the release's commit range. The join key already exists: `linear-sync` closes cards by reading the identifier out of the merged branch name (`agent/DRE-<n>-…`). Use the same source — merge commits whose head branch matches `^agent/DRE-(\d+)-` — rather than a regex over every commit body.

Cards that are only *mentioned* can be listed separately in the release notes as "referenced", never as shipped.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The release attaches only cards whose `agent/DRE-<n>-*` branch merged within the release's commit range; a test drives the resolver with a fixture log containing a prose mention and asserts it is NOT attached
- [ ] A `no-code` / `hand-built`-without-PR card is never attached
- [ ] Mentioned-but-not-shipped cards appear under a separate "referenced" heading in the release body, or not at all — never under shipped
- [ ] The v1.6.11 release is corrected by hand as part of this card: [DRE-2911](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2911/four-backend-surfaces-stop-asserting-what-they-never-read), [DRE-2912](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2912/four-frontend-surfaces-stop-asserting-what-they-never-read) and [DRE-2839](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2839/operator-prove-phase-6-the-board-can-be-read-during-the-cutover) detached, and the PR says which others were reviewed and kept
- [ ] The card-closing rule and the release-attaching rule cite the same branch-name parser, so they cannot drift

## File footprint

`infra/deploy-console.sh` (the `[release]` step) and whatever helper it calls to resolve cards (`scripts/linear_release.py`), plus tests. Nothing in the deploy or rollout path itself.

cards.title: SECURITY · The 403-vs-404 oracle is wider than the shelf — it covers every ordinary document
cards.description:
Found by the agent implementing [DRE-2906](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2906/security-7-stops-at-four-surfaces-every-write-gate-is-a-403-vs-404), in its own first cut, and **deliberately narrowed back out of scope rather than smuggled in**. Reported on PR #371.

Branch: `agent/DRE-<n>-<slug>`, not the `sid/…` name Linear suggests.

## What [DRE-2906](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2906/security-7-stops-at-four-surfaces-every-write-gate-is-a-403-vs-404) fixed, and what it left

[DRE-2906](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2906/security-7-stops-at-four-surfaces-every-write-gate-is-a-403-vs-404) brought the write gates under §7 **for form templates**: a non-moderator now gets the same bytes for a shelf template as for an id that never existed. That closes the oracle over the shelf.

**The same oracle still exists over every ordinary document.** A non-moderator who holds no role on a real document gets **403**, where an id naming nothing gets **404**. That pair confirms the document exists — the identical disclosure, on a far larger population: **95 real customer documents across five live portals**, versus zero templates in production today.

## Why it was not fixed in [DRE-2906](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2906/security-7-stops-at-four-surfaces-every-write-gate-is-a-403-vs-404)

The agent's first cut collapsed this too, and **it broke nine tests across six suites** that pin that 403 as the escalation refusal *in those exact words* — [DRE-2294](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2294/upload-never-completes-client-registers-the-doc-under-a-minted-id)'s re-upload guard among them. Those tests are not wrong; they encode a deliberate decision that a subject who is *in the project* but lacks a role should be told "you may not", not "there is nothing here".

So this is a **product decision before it is a fix**, and it is genuinely contested:

* **For collapsing it:** an existence oracle over customer documents is a real disclosure, and §7 exists precisely to close that class. The share model's boundary is the grant, not project membership.
* **Against:** a project member meeting a 404 on a document a colleague just linked them has no way to tell "I need access" from "that link is broken". The 403 is what makes "ask for access" a sensible next step, and [DRE-2294](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2294/upload-never-completes-client-registers-the-doc-under-a-minted-id) chose it knowingly.

**Do not just pick one.** The honest answer may be a third thing — a refusal that admits the item exists but names no attribute of it, or a distinction between project members and strangers.

## Where it stands recorded

Not silently left: the gate's header and `disclosure.test.ts`'s governed-surface list both now say this is **not yet governed**, so the next reader meets the gap rather than inferring the rule is universal.

## Scope

1. **Decide the rule with the operator first.** Which refusal does a project member with no grant get, on a document that exists?
2. Only then implement, and update the nine pinning tests **to the new decision** rather than deleting them — each carries the reason its 403 was chosen.
3. Whatever is chosen must be **one rule**, reached from the existing ladders, not a per-route judgement call.

## Do not

* Do not weaken the template gate [DRE-2906](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2906/security-7-stops-at-four-surfaces-every-write-gate-is-a-403-vs-404) landed.
* Do not tighten the grant walk or the zero-grant fallback — load-bearing for five pre-cutover portals.
* Do not delete a pinning test to make a suite green; that is the failure mode this epic has already paid for three times (a test pinning a vulnerability as correct).

## Acceptance

* ☐ The operator's decision on the refusal is recorded on this card before any code
* ☐ One rule, on the existing ladders, applied to every surface that can refuse on an item id
* ☐ The nine pinning tests updated to the decision, with their reasons rewritten, not removed
* ☐ `disclosure.test.ts`'s governed list grows to include it
* ☐ Mutation-proven per surface

## CEO decision, 2026-09-05

The decision was already made on 2026-09-01 and is reproduced here so the classifier reads it from the body:

## Operator decision, 2026-09-01 — collapse to 404, and give the reader a path that leaks nothing

This card asked for the rule to be decided before any code. Here it is.

**The rule:** a caller with no grant on an item gets the **same bytes** whether or not that item exists. 404, `{"error":"not found"}`, on every surface that can refuse on an item id. No 403-vs-404 pair survives anywhere.

**And, because the 403 was doing real work:** any 404 on an item id offers **request access**, and that action is **existence-blind** — it accepts identically for a real id and for one that never existed, and tells the caller nothing either way. The moderator receives the request and decides. That gives back what DRE-2294 was protecting without paying for it in disclosure.

## What decided it

The card called this genuinely contested, and it framed the cost as a project member meeting a 404 on a link a colleague sent them. **Measured against the live pool, that framing is wrong.** The `vericorr` Cognito group holds four organisations:

```
vericorr.com                  3
chapmanengr.com               2
trophyintegrityservices.com   1
dreadnoughtfoundry.com        1
```

A "project member with no grant" is therefore **Chapman Engineering asking whether Trophy Integrity Services' document exists** — two unrelated customers who share a group because they share a portal. Not a colleague.

Two facts break the tie the card described:

1. **The ids are guessable.** Library ids are deterministic path slugs, and the real ones in that partition include `d-chapman-ai-survey-data-assessment`, `d-trophy-coupon-data-review`, `d-sallyport-mou-heads-of-terms` — derived from titles. This is not a brute-force oracle; it is a "guess the competitor's document name" oracle.
2. **"Ask for access" never required the 403.** That was an assumption, not a constraint. An existence-blind request-access path serves the same reader without confirming anything.

## What this means for the nine pinning tests

They are **rewritten to this rule, not deleted.** Each one records why a 403 was chosen on DRE-2294; each keeps that history and states what replaced it and why. A test deleted to make a suite green is the failure mode this epic has already paid for three times.

## Scope, restated with the decision made

1. One rule, reached from the existing ladders — not a per-route judgement call, and not a fourth naming pattern for refusals.
2. Every surface that can refuse on an item id, not just the ones in front of us.
3. The request-access path is part of this card, because without it this change strictly worsens the reader's day.
4. `disclosure.test.ts`'s governed list grows to include it; the gate header's "not yet governed" note comes out.
5. Mutation-proven per surface.

## Explicitly not in scope

* Do not weaken the template gate DRE-2906 landed.
* Do not tighten the grant walk or the zero-grant fallback — load-bearing for five pre-cutover portals.
* Do not resolve group principals to respondent partitions; that is DRE-2948's neighbourhood and a separate, larger question.

cards.title: The shelf route now issues one Query per form — new read pressure on the ADR-0003 trigger partition
cards.description:
Disclosed by the agent on PR #364 ([DRE-2888](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2888/compliance-answered-means-three-different-things-the-operator-gets-the)), in its own report, unprompted. **Not a defect and not a reason to block that PR** — a consequence worth having written down before anyone is surprised by it.

Branch: `agent/DRE-<n>-<slug>`, not the `sid/…` name Linear suggests.

## What changed

[DRE-2888](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2888/compliance-answered-means-three-different-things-the-operator-gets-the) unified four disagreeing definitions of "answered" into one rule. Answering it honestly for a **file question** requires knowing whether an attachment exists — a fact the shelf did not previously need. So `form_progress_lib` gained `queryFormAttachedFieldIds`, and **the shelf route now issues one Query per form.**

That is the right correctness trade: the alternative was the shelf continuing to report a removed file as a supplied document, which is the compliance defect [DRE-2886](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2886/compliance-a-removed-file-still-exports-as-a-supplied-document) was opened for.

## Why it is worth recording anyway

CLAUDE.md's ADR-0003 trigger table names exactly one detector that an item count will never warn you about:

> **Throughput** — any sustained DynamoDB `UserErrors`/throttle on the `lib#<project>` partition → re-architecture: jittered stale-while-revalidate on the container cache, or GSI1.

and says why it is the trigger most likely to fire first: every mutation bumps `meta#epoch`, invalidating **every** warm container's cache at once, after which the next burst of readers each performs a full partition Query. **The failure mode is a correlated burst, not a big table.**

A shelf load that was O(1) partition reads is now O(number of forms). Today that is **zero** — production holds no `artifactKind = 'form'` rows in any partition, measured 2026-08-31. It becomes N the moment templates are placed at scale, and the shelf is a moderator screen that gets opened repeatedly.

## What this card is NOT

* **Not** a request to add GSI1. The ADR is explicit that both index shapes are added **only on a measurement**, and a card that adds one before its trigger fires is out of scope. That has not changed.
* **Not** a request to revert or weaken [DRE-2888](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2888/compliance-answered-means-three-different-things-the-operator-gets-the)'s correctness.
* **Not urgent.** With zero forms it costs nothing.

## What to actually do

1. Confirm the DynamoDB throttle alarm (`portico-<acct>-ddb-throttles`) still exists and is the detector for this. **It currently has no action wired** — see `docs/worklist.md` §10, "All 15 alarms have zero actions" — so today it would fire into nothing. That is the part worth fixing first, and it is arguably a bigger gap than this card.
2. Decide whether the per-form Query should be batched or folded into the single partition read the shelf already does. The attachment rows live in `att#<project>#<docId>`, a different partition, so this is not free — say so either way.
3. Write the measurement into the ADR's trigger table if it changes when the throughput trigger is expected to fire.

## Acceptance

- [ ] The read amplification is stated in `form_progress_lib`'s header, in the shape the rest of this repo uses (what it costs, and why it is still right)
- [ ] The throttle alarm is confirmed as the detector, and its missing action is either fixed here or filed
- [ ] A decision recorded on batching vs leaving it, with the reason
- [ ] No GSI added without a measurement that fires the documented trigger

cards.title: CI runs only e2e/visual — every other Playwright spec is unenforced, and 17 of them are already failing
cards.description:
`.github/workflows/ci.yml:405` runs `npx playwright test e2e/visual` — the specimen pixel gate. That is the only Playwright invocation in CI. Every other spec under `client/app/e2e/` is written, committed, and executed by nobody.

This is not a gap in coverage. It is a gap in *enforcement*, and it makes a whole class of test in this repo decorative — including the specs written specifically because unit tests cannot see what they see.

## What it has already cost

* **17 e2e specs are failing on** `main` **right now** and have been for some time: `answer-actions` ×6, `answer-sync` ×2, `shared-answers` ×4, `share-openers` ×2, `identity-signout`, `kebab-flip`, `reader-flow`. Nobody knows how long, because nothing reports it.
* `share-openers` waits for a control named `Manage access — 2 grants`. **No such label exists anywhere in** `src` — the only one is `FolderCard`'s `Manage access on ${name} — ${spoken}`. The spec is stale against the product and has been passing nothing for however long.
* [DRE-2867](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2867/a-moderator-can-add-a-person-from-the-ui-access-and-sign-in-in-one) added two specs to catch the exact defect class that unit tests miss — a control rendered underneath another one — then broke three of its own assertions in a later commit in the same card and merged green. Repaired in [DRE-2919](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2919/the-people-panels-e2e-assertions-rotted-against-a-copy-change-in-the).

The pattern is the one CLAUDE.md already names: this repo has certified behaviour that never happened live at least five times. An unenforced suite is a fifth way to do it.

## The decision this card has to make first

Turning the suite on with 17 known failures just paints CI red and teaches everyone to ignore it. So the first task is triage, not wiring:

* which of the 17 are **stale specs** describing a product that moved (like `share-openers`) — fix or delete;
* which are **real defects** — file them;
* which are **flake** — quarantine explicitly, with the reason, not silently.

Only then is the workflow change safe to land.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every spec under `client/app/e2e/` is either passing in CI, or excluded by an explicit list that names each exclusion and why.
- [ ] CI fails when a spec in the enforced set fails. Proven by breaking one deliberately and watching the run go red.
- [ ] The runner uses Node 24 — the suite cannot start on Node 22 (`@mswjs/http-middleware` → `require("msw")` dies); `.nvmrc` already says 24.
- [ ] The 17 current failures are each dispositioned in the card's comments: fixed, filed, or quarantined-with-reason.
- [ ] Runtime is stated. If the full suite is too slow for every PR, say so and split it — a nightly that nobody reads is this card's problem all over again.

## Note on cost

The visual job already builds the app and runs Playwright in a pinned container, so most of the machinery exists. This is mainly a question of which specs to trust, not of new infrastructure.

cards.title: CI · The account-roster check can't see prose — "all three accounts" walks past it
cards.description:
Raised by the QA critic on PR #360 ([DRE-2909](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2909/docs-claudemd-still-names-a-deleted-config-vericorr-is-a-project-not)), and agreed with — deliberately **not** fixed there, under a merge deadline, because the naive version breaks the very documents that PR just wrote.

Branch: `agent/DRE-<n>-<slug>`, not the `sid/…` name Linear suggests.

## The gap

`infra/test/account_roster_in_docs.test.ts` gained a property that catches an account slug used as an instruction — `--profile <slug>`, `--table docs-comments-<slug>`, `DocsComments-<slug>`. It found six files the first property missed.

It cannot see the same fact written as **prose or as a bare table cell**:

* `docs/runbooks/migration-om2.md:42` — "The moderator group is `moderators` in all three accounts", sitting **directly below** the paragraph that PR added saying "Two accounts, not three."
* the same file's Step 1 record table — a row whose only content is `vericorr`, no `--profile`, no `--table`.
* "All of them, **for all three accounts**, in one sitting."

All three were fixed by hand on #360. Nothing stops them coming back, and the file they were in is explicitly a **reusable template for the next milestone** — so a stale count there walks the next operator into a destroyed account.

## Why the obvious fix is wrong

`/\b(two|three|four)\s+accounts\b/` fails immediately, and it fails **on the good documents**:

* `CLAUDE.md:41` — "The ADR says **three accounts** and said so correctly on 2026-07-27" — deliberate, and marked as the count at decision time. ADR-0003's argument rests on each account being separately billed, not on how many there are; correcting it to "two" would misrepresent an Accepted decision record.
* `docs/worklist.md` — several dated incident narratives ("hand-drove three accounts one command at a time") that were true when written and are the record of why a rule exists.
* `docs/build-plan/**` — a planning corpus written against the estate of the time. It should not be rewritten and probably should not be scanned at all.

A check that flags those gets one of two responses: somebody deletes the history to make it green, or somebody deletes the check. Both are worse than the gap.

## What is actually wanted

The distinction is **tense and audience**, not vocabulary: a count in an INSTRUCTION someone will follow is a defect; a count in a RECORD of what happened is correct. Some options, in rough order of how promising they look:

1. Scope by file: apply the prose rule only to `docs/runbooks/**` and `infra/README.md` — the operator-facing corpus — and never to `docs/build-plan/**` or ADR summaries.
2. Reuse the two exemptions that already exist and work: the `SAYS_ITS_GONE` same-line predicate, and the first-30-lines `HISTORICAL RECORD` / `RETIRED` banner.
3. Consider whether a bare table cell is worth chasing at all, or whether the file-level banner is the honest tool for a file with a retired account in a table.

Whatever is chosen, **write down why the excluded corpora are excluded** — that reasoning is the whole value, and its absence is why this gap existed.

## Do not

* Do not edit ADR-0003's body, or any decision record, to match a later world.
* Do not rewrite `docs/build-plan/**`.
* Do not make the check so broad that the fix is to delete history.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A stale count in an operator-facing INSTRUCTION fails CI, with a message naming the file and line
- [ ] `CLAUDE.md`'s ADR-0003 note, `docs/worklist.md`'s incident narratives and `docs/build-plan/**` all still pass
- [ ] The exclusions carry a written reason in the test file
- [ ] Proven by restoring one of the three lines #360 fixed and watching CI fail
- [ ] Mutation-proven: with the new rule removed, that same line passes

cards.title: COMPLIANCE · An answer to a question the form never asked exports as an ordinary answer, and reads 12/11
cards.description:
Settled from [DRE-2895](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2895/investigate-three-suspected-export-defects-the-review-could-not-close), finding 3. **The arithmetic is reproduced by execution; the write leg is established by reading the route.** Verdict: defect.

Nothing checks a stored field id against the instance's frozen definition — not at the write, not at the count, not at the export. So a form that asks eleven questions can hold twelve answers, and the twelfth rides into a signed compliance return with nothing marking it as unasked.

Branch: `agent/DRE-<n>-<slug>`, not the `sid/…` name Linear suggests.

## The probe

`cd infra && node --import tsx probe.ts`:

```ts
import { buildFolderFormTotals, buildFormInstanceItem, buildFormTemplateItem } from '<repo>/infra/lambda/items_lib.ts';
import { answeredFieldCount, buildSubmissionExport } from '<repo>/infra/lambda/response_export_lib.ts';
import { buildFieldItem, validateFieldId, fieldSk } from '<repo>/infra/lambda/responses_lib.ts';

// an 11-question template, placed as an instance (the definition is frozen onto it)
// then 12 stored answers: q1…q11, plus q99 — an id the definition does not contain
```

```
totals from the frozen definition: [{"docId":"d1788…","total":11}]
validateFieldId accepts an id no question has: q99
  …and it becomes a real sort key: f#q99

what the shelf renders:  v1 · 12/11
export answer ids: q1, q10, q11, q2, q3, q4, q5, q6, q7, q8, q9, q99
export answer count: 12 vs questions asked: 11
```

## Where the check is missing

`PUT /d/{docId}/responses/{fieldId}` (`routes/responses.ts:739`) calls `fieldSk(fieldId)`, and `validateFieldId` checks the **charset** and length only — `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$`, 128 characters. It is the id the caller asked for or a 400; it is never compared to anything the form asks. `answeredFieldCount` then counts distinct stored ids and `buildFolderFormTotals` counts questions in the frozen definition. The two numbers come from sources that never meet, and the route prints them as one fraction.

## What can actually produce it

The SPA cannot, and that matters for severity. `/render` hands `FormPane` the frozen definition, so the ids the frame reports come from the definition itself. The live mechanisms are:

* a hand-made `PUT` from any respondent already granted on the document — not privilege escalation, but any of them can add a question to their own return;
* a hand-edited or migrated `form.definition` on the instance row, which the seed and migration scripts write directly;
* a frame bug.

The freeze holds otherwise. `buildFormInstanceItem` deep-copies the definition at placement, and no route rewrites it — `PATCH /library/docs/{id}` does not touch the form facet. So a stored id outside the definition is never a definition that moved. It is a row that should not exist.

## Surface it; do not clamp it

The freeze exists so a customer's questionnaire cannot change under them. A stored id outside it is therefore a **signal** — a client bug or a hand-written write — and clamping `answered` to `total` would hide the only place that signal is visible. Report the extras instead: the count says how many of the asked questions are answered, and anything outside the definition is named separately, on the shelf and in the export.

The check is affordable at the write. `gate()` in `routes/responses.ts` already reads the whole library partition through `splitLibPartition`, and the instance row in that read still carries `form.definition` — probed. An id check at write time costs no extra query. Whether to **refuse** an out-of-definition write or accept and flag it is the open part: refusing is cleaner, but it would 400 a respondent whose row already exists from before the check.

## Related

* [DRE-2888](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2888/compliance-answered-means-three-different-things-the-operator-gets-the) — the numerator's definition of "answered". Fixing it does not close this: a stricter numerator still counts `q99`.
* [DRE-2889](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2889/the-shelf-guesses-a-confident-0n-and-can-never-say-submitted) — the same fraction, the other failure: a guessed zero printed as a known one.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `answered` can no longer exceed `total` without the surface saying why
- [ ] An answer whose id is not in the instance's frozen definition is visible as such — on the shelf and in the submission export — rather than counted as an ordinary answer
- [ ] The write path's treatment of an out-of-definition id is decided and written down in the code (refuse, or accept and flag)
- [ ] No new query on the write path or the progress path — the definition is already in the partition both already read
- [ ] Mutation-proven: removing the check turns a named test red

## CEO decision, 2026-09-05

Accept the answer and flag it. An answer to a question the form never asked is never rejected or dropped: it is kept, exported, and marked as out-of-form so a reviewer sees it. Compliance work must never silently lose what a customer wrote.

cards.title: COMPLIANCE · An autosave overwrite inherits the replaced author's status, and signs it with the wrong name
cards.description:
Settled from [DRE-2895](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2895/investigate-three-suspected-export-defects-the-review-could-not-close), finding 2. **Reproduced by execution, both halves.** Verdict: defect.

An answer can be exported as *Answered by Hagen · Answered* when Hagen wrote "Not sure — need to ask the security team" and never touched the status. The word *Answered* was Yannan's, about text that no longer exists.

Branch: `agent/DRE-<n>-<slug>`, not the `sid/…` name Linear suggests.

## What happens

Two people in one organisation are in the same field. Yannan's write lands first and she marks the answer **Answered**. Hagen's autosave is refused (409), and `useAnswerSync`'s re-send adopts the stored version and re-sends **the value only** — `putResponse(project, docId, field, value, version)`, five arguments, no status. `applyFieldWrite` reads an absent status as `unchanged` and carries the stored one forward, while stamping `actor`/`actorEmail` from Hagen's token.

The row that results contradicts itself, and every surface repeats it: the reading view (`rowsOf` carries `status` beside `actor`), and `ExportAnswer`, whose row holds `status` and `answeredBy` with nothing to say they came from different people.

## The probe

Client half — the wire. Drop this in `client/app/src/features/viewer/sync/`, run `npx vitest run` on it, delete it:

```tsx
// 409 whose stored row carries {actor: sub-yannan, status: "answered", version: 7}
// then the reader types their own different text.
PUT bodies: [
  { "expectedVersion": 0, "value": "Not sure — need to ask the security team." },
  { "expectedVersion": 7, "value": "Not sure — need to ask the security team." }
]
note to the reader: "Your answer to q1 replaced yannan's. Theirs is under 'changed elsewhere'."
replaced row kept on screen:
  [{"field":"q1","value":"We rotate keys every 90 days.","who":"yannan",
    "whoEmail":"<redacted-email>","updatedAt":"…","replaced":true}]
```

No `status` key on the re-send, and no `status` on the strip row that keeps the replaced answer readable.

Server half — `cd infra && node --import tsx probe.ts`:

```ts
import { applyFieldWrite, type ResponseStore, type FieldRecord } from '<repo>/infra/lambda/responses_lib.ts';

const pk = 'resp#oncor#d-form#oncor.com';
const stored: FieldRecord = {
  pk, sk: 'f#q1', value: 'We rotate keys every 90 days.', version: 3, seq: 7,
  actor: 'sub-yannan', actorEmail: '<redacted-email>',
  updatedAt: '2026-08-30T10:00:00.000Z', status: 'answered',
};
const store: ResponseStore = new Map([[`${pk}#f#q1`, stored]]);
store.set(`${pk}#meta#state`, { pk, sk: 'meta#state', seq: 7, updatedAt: stored.updatedAt,
  lastActor: stored.actor, lastActorEmail: stored.actorEmail } as never);

console.log(applyFieldWrite(store, {
  claims: { sub: 'sub-hagen', email: '<redacted-email>', name: 'Hagen' } as never,
  project: 'oncor', itemId: 'd-form', group: 'oncor.com', fieldId: 'q1',
  value: 'Not sure — need to ask the security team.',
  expectedVersion: 3, nowMs: Date.parse('2026-08-30T10:00:05.000Z'),
}));
```

```
record: {
  value: "Not sure — need to ask the security team.",
  actor: "sub-hagen", actorEmail: "<redacted-email>",
  status: "answered",            ← Yannan's, on Hagen's text
  version: 4, seq: 8
}
```

## Why this is a side effect and not a decision

The two halves shipped seventeen days apart and never met. `9003e96` (2026-08-12) is the re-send; its header lists **four** things that have to be true for the overwrite to be a fix rather than data loss, and none of them is the status. `a39e46c` (2026-08-29) added the status and touched only `responses_lib.ts` and `routes/responses.ts`; `110e7e1` (2026-08-30) wired `putResponse` and touched only `queries/responses.ts`. Neither opened `useAnswerSync.ts`.

Carry-forward itself **is** deliberate, and stays: `responses_lib.ts:593` and the pinned test *"a value write wiped the status"* both say a colleague's value edit must not wipe a status somebody set. That rule was written for an edit a person makes with the answer in front of them. This is an automatic overwrite of text the reader never saw.

The compensating control the 2026-08-12 amendment named — *the reader is never asked, but is always told whose answer they replaced* — does not extend here. `overwriteNote` names the person; the `replaced` strip row carries value, author and time. Neither carries the status, so the status choice survives with no provenance anywhere.

## The fix, and the decision inside it

Three options; the third is the weakest:

1. **Clear it.** The re-send sends `status: null`, which the route already reads as *take the status off*. The answer is unlabelled until somebody labels it — honest, and cheap.
2. **Keep it and say so.** Carry it, and add the replaced status to `overwriteNote` and to the strip row, so the reader is told they inherited a label as well as replaced an answer.
3. Leave it. Then the export needs a way to say who set the status, because `answeredBy` is not that person.

My recommendation is (1) for the overwrite path only, leaving the ordinary co-editor carry-forward untouched. An automatic overwrite is not somebody asserting a status.

Clear writes value-only too. `useAnswerSync.ts:549` sends `putResponse(project, docId, field, "", version)` — the same shape, so a cleared answer keeps whatever status it had and reads as an empty string labelled *Answered*. Decide it in the same fix rather than leaving a second value-only writer behind.

## Related

* [DRE-2894](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2894/setting-a-status-wipes-the-answers-byline-permanently-if-the-write-is) — same pane, same family: a status write that loses the byline. That one is the optimistic update; this one is the re-send.
* [DRE-2888](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2888/compliance-answered-means-three-different-things-the-operator-gets-the) — what "answered" counts as. A status inherited by the wrong person is a second way the operator's number stops meaning what it says.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A conflict re-send does not leave the replaced author's status on the overwriter's different text
- [ ] The ordinary co-editor case still carries a status forward through a value-only edit (`responses_lib` test *"a value write wiped the status"* stays green)
- [ ] Whatever the overwrite does to the status, the reader is told — in `overwriteNote`, the strip row, or both
- [ ] Clear (`useAnswerSync.ts:549`) is decided in the same change — an emptied answer does not keep a status that describes text that is gone
- [ ] Mutation-proven: reverting the re-send to value-only turns a named test red

cards.title: The People panel's stranded roster is scoped to the acting moderator's own grants, not the project
cards.description:
The People panel ([DRE-2867](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2867/a-moderator-can-add-a-person-from-the-ui-access-and-sign-in-in-one)) shows moderators who has been granted access but cannot sign in. That list is only as complete as the acting moderator's own visibility, and the panel currently says so in words rather than being right.

Found by the QA critic on PR 357 and verified: `GET /library` Queries the whole `lib#<project>` partition and then filters it through `visible(subject, …)` (`infra/lambda/access_lib.ts:233`), which keeps only items whose `effectiveRole` is non-null **for the caller**. There is no moderator bypass on that path — `MODERATOR_GROUP` is not referenced anywhere in `access_lib.ts`; bypasses exist only for writes (`assertItemWrite`). So a moderator who holds no grant on a folder never receives that folder, and anyone stranded on it is absent from the panel's roster, its "Cannot sign in" section, and its header count.

## Why it is not urgent, and why it is still real

Most moderators hold `grant#root#g:moderators` today (`docs/runbooks/migration-om2.md:150`), so they see everything and the panel is complete in practice. But that is a **data convention, not an invariant** — [DRE-2431](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2431/root-grants-are-moderators-the-companys-own-domain-and-nothing-else) records that six of seven projects already violate the root-grant convention — and the panel is the tool people will use to catch exactly this class of silent gap. A tool that can be quietly incomplete about lock-outs reproduces, one level up, the failure [DRE-2867](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2867/a-moderator-can-add-a-person-from-the-ui-access-and-sign-in-in-one) exists to fix.

## What [DRE-2867](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2867/a-moderator-can-add-a-person-from-the-ui-access-and-sign-in-in-one) shipped instead

The panel stops claiming project-wide completeness: the header reads "… cannot sign in, of the folders you can open", and the section says a moderator with access to more folders may see more. Three tests pin that wording so it cannot drift back. That is honest, not correct.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A moderator sees every stranded person in the project, regardless of which folders their own grants reach.
- [ ] The scoping caveat is removed from `PeoplePanel` — the header and the section no longer qualify the count — and the tests that pin that wording are removed with it.
- [ ] A non-moderator gains no new visibility from whatever mechanism is used.
- [ ] Test: a moderator whose own grants cover one folder still sees a person stranded on a different folder. This is the case [DRE-2867](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2867/a-moderator-can-add-a-person-from-the-ui-access-and-sign-in-in-one) could not construct and therefore shipped untested.

## Approach, not prescriptive

Most likely a moderator-only read that bypasses `visible()` the way `assertItemWrite` already bypasses it for writes — a new route, or a flag on `GET /library` honoured only for a caller in `MODERATOR_GROUP`. Note this makes it a **backend** change, which is why it was out of scope for [DRE-2867](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2867/a-moderator-can-add-a-person-from-the-ui-access-and-sign-in-in-one) (client-only by construction).

Whatever the shape: the payload must return the *principals*, not the documents. A moderator needs to know who is stranded, which does not require handing them the titles and contents of folders they were not granted — and shipping those would be a real disclosure where the current gap is only an omission. Check the same question against `GET /access` and `GET /access/destinations` before closing.

cards.title: INVESTIGATE · Three suspected export defects the review could not close
cards.description:
Three findings the adversarial data-integrity review (2026-08-31) raised as **SUSPECTED** and deliberately did not claim as confirmed. Each needs a decision or a probe, not necessarily a fix.

Filed together because they are all small, all in the export, and all cheap to settle — but each could silently corrupt a compliance return, which is why none should be left as a shrug.

## 1 · Cross-group file attribution — PROBED, but the intent is unclear

`response_export_lib.ts` does `files: filesByField.get(fieldId) ?? []` **with no group filter**.

Probed: with `oncor.com` and `everybite.com` both answering `q1`, EveryBite's answer row lists `oncor-only.pdf` among its files.

Each `ExportFile` carries `uploaderGroup`, so a careful reader *can* tell them apart — but the row structure asserts the file belongs to that group's answer, and any per-group file count double-counts.

**The question is intent, not code:** are attachments per-QUESTION (shared by everyone answering it) or per-ANSWER (belonging to the group that uploaded them)? `form_attachments_lib.ts` says attachments are deliberately shared, justified by same-org co-editors — which does not obviously extend across companies. **This overlaps** [DRE-2884](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2884/operatorsecurity-audit-grantroot-across-all-three-accounts-before-the)**'s open attachment-scoping question and should be answered with it.**

## 2 · Status carry-forward after a last-write-wins overwrite

`useAnswerSync`'s conflict re-send sends **value only**, so `applyFieldWrite` carries the stored status forward. The replaced author's `answered` then labels the overwriting reader's **different text**, with `answeredBy` changed to the overwriter.

Result: an answer marked *Answered* by someone who never chose that status, on text they did write. Not probed end to end.

**Decide:** should a value-only overwrite inherit the previous author's status, clear it, or keep it and say so?

## 3 · `answered` can exceed `total`

Nothing constrains a stored field id to the instance's frozen definition, and `total` is `questionCountOf` over that definition. A definition revision, or a frame writing ids outside it, yields e.g. `12/11`. Not reproduced.

Note this interacts with the freeze: an instance is frozen at its template's version precisely so a customer's questionnaire cannot change under them — so a stored id outside the frozen definition is itself a signal worth surfacing, not just a count to clamp.

## How to work

Probe first, decide second. A finding that turns out to be intended behaviour should be **written down as intended** — in the code, where the next reviewer will find it — rather than closed silently. That is the cheapest way to stop it being re-raised every review.

## Acceptance

* ☐ Each of the three is either reproduced and filed as a defect, or documented as intended with its reasoning in the code
* ☐ (1) is answered together with [DRE-2884](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2884/operatorsecurity-audit-grantroot-across-all-three-accounts-before-the)'s attachment-scoping decision
* ☐ Any that is a defect gets its own card with a probe attached

## CEO decision, 2026-09-05

Two answers. (1) A file one company uploads belongs ONLY to the company that uploaded it; it is never visible as part of another company's answer to the same question. (2) When one person's answer overwrites another's, the overwritten answer's 'Answered' status is CLEARED on the new text, and a note records who the previous answer came from.

cards.title: OPERATOR/SECURITY · Audit grant#root#* across all three accounts before the forms release
cards.description:
**Yours — this is a production-state question, not a code change.** Raised by the adversarial security review, 2026-08-31.

## What the review found

The legacy bridge grant is not a new bug — `infra/scripts/summit_fold_lib.ts` names it precisely:

> While the bridge row exists, group membership by itself resolves to viewer on EVERY item in `lib#vericorr` … ADR-0005 makes the project the trust boundary; **the bridge is the row that suspends it.**

**What is new is what now sits behind it.** Before Epic A the bridge exposed published documents. It now additionally exposes, to every member of the project group:

* another customer's **answers** (the submit export — fixed in [DRE-2881](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2881/security-the-submit-export-returns-every-companys-answers-to-the), but the bridge is what made it reachable at scale);
* another customer's **attachments** — `GET /d/{docId}/attachments` gates only on *"can you open the form"*;
* `DELETE /d/{docId}/attachments/{attachmentId}`, gated on `attachmentWriteGate` — so an unrelated project member can **destroy a customer's uploaded evidence**.

The attachment sharing is documented as deliberate (`form_attachments_lib.ts`), but its justification is same-org co-editors: *"Hagen and Yannan … curate the same files." ***That reasoning does not extend to two different companies**, and the attachment partition `att#<project>#<docId>` carries no group component at all — `uploaderGroup` is recorded on the row but never used as a key.

This is not hypothetical: Summit's staff were deliberately given `vericorr` group membership (`summit_fold_lib.ts`), so "an outside customer holds the project group" is the **documented current state**, not a scenario.

## What to do

The detector already exists — `infra/scripts/verify-portal.sh` tests for `grant#root#g:$PROJECT`.

1. Run it against **everybite**, **dreadnought** and **vericorr** and record which accounts still carry a `grant#root#*` row (group **or** domain principal — both leak; see [DRE-2883](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2883/security-template-titles-and-definitions-leak-via-changelog-render)'s table).
2. For each that does, confirm whether `POST /access/cutover {mode:'enforced'}` has been run.
3. Decide per account whether to finish the cutover **before** the forms release or accept the exposure knowingly and in writing.

## Why it is on your desk

Reading production grant state and running a cutover are operator actions. An agent should not, and this one has not.

## Related

* [DRE-2881](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2881/security-the-submit-export-returns-every-companys-answers-to-the) — the submit export leak, fixed; the bridge amplified it.
* [DRE-2883](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2883/security-template-titles-and-definitions-leak-via-changelog-render) — template enumeration, which the bridge also amplifies.
* An **attachment scoping** decision is still open: whether two companies on one form should see each other's files at all. That is a product decision, not a bug, and it needs your answer before anyone codes it.

## Acceptance

* ☐ Each of the three accounts is recorded as bridge-present or bridge-absent
* ☐ For each bridge-present account, a decision: finish cutover now, or accept knowingly
* ☐ The attachment-visibility question is answered — same-company only, or all respondents on the form

cards.title: Planning has no verdict for "already done" — the vocabulary asks who builds a card, never whether it should be built
cards.description:
**Operator observation, 2026-08-29:** *"any time the planner gets a new card as part of the onboarding process, it should check to make sure that card is still valid and has it been either done or replaced by something else."*

It does not. And the gap is structural rather than an oversight.

## The vocabulary has five verdicts and none of them is this

`config/routing-verdicts.json` declares **FLEET · WORKBENCH · OPERATOR · PARKED · NEEDS WORK**. The closest is NEEDS WORK, whose stated meaning is *"not buildable as written"* — but **a card that has already been built is perfectly buildable as written.** It just must not be built again.

The precedence chain has the same shape. Its four steps are: an explicit role label, the anchored title convention, *"can an unattended agent SATISFY the acceptance criteria?"*, then a judgement call. **Every one asks who builds it. None asks whether it should exist.**

So a stale card entering Planning is classified FLEET, promoted, dispatched — and produces a pull request that changes nothing, which the critic then has to reject. A wasted build run and a wasted review round, per stale card.

## Today's evidence, all of it from one day's groom

| Card | What it turned out to be |
| -- | -- |
| [DRE-2239](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2239/pipeline-stubs-consume-main-but-the-self-host-adr-claims-v1-the-canary) | Asked the operator to pick between two options. **Option 1 had already shipped** — all nine stubs verified on `@stable`, three cards Done |
| [DRE-2361](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2361/pipeline-failure-model-drift) | A machine-filed notification, duplicate of [DRE-2580](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2580/the-model-drift-alarm-has-never-once-succeeded-it-pushes-to-a), sat in Triage sixteen days |
| [DRE-2610](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2610/retracted-the-unowned-branch-watchdog-works-it-was-inside-its-120) | Self-retracted a week earlier: *"the premise was wrong… nothing to build"* |
| [DRE-2432](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2432/session-state-2026-08-1213-everything-open-at-the-context-boundary) **/** [DRE-2402](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2402/open-threads-everything-left-unconcluded-from-the-2026-08-1112-session) | Parked checklists, mostly executed, with live residue nobody could see without reading them line by line |
| *(the August questionnaire cluster)* | Eleven portico cards found superseded only because a human read the whole cluster — cited as the pattern, NOT a fixture: they are not enumerated here and the fixture set below is the five named cards |

**And the way** [DRE-2239](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2239/pipeline-stubs-consume-main-but-the-self-host-adr-claims-v1-the-canary) **was found is the point.** It surfaced because someone happened to notice a mention in `CLAUDE.md`, not by any method. The research agent said so plainly: *"the 'asked-for fix has since shipped' category is inherently under-covered… more cards of that shape may exist."* Nothing looks for them.

## Why this becomes urgent at the cutover

[[[DRE-2728](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2728/the-cutover-an-adr-that-dates-the-new-model-and-every-old-card-has-to)]] moves **every** Backlog card — currently 220+ — through Intake and Planning on a dated day. Each one gets classified. **Without this check, Planning will confidently route already-finished work as buildable**, at exactly the moment the queue is at its largest and its output is least scrutinised.

The cutover's own argument is that a card must earn its way in. *Earning your way in has to include still being needed.*

## What to build

A **sixth verdict**, or a pre-verdict gate before the five — the card should decide which and say why:

* **SUPERSEDED** — another card did this, named. The classifier must produce the identifier, not a vague claim, so it can be recorded as a duplicate rather than cancelled blind.
* **ALREADY DONE** — the acceptance criteria are already satisfied by shipped work, with the evidence named: the merge, the file, the live check.

Both route to a human for confirmation. **Neither may cancel a card on its own** — [DRE-2683](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2683/the-groomer-sequences-the-whole-backlog-into-cycles-portico-first-and) already sets that rule: *"the groomer recommends and never cancels. Cancelling is destructive and belongs to the operator."*

## The hard part, stated up front

**Proving a card is already done is strictly harder than routing it**, and a wrong "already done" is worse than a wrong route: it silently drops real work rather than sending it somewhere inconvenient. So:

* the check must **fail open** — uncertain means route it normally, never discard it
* it must **name its evidence** so a human can check the claim in seconds, the way today's groom cites merge SHAs and card ids
* it should lean on what is cheap and certain first — a card whose acceptance names a file that now contains the thing, a card whose linked PR merged, a card whose named superseder is Done

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A card whose work has demonstrably shipped is not routed as buildable
- [ ] Every such verdict names its evidence — a card id, a merge, or a check — never an unsupported assertion
- [ ] Uncertainty routes the card normally; the check never discards on a guess
- [ ] No verdict of this kind cancels a card by itself; it recommends to a human
- [ ] Five named fixtures, each correctly identified with its evidence: [DRE-2239](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2239/pipeline-stubs-consume-main-but-the-self-host-adr-claims-v1-the-canary) (ALREADY DONE — option 1 shipped, three cards Done), [DRE-2361](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2361/pipeline-failure-model-drift) (SUPERSEDED — duplicate of [DRE-2580](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2580/the-model-drift-alarm-has-never-once-succeeded-it-pushes-to-a)), [DRE-2610](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2610/retracted-the-unowned-branch-watchdog-works-it-was-inside-its-120) (ALREADY DONE — self-retracted, nothing to build), [DRE-2432](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2432/session-state-2026-08-1213-everything-open-at-the-context-boundary) and [DRE-2402](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2402/open-threads-everything-left-unconcluded-from-the-2026-08-1112-session) (routed normally — parked checklists with live residue are NOT done, and the check must not call them done)
- [ ] A card that is genuinely still needed is **not** misread as done — a false-positive fixture, because that failure is the expensive one
- [ ] `docs/routing-verdicts.md` regenerated and the vocabulary's `_readme` updated

## Phase

Not yet placed. It belongs with [[[DRE-2719](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2719/everything-goes-to-planning-which-decides-one-off-epic-or-wave)]] in Phase 5 — Planning cannot classify honestly without it, and the cutover is where the cost lands. **Placing it needs its own declaration card**, per the pattern in [[[DRE-2834](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2834/declare-dre-2831-into-the-phase-5-roster-the-fleet-debt-has-no-phase)]].

cards.title: The deploy says "skipped" when the rollout already happened — a healthy deploy reads as a no-op
cards.description:
**The console deploy of 2026-08-29 (v1.6.10) ended with both services reporting** `no change, skipped`**. It read as though nothing shipped. Everything had shipped.**

```
==> [6/6] Roll out (CONCURRENTLY) ONLY services whose image differs from what is live
    backend: already running sha256:a649242… — no change, skipped
    web: already running sha256:6e4ebecb… — no change, skipped
```

That is the last thing printed before DONE, so it is the line the operator reads. The obvious conclusion — the images were identical, nothing was deployed, the console is still on the old code — is **wrong**, and it is wrong in the direction that matters: it invites a second deploy or a hunt for why the fix is not live.

**What actually happened. **`BackendStack` and `FrontendStack` are deployed by CDK in step [5/6], and **that CDK deploy performs the rollout** — 247s and 175s respectively. By the time step [6/6] compares digests, the services are already running the new image, so it correctly finds nothing to do. Confirmed against App Runner: `UPDATE_SERVICE SUCCEEDED`, 12:50→12:54 PDT, inside this deploy.

So the skip is **correct behaviour reported in a way that reads as failure to act** — the same shape as the fix run that declines and reports `success`, and the console panel that says `fix agent not engaged` while an agent is mid-run. It belongs to this epic because it is the same defect one layer out: **a system describing its own state in words that mean the opposite of what happened.**

## Cost, measured

Verifying it took an `aws apprunner list-operations` call and a read of the deploy script's structure. Small — but it is paid on **every** deploy, by whoever is watching, forever, and the whole point of this epic is that the operator should not have to check whether a green thing is really green.

## The fix

Say why it was already running:

```
backend: already rolled by CDK in step 5 (sha256:a649242…) — nothing further to do
web:     already rolled by CDK in step 5 (sha256:6e4ebecb…) — nothing further to do
```

And distinguish it from the case this step exists for — an image genuinely unchanged since the last deploy, where nothing rolled at all and that is also fine:

```
backend: unchanged since v1.6.9 (sha256:…) — not rolled, not needed
```

**Two different situations that today print the same sentence.** One means "the new code is live"; the other means "the old code is still live and that is correct". The operator needs to tell them apart.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A service rolled by the CDK step says so, naming the step that rolled it
- [ ] A service whose image is genuinely unchanged since the previous deploy says that instead, and the two messages are not interchangeable
- [ ] The final DONE block states which services rolled in this deploy and which did not
- [ ] A test drives both paths — a rolled service and an unchanged one — asserting the messages differ

## Why it is XS and still worth filing

One string change in `infra/deploy-console.sh`, plus a test. Filed rather than fixed in passing because **the pattern is the point**: this is the fourth instance today of a correct mechanism describing itself misleadingly, and counting them is how the epic earns its priority.
