cards.title: Extend the shipped watcher check to resolve every act's subscriber
cards.description:
**Extend** `scripts/check_workflow_watchers.py`**. Do not write a second derivation.**

[[[DRE-2820](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2820/red-main-repair-watches-one-workflow-of-two-the-harness-can-be-red-on)]] shipped that script on 2026-08-29 (PR #203) with two rules — a red commit must reach a repair caller, and any workflow that can run at all must have some watcher — plus a data-declared exemption and live-workflow tests. It is the mechanism that would have caught the harness being red on `main` all day, seven weeks before it bit.

**A design pass proposed building a parallel derivation beside it. That was rejected, and the reason matters:** the proposed version *fails today* against the real 27 workflows — `Linear Sync` is watched but its stub is `pull_request`-only, and `Verify (reusable)` has no self-stub. **Two independent checks over the same fact is the hazard that caused the incident this epic exists for.** One check, extended.

## What is genuinely new

`config/pipeline-acts.json` ([[[DRE-2825](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2825/one-registry-declares-every-autonomous-act-and-one-module-writes-its)]]) gives every act a `subscriber` — the workflow expected to act on it. **Nothing today asserts that the subscriber exists, or that it accepts the trigger the act arrives on.**

That is the static half of the epic's claim, and the more valuable one: it fires **before** the incident rather than reporting it after. Instance D was found by an agent reading a log fourteen hours late; this class of check would have failed the PR that introduced the gap.

Add to the existing script:

* every act's `subscriber` resolves to a workflow that exists
* that workflow's triggers **actually admit** the event the act arrives on
* an act with no subscriber, or an unreachable one, fails CI

## The trap to avoid, named by the design pass itself

`workflow_call` **reusables run under the CALLER's workflow name.** A derivation that maps an act to a reusable by name will silently under-cover — which is precisely the failure it exists to prevent. Most bureau-pipeline workflows are reusables consumed by thin `self-*` stubs, so this is the common case, not the edge.

Read how the shipped script already handles the stub-to-reusable mapping and follow it. If it does not handle it, that is a finding to report rather than route around.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The new assertions live **inside **`check_workflow_watchers.py`; no second derivation exists
- [ ] An act naming a subscriber that does not exist fails CI
- [ ] An act naming a subscriber whose triggers cannot admit that event fails CI
- [ ] `workflow_call` reusables resolve through their calling stubs, with a test proving it — a fixture where the act's subscriber is a reusable and the assertion still passes correctly

## Why this card is small and still load-bearing

Everything else in this epic reports at runtime, within a sweep. **This one refuses the gap at merge time.** Of the eighteen known instances, it is one of only two that would have been caught before anything went wrong.

cards.title: [EPIC] The system can be read — what is happening, who acts next, and what is merely quiet
cards.description:
**The pipeline is well instrumented for failure and blind to everything else.** It can say a run failed. It cannot say a run refused, a repair is underway, a human has already answered, or that nothing is watching at all — and every one of those renders as either a red pill or silence.

On 2026-08-29 one pull request produced **five separate instances**, cost about fourteen hours, and none of them was a code defect. Every run involved reported `success`, `cancelled` or `skipped`. Nothing failed, so no medic fired, no alarm rang, and the only reason any of it surfaced was a fix agent that refused to push and read a log a human had walked past four times.

## The claim

**An unattended system is only as good as the account it gives of itself.** Autonomy is the point of this programme; the operator's read is what makes autonomy safe to leave alone overnight. Today that read is wrong often enough that the honest instruction is "don't trust the dashboard, go read the API" — which is the opposite of the product.

## What it covers

**The run layer.** A run that declines to do work must not report the same conclusion as one that did it. A queue eviction must not spell the same as a deliberate cancel ([[[DRE-2816](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2816/a-run-that-declines-to-do-work-reports-the-same-success-as-a-run-that)]]).

**The watch layer.** Every workflow that can go red on a default branch must be watched by something, and the list must be derived or asserted rather than remembered ([[[DRE-2820](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2820/red-main-repair-watches-one-workflow-of-two-the-harness-can-be-red-on)]]).

**The console layer.** One derived answer to *what is happening to this right now*, with **recovery in flight** as a first-class value, read from the receipts the pipeline already posts ([[[DRE-2821](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2821/every-automatic-recovery-is-invisible-to-the-console-it-shows-the-last)]]). Its two shipped predecessors are [[[DRE-2811](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2811/the-console-cannot-tell-a-working-fix-loop-from-a-stalled-one-both)]] and [[[DRE-2814](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2814/console-noise-the-dashboard-keeps-asking-for-a-human-who-already)]].

**The standing rule under all of it,** already held by the abandoned-work sweep and worth generalising: **unreadable is UNKNOWN, never a negative claim.** "Not engaged", "blocked", "needs you" are assertions and must be earned from something actually read.

## Why this belongs before the cutover, not after

[[[DRE-2728](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2728/the-cutover-an-adr-that-dates-the-new-model-and-every-old-card-has-to)]] switches the fleet to a fail-closed front door on a dated day. **191 Backlog cards become un-promotable at once**, and the backlog stops flowing until the drain catches up — by design.

That is a defensible plan **only if the operator can tell a card blocked on purpose from a card blocked by a defect.** Today the console renders those identically. Cutting over first means starting the hardest week this programme has planned with the instrument known to be unreliable.

## Explicitly out of scope

* [[[DRE-2810](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2810/the-fix-loop-evicts-its-own-next-attempt-a-notice-comment-cancels-the)]] and [[[DRE-2813](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2813/a-hand-dispatch-on-a-held-pr-silently-disarms-the-operator-decision)]] — the fix loop's own defects. They were found through this lens but they are behaviour, not reporting.
* [[[DRE-2817](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2817/the-fix-budget-counts-attempts-when-it-should-measure-convergence)]] — the attempt budget. Also behaviour.
* [[[DRE-2815](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2815/a-console-deploy-must-not-kill-in-flight-work-preflight-drain-and-a)]] — deploy safety, which belongs to [[[DRE-2713](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2713/epic-deploy-safety-make-the-rollback-real-before-deploying-more-often)]] and is where three console fixes are currently stacked waiting to be deployed.

Keeping those out is deliberate: this epic is about **whether the system can be read**, not about whether it behaves. Mixing the two is how the console cards came to be filed one incident at a time in the first place.

## Acceptance for the epic

- [ ] The four states — being worked on, waiting on a gate, recovering, genuinely stuck — are distinguishable from one derived value, in the console and from the CLI
- [ ] No panel asserts a negative it has not read; unreadable renders UNKNOWN
- [ ] Adding a workflow or a recovery without teaching the watchers fails a test rather than passing quietly
- [ ] The five 2026-08-29 instances are fixtures, and each would have been surfaced within one sweep
- [ ] A deliberate stall drill: park a PR on purpose, and confirm the operator's read names it as parked rather than broken

cards.title: A run that declines to do work reports the same success as a run that did it
cards.description:
**Every one of the four breakages on PR #199 reported** `success`**,** `cancelled` **or** `skipped`**. Nothing failed. So no medic fired, no red-main repair ran, no alarm rang, and the PR sat for eleven hours looking exactly like a PR nobody had gotten to yet.**

The pipeline is thoroughly instrumented for *failure* and blind to *refusal*. Those are different states and the system spells them the same way.

## The four, all from one PR on 2026-08-29

| What happened | How it reported |
| -- | -- |
| the real REQUEST_CHANGES trigger evicted from the concurrency queue ([[[DRE-2810](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2810/the-fix-loop-evicts-its-own-next-attempt-a-notice-comment-cancels-the)]]) | `cancelled` — same as a harmless duplicate dispatch |
| the run that evicted it, refusing on its author check | `skipped` — same as any correctly-ignored comment |
| a hand dispatch that found the budget spent, did nothing, and re-posted the hold ([[[DRE-2813](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2813/a-hand-dispatch-on-a-held-pr-silently-disarms-the-operator-decision)]]) | `success` |
| the restart sweep re-dispatching into a still-spent budget, re-holding 12 seconds later | `success` |

The last two are the sharpest: a run that walked in, read one number, declined, and walked out is indistinguishable at the API from a run that repaired the code and pushed.

## Why "just read the logs" is not the answer

Three separate readers already try to answer *is this PR being worked on* from run conclusions — the console panel, the reconcile sweep's backoff, and a human at a terminal. All three got it wrong today, in both directions. **A conclusion is the only thing cheap enough to poll, so it has to carry the distinction.**

## What to build

A run that took no action must be **distinguishable without opening it.** The cheapest honest signal is the conclusion itself:

* a job that refuses at a precondition should end `neutral`, not `success` — GitHub supports it, and it reads as "ran, did nothing" rather than "ran, done"
* the refusal reason belongs in the run's own title or annotation (`budget spent`, `no verdict on head`, `not the qa-bot`), so a listing shows it without a log fetch
* `cancelled` on a run that never started a job should be reported as **evicted**, because a queue eviction and a deliberate cancel are the same word for very different events

Then the readers can stop guessing: **anything that is not** `success` **is not progress**, and `success` means work happened.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A fix run that refuses at the budget check ends `neutral`, not `success`
- [ ] A fix run that refuses at the author check ends `neutral` with the reason readable from the run listing
- [ ] A run evicted from a concurrency queue is distinguishable from a deliberately cancelled one
- [ ] The console's fix-loop reading and the sweep's backoff both consume the new signal rather than re-deriving it from conclusions ([[[DRE-2811](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2811/the-console-cannot-tell-a-working-fix-loop-from-a-stalled-one-both)]], [[[DRE-2814](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2814/console-noise-the-dashboard-keeps-asking-for-a-human-who-already)]])
- [ ] A test asserts the four #199 cases each produce a conclusion that is not `success`
- [ ] No run that performed real work is downgraded — verified against a normal fix→push→approve cycle

## The general rule this is an instance of

**Silence and refusal must never render as completion.** The abandoned-work sweep already holds to its half of this — a repo it cannot read reports UNKNOWN, never 0. This is the same rule applied to the run layer, and it is the single change that would have surfaced three of today's four failures within minutes rather than hours.

cards.title: Add-document by link stores the sign-in page when the URL is Portico's own gated document
cards.description:
Adding a document by link to a URL on the portal's **own** gated domain silently ingests `auth-gate.html` instead of the document. The reader gets a library entry that opens the sign-in page, titled "auth gate", and nothing says anything went wrong.

Hit on 2026-08-29 registering a published VeriCorr doc into the Chapman Engineering folder. The stored row records the whole failure:

```
url       https://share.vericorr.com/chapman-ai-survey-data-assessment
finalUrl  https://share.vericorr.com/auth-gate.html?return=%2Fchapman-ai-survey-data-assessment
kind      link
title     auth gate
bytes     40448          <- the gate; the document is 288,834
```

`ingestState` came back `ready`, so every downstream check passed. The operator's only signal was the rendered page.

## Why it happens

`link_fetch.ts` follows redirects by hand (`redirect: 'manual'`, `MAX_REDIRECT_HOPS`) and re-checks every hop. That is deliberate and correct — it is what makes the SSRF address rules enforceable, per the file's own header comment. But the hop check is about *addresses*, not about *what the page is*. `share.vericorr.com` is allow-listed, so the 302 to `auth-gate.html` is a legal hop, and the gate's HTML is stored as the document.

The concept already exists elsewhere: `legacy_migration_lib.ts:159` lists `/^auth-gate\.html$/` first in `PLATFORM_KEYS`, precisely so the migration never treats the gate as content. The link path has no equivalent.

## Scope note

This is narrower than "links are broken". Fetching an *external* URL is the feature working as designed. The bug is fetching a URL the portal itself gates, where an unauthenticated fetch can only ever return the gate. Any same-origin document is by definition already published and does not need fetching at all.

## Approach

Refuse the hop rather than store the result. Add a verdict to `redirectHopVerdict` in `link_source_lib.ts` for a redirect whose target is a known platform page, and surface it as a real error on the Add-document response so the operator sees why. Reuse the `PLATFORM_KEYS` shape from `legacy_migration_lib.ts` rather than writing a second list — one definition of "this is chrome, not content".

Worth considering as part of the same change, but confirm before building: a same-origin URL arguably should not take the link path at all. The bytes are already in the portal bucket, so it could register directly the way a publish does. If that is the better shape, say so on the card rather than building both.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Adding a document by link to a gated same-origin URL fails with a clear message naming the gate as the reason; no library row and no artifact are created
- [ ] The failure message tells the operator what to do instead (upload the file, or that the document is already published)
- [ ] A redirect to any `PLATFORM_KEYS` page is refused on every hop, not only the first
- [ ] Adding a document by link to a genuine external URL still works unchanged
- [ ] The SSRF address rules and `MAX_REDIRECT_HOPS` behaviour are untouched — this adds a check, it does not relax one
- [ ] `PLATFORM_KEYS` (or its equivalent) has exactly one definition shared by the migration and the link path
- [ ] Test: a 302 to `auth-gate.html?return=...` produces a refusal verdict, not a stored artifact
- [ ] Test: an external 302 chain within the hop limit still resolves and ingests

## Operator note

The workaround is the file picker — uploading the local file ingests the bytes directly and never touches the gate. Worth keeping in mind when judging urgency: this blocks link-registration of any portal-hosted document, which is currently how a published doc gets into the library.

cards.title: A fix loop blocked on an operator decision reads as "fix agent working" — the console shows progress where a human is the blocker
cards.description:
**Observed live by the operator, 2026-08-28, on PR #2166.** In their words:

> *"this is an example of misleading information on the display… right now it just says 'fix agent working'. If I hadn't asked you, I wouldn't know I needed to do those things."*

The fix loop had **stopped**. It posted `🛑 Fix attempt 2 blocked`, moved DRE-2792 to `Green Light`, turned the PR into a draft, and asked for a comment beginning `Operator decision`. Nothing could move until a human answered. **The console showed the row as a working fix agent.**

The PR then sat for **63 minutes** — 16:52 blocked, 17:55 answered — and was only found because the operator asked directly.

## The mechanism for this already exists and does not cover this case

`console/backend/inflight.py:290` defines the degraded states that set `needs_attention`, and `fixLoopGroupMapping.ts:29` states the intent exactly right:

> *"true when the row's PR wears a degraded reason … the row genuinely needs an operator, so the group must not claim 'self-healing, no action needed'."*

The five it knows:

```
CRITIC_CRASHED           Critic crashed — re-review needed
FIX_FAILED               Fix attempt failed — retrying / held
FIX_STALLED              Checks failing — fix agent not engaged
APPROVED_BLOCKED         Approved — blocked by conflict / failing check
REJECTED_HUMAN_DECISION  Rejected — human decision
```

**None of them is "the fix loop stopped and is waiting for a person to answer a question."** That state is invisible to the flag built for exactly this purpose, so the row keeps its happy-path copy.

## Why it is the sharper half of a known problem

There is a second, compounding fact already on the books: an `Operator decision` **comment does not restart the fix loop** — it needs a hand `workflow_dispatch`. `agent-fix.yml`'s own source says so: *"The PR sat still for 42 minutes and needed a hand workflow_dispatch."*

So the operator is asked a question the board does not surface, and answering it does not resume anything. Two silent stalls in series.

## What to change

1. **A degraded reason for it** — e.g. `AWAITING_OPERATOR_DECISION`, added to `_PR_REASON_OVERRIDES` / `enrich.NEEDS_ATTENTION_REASONS` (they are deliberately kept in lockstep), with copy that names the ask: *"Fix loop held — needs your decision"*.
2. **Derived from evidence, not a label.** The signal is a `🛑 … blocked` comment from the fix bot that is newer than the last human comment on the PR. Reading a label would repeat the mistake this wave keeps finding — a marker nothing writes.
3. It should reach the same queue as everything else needing the CEO. `Green Light` is where the fix agent already puts the card; the console's "needs you" surface should agree with it, so one place answers *what is waiting on me*.
4. **Say how long it has waited.** The row already carries `ageInState`; a held row's age is the number that matters, and 63 minutes is the number that would have shown here.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A fix loop held for an operator decision sets `needs_attention` and reads as waiting on a human, not as an agent working.
- [ ] The state is derived from the PR's own comment history, not from a label anything has to remember to apply.
- [ ] The held row's copy names what is being asked and how long it has waited.
- [ ] Backend and frontend agree — no row can read "self-healing" while its PR is held.
- [ ] Proven against the real thing: PR #2166's timeline replayed as a fixture, red before the fix.
- [ ] The `workflow_dispatch`-to-resume gap is either fixed here or carded, so answering the question actually restarts the loop.

---

**This is the wave's own thesis pointed at the console.** Phase 1 read *10/10 complete* while its central deliverable did not exist; this row reads *fix agent working* while nothing is running. Same defect class: a surface reporting the state it expects rather than the state that holds.

---

## Second occurrence, same day, second PR — and it is FOUR surfaces, not one

**Observed by the operator 2026-08-28 13:23 PT on PR #2169**, roughly two hours after this card was filed. Same defect, different card. It is not a one-off.

One screen said all of the following at once, while the PR had been stopped and waiting on a human for over an hour:

| where | what it said | what was true |
| -- | -- | -- |
| in-flight header | `1 card across 3 epics — all moving` | nothing was moving |
| Fixed-loop group | `1 in repair · self-healing, no action needed` | only a human could unblock it |
| Open PRs row | `Fix agent working` | the fix agent had stopped and asked for the operator |
| [DRE-2795](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2795/the-release-step-has-never-once-worked-the-access-key-graphql-fragment) row | `90% · #2169 · CI failed` | CI passed; see below |

`self-healing, no action needed` is **the exact string **`fixLoopGroupMapping.ts:29` **says the group must not claim** in this situation. The intent is already written down in the code; only the condition is missing.

## A second, separate defect: `CI failed` is the wrong remedy

This one is a mislabel rather than a fabrication, and it points the operator at the wrong repair.

* All **eight** workflow runs on the branch returned `success` — `gh run list` conclusions are `["success"]` and nothing else.
* The single red check is named `QA critic review`, conclusion `FAILURE`, because the critic returned `REQUEST_CHANGES`. That is a *verdict*, not a broken build.

So the console reduces "the critic asked for changes" to "CI failed." An operator reading that goes looking at the build. The actual remedy is to post a comment. This is the standing `call/review = SUCCESS` hazard running in the opposite direction: there, a green check hid a rejection; here, a red check hides a question.

**These want fixing together but they are not the same bug.** One is a missing state (`awaiting operator decision` is not among the five degraded reasons). The other is a label that collapses two unrelated failures — build broken, review rejected — into one word.

## Why this keeps costing real time

Both occurrences were found only because the operator asked a person directly. The information needed to render the truth is already on the PR: the bot's own comment begins `🛑 Fix attempt 1 blocked` and says *this needs you*. The console is not missing the data. It is not reading it.

> *"this is also another case for the ui not telling me what I need to do"* — operator, 2026-08-28

---

## Third occurrence, 2026-08-28 — this time nothing is displayed AT ALL

**Operator: "we should use this as another example of not being clear on cards and what to do."**

The first two occurrences were the console describing a stopped PR as moving. This one is worse in one specific way: **there is no wrong message, because there is no message.**

### What happened

[DRE-2801](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2801/retire-in-design-review-and-in-qa-on-the-board-dre-2726-declared-it) was the last card standing between Phase 2 and its sign-off. It sat in `Backlog` and would have sat there forever.

It carried `needs-human` — reconcile's `HOLD_LABEL`. `promote_ready` skips those with a bare `continue`:

```python
if HOLD_LABEL in labels:
    continue  # held for a human (DRE-1403) — never auto-promote
```

No print, no comment, no state change. The sweep ran twice, reported `completed/success` and `0 card(s) promoted (WIP 0+0/12)`, and was correct both times.

### The comparison that makes it a defect rather than a preference

**In the same sweep, a different card explained itself:**

```
promotion: DRE-2789 was added to its epic after the green light
           and carries no verdict — skipping
promotion: 0 card(s) promoted (WIP 0+0/12)
```

[DRE-2789](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2789/nothing-records-which-relay-commit-is-live-merged-but-never-deployed) got a reason. [DRE-2801](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2801/retire-in-design-review-and-in-qa-on-the-board-dre-2726-declared-it) got silence. **The mechanism to say why a card was skipped already exists and is already used one branch over** — this path just does not use it.

### How it was actually found

By reading the sweep's raw log, noticing [DRE-2801](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2801/retire-in-design-review-and-in-qa-on-the-board-dre-2726-declared-it) was not even named as a candidate, then reading `promote_ready` line by line to find which of six silent `continue`s it hit, then querying the card's labels. Four steps, none of them visible from any surface a person looks at.

Nobody had applied that label deliberately for that reason — it was created without it — and no record says when or why it arrived.

### The hold itself was also wrong, which is the compounding half

Only **one** of [DRE-2801](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2801/retire-in-design-review-and-in-qa-on-the-board-dre-2726-declared-it)'s four steps is operator-only (`make linear-apply`). The other three — declaring the states retired in config, stripping the lanes from the console, deleting the contract entries — are ordinary agent work. **A card held for one operator step in the middle is a card nobody ever starts**, and nothing anywhere said it was held.

### What to change

1. **A silently held card must say so. **`HOLD_LABEL` should print the same shape [DRE-2789](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2789/nothing-records-which-relay-commit-is-live-merged-but-never-deployed)'s skip does — card, reason, what would clear it — and the card itself should carry it. A hold nobody can see is indistinguishable from a card nobody has got to.
2. **Every silent** `continue` **in** `promote_ready` **deserves the same treatment.** There are six; one prints. A sweep reporting `0 promoted` should be able to say *why zero*, per candidate.
3. **The console's "needs you" surface should show held cards**, since a hold means exactly that. Today it shows nothing, which is how this reached the last card of a phase before anyone noticed.

### Why it belongs on this card

Same defect, third surface. The console says *no action needed* about work that is stopped; the sweep says *nothing at all* about a card it will never promote. Both are the system holding a state it declines to report.

**The fix for this one is not in the console** — it is in `reconcile.promote_ready` (bureau-pipeline) plus a console surface for held cards. If this card is picked up by a frontend agent, item 3 is the only part that belongs to it, and items 1–2 want their own card.

cards.title: phase-check is blind to card-to-card edges and has no cycle detection
cards.description:
`make phase-check` reported *"the board matches config/phase-chain.json — no drift"* while three of Wave 1.5's seven phases were deadlocked. The drift check cannot see the class of edge that deadlocked them.

## The blind spot

`scripts/phase_chain.py::fetch_live` reads the **seven proof cards** and nothing else (`_PROOF_Q`, phase_chain.py:403-410, called at :456-466). Its comment states the assumption plainly: *"Reading the seven PROOF cards is enough to see every edge the chain declares, because every declared edge has a proof card at one end."*

That is true of every **declared** edge and false of the board. A `blocks` edge drawn directly between two phase CARDS — neither of them a proof card — touches no proof card, so it never enters `live["edges"]`, so `diff` never compares it, so `_diff_roster` never sees it either. It is **structurally invisible**, not merely unreported.

Three such edges froze Phase 2 and Phase 3 (DRE-2792): `DRE-2680 → DRE-2681`, `DRE-2725 → DRE-2726`, `DRE-2719 → DRE-2724`. Each was creation-time bulk wiring, each pointed backwards from a later phase, and each closed a loop nothing could escape — the blocker could not start until the phase closed, and the phase could not close without the blocker. All three had to be found by hand.

## The second half

`validate()` (phase_chain.py:184-256) checks numbering, duplicate rosters, identifier shape and self-blocking. It has **no cycle detection and no back-edge detection at all**. A card in phase N blocking a card in phase M < N inverts the wave's order, and nothing in the file or the check says so.

The two halves compound: the check cannot see the edge, and could not judge it if it could.

## What to build

Extend the read so every chain member's relations are collected, not just the proof cards', then judge the edges the wider read exposes:

* **A back-edge** — blocker in a later phase than the card it blocks — is a **defect**, reported as an unfixable change like `relation.unexpected` (never removed automatically; the file's own rule is that only a human can say whether an undeclared edge was meant).
* **A cycle** anywhere in the `blocks` graph over chain members is a defect, reported with the cards on the loop so it can be read without a graph tool.

Cost is the constraint the current design was chosen for: the module comment rejects reading all members as *"Forty-four reads … six times as much."* Page the members in one query rather than one call per card, or read them only when `check` is asked for the deeper pass — the design choice belongs to whoever builds it, but the cost note is why the shortcut exists and should be answered rather than ignored.

`validate` and `diff` are pure and take dicts, so both halves are testable offline in `scripts/tests/test_phase_chain.py` with no network and no key — same as every existing case there.

## Why it matters

Wave 1.5's phase order is enforced entirely by these relations, and `make phase-check` is the only thing that watches them. Without this, the next stale edge deadlocks a phase exactly as silently as the last three did, and it is again found only when somebody notices a phase has not moved.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `fetch_live` (or its replacement) sees a `blocks` edge between two non-proof chain members
- [ ] A regression test drives the exact DRE-2792 shape — a card-to-card back-edge between two phase cards — and fails against today's proof-card-only read
- [ ] `validate` (or `diff`) reports a back-edge, naming both cards and both phases
- [ ] `validate` (or `diff`) reports a cycle over chain members, naming the cards on the loop
- [ ] Both are reported as needing a human decision — nothing removes a relation automatically
- [ ] The read's cost is stated in the code, with the reasoning for whatever query shape is chosen
- [ ] `make phase-check` still exits 0 against the current clean board

cards.title: The relay can be deployed but not rolled back — publish versions, alias them, and prove the dispatch path before shifting traffic
cards.description:
**Deliberately NOT Phase 1 work.** Phase 1 needs one thing from the relay — a redeploy so DRE-2723's Triage parking goes live. This card is the hardening that stops the *next* relay problem, and it should not gate the wave.

Queued after Phase 1, and after [DRE-2789](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2789), which is its prerequisite.

## Why the relay is the wrong shape for what it does

It is the single point of failure for **all** dispatch — no card in any repo builds if it is wrong — and its failures are **silent**: a card simply does not move. Today:

* `FN_NAME="bureau-linear-relay"` — one function, **no** `--publish`**, no alias, no versions**.
* **Rollback means re-running the whole deploy script**: wheel resolution, runtime sync, the lot. Minutes of no dispatch, on top of however long it took to notice.
* Nothing records which commit is live, so noticing is the hard part — that is DRE-2789.

## Why the other surfaces' patterns do not fit

**Not the pipeline's moving** `stable` **tag.** That exists because consumers *reference* it (`uses: …@stable`). Nothing references the relay; it is deployed, not consumed. A channel tag would be ceremony with no reader.

**Git tags alone are the weaker half.** A tag records that a deploy was *started*; the sha on the function records what actually *answered*. DRE-2789 takes the stronger half. This card takes what a tag cannot give at all: a rollback that does not rebuild.

## The work

1. `--publish` **on the update path**, so every deploy leaves an immutable numbered version behind.
2. **An alias** (`live`) that the Linear webhook and the EventBridge heartbeat target, instead of `$LATEST`.
3. **Rollback = repoint the alias.** Seconds, no rebuild, no wheel resolution, no runtime sync. Document it in `infra/` beside the console's rollback.

## What must come BEFORE any canary — and why a canary is not in this card

A canary needs a signal to fail against, and the relay's current one is not enough. The **heartbeat** (DRE-2006) fires every minute but only proves the Lambda *boots* — it broadcasts a WebSocket liveness frame and never touches routing. It would have caught the DRE-1894 cryptography-import outage within a minute. **It would not catch a routing bug.**

So a 10% canary today would strand ~10% of cards **silently** until the stranded-card watchdog fires at 30 minutes. You learn at the same speed, having broken less — a marginal gain for real complexity.

**The missing piece is a synthetic dispatch check**: the deploy fires one card end-to-end through webhook → route → `repository_dispatch` and asserts it dispatched. That proves the path, not just the boot. Only then does a canary have something to auto-rollback on, and only then is it worth building.

Sequence: **DRE-2789 (sha) → this card (versions + alias) → synthetic dispatch check → canary.** Each step earns the next; skipping to a canary buys an unobservable deploy behind an alias.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every relay deploy publishes an immutable version; `$LATEST` is not what serves traffic.
- [ ] An alias serves the webhook and the heartbeat, and repointing it is the documented rollback.
- [ ] Rollback observed for real: deploy, repoint to the previous version, confirm dispatch still works — timed, and recorded on this card.
- [ ] `make deploy-lag` reads the alias's version, so the reported number describes what is serving rather than what was last built.
- [ ] The canary is explicitly OUT of scope here, with the synthetic-dispatch prerequisite named — so the next reader does not build it early.

cards.title: A deploy after a rollback silently leaves the console on two versions — start-deployment cannot move a digest-addressed service
cards.description:
**A deploy after a rollback left the console running two different versions — backend v1.6.5, frontend v1.6.1 — and reported success.** Found by the CEO, who noticed a dashboard panel had vanished.

Observed live 2026-08-27 ~17:00 PT. The visible symptom was the Abandoned work panel ([DRE-2738](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2738)) missing from the right rail. The cause was that the frontend was serving a **3-day-old build** that predates the panel.

```
backend : @sha256:9541245e...  v1.6.5   ✅
web     : @sha256:5788ced4...  v1.6.1   ❌  (Aug 24)
```

## What the deploy said it did

```
[6/6] web: image moved (running=5788ced4... -> new=1beeb39a...) — rolling out
      web: rollout SUCCEEDED (after 150s)
```

It detected the drift correctly, acted, waited, and reported success. **The service never moved.**

## Why — and it is the same defect we closed this morning, one file over

`deploy-console.sh` step `[6/6]` rolls a service out with `aws apprunner start-deployment`. That redeploys the service's *configured source*. Since [DRE-2716](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2716) the configured source is an immutable digest, so `start-deployment` re-pulls **the same image** and succeeds.

This is precisely [DRE-2775](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2775) — *"digest addressing made the legacy rollback path a silent no-op"* — which we fixed in `rollback-console.sh` this morning and gave a read-back. **The deploy path has the identical mechanism and neither the fix nor the read-back.**

## The step that should have caught it did not, and here is why

Normally `cdk deploy` at `[5/6]` sets the identifier, and `[6/6]` is a no-op. That failed here because **a rollback moves the service out-of-band and CloudFormation never learns**:

```
FrontendStack template : @sha256:1beeb39a...   (what CFN believes)
live service           : @sha256:5788ced4...   (what the rollback set)
```

CFN compares its template to its own last-known state, sees no diff, and reports `FrontendStack (no changes)`. It never writes the identifier, so the drift survives.

**The backend escaped only by luck of shape.** Its `CONSOLE_VERSION` env var changes every deploy, so `BackendStack` always has a real diff and CFN rewrites the identifier along with it. The web has no version stamp — the rollback itself prints *"web: declares no version stamp — nothing to correct"* — so `FrontendStack` has nothing to diff on, forever.

**A rolled-back service with no per-deploy env var can never be corrected by a subsequent deploy.** It is stuck until something calls `update-service` directly.

## Why the D4 proof missed it

[DRE-2732](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2732)'s step-3 verdict compared **only the backend** digest, twice, and passed both times. The backend genuinely did move. The web did not, and nothing looked.

That is a real gap in the proof and it is recorded on that card, not hidden. The rollback path verifies BOTH services because DRE-2775 made it; the deploy path verifies neither.

## Recovered

`make rollback-console VERSION=agent-bureau-console-v1.6.5` — direction-agnostic, uses `update-service`, verified both services landed. Both now on v1.6.5, confirmed by `describe-service`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `deploy-console.sh` moves a service by `update-service` **with the built digest**, not `start-deployment` — so it works whether or not CloudFormation's model is current.
- [ ] After every deploy, **each service's live identifier is read back and compared to the digest just built**; a mismatch fails the deploy loudly. The rollback has done this since DRE-2775; the deploy must too.
- [ ] A test covers **the state this actually occurred in**: CFN's template current, the live service drifted out-of-band, `cdk deploy` reporting no changes. That combination is what the harness never modelled.
- [ ] The proof of D4 checks **both** services, not just the backend — the asymmetry that hid this.
- [ ] Each guard is demonstrated failing under a deliberate mutation and passing after revert.

## The pattern, stated once

Five defects in one day, all one shape: **a mechanism whose stated behaviour and real behaviour disagree, failing silently and reporting success.** Four were found by running the real thing. This one was found because a human noticed a panel was missing — which is a worse detector than a read-back, and the reason the read-back belongs in the deploy path too.

cards.title: A zero WIP cap makes wip_health nag forever — a deliberate hold reads as a board about to jam
cards.description:
Split out of [DRE-2759](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2759/promotion-fills-to-the-wip-cap-and-ignores-phase-order-phase-4-is), where it was found. It was never that card's work, and attaching it there would have auto-closed a six-item card on a two-file diff (agent-bureau PR #2144, closed for exactly that reason).

## The defect

`console/backend/monitors/wip_health.py` warns once `wip >= cap - 1`. **At cap 0 that reads** `wip >= -1` **— true for every possible WIP.**

So a fleet whose promotion is deliberately held would raise

> *"WIP nearing the cap — the next card will stall. Bump the cap or land work."*

on **every tick, forever**, advising the operator to undo the hold they had just set on purpose. Technically correct, practically noise, during a state that was chosen.

Entering a hold must also **resolve a warn that is already open**. The realistic order is: the board fills to the cap and warns, then the operator holds promotion. Suppressing new alerts while leaving the old one standing describes a condition that has been deliberately resolved — worse than noisy, because it is stale.

## Found by trying it

[DRE-2759](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2759/promotion-fills-to-the-wip-cap-and-ignores-phase-order-phase-4-is) attempted to pause promotion by setting the cap to zero. This monitor was the thing that would have turned a quiet pause into a permanent alert. **The hold was ultimately done another way** — deactivating the epic, the mechanism `reconcile.py`'s dependency gate already reads — so nothing currently sets the cap to zero.

**The guard is still worth having. **`cap` is a parameter (`check(store, now, *, cap=DEFAULT_MAX_WIP)`), nothing stops a caller passing zero, and [DRE-2759](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2759/promotion-fills-to-the-wip-cap-and-ignores-phase-order-phase-4-is)'s real fix may yet introduce a hold state. Both tests exercise it directly by passing `cap=0`, so this is tested behaviour rather than unreachable defensive code.

## The work

Small and already written — it is on the closed PR #2144 (`e4226788`), which can be cherry-picked, **but not as-is**: that commit put the test and the fix together and must be re-split red-first.

* `wip_health.check` returns early on `cap <= 0`, resolving any open alert
* `test_a_zero_cap_is_a_deliberate_hold_and_never_warns`
* `test_a_zero_cap_resolves_a_warn_that_was_already_open`

## Acceptance

- [ ] Red first, in its own commit: a test proving the monitor warns at `cap=0` today
- [ ] A cap of zero or less raises nothing, and **resolves** an alert already open
- [ ] Every existing `test_wip_health.py` case still passes — the normal `cap - 1` threshold is untouched
- [ ] **Not** fixed here: a pre-existing `E402` in `wip_health.py` (the import below its explanatory comment). Verified against `origin/main` — it predates this work, and reformatting a neighbouring file inside a two-line fix is how a small PR becomes a review.

cards.title: [OPERATOR] Prove Phase 8 — the old structure archived, and the wave closed
cards.description:
> **Renumbered 2026-08-29.** This card was titled *"Prove Phase 6"*. Phase 6 is now **the read layer**; archiving the old structure and closing the wave is **Phase 8**, the last phase. Nothing about this card's job changed — only its position, because three phases were inserted ahead of it.
>
> It is now blocked by [DRE-2840](<https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2840>) (Phase 7's proof) rather than by Phase 5's, which is what puts it back at the end of the chain.
>
> **This is the card that closes the wave, so it inherits the KPI scoring** that [DRE-2765](<https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2765>) used to carry. [DRE-2668](<https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2668>) predicted five KPIs before any work started, and a prediction that is never scored is a guess. Baselines: KPI 9 board honesty at **120** cards over 24h in a non-terminal lane (2026-08-18 20:30 PT); KPI 1 walk-away rate; KPI 2 cards stalled over 6h; KPI 8 wasted inference; and a new dispatch-to-escalation rate. Mark each right or wrong — including the one predicted to get **worse first**, which is the honest half of the exercise.

Phase 6's proof, and the last gate in the wave. **Runs after **[DRE-2765](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2765/operator-prove-phase-5-cards-flow-through-the-new-front-door) **(Phase 5).**

## ⚠️ This phase is one third done, and it went first instead of last

[DRE-2755](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2755/retire-the-wave-room-the-board-is-built-on-a-word-this-design-deletes) **— "Retire the wave room" — is already Done.** Phase 6 is *"the old structure archived"*, and part of it was archived while Phase 3 (*"the gates proven against every card type"*) sat at 0%. **The old thing was removed before its replacement was proven.**

That is the single clearest piece of evidence for why the phases are now chained ([DRE-2759](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2759/promotion-fills-to-the-wip-cap-and-ignores-phase-order-phase-4-is)), and it is why this card exists as a gate rather than a checklist.

Remaining: [DRE-2744](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2744/delete-the-two-redundant-product-keys-and-the-third-call-site-that) (delete the two redundant product keys — see its own comment: the label cull is partly done already), [DRE-2752](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2752/the-last-card-archive-the-old-structure-once-nothing-live-depends-on) (the last card — archive the old structure once nothing live depends on it).

## What "proven" means here

Phase 6 is different from every phase before it: **it deletes things.** So the proof is not "did the change land" but *"is anything still standing on what we removed"*.

- [ ] [DRE-2752](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2752/the-last-card-archive-the-old-structure-once-nothing-live-depends-on)'s own precondition is checked, not assumed — *"once nothing live depends on it"*. Name what was checked and how. A grep is not a dependency check; a card that references the old structure is not the same as code that reads it.
- [ ] [DRE-2744](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2744/delete-the-two-redundant-product-keys-and-the-third-call-site-that)'s three deletions go together or not at all, as its card says. In particular `require_initiative` at `linear_ops.py:676` — delete the labels without it and `cmd_subissue` **raises and the planner loses its entire output path**. Prove a real sub-issue is created after the deletion, live.
- [ ] Retire, do not delete. `issueLabelRetire` keeps a label on the cards already carrying it; deleting rewrites history to tidy a menu. The operator ratified 21 retirements on 2026-08-26 on exactly that basis.
- [ ] **A card with no **`repo:` **label is bounced with a message naming the label it needs** — observed live ([DRE-2744](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2744/delete-the-two-redundant-product-keys-and-the-third-call-site-that)'s own criterion). After this phase, `repo:` is the only routing key and a bad card can only be *bounced*, never repaired.

## Closing the wave

[DRE-2668](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2668/wave-15-the-intake-gate-a-card-is-proven-before-it-is-work)'s exit criteria are proven across [DRE-2763](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2763/operator-prove-phase-3-the-gates-proven-against-every-card-type) (the card-type matrix, the Portico comparison) and [DRE-2765](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2765/operator-prove-phase-5-cards-flow-through-the-new-front-door) (the KPI re-measurement). **This card is where the wave is declared closed** — and it should not be closed while any of them is unticked.

- [ ] Every [DRE-2668](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2668/wave-15-the-intake-gate-a-card-is-proven-before-it-is-work) exit criterion is ticked, or explicitly waived with a reason
- [ ] `max_wip` **comes off zero** ([DRE-2759](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2759/promotion-fills-to-the-wip-cap-and-ignores-phase-order-phase-4-is)) and the epic returns to In Progress — the wave is over, so the hold ends
- [ ] The post-mortem is written: which predictions were wrong, and what the phase-ordering failure cost

## The one to be honest about

**Phases 4, 5 and 6 all had work merged before their predecessors were proven.** The chain now prevents a repeat, but this wave already paid for it. Write down what that cost — including anything that had to be redone — because the next wave inherits the ordering and should also inherit the reason for it.

cards.title: A repo-wide "this string appears nowhere" test breaks on every unrelated merge — the guard's correctness depends on the repo standing still
cards.description:
**Observed live 2026-08-26.** PR #189 ([DRE-2722](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2722/rename-plan-review-to-green-light-and-move-the-escalations-to-triage)) sat blocked with a critic **APPROVE** and a red unit test that named nothing the PR had done wrong.

## What happened

[DRE-2722](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2722/rename-plan-review-to-green-light-and-move-the-escalations-to-triage) renames the `Plan Review` lane to `Green Light`, and ships `tests/test_green_light_rename.py::test_the_old_lane_name_is_gone_from_every_tracked_file` — a sweep asserting the retired name appears in **no tracked file**.

**PR #188 merged at 15:13 PT, after #189's branch was cut**, and introduced three files containing the string:

```
architecture/decisions/adr-layer-1-guard-scope.md:18
scripts/lane_scope.py:8,57,59,62
tests/test_lane_scope.py:4..107
```

The test runs against the **merge ref**, so it sees `main`'s new files. #189 went red for something a *different* PR did, minutes after being approved.

## Why this is a pattern, not an incident

**The test's correctness depends on the rest of the repo standing still.** Every merge to `main` that introduces the string breaks every open PR carrying the sweep — and the PR that breaks is never the one at fault.

**It gets worse as the fleet gets faster.** This is the same shape as [DRE-2716](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2716/ci-un-does-every-rollback-latest-is-both-the-deploy-pointer-and-the)'s `:latest` race: a defect whose window is inversely proportional to merge frequency, in a programme whose whole point is merging more often.

It also cost more than the fix. The fix loop **could not engage** — it triggers on `REQUEST_CHANGES`, and the verdict was `APPROVE`. The approved-but-red backstop lives in the reconcile sweep, which was 21 minutes late on a 15-minute cron. A one-line-equivalent problem sat blocked behind two mechanisms that were each behaving correctly.

## The shape of a fix — not decided here

1. **Run the sweep on** `main`**, not on PRs.** A post-merge check; a red `main` already has a designed owner in `red-main-repair`. Keeps the completeness guarantee, moves the failure to where the offending merge actually is. Cost: the string can land on `main` for one cycle.
2. **Assert no NEW occurrences relative to the merge base.** Stable under concurrent merges by construction, and the failure always names the PR that caused it. Cost: it stops proving the rename is *complete*, only that it is not getting worse.
3. **Scope the sweep to files the PR touches.** Smallest change, and the weakest — it stops catching stale uses anywhere else, which is the thing the sweep exists for.
4. **Keep it, and make the failure self-describing.** Leave the semantics alone but have it say *"these occurrences arrived on* `main` *after this branch was cut — rebase"*, so nobody spends the diagnosis time twice.

**Recommend 1 or 2.** 4 is worth doing regardless of which lands, because it is cheap and it is the part that actually wasted the time.

## Worth checking while here

`test_the_old_lane_name_is_gone_from_every_tracked_file` is unlikely to be the only sweep of this shape. Any assertion of the form *"X appears nowhere in the repo"* has the same property. Enumerate them before choosing, so the fix lands once rather than per-sweep.

## Acceptance

- [ ] The chosen shape is implemented, with the reasoning recorded where the next person will look
- [ ] Red first: a test proving the guard no longer fails on a PR whose only offence is being cut before an unrelated merge
- [ ] The completeness guarantee is either preserved, or its loss is explicitly stated and accepted on this card
- [ ] Every other repo-wide absence sweep is enumerated, and each is either converted or deliberately left with the reason recorded
- [ ] The failure message names *why* it failed and what to do — rebase, or fix a real occurrence

cards.title: D4 survives digest addressing — a re-deploy after a rollback pins App Runner to a different commit's build
cards.description:
**D4 is no longer read-verified. It EXECUTES, and** [DRE-2716](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2716/ci-un-does-every-rollback-latest-is-both-the-deploy-pointer-and-the) **did not remove it.**

[DRE-2734](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2734/deploy-consolesh-is-untestable-it-runs-npx-cdk-four-times-so-the) gave the harness a `volta` seam, so `deploy-console.sh` now runs offline. The first thing it settled is that [DRE-2716](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2716/ci-un-does-every-rollback-latest-is-both-the-deploy-pointer-and-the)'s central claim is wrong.

## What [DRE-2716](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2716/ci-un-does-every-rollback-latest-is-both-the-deploy-pointer-and-the) believed

> **D4** (a re-deploy after a rollback corrupts `:<sha>` and ships old code) stops existing — nothing recomputes a tag, so nothing overwrites one.

## What actually happens, measured

`retag_latest_to_sha` is untouched by [DRE-2716](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2716/ci-un-does-every-rollback-latest-is-both-the-deploy-pointer-and-the) and still runs on the reuse path. [DRE-2716](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2716/ci-un-does-every-rollback-latest-is-both-the-deploy-pointer-and-the) changed what **consumes** the tag, not what **corrupts** it — and the corruption now feeds the digest path instead of the `:latest` path.

Reproduced end to end in `infra/test/rollback/test_deploy_after_rollback.py`:

1. Roll back to the good version → `:latest` = the old image.
2. Re-deploy the **same** commit (`abc1234`). Nothing changed, so `needs_build` takes the REUSE path.
3. `retag_latest_to_sha` re-puts the manifest under `:latest` — now the OLD image — as `:abc1234`. **The tag naming the current commit's build now names a different build.**
4. The deploy then resolves the rollout digest **from that corrupted tag** and hands it to CDK.

The observable proof, straight from the recorded `cdk deploy` invocation:

```
--context consoleBuildSha=abc1234
--context backendDigest=sha256:a1a1…      ← the ROLLED-OFF build
```

Commit `abc1234`'s real image is `sha256:b1b1…`. **So the console would report commit** `abc1234` **and run a build from a different commit** — pinned by an immutable digest, which makes it durable rather than transient.

## Why the digest fix did not catch it

Digest addressing guarantees *"what runs is exactly the manifest we named"*. It says nothing about whether the manifest we named is the **right** one. Garbage in, immutably pinned.

## The specs are already written and red

Two `strict` xfails in `test_deploy_after_rollback.py`, both failing today:

* `test_spec_a_deploy_must_never_overwrite_an_existing_sha_tag` — `:<short-sha>` addresses one build. A deploy may CREATE it; it must never repoint an existing one.
* `test_spec_a_redeploy_must_not_pin_the_service_to_another_commits_build` — asserted on the `cdk deploy` context, deliberately, because `cdk deploy` is stubbed and the resulting service state is a harness artifact.

## Shape of the fix — not decided here

1. `retag_latest_to_sha` **refuses to overwrite an existing** `:<sha>`**.** Smallest. If the tag exists, that IS the commit's build; use it rather than re-stamping `:latest` over it. Turns both specs green and matches [DRE-2716](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2716/ci-un-does-every-rollback-latest-is-both-the-deploy-pointer-and-the)'s unticked acceptance box *"a deploy following a rollback cannot overwrite an existing* `:<sha>` *image"*.
2. **The reuse path resolves its digest from** `:<sha>` **before any re-tag**, so the corruption cannot reach the rollout decision even if it happens.
3. **Drop** `retag_latest_to_sha` **entirely** — ask whether the reuse path needs a re-tag at all now that the identifier is a digest rather than a tag.

Recommend **1**, possibly with **3** as a follow-up once someone establishes what the re-tag was for.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Both specs above go green, with the `strict` markers removed
- [ ] `test_a_redeploy_after_a_rollback_overwrites_the_sha_tag` — the characterization — is updated to pin the FIXED behaviour, not deleted
- [ ] [DRE-2716](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2716/ci-un-does-every-rollback-latest-is-both-the-deploy-pointer-and-the)'s description is corrected: option 1 did not delete D4
- [ ] [DRE-2732](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2732/operator-prove-the-console-rollback-actually-works-forward-back)'s live proof adds a fourth step — forward → back → **forward on the same commit** — since that is the sequence that triggers this

cards.title: The last card — archive the old structure once nothing live depends on it
cards.description:
**The wave ends with a clean board, not a working board surrounded by residue.**

Every other card in this wave adds or changes something. This one removes what those changes made obsolete — and it is deliberately last, blocked by everything, because **you cannot tell what is dead until the new model is live and proven.**

## Archiving is not deletion, and that distinction settles an earlier argument

The cutover section says the old wave epics are not archived, because they are the programme's audit trail. **That was stated too strongly, and this card corrects it.** What must never happen is *conversion* — rewriting finished history into a structure it was never built in. Archiving does not do that: in Linear an archived issue keeps its body, comments, relations and history, and simply stops appearing in active views.

So the rule has three parts, and only the middle one was written down before:

* **Never convert.** Old epics stay parent issues, forever.
* **Never archive early.** While cards are still being classified out of the old structure, you need to see it.
* **Archive at the end.** Once nothing live depends on it, a finished structure sitting in active views is noise that makes the board harder to read — which is the thing this wave exists to fix.

## What gets archived

Computed at the time, not remembered — the counts below will be wrong by the time this runs, which is why the card asks for a live census rather than quoting one.

**Closed wave epics.** The `[WAVE N]` parent issues whose children are all terminal. They stop being extended at the cutover line; archiving is what stops them cluttering.

**Initiatives that became nothing. **[DRE-2742](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2742/the-five-product-initiatives-become-objectives-the-hierarchy) dispositions the five product Initiatives; whichever are resolved as "becomes nothing" are archived here, not there — that card decides, this one cleans up.

**Completed and cancelled projects.** With a caveat verified 2026-08-26: **there is no** `projectArchive` **mutation.** Projects can be updated but not archived through the API, so this is either a status change or an operator action in the UI. Say which; do not assume a script can do it.

**Retired labels. **[DRE-2744](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2744/delete-the-two-redundant-product-keys-and-the-third-call-site-that) does the cull. Note it should use `issueLabelRetire` rather than `issueLabelDelete` — retiring keeps the label on cards that already carry it while removing it from pickers, which is what preserves the record.

**Terminal cards past a stated age.** Done, Canceled and Duplicate cards older than a threshold. **State the threshold and its reason**; do not pick one silently.

## What must not be touched

**Anything still referenced by a live card, an open PR, or a document that is current.** The check runs before the archive, not after.

**The audit trail's readability.** An archived epic must still be reachable by id from a post-mortem that cites it. If archiving breaks a link in `architecture/`, the link is the thing to fix — not by un-archiving, but by making the reference explicit about what it points at.

## Why this is not just tidying

The wave's own thesis is that a board should be honest, and **a board carrying two years of finished structure is not lying but it is not readable either.** The cost shows up the same way: someone scanning for what needs attention scans past things that do not, and the cost is attention — the resource this whole wave exists to protect.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A live census is taken first and recorded on this card: how many wave epics, initiatives, projects and terminal cards are candidates, with the rule that selected each.
- [ ] Nothing is archived that is referenced by a non-terminal card, an open pull request, or a current document — asserted by a check that runs before the archive.
- [ ] The archive runs through [DRE-2751](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2751/the-linear-workspace-configuration-becomes-code-declared-as-data)'s script, not by hand, so what was archived is a reviewable diff.
- [ ] Projects are handled explicitly, with the missing `projectArchive` mutation named and the chosen approach stated.
- [ ] Labels are **retired**, not deleted, and a closed card is observed still carrying its retired label.
- [ ] The terminal-card age threshold is one named constant with its reason in the PR.
- [ ] An archived wave epic is still reachable by id from a post-mortem that cites it, checked on one real link.
- [ ] Board occupancy before and after is recorded, so the cleanup's effect is a number rather than an impression.

cards.title: The critic reads a private repo it can't see as a repo that doesn't exist — a 404 becomes "fabricated claim"
cards.description:
The QA critic runs `gh` on a **GitHub App installation token**. That token can only see repos the App is installed on — and GitHub returns **404, never 403**, for a private repo the caller is not authorised for.

So the critic cannot distinguish *"this repo does not exist"* from *"I am not allowed to see it,"* and it currently reports the first.

## The live case

agent-bureau PR #2136 ([DRE-2733](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2733/the-version-annotation-records-a-mutable-tag-so-a-rollback-resolves)) cited its mirror PR in `dreadnought-foundry/project-template`. The critic returned **REQUEST_CHANGES** `cause:unverified-claim`, on this reasoning:

> `gh api repos/dreadnought-foundry/project-template` → `404 Not Found` … `gh api orgs/dreadnought-foundry/repos --paginate` lists only `Auto-Claude, agent-bureau, ai-playbook, bureau-pipeline, claude-maestro, maestro-agents, mcp-server-linear` — no `project-template`.

Measured from an operator token at 2026-08-26 10:29 PT, the repo and the PR both exist:

```
$ gh api repos/dreadnought-foundry/project-template --jq '{full_name,private,created_at}'
{"created_at":"2026-06-21T15:36:40Z","full_name":"dreadnought-foundry/project-template","private":true}

$ gh api repos/dreadnought-foundry/project-template/pulls/9 --jq '{number,state,changed_files}'
{"changed_files":3,"number":9,"state":"open"}
```

**The org listing is the tell.** The critic saw **7** repos; an operator token sees **19**, and the 7 are a strict subset:

```
Auto-Claude agent-bureau agent-bureau-demo ai-playbook bureau-harness bureau-pipeline
charter citadel claude-maestro crucible deltasolv-archive dreadnought-core gridcorr
maestro-agents mcp-server-linear portico project-template strata vericorr
```

`portico`, `vericorr` and `deltasolv-archive` are absent from the critic's list too, and those are unambiguously real. It was not looking at the org; it was looking at its own installation.

## Why this is worth fixing rather than working around

The finding it made was a **good** one in principle — an unverifiable claim in a PR body is a real hazard, and worse than a bug in a pipeline nobody reads line by line. The problem is that its evidence does not support its conclusion, and it is confident.

It fails in **both** directions:

* **False negative (blocking):** a true, verifiable claim is reported as fabricated, and a correct PR is bounced. Every cross-repo card — every mirror, every fan-out, every fleet sweep — is exposed, and those are exactly the cards where the claim matters most.
* **Worse, silently:** "I could not find it" currently carries **no information**, so a genuinely false cross-repo claim looks identical to a true one the App cannot see. The check reads as working while catching nothing.

## The fix — a direction, not a prescription

The critic should treat a bare 404 on a cross-repo lookup as **unknown**, not **absent**, and say so in the verdict. Options worth weighing on the card:

1. **Probe its own visibility first. **`gh api installation/repositories` (or the org listing) tells it what it can see. A repo outside that set is out of scope: report *"cannot verify — not installed on* `<repo>`*"* and do not block on it.
2. **Distinguish the two 404s.** An org-level lookup that succeeds while the repo lookup 404s is strong evidence of a private repo, not a missing one.
3. **Prefer the Linear card as the cross-repo anchor.** The critic already has a Linear key; a card id is checkable through an API it *is* authorised for, and does not depend on GitHub App installation at all.
4. **Install the App more widely** — simplest, and it is the operator's call, but it does not fix the *reasoning*, only this instance of it. Options 1–3 should land regardless.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Red first: a test proving the critic's cross-repo verification reports "unknown/not-installed" rather than "does not exist" on a 404
- [ ] A verdict that cannot verify a cross-repo claim says so explicitly and does **not** block on it alone
- [ ] The existing value is kept: a claim about a repo the critic **can** see, that is genuinely absent, still blocks
- [ ] Guidance in `briefs/` for what a PR body should cite for cross-repo work — repo + branch + Linear id, not a bare URL a reviewer may not be able to open

cards.title: Alerts leave Linear for the console — deferred out of Wave 1.5, behind DRE-2535
cards.description:
**Filed with no parent epic deliberately.** This was cut from Wave 1.5 on 2026-08-25 (D1) and has no home wave yet. It is filed rather than remembered, because the alternative is a decision that exists only in a conversation.

## What it is

Stop filing pipeline notifications as Linear cards. Raise them as console alerts instead.

Measured 2026-08-24: **17 cards in Triage, every one created there by automation, every one with zero state transitions since, the oldest 27 days.** They are not work — they are notices. "Pipeline failure: CI", "Model drift", "Release channel held". Someone reads one and it is done. Filing them as issues put them in a lane with no reader.

## Why it must not ship before [DRE-2535](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2535/alert-delivery-that-leaves-the-console-push-and-email-wired-in)

**The console's alerts have never reached anyone.** No `ALERT_*` variable is set in production; `default_email_sender` logs "alert email skipped" and returns, `default_push_sender` logs "alert push skipped" and returns. **Both fail silently at info level.** Every CRITICAL the console has raised has been panel-only.

Move the alerts before [DRE-2535](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2535/alert-delivery-that-leaves-the-console-push-and-email-wired-in) lands and they go from a lane nobody reads to a panel nobody is notified about — **the same failure at a new address.**

Meanwhile, leaving them in Linear costs a cluttered Triage lane, which is visible and counted. That is the cheaper of the two failures, and it is why this waits.

## Relationship to Wave 1.5

[DRE-2723](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2723/triage-becomes-the-broken-card-lane) keeps the other half: Triage becomes the lane for a card that went wrong. **Dispositioning the 17 existing notice-cards stays there too** — that is what empties the lane so Triage can mean one thing. Only the *mechanism change* — where future notices go — is here.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] [DRE-2535](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2535/alert-delivery-that-leaves-the-console-push-and-email-wired-in) has landed and a CRITICAL is observed reaching the CEO out of band, with the receipt — before any of the work below starts.
- [ ] A pipeline failure is observed raising a console alert and **not** creating a Linear card.
- [ ] Every writer that currently files a notice card is repointed, enumerated rather than fixed one at a time.
- [ ] A repeated failure does not mint a second alert — the duplicate suppression that lives in `medic.yml`'s prompt today has an equivalent on the console side.
- [ ] Triage contains no automation-filed notices after this ships.
- [ ] This card is given a parent epic when its wave is decided; it is not built while parentless.

cards.title: The push-ingest alert cannot tell a quiet fleet from a deaf one — nine raises, nine self-recoveries, nine nights running
cards.description:
`push_ingest_health` raises **"Live github updates stopped arriving Nh ago"** every night the fleet is idle, then clears itself every morning when someone merges something. It has done this **nine times on nine consecutive days** — 08-17 through 08-25 — all WARN, all self-recovered.

Its own alert body says *"this one does NOT self-heal, so it needs a look."* That claim is false nine times over.

## What it actually measures

`console/backend/monitors/push_ingest_health.py` → `_check_source` reads `ingest_freshness.push_stale_for(store, now, "github")` = `now − poll_health.last_webhook_at`. Thresholds: WARN at `PUSH_STALE_AFTER_SECONDS` = **6h**, CRITICAL at 24h.

"Delivered an event" means exactly one thing: `ws_ingest.apply_ws_message` received a frame carrying `pr_node` and reached `store.record_webhook_received("github", …)` (`ws_ingest.py:315`). **Heartbeats do not count** — they stamp `last_frame_at` only.

So the predicate is *"GitHub produced no PR event in 6 hours."* On a fleet that sleeps overnight, that is a normal state.

## The measurement that settles it

The 2026-08-25 raise (00:55 PT, auto-resolved 06:49 PT) covered a genuine **11.9-hour** silence, 18:55 PT → 06:48 PT. But:

* **Nothing merged in that window.** Checked agent-bureau, portico and bureau-pipeline: no PR merged or updated between 01:55Z and 13:48Z.
* **The path was never deaf.** PR #2134 merged at `14:30:43Z`; `ws ingest: github agent-bureau#2134 ingested` appears at `14:30:47Z` **— four seconds later**, inside a burst of ~104 github ingest lines.
* Observed overnight gaps: **11.9h on two consecutive nights.** A 6h threshold is less than half a routine quiet period.

## Why only github fires, and this is the real bug

`ws_ingest.catch_up` stamps `record_webhook_received(LINEAR, …)` on **every reconnect, even when it ingests 0 changed cards** (`ws_ingest.py:214` — the "push gap closed" line, which ran every 1–2h all night).

**So Linear's staleness clock is reset by mere reconnects. GitHub has no equivalent and can only be reset by a real PR event.** The two sources are not held to the same standard: one counts liveness, the other counts activity.

## ⚠️ Do NOT just raise the threshold or delete the monitor

This monitor exists because of [DRE-2398](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2398/ws-ingest-push-path-dead-32-days-on-both-sources-console-running-on-15)**: "WS ingest push path dead 32 days on both sources — console running on 15-min poll-only, no alert fired."** A real 32-day silent failure is what bought it. Raising 6h to 24h would have let a large part of that outage pass unremarked again.

The fix must distinguish **quiet** from **deaf** — not trade one blind spot for the other:

* credit a positive liveness signal that a healthy-but-idle socket still produces (the relay heartbeat already arrives; it is discarded for this purpose), or
* gate the staleness clock on whether there was anything to deliver — no merged PRs in the window means no expected events, and silence is then information-free.

Whichever shape is chosen, **record why the 6h/activity-only version is superseded**, the way the channel guards were superseded rather than deleted — [DRE-2398](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2398/ws-ingest-push-path-dead-32-days-on-both-sources-console-running-on-15)'s incident is the reason it existed and must outlive it.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A night with zero fleet merges raises nothing
- [ ] A genuinely dead socket still raises — **proven by breaking it on purpose**, not by reasoning. [DRE-2398](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2398/ws-ingest-push-path-dead-32-days-on-both-sources-console-running-on-15) went unnoticed for 32 days precisely because nobody tested the detector
- [ ] The alert body no longer claims it does not self-heal, or it becomes true
- [ ] Linear and github are held to the same standard, or the asymmetry is documented with its reason

Related: [DRE-2398](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2398/ws-ingest-push-path-dead-32-days-on-both-sources-console-running-on-15) (the 32-day outage this monitor was built for), [DRE-2663](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2663/three-pool-alert-kinds-are-unclassified-so-a-warn-saying-nothing-to-do) (pool alert kinds unclassified — same family of alert-quality work).
