cards.title: We have about 3.6 days of rollback history, and it shrinks every time we deploy more often
cards.description:
**Nobody has ever answered “how far back can we roll?”** The answer is currently a side effect of a default, and it is far shorter than anyone would guess.

## The measurement

`infra/lib/release-stack.ts:43-50,58-65` sets `maxImageCount: 20` with `tagStatus: ANY` on both console ECR repos.

Live-verified: **39 console-release runs in the last 7 days** ≈ 5.6 pushes/day.

**20 ÷ 5.6 ≈ 3.6 days of rollback history.**

`tagStatus: ANY` means the rule expires images regardless of their tags — so a `:<short-sha>` image an operator is relying on as a rollback target is collected on the same schedule as everything else.

*Confidence note: read from the CDK source, not confirmed against the live account. Step 1 of the operator proof sequence includes* `aws ecr get-lifecycle-policy`*, which settles it. Do that before changing anything.*

## Why it matters more than it looks

**Git version tags live forever. The images they point at do not.** `rollback-console.sh:55` lists every version tag ever cut, so it cheerfully offers an operator a version whose image was garbage-collected weeks ago. The failure arrives as `manifest unknown` at the worst possible moment — and by then, per [DRE-2715](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2715/rollback-consolesh-reports-success-on-a-failed-rollback-and-can-strand)'s D5, the other repo's `:latest` has already moved.

**And it scales the wrong way.** Deploy twice as often and the horizon halves. The epic exists to enable more frequent deploys, so this number falls exactly as the change lands.

## What to decide, and it is a real question

**How far back should we be able to roll, in days?** Not in images — in days, because that is the unit an incident is measured in. “We noticed on Monday that something broke on Friday” needs a horizon longer than a weekend.

Then set `maxImageCount` from that number and the observed push rate, with a comment recording both inputs so the next person can see whether the assumption still holds. A bare number with no derivation is how we got 20.

**Worth considering:** a second lifecycle rule that keeps tagged `:<short-sha>` images longer than untagged layers, rather than one `ANY` rule for everything. Rollback targets and build intermediates have no reason to share a retention policy.

## Acceptance

- [ ] The live lifecycle policy is read and recorded on this card, confirming or correcting the CDK reading
- [ ] A target rollback horizon is chosen **in days** and written down with its reasoning
- [ ] `maxImageCount` derives from that horizon and the measured push rate, with both inputs in a comment
- [ ] The rollback script refuses, before mutating anything, when a requested version's image no longer exists — and says so in terms of the horizon
- [ ] Mirrored into `project-template`, since `new-project-playbook.md:124` copies this stack shape into every new Newco repo

---

## ✅ DECIDED (operator, 2026-08-25): **30 days**, expressed in days — not a derived count

### First, the live read the card asked for — done, and it corrects one number

`aws ecr get-lifecycle-policy` against the live account, both repos:

```json
{"rules": [{"rulePriority": 1, "description": "Keep last 20 images",
  "selection": {"tagStatus": "any", "countType": "imageCountMoreThan", "countNumber": 20},
  "action": {"type": "expire"}}]}
```

**The CDK reading was correct.** `maxImageCount: 20`, `tagStatus: ANY`, on both. The confidence note can be struck.

But the horizon figure was not:

|  |  |
| -- | -- |
| images held | **exactly 20** in each repo — the cap is biting *now*, every deploy evicts the oldest |
| oldest | 2026-08-20 16:11 PT (`98bc38f6…`) |
| newest | 2026-08-25 07:31 PT (`ab1929ea…`, the #2134 merge) |
| **measured horizon** | **4.64 days** at **4.3 images/day** |

Not 3.6. The estimate divided by *release runs* (5.6/day), but the change-aware build reuses images, so fewer runs actually push one. **4.6 days measured, and the shelf is full.**

### The cost, which is what settles it

Backend images average **202 MB**, web **52 MB**. All 40 = 5.07 GB.

| horizon | images/repo | storage | $/month |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 4.6 days *(today)* | 20 | 5.1 GB | **$0.51** |
| 14 days | 60 | 15.2 GB | $1.52 |
| **30 days** | ~130 | 33 GB | **$3.30** |

**We are buying a four-day safety net to save three dollars a month.** That is the entire trade.

### Why 30 and not 14

14 days covers a holiday. 30 covers *"we found it after the quarter closed"* — a two-week absence, plus a week of not noticing, plus reaction time. The unit an incident is measured in is calendar time, and the expensive incidents are the ones nobody spots quickly.

### ⚠️ Do NOT derive `maxImageCount` from the push rate

This card says *"set* `maxImageCount` *from that number and the observed push rate."* **Do not do that.** A count derived from today's rate silently shortens as the rate rises — and **this epic exists to raise it**. At 10 pushes/day a "30-day" count of 130 is a 13-day policy, with nothing announcing the change.

That is the failure this fleet keeps paying for: a derived number frozen into config, drifting the moment its input moves (`adr-one-writer-per-fact`, [DRE-2605](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2605/which-repos-still-ride-main-is-computed-from-the-roster-not-remembered), and [DRE-2312](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2312/a-fix-run-that-exhausts-its-60-turn-budget-is-reported-as-an-ai)'s stale-classifier family).

**Use** `sinceImagePushed` **with** `countUnit: days`**.** Say 30 days and let ECR do the arithmetic. The horizon then holds regardless of deploy frequency, and the config states the actual intent rather than an encoding of it.

### The wrinkle this card must decide

A pure `sinceImagePushed` rule **empties the shelf during a genuinely quiet month** — 30 quiet days and there is nothing to roll back to. ECR cannot express *"30 days OR at least N images, whichever keeps more"* in a single rule; rules evaluate by priority and the first match acts.

So pick a shape and write down why:

* days-only, accepting that a quiet month leaves no targets, or
* a count floor as a lower-priority rule, or
* keep a small count rule for `:latest`/`:deployed` specifically so the running images are never collectable

**This is the one real design call in the card. It is not a detail.**

### Free win, take it in the same PR

`tagStatus: any` expires the `:<short-sha>` images an operator rolls back to **on the same schedule as untagged build intermediates**. Those have no reason to share a retention policy. A separate short rule for `tagStatus: untagged` costs one rule and stops build garbage crowding out rollback targets.

### Acceptance updates

- [X] The live lifecycle policy is read and recorded — above; CDK reading confirmed, horizon corrected to 4.64 days
- [X] A target horizon chosen in days, with reasoning — **30 days**

cards.title: [EPIC] Deploy safety — make the rollback real before deploying more often
cards.description:
**TRACK-ONLY epic, deliberately not** `agent:planner` — the children are already written and specified. Adding the planner label would re-decompose work that does not need it. Precedent: [DRE-1875](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-1875/epic-clean-by-hand-merges-local-console-reflects-reality).

## Why this exists as its own epic

The operator asked whether to stop batching deploys and let merge trigger them. The argument for it is strong: [DRE-2608](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2608/the-deploy-refuses-a-checkout-that-is-behind-its-branch-the-4-sighting) shipped a build **77 commits behind** `origin/main` to production and reported success, and Wave 0 shipped ten cards while observing two working — every card between merge and deploy is unobservable, so batching directly suppresses the number the programme exists to move.

The argument rested on `infra/rollback-console.sh` existing and being sound. **It is not sound.** A devops agent executed it against stubbed `aws`/`docker`/`git` on 2026-08-24 and found thirteen defects. Verdict: *not trustworthy enough to increase deploy frequency on top of* — and the two most severe defects **get worse in proportion to deploy rate**, so acting on the original recommendation would have degraded the safety net cited as making it safe.

**Filed as a new epic rather than folded into an existing wave**, because a census of the programme the same night found seven cards already completed out of waves that were never started, with no record of why any of them moved. Putting deploy-safety work under an intake epic would be one more of those.

## The finding that matters most

The script *reads* correctly. Clear header comment, sound mechanism, explains itself. **Five of the thirteen defects are things it does after partially mutating ECR** — invisible to reading, found only by execution. There is currently **no test coverage of the rollback path at all**: no workflow, no test, nothing. The only reference is a test asserting the *deploy* script prints the rollback command.

## Children

1. **The harness** — the stub-based test suite that found these, plus its CI wiring. Ships first so every fix below has a red test to turn green.
2. **Make the script safe to run** — verify the rollout, pre-flight both images, stop lying about the version, fix the version list.
3. **Resolve the** `:latest` **addressing conflict** — the design problem underneath D1, D4 and D11.
4. **Size the ECR lifecycle policy to the intended deploy rate** — today it yields roughly 3.6 days of rollback history.

## Not in scope

Increasing deploy frequency. That is the point of the epic, not part of it — it happens after these land and after one real forward-back-forward proof on the live console.

## Exit

- [ ] Every defect has either a fix or a recorded decision not to fix it
- [ ] The rollback path has test coverage that runs in CI
- [ ] One real rollback and roll-forward observed on the live console, by the operator, using the corrected sequence — not the naive one, which triggers a defect
- [ ] A written answer to “how many days of rollback history do we have, and at what deploy rate”

## Propagation

`architecture/new-project-playbook.md:124` lifts `deploy-console.sh` and `make rollback-console` into every new Newco repo. This defect class is copied outward on each onboarding, so fixes mirror into `project-template` per the standing rule.

cards.title: Two bureau-pipeline docs still say the fleet rides vN — and a guard test requires the false sentence, so fixing them fails CI
cards.description:
[DRE-2706](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2706/bureau-pipelines-readme-still-says-nothing-pins-stable-the-wave-that) / PR #182 corrected `README.md` — the document Wave 1's post-mortem §8 named. A sweep run while fixing it found the pre-`@stable` world described in **two more documents**, and a guard test that makes fixing them fail CI.

## Still false on `main`, verified 2026-08-25

`docs/self-hosting.md`

* line 53–54 — *"re-pointed no stub. The fleet is on* `vN` *with a matching* `pipeline_ref: vN`*, unchanged."*
* line 79 — *"…until it is made and written here,* `vN` *is the only fleet-facing channel."*

`standards/engineering.md`

* line 117 — *"fleet consumes tagged releases (*`vN`*, paired* `pipeline_ref`*), never this"*

Ground truth since 2026-08-23: five consumer repos ride `@stable`, `pipeline_ref: stable` is required ([DRE-2689](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2689/make-pipeline-ref-a-required-input-a-stub-can-no-longer-be-half-pinned)), and no repo consumes a `vN` tag. Derivable at any time from `agent-bureau`'s `config/pipeline-channel.json` via `make check-channel-fleet` — do not hardcode a count here.

## The guard is the load-bearing part

`tests/test_self_hosting_docs.py`, `TestStableChannelDocumented.REQUIRED`:

```python
REQUIRED = (
    # nothing consumes it — the fleet is not on this ref
    "no product repo pins",
    # ...and the cut that the fleet IS on stays a human act
    "operator-only",
    "vN",
)
```

It asserts that **both** docs contain the literal string `"no product repo pins"` — the exact sentence that is false. Its docstring says *"nothing pins* `stable` *yet"*, which was true when written and was reversed by [DRE-2553](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2553/step-4-pin-agent-bureau-and-bureau-pipeline-to-the-channel-and-fold)/2689.

So the guard does not merely fail to catch the staleness — **it requires it.** Delete the false sentence from `self-hosting.md` and CI goes red.

Worth knowing: PR #182 passed this test **by accident**. Its corrected README quotes the old claim inside *"this section used to say the opposite — 'no product repo pins* `@stable`*…'"*, and `assertIn` cannot tell a live assertion from a quotation of a retired one. The guard is now green on a document that says the opposite of what the guard intends.

## Scope

1. Correct both documents to the `@stable` reality, pointing at the derivable source rather than freezing a number.
2. **Supersede the guard, do not delete it.** Follow the house pattern (EveryBite/atlas#147, DeltaSolv/deltasolv#214): the replacement carries the old contract's reason in its header — it was correct under `vN`, reversed by [DRE-2553](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2553/step-4-pin-agent-bureau-and-bureau-pipeline-to-the-channel-and-fold)/2689 — plus a revisit clause: if channel promotion ever becomes a human act again, this guard is enforcing the July design and must be revisited, not quietly dropped.
3. The new assertion should guard the *new* scoping: promotion of `stable` is automatic, the fleet consumes it, and what stays manual is `CHANNEL_HOLD` and the `vN` cut (which nothing rides). A quotation must not satisfy it — assert on a live claim.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Neither document asserts the fleet is on `vN`, anywhere
- [ ] `make check-channel-fleet` in agent-bureau is the cited source; no count is written into prose
- [ ] The guard asserts the current contract and would **fail** on the pre-2026-08-23 text
- [ ] The guard cannot be satisfied by a document merely *quoting* a retired claim
- [ ] The superseded contract and its reason survive in the replacement's header

This is [DRE-2701](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2701/four-per-repo-facts-are-maintained-by-hand-in-n-places-and-each-guard)'s class — *each guard encodes an obsolete version of its rule* — found the way §1 clause 5 found the atlas and deltasolv guard rows: by running the machinery rather than reading it. Related: [DRE-2706](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2706/bureau-pipelines-readme-still-says-nothing-pins-stable-the-wave-that) (the README half, merged as bureau-pipeline#182), [DRE-2545](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2545/the-same-pr-document-rule-must-reach-the-build-agents-not-just-this) (the same-PR document rule), [DRE-2701](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2701/four-per-repo-facts-are-maintained-by-hand-in-n-places-and-each-guard).

cards.title: A new console instance mints a Claude token twelve seconds after boot, revoking the one the fleet holds — every deploy does this, and BUREAU_FLEET_OWNER cannot prevent it
cards.description:
**Operator, 2026-08-23:** *"You were able to change subscriptions back and forth and do the whole rotations of the Claude account without a problem. Something must be going on in deploy that kills that."*

Correct. Verified from the live logs of today's own deploy, with no human involved:

```
14:27:31 PT  [new instance]  Started server process
14:27:31 PT  [new instance]  starting cost-usage cache warmer: interval=240s
14:27:43 PT  [new instance]  fleet-sync: VeriCorr rotated — 6 repo(s) re-pointed
```

**Twelve seconds from boot to a chain advance plus a fleet-wide secret rewrite.** `token()` (`console/backend/claude_oauth_token.py:473-525`) mints unconditionally when its cache is empty, and **a new process always has an empty cache**. So booting is minting.

## Why it revokes rather than merely duplicates

Claude OAuth refresh is **chain-scoped**: minting a new access token invalidates the one issued alongside the previous refresh link. The fleet is holding that previous token. A boot-time mint therefore kills the credential every repo currently has.

## Why `BUREAU_FLEET_OWNER` does not prevent it

It is **service-level config** (`infra/lib/backend-stack.ts:591`), not per-instance — so **every** instance is a fleet owner. And the old instance does not die when the deploy ends:

* deploy completed **14:30:01 PT**
* the previous instance (booted 08-22 16:28 PT) kept serving *and warming* until `Application shutdown complete` at **14:37:46 PT** — a **7m45s drain**

For that window there were multiple live owners, each believing it held exclusive rotation rights. Their reaction to having the chain link stolen is in the log, from **two different dying instances**:

```
14:28:35 PT [old 7fff2a72] claude-pool: vericorr now bills EveryBite (was VeriCorr, failover)
14:28:48 PT [old 4508eb7d] claude-pool: refusing to re-point vericorr — credential did not authenticate
14:36:24 PT [old 7fff2a72] cost-usage probe for VeriCorr returned HTTP 401
```

That is [DRE-2620](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2620/the-pool-failover-has-no-owner-any-console-can-move-repos-and-rewrite) observed live — a dying owner still writing pool decisions from a revoked credential. Note it is **revoked but confident**: its cached expiry is untouched, which is exactly the recorded `hours_remaining: +7.76` symptom from 2026-08-21.

## Nothing serialises rotation

`is_fleet_owner` is a bare env read (`fleet_credential_sync.py:61-68`); the only lock is a per-process `threading.Lock`. Exclusivity is **assumed from the env var alone**. Autoscaling is `MinSize=1, MaxSize=25`, so a scale-out event creates extra owners with no deploy at all.

## Two mechanisms, and they must not be conflated

**A — deploy/boot mint.** Pre-[DRE-2614](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2614/the-console-revokes-the-credential-it-just-gave-the-fleet-the-rotation) this stranded the fleet: the historical *"a deploy kills it."*
**B — the reconnect follow-up mint** ~2.5 min later, which is [DRE-2614](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2614/the-console-revokes-the-credential-it-just-gave-the-fleet-the-rotation)'s *designed* revoke-then-re-point.

Today's exposure window was ~10–13 minutes, opening at new-instance boot (**before** the deploy reported success) and closing at 14:37:46. That comfortably covers every observed 100s-to-11min gap.

## Today self-healed, and that is why it is Urgent rather than an outage

[DRE-2614](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2614/the-console-revokes-the-credential-it-just-gave-the-fleet-the-rotation)'s listener is in the deployed sha `122c3b9f`, and the operator's 14:37 reconnect was followed by `14:40:18 PT fleet-sync: Dreadnought rotated — 6 repo(s) re-pointed`, matching all six repo secret timestamps at 21:40:15-18Z. **The fleet is healthy right now.** But the fan-out at 14:37:38-40 beat old-instance shutdown by **six seconds** — survival depended on the listener, not on timing, and a deploy with no reconnect after it leaves the fleet on a revoked token until someone notices.

## The smallest fix

**Seed the provider's access-token cache at construction from the vaulted bundle.** `claude_reconnect.py:692-701` already stores `access_token` and `expires_in`. A fresh instance would then serve the existing token until it genuinely nears expiry, instead of minting at boot. One small change in `ClaudeOAuthTokenProvider.__init__`; no infra change; **closes both windows A and B.**

For real multi-instance safety this also needs a **DB lease** so only one process may advance the chain. The env var cannot do that job, and today proved three owners can be live at once.

## Conclusive proof, if wanted

Redeploy the console touching nothing else and watch the six repos' `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` `updated_at`. If they move within ~60s of the new instance's boot with no human action, the deploy alone advanced the chain. **Today ran that experiment by accident and the answer was yes.**

## Two things checked and cleared

* **No active seed-reversion bug.** All four `claudeOauthRefresh*Arn` in `infra/cdk.json:18-21` are empty strings, so `CLAUDE_OAUTH_REFRESH_*` is never set on App Runner and boot always adopts the stored vault chain. That failure mode goes live the day an operator provisions any of those ARNs — worth a guard, but latent, not the cause.
* The `"provisioned Claude refresh seed changed"` line (`claude_oauth_token.py:391-396`) fires because Reconnect writes the new seed into the *running* process's `os.environ` (`claude_reconnect.py:859-862`), flipping the provider cache key so it rebuilds and mints on the next warm tick. That is the 2026-08-21 101-second kill, before the listener existed.

## Residual gap, worth its own card

In `rotation_sync_for`, *"not proven → the previous token stays in place"* is **inverted after a chain advance**: the previous token is already dead by then, so a transient 429 at that instant strands the fleet on a corpse for ~8h.

## Done when

- [ ] A fresh instance serves the vaulted token rather than minting at boot
- [ ] Only one process may advance the chain, enforced by a lease rather than an env var
- [ ] **Proof:** a console deploy with no human action leaves all six repo secret timestamps unchanged
- [ ] The `rotation_sync_for` inversion is fixed or carded

## Related

[DRE-2614](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2614/the-console-revokes-the-credential-it-just-gave-the-fleet-the-rotation) (the console revokes the credential it just gave the fleet — the listener that saved today), [DRE-2620](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2620/the-pool-failover-has-no-owner-any-console-can-move-repos-and-rewrite) (the pool failover has no owner — observed live above), [DRE-2599](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2599/one-writer-two-transports-the-fleets-credential-is-written-from-three) (one writer, two transports), [DRE-2615](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2615/the-pipeline-credential-alarm-watches-the-consoles-vault-not-what-the) (the alarm watches the vault, not what the repos present).

cards.title: A Verifier FAIL is a permanent silent deadlock — no gate arm acts on it, the fix loop cannot be triggered by it, and nothing re-runs verify
cards.description:
Found by the silent-decision census at Wave 1's close, 2026-08-23. **The worst instance of the class**: a card with critic APPROVE, green CI and a Verifier FAIL sits In QA forever, consuming a WIP slot, while the sweep reports progress every two hours and tells nobody.

Verified by reading four hops, each one correct in isolation.

## The chain

**1 · The gate decides correctly.** `bureau-pipeline/scripts/merge_gate.py:606`

```python
return Decision("hold", "latest verifier verdict is not PASS — holding"), ""
```

**2 · The workflow discards every non-merge decision.** `merge-gate.yml:390`

```bash
[ "$DECISION" = "merge" ] || exit 0
```

The `conflict` arm dispatches a fix agent; the `human` arm posts a note. `hold` **and** `wait` **produce a green run and nothing else** — no PR comment, no card comment, no label, no counter.

**3 · The fix loop cannot be triggered by it.** `agent-fix.yml:57-59` requires

```
contains(github.event.comment.body, 'VERDICT: REQUEST_CHANGES')
```

while `verify.yml:481` mandates the Verifier's first line be exactly `VERDICT: PASS` or `VERDICT: FAIL`. **A FAIL can never match.** Not a bug in either file — they were written against different vocabularies and nothing reconciles them.

**4 · Nothing re-runs verify.** Every `_nudge()` call site in `reconcile.py` (six) targets `review_workflow()` or `gate_workflow()`. `verify.yml` is dispatched by nothing, and its only triggers are `pull_request [opened, reopened, synchronize]` plus `workflow_dispatch`. No commit is ever pushed, because the fixer never runs.

## What the operator sees

Nothing. `reconcile.py:3262-3268` finds `verdict_bound(pr)` true — it reads only `"QA Critic"` comments (`merge_gate.py:231`), so the Verifier's FAIL is invisible to it — and re-nudges the gate every ~2h forever, posting:

> 🧹 Reconcile: verdict present but merge never happened — merge gate re-triggered.

**That message is the opposite of the truth.** The gate ran, decided correctly, and declined. The card counts toward `mine` in `reconcile.py:3117`, so it permanently occupies a WIP slot; the only KPI that moves is `wip_health`, whose alert action label is literally **"Raise WIP cap"** — the remedy that hides the stall.

## Two aggravating factors

**The In QA / In Review gate nudges are the only uncapped repair loop in the sweep.** Every sibling is bounded — `REQUEUE_CAP` on both dead-run paths, `DEPENDABOT_RECEIPT_CAP`, and `CRASHED_REVIEW_RETRY_CAP`, which explicitly *escalates* at the cap rather than looping (the [DRE-1921](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-1921/stop-self-inflicted-github-quota-burn-break-the-mediccritic-infra) lesson). These two nudge forever and never escalate. That is the delivery mechanism for this deadlock.

**The console cannot see it either.** `monitors/pipeline_stuck.py:319` defines `_MID_FLIGHT_STATES = ("In QA", "In Review")` and `:394-395` returns healthy from the state name **before the PR is read**, short-circuiting the needs-human, blocker, dead-run, loop and heartbeat checks. The one monitor built to answer "is this card stuck" structurally cannot fire for the two lanes closest to merge.

## Scope today

`verify.yml` is **not in the scaffold** — the 9 customer stubs have no verify — so this is agent-bureau-only. It becomes fleet-wide the moment verify is scaffolded, which makes now the cheap time to fix it.

## What to change

1. `hold` **must leave durable evidence.** The epic's own scope line: *the silent gate exits leave durable evidence, including "declined, and why."* A hold that produces a green run and no record is the canonical violation.
2. **Reconcile it with the fix loop's vocabulary** — either the Verifier emits a verdict the fixer matches, or the fixer matches FAIL. One of the two, decided and written down, not both drifting.
3. **Something must re-run verify**, or the FAIL must escalate. A verdict with no path back is the same defect as [DRE-2694](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2694/a-required-check-that-only-a-history-rewrite-can-satisfy-the-fix-loop) and [DRE-2698](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2698/the-merge-gate-cannot-recover-when-a-draft-clears-it-decides-merge) in a third location.
4. **Cap the In QA / In Review nudges** and escalate at the cap, matching `CRASHED_REVIEW_RETRY_CAP`'s already-decided behaviour.
5. `pipeline_stuck` **must not infer health from a state name** — that is `inferred-from-adjacent-signal`, the pattern [DRE-2536](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2536/the-learning-ledger-make-a-lesson-survive-as-a-test-and-measure) already set a threshold for.

## Done when

- [ ] A Verifier FAIL produces a durable record on the PR or the card, naming the verdict and that the gate declined
- [ ] The FAIL either reaches the fix loop or escalates to a human — never neither
- [ ] The In QA / In Review nudges are capped and escalate at the cap
- [ ] `pipeline_stuck` reads the PR before calling an In QA card healthy
- [ ] **Proof in production:** a PR with APPROVE + green CI + Verifier FAIL is surfaced within one sweep interval, without a human looking

## Related

[DRE-2694](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2694/a-required-check-that-only-a-history-rewrite-can-satisfy-the-fix-loop) (a required check with no repair path), [DRE-2698](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2698/the-merge-gate-cannot-recover-when-a-draft-clears-it-decides-merge) (the gate that decides merge on a draft and never looks again), [DRE-2626](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2626/a-pr-whose-blocker-is-resolved-outside-the-diff-strands-forever-the) (a review that could not re-fire), [DRE-1921](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-1921/stop-self-inflicted-github-quota-burn-break-the-mediccritic-infra) (why a retry cap escalates rather than loops), [DRE-2536](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2536/the-learning-ledger-make-a-lesson-survive-as-a-test-and-measure) (the `inferred-from-adjacent-signal` threshold).

cards.title: Four per-repo facts are maintained by hand in N places, and each guard encodes an obsolete version of its rule — derive them the way the channel roster is derived
cards.description:
Found by the silent-decision census run at Wave 1's close, 2026-08-23. Four of its thirteen verified findings are **one structural defect**, not four bugs — and the estate already solved this exact problem once, deliberately, and never extended the treatment.

## The shape

**A per-repo fact is maintained by hand in N places. Where a guard exists, it encodes the version of the rule that was current when the guard was written.** Every live repo fixed its own copy independently; nothing propagated back to the template, and the template's guard reports green while asserting the obsolete rule.

## The four instances, each verified by reading the files

**1 · The medic's watch list.** `reconcile.py` is built end to end on one promise — a red sweep exits 1 so the medic diagnoses it onto a card. Six places in that file say so in comments (`:331`, `:407`, `:1214`, `:2386`, `:2498`, `:3310`). **In four of six repos and in the scaffold,** `Reconcile` **is not in the medic's** `workflow_run` **watch list**, so no medic run is ever triggered by a red sweep.

| repo | watches `Reconcile`? | also missing |
| -- | -- | -- |
| bureau-pipeline | yes (16 entries) | — |
| portico | yes (10) | — |
| agent-bureau | **no** (8) | `Agent Fix` |
| atlas | **no** (6) | `Agent Fix`, `Verify` |
| deltasolv | **no** (6) | `Agent Fix`, `Verify` |
| agent-bureau-demo | **no** (6) | `Agent Fix`, `Verify` |
| **scaffold** | **no** (6) | `Agent Fix`, `Verify` |

`self-medic.yml:7-9` states the rule outright — *"*[DRE-2036](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2036/medic-must-watch-reconcile-agent-fix-runs-both-repos-watch-lists-the) *widened the rule: EVERY workflow that runs under its own name is watched"* — and three tests enforce it. **All three apply only to** `self-medic.yml`**.** agent-bureau's own test implements the older [DRE-2028](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2028/add-infra-ci-to-merge-gate-medic-watch-lists-with-a-ci-assertion-that) rule ("every workflow triggered by `pull_request`"), which Reconcile is not, so **its CI actively certifies the pre-**[DRE-2036](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2036/medic-must-watch-reconcile-agent-fix-runs-both-repos-watch-lists-the) **list as correct.** portico independently rediscovered the gap and fixed only itself.

**2 · The dispatch-pool secrets.** `agent-task.yml` declares 13 secrets; the scaffold's stub maps 7. The six pool names are absent, so a scaffold-built repo runs every agent on one 5,000 req/hr App bucket instead of four. The pool exists because that bucket was exhausted **twice in one day** on 2026-06-28. Live: atlas and deltasolv wired by hand; **portico and agent-bureau-demo are not wired at all** — the pool was never promoted to org level where `visibility=all` would have covered everyone. The guard, `test_stubs_map_every_canonical_secret_explicitly`, iterates a **hardcoded seven-name list** whose authority is prose in another repo's CLAUDE.md: it asks "are these seven present?", never "does this match what the reusable declares?"

**3 · The** `reconcile` **dispatch trigger.** The relay emits `repository_dispatch: [reconcile]`; the scaffold's `reconcile.yml` has only `schedule` + `workflow_dispatch`. **agent-bureau-demo is in the SSM route map and receives dispatches nothing consumes** — the [DRE-1980](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-1980/delete-the-retired-propose-gate-from-the-relay-and-make-every-stranded) shape at reduced severity, since the cron backstops it at 78–100 min drift.

**4 · Branch-protection required contexts.** `check_branch_protection.py` covers **2 of 6 repos** and compares live settings against a declared list — it never checks that a required context corresponds to a job any workflow actually publishes. So portico's [DRE-2491](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2491/ci-one-aggregate-synth-check-the-matrix-cant-drift-from-branch) fix is **installed and inert**: `synth — all accounts` exists precisely so protection can require one stable name, and protection still requires the per-account matrix legs it was built to replace. Both failure directions that card closed remain open.

## The fix already exists, one directory over

`make check-channel-fleet` computes the roster from `config/repo-map.json` and compares it live, rather than remembering it. The reason is written into `config/pipeline-channel.json` itself:

> *an enumeration of a derivable set drifts the moment the set changes*

That is exactly what all four instances are. **The channel got the treatment; the watch lists, the secret maps, the triggers and the protection contexts did not.**

## What to build

**Derive each fact from its source rather than from a hand-copied list**, and make the fleet check report it:

* **Watch lists** — derive from the set of workflows in the repo, per [DRE-2036](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2036/medic-must-watch-reconcile-agent-fix-runs-both-repos-watch-lists-the)'s rule. A workflow that runs under its own name and is unwatched is reported.
* **Secret maps** — derive the expected map from the reusable's own `on.workflow_call.secrets:` block. A stub that maps fewer than its reusable declares is reported. This replaces the hardcoded seven-name assertion, which cannot fail on a newly-added secret by construction.
* **Triggers** — derive from what the relay actually emits.
* **Protection contexts** — cross-check each required context against the jobs the repo's workflows publish, in **both** directions: a required context no job publishes (portico's stale `synth — vericorr` blocked PR #318 with eleven green checks), and a job that should be required and is not (silent, and worse).

Extend `make check-channel-fleet`, or build its sibling. It already reads every repo live and already knows the roster.

## Done when

- [ ] Each of the four facts is computed from its source, not from a list someone maintains
- [ ] The fleet check reports drift on all four, per repo, the way it reports channel drift today
- [ ] The scaffold's copies are regenerated from the same derivation, so a new repo cannot be born behind
- [ ] A guard that asserts a floor rather than completeness is replaced, not extended — the seven-name secret assertion is the worked example
- [ ] The four live gaps above are closed as a consequence, not as four separate patches

## Why size L

Four derivations plus a fleet-check surface. It could be split, but splitting invites exactly the per-instance patching that created the problem — each repo has already been fixed once by hand.

## Related

[DRE-2699](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2699/the-scaffold-ships-a-file-no-lint-here-ever-reads-the-strictest) (the same lesson, first sighting: the scaffold ships a file no lint here reads), [DRE-2605](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2605/which-repos-still-ride-main-is-computed-from-the-roster-not-remembered) (which established derive-don't-remember for the channel roster), [DRE-2036](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2036/medic-must-watch-reconcile-agent-fix-runs-both-repos-watch-lists-the) (the widened medic rule that never propagated), [DRE-2491](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2491/ci-one-aggregate-synth-check-the-matrix-cant-drift-from-branch) (portico's protection fix, installed and inert), [DRE-2131](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2131/onboarding-template-defects-demo-stubs-use-secrets-inherit-drops) (why the scaffold maps secrets explicitly), [DRE-2013](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2013/dispatch-pool-selection-agent-task-token-mint-picks-the-app-with-most) (the dispatch pool).

cards.title: The merge gate cannot recover when a draft clears — it decides merge, GitHub refuses, and nothing ever looks again
cards.description:
**Measured live, 2026-08-23.** `DeltaSolv/deltasolv#214` sat green, approved and mergeable while nothing was coming for it. The gate had already run, already decided, and already given up.

From merge-gate run `32659878117` at 19:02 PT:

```
decision=merge
GraphQL: Pull Request is still a draft (mergePullRequest)
##[error]Process completed with exit code 1
```

The PR was marked ready **after** that run. It then sat idle, CLEAN and MERGEABLE, with all four checks green and a critic APPROVE, until a human noticed it on the board.

## Why it never recovers

The stub's triggers (`deltasolv/.github/workflows/merge-gate.yml`, and the same shape fleet-wide):

```yaml
on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [CI, QA Review]
    types: [completed]
  issue_comment:
    types: [created]
  workflow_dispatch:
```

**There is no** `pull_request` **trigger at all**, so `ready_for_review` fires nothing. A PR whose *only* change is the draft flag clearing has no path back into the gate: CI does not re-run, no comment is posted, and the gate never looks again.

This is deterministic, not a race. **Any PR that is drafted, approved, then readied lands here every time** and stays until a human intervenes.

## Three distinct defects, and they need separating

**1. The gate evaluates a draft and then errors.** It computed `decision=merge` on a PR it could not possibly merge, then took a hard API failure. A draft is an author's explicit hold — the gate should recognise it *before* deciding and decline with a stated reason.

**2. The failure renders as a broken gate.** A red merge-gate run reads as "the machinery is broken," not "this PR is deliberately held." Anyone triaging that run learns the wrong thing. This is precisely the scope line in this epic — *the silent gate exits leave durable evidence, including "declined, and why."* Today the evidence exists only as a stack trace in a log nobody opens.

**3. Nothing re-evaluates on un-draft.** Even with (1) and (2) fixed, the PR still needs something to look again when the hold clears.

## Fleet-wide, and one repo is worse

`workflow_dispatch` is the sanctioned manual re-trigger and it worked here — `gh workflow run merge-gate.yml -f pr_number=214`.

**CORRECTION, 2026-08-23.** This card first claimed bureau-pipeline's own gate had no `workflow_dispatch` and was therefore the least recoverable repo in the fleet. **That is false.** `self-merge-gate.yml` declares `workflow_dispatch` with a `pr_number` input, exactly like the consumer stubs, and dispatching it on #178 worked first time.

The error came from naming the wrong file: `gh workflow run merge-gate.yml --repo dreadnought-foundry/bureau-pipeline` returns HTTP 422, because in that repo `merge-gate.yml` is the **reusable workflow consumers call** — it has no dispatch trigger and is not meant to. The repo's own stub is `self-merge-gate.yml`, one of eight `self-*.yml` files. A 422 was read as "this repo cannot be nudged" when it meant "that is not the stub."

Worth keeping, because it is a trap the next person will hit: **bureau-pipeline holds both halves — the reusables every consumer calls, and its own** `self-*` **stubs that call them.** Same names, opposite roles. Any tooling that dispatches by workflow filename must pick the `self-` prefixed one here and the bare one everywhere else.

## Why this is not "just don't use drafts"

Drafts are the **sanctioned mechanism** for holding a PR in an ordered sequence, and the release-channel rollout depends on them: #343 → #214 → #178 had to merge in that order, and the draft flag is what enforced it. The pattern is correct. A gate that cannot recover when a deliberate hold clears is a gap in the design, not a consequence of misuse.

## Relationship to the console defect

[DRE-2538](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2538/the-merge-button-is-offered-while-the-gate-runs-and-while-the-verifier) is the **console** half — it offers an active Merge button on a draft PR, which either errors or silently defeats the hold. This is the **gate** half, and it is worse in one specific way: the console merely offers a button that fails; **the gate stops trying altogether, with no surface saying so.**

Both were sighted on the same PRs on the same day. Filed separately because the fixes live in different repos and neither implies the other.

## What to change

1. **Check draft state before deciding.** A draft yields a stated decline — `decision=held-as-draft` — not `decision=merge` followed by an API error. Not a failure; a recorded, non-red outcome.
2. **The decline reaches the card and the PR**, so "held as a draft" is visible where someone looks, rather than only in a run log.
3. **Re-evaluate when the hold clears.** Either add `pull_request: [ready_for_review]` to the stubs, or have the reconcile sweep pick up a PR that is non-draft, mergeable, approved, and has had no gate run since it was readied. The sweep route covers more cases and needs no fleet-wide stub edit — decide deliberately and record which and why.
4. **Give** `self-merge-gate.yml` **a** `workflow_dispatch` **trigger** so the repo that gates the fleet is at least as recoverable as its consumers.

## Done when

- [ ] A draft PR produces a stated, non-red gate outcome naming the hold — never `decision=merge` followed by a refusal
- [ ] The hold is visible on the PR or the card, not only in a run log
- [ ] A PR readied after approval is re-evaluated with no human action, proven on a real PR
- [ ] `self-merge-gate.yml` can be re-triggered manually
- [ ] **Proof in production:** draft a PR, let it go green and be approved, mark it ready, and observe it merge with no dispatch and no comment

## Related

[DRE-2538](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2538/the-merge-button-is-offered-while-the-gate-runs-and-while-the-verifier) (the console half, same PRs same day), [DRE-2682](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2682/wave-15-phase-3-the-promoter-and-the-relay-must-obey-the-verdict-today) (Wave 1.5 Phase 3 — this is **case D** in that card's escape-route census, where a forgotten draft and a deliberate hold are indistinguishable; that census covered the observability side, this covers the gate that stops acting), [DRE-2626](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2626/a-pr-whose-blocker-is-resolved-outside-the-diff-strands-forever-the) (a review that could not re-fire — same family: a correct verdict with no available recovery).

cards.title: A repo's pipeline config is set once at birth and never re-derived — the scaffold gets fleet decisions, the repos never do
cards.description:
**Operator, 2026-08-23:** *"We need to create these projects not by hand, but by a configuration, so we get this always right."*

Found by atlas refusing to be repointed — and being right to refuse.

## The evidence, in one comparison

`scaffold/customer-repo/.github/workflows/` — what a repo created **today** is born with, verified 2026-08-23:

```yaml
uses: dreadnought-foundry/bureau-pipeline/.github/workflows/agent-task.yml@stable
with:
  pipeline_ref: stable
```

`EveryBite/atlas` — created earlier, configured by hand — carries a **test forbidding exactly that**:

> *"The tag release channel is retired (operator decision, 2026-08-07): every stub's* `uses:` *ref must point at @main and no stub may pass* `pipeline_ref`*."*

Both are faithful records. They record **decisions twelve days apart** pointing opposite ways, and only the newer one reached the template.

## The actual defect

**A repo's pipeline configuration is written once, at creation, and never derived again.** The scaffold is a starting point, not a source of truth. So:

* a fleet decision updates the template and reaches **only repos created after it**
* every existing repo needs a hand pass, which is how they drift
* nothing detects the drift, because each repo is internally consistent — atlas's stubs and atlas's tests agree with each other perfectly

`make check-channel-fleet` compares each repo's refs against a declaration we maintain. **It cannot see that atlas holds a test asserting the opposite**, because that is inside the repo and outside the roster's model.

## Why per-repo passes will not fix it

This is the second time this class has cost real work today. [DRE-2605](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2605/which-repos-still-ride-main-is-computed-from-the-roster-not-remembered) already established the principle for the channel: *which repos ride which ref is computed from the roster, never remembered in prose*. That fixed the **record**. This is the same failure one layer down — the **configuration itself** is remembered per repo rather than derived.

A repoint pass gets the fleet consistent on the day it runs. The next fleet decision starts the drift again, and the pass has to be rediscovered along with whatever guards the repos have grown in between.

## What "configuration-driven" has to mean to be worth building

Not a better scaffold — the scaffold is already correct. The properties that matter:

1. **Derivable, not copied.** A repo's pipeline config is generated from central configuration, so a fleet decision changes one place.
2. **Drift is detectable.** A repo whose live config differs from what the configuration says it should be is reported — including a repo carrying a *guard* that contradicts it, which today is invisible.
3. **A repo may deliberately differ, and must say so.** `bureau-pipeline` legitimately stays on `@main` and is declared in `config/pipeline-channel.json` with its reason; `bureau-harness` is exempt by design. Divergence is not the enemy — **undeclared** divergence is.
4. **Re-derivation is safe to run repeatedly.** If it can only be run once, it is a scaffold with extra steps.

## The hard part, which should be decided before building

**A repo's tests can contradict the central configuration**, and atlas proves this is not hypothetical. Re-deriving config without touching a guard produces a repo whose CI fails; re-deriving it *and* rewriting the guard silently discards whatever incident put it there.

So the design has to answer: **what happens when generated configuration meets a repo-local assertion that forbids it?** The wrong answer is "the generator wins" — that deletes recorded decisions. A plausible right answer is that the mismatch is surfaced as a decision for a human, and the generator refuses until it is resolved. That is a genuine design question, not an implementation detail.

## Done when

* A repo's pipeline configuration can be regenerated from central configuration, repeatedly, without a hand pass.
* A repo whose live configuration diverges from the declared intent is reported — including divergence expressed as a repo-local test.
* Deliberate divergence is declarable, with its reason, and does not read as drift.
* A generated change that would contradict a repo-local guard **stops and asks**, and cannot silently rewrite it.

## Related

[DRE-2677](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2677/repoint-atlas-onto-the-stable-release-channel-both-halves-in-one-edit) (atlas, on hold — the instance), [DRE-2669](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2669/four-customer-repos-still-ride-main-and-pipeline-ref-is-still-optional) (the repoint pass this makes unnecessary next time), [DRE-2605](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2605/which-repos-still-ride-main-is-computed-from-the-roster-not-remembered) (computed, not remembered — same principle, one layer up), [DRE-2553](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2553/step-4-pin-agent-bureau-and-bureau-pipeline-to-the-channel-and-fold) (the channel), and `architecture/new-project-playbook.md` §2, which is the hand procedure this would replace.

cards.title: Move the VeriCorr Claude account under Dreadnought — do it while it bills nothing, which is now
cards.description:
**Operator decision, 2026-08-23:** the VeriCorr Claude account moves under Dreadnought as `<redacted-email>`, so the whole team sits on one Dreadnought team plan and can share artifacts.

This card is about **when**, because the window matters more than the mechanics.

## Why now is unusually good, and why that expires

The account's last production duty was removed hours ago. [DRE-2672](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2672/retire-vericorr-from-the-agent-fleet-remove-the-route-keep-the-claude) retired the `vericorr` repo from the fleet and removed `repo_accounts["vericorr"]`, so **the account currently bills no repo.** Its only remaining role is standby capacity in the failover pool.

An account with no repos is the cheapest thing in this system to disturb. Once it acquires a repo again — or once a failover points work at it — the same move costs a live outage.

**The window is open because we just opened it. It closes the moment the pool fails over to this account.**

## What the move actually is, mechanically

It is a **Reconnect plus a rename**, and the Reconnect half is the dangerous half. Moving an account to a different organisation means re-authenticating, which mints a new OAuth chain. Everything today taught about that applies:

* A mint **revokes the access token issued alongside the previous refresh link**. Any agent run holding the old token dies mid-sentence — on 2026-08-22 that cost a run 23 turns and $1.82 in ([DRE-2659](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2659/the-root-cause-bureau-fleet-owner-is-an-env-var-and-a-rolling-deploy)).
* The console's own stored pool credential for an account is written **only** by Reconnect (`claude_reconnect.py:699-701`). So the move will repair that binding rather than break it — but only if the Reconnect completes.
* App Runner's rolling deploy briefly runs **two backend instances that both claim fleet ownership** ([DRE-2659](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2659/the-root-cause-bureau-fleet-owner-is-an-env-var-and-a-rolling-deploy), open). **Do not do this during a console deploy**, or two processes will mint on the same chain three minutes apart.

## The window

Pick a moment with **no agent runs in flight and no console deploy**. Concretely:

1. `gh run list` across the roster shows no `agent-task` / `qa-review` / `agent-fix` in progress
2. No App Runner deployment in progress
3. Then: move the account, Reconnect, and watch the fan-out reach all repos in the routing map

## After the move — verify, do not assume

* The fan-out wrote every repo in `config/repo-map.json` within seconds of each other (a split fan-out is the dangerous state, not a slow one)
* `console/backend/claude-accounts.json` reflects the new identity — the account entry still carries `<redacted-email>`
* The account still appears as a **failover target** in the pool, since that is now its whole job
* One real agent run completes afterwards. A green check means the workflow ran; a completed card means the credential works

## Two things this unlocks, worth stating

**Shared artifacts.** The reason for the move. Worth noting alongside [DRE-2673](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2673/the-wave-rooms-footer-names-a-generator-that-has-never-existed-twice)'s wave-room generator: that work makes the programme board reproducible from the repo so it never depends on an artifact URL. This makes artifacts *shareable* when we choose to publish one. Both are wanted — the generator is the source of truth, an artifact is a presentation of it.

**One billing pool.** The team plan simplifies the account roster the pool reasons about.

## Done when

* The account is `<redacted-email>` under Dreadnought
* The fan-out reached every roster repo in one window
* One agent run has completed on the new credential — observed, not merely green
* No run was killed by the move, or if one was, it was expected and requeued

## Related

[DRE-2672](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2672/retire-vericorr-from-the-agent-fleet-remove-the-route-keep-the-claude) (retired the repo, which opened this window), [DRE-2659](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2659/the-root-cause-bureau-fleet-owner-is-an-env-var-and-a-rolling-deploy) (two instances mint on one chain — do not deploy during this), [DRE-2660](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2660/a-chain-rotation-kills-the-consoles-own-stored-pool-credential-and) (a rotation kills the console's stored pool credential), [DRE-2614](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2614/the-console-revokes-the-credential-it-just-gave-the-fleet-the-rotation) (the ownership flag).

cards.title: [WAVE 1.5] The intake gate — a card is proven before it is work
cards.description:
**Wave 1.5 of the Bureau: Unattended Operation programme.** Sits between Wave 1 and Wave 2 because every later wave consumes cards, and a layer that cannot trust its input cannot be fixed from above.

**Status: APPROVED 2026-08-23. Scope EXPANDED 2026-08-25** at the operator's direction, after a working session that revised the design substantially. The plan of record is `architecture/wave-plans/wave-1.5-the-intake-gate.md`; the CEO-facing artifact is [https://claude.ai/code/artifact/b7030053-45ab-40b9-9aee-7b370b45c6cd](<https://claude.ai/code/artifact/b7030053-45ab-40b9-9aee-7b370b45c6cd>) — read those, not this summary.

## Why the scope grew, and why that is not scope creep

The original wave was one gate: examine a card before it reaches Backlog. Working through it produced a design that is **larger but not looser** — and the parts are coupled, not merely related.

An Intake lane with nothing consuming it is a holding pen. A guard that bounces cards has nowhere to bounce them to without Intake. A Green Light lane with no artifact template in it is a rename. And Planning cannot produce an artifact at all, because **no agent in this fleet can search the web** — `plan.yml:206` grants `Bash, Edit, Write, Read, Glob, Grep`, and so do the other eight invocations.

**Ship a third of this and the system is worse than before**: cards get bounced into a lane nothing grooms. That is the intermediate state the wave has to avoid, and it is why the cut is drawn around the coupled core rather than at a card count.

## The shape

```
any idea, any shape → INTAKE → PLANNING ─┬─ epic → artifact → critic → GREEN LIGHT → critic → BACKLOG
                                          └─ one-off → structural check ────────────────────→ BACKLOG
```

**One path in.** Everything goes to Planning, which decides epic or one-off — no separate sizing agent, one path to harden. A one-off gets a structural check and goes straight to Backlog, **never reaching the CEO**; otherwise a one-line fix waits on a green light and we have rebuilt the bottleneck one lane earlier.

**Two critics, different questions.** The first asks whether the plan is fit to take the CEO's time. The second runs *after* approval, against a frozen plan, and asks what is missing. An adversarial pass is only sharp against a fixed target. How often the second sends a plan back measures how good the first is.

**The rule the wave comes down to:** a card without a verdict cannot rest in Backlog or Todo, and a child cannot move without its epic. Both are checks on the *card*, not on who moved it — Linear has no per-lane permission, so any rule about *who* is unenforceable.

## In scope

 1. **Intake** — the lane, and every writer pointed at it.
 2. **Planning as the single route** — the epic/one-off branch and the structural check.
 3. **The artifact template** — business case, KPIs *as structured data*, risk assessment, outcome, visual model, cards, proof-and-demo plan.
 4. **Two critics** — pre-review and post-approval, with a bound of two rounds each.
 5. **Green Light** — `Plan Review` renamed. **Must ship with the escalation move**: `reconcile.py:623` and `lambda_function.py:576` hardcode the string `"Plan Review"` for the escalation meaning, so renaming first orphans both.
 6. **Triage repurposed** — the lane for a broken card, taking the escalations Green Light should never have held. Alerts leave Linear for the console.
 7. **The guard** — verdict clause and epic clause, enforced by moving the card back to Intake.
 8. **Routing verdicts** — FLEET / WORKBENCH / OPERATOR / PARKED / NEEDS WORK, read from what the acceptance criteria actually require.
 9. **The planner's tooling** — web search and fetch ([DRE-2712](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2712/give-the-planner-and-the-critic-web-search-in-the-same-change-never)), plus a publish path for the artifact.
10. **Releases** — [DRE-2710](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2710/operator-turn-linear-releases-on-one-continuous-pipeline-for-agent), [DRE-2711](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2711/split-merged-from-done-a-release-closes-the-card-not-the-merge). Separable, already carded, and cheap now the plan is upgraded.
11. **Proof and demo per epic** — a convention plus the card shape that carries it.
12. **The contract as data** — lane entrance/exit/writers in one file, asserted by the harness. Retire `In Design Review` and fold `In QA` into `In Review`.

## Explicitly deferred, and this list is the discipline

* **Workbench sub-routing by agent** — which of the four agents owns a card.
* **Operator-first batch ordering** — unblocking operator work at the front of a batch.
* **Cross-epic collision detection** — folded into the second critic later, not built now.
* **The groomer as a separate agent** — its jobs redistribute; revisit if collisions start reaching Backlog.

All four are downstream of Backlog and unvalidatable until the front runs. Several exist to catch problems better planning prevents, so some may never be needed.

## The test case is real, and it was designed as one

**Portico's Forms card set. **[DRE-2649](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2649/critic-review-the-whole-forms-card-set-before-any-of-it-starts) is an independent adversarial review of exactly that set — 482 lines, merged as portico PR #340 — and its per-card judgments are **deliberately unread**, held back as the validation set. Run the new intake over the set and compare. Agreement is evidence; disagreement is a finding either way. One dimension is contaminated and excluded by name: the reviewer's `hand-built` finding was quoted during planning.

## KPIs predicted, before the work

| KPI | Baseline | Prediction |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 9 · Board honesty — cards >24h in a non-terminal lane | 120 (2026-08-18 20:30 PT) | **Worsens first, then improves** — Intake absorbs before it drains |
| 1 · Walk-away rate | not re-measured | Improve |
| 2 · Cards stalled >6h with nothing surfacing why | not re-measured | Improve |
| 8 · Wasted inference | not re-measured | Improve — [DRE-2695](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2695/the-console-signs-you-out-every-hour-cognito-issues-a-30-day-refresh) burned two runs on a card that could not close |
| New · dispatch-to-escalation rate | none | **Baseline captured** |

## Exit

- [ ] A card created by hand in any lane is observed arriving in Intake, from its own state history
- [ ] A one-off is observed reaching Backlog without passing through Green Light
- [ ] An epic's artifact is reviewed and sent back at least once — the loop works in both directions
- [ ] A card dragged into Backlog without a verdict is observed being returned
- [ ] The Portico comparison is run and scored against [DRE-2649](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2649/critic-review-the-whole-forms-card-set-before-any-of-it-starts), either way
- [ ] Every KPI above is re-measured and the prediction marked right or wrong

## Amendment log

**2026-08-25 — scope expanded.** Added Planning-as-single-route, the artifact template, the second critic, Green Light, Triage's new job, the planner's tooling, Releases, proof-and-demo, and the contract-as-data. Withdrawn: the `Merged` lane (a release records merged-but-not-live already, and a lane would jam the dependency gate). Corrected: `Planning` is kept, not retired — it was unwired, not dead; and UI can go to the fleet, because `Read` renders images in `claude-code-action` and the critic is handed screenshots today.

cards.title: Three pool alert kinds are unclassified, so a WARN saying "nothing to do" arrives as HIGH
cards.description:
**Three pool alert kinds have no category, so a warning that says "there is nothing for you to do" lands in the needs-a-human queue looking exactly like an emergency.**

`claude_pool_failover:*`, `claude_pool_credential_refused` and `claude_pool_exhausted` are not registered in `alerts_v2._SYSTEM_CATEGORY`. They fall through to the `NEEDS_HUMAN` default, and `urgency_for` in `console/backend/alerts_v2.py` gives that category a fixed HIGH — the urgency is not derived from the alert's severity at all.

During the 2026-08-22 incident the operator saw three HIGH "needs a human" rows. One of them was a WARN whose own body said no action was needed. Nothing on the screen distinguished it from the one that genuinely required a click.

## Why this matters

An alert panel where a warning and an emergency look identical trains the reader to ignore both. That costs more than having no panel, because it also spends the trust the real alerts depend on.

## The decision this card records: do not suppress alerts during a deploy

The tempting fix is to mute pool alerts while a rollout is in progress. **We are not doing that.** Suppression during a deploy is precisely how a failure caused by a deploy goes unseen — and the 2026-08-22 failure was caused by a deploy. The fix is severity classification, plus removing the cause, which is [DRE-2659](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2659/the-root-cause-bureau-fleet-owner-is-an-env-var-and-a-rolling-deploy) (the rolling-deploy chain-owner race).

## Fix direction — do not implement from this card

Register the three kinds under a real category (CLAUDE_ACCOUNT), and make `urgency_for` read the alert's severity instead of returning a constant per category.

While in there, check whether other categories carry the same fixed-urgency shape. That is an expectation, not something measured on the day — say what you find either way.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A WARN pool alert does not render at the same urgency as a CRITICAL one
- [ ] The three named kinds no longer fall through to the NEEDS_HUMAN default
- [ ] No alert is suppressed on the grounds that a deploy is in progress

cards.title: A medic retry pulled a card out of the CEO's queue 21 seconds after an agent parked it there
cards.description:
**A delayed medic retry pulled a card out of the CEO's queue 21 seconds after an agent had parked it there.**

On 2026-08-22 at 16:43:36 PT the successful run on [DRE-2649](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2649/critic-review-the-whole-forms-card-set-before-any-of-it-starts) finished a 14-finding adversarial review, escalated a genuine A-vs-B product decision, and moved the card to **Plan Review** — the "needs you" lane. At 16:43:57 PT, twenty-one seconds later, a medic retry started and moved it back to In Progress, where it re-did the review that had just completed. [DRE-2649](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2649/critic-review-the-whole-forms-card-set-before-any-of-it-starts)'s own Linear state history records both transitions:

```
Plan Review    2026-08-22T23:43:36Z → 23:43:57Z
In Progress    2026-08-22T23:43:57Z → 2026-08-23T00:17:39Z
```

That retry was dispatched at 16:28:57 PT — fifteen minutes before it ran. It sat queued behind the per-card lock while the original run was still working. By the time it acquired the lock, the failure it was retrying had already been resolved by the run holding it.

## Why this matters

The escalation left the queue it was addressed to. A decision the CEO was asked to own became invisible to him, while a second agent spent tokens repeating finished work. The whole escalate-by-exception contract rests on Plan Review being sticky once an agent puts a card there; if automation can quietly undo it, an agent asking a question is not reliably heard.

## Fix direction — do not implement from this card

Before a retry moves a card or begins work, it must answer one question: am I still this card's current run? A superseded run defers rather than acting.

Respect the existing bounds. [DRE-2024](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2024/reconcile-re-dispatches-a-doomed-agent-fix-every-sweep-for-a-needs) (reconcile re-dispatching a doomed fix every sweep) and [DRE-2032](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2032/reconciles-dead-run-requeue-kills-live-builds-no-pr-after-45min-reads) (a redispatch that cancels a live build through the concurrency group) are the two failure modes any new check must not reintroduce — a genuinely stuck card must still be retried, and a live run must not be cancelled.

Whether the right marker is the [DRE-2032](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2032/reconciles-dead-run-requeue-kills-live-builds-no-pr-after-45min-reads) run receipt or the card's own state history is a design question this card does not settle.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A queued retry that acquires its lock after a newer run has finished does not move the card or start work
- [ ] A card an agent parked in Plan Review is not moved out of it by any automated retry
- [ ] [DRE-2024](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2024/reconcile-re-dispatches-a-doomed-agent-fix-every-sweep-for-a-needs) and [DRE-2032](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2032/reconciles-dead-run-requeue-kills-live-builds-no-pr-after-45min-reads) behaviours both still hold — genuinely stuck cards are still retried, live runs are still not cancelled

cards.title: The root cause: BUREAU_FLEET_OWNER is an env var, and a rolling deploy hands it to two processes at once
cards.description:
`BUREAU_FLEET_OWNER=1` **is an environment variable, so a rolling deploy hands it to two processes at once. This is the root cause of the 2026-08-22 incident.** Everything else that went wrong that afternoon — a paid agent run killed mid-flight, a spurious account failover, a 38-minute refusal loop — followed from two console instances both believing they were the fleet's sole credential owner.

[DRE-2614](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2614/the-console-revokes-the-credential-it-just-gave-the-fleet-the-rotation) established the rule ("only one process may hold the chain") and [DRE-2620](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2620/the-pool-failover-has-no-owner-any-console-can-move-repos-and-rewrite) gave the failover an owner. Both enforced it with this env flag, and [DRE-2614](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2614/the-console-revokes-the-credential-it-just-gave-the-fleet-the-rotation)'s own body says what the flag was designed for: *"Off by default, so a laptop copy is inert."* That solves the wrong-machine problem. It cannot solve two instances of the same service, because App Runner deliberately runs the old and the new instance side by side during every rollout, and both read the same environment.

## Measured, 2026-08-22 (all times PT)

Console v1.5.54 deployed.

| Time | Event | Evidence |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 16:25:01 | instance `7c21af96` starts while `f5e92000` is still serving | CloudWatch log-stream creation times |
| 16:25:14 | `7c21af96` refreshes the shared VeriCorr login: `fleet-sync: VeriCorr rotated — 7 repo(s) re-pointed.` | CloudWatch, verbatim |
| 16:26:18 | portico agent run `32605217460` starts and picks up that token | `gh api` |
| 16:26:58 | old instance `f5e92000` can no longer authenticate as VeriCorr, concludes the account is dead, and moves a repo: `claude-pool: vericorr now bills EveryBite (was VeriCorr, failover)` | CloudWatch, verbatim |
| 16:28:32–38 | a SECOND chain refresh, 3.4 minutes after the first, writes a new token to all 7 repos | `gh secret list` updatedAt |
| 16:28:34 | portico's in-flight run dies: `401 OAuth access token has been revoked` — after 23 turns, 99.5s, **$1.82 spent** | `gh run view 32605217460 --attempt 1 --log`, verbatim |
| 16:28:41 | a fresh run is dispatched and succeeds 15 minutes later | `gh run view` |

Two chain mints 3.4 minutes apart, from instances with overlapping lifetimes, both emitting owner-gated log lines. VeriCorr's account was never unhealthy — it sat at 20% of its 5-hour cap throughout.

## Why this matters

Every deploy can revoke the token its own in-flight agents are holding, kill paid work mid-run, and trigger a failover on a perfectly healthy account. **This recurs on every deploy** — it is not a one-off. On 2026-08-22 it cost $1.82 and 15 minutes on a single card. A deploy landing in the middle of a busy overnight run costs proportionally more, and the failover it triggers moves billing to an account nobody chose.

## Fix direction — do not implement from this card

A lease held in the database, carrying an owner id and an expiry, so exactly one process holds the chain regardless of how many are running.

Two honest constraints. The console's own database is the natural store, so this needs no new dependency. And the lease must be reclaimable if an instance dies without releasing it — otherwise a crashed instance freezes the fleet's credential until a human intervenes, which trades one outage shape for another.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A rolling deploy with two live instances mints exactly one chain — proven with overlapping instances, not a single-process test
- [ ] An instance that dies holding the lease does not block the next owner indefinitely
- [ ] A non-owner process still cannot advance the chain — the [DRE-2614](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2614/the-console-revokes-the-credential-it-just-gave-the-fleet-the-rotation) property does not regress

cards.title: A branch that names no card gets no signal for 120 minutes — today a PR opened and merged in under 13
cards.description:
When a pull request opens on a branch that names no card, nothing says so for 120 minutes. Today a PR opened and merged in under 13, so the one signal we have never fired.

## What happened, 2026-08-22

Portico PR **#337** ([DRE-2495](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2495/the-external-document-screen-open-in-a-new-tab-and-say-who-controls)) opened **4:25:38 PM PT** on branch `ui/forms-spec` and merged **4:38:17 PM PT**. Open for 12 minutes 39 seconds.

Because the branch is not `agent/DRE-<n>-<slug>`, `linear-sync` could not read a card id out of it, so the card sat In Review after its PR merged. On the way in, the PR also got no merge gate and no fix agent.

The watchdog built for exactly this, `flag_unowned_prs` ([DRE-2426](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2426/branch-ownership-is-hand-copied-eight-times-so-the-sweep-that-finds)), works. It simply was not due: `UNOWNED_MINUTES = 120` at `reconcile.py:1701`. It was outrun by about 107 minutes.

## The 120 minutes is not sloppiness — do not shorten it

[DRE-2610](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2610/retracted-the-unowned-branch-watchdog-works-it-was-inside-its-120) is a **retracted** card, filed against this same watchdog by someone who had not realised it was inside its quiet window. The window is there so the watchdog does not cry wolf on a branch that is seconds away from becoming a proper PR. Tightening it is the change that gets this mechanism muted, and a muted watchdog is worse than a late one.

## A second instance, the same day

Portico PR **#338** is titled *"Write down the branch rule that cost* [DRE-2495](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2495/the-external-document-screen-open-in-a-new-tab-and-say-who-controls) *its auto-Done"*. It is on branch `docs/forms-plan-branch-rule`, and it is sitting unmerged waiting for a human. A pull request documenting the branch rule, blocked by the branch rule.

## Where this sits against the cards that already exist

Saying this out loud, because the boundary is the whole point and one of these cards made the opposite call deliberately.

| Card | Covers | State |
| -- | -- | -- |
| [DRE-2423](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2423/a-card-carrying-pr-on-a-misnamed-branch-opts-out-of-the-whole-pipeline) | branch names a card **out of position** (`feat/DRE-2419-…`) | Backlog |
| [DRE-2611](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2611/a-branch-that-looks-carded-is-never-verified-pipeline-owns-is-a-prefix) | branch **looks** carded; nothing resolves the card | Backlog |
| this card | branch names **no card at all** | — |

[DRE-2423](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2423/a-card-carrying-pr-on-a-misnamed-branch-opts-out-of-the-whole-pipeline) chose silence for the third case on purpose: *"a genuinely cardless branch is a legitimate choice, not a mistake — silence there."* [DRE-2495](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2495/the-external-document-screen-open-in-a-new-tab-and-say-who-controls) is the evidence that revisits that choice. `ui/forms-spec` names no card and **had** one. Cardless-looking is not the same as cardless, and the cost of the silence was a card left open and three gates skipped.

## The card gate cannot cover this

`validate_card.py` runs at Todo and checks card **content** — the repo label, the agent label, the initiative. The branch does not exist at that moment. This is a structural gap, not a broken gate.

## Fix direction

Signal when the PR opens, not on a timer. One comment or one status saying the branch names no card, and naming what it therefore does not get: no merge gate, no fix agent, no automatic Done. Keep `UNOWNED_MINUTES = 120` for escalation. What costs us is the silence in the first two hours, not the escalation after them.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Red first: a PR opened on a branch carrying no `DRE-<n>` anywhere in its name gets exactly one notice at open, naming all three gates it does not get.
- [ ] A correctly named `agent/DRE-<n>-<slug>` branch gets no notice.
- [ ] Re-running on the same PR posts no second notice — idempotent on the comment record, the shape merge-gate's `human` arm already uses.
- [ ] The notice never blocks a merge and never changes the PR's checks; pinned by a test.
- [ ] A PR that opens and merges inside 13 minutes still receives the notice — the PR #337 timing is the fixture.
- [ ] `UNOWNED_MINUTES` stays 120, and a test asserts the escalation path still exists.
- [ ] If this ships as one check alongside [DRE-2423](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2423/a-card-carrying-pr-on-a-misnamed-branch-opts-out-of-the-whole-pipeline)'s, the PR says so and says which card owns which trigger.

cards.title: bureau-harness sits outside the credential fan-out and its token is 32 days old — establish whether the repo that gates the channel can still run
cards.description:
We do not know whether `bureau-harness` can still run. Its Claude credential is 32 days old, today's fleet re-issue skipped it, and it is the repo that proves a commit before the release channel advances. This card establishes the answer. It does not assume one.

## Evidence, 2026-08-22

* Today's credential re-issue wrote all **7** repos listed in `config/repo-map.json` inside a 6-second window, **4:28:32–4:28:38 PM PT**.
* `bureau-harness` is not in `config/repo-map.json`, so it received nothing.
* Its own `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` is dated **2026-07-20 17:45 PT** — 32 days stale.

## Why this repo and not any other

`bureau-harness` is what proves a commit before `promote-channel.yml` advances the `stable` tag ([DRE-2551](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2551/step-2-the-harnesss-green-verdict-moves-the-tag-so-no-human-is-in-the)). It rides `@main` on purpose: pinning it to the channel it validates would make promotion self-validating. That is why it sits in `config/pipeline-channel.json` under `not_in_the_roster` rather than in the roster `make check-channel-fleet` reads ([DRE-2605](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2605/which-repos-still-ride-main-is-computed-from-the-roster-not-remembered)).

Being outside the **channel roster** is a decision. Being outside the **credential fan-out** may just be an oversight that inherited the same shape. Those are different lists, and nothing today says which one this is.

## The bad case

If today's re-issue invalidated prior tokens, the harness's next real run dies with the `is_error, 1 turn, $0` signature and channel promotion stops. Wave 1's remaining work repoints four customer repos onto that channel, so a channel that has quietly stopped advancing is exactly the state we are about to make more repos depend on.

## What we already have, and what it does not tell us

[DRE-2552](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2552/step-3-alarm-when-the-channel-goes-quiet-the-one-signal-whose-absence) shipped an alarm for a channel that has stopped moving, so a stall is **not** silent — do not write this card up as if nothing would notice. But that alarm fires after the fact and says nothing about the cause. A dead harness credential would present as "the channel went quiet," with no pointer to the credential. That is a slower and more confusing route to the same repair.

## Status: unproven in either direction

Nothing has exercised the harness recently. "The token is dead" and "the token is fine" are both currently unsupported. Token age is not evidence of revocation, and a clean `make cred-doctor` is not evidence a credential works — its `token-live` link skips unless you hand it the value.

## The question this card must answer

Does `bureau-harness` still hold a working Claude credential — and if not, does it belong in the fan-out, or deliberately outside it with its own refresh path and a named owner?

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The harness credential is exercised against its real dependency and the result recorded — a live check with the captured output, not a reading of the token's age.
- [ ] The finding is written down either way, with the command run and what it returned.
- [ ] A decision is recorded: `bureau-harness` joins the fan-out, or stays outside it with a named refresh path and a named owner. "Outside by accident" is not one of the options.
- [ ] Whichever is chosen is derivable from a file rather than remembered in prose — the same correction [DRE-2605](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2605/which-repos-still-ride-main-is-computed-from-the-roster-not-remembered) made for the channel roster.
- [ ] If the credential is dead, it is repaired and the harness is shown running green before this card closes.
