cards.title: The "pending release" panel answers "what is deployed" by asking "what was tagged last" — and on a rollback it reports the reverted work as shipped
cards.description:
The dashboard's "Pending release" group answers the question "what is deployed?" by asking "what was tagged last?" Those are different questions. Today they gave different answers, and the panel gave the wrong one.

## What happened, 2026-08-22

After deploying `agent-bureau-console-v1.5.54`, the dashboard's "Pending release" group read **7** — PRs #2099, #2103, #2104, #2105, #2106, #2107, #2108. Six of those shipped **in** v1.5.54. Only #2108 merged after the build.

The observed 7 is exactly this, and nothing else:

```
git log agent-bureau-console-v1.5.53..origin/main --merges
```

Against v1.5.54 the count is 1. The panel compared against the **previous** release.

## Where it breaks

`console/backend/schema.py:2519-2526` anchors on `releases[0]` — the newest tag from a 300-second memoised GitHub fetch (`console/backend/sources.py:1372-1373`) — not on the release this container is running.

That is enough on its own, and the deploy order makes it near-certain. `infra/deploy-console.sh` rolls out App Runner at line 493 and cuts the tag at line 528. A new backend starts serving **before its own tag exists**, then caches a tag list headed by the old release for five minutes. The frontend refetches only on live events (`console/web/src/lib/useLiveQuery.ts:118-119`), so the stale render sits there afterwards.

## Two cards this is NOT, so nobody re-litigates them

**Not** [DRE-2618](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2618/deploy-lag-is-computed-per-surface-merged-and-running-are-different)**.** Its deliverable, `scripts/check_deploy_lag.py`, is correct: it anchors on the newest tag by creatordate (lines 147-170), and the console never imports it. The wrong number comes from an older resolver in the GraphQL layer.

**Not** [DRE-2079](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2079/shipped-panel-pending-release-over-counts-release-deployedat-derived) **regressing.** Its commit-ancestry fix landed and works — today's 7 matches ancestry exactly. The compare is right; the **base release it compares against** is wrong.

## The direction that matters

`infra/rollback-console.sh:22` states that rollback does not touch git tags. So after a rollback the newest tag is not what is running, and the panel reports rolled-back work as **deployed**.

It fails in the reassuring direction. That is the failure class this console exists to prevent.

## One more disagreement, worth settling in the same pass

The backend orders tags by `TAG_COMMIT_DATE` (`sources.py:1392`); the CLI uses `-creatordate` (`check_deploy_lag.py:158`). The CLI's key is the correct one. v1.5.53 tagged a commit that was already about 19 hours old, so the two keys can genuinely name different "newest" releases here — this is not theoretical.

## Fix direction (a direction, not a prescription)

Anchor on the release entry whose version equals `os.environ["CONSOLE_VERSION"]`. The container knows its own release before the tag exists (`deploy-console.sh:282`). Fall back to `releases[0]` only when nothing matches. The same change closes the rollback case, because a rolled-back container carries the older version string.

Also fix `schema.py:726-732`. It currently documents the field as anchoring on the latest release — the bug written down as the contract.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Red first: a fixture where the newest tag is not the running release asserts the count is computed against the **running** release. Today's case — running v1.5.54, fetched tag list headed by v1.5.53, 7 merges since v1.5.53, 1 since v1.5.54 — renders 1.
- [ ] A rollback fixture (running version older than the newest tag) reports the rolled-back commits as pending, not as deployed.
- [ ] When no release entry matches `CONSOLE_VERSION`, the fallback is deliberate and covered by a test, and the panel says it is falling back. "We could not tell" must not render as "it is current."
- [ ] Tag ordering uses the same key as `check_deploy_lag.py` (`-creatordate`), so the CLI and the console cannot disagree about which release is newest.
- [ ] The field documentation at `schema.py:726-732` describes the new behaviour.
- [ ] `scripts/check_deploy_lag.py` is untouched — it is already correct.

cards.title: A HAND-BUILT card branch pushed with no PR is unwatched — the dispatched path already handles this, and the designed stall clock will not
cards.description:
**Scope corrected 2026-08-22 3:35 PM PT, before anything was built. The original card claimed "no lane in the system has an opinion about it." That is wrong for the dispatched path, and the correction shrinks this card considerably.**

## What was proven, and how

### The dispatched path already handles it — this claim was false

`agent-task.yml`'s `check-agent-result` step ends in an `else` branch reached precisely when there is **no PR and no blocker**. It is a named failure class ("silent death"), and it does three visible things:

```
linear_ops.py comment    "$CARD" "$BODY"
linear_ops.py add-label  "$CARD" needs-human
linear_ops.py state      "$CARD" "Backlog" --park
```

It shares a hold cap with the hung and `is_error` classes, counted by the `dead-run-requeue` tag, and it has been hardened repeatedly — [DRE-1403](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-1403/bureau-pipeline-hung-agent-runs-escape-medic-add-job-timeout-sticky) (the cap), [DRE-1354](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-1354/bureau-pipeline-model-fallback-on-is-error-switch-opusfable-on-retry) (`is_error` deaths count), [DRE-1300](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-1300/console-swim-lane-mode-by-project) (an 18× loop), [DRE-2074](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2074/dead-run-watchdog-still-kills-live-builds-a-run-that-is-in-progress) (a cancelled run is not a death), [DRE-2032](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2032/reconciles-dead-run-requeue-kills-live-builds-no-pr-after-45min-reads) (receipts).

**So a dispatched agent that pushes a branch and fails to open a PR is caught inside its own run.** Nothing needs building for that case, and building it would duplicate a mechanism with a cap.

### The hand-built path genuinely is unwatched — this claim held

Three layers, none of which apply:

| layer | keys on | sees it? |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `flag_stranded` | a card with no run receipt | **no** — skips `hand-built` cards outright, by design ([DRE-2524](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2524/teach-the-stranded-watchdog-that-a-hand-built-card-is-not-stranded)) |
| PR-level backstops | a pull request | **no** — there isn't one |
| the designed stall clock | **an open PR** whose state has not changed | **no** — same reason |

That third row is the one worth noting. `adr-gate-repair-and-stall-detection.md` decision 1 is the load-bearing fix for this whole area, and it is explicit that the clock keys on the pull request rather than the card — which is what makes it close thirteen silent exits at once. But a branch that never became a PR is outside even that clock. **Wave 5 /** [DRE-2518](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2518/wave-5-layer-3-gates-and-the-critic-every-verdict-gets-an-owner) **will not cover this.**

### Both observed instances are hand-built. Zero are dispatched.

Every `agent/DRE-*` ref on origin, against all 146 card PRs ever opened:

* **9 live branches, 2 with no PR.**
* [DRE-2604](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2604/the-console-deploys-pre-flight-uses-ambient-node-while-every-deploy) — built by hand in a session on 2026-08-22; no `agent-task` run exists for it that day.
* [DRE-2597](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2597/the-one-writer-adrs-two-open-questions-are-answered-record-the) — carries the `hand-built` label.
* The other 7 all merged.

## What this means for priority

**This is a backstop for hand-built work, not a guardrail for unattended operation.** The unattended path is covered, and covered thoroughly. Dropped from High to Medium accordingly.

It is still worth building — hand-built work is a permanent category, not a transitional one, and it lost two branches in three days, one of which sat two days — but it does not block Wave 1 and it is not on the critical path for running the pipeline unattended.

## Risks this must not introduce

Named because a branch watchdog has already misfired here once.

1. **Do not double-report a dispatched silent death.** That card is already commented, labelled and parked. A second flag on the same card is the [DRE-2024](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2024/reconcile-re-dispatches-a-doomed-agent-fix-every-sweep-for-a-needs) shape — a sweep re-acting on a card that is already held. Skip any card carrying the dead-run hold.
2. **A quiet window is mandatory, and it must exceed push-to-PR time.** [DRE-2610](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2610/retracted-the-unowned-branch-watchdog-works-it-was-inside-its-120) is a *retracted* card filed against the unowned-branch watchdog for exactly this: the premise was wrong and the mechanism was fine — it was inside its 120-minute quiet window. A watcher that fires between a push and the PR would flag normal work every time.
3. **Merged branches linger.** 7 of the 9 live card branches are merged-but-undeleted, so "has a branch" is not evidence of anything on its own. The check must be "no PR in any state — open, merged, or closed", not "no open PR".
4. **Report, never act.** No requeue, no dispatch, no state move. One comment naming the branch, its age, and its drift from main.

## Done when

* A hand-built card branch pushed with no PR is reported once, after a quiet window, whatever the card's lane.
* A card already parked by the dispatched silent-death path is never flagged by this.
* A test drives the `hand-built` + Backlog case ([DRE-2597](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2597/the-one-writer-adrs-two-open-questions-are-answered-record-the)'s exact shape) and the merged-but-undeleted case (7 live examples).

## Related

[DRE-2626](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2626/a-pr-whose-blocker-is-resolved-outside-the-diff-strands-forever-the) — a PR that exists and cannot be re-reviewed — is the sibling, and unlike this one it **is** subsumed by the ADR's PR-keyed stall clock. [DRE-2518](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2518/wave-5-layer-3-gates-and-the-critic-every-verdict-gets-an-owner) (Wave 5) owns that. This card is the remainder that the clock cannot reach.

cards.title: SIGN-OFF (OPERATOR): link-out documents behave the way they are supposed to
cards.description:
Yours.

## The one that actually needs your judgement

This epic **accepts a real risk on purpose**: a Google Doc sits behind Google's sharing, so removing a partner from Portico does not remove their access to it, and Portico cannot see or fix that. The agreed compensating control is **disclosure** — the document says so, and the share panel says so.

The demo shows that happening. What only you can decide is whether **the disclosure is strong enough to make the trade acceptable** when a real partner is on the other end of it.

## What to check

* Read the sentence on the external document screen. Would a partner understand what it means?
* Remove someone's access in the share panel. Does it tell you clearly enough that you would actually go and revoke the Google file?
* A Google Doc and a form side by side: is it obvious that one is gated by you and the other is not?

## The answer

**Yes** → the epic closes.

**No, the disclosure is not enough** → that is worth hearing now. It might mean stronger wording, or it might mean this shape is wrong for documents that matter, in which case convert-to-PDF ([DRE-2459](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2459/epic-every-document-format-readable-in-place-not-just-downloadable)) becomes the route for those instead. Either is cheaper to decide here than after a partner keeps reading something they should not.

cards.title: DEMO: link-out documents — prove a Google Doc opens, and that the screen is honest about who controls it
cards.description:
> **Branch:** `agent/DRE-2650-<slug>`**.** Not `ui/*`, not `feat/*`, and **not the** `sid/dre-2650-…` **name Linear suggests** — `linear-sync.yml` reads the card id out of the merged branch, so any other prefix means this card does not close itself. `hand-built` decides who writes the code, not where it lands. One card, one branch, one PR. **This epic has already lost one card to that mistake** — [DRE-2495](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2495/the-external-document-screen-open-in-a-new-tab-and-say-who-controls) merged as `ui/forms-spec` and had to be closed by hand.

Added 2026-08-22 under the standing rule: **every epic ends with a demo that proves it by being run, and a sign-off that is the operator's.**

## The claims

1. **A moderator adds a Google Doc by pasting a link**, and it is stored as a pointer — not fetched, not snapshotted.
2. **A partner opens it** from the library: a Portico screen with title, status and rail, then Open, then the file on Google in a new tab.
3. **The screen is honest.** It says plainly that Google controls who can open this, and Portico cannot. Show the wording.
4. **The share panel is honest too** — a folder containing one discloses it, with a count, and removing someone's access says the external file must be revoked where it lives.
5. **A partner who cannot open the Google file can still speak.** Portico's own thread works on it, and is labelled so it is not mistaken for Google's comments.
6. **The accepted risk, demonstrated rather than described.** Remove a partner from the project. Their Portico documents go dark. **The Google link still works.** This is the epic's one real risk and the demo should show it happening rather than let it be discovered later.

## Also worth showing here

A Google Doc and a **form** side by side in the same folder, each saying something different and true about who controls it. That contrast is the clearest statement of what this release delivers.

## Acceptance

- [ ] All six claims run against the real build
- [ ] Claim 6 is executed, not narrated
- [ ] A walkthrough artifact handed over before the sign-off opens

cards.title: [EPIC] Forms — working on an answer together
cards.description:
Two people fill one form. This epic is everything that happens to an answer after it is written: somebody disagrees with it, somebody proposes better wording, somebody wants to know who changed it, and nobody wants to duplicate work already in progress.

**Every answer is a small document** (operator's words, 2026-08-22): an editable value, suggested edits to accept or reject, tracked history, its own comment thread, and a status.

**And the mechanic does not stop at forms.** Amended 2026-08-22, same session: *"make sure to include suggestions into our normal document behavior where people can leave comments and suggested changes in the document too."* So this epic covers suggested edits on **an answer or a published passage** — one store, one state machine, two subjects ([DRE-2640](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2640/b1-suggested-edits-the-store-a-proposal-never-changes-the-answer)), and the second surface is **B7 /** [DRE-2654](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2654/b7-suggest-an-edit-on-a-document-passage-the-same-mechanic-outside-a). The half that genuinely differs is what accepting DOES: an answer gets written, a document cannot be — its revision is immutable and its source is not in this repo — so an accepted passage records the agreement and the wording changes at the next publish. Saying that on screen is a requirement of B7, not a caveat in it.

Spec: `docs/design/forms/forms-prototype.html`, **on main since 2026-08-22**. Open it — press the buttons under the app to make other people act. Each card carries a **Design:** line naming the surface it builds.

## Who may write which answers — decided 2026-08-22, and it reshapes three cards in this epic

**Answers are partitioned by the answerer's email domain** (`responses_lib.ts:112`, the [DRE-2384](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2384/operator-two-decisions-before-any-answer-is-stored-the-confidentiality) key). This epic was written as if everyone shared one set. They do not, and the partition stays.

**The decision is "read and suggest across, write within":** our staff read the customer's answers, comment, and propose wording; **only the customer accepts**, and that write lands in their own partition. Our staff cannot type an answer on their behalf. Full reasoning on [DRE-2628](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2628/epic-forms-a-form-is-its-own-object-in-portico).

What it changes here:

* **B1** builds a **cross-group read** on the poll, and **accept authorised by group** — accepting a suggestion in another group is refused. It also has to say who may accept at all, which it never did.
* **B2** draws two states of one panel: an answer that is yours (editable, Accept/Reject) and one that is not (Suggest + thread only), with the difference legible rather than a disabled control.
* **B4** needs **presence moved out of the domain partition** — today it is `p#<sub>` *inside* the group, so "see it across groups" is not achievable as the store stands. B4 is now blocked by B1.
* **B-DEMO** must run **cross-company**. It used Hagen and Yannan, who share a domain — so it would have passed while the thing it exists to prove was broken.

**The prototype is wrong on this point** (it opens as Sid and edits the customer's form) and gets corrected in the same PR as the behaviour.

## This supersedes the transport half of [DRE-2383](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2383/epic-shared-answers-for-the-oncor-intake-questionnaire-per-field-sync), and keeps the rest

[DRE-2383](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2383/epic-shared-answers-for-the-oncor-intake-questionnaire-per-field-sync) built shared answering with the answer boxes **inside** the document, carried across the sandbox by `postMessage`. It is finished and correct and sits unmerged on `gridcorr:feat/DRE-2390-frame-answer-sync`. It is superseded because it only ever works for one document kind, and because reopening it shows an empty form — `pushableFields` allows only `origin === "frame"`, so a reader's own prior answers structurally cannot cross back in.

**What survives, and is reused here rather than rebuilt:**

* the storage design — one item per answered field, server-assigned versions, stale writes refused, actor from the verified JWT (`responses_lib.ts`, live)
* the routes — `GET /d/{docId}/responses`, `PUT …/{fieldId}`, `POST …/submit` (deployed)
* `answerSyncPolicy.presence` — the 45-second window, one field per person, the name/count collapsing and the is/are verb
* the measured constants — 2s autosave debounce, ~3s poll

**What retires:** the frame transport and its handshake. Portico owns the answer boxes now, so nothing crosses the boundary — which is also why presence gets simpler, see B4.

## Order

**Wave 3** — after A2 and A3 land: B1, B6 in parallel; then B2, B3, B4.
**Wave 4** — B5 and B7, then B-DEMO and B-OK.

`hand-built` cards are built locally and looked at in a browser before being committed, then pushed as one PR for CI.

### The branch name is what closes the card, and `hand-built` does not change it

**Every card here lands on** `agent/DRE-<n>-<slug>` — hand-built ones included, and this epic is mostly hand-built.

`.github/workflows/linear-sync.yml` reads the card id out of the merged branch name. `ui/*`, `feat/*`, `fix/*`, `docs/*` auto-Done **nothing**. The label says **who writes the code**; the branch prefix says **whether the pipeline is watching**. **Do not copy Linear's suggested** `sid/dre-<n>-<slug>` — wrong prefix, silent cost. One card, one branch, one PR.

Full reasoning in [DRE-2628](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2628/epic-forms-a-form-is-its-own-object-in-portico). Learned on [DRE-2495](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2495/the-external-document-screen-open-in-a-new-tab-and-say-who-controls), 2026-08-22.

## B3 is blocked on [DRE-2496](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2496/the-comment-rail-survives-a-document-portico-does-not-host-and-says), and the reason is file ownership

Both edit `rails/CommentsRail/`, `Thread.tsx` in particular. [DRE-2496](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2496/the-comment-rail-survives-a-document-portico-does-not-host-and-says) **lands first** — B3 builds on the rail it leaves behind. The other order means rebasing through the most-tested component in the viewer. This is a formal blocked-by relation on B3, not a note.

**B7 makes it three cards on that one file**, and the order is [DRE-2496](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2496/the-comment-rail-survives-a-document-portico-does-not-host-and-says) → B3 → B7, all as real relations. Three cards deep on the most-tested component in the viewer is worth watching deliberately rather than discovering during a rebase — if any of the three slips, the two behind it slip with it, and that is the sequence to check first when this epic looks stalled.

## B6 is not optional

The per-subject mutation budget is 30 tokens refilling at 1/second, and `guardMutations` writes an idempotency row per write with a 24-hour TTL — its own header assumes "a handful of rows per active moderator". **Two people autosaving a 132-question form is precisely the load that assumption excludes.** [DRE-2383](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2383/epic-shared-answers-for-the-oncor-intake-questionnaire-per-field-sync) named this as a sequencing risk and never resolved it. Resolve it before a customer meets it, not after.

## Acceptance for the epic

- [ ] Two real browser sessions: one answers, the other sees it within a few seconds without reloading
- [ ] A suggested edit does not change the answer until it is accepted, and the acceptance is in the history with who made it
- [ ] A thread resolves, and resolved means settled — settled threads get out of the way and can be reopened
- [ ] Presence names who is in a question, and lapses on the existing 45-second window
- [ ] A mention offers only people who can already open the form, and adds one recipient to the existing notification path
- [ ] Typing through a poll does not lose the sentence, and scrolling does not throw the reader to the top
- [ ] A sustained two-person editing session does not trip the write budget
- [ ] The same suggest-an-edit mechanic works on a published document passage, and accepting one is honest that the wording appears at the next publish rather than claiming the document changed
- [ ] B-DEMO is executed, and B-OK is signed
- [ ] Every card in this epic closed itself on merge — if one had to be moved to Done by hand, its branch was named wrong

cards.title: [EPIC] Forms — a form is its own object in Portico
cards.description:
Portico can send documents out but nothing comes back. Every document type is one-way: readers can comment, and that is all. A **form** is the object that captures.

A moderator defines a **template**. Dragging it into a customer folder creates an **instance**, frozen at that version and named for that customer, which inherits the folder's people. The customer fills it in; Portico knows who they are because they came through the gate.

## The spec is a working prototype, not this card

`docs/design/forms/forms-prototype.html` — committed, runs in a browser, no build and no server. Open it and use it. Also published as an artifact for reading.

**Where a card and the prototype disagree about behaviour, the card is wrong.** When behaviour genuinely changes, the prototype changes in the same PR. Every child card carries a **Design:** line naming the exact surface it builds.

## Decisions already taken (operator, 2026-08-22)

| Decision | Choice |
| -- | -- |
| Template → instance | **Snapshot at drag time.** A customer's form never changes under them |
| Authoring a template | **A definition file.** Visual builder later, on the same definition |
| Attachments | **Both** — per question, plus a general "anything else" area |
| Answer vs discussion | The answer stays a **value with a status**; threads hang off it |
| Presence | **Name them, don't block** |
| Who sees whom | **Everyone on the form sees everyone**, ours and the customer's |
| **Who WRITES what** | **Read and suggest across, write within** — decided 2026-08-22, see below. This row was missing and its absence was the review's one blocking finding |
| The frame sandbox | **Untouched.** Portico owns the answer boxes, so nothing crosses it |

## Who may write which answers — decided 2026-08-22, after the critic review

**The plan assumed everyone worked on one shared set of answers. The shipped store does the opposite**, and no card had noticed. `responses_lib.ts:112` keys every answer `resp#<project>#<itemId>#<group>` where `group` is the **answerer's email domain** — recorded at `:17-24` as the operator's [DRE-2384](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2384/operator-two-decisions-before-any-answer-is-stored-the-confidentiality) decision of 2026-08-11, with the warning that it *"cannot be changed once answers exist without migrating a customer's live data."*

**The decision: read and suggest across, write within.**

|  | our staff | the customer |
| -- | -- | -- |
| read the customer's answers | **yes** | yes |
| comment on them | **yes** | yes |
| **suggest** wording | **yes** | yes |
| accept a suggestion | **no** | yes — the write lands in their own partition |
| type an answer directly | **no** | yes |
| presence | **sees them, and is seen** | same |

The partition key does not change and there is no migration. **The suggestion mechanic IS the safe way across the company line** — a proposal does not change an answer until somebody in that group accepts it, which is exactly the guarantee [DRE-2384](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2384/operator-two-decisions-before-any-answer-is-stored-the-confidentiality) was protecting, expressed as a feature rather than a wall. Merging the partitions would have re-opened the risk that decision closed: *Sid overwrote Hagen's answer, last-write-wins, Hagen was told afterwards* — on a compliance form.

**What it gives up, said plainly:** our staff cannot type an answer on a customer's behalf. **The prototype shows Sid doing exactly that, so the prototype is wrong on this point and gets corrected in the same PR as the behaviour** — which is this epic's own rule, applied to itself.

Three things to build, none a partition-key change: a **cross-group read** on the poll (B1), **accept authorised by group** (B1), and **presence moved out of the domain partition** (B4, now blocked by B1).

## Where each card is built

`hand-built` means **built locally by the UI engineer and looked at in a browser before it is committed**, then pushed as one PR for CI like anything else. Spacing, states, drag behaviour and whether a long form is bearable to fill in do not survive being described in a ticket and checked by a test.

Everything else is dispatched normally.

### The branch name is what closes the card — `hand-built` does not change it

**Every card in this epic lands on** `agent/DRE-<n>-<slug>`**. Hand-built ones included.**

`.github/workflows/linear-sync.yml` reads the card id **out of the merged branch name**. A branch named anything else — `ui/*`, `feat/*`, `fix/*`, `docs/*` — auto-Dones **nothing**, and the card sits in In Review with its own work already live in main. That is deliberate, not a bug: the rule exists so operator-authored work does not close cards it has nothing to do with. It just means a card's work has to be in the bucket the pipeline watches.

So the two things are orthogonal, and conflating them is the trap:

|  | decides |
| -- | -- |
| the `hand-built` **label** | **who writes the code** — a person, locally, looking at it in a browser |
| the **branch prefix** | **whether the pipeline is watching** — auto-Done, and the card's link back to its PR |

**Do not use the branch name Linear suggests.** Linear's own `gitBranchName` on these cards is `sid/dre-<n>-<slug>` — lowercase, wrong prefix. Copying it costs the auto-Done silently.

**One card, one branch, one PR.** Bundling two cards' work — or a card plus unrelated docs — onto one branch closes at most one of them.

Learned on [DRE-2495](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2495/the-external-document-screen-open-in-a-new-tab-and-say-who-controls), 2026-08-22: merged as `ui/forms-spec`. The merge gate and the critic both ran fine — they key on the PR — and the card still had to be moved to Done by hand.

## Order, and why

### Wave 1 — SERIAL, alone. Nothing else may start.

| Card | Why it is alone |
| -- | -- |
| **F1 · the client tolerates a form** | The SPA and the backend deploy on independent paths and `queries/render.ts` throws on an unknown kind. If the server emits a form before the bundle understands one, every reader on a cached bundle drops into the viewer's error state — across their whole library. This is exactly [DRE-2493](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2493/client-tolerates-an-external-artifact-kind-ships-alone-before-the), which shipped alone ahead of its own epic for the same reason. **Copy it line for line.** |

F1 must be merged **and deployed**, not merely merged.

### Wave 2 — parallel once F1 is deployed. Three cards, no shared files.

A1 (definition parsing) · A2 (the item kind and instantiate-on-drop) · A3 (the reading view).

A3 builds against the payload shape F1 fixed, so it does not wait for the backend.

### Wave 3 — after A2.

A4 (place a form from the library) · A5 (answer status) · A6 (attachments on an answer) · A7 (submit and export).

### Wave 4 — the close.

A-DEMO, then A-OK. **Every epic now ends this way** (operator, 2026-08-22): a demo that proves it by being run, and a sign-off that is the operator's, not an agent's. Merged is not done and a green suite is not proof.

## Two collisions with [DRE-2492](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2492/epic-link-out-documents-a-file-that-lives-elsewhere-indexed-and-gated) — do not run them concurrently

[DRE-2492](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2492/epic-link-out-documents-a-file-that-lives-elsewhere-indexed-and-gated) delivers the other new entity (documents held elsewhere). Between them Portico holds everything it is asked to hold. But two cards break the disjoint-file rule:

* [DRE-2497](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2497/add-document-paste-a-google-link-and-choose-to-link-to-it-not-copy-it) (paste a link) and **A4** (place a form) both edit `LibraryScreen.tsx` and `AddDocumentModal/`. [DRE-2497](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2497/add-document-paste-a-google-link-and-choose-to-link-to-it-not-copy-it) should also become `hand-built` and run here in sequence with A4. Splitting one surface across a local card and a dispatched card is how two agents produce one conflict.
* [DRE-2496](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2496/the-comment-rail-survives-a-document-portico-does-not-host-and-says) (the rail on a document we do not host) and **B3** (a thread on an answer) both edit `rails/CommentsRail/`. **2496 lands first** — see the sibling epic.

## Acceptance for the epic

- [ ] A moderator can define a template and place it in two different customer folders, each frozen independently
- [ ] The instance inherits the folder's people, using the existing grant walk and no new access model
- [ ] Somebody from another customer's folder gets the same uninformative refusal a document gives
- [ ] Every field type in the prototype works, including repeating rows
- [ ] Answers autosave attributed to the verified identity, and survive a poll firing mid-keystroke
- [ ] The frame sandbox and `pushableFields` are untouched
- [ ] A-DEMO is executed, and A-OK is signed
- [ ] Every card in this epic closed itself on merge — if one had to be moved to Done by hand, its branch was named wrong

cards.title: A PR whose blocker is resolved outside the diff strands forever — the only re-review lever the sweep has runs against main, not the PR
cards.description:
## What happened

PR #2099 ([DRE-2618](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2618/deploy-lag-is-computed-per-surface-merged-and-running-are-different)) sat blocked for ~19 hours with its work finished. The critic asked for one thing: file the follow-up card. It was filed — [DRE-2623](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2623/the-relays-deploy-leaves-no-record-of-what-version-is-live-so-deploy), 2026-08-22 1:22 PM PT — and recorded in the PR body. The PR still showed `REQUEST_CHANGES` and stayed unmergeable.

Nothing was wrong with the code. The blocker was satisfied. **There was no event that could tell anyone.**

## Why nothing recovered it

Two facts combine into a trap, both measured on 2026-08-22, not recalled:

**1. Only three events re-fire the critic.** `qa-review.yml` declares `types: [opened, reopened, synchronize]`. Every one of them requires a push or a state change. Editing a PR body, posting a comment, and filing a Linear card fire none of them. A blocker that lives outside the diff can never announce that it cleared.

**2. The backstop that exists for this cannot reach the PR.** `reconcile.py::_nudge()` re-triggers review with `gh workflow run <stub> -f pr_number=N` — a `workflow_dispatch`. Every dispatched review run in this repo's history landed on the wrong ref:

```
gh run list --workflow qa-review.yml --event workflow_dispatch
2026-08-22T00:25:33Z  head=main  success   <- the sweep nudging #2099
2026-08-21T04:00:12Z  head=main  failure
2026-08-20T18:24:12Z  head=main  failure
... 8 of 8, all head=main
```

Run `32540301538` reviewed `main` at sha `c9979915`. #2099's head is `9898724e`. **The sweep fired, succeeded, reviewed the wrong code, and wrote its check to the default branch.** The PR's own check never moved. This is the worst failure shape available: a backstop that reports success while doing nothing.

The fix agent, correctly, declined to paper over it:

> "I am deliberately not pushing. The diff since the head the reviewer rejected is empty, and a cosmetic commit would burn a full review round without moving the one item that is actually open."

It was right. The escape hatch it was left with — a human — is the thing this pipeline exists to remove.

## The lever that does work

`close` then `reopen` fires `pull_request: reopened` **on the PR head**, so the review runs against the right code and the check lands on the right ref. Used on #2099 on 2026-08-22; a fresh `call / review` started on head `9898724e` within 25 seconds.

Verified safe before use: `linear-sync.yml` guards both jobs on `github.event.pull_request.merged == true`, so a close/reopen cannot transition the card. Observed: `call / card-done` SKIPPED. The cost is a full CI re-run, which is bounded and visible.

## Scope

1. **The sweep's re-review path uses close/reopen instead of** `workflow_dispatch`**.** Keep `workflow_dispatch` where it is correct (agent-fix, merge-gate); it is only the *critic* whose check must bind to the PR head. Guard it: card branches only, never on an already-closed PR, and bounded per head so it cannot cycle.
2. **A test that fails on the old behaviour** — assert the re-review path does not reach for `workflow run` on the review stub, and that a nudge names the PR head, not the default branch.
3. **The sweep notices this shape at all.** Today "open PR + REQUEST_CHANGES + head unchanged + no run since the head last moved" is invisible. Detect it, re-review once, then escalate loudly rather than silently re-dispatching (the [DRE-2024](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2024/reconcile-re-dispatches-a-doomed-agent-fix-every-sweep-for-a-needs) lesson).

## Done when

* A PR whose blocker cleared outside the diff gets re-reviewed without a human and without a cosmetic commit.
* No re-review path in the sweep can write its check to the default branch.
* A test goes red if either regresses.

## Related

[DRE-2282](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2282/a-crashed-critic-parks-a-pr-forever-bounded-per-head-re-review-then) (crashed critic parks a PR forever) shares the symptom, but its remedy is the same dispatch that lands on main — so it did not cover this. [DRE-2024](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2024/reconcile-re-dispatches-a-doomed-agent-fix-every-sweep-for-a-needs) (doomed re-dispatch every sweep) is the bound this must respect. [DRE-2618](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2618/deploy-lag-is-computed-per-surface-merged-and-running-are-different) / PR #2099 is the instance.

cards.title: The fix loop stops at a counter, not at \"we cannot fix this\" — three attempts is arbitrary in both directions
cards.description:
**Operator, 2026-08-21:** *"It shouldn't be a number like three. It should be when we just can't fix it for whatever reason."*

**Operator, 2026-08-21:** *"I have never once been asked to look at something like this."* — **and that is literally true. Verified: the hold has never fired.** A comment search across the whole `dreadnought-foundry` org for the hold's recovery sentence (*"To release this PR…"*) returns **zero** actual hold comments. The one search hit, portico #318, matched the phrase in a diff, not in a comment.

So three mechanisms in this path are **declared but never invoked** (the [DRE-2564](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2564/scan-for-mechanisms-that-exist-and-never-run-the-declared-but-never) class):

1. the 3-attempt hold itself,
2. the operator-decision escape hatch it advertises, and
3. reconcile's auto re-dispatch on that decision (`reconcile.py:2217-2234`, [DRE-2409](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2409/the-operators-escape-hatch-needs-an-exact-undocumented-token-a-natural)).

All three are verified **in code** and none has ever run **in production**. Anything this card builds must therefore be provable without waiting for a natural occurrence — the replay tests in the acceptance criteria are the substitute.

## Where the number actually lives — nowhere manageable

| site | value | how it is set |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `agent-fix.yml:213` | `ATTEMPTS >= 3` → hold | **hardcoded shell literal** |
| `agent-fix.yml:208` | `ATTEMPT == 3` → re-derive framing | **hardcoded shell literal** |
| `agent-fix.yml:177` | `RESOLVED >= 5` → conflict hold | **hardcoded shell literal** |

The reusable workflow's **only** input is `pipeline_ref`. No config file, no env var, no per-repo override. Changing the budget means editing the shared workflow and shipping it to the whole fleet at once.

**Operator, 2026-08-21:** *"We can't have hard-coded values like this."* So this card also owns making the budget a declared value rather than a literal — somewhere a human can read and change it without a pipeline release, and somewhere a guard can assert it.

## And it must ASK, not just stop

**Operator, 2026-08-21:** *"It should then prompt the user, me, the operator, to say 'should we give it more cycles or not?' Not just stop and all of a sudden it's dead in the water. That's what gets us where we don't trust things."*

What exists today asks for a **substantive answer** — *"comment with a first line starting Operator decision"* — which assumes the human has diagnosed the problem. There is no *"it was making progress, give it more"* reply. The cheapest useful version is a second recognised answer meaning exactly that: extend the budget and re-dispatch, no diagnosis required.

The hold must also reach the CEO where he actually reads, and say what it needs in one line. Today it comments on the PR and on the card; whether either surfaces to him is the open half of "never once been asked."

`agent-fix.yml` holds a PR for a human when `ATTEMPTS >= 3`:

```
ATTEMPTS=$(gh api .../comments --jq '[... contains("🔧 Fix attempt")] | length')
if [ "$ATTEMPT" -eq 3 ]; then   # escalate the FRAMING — re-derive from scratch
if [ "$ATTEMPTS" -ge 3 ]; then  # "Fix budget exhausted" — hold
```

A counter is wrong in **both** directions. A loop that is genuinely converging gets cut off at three; a loop re-making the identical mistake still burns three full agent runs before anyone notices. The count measures how many times we tried, which is not the question. The question is whether we are getting anywhere.

## The evidence is already on #2097

Three verdicts, three DIFFERENT findings — it was converging, and the critic said so in round 3: *"It closes the specific bug from August 21st and the two follow-on defects a prior review round already found and blocked on — those are genuinely fixed now."*

| round | verdict content hash |
| -- | -- |
| 1 | `content:dc76c3c2…` |
| 2 | `content:2ef3c8e4…` |
| 3 | `content:8d817265…` |

Attempt 1 fixed two of three defects. That is progress, and under the counter it gets exactly one more swing regardless. Meanwhile a loop that returned the same hash three times would get the same three swings.

## The signal that already exists

Every critic verdict carries `@<head-sha> content:<hash>`. **Two consecutive verdicts with the same** `content:` **hash, on different heads, is the real "we cannot fix this"** — the agent changed the code and the critic's objection did not move. That is a stall, and it is detectable on the second occurrence rather than the fourth.

The `cause:` token (`cause:defect`, `cause:unverified-claim`) gives a coarser version of the same signal.

Note the existing `ATTEMPT -eq 3` framing change — *"Two previous fix attempts failed… re-derive from scratch"* — is the right instinct already: it recognises that repetition is not progress. It is just keyed to a count instead of to whether the finding repeated.

## Scope

* Replace the fixed budget with a **convergence** test: hold when the critic's verdict content repeats across attempts on different heads, rather than at a fixed count.
* Keep a high absolute ceiling as a runaway backstop only — not as the normal exit — so a pathological loop still terminates.
* Move the fresh-eyes re-derivation framing to the first REPEAT rather than to attempt 3.
* The same argument applies to the conflict path's `RESOLVED >= 5`; decide whether it gets the same treatment or is genuinely different (main moving underneath is not the agent failing to converge).

## Out of scope

* [DRE-2617](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2617/the-fix-loop-cancels-its-own-next-round-a-no-op-comment-run-evicts-the), the concurrency eviction — different bug in the same file, already fixed in PR #2100.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Red first: a replay where three attempts produce three DIFFERENT verdict hashes does **not** hold, and one where two consecutive hashes match **does** — the current code fails both.
- [ ] The runaway ceiling still terminates a loop that never repeats and never converges.
- [ ] The hold message says which finding repeated and quotes it, so the human is not re-reading the whole trail to find out why it stopped.
- [ ] Proven by mutation: remove the convergence check and a named test goes red.

cards.title: test_lifespan_seed_makes_project_surfaces_nonempty is intermittent — one red in three identical runs
cards.description:
Observed 2026-08-20 while adding CI coverage under [DRE-2609](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2609/a-test-under-scripts-is-never-run-by-ci-the-forensics-index-gate-has).

`console/backend/tests/test_app_wiring_scenario.py::test_lifespan_seed_makes_project_surfaces_nonempty` failed once and then passed twice under conditions that did not change:

| run | branch state | result |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | with a new test file added | **1 failed**, 3925 passed |
| 2 | that file moved aside | 0 failed, 3924 passed |
| 3 | file restored — **identical to run 1** | 0 failed, 3926 passed |

It also passes in isolation (5 passed).

Run 1 and run 3 are the same tree. So this is **intermittent**, not order-deterministic — and the two-run A/B that seemed to implicate the new file was a false signal, because the flake simply did not recur in run 2.

## Why it is worth a card rather than a shrug

A test that fails once in three identical runs will eventually go red on a PR that changed nothing near it. The cost is not the red — it is the **diagnosis**: someone will spend real time proving their diff innocent, exactly as happened here.

It is also a *"green that proves nothing"* in reverse. A suite with an intermittent member cannot distinguish "this change broke something" from "the dice came up wrong", which is precisely the property a gate is supposed to have.

## Scope

* Reproduce it. `-p no:randomly` and repeated runs will say whether it is ordering, timing, or shared state; a lifespan/seed test touching a store is the obvious suspect for leaked state between tests.
* Fix the isolation rather than retrying the test. A retry hides the leak and leaves the next reader with the same puzzle.

## Acceptance

- [ ] The intermittency is reproduced deliberately, and the mechanism named
- [ ] The fix is isolation, not a retry or a sleep
- [ ] Proven by running the suite N times green after the fix, with N stated
- [ ] If it turns out to be environmental rather than a leak, that is recorded here and the card closed on the evidence

cards.title: A branch that LOOKS carded is never verified — pipeline_owns is a prefix check, nothing resolves the card
cards.description:
**Narrowed 2026-08-21, after verifying rather than assuming.** The original claim — *"work can enter the repo with no card at all and nothing notices"* — is **wrong**, and the correction matters.

## What was wrong

`flag_unowned_prs` ([DRE-2426](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2426/branch-ownership-is-hand-copied-eight-times-so-the-sweep-that-finds)) **does** catch uncarded work. It iterates every open PR, reports those `pipeline_owns()` returns false for, and it **fired on PR #2092 at 03:32:56Z** with a notice naming all three skipped gates and the rename. I filed the original claim after checking at 02:07 — 51 minutes into a 120-minute quiet window. Nothing was broken; I looked early.

[DRE-2610](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2610/retracted-the-unowned-branch-watchdog-works-it-was-inside-its-120) carries the full retraction.

## What is actually true, and still a hole

```python
def pipeline_owns(head_ref: str | None) -> bool:
    return _has_prefix(head_ref, PIPELINE_BRANCH_PREFIXES)
```

**A prefix check, and nothing more.** Verified 2026-08-21: nothing in `reconcile.py` or `linear_ops.py` resolves the card id out of a branch and confirms it exists.

So the gap is not *uncarded work* — that is covered. It is **work that LOOKS carded**:

* `agent/DRE-9999-anything` where DRE-9999 does not exist
* a typo'd number — `agent/DRE-2613-…` vs `agent/DRE-2631-…`
* a branch whose card was later deleted or merged away

Each passes `pipeline_owns()`, so the unowned watchdog **skips it** — the branch looks owned. The merge gate accepts the prefix. `linear-sync` then tries to close a card that is not there.

**The one case the watchdog cannot catch is the one that looks correct.** That is the inverse of the original claim and a smaller hole, but a sharper one: a malformed branch is loud, a plausible-but-wrong branch is silent.

`validate_card.py` does not help here — it validates cards entering Todo ([DRE-1405](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-1405/todo-entry-card-gate-auto-repair-missing-reporole-bounce-only-if)), and `tests/test_card_branch_lookup_anchored.py` covers *anchoring* ([DRE-2025](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2025/anchor-the-card-to-branch-grep-in-agent-taskyml-so-dre-142-cant-match)), not existence.

## Scope, revised

* Resolve the card id from the branch and confirm it exists, once, in one place — `pipeline_owns()` answers *"will automation touch this?"*, which is a different question from *"is there a card behind it?"* and should stay separate.
* An `agent/DRE-*` branch whose card does not resolve gets a notice in the same shape the unowned watchdog already uses — it is a good notice and should not be re-invented.
* Do **not** block on it. A card can legitimately be deleted after a branch is cut; the failure mode to remove is silence, not the situation.
* Keep the existing unowned path exactly as it is. It works, and it was doing its job while this card claimed otherwise.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Red first: a PR on `agent/DRE-<nonexistent>-x` currently produces no notice from any sweep
- [ ] After: it is reported, naming the unresolvable card
- [ ] A real carded PR sees no change and no new noise
- [ ] A non-`agent/` branch still gets the existing unowned notice, unchanged — not two notices
- [ ] Idempotent: one notice per PR
- [ ] The card-existence question has exactly one implementation, separate from `pipeline_owns()`

cards.title: The channel-staleness alarm stops at Linear and never reaches the console dialog
cards.description:
**The channel-staleness alarm now exists, and it lands one hop short of the surface the CEO actually reads.** DRE-2552 built the detector in `bureau-pipeline`: it runs daily, and when the release channel stops moving while the engine keeps moving — or when the channel is deliberately held — it raises one deduplicated Linear card, the same way red-main-repair and model-drift raise theirs.

What it does not do is reach the **blocking dialog DRE-2531 built**. That dialog renders an open CRITICAL alert raised inside the console, and only console code can raise one. DRE-2552 was a `repo:bureau-pipeline` card, so the console half was out of its write scope (Wave 1's own rule: one card per repo, because a card spanning two repos cannot be finished by the fix loop).

**Two gaps, and the second is the one that matters more:**

1. **The alarm arrives in Linear, not in the un-missable channel.** A card on the board is a real signal — but it is not the "blocking, un-missable, carries the action" surface the CEO asked for on 2026-08-18, and the whole point of an alarm on the safety rail is that it is believed and seen.
2. **Nothing notices if the watcher itself stops for good.** A red run of the watcher is diagnosed by the medic, and a watcher that skips a tick reports its own gap when it next runs. A watcher that stops permanently — cron dropped, workflow deleted, schedule disabled — is detected by nothing. The console is the natural place to catch that, because it is a separate always-running system: it can read how long ago the watcher last ran at the same time as it reads the channel.

**Suggested scope:** the console reads the channel state itself (the `stable` tag's age against `main`, plus the age of the last Channel Watch run), raises the alert kind that the blocking dialog renders, and resolves it when the channel moves again. The thresholds and their derivation are written down in `bureau-pipeline`'s README under "Channel staleness alarm" — reuse the numbers rather than picking new ones, or the two halves will disagree about what "stale" means.

Repo: agent-bureau. Related: DRE-2552 (the pipeline half), DRE-2531 (the dialog).

cards.title: Split "which account is active" into two facts — the exhaustion alarm must not clear on a label move that reached no repo
cards.description:
Resolves open question 2 of `architecture/decisions/adr-one-writer-per-fact.md`, decided by the CEO on 2026-08-20: **split the fact in two.** [DRE-2597](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2597/the-one-writer-adrs-two-open-questions-are-answered-record-the) records the decision; this card builds it.

One setting, `active_account`, currently means two different things, and its two writers disagree about which:

| writer | moves the label | fans a token to the repos |
| -- | -- | -- |
| the Reconnect rotation (`claude_reconnect`) | yes | **yes** — and records which repos took it and which failed |
| the soft utilization failover (`subscriptions.auto_advance_active_account`) | yes | **no** |

So after a failover tick the label can name an account no repo is on. `claude_reconnect.py:916-923` already declares this as a known second writer and points at the ADR — this card closes it.

**Do not follow the "**[DRE-1607](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-1607/epic-production-demo-environment-drop-work-in-watch-agents-fan-out)**" citation.** `subscriptions.py` and the declared-writer entry in `test_rotation_records_active_account.py` both attribute the soft failover to [DRE-1607](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-1607/epic-production-demo-environment-drop-work-in-watch-agents-fan-out), but that identifier resolves to an unrelated epic ("Production demo environment"). The code is the authority on what the failover does. If the correct card turns up, fix the citation in both places as part of this work; otherwise drop it rather than leaving a pointer that misleads the next reader.

## Why this is not cosmetic

Two readers act on that label, and one of them silences an alarm.

* `agent_dispatch._active_oauth_env_for_store` picks the dispatch credential from it. For console-initiated runs that is **correct** — this reader wants "the account the console bills."
* `monitors/claude_account_health._swapped_away` infers "the pipeline has been swapped off this capped account" from a **change** in the label, and on that inference resolves the CRITICAL "account at its usage limit" alert (`claude_account_health.py:255-260`), replacing it with a revert reminder.

The ordering that makes it live: the cap alert is raised while the recorded baseline still names the capped account, then the failover moves the label with no fan-out. The alarm goes quiet while the fleet is still running on the exhausted account. Running out of account capacity has taken the fleet down before, so a falsely-cleared capacity alarm is the expensive kind of wrong.

The honest sibling already exists in the same file: `_pool_absorbed` reads the per-repo pool assignments and its own docstring draws the distinction — *"the answer is read, never inferred."* `_swapped_away` is the inferred one.

## Why this is cheaper than the ADR estimated

The ADR priced option (b) at "a setting, a migration, and a panel row." Most of the substance is already recorded:

* The rotation receipt (`ROTATION_SETTING_KEY`) already stores `repos_rotated` and `repo_failures` — "which account the repos hold" is largely written down, by exactly one path.
* `make cred-doctor CHECK=fleet-freshness` is the existing read-back and needs no new fan-out.

So the work is mostly pointing the alarm at evidence that already exists, rather than building a new source of truth.

## Scope

* Split the setting in two: **the account the repos hold** (written only by the rotation, derived from its own receipt) and **the account the console bills** (written by the failover and by an explicit operator choice).
* Point the exhaustion-alarm logic at the repos-hold fact, so a standing cap alert can only clear on evidence that a repo actually took a new token.
* Leave `agent_dispatch` reading the console-bills fact — that is the right fact for console-initiated runs.
* Migration for the new setting, backfilled from the latest rotation receipt.
* Subscriptions panel: show both, labelled so they cannot be confused.
* Update the one-writer AST guard and retire (or re-scope) the declared exception in `test_rotation_records_active_account.py`, per the ADR's rule that an exception must expire rather than rot.
* Clear the four comments that still describe this as an **open** question, now that it is answered ([DRE-2597](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2597/the-one-writer-adrs-two-open-questions-are-answered-record-the)). Leaving them is exactly the stale-claim failure this ADR is about:
  * `console/backend/claude_reconnect.py:920`
  * `console/backend/tests/test_rotation_records_active_account.py:339`
  * `console/backend/tests/test_rotation_records_active_account.py:524`
  * `console/backend/tests/test_rotation_records_active_account.py:589`

## Out of scope

* Reading the authoritative value back off the repos. GitHub's secrets API returns a name and a last-updated timestamp, never a value — there is no call that answers "which account's token does this repo hold." Recorded in [DRE-2597](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2597/the-one-writer-adrs-two-open-questions-are-answered-record-the) so it is not re-proposed.
* Anything in [DRE-2416](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2416/the-freshness-bot-races-the-merge-step-an-agent-branch-can-be-starved) (branch currency).

## Acceptance

- [ ] Red-first: a test proves that today, a failover moving the label with **zero** repos rotated clears a standing exhaustion alert — then goes green once the alarm reads the repos-hold fact.
- [ ] A rotation that genuinely reaches the repos still clears the alert and still raises the revert reminder. No regression on the real path.
- [ ] A rotation where **every** repo fails does not clear the alert.
- [ ] The Subscriptions panel shows both facts distinctly, and a drifted pair is visibly a drifted pair rather than one number.
- [ ] The one-writer guard covers both settings, and the declared exception for the soft failover is gone or carries a new expiry reason.
- [ ] `make cred-doctor CHECK=fleet-freshness` still passes against the live fleet.

cards.title: Nothing thaws: when the credential comes back, a human still has to re-run every gate that died on it
cards.description:
**Operator, 2026-08-20:** *"When something gets stuck on the token and the Critic crashes, we need, once we reset it, for it to unstick itself automatically."*

## The gap, stated exactly

[DRE-2439](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2439/stop-retrying-into-a-dead-credential-freeze-repairs-until-it-is) is the **freeze**: stop retrying into a dead credential. This card is the **thaw**: when the credential is live again, the runs that died on it must re-drive **themselves**.

Today nothing does. Recovery is a person remembering which runs died and typing `gh run rerun <id> --failed`. On 2026-08-20 that person was an agent in a chat session; at 03:00 it is nobody, and the PR sits until morning.

## Evidence — 2026-08-20, and it is the second time in 20 hours

`architecture/forensics/credential-fanout-2026-08-20.md`. The credential went live again at **11:53:07 PT**. Nothing moved.

|  |  |
| -- | -- |
| 11:53:07 | fleet credential healthy again |
| 11:53 → 11:54 | **nothing happens** — no sweep notices, no gate re-runs |
| 11:54:37 | a human re-runs two runs by hand |
| 11:58:44 | PR #2079 merges, APPROVE |

**Five of the 44 minutes were the outage being fixed. The rest was waiting for someone to notice it was fixed.** Reconcile ran at 11:43 and reported success — it does not look for gates that died on a credential.

## Why the existing medic does not cover this

* It retries **once, immediately, with identical parameters** — during a credential outage attempt 2 fails exactly as attempt 1 did, burning a run to learn nothing. That is [DRE-2428](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2428/nothing-repairs-a-broken-gate-four-approved-prs-sat-blocked-overnight)'s finding and it is still true.
* The retry fires **at crash time**, which is the one moment the credential is guaranteed still dead. The useful moment is *later*, on the edge where the credential goes dead → live.
* Nothing subscribes to that edge. The console knows when a rotation succeeds; the pipeline never hears about it.

## Scope

* **Detect the recovery edge**, not a timer. A rotation that writes a live credential is an event the console already produces (its receipt); this needs to reach the pipeline.
* **Re-drive what died of THIS cause only.** A gate that died with `401` / `is_error, 1 turn, $0` is recoverable; a gate that died on a real code failure is not, and must not be re-run into a green that means nothing.
* **Re-run the ORIGINAL** `pull_request` **run** — `gh run rerun <id> --failed`. **Never** `workflow_dispatch`: a hand-dispatched review writes its check to `main`, leaving the PR blocked to humans and the console while the gate believes itself satisfied. This trap has cost time twice and belongs in the implementation as a comment, not just here.
* **Bounded and logged.** One automatic thaw per head, and it says so on the PR. An unbounded thaw plus a still-sick credential is the medic↔critic loop [DRE-1921](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-1921/stop-self-inflicted-github-quota-burn-break-the-mediccritic-infra) already paid for once.

## Deliberately NOT in scope

Fixing the credential. That is the operator's, and [DRE-2592](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2592/the-break-glass-swap-script-hands-the-whole-fleet-a-credential-it) covers the writer that broke it. This card assumes the credential is healthy and only removes the human from the *resume*.

## Sequencing note

Pairs with [DRE-2439](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2439/stop-retrying-into-a-dead-credential-freeze-repairs-until-it-is) — freeze and thaw are one behaviour split for reviewability, and shipping the freeze alone makes stalls **longer**, not shorter. Whichever goes first, the second should follow immediately.

Filed under Wave 5 because *"every verdict gets an owner"* is exactly this: a crashed critic produces no verdict, and today nobody owns re-obtaining it. **Candidate to pull forward** — it has cost 38 minutes twice in 20 hours, and the wave that owns it is five waves out. That is the CEO's call, not mine.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A gate that died on a credential fault re-runs itself once the credential is live, with no human action
- [ ] Recovery is triggered by the credential-healthy edge, not a fixed delay
- [ ] Gates that died of real failures are **not** re-run — proven by a test
- [ ] The re-run targets the original `pull_request` run, never a fresh dispatch
- [ ] Bounded per head, and visible on the PR
- [ ] **Observed in production:** a credential outage recovers with nobody touching a run

cards.title: "Done" means merged, but the programme's own law says it means observed — every card with a production-observation criterion auto-closes before meeting it
cards.description:
Found while shipping Wave 1 Step 1. Filed under **Wave 2**, whose subject is exactly this — truth and state ownership — rather than fixed inside Step 1, because it is a pipeline behaviour change and not a plumbing edit.

## The contradiction, in two sentences from our own documents

`linear-sync.yml` sets a card **Done** on the merge event. The programme's endorsed law says:

> **A card is not Done when it merges — it is Done when someone has seen it work in production.**

Both are currently true of the system, and they disagree. `linear-sync` is *right* about merging — it is ground truth for that, deliberately, so no agent can claim a merge that did not happen (and that property must not be lost). It is simply **not evidence about observation**, and nothing distinguishes the two.

## The concrete instance

[DRE-2586](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2586/step-1b-agent-bureau-adopts-the-shared-node-plumbing-and-the-burn-cut) merged 2026-08-20 10:50:40 PT; `linear-sync` set it Done at 10:50:56 PT. Its final acceptance item —

> - [ ] **Observed in production:** a later PR run shows a `node_modules` cache hit with install skipped

— **was not met, and could not have been.** Actions caches are branch-scoped, so the observation is only possible on a *later* PR reading the cache the merge seeded. The card's own text says so explicitly. It was closed 16 seconds after merge regardless.

## Why this is more than bookkeeping

**This is a plausible mechanism for Wave 0's headline failure.** Wave 0 shipped ten cards and observed two working in production, and its post-mortem treated that as a discipline problem. But if every card auto-closes on merge, the queue of "merged, not yet observed" work **has no home and no name** — nothing lists it, nothing nags, and the board reads 10/10 complete. Discipline is being asked to do a job the state machine actively works against.

It also silently weakens every wave's exit test. Wave 1's demands "a production observation per deliverable"; a lane that cannot represent *merged-but-unobserved* means that test is graded by whoever remembers to look.

## The SECOND face of the same mechanism — partial scope closes a whole card (added 2026-08-26)

The contradiction above is about *observation* criteria falling through. There is a second one with the same root, found the hard way today, and any fix should address both or say why not.

`linear-sync` **reads the card id out of the branch name.** So an `agent/DRE-N-*` branch is an implicit promise that the PR completes **all** of DRE-N. A PR that satisfies three of six acceptance items still closes the card on merge, and the other three lose their home in the same instant.

**The concrete instance. **[DRE-2759](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2759/promotion-fills-to-the-wip-cap-and-ignores-phase-order-phase-4-is) was written with six acceptance items — an immediate stopgap *and* the permanent fix — and its own text said *"Immediate stopgap, in this card's first commit."* That sentence guaranteed the failure: the first PR was designed to satisfy item 1 of 6, and merging it would have marked five unbuilt items Done under a closed card. It compounded when the stopgap turned out to be the wrong mechanism and the PR was reduced to a two-file monitor fix still attached to a six-item card.

**The critic caught it, twice, and was right both times** (agent-bureau PR #2144, closed 2026-08-26; the fix re-filed as [DRE-2769](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2769/a-zero-wip-cap-makes-wip-health-nag-forever-a-deliberate-hold-reads-as)). So the gate works — this is about not handing it avoidable work.

### The rule this implies, whatever the fix

**A card is one mergeable unit.** If a card's acceptance items will land in different PRs, it is more than one card. The tell at authoring time is any phrase like *"in this card's first commit"* or *"immediate stopgap, the fix is below"* — that is the moment to split, not after CI refuses.

### What it changes about the options below

Option 2's `awaiting-observation` label does **not** cover this face: the items left behind are unbuilt, not unobserved. Either the fix distinguishes "merged but unobserved" from "merged but incomplete", or this half stays a discipline problem — which is exactly what the section above argues does not work.

Worth considering as a cheap addition to whichever option lands: **the merge gate reads the card's acceptance checklist and refuses to close it while items are unticked**, leaving the card open with the PR merged. That keeps `linear-sync` as ground truth for the merge while removing its unearned claim about completeness.

## Shape of a fix — deliberately not decided here

This is a **CEO-visible lane change**, so the options go up rather than get chosen by an agent:

1. **A terminal-but-unverified state.** Merge moves the card to something like `Merged` / `In Verification`, not `Done`; a separate signal (an observation comment, a reconcile check, a human) moves it to Done. Highest fidelity, most disruptive — the CEO's "needs you" queue and every board view change shape.
2. **Done stays, plus an **`awaiting-observation` **label** applied at merge when the card's body carries an observation criterion, and cleared when the observation is recorded. Cheap, non-disruptive, keeps the queue nameable and listable. Reconcile can nag on age.
3. **Nothing changes; the exit test carries it.** Honest option, recorded so it is a decision: the wave's closing ceremony diffs merged-vs-observed by hand. It is what happens today, and Wave 0 is the evidence of how well it works.

**Recommendation: (2).** It creates the missing queue without touching the lanes the CEO reads, and it is reversible. **Strongest argument against:** a label nobody clears becomes noise, and Wave 0's whole diagnosis was that we already have mechanisms nobody reads — so it needs the nag, or it is decoration.

## Not to be broken by any fix

* `linear-sync` remains the **only** thing that closes cards on merge evidence. No agent-claimed completion — that property is why it exists.
* No gate may block a merge on an observation: observation is by definition after the merge, and a gate that waits for it would deadlock the pipeline.
* Autonomy by default. This must not become a human approval step on every card.

## Acceptance

- [ ] The chosen option is recorded with its date and its rejected alternatives
- [ ] Merged-but-unobserved work is **listable** — a query, a lane, or a label, not a memory
- [ ] `linear-sync` still closes on merge evidence alone, with no agent claim in the path
- [ ] [DRE-2586](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2586/step-1b-agent-bureau-adopts-the-shared-node-plumbing-and-the-burn-cut) is the first test case: its observation lands, and the mechanism reflects it
- [ ] Observed working on a real card, not asserted by a test

cards.title: Every project slug is hand-copied into five presentation files — and bureau-pipeline is already missing from four
cards.description:
The **routing** plane is generated from `config/repo-map.json` — six mirrors, regenerated by `make sync-mirrors`, gated in CI (`ci.yml:91`). That work is done and it works.

The **presentation** plane was never included. Five files each carry a hand-maintained per-slug map, with no generator and no parity test:

| file | symbol | slugs |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `console/backend/sources.py:176` | `PROJECT_IDENTITIES` | 7 |
| `console/web/src/components/cards/repoLabel.ts:22` | `REPO_DISPLAY_NAMES` | 5 |
| `console/web/src/components/chat/projectColors.ts:17` | `SLUG_TO_TOKEN` | 6 |
| `console/web/src/theme/tokens.css:130-143` | `--project-*` | 6 |
| `console/web/src/components/atoms/ColorSwatchPicker.tsx:28` | `PROJECT_SWATCHES` | 6 |

## It has already drifted

`bureau-pipeline` **— a live routable slug that dispatches agents today — is missing from four of the five.** No board chip name, no colour token, no swatch. `agent-bureau-demo` is missing from `repoLabel.ts`.

So a card on the repo that hosts the entire fleet's pipeline renders unnamed and uncoloured in the console.

## This was predicted in writing

`architecture/project-registry-plan.md:45-55` lists this exact cluster as "all HAND today." It still is. Two other files on that list (`cardMeta.ts`, `demo_library.py`) **have** since been folded into the generator — the plan document is now the stale copy on that point.

## What to change

Extend `scripts/sync_repo_mirrors.py` to cover these five the same way it already covers the routing six: `BEGIN generated` / `END generated` markers, regenerated from one source, `--check` in CI.

The open question is what the source should be, since display name / colour token / swatch are not in `repo-map.json` today. Cheapest shape is to widen the snapshot from `{slug: "owner/repo"}` to carry `displayName` and `colorToken` per slug — one file, one edit per new project. Confirm that against [DRE-2576](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2576/the-routing-record-lives-in-four-stores-and-two-scripts-disagree-on) first, since that card may move which file is canonical.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All five maps generated from one source, with `BEGIN generated` markers
- [ ] `make sync-mirrors --check` covers them and runs in CI
- [ ] `bureau-pipeline` and `agent-bureau-demo` present everywhere — the current drift is closed by the generator, not by hand
- [ ] Adding a slug to the source and running the generator is sufficient to make it render correctly in the console
- [ ] `project-registry-plan.md`'s stale "HAND today" rows corrected

cards.title: The standards drift gate cannot fail, and its self-heal cannot merge
cards.description:
`standards-sync.yml` generates the `dreadnought-standards` plugin skills from `bureau-pipeline/standards/`. The generator is good. Both of its safety properties are inoperative.

## 1. The check runs only where it cannot fail

`standards-sync.yml:16-20` triggers on `workflow_dispatch` and a nightly cron — **there is no** `pull_request` **trigger.** And the job **regenerates at** `:48-51` **before checking at** `:58-61`, so the check is always comparing freshly generated output against itself. It passes by construction.

The workflow says so itself at `:12-14`: *"Nothing here gates ordinary agent-bureau PRs."*

Consequence: a hand edit to a file stamped "GENERATED — do NOT hand-edit" ships clean through CI.

## 2. The nightly self-heal cannot merge its own fix

When the cron does find drift it opens a PR on `branch: bot/standards-sync` (`standards-sync.yml:85`). But `merge-gate.yml:126` matches only `agent/*|repair/*|dependabot/*`.

So `bot/*` gets **no merge gate, no fix agent, no auto-Done** — the exact trap documented in CLAUDE.md. Every drift the alarm catches needs a human to notice a PR nobody is told about.

## What to change

1. Add `pull_request` to the triggers, **check-only** — no regenerate step on that path, or it passes by construction again.
2. Move the repair branch from `bot/standards-sync` to `agent/*` (or `repair/*`) so the pipeline can actually merge it.

## Related finding, same file, worth folding in

`sync_standards_skills.py:53-111` ships **5 of the 9** files in `bureau-pipeline/standards/`. Omitted: `console-honesty.md`, `design-parity.md`, `untrusted-content.md`, `vendor-boundaries.md`.

`untrusted-content.md` is universal on the CI rail — `assemble_context.py:101` describes it as required for *"EVERY role that reads text authored outside the trust boundary"* — and it reaches **no** interactive surface. Nothing flags the omission. Either ship all nine or make the exclusion list explicit and tested.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A hand edit to a generated SKILL.md fails a pull request
- [ ] The check path does not regenerate before comparing
- [ ] The repair PR lands on a branch the merge gate matches, verified by one real drift-and-heal cycle
- [ ] The 5-of-9 selection is either completed or made explicit with a test asserting the intended set

cards.title: The model-drift alarm has never once succeeded — it pushes to a protected branch and degrades to an empty catalog
cards.description:
`bureau-pipeline/.github/workflows/model-drift.yml` has run **exactly twice** — 2026-08-10 and 2026-08-17 — and **both failed**, at the final step:

```
remote: error: GH006: Protected branch update failed for refs/heads/main
```

It tries to push its refreshed snapshot straight to a protected `main`. It cannot, and never could.

Two failures stacked on top of each other:

1. **It cannot write.** Direct push to protected `main` is rejected.
2. **Its input is empty.** Every entry in `config/models.json` reads `in_catalog: false`, meaning the catalog fetch is also returning nothing. `model-drift.yml:90-99` treats an empty catalog as a **warning** and keeps the job green, so even the fetch failure is invisible.

`models.json`'s only two commits are hand-authored (2026-08-09, 2026-08-12). Nothing has ever been machine-refreshed.

## Why this matters more than a broken cron

**A dead alarm reads as "no drift."** That is the exact failure `bureau-pipeline/monitors/routing_drift.py:19-21` was written to avoid, in the same repo.

And the incident it guards against already happened: the model ladder auto-promoted every build agent to Fable the moment Anthropic enabled it, drained the account, and parked good cards. The lesson recorded from that was *availability is not permission* — which is precisely what a working model-drift alarm is supposed to enforce. It has been silently offline for the entire period since.

## What to change

1. **Give it a way to write.** Open a PR on an `agent/DRE-<n>-<slug>` branch instead of pushing to `main`. Note `bot/*` will not work either — `merge-gate.yml:126` only matches `agent/*|repair/*|dependabot/*`, so a `bot/*` branch gets no merge gate and the PR sits forever.
2. **Make an empty catalog fail loudly.** `model-drift.yml:90-99` currently warns and stays green. An alarm whose input is empty must go red — otherwise it reports health it cannot possibly have observed.
3. Confirm why the catalog fetch returns nothing (auth? endpoint? shape change?) before trusting the first green run.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Cause of the empty catalog identified and stated
- [ ] An empty or unparseable catalog fails the job
- [ ] The refresh lands via a PR on a branch the merge gate actually matches
- [ ] One successful end-to-end run, with `models.json` showing `in_catalog: true` for at least the current models
- [ ] A deliberately stale `models.json` makes the job go red — verified, not assumed
