cards.title: The routing record lives in four stores and two scripts disagree on which is canonical
cards.description:
One fact — which repo a slug means — is stored in four places, and the code contradicts itself about which one is authoritative.

## The contradiction, in the repo's own words

* `scripts/check_routing.py:6` calls **bureau-pipeline's** `config/repo-map.json` *"THE routing record (operator-ratified, plan D1)"*
* `scripts/sync_repo_mirrors.py:19` calls **agent-bureau's** `config/repo-map.json` *"the single canonical routing snapshot"*

Both cannot be the single source. And `make sync-mirrors` generates the five downstream mirrors from agent-bureau's copy — so if bureau-pipeline's is canonical, the generator derives from the wrong file.

## The four stores

| store | how it changes |
| -- | -- |
| `bureau-pipeline/config/repo-map.json` | by PR |
| `agent-bureau/config/repo-map.json` | by PR, + regenerates 5 mirrors |
| SSM `/bureau/relay/repo-map` | **hand-edited by operators** |
| `REPO_MAP` env var on both relay Lambdas | set from agent-bureau's file at deploy |

`cloud/relay/deploy.sh:212` seeds SSM **once and then never touches it**, commented: *"operators onboard customers by editing this parameter, and a deploy must not clobber those live edits."* So SSM is a genuine independent writer that no automation reconciles.

`check_routing.py` exists solely to detect the resulting three-way drift. **A drift detector is a confession that the design has more than one writer** — the exact thing the "one writer per fact" ADR on PR #2054 forbids.

Confirmed live 2026-08-20: all four held identical content, so nothing is broken today. The problem is that staying identical depends on nobody forgetting.

## Proposed shape — this removes stores, it does not add one

1. **One authored file.** Recommend bureau-pipeline's, since every repo already consumes that pipeline and `check_routing.py` already names it canonical.
2. **SSM becomes derived.** A small push step writes it from the canonical file on merge; operators stop hand-editing it. This does **not** reintroduce "redeploy per customer" ([DRE-1624](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-1624/featrelay-read-repo-routing-from-ssm-at-runtime-data-driven-no)'s actual concern) — it is a parameter write, not a Lambda deploy.
3. **agent-bureau's copy stops being a source** — deleted and fetched in CI, or kept as a cache that CI *fails the build* on drift. Never hand-edited.
4. The five generated mirrors stay exactly as they are. Those are already derived correctly ([DRE-1778](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-1778/generate-the-4-project-slug-mirrors-from-configrepo-mapjson-kill-the) did that work).
5. `check_routing.py` becomes a CI gate, and eventually redundant — derived copies cannot drift.

Net: **one place a human types a slug.**

## The trade to accept deliberately

Onboarding a customer becomes "merge a PR" rather than "edit SSM live" — minutes slower, but auditable and incapable of drifting. Onboarding is rare; drift is permanent.

## Sequencing and risk

**High blast radius: a malformed routing value kills dispatch for every repo in the fleet.** Do not bundle this with anything. Also fold in [DRE-2575](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2575/take-vericorr-out-of-the-agent-routing-dispatch-there-would-auto-merge)'s leftover: `vericorr` was removed from SSM on 2026-08-20 but deliberately left in both `config/repo-map.json` files, so there is known drift to reconcile as part of this — do not "fix" it by re-adding the slug.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Exactly one file is authored by hand; every other copy is generated or written by automation
- [ ] The canonical file is named identically in `check_routing.py` and `sync_repo_mirrors.py` — the contradiction is gone
- [ ] SSM is written by automation from the canonical file; no runbook step tells an operator to edit it
- [ ] The vericorr drift from [DRE-2575](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2575/take-vericorr-out-of-the-agent-routing-dispatch-there-would-auto-merge) is reconciled by removal, not restoration
- [ ] A drift check runs in CI rather than on request
- [ ] Onboarding a new slug is documented as one edit in one file

cards.title: [EPIC] The ~25 deprecated-runtime Lambdas in EveryBite's account — 2 on nodejs16, 8 on nodejs18, and no owner
cards.description:
[DRE-2474](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2474/epic-portico-off-nodejs20x-deprecated-in-april-blocks-cdk-deploy-in) named this and deliberately left it: *"Portico is 12 of 47 functions on deprecated runtimes across the three accounts. The other 35 sit outside this repo and need their own owner. Worth a separate epic; naming it here so the number is not lost."* This is that epic.

**Do not dispatch this card yet.** Step one is a question, not a code change — see below.

## What is actually there

Read live 2026-08-20 with `aws lambda list-functions --profile everybite-admin --region us-east-1`. Two things to note before reading the list: the `default` AWS profile resolves to this **same account**, and `us-west-2` in it is clean.

**nodejs16.x — deprecated June 2024, two years past support**

```
AthenaWidgetQuery
customWidgetAthenaQuery-js
```

**nodejs18.x — Cognito triggers, production and stage**

```
everybite-prod-presignup          everybite-stage-presignup
everybite-prod-postconfirm        everybite-stage-postconfirm
everybite-prod-postauthentication everybite-stage-postAuthentication
everybite-stage-preview-postConfirmation
everybite-staging-preview-preSignUp
```

**nodejs20.x — the self-serving auth-challenge set, plus two others**

```
self-serving-{,prod-,stage-}create-auth-challenge
self-serving-{,prod-,stage-}define-auth-challenge
self-serving-{,prod-,stage-}verify-auth-challenge
self-serving-stage-post-sign-up      self-serving-stage-pre-sign-up
exportS3ALBLogs
DocsComments-everybite-{Ingest,Coalescer,SesBounce}Fn
```

The three `DocsComments-everybite-*` functions are **already tracked by** [DRE-2485](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2485/the-three-lambdas-in-libparts-are-still-nodejs20x-ingestfn-coalescerfn) and are not in this epic's scope — they are portico's, they just live in this account.

## Why the ordering is not what the deadline suggests

The nodejs20 deadline (2027-03-03) is the one the rest of the fleet has been working to, but **nodejs16 and nodejs18 are already past end of support** — no security patching, and Lambda already blocks creation on them. The eight nodejs18 functions are **Cognito sign-up, sign-in and post-confirmation triggers in production**: if one fails to start, users cannot register or log in. That is a fail-closed path on an unsupported runtime, which makes it the most exposed thing on this list despite having no upcoming date attached.

## The blocking question — this is why the card is not dispatchable

**These functions are not in a repo on the platform list.** `menu-sync-to-everybite-*`, `self-serving-*`, `spreadsheet-analyzer-*`, `olo-vendor-export-*` and `everybite-{prod,stage}-*` do not correspond to `agent-bureau`, `bureau-pipeline`, `portico`, `vericorr`, `atlas`, `deltasolv` or `project-template`. Several look Serverless-Framework-managed rather than CDK, judging by the `service-stage-function` naming.

So before any code card can exist:

1. **Which repos own these functions?** They may not be under `dreadnought-foundry` at all.
2. **Are those repos on the platform?** If not, the platform's reach does not extend to them and the CEO has to decide who does the work — this cannot be answered by an agent.
3. **Which are still live?** `everybite-stage-preview-*` and `everybite-staging-preview-*` read like abandoned preview environments. A function nobody calls should be deleted, not upgraded, and deleting is cheaper than migrating.

Question 3 is worth doing first regardless of the answers to 1 and 2: CloudWatch invocation counts over 90 days would likely retire a meaningful share of this list at no risk.

## Proposed shape, once the questions are answered

Split by blast radius, not by runtime version:

* **The nodejs18 Cognito triggers** — fail-closed on sign-in, so one card, its own deploy, prod after stage is proven.
* **The self-serving auth-challenge set** — also auth, but custom-challenge flows; group by service.
* **nodejs16 +** `exportS3ALBLogs` **+ the Athena widgets** — low blast radius, batch them.
* **Anything with no invocations in 90 days** — a deletion card, not an upgrade card.

## Acceptance criteria for THIS epic

- [ ] Every function above mapped to a repo, or explicitly marked "no repo found"
- [ ] Each owning repo marked on-platform or off-platform
- [ ] 90-day invocation counts recorded per function, and the dead ones separated out
- [ ] CEO decision recorded on who owns the off-platform work
- [ ] Child cards created for what survives that triage — and not before

## What this epic is not

Not a request to change anything in EveryBite's estate. It is the inventory and the ownership question that [DRE-2474](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2474/epic-portico-off-nodejs20x-deprecated-in-april-blocks-cdk-deploy-in) said someone had to ask.

cards.title: Prove UI in the workbench console before shipping it — the second environment exists to be used
cards.description:
**Operator, 2026-08-20:** *"Now that we have the two environments set up, you should prove it works in the UI benchmark before we ship it. That way we know it works."*

Correct, and it is the answer to a defect that shipped twice in one evening.

## The evidence for it, from one feature

[DRE-2556](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2556/the-console-cannot-tell-you-which-code-you-are-looking-at-mark-the) shipped a sidebar marker. **Two layout defects reached** `main`, and a human found both by looking at a screen:

|  |  |
| -- | -- |
| First (QA caught it) | the **version** rendered at `width: 0` on any real branch name |
| My fix | gave the version `shrink-0` and let the branch truncate |
| Second (the operator caught it) | the **branch pill** now renders at `width: 0` — same bug, mirrored |

**62 unit tests passed through all of it**, including a guard written specifically for it. jsdom has no layout engine, so every bounding box is 0 and a collapsed element is indistinguishable from a rendered one.

**A second environment was standing there the whole time and was never used to look.**

## The rule

> **A change to the console is not ready to ship until it has been rendered and read in a running console.**

Not *tests green*. Not *the diff is right*. **Loaded in a browser, and the element it changes measured.**

## Why the workbench console specifically

It is already the right shape for this:

* **it exists and runs** — `:5273`, up for days, no setup cost
* **it is not** `main`, so proving something there does not require the change to have shipped
* **it is bind-mounted**, so a branch's code appears on disk with no rebuild
* **the design system lives there**, which is where UI work is authored anyway

That last point is the real argument: **the environment built for looking at design work is the one that should have been looked at.**

## And the honest caveat, or this becomes a fifth never-invoked mechanism

**The workbench console was 86 commits behind** `main` **tonight** and did not contain the code under test. A proving ground that silently drifts out of date proves nothing — it becomes another mechanism that exists and does not do its job.

So the rule needs a companion, and it is the harder half:

* **the workbench console must be current before it is trusted**, and something must say when it is not
* the branch/sha marker ([DRE-2556](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2556/the-console-cannot-tell-you-which-code-you-are-looking-at-mark-the), once [DRE-2568](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2568/the-branch-pill-renders-at-width-0-and-the-favicon-is-monochrome-the) makes it visible) is exactly that signal — **the console will state which code it is serving**, so "I checked it in the workbench" becomes verifiable rather than asserted

**Without the marker this rule is unenforceable**, which is why the two cards belong together.

## Relationship to [DRE-2565](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2565/a-60-second-browser-smoke-before-the-pr-stop-spending-the-verifier-on)

They are the same insight at two levels of formality:

* **this card** is the *habit* — a human loads it and looks, and it costs a minute
* [DRE-2565](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2565/a-60-second-browser-smoke-before-the-pr-stop-spending-the-verifier-on) is the *gate* — a scripted 60-second browser check that asserts `isVisible()`

Per [DRE-2536](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2536/the-learning-ledger-make-a-lesson-survive-as-a-test-and-measure)'s hierarchy the gate is worth more, since a habit can be skipped. **But the habit is available tonight and the gate is not**, and tonight's defect would have been caught by either.

## Scope

1. **Write the rule down** where it reaches the people and agents doing console work — a line in the standards, since `bureau-pipeline/standards/` is the single source that reaches every surface.
2. **State what "proved" means**: the element was rendered and *measured*, not merely present. `toBeInTheDocument()` was true for a zero-width pill.
3. **Say how to tell the workbench is current** — read the marker, do not assume.
4. **Name the exception**: a change that cannot be seen in a console (a backend-only field, a migration) is proved by its own means, and saying so keeps the rule from being ignored wholesale the first time it does not apply.

## Acceptance

- [ ] The rule is in the shared standards, with what "proved" requires
- [ ] It names the marker as the way to confirm the workbench is current
- [ ] It states the exception, so the rule survives the first case it does not fit
- [ ] Applied once, visibly, on the [DRE-2568](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2568/the-branch-pill-renders-at-width-0-and-the-favicon-is-monochrome-the) fix — **that fix is proved in the workbench console before it ships**, which is both the first use and the best possible test of the rule

## Not in scope

The `bureau-pipeline/standards/` edit is a different repo. Per [DRE-2545](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2545/the-same-pr-document-rule-must-reach-the-build-agents-not-just-this), one card per repo — the sibling gets filed when this one starts.

cards.title: The branch pill renders at width 0 and the favicon is monochrome — the marker cannot actually distinguish two consoles
cards.description:
**Operator, minutes after** [DRE-2556](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2556/the-console-cannot-tell-you-which-code-you-are-looking-at-mark-the) **merged:** *"I don't see the icon on the tab, and I don't see any color tab... on the main version, it's not colored. I don't know what happened to the color."*

Both observations correct. Measured from the live DOM at `:5373`, not inferred:

```
envText:            "main"                  ← the text exists
envWidth:           0                       ← THE PILL IS ZERO WIDTH
envVisible:         false
toneAttr:           "green"
toneComputedBg:     rgb(20, 42, 29)         ← the green IS applied
verText:            "1.5.50+101 · d2a9150"
verWidth:           97                      ← the version survived
```

**The "green dot" in the screenshot is the pill's background at zero width.** The branch name is in the DOM, styled, toned, and invisible.

## Defect 1 — I fixed the overflow in the wrong direction

QA's FAIL on #2070 measured the *version* at `width: 0`. My fix gave the version `shrink-0` and let the branch truncate. **The collapse simply moved.** Same bug, mirrored, shipped.

`min-w-0 max-w-[6.5rem] overflow-hidden` on the Badge with `block truncate` inside gives the pill **no floor** — `min-w-0` explicitly permits zero.

### And flex tuning is not the fix

The row is **\~113–150px**. The content is `main` plus `1.5.50+101 · d2a9150` — the version alone measures **97px**, and a legible pill needs ~40px plus padding. **It does not fit, and no combination of shrink and truncate will make it fit.** Three iterations have now put the zero-width on each element in turn, which is the signal that the constraint is wrong rather than the CSS.

So the fix is **less content, not better flex**:

* **drop the sha** — `1.5.50+101` already encodes distance from the release, and the sha is one hover away in the `title`. That frees ~60px, which is the whole problem.
* **or stack** onto two lines — the pill above, the version below.
* **or shorten the pill** — first path segment only (`agent/…`, `ui/…`) with the full name in `title`.

**Whichever is chosen, the pill needs a minimum width and the version becomes the thing that yields.** The branch is the identity; the version is the detail. I had that backwards.

## Defect 2 — the favicon is monochrome, so it distinguishes nothing

`documentIdentity.ts` builds a data-URI SVG favicon and **does** vary the label — `aria-label="Agent Bureau — main"` — but the fill is `--mark: #1A1A1A`, or white in dark mode. **Every environment gets an identical-looking icon.**

The tab title works (`main · Agent Bureau`), so the surface is half right. But the design's whole argument for the favicon was that **it reads at a glance without reading** — the mistake happens while *switching* tabs, and a title has to be read. A monochrome icon that differs only in its accessible name is exactly as useful as no icon for that purpose.

**Tone the mark:** green for main, amber for a branch, red for unknown — the same `environmentTone` vocabulary the pill already uses, so colour stays a property of state.

## Why this got through, and it is the point of [DRE-2565](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2565/a-60-second-browser-smoke-before-the-pr-stop-spending-the-verifier-on)

**62 unit tests passed and still pass.** jsdom has no layout engine: `envWidth` is 0 there for every element, so a zero-width pill is indistinguishable from a rendered one. The class-contract guard I added asserts `truncate` is present and `shrink-0` is absent — **both true here, and both true of the broken state.**

> A test that cannot observe the failure cannot prevent it, however carefully it is written.

This is the second defect in one feature that only a browser could see, and the operator found both by looking at a screen. [DRE-2565](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2565/a-60-second-browser-smoke-before-the-pr-stop-spending-the-verifier-on)**'s 60-second browser smoke would have caught both**, and this card is the strongest available argument for building it.

## Acceptance

- [ ] The branch pill renders at a **non-zero, legible width** on `main`, on a long agent branch, and in the unknown state — asserted in a **browser**, on `getBoundingClientRect().width`
- [ ] The version also renders. If both cannot fit, the **content** is reduced rather than one silently collapsing
- [ ] A **minimum width** on the pill, so it can never reach zero again — the third iteration of this bug is the argument for a floor rather than a ratio
- [ ] The favicon is **visibly different** per environment, using `environmentTone`
- [ ] Verified by loading both consoles and reading the DOM — the same method that found this
- [ ] **Observed:** two tabs open, told apart without reading either title

## The honest note for the post-mortem

Three layout iterations, and I put the zero-width on the version, then on the branch. Each time I reasoned about flex behaviour instead of measuring the row. **The row's width was one** `getBoundingClientRect()` **away throughout** — the same defect class as every other error today: inference where measurement was free.

cards.title: git_describe_version caches its own failure — one transient miss pins the version to unknown forever
cards.description:
## ROOT CAUSE MEASURED 2026-08-20 — it is a timeout, and the cache turns it permanent

The card was filed on the theory that a transient failure gets memoised. That is half of it. The other half is *why* the call fails, and it is not transient at all:

| Call | Time in the dev container |
| -- | -- |
| `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` | **0.02s** |
| `git describe --tags --dirty --match 'agent-bureau-console-v[0-9]*' …` | **2.42s cold, 1.46–1.69s warm** |
| `_GIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | **2.0** |

So `describe` straddles the timeout. `rev-parse` never comes close, which is exactly why `consoleBranch` and `consoleBuildSha` are always right while `consoleSemver` is empty — the same code path, one call slow enough to be killed.

Then `@lru_cache` makes one marginal miss permanent for the process. Proven live on the workbench console: the field was empty, a container restart did **not** fix it, yet a fresh process in the same container returned the correct value —

```
docker exec -w /repo bureau-dev-work-back-1 python -c "from console.backend import build_info as b; print(b.build_semver())"
→ '1.5.50+131'
```

— while the running server kept answering `""`. Nothing is wrong with the parsing, the tag match, or the worktree; the value is simply a cached timeout.

**Why** `describe` **is slow here:** it walks history and refs over a bind-mounted git dir on macOS VirtioFS. Two seconds is a reasonable budget on a local disk and is not one here.

### What the fix has to cover

1. **Do not cache failures**, so a marginal miss self-heals on the next request instead of pinning the field for the process lifetime.
2. **Raise the timeout** — 2.0s is below the measured cost of the call, so today the code is asking for a result it will not wait for. A modest bound still matters: the docstring's promise that these stamps "never fail a request" also means never hanging one.
3. Consider computing it **off the request path** entirely, so no user request pays 1.5–2.5s for a value that changes only on deploy.

A negative-cache TTL satisfies 1 and 2 together and bounds the retry cost: at most one slow call per interval, and it recovers on its own.

---

Found within minutes of [DRE-2556](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2556/the-console-cannot-tell-you-which-code-you-are-looking-at-mark-the) merging, by checking the field actually rendered rather than trusting that it would.

## Proven by experiment, not inferred

|  |  |
| -- | -- |
| Live endpoint, first boot after merge | `consoleSemver: ""` |
| The same function, called directly **in the same container** | `'1.5.50+101'` |
| `git describe` run by hand in that container | `agent-bureau-console-v1.5.50-101-gd2a91500`, exit 0 |
| The resolver | correct — `return build_info.build_semver()` |
| **After one more** `docker restart`**, no code change** | `consoleSemver: "1.5.50+101"` |

Identical code, identical checkout, identical tags. **The only variable was the process.**

## The defect

```python
@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=1)
def git_describe_version() -> str:
    ...
    return _git_stdout("describe", "--tags", "--dirty", *matches)
```

`_git_stdout` returns `""` on **any** failure — no git binary, a timeout, a non-zero exit, a momentarily locked index. `lru_cache` **then stores that** `""` **for the life of the process.**

So a single transient miss at startup pins the field to unknown permanently. There is no retry, because from the cache's point of view the question has been answered.

Startup is precisely when the miss is most likely: the container had just been restarted seconds after a `git pull`, and `--dirty` runs a `diff-index` that can need to refresh `.git/index` — which the pull may still have been touching.

## Why it hid so well, and this is the interesting part

**The honesty path worked exactly as designed.** [DRE-2556](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2556/the-console-cannot-tell-you-which-code-you-are-looking-at-mark-the) deliberately renders an unknown semver as nothing rather than `0.0.0`, on the grounds that a plausible default is indistinguishable from a real answer. That was right.

**But a correct fallback masked a sticky failure.** The console truthfully said *"I don't know"* — and would have said it forever, with no error, no log line, and no way to tell a genuinely tagless checkout from a cached miss.

> **Failing safe is not the same as failing visibly.** A graceful degradation that never retries is indistinguishable from the condition it degrades for.

## `build_branch` has the same shape but not the same exposure

`git_head_branch()` is cached identically. It is less exposed because prod stamps `CONSOLE_BUILD_BRANCH` and locally the branch rarely fails to read — but **the mechanism is the same and should be fixed together.** `git_head_sha()` too, though it has the env-var path in prod.

## The fix, and the trap in it

**Cache the success; do not cache the failure.** An empty result should not be memoised.

**The trap:** the reason for `lru_cache` is real and must not be lost — *a request must never shell out*, and the comment in `build_info.py` says so. Retrying on every request would reintroduce exactly that. So the retry has to be bounded: retry a failure a small number of times, or once after a short interval, and **never per-request**.

Getting this wrong in the other direction turns a cosmetic stamp into a subprocess on the hot path — the `reconcile.py` fail-open→fail-closed inversion is the local precedent for over-correcting a real fix.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Red first: a stub where the first call fails and the second succeeds — asserting the second result is used, **not** the cached `""`
- [ ] Red first, the other direction: a **successful** result is still resolved **at most once**, so the no-shell-out-per-request contract holds. This is the assertion that stops the fix becoming a regression
- [ ] The retry is bounded and the bound is stated with its reasoning — not "retry until it works"
- [ ] Applied to `git_head_branch` and `git_head_sha` as well, since the shape is identical
- [ ] A genuinely tagless checkout is distinguishable from a failed read — in a log line at minimum, so "unknown" can be diagnosed rather than guessed at

## That last box is the one that matters beyond this bug

Today produced four instances of *an operation that could not report its own failure*, and this is a fifth in the product rather than in tooling. **An empty string carries no reason.** Whatever replaces it should make "no tag exists here" and "the read failed" tell-apart-able, because tonight the only way to distinguish them was to restart the container and watch the value change.

cards.title: A 60-second browser smoke before the PR — stop spending the Verifier on CSS overflow
cards.description:
**Operator, 2026-08-19:** *"Does it make any sense to run a quick verifier before we do the PR or another quick test to find these little things so we don't have to waste the cycle?"*

Yes — and the specific gap is **a browser**, not more tests.

## The case, measured

PR #2070 shipped a sidebar where a branch pill with `shrink-0` and no truncation pushed the version number to `width: 0` — present in the DOM, invisible. QA caught it by driving Playwright against a running console and reading `getBoundingClientRect()`:

| `consoleBranch` | pill width | version visible |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `main` | 28px | **yes** |
| `ui/workbench` | 78px | **yes** |
| `agent/DRE-2070-fix-thing` (24 chars) | 151px | **no** |
| the PR's own branch (51 chars) | 334px | **no** |

**40 sidebar unit tests passed while this was broken.** They still pass. They always would have.

## Why the existing tests could never have caught it

**jsdom has no layout engine.** Every bounding box is 0×0, so an element at `width: 0` is indistinguishable from a visible one. `toBeInTheDocument()` was true the whole time.

**So "write more unit tests" is not the remedy.** However many are added in that medium, none of them can see this. The defect class is *rendered visibility*, and only something that renders can observe it.

## What already exists, and what does not

`playwright ^1.62.1` is **already a devDependency.** What is missing is a harness: no `e2e/` directory, no make target, no fixture. QA had to stand one up from scratch, which is part of why its run took **14m6s**.

## Scope — deliberately narrow, and the narrowness is the point

**A smoke, not a suite.** Under 60 seconds, run before opening a PR that touches the console UI.

1. Boot the app against a **mocked GraphQL layer** — no backend, no database, no credentials. Fast and deterministic.
2. Assert `isVisible()`, never `toBeInTheDocument()`. The whole value is in the difference.
3. Sweep each element under test with **adversarial values**: the longest real string available, the empty string, the unknown state.

**Resist growing this into a full e2e suite.** A slow suite gets skipped, and a skipped check is a sixth never-invoked mechanism ([DRE-2564](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2564/scan-for-mechanisms-that-exist-and-never-run-the-declared-but-never)). If it stops running in under a minute it has failed regardless of what it asserts.

## The cheaper half, which costs nothing

**The Verifier's winning move was not a tool — it was the data.** It used *this PR's own branch name*: 51 characters, sitting in the prompt, free. The engineer mocked `main` and `ui/workbench`, both short, and the design mockup looked correct **because the inputs had been chosen to make it look correct.**

> **A mockup with hand-picked data is a demo, not a test.**

So this card has two deliverables, and the first is a habit rather than code: **when mocking anything, use the nastiest real value in reach.** No harness would have been needed here.

## The honest counter-argument

**QA already found it.** The question is not whether this class is catchable, but whether catching it 15 minutes earlier justifies the setup.

For: the Verifier is expensive and adversarial by design — **spending it on CSS overflow wastes a good reviewer**, and a cycle costs a ~14-minute run plus a fix round. Against: it is real work for a defect an existing gate already catches, and every new check is something else that can rot.

The tiebreaker is recurrence: **layout-visibility defects in a console UI will happen again.** A gate that catches a recurring class is worth more than its build cost; one that catches a one-off is not.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A single command, under 60 seconds, runnable before a PR
- [ ] It asserts **visibility**, and a test proving it FAILS on the #2070 defect — replay that exact commit
- [ ] It fails on the adversarial values (long, empty, unknown), not just the happy path
- [ ] Runs with no backend, no database, no credentials
- [ ] A stated rule that it stays a smoke — with the reason a slow one gets skipped
- [ ] The habit is written down: mock with the nastiest available real value

## Why it belongs to Wave 2

This is **KPI 5 — shift-left rate**: findings moving from the critic and the Verifier to something cheaper and earlier. That KPI is currently *unmeasured*, and this would be its first real mover. It also pairs with [DRE-2560](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2560/the-replayable-incident-corpus-a-fix-is-not-done-until-its-incident): the corpus records what broke, this catches the same class before a reviewer has to.

cards.title: Scan for mechanisms that exist and never run — the "declared but never invoked" check
cards.description:
**Operator, 2026-08-19:** *"Is it possible to build a critic agent like Dependabot that looks through all our operations and keeps everything up to date and finds holes in our process?"*

Yes — and **one check is worth more than the rest combined**, because it detects the *absence* of activity, which is the one thing no other signal can see.

> **A mechanism that exists, is correct, is tested, and never runs.**

## Five instances, all already documented, all the same shape

| Mechanism | State | Found |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `release-gate.yml` | **1 run in its life** (2026-07-21); `main` is 174 commits past `v5` | 2026-08-19 |
| `scripts/console_ports.py` | correct, tested — **hooks** `make front`**/**`make back`**, which nobody runs** | 2026-08-19 |
| `Plan Review` lane | **0 cards, ever**, across 1,750 | the diagnosis |
| watchdog signatures | **5 of 16 have never fired** | the diagnosis |
| Wave 0's five | built, tested, merged, **never once doing their job** | Wave 0 post-mortem |

**Every one was found by a human noticing, weeks or months late.** None was found by a mechanism. That is the gap.

And note the second row: **the guard against "two consoles" was built 2026-08-08 for exactly the confusion rediscovered on 2026-08-19.** It did not fire because the path it hooks fell out of use. **A guard on a path nobody takes is a guard that does not exist** — and nothing anywhere reports that.

## Why this check and not a general "process critic"

The temptation is an agent that reads everything and opines. **That produces noise, gets muted, and then misses the real thing.** KPI 3 is a live constraint — the sandbox alone once generated ~61 alarms/day and the fleet learned to ignore it.

So: **mechanical checks only, each provably true or false, no judgement.** Dependabot works because it has an oracle (a version registry). This check has one too: **run records**. It is not an opinion whether a workflow has executed in 30 days.

## The checks, in order of confidence

**1. Workflows with no run in N days** (highest confidence — pure `gh run list`). Compare against a declared expectation: *scheduled* → must have run recently; *event-driven* → must have run when its event last occurred. `release-gate.yml` fires on tag push, so the honest form is *"the engine advanced 174 commits and this never fired."*

**2. Lanes and states with no occupants.** `Plan Review`: 0 of 1,750. A state nothing enters is either dead or a bug, and both need a decision.

**3. Alarm signatures that have never fired.** 5 of 16. A watchdog that has never triggered is untested in production, whether or not it has unit tests.

**4. Monitors whose output nothing reads.** Harder — needs a consumer map. Wave 0's central finding, so worth the difficulty, but land 1–3 first.

## What it must NOT do

**Never conclude "unused, delete it."** A gate that has not fired may be *working perfectly* — a guard whose condition has not occurred is doing its job silently. **The finding is "this has not been exercised", not "this is dead."** Confusing them would delete the safety net.

**Never fire on a mechanism declared dormant.** Something explicitly marked *"expected quiet"* with a reason is not a finding. Without that escape hatch it becomes noise within a week and gets muted — and then it is the sixth never-invoked mechanism.

**Report, do not repair.** It files a card. A scanner that also "fixes" things is a second unreviewed writer in the estate.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Red first: a fixture with a workflow that has not run in N days while its trigger condition demonstrably occurred — asserting a finding
- [ ] Red first, the other direction: a workflow correctly quiet because its condition has **not** occurred produces **no** finding
- [ ] **Replayed against 2026-07-21 → 2026-08-19 and finds** `release-gate.yml` — the case that motivated it
- [ ] An explicit dormant-declaration mechanism, with a reason, that suppresses a finding
- [ ] Findings are cards, never automatic edits
- [ ] It checks **itself**: a scanner that stops running is the joke this card cannot afford

## That last box is not a joke

**This scanner is exactly the kind of mechanism it exists to find.** If it is scheduled and silently stops, nothing notices — and it will have become the sixth row in the table above. Whatever proves it alive must be independent of it: a heartbeat that something else watches, or a finding that is *expected* to appear and whose absence is itself alarming.

## Relationship to [DRE-2536](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2536/the-learning-ledger-make-a-lesson-survive-as-a-test-and-measure)

[DRE-2536](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2536/the-learning-ledger-make-a-lesson-survive-as-a-test-and-measure) is the ledger for lessons that **recur**. This is the check for mechanisms that **never ran at all** — the inverse, and invisible to a repeat-counter, because a thing that has never fired produces no findings to count.

The two together are the process critic: **one measures what keeps happening, the other what never started.**

cards.title: Generate the outage report from the receipts — the law must not depend on remembering
cards.description:
**Operator, 2026-08-19:** *"It would be better if we had a system that wrote the outages automatically instead of depending on someone to remember. You said earlier that remembering is a bad way to do it."*

Correct, and it applies to the law written the same evening ([DRE-2562](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2562/an-outage-must-produce-a-written-report-the-law-the-format-and-the-one)). **That law is a rule** — the weakest form in [DRE-2536](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2536/the-learning-ledger-make-a-lesson-survive-as-a-test-and-measure)'s hierarchy, and one a human has to recall while an outage is in progress, which is the moment they have least capacity for it.

**This is the release channel's failure shape exactly:** promotion there was correct, tested, well-built — and a human ritual. The ritual stopped after ten days and nothing noticed for a month. **A law that fires on recall will decay the same way, and the first missed report will be invisible.**

## The insight that makes this buildable

**An outage report has two halves, and only one needs a person.**

**Machine-derivable, entirely from run records:**

| Section | Source |
| -- | -- |
| Timeline | run `created_at` / `updated_at` / `conclusion` per attempt |
| Detection | the first failing run and its signature |
| **Time to detect / recover** | first symptom → first human action → first green |
| Blast radius | which repos and PRs had a gate failing, and for how long |
| Recovery receipts | when each surface returned, with turn counts |
| Fixes shipped | PRs merged in the window, with `mergedAt` |

**Needs judgement, cannot be generated:** ranked root causes · *why now* · **diagnoses tried and discarded** · what worked and must not regress · lessons and what each became.

So: **generate the skeleton and every receipt; leave the judgement sections as explicit, unmissable stubs.**

## Why this is stronger than a reminder

It does not remind anyone. **It opens a draft PR**, titled for the incident, with the timeline already filled and the judgement sections empty.

> **The incident is not closed until that PR merges.**

That converts *remember to write one* into *there is an open PR with your name on it* — a different and much stronger obligation, and one that is **visible when it is not done.** A missed report becomes an open PR sitting in the queue rather than an absence nobody can see.

**Absence is the enemy here.** Nothing can detect a report that was never written; anyone can see a stale open PR.

## What triggers it

Deliberately narrow to begin with — a generator that fires on ordinary flakes produces noise, gets muted, and then misses the real one (KPI 3 is a live constraint, not a theoretical one).

Start with the signature this incident had, which is unambiguous:

**the same terminal failure across ≥2 repos within one window** — that is a shared-mechanism fault by definition, and it is what "outage" means in the law.

Tonight's would have fired at **00:10:45Z**, when portico's critic failed with the identical signature agent-bureau's had at 00:07:54. **That is \~90 seconds after the second symptom and roughly 15 minutes before a human noticed** — so the generator is also the missing alarm (RC3 of the report).

## What it must not do

**Never invent the judgement half.** A generated *"root cause: credential expiry"* would be a plausible-sounding guess presented with the authority of an artefact — the exact defect this whole programme is about. Tonight's real RC1 (*a rotation with no liveness check*) is not derivable from any run record.

**Leave the stubs visibly empty.** A section reading *"(unfilled — the incident is not closed)"* is honest. A generated paragraph of hedged prose is worse than a blank, because it looks finished.

**Do not let it close the loop by itself.** A generator that writes and merges its own report produces a directory full of timelines nobody read, which is the archived-post-mortem outcome in a new costume.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Red first: given run records for a two-repo identical failure, a report is generated with the timeline, blast radius and both time-to-* figures correct
- [ ] Red first: the judgement sections are present and **visibly unfilled** — asserting no generated prose appears in them
- [ ] It opens a **draft PR**, does not merge, and names the incident
- [ ] Trigger tested in both directions: fires on a cross-repo shared failure; does **not** fire on a single flaky run
- [ ] Time-to-detect is computed from the **first symptom**, not from when the generator ran — otherwise it reports its own latency and always looks excellent
- [ ] **Replayed against tonight's incident** and produces a report matching the hand-written one on every machine-derivable section

## That last box is the real test

The hand-written report exists (`architecture/forensics/critic-oauth-fanout-2026-08-19.md`). **Replay the generator against the same window and diff it.** Anywhere it disagrees, one of them is wrong and it is worth knowing which — a generator validated only against synthetic fixtures proves it can format, not that it can observe.

cards.title: Every state chip must carry its own freshness — the console says "Critic crashed" while the critic is running
cards.description:
**Operator, 2026-08-19:** *"As soon as the critic starts running, it should propagate its state out to the console so we can see it. A lot of them don't do that, and then we just sit there. We can't tell if it's running or not."*

## Caught in the act, with both sides timestamped

|  |  |
| -- | -- |
| **Truth, 2026-08-20 00:37:42Z** | `QA Review` `in_progress` on PR #2068 |
| **Console, same moment** | *"Critic crashed — re-review needed"* |

**It is not that the console lacks a running state. It is showing a terminal state that is false**, with the same visual confidence as a true one.

The screenshot also shows #327 as *"Fix agent working"* — plausibly right, since portico's critic had just returned REQUEST_CHANGES. **So one chip was right and one was wrong and they looked identical.** That is the part that makes the surface unusable: there is no way to tell which kind you are looking at.

## The data already exists — this is a plumbing and freshness gap, not a feature gap

`console/backend/sources.py::_run_state()` already returns exactly what is needed:

> `"live"` while queued/in_progress, else its terminal conclusion

with a stamped vocabulary of `""` unknown · `live` · a terminal conclusion · `none`. So the backend can already say *the critic is running*. Something between that function and the chip is either not asking again, or not rendering `live`.

The likely mechanism, from `docker/docker-compose.yml`: a **900-second poll**, with a WS ingest consumer that exists to make updates *"arrive in real time instead of the 900s poll."* A chip computed once and held for up to fifteen minutes will be wrong for most of a critic run — which is roughly 3–5 minutes.

## The real fix is not a "running" chip

Adding a `live` state fixes today's symptom and leaves the class intact. **The class is that a chip cannot say how old its claim is**, so a reader cannot calibrate trust, and neither can anyone reading a screenshot later.

> **Every state element carries its own as-of time, and a stale claim renders as stale — never as current.**

That is `standards/console-honesty.md` rule 2 (*unknown shown as unknown, never last-known*) applied to the age of a claim rather than its absence. With an as-of stamp, a 14-minute-old "crashed" is visibly suspect; without one it is indistinguishable from a fresh one.

## Third instance of this exact rule, today

| Chip | Said | Reality |
| -- | -- | -- |
| [DRE-2509](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2509/reconnect-re-points-the-whole-fleet-without-recording-it-the-panel) | *"Fix agent working"* | the loop was **held**, ~12 hours |
| [DRE-2509](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2509/reconnect-re-points-the-whole-fleet-without-recording-it-the-panel) | *"Pipeline gave up"* ([DRE-2555](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2555/pipeline-gave-up-fires-on-a-card-that-never-gave-up-the-alert-reads)) | it had not — merged 18 min later |
| #2068 | *"Critic crashed"* | critic **running**, right now |

**Three violations of rule 1 — derive from truth, never infer from adjacent signals — in one day, in the same surface.** Not a coincidence: the surface has no notion of claim age, so every chip is structurally a guess about the present built from a past observation.

## And it caused a real wrong action, mine

Reading *"crashed"*, I tried to re-run the critic and got `run cannot be rerun; This workflow is already running`. **The stale chip produced a wrong action from a careful reader** — which is the strongest argument here: it is not merely uninformative, it actively misleads someone who is paying attention.

## Scope

1. **Render the** `live` **state** the backend already computes, for the critic and the fix loop — the immediate symptom.
2. **Give every state element an as-of timestamp**, surfaced (relative time is fine: "as of 14 min ago").
3. **Define a staleness horizon per state** and render past it as **unknown**, not as last-known. A critic run takes ~3–5 min, so a claim older than that is not evidence about now.
4. **Confirm whether workflow-run transitions reach the WS ingest path at all** — if they only arrive on the 900s poll, real-time is not available to this surface no matter how the chip is written. Measure it; do not assume.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Red first: a fixture where the newest run is `in_progress` and the previous one `failure` — asserting the chip reads **running**, not crashed
- [ ] Red first: a state older than its horizon renders as **unknown**, never as the last-known value
- [ ] Every chip on this surface exposes its as-of time
- [ ] A test per state element for the stale/absent case — `console-honesty` rule 3, which exists precisely so this is not optional
- [ ] Measured: the observed latency from a run starting to the chip changing, recorded with its method
- [ ] **Observed in production:** start a critic and watch the chip change without a manual refresh

## The trap

**Do not fix this by polling harder.** A 30-second poll makes the window smaller and the class survives — the chip still cannot say how old it is, and a reader still cannot tell a fresh claim from a stale one. **The freshness stamp is the fix; the faster feed is an optimisation.** Shipping only the poll change would look like a fix and leave the next screenshot just as untrustworthy.

cards.title: The replayable incident corpus — a fix is not done until its incident cannot recur silently
cards.description:
**Checked first: no corpus exists.** `architecture/forensics/` holds prose write-ups; `cloud/relay-gh/fixtures` is a unit-test directory for one component. There is nothing replayable, and no card. The programme's plan has called this Wave 2–3 work and **a precondition for Layer 4** since it was written.

## Why it is a precondition, not a nice-to-have

You cannot safely cut a boundary through `console/backend/schema.py` — **8,798 lines, 478 classes, 26 fix commits** — without a behavioural regression corpus. Layer 4's whole premise is *refactor or patch, per module, on evidence*, and the evidence that a refactor preserved behaviour is a suite that would have caught each historical incident.

Without it, Layer 4 is a rewrite with no safety net on the file every change already has to touch.

## The rule the corpus enforces

> **A fix is not done until its incident cannot recur silently.**

The history shows the same defect class re-fixed three to five times. In every case the missing artefact was the same: **a test that would have failed.** Recent, unambiguous examples:

* a turn ceiling set below the work — found **four times** in one week
* a console inferring state from an adjacent signal — **three** sightings
* `no-code` / `hand-built` / phase numbers — **three** labels in one day that meant something other than what they said

## Two things this corpus must do that most do not

### 1. Capture the behaviours that WORKED

During the 2026-08-19 credential outage ([DRE-2559](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2559/a-token-rotation-with-no-liveness-check-turned-one-dead-credential)) the merge gate said *"QA Critic could not run (infra error) — this is NOT a code rejection"* and held. **That is the one thing that went right**, and it had no test.

Wave 0's finding was five mechanisms that *never worked*. **The inverse risk is a mechanism that works today and is quietly broken by a refactor tomorrow** — and a corpus of failures alone leaves every working behaviour undefended. Since Layer 4's job is refactoring, that is precisely the exposure.

So the corpus holds both: *this must not happen again*, and *this must keep happening*.

### 2. Refuse fixtures that pin implementation

> Assert **behaviour**, not implementation — or the corpus blocks the refactor it exists to enable.

*"Given a dead credential, no secret is written"* survives a rewrite. *"The rotation calls* `token_live()`*"* does not, and would veto the very change the corpus is meant to make safe.

**This is not hypothetical:** an audit already found a live test **pinning the banned model** — a fixture that had industrialised a bug into a guarantee. A corpus built carelessly manufactures more of those, at scale, and each one is harder to remove than the bug it froze.

## THE PATTERN THAT CROSSED THE THRESHOLD ON 2026-08-19

**A green signal that proves nothing about reality — three independent instances in one day, in three different technologies.** Every one has the same shape: **the check asserts the ARTIFACT, not the RUNNING SYSTEM.**

| Where | The green thing | The reality |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `call / verify` on agent-bureau #2070 | check published `pass` | the Verifier's verdict was **FAIL** — the check reports that the gate RAN, not that it passed |
| 40 jsdom sidebar tests | all **passing** | the version rendered at `width: 0`, invisible. jsdom has no layout engine, so `toBeInTheDocument()` was true throughout |
| portico `lambda_runtime.test.ts` ([DRE-2485](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2485/the-three-lambdas-in-libparts-are-still-nodejs20x-ingestfn-coalescerfn)) | **16/16**, including a sweep asserting *"NO Lambda is on a superseded nodejs runtime"* | **six real functions run** `nodejs20.x` **in two live accounts.** The test synthesises a stack from the working tree and asserts the template |

**Three occurrences is past the threshold** [DRE-2536](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2536/the-learning-ledger-make-a-lesson-survive-as-a-test-and-measure) **sets** for a pattern to stop being a note and become a gate. And the portico case is the most instructive, because **the sweep was written specifically to catch this class and is green while the class is present** — a guard asserting the right thing about the wrong subject.

### What the corpus does with it

This is the strongest argument for the **behaviour-not-implementation rule** above, from the other direction: a fixture that asserts *the template says X* is implementation-pinning dressed as verification. It survives every rewrite and catches nothing.

So each of the three needs its fixture written against the **running system**:

* the verify check must **fail** when the verdict is FAIL — assert the published status, not that a job completed
* the sidebar must be asserted in a **browser**, on `isVisible()` — [DRE-2565](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2565/a-60-second-browser-smoke-before-the-pr-stop-spending-the-verifier-on)
* the runtime sweep must read `aws lambda list-functions`, not a synthesised template — [DRE-2485](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2485/the-three-lambdas-in-libparts-are-still-nodejs20x-ingestfn-coalescerfn)'s own definition of done already says *"verified by reading the live estate, not a template"*

### And the rule this yields

> **A test that can pass while production is broken is not a test of production.** State what each fixture asserts *about* — the artifact or the system — and never let the first stand in for the second.

That sentence is the corpus's reason to exist, and it took three same-day instances to say it plainly.

## What is explicitly NOT corpus material

**Authoring mistakes.** During the same outage the recovery tooling had four defects — suppressed stderr, backticks executing a command, an invented CLI flag, a silent no-op branch. Every one was *an operation that could not report its own failure*, which is the programme's central defect class.

They belong in the post-mortem's **author-errors** section, because they inform how the work is done. **They are not corpus entries**: the code does not exist anywhere, so it cannot regress. A corpus that absorbs them becomes a diary and loses the property that makes it useful — that every entry can go red.

## Scope

1. **A home and a format.** One fixture per incident, each stating: what happened, the behaviour asserted, and *desired* rather than observed behaviour.
2. **The format doubles as the card-as-trace record** the diagnosis layer needs — one piece of work, two payoffs. Design it once, for both.
3. **Seed from the documented incidents since June**, newest first, since the recent ones are still verifiable. Prefer few good fixtures to a large thin sweep.
4. **Every fixture demonstrated RED first** — a fixture that has never failed proves nothing about the code and nothing about itself.
5. **A convention for pairing:** each entry says whether it guards against a recurrence or protects a behaviour, because they are read differently.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A corpus directory with a README stating the format and the behaviour-not-implementation rule
- [ ] Each seeded fixture shown red against the code as it was, green against the code as it is
- [ ] At least one **protective** fixture (a behaviour that worked) alongside the regression ones
- [ ] The format is the one the diagnosis layer will consume — verified against that need, not assumed
- [ ] A stated rule that authoring mistakes go to post-mortems, not here
- [ ] The banned-model test is found and dealt with, as the worked example of the trap

## The measure of success

Not fixture count. **The share of critic findings whose pattern was seen before** — KPI 4, the repeat-finding rate. If the corpus works, that number falls and findings shift from the critic to CI (KPI 5, shift-left). Both are currently *unmeasured*, blocked on [DRE-2536](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2536/the-learning-ledger-make-a-lesson-survive-as-a-test-and-measure), and this card is a large part of what makes them move.

cards.title: Injected context has no ceiling and no writer — portico's CLAUDE.md is 491 lines and grew six times in four days
cards.description:
**Checked first, as asked: no open card covers this.** Wave 3 ([DRE-2516](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2516/wave-3-layer-1-silence-the-noise-and-fix-the-record)) had **zero children** before this one. The nearest matches are all closed and all about the retired v1 platform — see *Prior art* below, which is the most interesting part.

## Measured 2026-08-19, not cited

Every `CLAUDE.md` in the fleet, read from the live default branch:

| Repo | Lines | Bytes |
| -- | -- | -- |
| **portico** | **491** | 32,543 |
| vericorr | 290 | 15,752 |
| agent-bureau | 130 | 8,117 |
| atlas | 79 | 5,805 |
| **bureau-pipeline** | **none** | — |
| project-template | **none** | — |
| bureau-harness | none | — |
| deltasolv | none | — |

Shared `standards/` — injected into **every CI build agent, fleet-wide** — is **680 lines across 10 files** (engineering 100, vendor-boundaries 96, architecture 82, card-quality 78, README 67, untrusted-content 58, console-honesty 49, design 50, design-parity 51, comms 49).

**Worst case, one engineer agent on portico: 1,171 lines before it sees the card, the diff, or any code.**

## It is actively growing, and nothing measures that

The wave plan recorded portico at **457 lines**. It measures **491** today. `git log` on that file shows **six commits in four days** (2026-08-15 → 08-18).

So the file is churning fast, in the repo with **the fleet's worst stall rate (13.4%)**, and **no mechanism anywhere reports the growth.** Whether 457 was ever exactly right is not the point — the point is that a load-bearing figure moved by ~7% inside a week and the only reason anyone noticed is that someone happened to re-measure it by hand.

**Correlation is a hypothesis, not a proven cause.** Portico is also the newest and busiest repo. This card must not assume context bloat causes stalls — but it also must not keep the largest injected prompt in the fleet growing unobserved.

## Prior art — and this is the finding worth carrying

**This problem was solved before. Twice. Both solutions died with the platform they were built for.**

* [DRE-880](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-880/regime-aware-claudemd-overlay-claude-slim-challenger-54percent-smaller) (Done, 2026-05-12) — *"Regime-aware CLAUDE.md overlay + claude-slim challenger (**54% smaller**)"*. The v1 platform's `CLAUDE.md` was ~28KB / ~7–8k input tokens re-ingested by **every spawned worker**. A regime-driven swap plus a slim variant cut it by more than half.
* [DRE-1109](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-1109/document-or-consolidate-the-claudemd-overlay-system-devslimprod) (Done, 2026-05-19) — documented a **three-file overlay**: `CLAUDE.md` 37k, `CLAUDE-slim.md` 16k, `CLAUDE-prod.md` 1.9k, selected by the spawner.
* [DRE-1977](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-1977/fix-false-and-dead-claims-in-claudemd-and-docsprotocol-add-a-doc-path) (**Cancelled**) — *"Fix false and dead claims in CLAUDE.md, add a doc-path lint."* The lint that would have caught rot was filed and cancelled.

And there is a costed precedent in the record: `adr-cost-emergency-prompt-reduction.md` cut a `CLAUDE.md` from **201 → 35 lines as a cost emergency.** Portico's is now **2.4× the emergency figure**.

Per the house rule *copy, not rebuild*: **read** [DRE-880](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-880/regime-aware-claudemd-overlay-claude-slim-challenger-54percent-smaller)**'s approach before designing anything.** The v1 mechanism does not transplant (no spawner now; headless CI agents get context by workflow injection), but the sizing work, the slim/full split, and the measurements are all reusable.

## The structural problem underneath

`CLAUDE.md` **has no owner and no writer discipline.** Anyone fixing anything appends to it, which is why it only ever grows. Meanwhile:

* `bureau-pipeline` **— the engine every product depends on — has no** `CLAUDE.md` **at all.** An agent working on the machinery gets less guidance than one working on a product.
* `project-template` **has none either**, so every new repo starts empty and grows its own. That is how the fleet ended up with four different sizes and no shared shape.
* The **operator's** `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` is a fourth copy of overlapping rules and is **outside git entirely** — no PR, no test, no critic. Same class as branch protection: config nothing in a repo can reach. Out of scope here, recorded so it is not mistaken for covered.

## Scope

1. **A measured census in the repo**, not a one-off — line counts per repo plus the standards layer, so the number is re-derivable rather than remembered.
2. **A tested ceiling.** A test that fails when a `CLAUDE.md` exceeds N lines. The ceiling is the deliverable: a rule can be ignored, a test cannot ([DRE-2536](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2536/the-learning-ledger-make-a-lesson-survive-as-a-test-and-measure)'s hierarchy).
3. **Cut portico's to the ceiling**, keeping what is load-bearing. Every removal must say where the content went — deleted as dead, or moved to `standards/` where it belongs once.
4. **Give** `project-template` **a starting** `CLAUDE.md` so new repos inherit a shape instead of inventing one.
5. **Decide** `bureau-pipeline`**'s** — it having none is either a real gap or a deliberate choice, and nobody has said which.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Red first: a test that fails against portico's current 491-line file
- [ ] The ceiling is a number with a stated reason, not a round figure
- [ ] Portico's `CLAUDE.md` is under it, and **every cut line is accounted for** — deleted or relocated, never silently dropped
- [ ] The census is a script, so the next reader measures rather than trusts this card
- [ ] `project-template` ships a baseline
- [ ] A written decision on `bureau-pipeline` having none
- [ ] [DRE-880](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-880/regime-aware-claudemd-overlay-claude-slim-challenger-54percent-smaller)'s approach is read and cited — reused, adapted, or explicitly declined with a reason

## The trap to avoid

**Do not cut for the sake of the number.** These files exist because their contents were paid for in incidents; the fleet's habit of appending to them is a symptom of things genuinely needing to be said. A cut that removes a hard-won rule to satisfy a lint is worse than the bloat. **The right move for most content is relocation to** `standards/` — one canonical copy, injected where it is needed — not deletion. If a rule cannot be justified, say so and delete it deliberately; do not shave lines to pass a test.

cards.title: The `no-code` label means two different things — the doc says one, the gate does the other
cards.description:
Found live on 2026-08-19 while shipping [DRE-2545](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2545/the-same-pr-document-rule-must-reach-the-build-agents-not-just-this). Small, cheap, and a textbook producer/consumer drift.

## What happened

[DRE-2545](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2545/the-same-pr-document-rule-must-reach-the-build-agents-not-just-this) merged (`bureau-pipeline`#165, 12:56 PT) and the card stayed in **Backlog**. `linear-sync` reported `success`, and its log said precisely why:

```
AUTO-DONE SKIPPED for DRE-2545: this card carries the 'no-code' label — its
deliverable is live operator work (a deploy, a migration, a secret), which a
merged runbook PR does not perform.
The merge was commented on the card; its state is untouched.
(Six false closes in portico: DRE-2242 x2, DRE-2241, DRE-2218, DRE-2253, DRE-2252.)
```

**The gate is not the bug.** It is one of the better-built things in the fleet: it names its reason in plain language, it comments the merge on the card so the state is never *silently* wrong, and it cites the six incidents that paid for it. Nothing here should change its behaviour.

## The actual defect: the label means two different things

| Where | What `no-code` means |
| -- | -- |
| `docs/protocol/card-quality-standard.md:38` | *"*`no-code` *for operator/non-build cards"* |
| `linear-sync.yml` card-done guard | *the deliverable is live operator work a merge cannot perform* |

A pure-documentation card is **"non-build"** on the plain reading of the doc, and is **not** operator work — for a docs card the merge *is* the entire deliverable. So the two definitions disagree, and **the label's name agrees with the wrong one.**

That is how the mislabel happened: the author read the documented definition, applied it correctly against that definition, and got a card that could never close.

## Why this is worth fixing rather than remembering

* **It fails silently in the direction that looks like success.** Every check is green, the merge happened, the code is live — and the card sits in Backlog, which is the lane Wave 4 already knows nothing watches. It becomes indistinguishable from the ~104 never-dispatched cards.
* **A near-miss on the sibling card.** [DRE-2540](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2540/wave-post-mortems-need-a-home-and-a-change-that-contradicts-a-document) carried the same label and would have merged-and-stayed-open too. It closed only because the label was removed **11 seconds** before `linear-sync`'s card-done step read it (removal `20:01:47Z`, close `20:01:58Z`). That is timing, not design.
* **It is one line of documentation.** The gate's semantics are right; the words describing them are wrong.

## Scope — the cheap fix first

1. **Correct the definition** in `docs/protocol/card-quality-standard.md` so it states the implemented meaning: `no-code` = *the deliverable is live operator action (deploy, migration, secret, infra change) that merging a PR does not perform*. Explicitly say what it is **not**: a docs-only or config-only card whose merge IS the deliverable must not carry it.
2. **Name the counter-example**, since that is the half that would have prevented this: a runbook, ADR, or post-mortem card is *not* `no-code`.

## Worth considering, not required

**Rename the label** to something that cannot be misread — `needs-operator` or `operator-action`. `no-code` describes the *diff*; the gate cares about the *deliverable*. A label whose name argues for the wrong reading will keep producing this mistake, and per [DRE-2536](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2536/the-learning-ledger-make-a-lesson-survive-as-a-test-and-measure)'s hierarchy a name is a cheaper carrier of meaning than a rule.

Not doing it in this card because renaming a label touches every card carrying it plus the workflow that matches on it — that is a coordinated change, and this one should stay one line.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `card-quality-standard.md` defines `no-code` by its implemented meaning, not "non-build"
- [ ] It names the counter-example: docs/config-only cards, where the merge is the deliverable, do NOT get the label
- [ ] A rename is either done or explicitly declined with a reason recorded

## Not in scope

Changing `linear-sync`'s guard. It behaved correctly, said so, and left the card's state honest rather than guessing. That is the behaviour this programme is trying to produce everywhere else.

cards.title: A quiet mark on folders that carry guidance, so people know there is something to open
cards.description:
**Blocked by:** [DRE-2542](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2542/a-folders-details-rail-show-the-description-nobody-has-ever-seen) — the mark opens the details rail, and there is nothing to open until that rail exists.

**Design:** see the linked proposal, **mock 3**.

A folder that carries guidance says so, quietly, so a reader knows the rail has something in it. Without this the description is discoverable only by chance.

## Scope

One small mark on the folder card and the list row (`components/molecules/FolderCard.tsx`, `features/library/Rows.tsx`, `ListView.tsx`), **shown only on folders that have a description**. No description, no mark, no change — that is what keeps this from becoming clutter on hundreds of folders.

Clicking it opens the details rail from [DRE-2542](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2542/a-folders-details-rail-show-the-description-nobody-has-ever-seen).

`FolderCard` already carries optional adornments — `warning`, `draftCount`, access labelling — so this follows an established pattern rather than inventing one. Read how those are drawn and sit beside them; in particular do not compete with the amber warning treatment, which means something more urgent.

## The operator's constraint, verbatim

*"I don't want it to pollute the interface."* This card is the one most at risk of doing exactly that. If it cannot be made to disappear on folders without guidance, and to read as quiet on the ones with it, **say so and drop it** — the epic's other two cards deliver the feature without it. That is a legitimate outcome, not a failure.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Folders with a description show one small mark; folders without show nothing at all
- [ ] Activating it opens the details rail
- [ ] It does not compete visually with the existing warning or draft-count treatments
- [ ] Keyboard reachable with a meaningful accessible name — not "i"
- [ ] Both light and dark themes checked
- [ ] Grid and list views both handled

cards.title: Show the folder's guidance while someone is filing a document into it
cards.description:
**Design:** see the linked proposal, **mock 2**. Build to that.

**This is the card that changes behaviour, and it is worth more than its sibling.** A description in a panel is read once, by someone who went looking. The same sentence shown while a moderator is choosing where a document goes is read every time, by the person about to get it wrong — and it occupies no permanent interface at all.

## Where

Wherever a document's destination folder is chosen or changed:

* `client/app/src/features/library/AddDocumentModal/` — the add flow
* `client/app/src/features/library/MovePicker.tsx` and the move confirm in `features/library/dnd/` (`ConfirmOutwardMove` and neighbours)

Show the destination folder's `desc` as guidance, before the commit. That is this codebase's own standard — `Composer.tsx`'s header states it as *"state a consequence BEFORE the commit"*, and the add-document modal already states what will happen to a linked URL.

## The inheritance decision, and why it lives behind one function

The epic's default: **when the destination folder has no description of its own, show the nearest ancestor's.** If *External* says "everything here is visible to partners", that is exactly the warning someone filing three levels down needs, and nobody will have retyped it on every child.

**Put that lookup in one small pure function** (`nearestGuidance(folderId, tree)` or similar) in a `*_lib`-style module with its own tests. Two reasons: the repo's testing convention puts decisions in pure modules, and this is the assumption in the epic most likely to be reversed — behind one function, reversing it is a small diff rather than an archaeology exercise.

When the guidance is inherited rather than the folder's own, **say so** — "From External" or similar. A reader must be able to tell whether they are being told about the folder they picked or about the region it sits in.

## Do not

* Do not block, warn, or confirm. This is guidance, not enforcement — the epic's whole reasoning is that Portico cannot check what is in a document. Nothing here may look like a validation error.
* Do not show anything when there is no description and no ancestor with one. Silence is the default state.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Adding a document to a folder with guidance shows it before the commit
- [ ] Moving a document into one does the same
- [ ] The nearest-ancestor lookup is a pure, separately tested function
- [ ] Inherited guidance is visibly distinguished from the folder's own
- [ ] No guidance anywhere in the chain renders nothing at all — no empty box, no placeholder
- [ ] Nothing reads as a validation error or blocks the action
- [ ] Both light and dark themes checked

cards.title: A folder's Details rail — show the description nobody has ever seen
cards.description:
**Design:** see the linked proposal, **mock 1**. Build to that.

Open a folder's information and it tells you what the folder is for. The operator's original ask, in their words: *"when you open up information about that directory, it will tell you."*

## What already exists — do not rebuild it

* `desc?: string` on the folder row (`infra/lambda/items_lib.ts:126`), already populated for some folders and already editable via `EditDetailsDialog.tsx`. **Read it; do not add a field.**
* `client/app/src/features/viewer/railMode.ts` already defines three rail modes — `access`, `comments`, `details` — with titles, and its header explains why it is a MODE and not a set of booleans (a 352px column can only show one). **Read that header before adding any rail state.**
* The library already mounts a rail through a slot: `ChangeLogRailSlot` in `LibraryScreen.tsx:651`, component at `features/library/ChangeLogRail.tsx`. That is the pattern to follow.
* `RailFrame` is the existing frame component.

## Scope

A details rail for a **folder**, showing:

* the folder's description, given visual weight — it is the reason the rail exists, not a footnote
* a few facts worth having in the same place: document count, who it is visible to, last change

Reuse whatever the library already computes for access labelling (`lib/access/accessPeek.ts`, `accessLabelOf`) rather than deriving a second answer to "who can see this". Two code paths answering that question is how they drift.

**A folder with no description shows no empty-state noise.** Either the rail is not offered, or the section is simply absent — decide which reads better and say why in the PR. Do not draw a grey "No description" placeholder on hundreds of folders.

## Explicitly out of scope

* Editing the description here. `EditDetailsDialog` already does that; a second editor is a second thing to keep in sync.
* Any new field, any backend change, any rule-shaped metadata.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Opening a folder's details shows its description prominently
- [ ] A folder with no description produces no placeholder and no visual noise
- [ ] Access information reuses the existing access helpers rather than re-deriving them
- [ ] Rail state follows `railMode.ts`'s mode model — two rails cannot be open at once
- [ ] Keyboard reachable, focus visible, correct heading semantics
- [ ] Both light and dark themes checked
- [ ] No backend change; no new field on the row
