cards.title: [EPIC] Link-out documents — a file that lives elsewhere, indexed and gated by Portico
cards.description:
A Google Doc, Sheet or Slide deck can be added to a Portico library like any other document. Opening it shows a real Portico document screen — title, status, who shared it, the comment rail — with an Open button that takes the reader to the file where it actually lives, in a new tab. Google's own comments are used on the document itself; Portico keeps its own thread beside it for readers who cannot open the Google file at all. The same shape then covers .docx and .pptx by putting them in Drive, which renders them natively.

Decided by the operator 2026-08-18, in session. This answers [DRE-2311](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2311/decision-ceo-revisit-google-drive-read-only-mirror-or-createedit) with an option that card did not list.

## What this is NOT

**This is not Phase 6 and does not reopen it.** Phase 6 was mirroring *in*: a service account, the Drive API, a five-minute poll, a copy of the bytes in S3. It was cut on 2026-08-08 ([DRE-2173](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2173/decision-ceo-should-portico-use-google-drive-as-a-document-source)) and `infra/test/demo_phase6.test.ts` pins the cut — one of its mutation pairs is literally "filling the Drive seam with a Google API call FAILS the check".

**This is linking *out*.** A row that opens the file where it already is. No Google credential, no Workspace, no OAuth verification, no CASA, no service account. The compliance cost that killed Phase 6 does not attach to a hyperlink, and `parts/gdrive.ts` and `slots/gdrive.source.tsx` stay empty no-ops. Nobody working this epic should touch them.

## The four decisions this epic implements

1. **Hand-off, with the Portico screen kept.** Not a library row that jumps straight out — the reader gets a Portico document screen first. Costs one click and keeps the document's place in the library, its status, its audit trail, and somewhere to say who else can open it. It is also the pattern already shipped for PDFs (`client/app/src/features/viewer/panes/FilePane.tsx:182-189`), so this is a copy, not an invention.
2. **Two access systems, accepted and said out loud.** See below — this is the one real risk and it is being taken deliberately.
3. **Portico keeps its own comment thread** on these documents, relabelled so nobody confuses it with Google's.
4. **No Google credential, ever.** Portico cannot read the file's title, its modified time, or its sharing list. A moderator types the title; a dead link is a support message. If that bites in practice, *that* is the trigger to revisit — not now.

## The risk being accepted, in plain words

Everything Portico serves sits behind a fail-closed Lambda@Edge gate: a session cookie, a Cognito group, a grant resolved down the folder tree. **A Google Doc sits behind Google's sharing and nothing else.**

So: remove a partner from a project in Portico and their Portico documents go dark immediately — while the Google link in their browser history still works. Portico shows no trace of it, because Portico never knew. Two access lists governing one document, drifting apart the moment either changes.

The operator has accepted this rather than trying to police it, because Portico **cannot verify a Drive ACL without the Google credential decision 4 refuses**, and an unenforced policy is a false sense of one. The compensating control is disclosure, not enforcement: every externally-hosted document says so, on the document and in the share panel. This is the CEO-2 item raised at `docs/build-plan/plan.md:821` and never answered — it is now answered.

**A card that tries to "fix" this by checking Google permissions is out of scope and should be bounced.**

## Audience note that shapes the work

Portals face external partners, not staff. The operator's read is that partner Google-account coverage is **uneven** — some work accounts, some personal, some none. A partner without access to the Google file gets a *Request access* screen. That is exactly why decision 3 exists: Portico's own document-level thread has to survive on these rows, or those readers have nowhere to speak.

## AMENDED 2026-08-22 — this epic is half of one release, not a release of its own

The operator's forms work ([DRE-2628](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2628/epic-forms-a-form-is-its-own-object-in-portico) and [DRE-2629](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2629/epic-forms-working-on-an-answer-together)) adds the other new entity. Between them Portico can hold **everything it is ever asked to hold** — written documents, uploaded pages, interactive documents, spreadsheets, files, documents held elsewhere, and forms. That is one sentence to a customer, one demo and one capability grid, so the three are planned and demonstrated together.

Nothing in the waves below changes. What changes is three things:

### 1. Two cards collide with the forms epics — do not run them concurrently

The house rule is disjoint file ownership. These two break it:

| This epic | Forms epic | Shared files | Rule |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| [DRE-2496](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2496/the-comment-rail-survives-a-document-portico-does-not-host-and-says) — the rail on a document we do not host | **B3** — a thread on an answer | `rails/CommentsRail/`, `Thread.tsx` | [DRE-2496](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2496/the-comment-rail-survives-a-document-portico-does-not-host-and-says) **lands first.** B3 is formally blocked by it. The other order means rebasing through the most-tested component in the viewer |
| [DRE-2497](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2497/add-document-paste-a-google-link-and-choose-to-link-to-it-not-copy-it) — paste a link | **A4** — place a form into a folder | `LibraryScreen.tsx`, `AddDocumentModal/` | Do them in sequence, both local. Splitting one surface across a dispatched card and a local one is how two agents produce one conflict |

### 2. The frontend cards here are now `hand-built`

A new standing rule (operator, 2026-08-22): **anything with UI implications is built locally by the UI engineer and looked at in a running browser before it is committed**, then pushed as one PR for CI like anything else. Spacing, states and drag behaviour do not survive being described in a ticket and checked by a test.

[DRE-2495](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2495/the-external-document-screen-open-in-a-new-tab-and-say-who-controls), [DRE-2496](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2496/the-comment-rail-survives-a-document-portico-does-not-host-and-says), [DRE-2497](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2497/add-document-paste-a-google-link-and-choose-to-link-to-it-not-copy-it) and [DRE-2498](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2498/the-share-panel-tells-the-truth-about-documents-portico-cannot-gate) are therefore `hand-built`.

`hand-built` **does NOT change the branch name, and getting that wrong has already cost this epic a card.** Every card here lands on `agent/DRE-<n>-<slug>`. `.github/workflows/linear-sync.yml` reads the card id out of the merged branch, so `ui/*`, `feat/*`, `fix/*` and `docs/*` auto-Done **nothing**. The label decides **who writes the code**; the prefix decides **whether the pipeline is watching**. **Do not copy Linear's suggested **`sid/dre-<n>-<slug>`. One card, one branch, one PR — bundling closes at most one of them. Full reasoning in [DRE-2628](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2628/epic-forms-a-form-is-its-own-object-in-portico). [DRE-2494](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2494/add-a-document-by-link-without-fetching-it-the-row-the-route-and-a) stays dispatched — it is a row, a route and a payload, and nobody needs to look at a screen to know whether it is right.

### 3. Every epic now ends with a demo and a sign-off

Also new, and standing: a **DEMO** card that proves the thing by running it, and a **SIGN-OFF** card that is the operator's. Merged is not done and a green suite is not proof. This epic needs both adding — the demo's claim is *a moderator adds a Google Doc, a partner opens it, and the screen says plainly that Google controls who can*.

### [DRE-2495](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2495/the-external-document-screen-open-in-a-new-tab-and-say-who-controls) is DONE — merged 2026-08-22 4:38pm PT

[dreadnought-foundry/portico#337](<https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/review/the-external-document-screen-and-the-forms-release-plan-as-a-page-you-50ce1abcabb8>), `8eae441`. Seven tests, two mutation-checked, merged by the qa-bot after a critic APPROVE.

The copy revision this section used to ask for is made. The pane no longer claims Portico controls access — it names the host as the decider, which is true of a Google Doc and of one of our own gated pages alike:

> Portico controls who sees this document listed here. Whether you can open the file itself is decided by `<host>`, not by this library.

**It does not yet fork by kind**, and that is a real dependency rather than a shortfall: the Google-specific wording needs to know the row IS a Google file, and the render payload carries no `ext` to say so. Forking on the hostname would turn an access claim into a guess. [DRE-2494](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2494/add-a-document-by-link-without-fetching-it-the-row-the-route-and-a) **must carry the row's **`ext` **on the external render payload** — asked for in a comment there. That is what unblocks the sharper sentence and the `gsheet` tile together.

**Two things it leaves open.** It merged on a branch named `ui/forms-spec`, so it auto-Doned nothing and was closed by hand — the reason the branch rule above is now written down. And nobody has rendered the merged revision: the browser extension would not connect, so the 44px tile, the "`<kind>` · `<host>`" line and the reworded paragraph are test-verified but unlooked-at. Layout at 44px and both themes are [DRE-2650](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2650/demo-link-out-documents-prove-a-google-doc-opens-and-that-the-screen-is)'s demo to catch if nobody gets to it first.

## Order of work — what runs in parallel, what cannot

Three waves. Every dependency below is also set as a formal Linear `blockedBy` relation, so the pipeline enforces this rather than trusting anyone to read it.

### Wave 1 — SERIAL, alone. Nothing else may start.

| Card | Agent |
| -- | -- |
| [DRE-2493](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2493/client-tolerates-an-external-artifact-kind-ships-alone-before-the) · Client tolerates an external artifact kind | frontend |

**This one is genuinely serial and the reason is not style.** The SPA bundle and the backend deploy on independent release paths, and `client/app/src/features/viewer/queries/render.ts:225` **throws on an unknown **`artifactKind`. If the server emits `external` before the bundle understands it, every reader holding a cached bundle drops into the viewer's error state on that document. The client's tolerance must be merged **and deployed** first. It is deliberately small so this gate is short.

### Wave 2 — three cards, FULLY PARALLEL once [DRE-2493](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2493/client-tolerates-an-external-artifact-kind-ships-alone-before-the) is deployed

| Card | Agent | Touches |
| -- | -- | -- |
| [DRE-2494](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2494/add-a-document-by-link-without-fetching-it-the-row-the-route-and-a) · Add a document by link WITHOUT fetching it | engineer | `infra/lambda/routes/library.ts`, `routes/content.ts`, `model_types.ts` |
| [DRE-2495](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2495/the-external-document-screen-open-in-a-new-tab-and-say-who-controls) · The external document screen | frontend | `panes/` — new file + registry entry |
| [DRE-2496](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2496/the-comment-rail-survives-a-document-portico-does-not-host-and-says) · The comment rail survives a document we do not host | frontend | `rails/CommentsRail/` |

These three share no files, which is why they can run at once. [DRE-2495](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2495/the-external-document-screen-open-in-a-new-tab-and-say-who-controls) and [DRE-2496](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2496/the-comment-rail-survives-a-document-portico-does-not-host-and-says) build against the payload shape [DRE-2494](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2494/add-a-document-by-link-without-fetching-it-the-row-the-route-and-a) produces — that shape is fixed by [DRE-2493](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2493/client-tolerates-an-external-artifact-kind-ships-alone-before-the)'s validator, so they do not have to wait for the backend to land. **The contract string is **`artifactKind: 'external'`, written identically in all four cards.

### Wave 3 — two cards, PARALLEL with each other, after [DRE-2494](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2494/add-a-document-by-link-without-fetching-it-the-row-the-route-and-a)

| Card | Agent | Why it waits |
| -- | -- | -- |
| [DRE-2497](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2497/add-document-paste-a-google-link-and-choose-to-link-to-it-not-copy-it) · Add-document: link to it, don't copy it | frontend | needs the route to call |
| [DRE-2498](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2498/the-share-panel-tells-the-truth-about-documents-portico-cannot-gate) · The share panel tells the truth | frontend | needs the row kind to detect |

Both depend on [DRE-2494](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2494/add-a-document-by-link-without-fetching-it-the-row-the-route-and-a) only — **neither depends on the other**, and neither blocks anything.

### The critical path

[DRE-2493](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2493/client-tolerates-an-external-artifact-kind-ships-alone-before-the) **→ **[DRE-2494](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2494/add-a-document-by-link-without-fetching-it-the-row-the-route-and-a) **→ **[DRE-2497](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2497/add-document-paste-a-google-link-and-choose-to-link-to-it-not-copy-it). Three cards deep. Everything else runs beside it. [DRE-2495](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2495/the-external-document-screen-open-in-a-new-tab-and-say-who-controls) and [DRE-2496](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2496/the-comment-rail-survives-a-document-portico-does-not-host-and-says) finishing late does not delay the epic; [DRE-2494](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2494/add-a-document-by-link-without-fetching-it-the-row-the-route-and-a) slipping delays everything in wave 3.

### Done means

The epic is complete when a moderator can add a Google Doc and a partner can open it — which needs [DRE-2493](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2493/client-tolerates-an-external-artifact-kind-ships-alone-before-the), [DRE-2494](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2494/add-a-document-by-link-without-fetching-it-the-row-the-route-and-a), [DRE-2495](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2495/the-external-document-screen-open-in-a-new-tab-and-say-who-controls) **and **[DRE-2497](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2497/add-document-paste-a-google-link-and-choose-to-link-to-it-not-copy-it) at minimum. [DRE-2496](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2496/the-comment-rail-survives-a-document-portico-does-not-host-and-says) and [DRE-2498](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2498/the-share-panel-tells-the-truth-about-documents-portico-cannot-gate) are required for the epic's *stated conditions* (a surviving comment thread, and honest disclosure) and are not optional, but the feature is demonstrable without them.

## What this epic deliberately leaves out

* **Per-passage comments on a PDF** — a separate anchor scheme (page + rectangle) and a viewer that reports coordinates. Shares no code with today's block-based anchoring. Filed separately.
* **Spreadsheet formats beyond CSV/XLSX** — those already render as a real grid with sheet tabs; the operator has not yet said what is missing.
* **Rendering .docx/.pptx inside Portico** — that is [DRE-2459](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2459/epic-every-document-format-readable-in-place-not-just-downloadable)'s axis (convert at ingest), not this one. Under this epic a .docx becomes readable by living in Drive.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A moderator can add a Google Doc/Sheet/Slides URL to a library and it is stored as a link, not fetched and snapshotted
- [ ] Opening it shows a Portico document screen with title, status and comment rail, and an Open control that opens the file in a new tab
- [ ] Every externally-hosted document states plainly that Portico does not control who can open it — on the document and in the share panel
- [ ] Portico's own document-level comment thread works on these documents and is labelled so it is not mistaken for Google's
- [ ] No Google API call, credential, or SDK is added anywhere; `parts/gdrive.ts` and `slots/gdrive.source.tsx` remain empty
- [ ] `infra/test/demo_phase6.test.ts` still passes unchanged
- [ ] No change to `ingest_lib.ts` inline/download behaviour, so no re-ingest is required across the five companies
- [ ] Every card in this epic closed itself on merge — if one had to be moved to Done by hand, its branch was named wrong

cards.title: ship.sh skips the PR when a long-lived branch has ANY merged PR — it found one from two days ago
cards.description:
`ship.sh` step 4 looks up the PR for the current branch, sees `MERGED`, and reports *"PR #N is already MERGED — skipping to the re-sync"*. On a **long-lived branch it finds the wrong PR** — any previously merged one — and skips opening a PR for the commits it has just pushed.

## What happened, 2026-08-18

```
── 3 · push ──
  ✓ pushed ui/work            (6 new commits)

── 4 · pull request ──
  ✓ PR #308 is already MERGED — skipping to the re-sync
    https://github.com/dreadnought-foundry/portico/pull/308

── 7 · re-sync this checkout to origin/main ──
  ✗ 6 commit(s) on this branch are NOT on origin/main — refusing to move it.
```

**#308 merged on 2026-08-16**, two days earlier, from the same `ui/work` branch. It has nothing to do with the six commits pushed in this run. There was no open PR for them, and there still isn't — the lap pushed the work and then walked past the step that would have landed it.

## Why it did not cause damage, and why that is not the fix

**Step 7 caught it.** It refused to fast-forward over six unmerged commits and said so plainly — *"This script will not reset over commits nobody has merged. That is the one operation in this lap that can destroy work, and no flag turns it on."*

That refusal is the reason this is a Medium and not an incident. But the two steps disagree about the same fact: step 4 concluded the work was merged and step 7 proved it was not, three steps apart. **A lap that has to be rescued by a later guard is a lap that lied earlier.**

## The bug

The check asks *"does this branch have a merged PR?"*. The question it needs to answer is *"is **HEAD** merged?"*.

`ui/work` is deliberately long-lived — it is the operator's standing branch and has had many PRs over its life. Every one of them is a false positive for this check, forever, and the problem gets **worse over time** rather than surfacing once.

## Fix

Decide on the commits, not the branch. Any of these is sufficient and cheap:

* `git merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD origin/main` — the direct question, no API call
* Prefer an **open** PR whose head is this branch; only treat a merged one as relevant if its merge commit contains HEAD
* Compare the PR's `mergeCommit`/`headRefOid` against the current HEAD rather than reading `state` alone

Whichever, the step must **open a PR** when there are commits `origin/main` does not have, regardless of what merged previously.

## Two related things worth checking in the same pass

* The step's own message should name what it checked. *"PR #308 is already MERGED"* is true and irrelevant; *"HEAD is already on origin/main"* would have been false and caught immediately.
* `ship_sh.test.ts` already drives an `already-merged PR skips the merge and resumes at the release phase` case. That test passes today **and is the bug** — its fixture has HEAD genuinely merged, so it never distinguishes the two questions. Extend it: a branch with a merged PR **and** unmerged commits must still open a PR.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A branch with commits `origin/main` lacks opens a PR, even when a previously merged PR exists for that branch
- [ ] A branch genuinely merged still skips to the re-sync, unchanged
- [ ] The skip message states what was checked about **HEAD**, not about a PR number
- [ ] `ship_sh.test.ts` gains a case with a merged PR *and* unmerged commits, and that case fails before the fix
- [ ] The existing `already-merged` case still passes
- [ ] Full suite green (2129 at time of writing)

cards.title: Finish DeltaSolv — three renames marked Done, none actually finished
cards.description:
> **Re-scoped 2026-08-18 after the operator asked why this keeps coming back.** It was not one rename done badly — it was **three separate cards, each marked Done, none finished**. This card now closes all of them, and its acceptance criteria are written so it cannot close while any part of the old name survives.

## The three, and what is actually true today

| card | claim | measured 2026-08-18 |
| -- | -- | -- |
| [DRE-2433](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2433/rename-the-deltasolve-docs-bucket-to-deltasolv-an-origin-swap-not-a) “rename the deltasolve docs bucket” | **Done** | bucket is **still** `deltasolve-docs-442004016891` |
| [DRE-2406](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2406/portal-hostnames-use-three-different-conventions-decide-one-then) step 5, `docs.` → `share.` | **Done** | hostname is **still** `docs.deltasolv.com` |
| [DRE-2430](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2430/rename-the-deltasolve-project-slug-to-deltasolv-4-live-rows-and-1) slug `deltasolve` → `deltasolv` | **Done** | **8 scripts** still say `deltasolve` |

Every *other* DeltaSolv bucket in the account carries the correct spelling — `deltasolv-data-…`, `deltasolv-frontend-…`, `deltasolv-marketing-site-…`. The docs bucket alone kept the old one, and tonight's release published straight into it:

```
publishing deltasolv → s3://deltasolve-docs-442004016891
```

**What it has already cost.** [DRE-2430](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2430/rename-the-deltasolve-project-slug-to-deltasolv-4-live-rows-and-1)'s leftover `lib#deltasolve` rows blocked the Vericorr legacy-document migration on 2026-08-17 — a different project entirely — because `assertProjectsMatch` is account-wide. Two hours went into finding that. The rows are now gone; the scripts are not.

**The common failure, and the thing to fix once:** each card verified *its own step* and closed. None verified *the old name was gone*. A rename card must not be closeable while a grep still finds the old string.

---

`docs.deltasolv.com` is the last portal not on `share.<company>.com`. Every other one migrated under [DRE-2406](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2406/portal-hostnames-use-three-different-conventions-decide-one-then); this one was deliberately sequenced **last**, because it is the only survivor whose URL a reader may have bookmarked — and then never done. The repo has been carrying it as a written-down exception ever since.

`infra/test/portal_naming.test.ts`:

```ts
// The last `docs.` portal. Renamed to share.deltasolv.com LAST in DRE-2406's
// order of work, because it is the only survivor whose URL a reader may have
// bookmarked.
'docs.deltasolv.com': 'pending rename to share.deltasolv.com — DRE-2406 step 5',
```

`infra/scripts/close-out-hostnames.sh:294` carries the same step. The exception map is the mechanism working — the drift is visible instead of silent — but it has been visible for a while now.

## THE SPELLING IS `deltasolv`. NO TRAILING E.

`deltasolve` is the **retired** slug. Getting this wrong in DNS or a certificate recreates a mess that is still being cleaned up: tonight, stranded `lib#deltasolve` rows in `docs-comments-dreadnought` blocked an unrelated migration on a different project entirely, because `assertProjectsMatch` is account-wide. Those rows are now gone.

**Target:** `share.deltasolv.com`**.**

## Live state, measured 2026-08-17

|  |  |
| -- | -- |
| distribution | `E15EF21FJUBZMI` (dreadnought account, profile `dreadnought`) |
| aliases | `docs.deltasolv.com` — only |
| ACM cert | `arn:aws:acm:us-east-1:442004016891:certificate/1f6d9bb6-91ba-4877-9978-19ffd6fcb602` |
| edge gate | version `:10`, shared with vericorr and gridcorr |
| library | `lib#deltasolv` — grants provisioned 2026-08-17, **0 documents** |

## Two things that make this lower-risk than it looks

**The library is empty.** `lib#deltasolv` has root grants and nothing else. Nobody has a bookmark to a *document* on this portal, because there are no documents. The bookmark risk that justified sequencing this last is smaller than it was when the order was written — worth re-checking rather than inheriting the caution.

**The certificate is per-host.** A new cert covering `share.deltasolv.com` is needed before the alias can be added; the existing one covers only `docs.`. Request and validate it first — DNS validation on a zone in the dreadnought account.

## Order of work

1. Request + validate an ACM cert for `share.deltasolv.com` (us-east-1, DNS validation)
2. Add `share.deltasolv.com` as an **additional** alias on `E15EF21FJUBZMI`, keeping `docs.` — both live at once, no cutover moment
3. Route 53 A/AAAA alias for `share.deltasolv.com` → the distribution
4. `infra/config/dreadnought.json`: add the host to `portals` **AND** `docOrigins`. A host in one and not the other is a portal that loads and then cannot sign in — `portal_naming.test.ts` enforces this and will fail if you do half of it
5. Deploy so Cognito's callback/logout URLs pick up the new origin. **Cognito matches** `redirect_uri` **exactly including path** — `<origin>/auth-callback.html`, not the bare origin
6. Verify: signed-out request 302s to `auth-gate.html`, and a signed-in reader reaches the library, **on the new host**
7. Only then decide `docs.`: leave it as a second alias indefinitely, or retire it. Retiring means removing the alias, the DNS record and the config entry together
8. Delete the `'docs.deltasolv.com'` line from `EXCEPTIONS` in `portal_naming.test.ts` — the map's rule is that removing the entry is how the exception retires, and the test then insists the config caught up

## While you are in there — the same rename, still unfinished elsewhere

Marked Done, but the old spelling is still live in these:

* `docs.deltasolv.com/auth-gate.html` **renders the string** `deltasolve` to readers today. Verified live. Whatever bakes that needs the corrected slug.
* `infra/scripts/republish-app-doc.sh:160,254` — routes and documents `deltasolve`
* `infra/scripts/bucket_rename_lib.ts:63` — `OLD_BUCKET = deltasolve-docs-…`; fine as a record of a completed rename ([DRE-2433](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2433/rename-the-deltasolve-docs-bucket-to-deltasolv-an-origin-swap-not-a)), but confirm nothing still reads it as current

These are in scope only if they are cheap. If any is not, say so and file it separately rather than widening this card.

## A pattern worth naming

[DRE-2406](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2406/portal-hostnames-use-three-different-conventions-decide-one-then) **and** [DRE-2430](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2430/rename-the-deltasolve-project-slug-to-deltasolv-4-live-rows-and-1) **are both marked Done with steps that never ran**, and both cost time tonight — 2430's leftovers blocked a migration on an unrelated project. A rename card should not close until its own verification says the old name is gone. Worth a process note somewhere it will be read.

## Also in scope now: the bucket and the scripts

**The bucket** ([DRE-2433](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2433/rename-the-deltasolve-docs-bucket-to-deltasolv-an-origin-swap-not-a)'s unfinished half). `infra/scripts/rename-deltasolv-bucket.ts` and `bucket_rename_lib.ts` exist for this. Renaming an S3 bucket means create-new / copy / repoint-origin / delete-old, and the CloudFront origin must move with it — sequence it so no reader loses the portal. If that is genuinely too risky to do now, **say so on the card and leave the bucket**, but then delete the scripts that claim it was done, because a completed-rename record that did not complete is worse than no record.

**The scripts** ([DRE-2430](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2430/rename-the-deltasolve-project-slug-to-deltasolv-4-live-rows-and-1)'s unfinished half), all still carrying `deltasolve`:

`republish-app-doc.sh` · `reingest.ts` · `release.sh` · `ship.sh` · `close-out-hostnames.sh` · `verify-project-readable.ts` · `bucket_rename_lib.ts` · `rename-deltasolv-bucket.ts`

Some are legitimate historical references inside a rename tool. Judge each: a mention that *describes the old name* is fine; a mention that *routes on it* or *offers it as a current choice* is not.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `share.deltasolv.com` serves the portal — signed-out 302s to `auth-gate.html`, signed-in reaches the library
- [ ] The host is in **both** `portals` and `docOrigins` in `infra/config/dreadnought.json`
- [ ] Cognito callback/logout URLs include `https://share.deltasolv.com/auth-callback.html`
- [ ] `docs.deltasolv.com` either still works or is fully retired (alias + DNS + config together) — a decision, stated in the PR, not left ambiguous
- [ ] The `docs.deltasolv.com` entry is gone from `EXCEPTIONS` and `portal_naming.test.ts` passes
- [ ] No string `deltasolve` is served to a reader on any page of this portal
- [ ] `bash infra/scripts/ship.sh --verify dreadnought` reads current afterwards

### The criteria that stop this recurring — these are the point of the card

- [ ] `grep -rn deltasolve infra/ client/ docs/ --exclude-dir=node_modules` **returns only lines that DESCRIBE the historical name**, never one that routes on it or offers it as a choice. Every surviving hit is listed in the PR with a one-line reason.
- [ ] The docs bucket is either **renamed to** `deltasolv-docs-442004016891`, or the rename scripts that claim it was done are **deleted** and [DRE-2433](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2433/rename-the-deltasolve-docs-bucket-to-deltasolv-an-origin-swap-not-a) reopened. Not left as-is with a Done card pointing at it.
- [ ] **A test pins it**, so the next person cannot close a rename that did not happen. `attach_gate.test.ts` already flags `deltasolve` as known drift — promote that to an assertion over the repo, in the shape of `portal_naming.test.ts`'s EXCEPTIONS map: any surviving occurrence must be listed with a reason, and removing the entry is how it retires.
- [ ] [DRE-2433](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2433/rename-the-deltasolve-docs-bucket-to-deltasolv-an-origin-swap-not-a), [DRE-2430](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2430/rename-the-deltasolve-project-slug-to-deltasolv-4-live-rows-and-1) and [DRE-2406](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2406/portal-hostnames-use-three-different-conventions-decide-one-then) are each **reopened or explicitly closed with evidence** — not left marked Done over work that did not happen.

cards.title: A region renders its container's children, not the container — no self-referential External card
cards.description:
Found by the CEO reviewing the local build, 2026-08-16. The External region renders a card **named** `External` inside itself.

```
today                            proposed
─────────────────────            ─────────────────────
External  (region header)        External  (region header)
  ├ Field Ops                      ├ Sallyport
  └ External  ← the container      └ Summit Midfield
      ├ Sallyport
      └ Summit Midfield
```

## Why it looks like a bug (and partly is)

The `External` container carries **no grant of its own** — its children do. So `exposureMarkOf` (own-exposure) correctly says *nothing is granted here* and draws no stripe, while `subtreeExposure` (the rollup) correctly puts it in the External region because something inside reaches outside. **Both answers are right**, and the design deliberately has them disagree on a container.

But rendering the container as a card *inside its own region* makes that disagreement look like a rendering fault, and the operator read it as one immediately.

**It gets worse in the real tree.** After [DRE-2468](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2468/company-root-must-carry-zero-grants-two-roots-per-customer-grants) there are exactly two root folders. So you would get a region called `Internal` containing one card called `Internal`, and the same for External. Absurd.

## The fix

A region **is** its container. Render the container's children as the cards; the header carries the container's name, count and audience line. Nothing named Internal or External appears as a card.

This removes three problems at once: the self-referential card, the stripe-vs-no-stripe puzzle on a container, and the one-card-called-Internal absurdity. It also matches the approved D drawing ([https://claude.ai/code/artifact/9b76b6b6-d923-4fb2-ba68-7818a8458759](<https://claude.ai/code/artifact/9b76b6b6-d923-4fb2-ba68-7818a8458759>)), which showed customer folders directly under the External heading.

## The straggler question this exposes

`Field Ops` sits at root and belongs to neither container. [DRE-2468](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2468/company-root-must-carry-zero-grants-two-roots-per-customer-grants) **refuses any folder not present in its mapping**, so after the migration nothing is left at root — that is the intended answer. But the UI must not silently drop a root folder that is in neither region: if one exists, it has to render somewhere visible, not vanish.

Decide and record: a third region, or the Internal region as the fallback. **Do not let a folder disappear because it was not mapped** — that is the failure mode the migration's refusal exists to prevent, and the UI should not reintroduce it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No card named after a region container appears inside that region
- [ ] Region header carries the container's name, folder count and audience line
- [ ] Cards are the container's children
- [ ] A root folder in neither container still renders somewhere visible — a test pins that it cannot vanish
- [ ] The rollup (`subtreeExposure`) still decides region membership; own-exposure (`exposureMarkOf`) still decides card marking — the two must not be collapsed into one call
- [ ] `npm test` green, `npx vitest run` green, `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, visual baselines regenerated in the pinned Linux image per [DRE-2372](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2372/running-playwright-on-macos-turns-the-infra-suite-red-the-platform)

cards.title: The root is not a destination — refuse document creation with no parent folder
cards.description:
CEO decision 2026-08-16, reviewing the Internal/External build: **"for now let's not have the root able to create a document."**

Every document lands in a folder, so it has a defined audience from the moment it exists.

## Why — the current behaviour is fail-closed but surprising

Read from the code, not inferred. `POST /library/docs` does:

```ts
assertWrite({ ..., itemId: parentId ?? ROOT_ITEM_ID, ... })
```

and `assertItemWrite` allows editor-at-item, else falls back to `assertModerator`. After the two-root migration the root carries only `grant#root#g:moderators`, so:

| Who | Creating at root |
| -- | -- |
| Moderator | allowed, via the moderator fallback |
| Staff, not a moderator | **403** — no editor at root |

And `visible()` is grant-matched with **no moderator bypass**, so a root document is visible to **moderators only** — not to other staff, not to customers.

The safe direction, but it produces an invisible-document state: *"I created it and my colleague cannot find it."* Removing the root as a destination removes the state entirely rather than documenting it.

## Enforce on the server, then reflect it in the UI

**A UI-only guard is not the rule.** Hiding the button leaves `POST /library/docs` with `parentId: null` working, and any direct call creates the invisible document. The refusal belongs in the route; the UI reflects it.

Check whether folder creation at root should follow — `Internal` and `External` are themselves root folders, so the answer is probably *"only the migration creates root folders"*, but decide it explicitly rather than by omission.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `POST /library/docs` with an absent or null `parentId` is refused with a clear message naming what to do instead — not a 403 that reads as a permissions problem
- [ ] The upload/add flow requires a destination; no root option is offered to anyone, moderator or not
- [ ] Existing root documents (if any) still render and can be moved — this closes the door, it does not orphan what came through it
- [ ] The empty-root `Documents` section no longer says *"Every document has been moved into a subfolder"* — under this rule that section is either absent or explains that documents live in folders
- [ ] Decided and recorded: whether root **folder** creation is likewise restricted to the migration
- [ ] A test pins the refusal at the route, so a UI change cannot silently re-open it

cards.title: Crossing the boundary is an access change — confirm the drag, naming who becomes able to see it
cards.description:
**Design:** [https://claude.ai/code/artifact/9b76b6b6-d923-4fb2-ba68-7818a8458759](<https://claude.ai/code/artifact/9b76b6b6-d923-4fb2-ba68-7818a8458759>), final section.

Everything else in [DRE-2467](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2467/epic-internal-external-roots-make-who-can-see-this-visible-in-the) is preparation for one action: dragging a document from Internal into a customer's folder under External. That **is** an access change, and it should be confirmed like one — naming the document, the destination, and **who becomes able to see it**.

## Use the primitive that already exists

Portico already computes this. From the existing tests:

> `move carries NO domain grant — shedding domain reach is the entire point of restrict-by-move`
> `move materializes an inherited PERSON grant as origin carried — nobody loses access`

`restrict-by-move` and the move preview are built (`docs/design/addendum-restrict-empty.md`, `access_lib.ts`'s `classifyFolderAccess`). **The dialog is the honest rendering of what the system is already doing** — do not invent a second computation, and do not compute effective access in the client.

## Shape

Document name, destination path, and a line naming the newly-reaching principal — e.g. `newly visible to: summitmidstream.com`. Reads in the operator's terms, not the model's: it says who can see it, not which grant rows change.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Confirmation fires when a move crosses between zones, in either direction
- [ ] It does **not** fire for a move within the same zone — a dialog on every drag is a dialog nobody reads
- [ ] Names the destination and the principals that newly reach the document
- [ ] Internal ← External (narrowing) states what **loses** access, not just what gains it
- [ ] The preview comes from the existing move/restrict computation; no second implementation
- [ ] Cancel leaves the tree untouched
- [ ] `npm test` green, `npm run typecheck` clean

cards.title: Library UI — split the root into Internal/External (D) and mark external folders everywhere (B)
cards.description:
**Design:** [https://claude.ai/code/artifact/9b76b6b6-d923-4fb2-ba68-7818a8458759](<https://claude.ai/code/artifact/9b76b6b6-d923-4fb2-ba68-7818a8458759>) — four candidates rendered in Portico's own tokens. CEO decision 2026-08-16: *"the default should be D. I like the lighter than the harder."*

## Build D and B. Do NOT build C.

**D — split the company root (the default).** The root stops being a flat folder list and becomes `Internal` and `External` regions, each with a heading, a count and one line on who can see it. External's region carries the marking.

**B — mark external folders.** Edge stripe + tinted folder icon + the literal word `External` and the customer's domain. Three redundant signals on purpose: the stripe is position, the word is text, so it survives greyscale and colour-vision deficiency.

**Must travel into list view and search results**, not just the card grid. That is where documents get dragged from, and it is precisely why candidate A (chip only) was rejected.

**C (ambient page chrome) is explicitly out of scope** — the CEO chose the lighter treatments.

## Mark the exception, not both

Internal gets no colour, no chip, no stripe. It looks exactly like the product looks today. If both are marked the eye normalises them and neither warns. This is the design's central claim — do not "improve" it by styling Internal.

## Never colour alone

Every marked surface also carries the word `External` and the customer's domain. Colour is the fast path; the text is the one that is always right.

## One new token

`--outside`, a cool slate against the warm parchment, clear of the green already carrying `FINAL`. Light `#2C4A6E` / wash `#E7EDF4` / line `#B9C8DA`. Dark `#8FB3D9` / wash `#1A2430` / line `#33475E`. Both themes, through `tokens.css` — no hardcoded colours outside the token layer.

## Derive external from DATA, never from the folder's name

A literal match on "External" breaks the moment somebody renames it. This repo has been bitten by exactly that class repeatedly — `docs.vericorr.com` outlived its rename by eight months. An explicit attribute on the two roots with descendants deriving by ancestry is the obvious candidate; whatever is chosen, the API contract and the mock fixtures must agree.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Root renders as two labelled regions with counts and audience lines
- [ ] External folders marked by stripe + icon + word + domain in **grid, list and search**
- [ ] Internal carries no marking of any kind
- [ ] Both themes correct; no colour defined only inside a media or `[data-theme]` block
- [ ] Marking derives from data; a test pins that a **rename does not change it**
- [ ] Mock/seed fixtures carry a realistic Internal/External tree so the view can be reviewed locally
- [ ] Folder-card name and meta line do not collide — spacing comes from a flex `gap`, not a `margin-top` between inline elements
- [ ] At the narrow end of the grid (~216px cards) the added `External` + domain **wraps rather than truncating** — a domain cut to `summitmidstream…` is a plausible-looking half-truth, which is worse than none
- [ ] `npm test` green, `npm run typecheck` clean, visual baselines updated deliberately per `docs/runbooks/visual-baselines.md`

## Found in design review (2026-08-16)

The folder card rendered as `Compliance11 docs · updated 2026-08-06` — name and meta were inline spans, so the meta's `margin-top` did nothing and nothing separated them. Operator: *"If they're on one line, you got to give it more space."*

Fixed in the design artifact with a flex column and a real `gap`, because a gap holds whichever way the two end up laying out. **Check the real component has the same fix** — and note this card's own work puts *more* text on that line, so it is the line most likely to run out of room.

cards.title: Company root must carry zero grants — two roots, per-customer grants, reversible migration
cards.description:
The structural half of [DRE-2467](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2467/epic-internal-external-roots-make-who-can-see-this-visible-in-the). **Without this the visual design is decorative** — access is a monotone union with no deny, so a single root grant reaches every folder however it is coloured.

## Present state (`lib#vericorr`, measured 2026-08-16)

```
grant#root#g:vericorr                            group  vericorr    VIEWER   ← reaches everything
grant#root#g:moderators                          group  moderators  editor
grant#f1786727638360-mr7n4k#p:<redacted-email> person marko       editor
```

Three grants total. **Neither customer folder carries one** — the UI shows `all 2 inherited` on both Sallyport and Summit Midfield. `grant#root#g:vericorr` is the M2 bridge grant, always intended as transitional; the repo already names the consequence: *"THE HOLD: while* `grant#root#g:<project>` *exists, the group grants viewer on everything"*.

## What to build

A migration in the house shape — pure planner in `*_lib.ts` with no AWS imports, thin runner, dry-run default, `--apply` to write, reversible, `migration:{id,script,ranAt}` on every row, epoch bumped. Match M1–M6; do not invent a seventh shape.

Per project: create the two roots, re-parent existing top-level folders, issue the staff grant on Internal, issue per-customer domain grants on each External child, and **only then** remove `grant#root#g:<project>`.

## The order is safety-critical

Staff grants must land on Internal **before** the root grant is removed, or the operator locks themselves out of their own library mid-migration. Enforce structurally, not in prose.

## The mapping is the operator's decision, not the script's

Take folder→zone as **input**. Refuse anything unmapped rather than guessing: a folder silently defaulting to Internal is a document nobody can find; defaulting to External is a disclosure. For `vericorr` the answer is knowable — `Development`, `Compliance`, `Unfiled` internal; `Customers/{Sallyport, Summit Midfield}` become External's children — but do not hardcode a roster.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Dry run by default; `--apply` writes; every write reversible and stamped
- [ ] Refuses to remove the root grant unless the Internal staff grant already exists
- [ ] Refuses any folder not present in the supplied mapping
- [ ] External itself carries no grant; each child carries exactly one domain grant
- [ ] Verification asserts on **resolved effective access** (what `access_lib.ts` computes), not on grant rows — for each customer, reaches their own folder and nothing else
- [ ] Confirmed and stated: removing `grant#root#g:<project>` does **not** affect the edge gate, which checks Cognito group membership, a different mechanism
- [ ] Answered: what a document at a grantless root is visible to (expected: moderators only — fail-closed)
- [ ] Answered: whether customer write access needs `editor`, and whether that lets them move a document *out* of their folder

cards.description:
> ## ⛔ DO NOT DISPATCH 2468 / 2469 / 2470 — the work is BUILT and UNPUSHED
>
> Pipeline agents work off `main`. Most of this epic already exists on branches in worktrees on the operator's machine, **deliberately unpushed** because the operator reviews UI locally before anything reaches the remote. A pipeline agent sent at one of these cards finds no such screen and correctly refuses.
>
> That already happened: [DRE-2472](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2472/a-region-renders-its-containers-children-not-the-container-no-self) was filed as a correction to [DRE-2469](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2469/library-ui-split-the-root-into-internalexternal-d-and-mark-external), created in Todo while 2469 sat in Backlog. **Two frontend agents ran and both stopped** — the first blocked it (*"fixes a screen that does not exist in the repository yet"*), the second parked it in Plan Review asking where the screen was. Both were right.
>
> | Card | Where the work is |
> | -- | -- |
> | [DRE-2468](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2468/company-root-must-carry-zero-grants-two-roots-per-customer-grants) | `infra/two-root-migration` in `portico-tworoot` — built, dry-run proven against live data |
> | [DRE-2469](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2469/library-ui-split-the-root-into-internalexternal-d-and-mark-external) | `ui/outside-edge` in `portico-outside` — 8 commits, serving at :5210 |
> | [DRE-2470](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2470/crossing-the-boundary-is-an-access-change-confirm-the-drag-naming-who) | same branch |
> | [DRE-2471](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2471/the-root-is-not-a-destination-refuse-document-creation-with-no-parent) | **not built** — safe to dispatch, server-side refusal is independent |
> | [DRE-2472](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2472/a-region-renders-its-containers-children-not-the-container-no-self) | folded into 2469; Backlog, blocked |
>
> **These cards are RECORDS until their branches merge.** After that they are dispatchable in the normal way. The rule generally: do not file a pipeline card against code that is not on `main`.

Every company share gets two root folders: **Internal** (staff only) and **External** (a container whose children are per-customer). Documents flow draft → internal review → dragged into a customer's folder when ready. The split is visible in the UI, and moving a document across it is confirmed as the access change it is.

Design approved by the CEO 2026-08-16. Rendered candidates and the reasoning: [https://claude.ai/code/artifact/9b76b6b6-d923-4fb2-ba68-7818a8458759](<https://claude.ai/code/artifact/9b76b6b6-d923-4fb2-ba68-7818a8458759>) — decision was **"the default should be D. I like the lighter than the harder."** So treatment **D** (split root) is the default, **B** (stripe + icon + word) marks external folders anywhere they appear, and **C** (ambient page chrome) is explicitly **not built**.

## Why now

`share.vericorr.com` is about to receive Summit Midstream as an external customer ([DRE-2407](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2407/operator-decision-plan-fold-summit-midstream-into-vericorr-a-cross)). Today `lib#vericorr` carries `grant#root#g:vericorr` — a root **viewer** grant reaching every folder that will ever exist. Effective access is a **monotone union with no deny**; `docs/design/addendum-restrict-empty.md` states it outright: *"No folder can be narrower than the root."*

So the moment Summit's people can sign in, they can read Development, Research, Prototypes, Compliance and the other customer's folder. The UI shows `all 2 inherited` on both customer folders today — the folders carry no grants of their own and are not boundaries.

## The two claims this epic rests on

1. **Internal/External as folders create no boundary unless the company root carries ZERO grants.** The visual design is worthless without that.
2. **Mark the exception, not both.** Internal is home and stays unstyled; if both are marked the eye normalises them and neither warns.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every project's company root carries no grants; all grants sit on Internal or on an External child
- [ ] External is a container with no grant of its own — each customer folder carries exactly one domain grant, so no partner can see another partner
- [ ] The library root renders as two labelled regions (D)
- [ ] An external folder is unmistakable in grid view, list view and search results (B), by stripe + icon + the literal word and domain — never colour alone
- [ ] Dragging a document across the boundary confirms, naming who becomes able to see it
- [ ] Status (`draft`/`review`/`final`) stays orthogonal to location and remains invisible to the access resolver
- [ ] A folder rename never changes its internal/external marking

cards.title: Record which formats are already inline, and why SVG is refused
cards.description:
Two halves of the format picture that are **not** work — they are decisions that need to stay decided. This card exists so nobody re-opens either by accident, and so the epic's list is complete rather than only listing gaps.

## Already inline — no work needed

These render in place today and should not be re-litigated:

| Format | How |
| -- | -- |
| `.pdf` | Browser's native viewer. [DRE-2377](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2377/render-pdfs-inline-with-pdfjs-without-weakening-the-sandbox) tracks moving to PDF.js so the sandbox needn't be weakened — that is an improvement, not a gap. |
| `.png` `.jpg` `.gif` `.webp` | Inline images |

The mechanism is `INLINE_FILE_CONTENT_TYPES` in `infra/lambda/ingest_lib.ts`, matched against a type sniffed from the file's **magic numbers** — never the client's declared content type, which is attacker-controlled. Renaming `evil.svg` to `report.pdf` does not get it served inline.

## Deliberately refused — SVG

`.svg` is **excluded on purpose** and must stay excluded. It is active content: served inline off a signed URL it would execute **in the content origin**, bypassing the sanitizer entirely. That is not a theoretical concern — it is the whole reason the inline allowlist is an allowlist.

The risk this card guards against is someone reading "SVG is an image, images are inline" and appending one MIME string. The existing code comment says so; this card makes it visible in the tracker too.

## What to do

Nothing to build. Confirm the reasoning is written where a contributor will meet it **before** changing the list:

- [ ] `INLINE_FILE_CONTENT_TYPES` carries the SVG reasoning in a comment a reader cannot miss
- [ ] A test asserts SVG is absent from the inline set and fails loudly if added, naming the sanitizer-bypass reason
- [ ] The already-inline set is recorded somewhere the epic can point at, so the format list reads as complete rather than as gaps only
- [ ] Related: [DRE-2377](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2377/render-pdfs-inline-with-pdfjs-without-weakening-the-sandbox) (PDF.js) is linked and understood as an improvement to a working format, not a fix for a broken one

cards.title: Word documents readable in place — .docx converted to a frame at ingest
cards.description:
The most-requested format nobody can read in Portico. A `.docx` uploads, gets a library row, inherits access and takes comments — and the only thing a reader can do is download it, which puts an unwatermarked copy on their laptop and ends Portico's involvement.

**This is the large one, and it should not be started casually.** Word conversion done well is a project; done badly it is worse than a download link, because a document that renders subtly wrong is a document a partner may act on. Sequence it after [DRE-2460](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2460/a-download-only-document-says-so-instead-of-showing-an-empty-pane) (honest empty state) and [DRE-2461](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2461/markdown-uploads-become-real-documents-md-converted-to-a-frame-at)/[DRE-2462](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2462/plain-text-uploads-become-readable-txt-converted-to-a-frame-at-ingest) (the cheap text formats), and only when someone actually needs it.

## What makes it hard

Not the plumbing — the ingest branch and sanitizer hand-off are the same as `.md`. The difficulty is **fidelity**:

* Embedded images have to be extracted and stored, not left as broken references
* Tables, lists and nesting are where converters most visibly fail
* Fonts, page geometry and anything print-shaped have no meaning in a reflowed HTML frame
* Tracked changes and comments inside the Word file — decide whether they are dropped, and say so on screen if they are. Silently discarding a reviewer's Word comments would be its own incident.

## What to decide before writing code

1. **Which converter**, and its licence. It must run server-side in the Lambda, must fetch nothing, and its dependency lands under the frozen-lockfile discipline (`infra/package.json`'s `deps:verify` — adding a dependency is its own follow-on card).
2. **What "good enough" means**, concretely, with example documents. Without an agreed bar this card cannot be finished, only abandoned.
3. **What happens when conversion fails or degrades badly.** Falling back to the download card ([DRE-2460](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2460/a-download-only-document-says-so-instead-of-showing-an-empty-pane)) is a perfectly good answer and probably the right one — but it must be a decision, and the reader must be told which they are looking at.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A `.docx` upload opens as a readable document with its text, headings, lists and tables intact
- [ ] Embedded images are extracted and served, not broken
- [ ] Converted output goes through the existing sanitizer — a test proves active content does not survive
- [ ] It is `artifactKind: 'frame'` and takes anchored comments
- [ ] A conversion that fails degrades to the stated download card, never to a blank or half-rendered page
- [ ] Whether Word's own tracked changes and comments are dropped is decided, documented, and visible to the reader if they are
- [ ] The converter choice and its licence are recorded; the dependency is raised as its own lockfile card
- [ ] `.pptx` is out of scope — DRE-2464

cards.title: A download-only document says so, instead of showing an empty pane
cards.description:
Upload a `.docx`, `.md`, `.txt` or anything else outside the inline allowlist, open it, and the viewer shows a pane with nothing in it. The document is fine — it uploaded, it has a library row, it inherits folder access, it takes comments. It simply cannot be rendered, and nothing on screen says so.

This is the smallest card in [DRE-2459](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2459/epic-every-document-format-readable-in-place-not-just-downloadable) and it blocks nothing. It is worth doing on its own merits even if no format ever gains a renderer, because the current behaviour reads as a broken document rather than an honest limitation.

## What to build

For an `artifactKind: 'file'` document whose stored content type is **not** in `INLINE_FILE_CONTENT_TYPES` (`infra/lambda/ingest_lib.ts`), the pane states what the reader can do and offers it:

* What the file is — the format and its size, from the fields `/render` already carries (`fileContentType`, `fileName`, `bytes`)
* Why it is not shown — in plain words, no error voice. It is not a failure; this format has no reader yet.
* The download, as the primary action rather than the only discoverable one

The rail, the floating bar and comments all stay exactly as they are — a download-only document still takes comments, and that must keep working.

## Notes

* `FilePane` already exists (`client/app/src/features/viewer/panes/`) and handles the inline cases; this is the else-branch.
* The `DocMenu` label logic already distinguishes these: `payload.artifactKind === "file" ? "Download original" : "Download document"`, and its comment explains why the word "original" is only true for the `file` kind. Reuse that reasoning; do not contradict it.
* Copy follows the house voice — say what the reader gets, no apology, no "unsupported". `components/states/NotAvailable.tsx` is the nearest existing treatment; check whether it fits before adding a new one.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A `.docx` (or any octet-stream) document renders a stated, readable pane — never an empty one

- [ ] A PDF or image is unaffected and still renders inline
- [ ] Comments, the rails and the floating bar behave identically to any other document
- [ ] A test pins the else-branch by content type, not by extension — the byte-sniffed type is what decides

cards.title: [EPIC] Every document format readable in place, not just downloadable
cards.description:
Word documents, Markdown and plain text upload into Portico perfectly well today — and a reader's only option is to download them. For a partner portal that is the wrong default for the three most ordinary document formats there are, because a download puts an unwatermarked copy on someone's laptop and ends Portico's involvement with it.

This epic groups the work to close that, format by format, so it can be picked up and worked through rather than rediscovered each time.

## What is true today (verified 2026-08-14 against `infra/lambda/ingest_lib.ts`)

Every file type uploads. `GET /library/docs/upload-formats` returns `anyFile: true`, `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` is 50 MB, and `acceptFor(anyFile)` returns `""` so the picker never silently filters. What differs is what happens after.

**The extension picks the pipeline:**

| Extension | `artifactKind` | Reader gets |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `.html` `.htm` | `frame` | The full document — comments **and** anchoring |
| `.xlsx` | `grid` | A spreadsheet grid, comments |
| `.csv` | `grid` | A spreadsheet grid, comments |
| everything else | `file` | see below |

**For** `file`**, the BYTES then decide** whether it can be shown in place. `sniffContentType()` reads magic numbers only — never the client's declared content type, which is attacker-controlled. `INLINE_FILE_CONTENT_TYPES` is exactly:

`application/pdf`, `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/gif`, `image/webp`

Anything else stores as `application/octet-stream` and the viewer offers a download and nothing else.

## The constraint that shapes every child card

**Text formats cannot simply be added to the inline allowlist.** The byte-sniff rule that keeps SVG off that list keeps `.md` and `.txt` off it too — and SVG's exclusion is deliberate and load-bearing: it is active content, and served inline off a signed URL it would execute in the content origin and bypass the sanitizer entirely.

So the mechanism for text-shaped formats is **conversion to HTML at ingest, inside the sanitizer** — which is also the better outcome, because it makes them `frame` documents that gain comments *and* anchoring, not merely visible ones.

## Order, and why

1. **Honest empty state** — smallest, unblocks nothing, worth doing regardless. The viewer currently shows an empty pane for a download-only document instead of saying so.
2. `.md` **and** `.txt` **→ frame** — cheap, and turns two formats into first-class documents.
3. `.docx` **→ frame** — large. Fidelity, images, tables. Converting Word badly is worse than a download link, so this waits until someone actually needs it.
4. `.pptx` **→ frame** — after `.docx`, same machinery, lower demand.

## Already inline — do not re-open

`.pdf`, `.png`, `.jpg`, `.gif`, `.webp` work today. `.pdf` renders via the browser's native viewer; [DRE-2377](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2377/render-pdfs-inline-with-pdfjs-without-weakening-the-sandbox) tracks moving it to PDF.js so the sandbox needn't be weakened.

## Deliberately refused — do not "fix"

`.svg` stays off the inline allowlist. Anyone adding it needs to read `INLINE_FILE_CONTENT_TYPES`' comment first and argue with the sanitizer-bypass reasoning, not just append a MIME type.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every child card below is filed, labelled `repo:portico`, and scoped to one PR
- [ ] A reader never meets an empty pane with no explanation for any uploaded format
- [ ] `.md` and `.txt` become `frame` documents with working comments and anchoring
- [ ] The SVG refusal is written down somewhere a future contributor will read before reversing it

cards.title: board-retirement runbook still points the operator at the retired signin-gate.sh
cards.description:
**Repo:** portico

`docs/runbooks/board-retirement.md:288-293` still tells the operator to attach the Lambda@Edge gate with `~/Docs/_tool/aws/signin-gate.sh`, and its code block reads:

```bash
_tool/aws/signin-gate.sh everybite   # attaches the newest published version
```

That is the tool DRE-2427 was written to replace. It reads the gate version out of `config/<acct>.output.json`, which a plain `cdk deploy` leaves naming the PREVIOUS version — the 2026-08-13 incident where `:7` was re-attached to three dreadnought portals while the script printed success three times. `infra/scripts/attach-gate.sh` reads the version from the live stack and verifies by reading the distribution back.

Split out of DRE-2440 (which fixed the same stale reference in `infra/scripts/close-out-hostnames.sh`). The critic flagged this one as non-blocking, and it is not a one-line swap, which is why it is its own card:

* The runbook requires **two** distributions attached, in order: `E3KNRPMKYLENME` (`share.everybite.com`) then `E2RMB35YCG5A13` (`internal.everybite.com`, the redirect).
* `attach-gate.sh everybite` resolves the portal host from `infra/config/everybite.json`, which covers `share.everybite.com` only. `internal.everybite.com` is not a portal in that config, so the redirect distribution needs an explicit `--dist`/`--host` argument, and the exact form should be confirmed against `attach-gate.sh`'s argument handling rather than guessed — writing a runbook command that exits before it reaches CloudFront is precisely the defect DRE-2440 fixed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The runbook names `infra/scripts/attach-gate.sh`, never `_tool/aws/signin-gate.sh`.

- [ ] The commands are verified against `attach-gate.sh`'s actual argument resolution (a company it can resolve to a declared project, plus whatever the non-portal distribution needs).
- [ ] A test pins the runbook against the retired tool's name, in the shape of `infra/test/close_out_hostnames.test.ts`.

cards.title: Questionnaires E1 — stop the silent data loss
cards.description:
**Epic 1 of the shared-questionnaire programme.** Independent of everything else — no template, no protocol work. These are live defects in the answer path that a 132-question form will find in week one, and each one loses a reader's work without saying so.

Found 2026-08-13 by a Fable 5 critique of the programme plan, then verified against the code.

## The three defects

**1.** `queryResponse` **does not paginate.** `infra/lambda/routes/responses.ts:311-325` issues a single `QueryCommand` and reads `res.Items` — no `LastEvaluatedKey` loop. DynamoDB truncates a Query at 1 MB. With 517 controls of prose that is reachable, and the consequences are silent: a fresh session's full read misses fields, and `clear()` misses targets it should have cleared. This also breaks the harvest read in E6. The codebase's own rule is "refused, never coerced" — this coerces, silently.

**2. An oversize answer is dropped while the strip says "Saved."** `parseFrameMessage` returns null for `value.length > MAX_ANSWER_LENGTH` (8000, `client/app/src/features/viewer/bridge/postMessageProtocol.ts:163-165`). FramePane drops it, nothing enters `pending`, and the status line has nothing to report — so it reports the last good state. Silent parse-drop is correct for hostile input and wrong as the only defence for honest input. 222 free-text areas on a compliance form: somebody will paste a policy excerpt.

Note the caps are asymmetric — client 8000, server `MAX_VALUE_LENGTH` 8192 (`infra/lambda/responses_lib.ts:131`). The client is stricter, so nothing surprises the server; the template must enforce the client's number at the control.

**3. The fatal-state copy instructs data loss.** `answerSyncPolicy.ts:394` reads `"Not saved — reload"`. The write queue is in memory; a reload discards it.

## Demo — how this epic proves itself

A scripted demonstration, in the house `docs/demos/` style, executed and recorded:

* a response partition large enough to exceed 1 MB reads back **complete**, with the pre-fix run showing truncation
* an 8,001-character answer produces a **visible refusal** in the UI, and the strip does not say "Saved"
* with writes pending, an attempted navigation warns; the fatal copy no longer tells the reader to reload

Mutation-proof each: break the fix, watch the named test go red, restore from a copy (never `git checkout`), confirm with `git diff`.

cards.title: Stop retrying into a dead credential — freeze repairs until it is reconnected
cards.description:
**Slice 3 of 3.** [DRE-2436](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2436/detect-a-dead-pipeline-credential-watch-the-secret-ci-actually-uses) detects the dead credential; [DRE-2438](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2438/deliver-the-dead-credential-alert-on-three-paths-phone-email-and-a) tells the human. This card stops the machine burning money while it waits.

Blocked by [DRE-2436](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2436/detect-a-dead-pipeline-credential-watch-the-secret-ci-actually-uses) — it needs that classification to know when to freeze.

## The problem

No retry fixes an expired credential. Every attempt is guaranteed to fail identically, and today every repo kept trying for roughly fifteen hours.

This is the flaw [DRE-2428](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2428/nothing-repairs-a-broken-gate-four-approved-prs-sat-blocked-overnight) states in one line: *a retry that changes nothing is not a retry; it is the same request charged twice.* It is confirmed three times in the forensics record, the earliest on 2026-06-28, where the medic retrying a rate-limited critic **deepened the exhaustion** and drained the quota twice in one night.

The house rule already exists and is not wired to this condition: a repair may change **how** a gate runs, never **what** it decided — and if nothing can change, escalate instead of paying twice (`adr-gate-repair-and-stall-detection.md`, merged 2026-08-13).

## What to build

1. **While the credential is rejected, pause repair and retry dispatches** — the fix loop, the review re-dispatch, the dead-run requeue. A credential failure is not a code failure and must not be treated as one.
2. **Resume automatically on recovery.** No human step to un-freeze; the reconnect is the signal.
3. **Do not freeze the detector.** The health check must keep running — it is what lifts the freeze. `GET /rate_limit` and the token probe are the cheap reads that stay on.
4. **Say so once.** When the freeze engages, one line on the affected cards explaining that work is paused pending reconnect — not a per-sweep repeat.

## The trap to avoid

A freeze that outlives its cause is worse than no freeze. The 2026-08-09 incident poisoned its own cap by counting hold notices as evidence of failure, so an un-parked card re-held on its first subsequent death. Gate the freeze on the live credential state, never on a stored marker or a comment count.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Failing tests first.
- [ ] Repair and retry dispatches pause while the credential is rejected, pinned by a test.
- [ ] The health check keeps running while frozen — a test proves the freeze cannot make itself permanent.
- [ ] Repairs resume automatically on recovery with no human action.
- [ ] The freeze is derived from live credential state, never from a stored marker or comment count.
- [ ] One notice per freeze, not one per sweep.
- [ ] Scenario coverage — this spans the monitor and the pipeline's dispatch paths, so unit-green is not enough.

cards.title: Deliver the dead-credential alert on three paths — phone, email, and a blocking console dialog
cards.description:
**Slice 2 of 3.** [DRE-2436](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2436/detect-a-dead-pipeline-credential-watch-the-secret-ci-actually-uses) detects the dead credential and produces one fleet-level condition. This card delivers it to a human. DRE-2439 freezes repairs.

Blocked by [DRE-2436](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2436/detect-a-dead-pipeline-credential-watch-the-secret-ci-actually-uses) — do not build until its classification exists. Do not write a second detector here.

## Why three paths

On 2026-08-13 an expired token stopped every critic in seven repos from about 04:30Z. The CEO learned of it at 19:40Z, from a person. His directive: *"I need to know that right away because nothing's gonna work."*

He was offered console-modal, email, or Slack-to-phone, and chose **all three**. The reasoning matters for how this is built:

A console dialog only fires if someone has the console open. Today's outage ran fifteen hours because nobody did. The record is explicit about this failure mode — during the 2026-08-07 outage "a WARN sat quietly amber" for 90 minutes, and console-only severity is what let the 2026-07-10 push-ingest outage run 32 days.

`adr-cross-failure-domain-alarms.md` ([DRE-554](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-554/adr-cross-failure-domain-alarm-invariant-responder-subjects-failure)) is the governing rule: **an alarm whose subject could itself be the recipient must be delivered to a responder in a different failure domain.** Counting responders means counting failure domains, not addresses.

* **Slack to the phone** — the canonical second path in that ADR. The only one that reaches him away from a screen, which is when this will usually happen.
* **Email** — reuses the existing budget-health fan-out. Survives both Slack and the console being down.
* **Console modal** — blocking, not an amber banner. It is the richest surface and the least reliable trigger, which is exactly why it is third.

## What to build

1. **One alert per expiry, fleet-wide.** A single token death hits every repo at once; seven identical alerts is noise that teaches people to ignore alerts.
2. **Say the action, not the mechanism.** The CEO is non-technical for code. "The pipeline credential expired — nothing will build until you reconnect" plus the reconnect link. No 401s, no store names, no repo lists in the headline.
3. **Fan out to all three paths** from the single condition. A failure on one path must not suppress the others.
4. **Auto-resolve on recovery**, and do not re-fire for the same expiry.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Failing tests first.
- [ ] One fleet-level alert per expiry reaches Slack, email, and a blocking console modal.
- [ ] A test proves the Slack and email paths do not depend on the console being up — this is the [DRE-554](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-554/adr-cross-failure-domain-alarm-invariant-responder-subjects-failure) invariant and the reason the card exists.
- [ ] A failure delivering on one path still delivers on the other two, and is itself reported.
- [ ] The message names the action in plain business language, with no technical detail in the headline — pinned by a test against the banned terms in the comms standard.
- [ ] The alert auto-resolves on recovery and does not re-fire for the same expiry.
- [ ] No detection logic is added here; the condition comes from [DRE-2436](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2436/detect-a-dead-pipeline-credential-watch-the-secret-ci-actually-uses).
