cards.title: "The critic rejected this" is not a state the console can show — a six-hour-old crash notice outranks two good reviews
cards.description:
On 2026-08-13 portico #284 and #281 displayed "Critic crashed — re-review needed" while the critic had run fine and returned substantive `REQUEST_CHANGES` verdicts. The badge sent the operator to restart a working reviewer instead of reading findings that included a retired command which had already caused a real incident.

This is the third time this family has cost hours: [DRE-1916](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-1916/console-show-a-critic-crash-as-reviewer-down-not-critic-rejected) (a crash shown as "Critic rejected"), [DRE-2023](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2023/fixed-loop-badges-lie-critic-crash-renders-as-critic-rejected-fix) (crashed critics shown under "self-healing, no action needed"), and [DRE-2428](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2428/nothing-repairs-a-broken-gate-four-approved-prs-sat-blocked-overnight) failure 4 (a merged PR shown as "fix agent retrying"). Each was fixed at the display. The cause is one layer down.

## The worst finding: rejection has no representation

`console/backend/sources.py:498-524` — `_latest_critic_verdict()` returns exactly three values: `"APPROVE"`, `"CRASHED"`, or `""`. `REQUEST_CHANGES` **collapses into** `""`, which is byte-identical to "no critic has ever commented."

There is no `CRITIC_REJECTED` in `WAITING_REASONS` (`enrich.py:293-295`) for a card-carrying PR. The one rejection-shaped state, `REJECTED_HUMAN_DECISION`, is gated on `head_ref.startswith("dependabot/")` (`enrich.py:381`).

So an honestly-rejected agent PR **has no truthful badge available**. Its only reachable outcomes are "Critic crashed" or the fix-loop family ("Fix agent working" / "Checks failing"). The badge cannot show reality because reality is not in its vocabulary. Every previous fix rewrote the wrong string; none added the missing state.

## Why the crash marker wins forever

Same function, three defects in seven lines:

```python
if is_critic_crash_notice(body):
    verdict = "CRASHED"
    continue
bound = _VERDICT_SHA_RE.search(body)
if bound and head_sha and bound.group(1) != head_sha:
    continue  # a verdict for an older head
verdict = "APPROVE" if "VERDICT: APPROVE" in body else ""
```

1. The crash notice sets `CRASHED` with **no sha binding**, so it can never be judged stale.
2. A stale-sha verdict uses `continue`, which **preserves the previous value** instead of clearing it. The pipeline treats a stale verdict as *no verdict*.
3. `enrich.py:377-379` fires `CRITIC_CRASHED` on `verdict == "CRASHED"` with **no run evidence required**.

Live proof on #284 (head `cf5ebb84`): comments are a 17:32:02Z crash notice, then `REQUEST_CHANGES @413c93a6` at 19:59:44Z, then `REQUEST_CHANGES @f3fdc05b` at 22:03:40Z. Neither verdict names the current head, so both `continue` — and the 17:32 crash notice is still the answer at 22:00, six hours and two successful reviews later.

## Why it also never updates

`waiting_reason` is a stored TEXT column (`store.py:131`) computed once at ingest (`ingest.py:112`) and never recomputed at query time. Its inputs are not persisted, so nothing can re-derive it without a full refetch, and the column carries no timestamp — the UI cannot tell a fresh badge from a six-hour-old one. #281's badge is purely this: a stale string written during the 17:32→20:03 window.

Two refresh paths that disagree:

* Poller (`poller.py:244-257`, 900s) → `fetch_github_prs` → the **only** path that calls `attach_run_signals`.
* Webhook/WS → `fetch_github_pr`, which **never attaches run signals**, so `critic_run_state` is always `""` and the `critic_run != RUN_LIVE` guard at `enrich.py:377` is **inoperative on every event-driven refresh**.
* `github_targets` (`webhooks.py:127-153`) handles `pull_request`, `pull_request_review`, `check_run` — **not** `issue_comment`. The arrival of the verdict comment triggers no refresh at all.

## The root cause: a second verdict parser that has drifted

`bureau-pipeline/scripts/merge_gate.py` is the authority. The console re-implements it and has diverged materially:

|  | pipeline | console |
| -- | -- | -- |
| author check | `user.login == qa_login` (`merge_gate.py:294-309`) | none — substring `"QA Critic"` anywhere, any author. **A human quoting the bot flips the badge.** |
| marker position | first line only | anywhere in body |
| verdict value | structured token: `APPROVE`/`REQUEST_CHANGES`/`PASS`/`FAIL`/`SKIP`, `None` for a crash | three strings, rejection folded into `""` |
| stale sha | `Decision("wait", "treated as NO verdict")` | `continue`, keeps prior value |
| content binding | `carries_content()` (`merge_gate.py:461-480`, [DRE-2340](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2340/merge-gate-livelock-every-branch-update-destroys-the-approve-it-just)) — a verdict for an older commit still binds when the `content:` id matches | **none.** `grep "content:"` over `console/backend/` returns nothing. Both #284 verdicts carry `content:` ids the console discards. |

This is why the gate has been correct all day while the badge has not, and why display-level fixes keep not sticking.

## What to build

1. **One verdict parser.** Extract the pipeline's `latest_verdict_comment` / `verdict_token` / `carries_content` into a module both consume, or have the console call it. Do not write a third opinion. A test must fail if the two diverge.
2. `CRITIC_REJECTED` **becomes a real state** — distinct badge, distinct tone, pointing at the findings rather than at a re-run, for card-carrying PRs and not just dependabot.
3. **The crash marker binds to a sha** and loses to any later verdict, exactly as the pipeline treats it.
4. **A stale verdict clears the value** rather than preserving whatever preceded it.
5. `issue_comment` **triggers a refresh**, and the event path attaches run signals so the live-review guard actually works.
6. **The badge is derived at query time, or carries a computed-at timestamp** so a stale string is visibly stale.
7. **"Re-review running" is representable** — a live critic run currently loses to any failing check and is invisible on the event path.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Failing tests first, using #284's real comment history (crash notice, then two `REQUEST_CHANGES` bound to superseded shas) and asserting the badge reads "rejected", never "crashed".
- [ ] A single verdict parser is shared with the pipeline, pinned by a test that fails on divergence.
- [ ] A rejected agent PR renders a rejection badge that links to the findings.
- [ ] A crash notice never outranks a later verdict.
- [ ] A comment arriving on a PR refreshes its badge.
- [ ] A live re-review is distinguishable from a finished one on both refresh paths.
- [ ] A badge older than a configured age is visibly stale rather than silently confident.
- [ ] Scenario coverage — this spans the pipeline's parser, the console's ingest, and two refresh paths, so unit-green is not enough.

cards.title: SESSION STATE — 2026-08-12/13, everything open at the context boundary
cards.description:
A checklist, **not a card to build** — deliberately parked in Backlog with a `repo:` label, because a card in Todo is auto-dispatched. Nothing here should be built from this description; each item names its own home.

Written at the end of a long session so re-engaging means checking things off rather than reconstructing.

---

## 1 · OPERATOR — nothing else moves without these

- [ ] **Board retirement** (`DRE-2396`). The dry run **REFUSED twice**, correctly, on two real findings that are decisions, not bugs:
  - `url-unproven` — both board documents are library entries over published URLs with **no** `artifactKey`, and their bytes live in `board-docs-865022066059` **only**. Moving the rows to everybite makes them resolve against everybite's portal bucket, where the files do not exist → two documents that appear in the library and 404. Copy the bytes first, then re-run with `--dest-keys <file>` so the script can *prove* they landed.
  - `reach-widened` — `d-ecosystem-vendor-landscape` would become reachable by `p:<redacted-email>`, an outside personal address holding viewer on five everybite folders. Board material is investor/financial. Either scope that grant first, or accept explicitly with `--accept-reach p:<redacted-email>`. **Do not add the flag to make the error go away.**
- [ ] **Drafts fold** (`DRE-2424`) — plan is clean as of PR 274 + the guard fix. Resolver confirms: [lambdaworks.io](<http://lambdaworks.io>) viewer, everybite non-moderator no access, [**doordash.com**](<http://doordash.com>) **NO ACCESS**, moderator editor. Run `fold-drafts-project.ts --account everybite --profile everybite-admin` (dry run first).
- [ ] [DRE-2395](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2395/operator-re-publish-the-questionnaire-and-turn-shared-answering-on-for) — re-publish the Oncor questionnaire. Now unblocked (`canRespond` write path merged, PR 272). **Step 3 of that card is wrong**: `d-readiness` is already `ingestState: ready, frameSubKind: app`, so `migrate-legacy-docs.ts --as-app` plans `stub-only` and re-renders **nothing** while printing ✓. **Re-stage to quarantine instead** — `republish-app-doc.sh` (PR 281) does this.
- [ ] **Revoke the exposed OAuth token** in Claude account settings. Rotation replaced it everywhere (all 7 repos, 23:37Z, verified) but it stays valid for a year wherever else it exists.

## 2 · Open PRs

| PR | What | State |
| -- | -- | -- |
| **#273** | [DRE-2422](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2422/land-the-comment-actions-from-uiwork-text-buttons-and-in-place-edit) comment actions — the Words build, resolve carrying state | critic |
| **#279** | [DRE-2427](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2427/signin-gatesh-silently-re-attaches-the-old-edge-version-when-the) signin-gate reads the stack, not the file | critic |
| **#280** | [DRE-2430](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2430/rename-the-deltasolve-project-slug-to-deltasolv-4-live-rows-and-1) deltasolv rename plan + `verify-project-readable.ts` | **read the sequencing note before merging** |
| **#281** | the two operator runners | blocked |

**#280's sequencing:** once on `main`, the **next** dreadnought `cdk deploy` performs the Cognito group rename whether or not that deploy was about this card. Merge on a day you intend to deploy.

## 3 · Decisions made this session — do not re-open

* **Comment actions: the WORDS build wins** (`ui/work`), with resolve changed to carry state rather than toggle. `ui/viewer-comments` is deleted; `ui/work` **must survive** until its contents are harvested.
* **Drafts** → a `Drafts` folder in everybite carrying `d:lambdaworks.io` as a **folder** grant, preserving today's audience exactly. Three junk folders deleted.
* **Summit** → new URL is fine ("give them access to their folder"). **Migrate the one comment**, do not lose it — exact row recorded on `DRE-2407`.
* **Root grants** = `g:moderators` + the company's own domain, everything else per folder (`DRE-2431`). Applied **uniformly**, including adding `d:everybite.com` to everybite — which **widens** access there. Recorded consequence: board's material moves *into* everybite's Internal folder, so everybite staff would then read investor material.
* **The slug loses its** `e` — `deltasolv`, matching the company, the domain and every other AWS resource.
* **Auto-merge enabled on portico only.** The other six fleet repos are still at GitHub's default.

## 4 · Live findings not yet carded or closed

* `ui/port-viewer-2026-08-12` has **3 unpushed commits** — the other agent's viewer port, on one disk only.
* `doc#d-doordash-catalog-download-guide` has `parentId: f-unfiled` and **there is no** `folder#f-unfiled` **in** `lib#drafts` — a dangling parent, the [DRE-2382](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2382/migration-parents-every-new-document-to-f-unfiled-without-checking-it) orphan shape. Harmless for the fold; the library has been carrying a broken reference.
* **Every Lambda is** `nodejs20.x`, deprecated 2026-04-30, updates disabled 2027-03-03. Seven functions, three accounts. Hard deadline.
* Superseded `EdgeGateFn:7` versions are now deletable once CloudFront replicas drain (hours).
* All seven repos bill **VeriCorr** since the rotation. Per-company subscription billing is **not possible** via the fan-out — it writes one token everywhere. The only per-repo split is the API-key path.

## 5 · What went live tonight

`EdgeGateFn:8` on all three dreadnought portals — verified by reading each distribution back, not from the tool's message. It carries the `canRespond` write path, the anchor-bridge highlight CSS and the access-peek gate. Twelve PRs merged (#266–#278).

## 6 · The pattern worth carrying forward

**Four separate things tonight were complete, correct and non-functional**, each with a green signal over it: an access panel with 1,004 passing tests and none that opened it; `canRespond` read in four places and written in none; PyNaCl declared but never installed; and `signin-gate.sh` re-attaching the old version three times while printing success.

Every one was found by **executing the thing and reading the result back** — never by review. And twice a mutation that was supposed to prove a guard **silently did not apply**, which would have been recorded as proof. Assert that the mutation changed the file.

cards.title: Nothing repairs a broken gate: four approved PRs sat blocked overnight, and every retry was identical to the attempt that failed
cards.description:
The pipeline can repair a bad diff but not a broken gate. On the night of 12–13 August four pull requests sat blocked across three repos, and every one of them already had an approving critic verdict. None was a code defect. All four were failures in the machinery that judges code. `agent-fix.yml` rewrites bad code and `medic.yml` retries a failed run, but nothing repairs the reviewer, the verifier, or the merge gate itself. So a broken gate sits until a person notices — and while it sits, it looks like a rejection. That is the expensive part: a healthy PR wearing a red gate reads as "the critic said no," which sends everyone to argue with the diff instead of restarting the reviewer.

One number for the waste: a single critic crash burned $4.05 and produced no verdict. It ran out of turns at 41 of 40, retried with the same budget of 40, and ran out in the same place.

Good news: most of this already exists. `reconcile.py` is already a gate-repair engine — `recover_crashed_reviews()`, `_report_reviewer_down()`, `_report_stale_verdict()` and `flag_no_checks_prs()` all separate "the gate broke" from "the code is wrong." This card is not a request for a new agent. It asks for what reconcile and medic are missing.

Write the ADR first — [DRE-2434](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2434/adr-what-may-repair-a-broken-gate-the-stall-clock-the-trace-and-the), in review as agent-bureau PR #2047.

---

# What the 2026-08-13 audit added

A four-thread audit covered the pipeline source, the forensics record, **891** `agent/*` **pull requests** across seven repos, and **2,413 Linear cards**. It confirmed both flaws below and found four more the epic did not cover.

## The gate is not what breaks

Across **12,247 merge-gate runs the gate failed 74 times — 0.60%**, and 44 of those were deliberate `bureau-harness` probes. Real failures fleet-wide: 30. When it works it merges in a **median of 8 minutes**, and 96.0% of merged agent PRs were merged by `agent-bureau-qa-bot` as designed.

The gate succeeds, decides `wait`, and tells nobody.

## A stuck merge is green, so nothing watches it

Every `medic.yml` job gates on `conclusion == 'failure'` (`medic.yml:57, 90, 111, 140`). `cancelled`, `timed_out`, `skipped` and `startup_failure` are structurally invisible.

The gate has **thirteen code paths** that decline to merge and exit 0 with no comment, no check, no Linear write, and no red run — including `gh pr list` failing and reading as "no PR" (`merge-gate.yml:112`), a failed `update-branch` swallowed by `|| true` (`:286`), a failed `agent-fix` dispatch swallowed the same way (`:157`), and every `wait`/`hold` decision (`:302`). Only three paths in the whole gate leave durable evidence.

The medic is not broken. It is doing exactly what it was built to do, against a failure class nobody pointed it at.

## Every backstop is keyed to the card, not the PR

Reconcile re-triggers the gate from exactly two call sites: `In QA` with a bound verdict past 120 minutes (`reconcile.py:2873`), and `In Review` past 60 minutes (`reconcile.py:2913`). Both filtered to `card_repo(c) == REPO_SLUG`.

A mergeable PR whose card is in Backlog, Plan Review or Done, or carries a hold label, or has no `repo:` label, or has no card at all — `repair/*` PRs have none — is touched by nothing, ever.

That is how four PRs sat up to ten hours on 2026-08-12 (agent-bureau #2035, #2036, #2041, portico #270). The operator found them by eye, twice, hours apart.

## The repair layer shares fate with what it repairs

Portico medic run **31348743570** (2026-08-10 02:03) died with `"model": "claude-fable-5"`, `is_error: true`, `total_cost_usd: 0` — the identical signature to the critic crashes it was reacting to.

Same shape as 2026-06-28, when the critic and the relay minted tokens from one GitHub App and died together, and 2026-06-22, when the medic could not push a fix because it lacked the same `workflows` permission that blocked the engineer. This is the [DRE-554](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-554/adr-cross-failure-domain-alarm-invariant-responder-subjects-failure) invariant, and it applies to model capacity and quota buckets, not just hosts.

## The critic is the single point of failure

**242 of 2,405 critic runs failed (10.1%)** and 183 were cancelled (7.6%). On agent branches the dominant mode is the model returning `is_error: true` in under a second for $0 — portico run 31554748253: 634 ms, $0; retry 641 ms, $0.

## The failure message is redacted, so every diagnosis is a guess

The critic's result JSON on these deaths is stripped to `{"type":"result","subtype":"success","is_error":true,"duration_ms":1961,"num_turns":1,"total_cost_usd":0,"permission_denials_count":0}` — **no error field at all**. The step prints "full output hidden for security" and `--debug` does not lift it.

So `num_turns: 1, total_cost_usd: 0` is the only evidence anyone gets, and everyone guesses "credential" from it. That guess has now been wrong repeatedly. This is why the same failure costs hours every time, and it is a prerequisite for every other slice: a repair layer cannot classify what it cannot read.

## Nothing closes an alert

Eight "Pipeline failure:" cards sit unresolved in Triage, including [DRE-2346](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2346/pipeline-failure-merge-gate) — the day the gate went down fleet-wide. On 2026-07-21 the operator batch-closed eleven stale alert cards by hand in one minute, several about PRs merged three to four weeks earlier.

---

# The original four failures

| # | Failure | Evidence |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | GitHub App quota exhaustion | Installation 123249480 (agent-bureau-bot, pool slot 1) exhausted in steady state. Gates die in `claude-code-action` preflight before the model is reached. |
| 2 | Critic turn-budget overrun | `error_max_turns` at 41/40. `--max-turns 40` hardcoded twice (`qa-review.yml:486`, `:623`). Retry used 40 again. $4.05, no verdict. |
| 3 | TDD guard classifies by path, not content | A docstring-only edit to a `.py` file demands a RED test. |
| 4 | Fix-loop panel has no merged-PR predicate | `console/backend/inflight.py:320`. Shipped separately. |

# The two flaws underneath

**The retry changes nothing.** `verify.yml` and `qa-review.yml` each run the advisory agent then re-run it as the immediately following step — no sleep, no backoff, no jitter (`verify.yml:363`, `qa-review.yml:608`). Same model, same turn budget, same token, same app, byte-identical prompt. `medic.yml:101` re-runs the same run id with the same event payload and secrets. Against a deterministic failure, attempt two cannot succeed. Confirmed three times in the forensics record, earliest 2026-06-28. A retry that changes nothing is not a retry; it is the same request charged twice.

**Infrastructure failure destroys a good verdict.** `verify.yml:508-519` posts a crash notice carrying the `QA Verifier` marker but no `VERDICT:` line. `merge_gate.latest_verdict_comment()` takes the newest marker-bearing comment, so the crash notice replaces an earlier PASS and `evaluate_verifier()` returns hold. The reasoning was sound — never post a false FAIL — but an outage now erases work a healthy verifier already did. `qa-review.yml:780-792` does the same on the critic side.

# The watcher must not spend the quota it is watching

`reconcile.py` makes roughly 40–60 GitHub calls on a quiet repo and 200–400 on a busy one, every 15 minutes, per repo, with no caching — including ten separate `gh pr list --state open` calls per sweep over the same PR set. It runs entirely on `BUREAU_APP_ID`, pool slot 1. The sweep meant to detect the outage is a leading cause of it, and it goes blind exactly when it is needed. `GET /rate_limit` is exempt from the rate limit, so the health signal itself is free.

---

# Slices

Each is shippable alone, ordered by value. Slices 0 and 1 are worth doing even if nothing else is approved.

**0 · Make the failure name itself.** Unhide the critic's failure path — the reason only, not the transcript, which is why it was hidden. A dead credential says "credential," a rate limit says "rate limit." Everything downstream depends on this: a repair layer cannot classify what it cannot read, and today three days of investigation produced "I don't know, and neither does anyone else."

**1 · Stop the watcher draining the bucket it watches.** Wire `dispatch_pool.select` into the remaining ten token-minting workflows and collapse reconcile's ten duplicate `pr list` calls into one. Pure headroom recovery, no behaviour change.

**2 · The stall clock, keyed to the PR.** An open PR whose state has not changed in N minutes is stuck — regardless of card lane, branch name, repo label, or whether anything failed. This is the load-bearing slice: it closes all thirteen silent exits at once because it does not need to know why the gate declined. Every prior fix here addressed one mechanism ([DRE-2282](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2282/a-crashed-critic-parks-a-pr-forever-bounded-per-head-re-review-then) a crashed critic, [DRE-2261](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2261/nothing-notices-a-pull-request-that-has-sat-with-zero-checks-a-human) zero checks, [DRE-2426](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2426/branch-ownership-is-hand-copied-eight-times-so-the-sweep-that-finds) an unowned branch) and each left the next one uncovered.

**3 · A durable trace on every gate decision.** The gate writes one status onto the PR head naming its decision and reason. The `|| true` swallows at `merge-gate.yml:112`, `:157` and `:286` become loud.

**4 · Adaptive retry.** Re-select a pool app on a rate-limit crash, raise the turn budget once on `error_max_turns`, re-run on a different account on the `is_error`/1-turn/$0 signature, and make `--max-turns` a workflow input instead of a hardcoded 40. Never re-run with identical parameters.

**5 · Stop a crash superseding a verdict.** Let `merge_gate.latest_verdict_comment()` tell "never verified" from "verified, then the reviewer crashed," and hold in both cases without discarding the earlier result.

**6 · One fleet-level conclusion.** When several PRs show the same gate down at once, raise one alert and pause repair dispatches instead of posting N independent notes.

**7 · Alerts close themselves.** A "Pipeline failure:" card naming a PR closes when that PR merges.

# Self-heal or escalate

A repair may change **how** a gate runs, never **what** a gate decided.

| Failure | Action | Why |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Rate-limit crash, another pool app has headroom | **Self-heal** — re-run on that app | `dispatch_pool.choose()` already picks by headroom off the quota-exempt `/rate_limit`. Deterministic, free, changes a parameter. |
| Rate-limit crash, no headroom anywhere | **Self-heal by waiting** past the earliest reset | The reset instant is a fact, not a guess. Retrying sooner deepens the limit. |
| `error_max_turns` | **Self-heal once** at a larger capped budget | The budget is a knob we set. |
| `is_error` with 1 turn and $0 | **Self-heal once** on a different account | The 2026-08-10 and 2026-08-12 signature. Requires slice 0 to classify honestly. |
| APPROVE bound to head, CI green, PR open past N minutes | **Self-heal** — re-trigger the gate | The gate re-evaluates from scratch and keeps its own guards. Nothing is bypassed. |
| Critic returned REQUEST_CHANGES | **Never auto-retry** | That is a verdict, not a failure. Re-running to get a different answer is verdict shopping, and it destroys the only thing an adversarial critic is for. |
| A gate rule is wrong (the TDD guard) | **Escalate** | A watcher must never rewrite the rules it is judged by, unattended. |
| Steady-state quota exhaustion, nothing in flight | **Escalate** | No retry fixes a burn rate. A capacity decision the operator owns. |
| Same gate crashed N times on one head sha | **Escalate** | The self-heal was tried and did not work. An uncapped repair loop is how quota exhausted twice on 2026-06-28. |
| A cause the classifier cannot name | **Escalate** | Unknown is not a licence to retry blind. |

Escalation goes where the CEO already looks: a card comment plus the console's needs-you surface — the path `_report_reviewer_down()` uses today.

# Overlap to resolve during planning

[DRE-2289](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2289/the-fix-agent-is-blind-to-failing-checks-an-approve-verdict-plus-red) (fix agent blind to failing checks, Backlog since 2026-08-07) and [DRE-2312](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2312/a-fix-run-that-exhausts-its-60-turn-budget-is-reported-as-an-ai) (fix-agent 60-turn budget misreported as an AI outage) are the same root causes in different workflows. Fold them in or dedupe explicitly rather than shipping half-fixes.

# Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The ADR ([DRE-2434](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2434/adr-what-may-repair-a-broken-gate-the-stall-clock-the-trace-and-the)) is merged before any repair behaviour ships.
- [ ] The critic's failure reason appears in the run log in one line, without exposing the transcript or any token, and a test pins that the reason is present on a forced failure.
- [ ] `dispatch_pool.select` is wired into every `bureau-pipeline` workflow that mints a bot token, with a test asserting none is hardwired to slot 1.
- [ ] Reconcile reads pool headroom via the quota-exempt `/rate_limit` before its sweep, and below a configured floor runs only free reads plus escalation.
- [ ] Reconcile makes at most one `gh pr list --state open` call per sweep, pinned by a test on the call count.
- [ ] An open PR with no state change for N minutes is detected as stuck **regardless of card lane, branch name, or repo label**, with a test covering a `repair/*` PR that has no Linear card and a PR whose card is in Backlog.
- [ ] Every gate decision writes a durable status on the PR head naming the decision and reason. No path exits 0 silently, pinned by a test enumerating all thirteen.
- [ ] A gate that crashes on a rate limit is re-run on a pool app with headroom when one exists, otherwise scheduled past the earliest reset. Never re-run immediately with identical parameters.
- [ ] `--max-turns` for the critic is a workflow input, and an `error_max_turns` crash re-runs once at a larger capped budget.
- [ ] A crash notice no longer erases a prior passing verdict: `merge_gate` distinguishes "never verified" from "verified, then the reviewer crashed," and holds in both cases without discarding the earlier result.
- [ ] Every automatic repair is capped per head sha using the existing `_worker_receipt_count` receipt pattern, counting receipts rather than prose, and a spent cap escalates to the card and the console's needs-you queue.
- [ ] No repair path ever re-dispatches the reviewer on a bound `REQUEST_CHANGES` verdict, pinned by a test.
- [ ] When the same gate is down on three or more PRs at once, one alert is raised and repair dispatches pause until it clears.
- [ ] A "Pipeline failure:" card naming a PR closes automatically when that PR merges.
- [ ] Scenario tests cover the failures end to end through `bureau-harness`. This touches reconcile, medic, the workflows and `merge_gate`, so unit-green is not enough.

cards.title: Pointing a repo at a different Claude billing account should be a click, not a release — move the routing out of the shipped config file
cards.description:
Deciding which Claude billing account a repo runs on is an operating choice, not a code change — but today it can only be made by editing a file in the repo, which means a pull request, a critic review, a merge and a console deploy. That is a release cycle for a decision that carries no credential and no schema. It should be a control in the console that takes effect immediately.

## What the file actually holds

`console/backend/claude-accounts.json` mixes three different kinds of thing:

1. **The roster** — which accounts exist, their emails, plan tiers, failover order, and the name of the environment variable holding each one's token. This genuinely belongs in code: adding an account also needs a stored credential and, on the operator path, a Secrets Manager entry wired in `infra/lib/backend-stack.ts`. Leave it exactly where it is.
2. `repo_accounts` — which repo bills which account (`atlas` → EveryBite, `vericorr` → VeriCorr). Pure routing. No credential, no schema, no code.
3. `default_account` — the account every unlisted repo bills (Dreadnought today). Also pure routing.

Items 2 and 3 are the ones costing a release each time they change.

## We already solved this once, and the answer was not a file

The Linear→GitHub relay used to hardcode which repo a card went to. Since [DRE-1624](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-1624/featrelay-read-repo-routing-from-ssm-at-runtime-data-driven-no) it reads its routing from an SSM parameter (`/bureau/relay/repo-map`) at runtime, with the old in-code value kept only as a fallback if the parameter is unreadable. Onboarding a new repo is one write, no redeploy. That is the house pattern (`architecture/decisions/adr-one-shared-pipeline.md`); billing routing is the one place that still diverges from it.

## The half-built version already in the product

There is already a per-project account picker — Project Settings → Subscription — that writes the console database instantly and needs no deploy ([DRE-1534](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-1534/project-settings-per-project-subscription-llm-billing-account)/1695). Two things stop it from being the answer today:

* **Its list of accounts is a hardcoded copy in the frontend** (`console/web/src/pages/projectSettingsModel.ts`) that has drifted: it offers Dreadnought, EveryBite and VeriCorr only. **DeltaSolv is missing**, so no amount of clicking can route a repo to it — the config file is the only way, and that is a release.
* **The file still wins in places the picker does not reach.** Cost forecasting (`capital_spend.py`) and the project seed both resolve the billing account straight from the file, so a picker change and a file change can disagree about who is paying.

So the operator is right, and the fix is smaller than it looks: finish the runtime path and delete the file's routing half.

## Proposal

* **Keep the roster in** `claude-accounts.json`**.** It is credential-coupled; a PR is the correct cost for adding an account.
* **Move** `repo_accounts` **and** `default_account` **into console runtime state**, using the key/value store the Subscriptions screen already uses for its global settings (`subscription_setting` — the same table holding the auto-switch toggle and the pool's current assignments). The file's current values become the first-run seed and the fallback when nothing has been set, so behaviour on day one is identical and an empty store never means "unrouted".
* **Serve the roster to the frontend** instead of duplicating it as a literal, so the picker always offers exactly the declared accounts and can never drift again.
* **Edit the per-repo choice where it already lives** (Project Settings → Subscription) and **the fleet default on the Subscriptions screen**, beside the active account and failover order it belongs with.
* **One resolver.** Every consumer — the failover ring, cost forecasting, the project seed, the terminal board — must read the same runtime answer, so nothing can quietly bill against the old file.

This does not change which token CI presents; that actuator is [DRE-2318](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2318/claude-accounts-are-an-ordered-pool-with-automatic-failover-a-capped)'s and is unchanged. It changes only where the *decision* is recorded and how a human changes it.

## Why a runtime store, and not just a different file

The file sits inside `console/backend/` because that directory is the Docker build context — a repo-root file would not ship to App Runner (which is why `config/repo-map.json` needs generated mirrors). Any file, wherever it lives, still arrives by image build, so it still costs a deploy. The console database is already inside the running service and already carries operator settings; writing there is the only version of this that takes effect on save.

## Notes for the implementer

* `claude_accounts.POOL` is loaded once at import and `default_account_for_slug` is a module-level function with no store handle. Threading a store through the callers is the bulk of the work — do it once, in a single resolver, rather than adding a second lookup path.
* The drift gate (`console/backend/tests/test_claude_account_pool_config.py`) currently asserts routing derives from the file. It must be updated in the same PR to assert routing derives from the runtime store with the file as seed, and to keep asserting the roster comes from the file.
* The account picker currently accepts the "Anthropic Console" API-key account as a project's billing account, although it has no OAuth token a workflow could authenticate with and can never be a failover target. Serving the roster from the backend is the natural moment to offer subscription accounts only.
* `scripts/board.py` reads the file directly for its SUBSCRIPTIONS section; it needs the roster, not the routing, so it should keep reading the file for labels only.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Changing which account a repo bills is done in the console and takes effect on save — no PR, no deploy
- [ ] Changing the fleet default account is done on the Subscriptions screen and takes effect on save
- [ ] `repo_accounts` and `default_account` are gone from `claude-accounts.json`; the roster (labels, emails, plans, env names, kinds, order) stays
- [ ] On a store with nothing set, every repo resolves to exactly the account it resolves to today
- [ ] The account picker offers every declared subscription account, sourced from the backend — DeltaSolv included — with no hardcoded list in the frontend
- [ ] Cost forecasting, the project seed, and the failover ring all resolve the billing account through the one runtime resolver
- [ ] The drift gate is updated in the same PR and passes; the roster half is still gated
- [ ] Adding a NEW account still requires a PR (roster + credential), and a test says so

cards.title: A card-carrying PR on a misnamed branch opts out of the whole pipeline and says so only in a log line nobody reads
cards.description:
Three gates key on the head branch's prefix. A PR that names a card anywhere but the front of its branch gets none of them, and the only notice is a line buried in a workflow log.

## The rule, and how quietly it fails

`linear-sync.yml`:

```bash
CARD=$(printf '%s' "$HEAD_REF" | grep -oiE '^agent/DRE-[0-9]+-' | ...)
if [ -z "$CARD" ]; then
  echo "head branch '$HEAD_REF' is not a card's own agent branch — no automatic Done"
  exit 0
fi
```

`merge-gate.yml` and `agent-fix.yml` gate the same way (`agent/*|repair/*|dependabot/*`). So a branch like `feat/DRE-2419-anchor-bridge-server-half` — which **contains the card id** — gets:

* no merge gate (exits "not an agent branch — skip")
* no fix agent, ever
* no automatic Done

Four characters at the front of the branch decide all three. The anchoring itself is correct and deliberate ([DRE-2027](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2027/restrict-linear-syncs-done-transition-to-gate-merged-agent-branches-a)): the branch is the card's OWN branch, which is provenance, and PR titles are never read because a stray "[DRE-1234](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-1234/typed-overlay-data-access-query-doc-codegen-hook)" in prose would otherwise close someone's card. **This card does not propose relaxing that.**

## What it cost on 2026-08-12

| PR | Branch | Outcome |
| -- | -- | -- |
| portico #269 | `feat/DRE-2419-…` | merged 23:26 with 13/13 checks green; card sat In Review until closed by hand |
| agent-bureau #2035 | `fix/subscriptions-secret-drift-warning` | real REQUEST_CHANGES, ~9h, no fix agent will ever touch it |
| agent-bureau #2036 | `feat/claude-cred-doctor` | same |
| bureau-pipeline #141/#142/#143 | `fix/…`, `model/…` | all three hand-merged |

Every one authored by a LOCAL agent, which names branches by ordinary git convention (`feat/`, `fix/`) — correct practice everywhere except here, where the prefix is load-bearing. The operator's reaction on finding [DRE-2419](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2419/the-frame-bridge-scrolls-to-an-anchor-server-half-shipping-dark) open: *"I definitely don't want to sit here and close those. If they're done, they should be pulled off."*

## The change

**Say it on the PR, at the moment it opens.** When a head branch carries a `DRE-<n>` reference anywhere but the anchored `^agent/DRE-<n>-` position, post one comment naming the consequence and the fix:

> This branch won't auto-close [DRE-2419](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2419/the-frame-bridge-scrolls-to-an-anchor-server-half-shipping-dark), and it gets no merge gate and no fix agent — those key on `^agent/DRE-<n>-<slug>`.
> Rename to `agent/DRE-2419-anchor-bridge-server-half`, or expect to merge and close this by hand.

Requirements:

1. **Only when a card is actually referenced.** A genuinely cardless branch (`fix/some-hotfix`) is a legitimate choice, not a mistake — silence there. The trigger is "names a card but not in the anchored position."
2. **Once per PR.** Idempotent on the comment record, the same shape merge-gate's `human` arm already uses.
3. **Never blocks.** This is a notice, not a gate — the PR proceeds exactly as today.
4. **Names all three consequences**, not just Done. The merge gate and fix loop are the expensive ones; a PR that silently gets no fix agent is the 9-hour case above.

## Not in scope

Relaxing the anchor, reading PR titles, or auto-renaming branches. The rule is right; only its silence is wrong. Renaming someone's branch under them is worse than telling them.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A PR whose head branch references a card outside the anchored position gets exactly one comment naming the card, the three lost gates, and the correct branch name. A test drives `feat/DRE-2419-anchor-bridge-server-half` and asserts the comment content.
- [ ] A correctly-named `agent/DRE-<n>-<slug>` branch gets no comment.
- [ ] A branch with no card reference at all gets no comment — cardless work is legitimate.
- [ ] Re-running on the same PR does not post a second comment.
- [ ] The notice never changes the PR's checks or blocks a merge; pinned by a test.
- [ ] Case-insensitive matching, consistent with the existing `grep -oiE` behaviour.

cards.title: GET /library ships every project member the raw email addresses in accessSummary.people — the peek gate hides the panel, not the payload
cards.description:
`GET /library` is **not** moderator-gated, and every folder and doc in its payload carries `accessSummary { domains[], people[], groups[], canOpenCount }` where `people[]` is **raw email addresses** (added by [DRE-2200](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2200/p2-c1-library-payload-v2-assertitemwrite)). So any signed-in member of a project can read the full list of named individuals granted on every item in that project — including a partner's staff list — from the network tab.

## What [DRE-2410](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2410/access-peek-lands-moderators-only-the-chip-names-people-so-the-panel) did and did not do

[DRE-2410](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2410/access-peek-lands-moderators-only-the-chip-names-people-so-the-panel) (PR 265, merged `537f859`) gated the **access peek panel** on `GET /me`'s `isModerator`, so a non-moderator no longer sees those names rendered on hover. That was the operator's decision of 2026-08-12 and it is the right UI behaviour.

**It is a display gate.** It was written, reviewed and merged as one, and says so in `moderatorGate.ts`, in the commit and in the PR. It does not change what the route sends. The names are still on the wire, one devtools tab away, for exactly the same audience as before.

This card is the other half, and it was previously **unfiled** — the risk was recorded only in code comments and a PR body, which is not a place anyone goes looking.

## Why it is not simply "gate the route on moderator"

The library payload's access facts are load-bearing for non-moderators:

* the chips' COUNTS (`grantSplitOf` → people/domains) drive `FolderCard`, `ListView` and the breadcrumb, and a count is not a disclosure
* `classification` / `accessLabel` drive the direct-vs-inherited glyph
* `folderExposure` and the private-folder footer warning read the same summary
* the drop-overlay's consequence figures ("drops 41 partner viewers") are computed from it

Removing `accessSummary` wholesale breaks all of that. The shape wanted is: **counts for everyone, identities for moderators.**

## Suggested approach

Redact in the route, not the client. In `items_lib`'s `accessSummaryOf` (or at the `GET /library` boundary), when the caller is not a moderator for that project, emit the same object with `people: []` and `domains: []` while keeping `canOpenCount` and adding explicit `peopleCount` / `domainsCount`. Then `grantSplitOf` reads the counts rather than `.length`, and the client cannot draw what it was not sent.

Check the same payload for the same problem in `GET /access` and `GET /access/destinations` before closing.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A non-moderator's `GET /library` response contains **no** email address and **no** domain string anywhere in `accessSummary`.
- [ ] The chips, the classification glyph, the private-folder footer and the drop-overlay figures are unchanged for that same non-moderator — counts intact.
- [ ] A moderator's payload is unchanged.
- [ ] `GET /access` and `GET /access/destinations` audited for the same leak; findings stated either way.

## Verification

Not a unit test on a redaction helper — that passes whether or not the route calls it. Assert on the **route's response body** for a non-moderator subject, byte-scanning for `@` and for a known granted domain, then mutation-prove by removing the redaction call and watching it go red.

Portico has certified behaviour that never happened live at least five times; a green helper test is not evidence the wire changed.

cards.title: Teach the client eslint config the `^_` intentional-unused convention — two disable comments are standing in for it
cards.description:
`npx eslint .` was failing on `client/app` main with two `@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars` errors. Both are the same idiom — a binding that exists in order **not** to be read — and the codebase clearly already uses the `_` prefix to say so:

* `features/viewer/panes/registry.ts` — `pickPane(kind, _sourceUrl)` accepts and ignores the source, so `registry.test.ts` can hand it an HTML-looking source for a grid artifact and prove the grid pane still comes back. The parameter **is** the guarantee that the client never sniffs the source.
* `features/viewer/queries/render.test.ts` — `const { fileContentType: _omit, ...rest }` strips a key. Building the object without the field would stop testing the thing under test.

[DRE-2410](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2410/access-peek-lands-moderators-only-the-chip-names-people-so-the-panel) (PR 265) unblocked CI by adding a targeted `eslint-disable-next-line` at each site, with the reason. That is a stopgap: two authors independently reached for `_`, so the real defect is a config that does not honour a convention the codebase uses. The next `_`-prefixed binding errors again and gets a third comment.

## The fix

In `client/app/eslint.config.js`, on `@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars`:

```js
"@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars": ["error", {
  argsIgnorePattern: "^_",
  varsIgnorePattern: "^_",
  caughtErrorsIgnorePattern: "^_",
  ignoreRestSiblings: true,
}],
```

Then remove both disable comments — keeping the explanatory prose, which is worth having either way.

## Why it was not done in PR 265

That config's own header records why it is glob-based: *"any later rule card only ADD a file and never reopen this config — a shared config edited by two open PRs conflicts every sibling (engineering standard, shared-files rule)."* There were sibling branches in flight (`ui/*`, [DRE-2393](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2393/two-real-browser-sessions-prove-it-and-the-sandbox-and-csp-are-re), PR 255) when 265 landed. This wants a quiet tree.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `npx eslint .` clean in `client/app` with **no** `no-unused-vars` disable comments left in `registry.ts` or `render.test.ts`.
- [ ] A deliberately unused NON-underscored binding still errors — add one, see it red, remove it. The rule must not have been softened into silence.
- [ ] Full client suite still green.

cards.title: Bounces and complaints on user-pool auth mail are not recorded anywhere
cards.description:
Split out of [DRE-2408](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2408/the-sign-in-code-email-still-says-only-your-authentication-code-is), which asked to either cover this or split it. It is split because covering it inside DRE-2408 would have changed a second, riskier thing about the same live pool, and the riskier thing has a trap in it (below).

## The gap, confirmed by reading the code — no AWS access needed

`SesBounceFn` exists and works, but it only ever sees **notification** mail. The chain is:

* `lib/parts/ses.ts` creates the configuration set `docs-comments-<slug>` and subscribes `SesBounceFn` to the SNS topic that set publishes to.
* Only the CRUD Lambda names that set (`SES_CONFIGURATION_SET`), and only for comment/reply/resolve notifications.
* The **user pool** deliberately names no configuration set at all (`lib/comment-stack.ts`, the comment above the pool). So a bounced or spam-reported sign-in code produces no SNS event, no metric, and no record anywhere.

On the old `COGNITO_DEFAULT` sender that was AWS's reputation to manage. Since DRE-2394 the everybite pool sends as `<redacted-email>` on our own verified domain, so it is our sending reputation now, and we cannot see it.

## The trap — do not simply attach the existing set

The existing set has SES account-level suppression on for **bounces and complaints**. Attach it to auth mail and one reader pressing "spam" on a sign-in code suppresses that address for every future send — a silent, permanent sign-in lockout for a person who is still entitled to read. That is why the pool has no configuration set today, and it is the constraint any fix has to design around.

## What a fix probably looks like

* A **second, auth-only** configuration set, suppression **off**, attached to the pool via `EmailConfiguration.ConfigurationSet`, publishing bounce + complaint events to the same SNS topic.
* Source attribution in `bounce_lib`: a bounce on `no-reply@<domain>` is not a project notification. Today `mail.source` is reverse-mapped through `NOTIFY_FROM`, so an auth-mail bounce would attribute to `unknown` and flip the notification pref off for **every** project — wrong, and worse than not recording it. Auth mail needs its own classification that records and alarms but writes no pref.
* An alarm on the auth-mail bounce/complaint metric, since the failure it detects (readers not receiving codes) is invisible from the product side.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A bounce or complaint on a sign-in / sign-up / invite email is recorded with a metric, same shape as the notification path
- [ ] No complaint on auth mail can suppress a reader's address or disable their notification prefs — pinned by a test
- [ ] Wired in CDK; the notification configuration set and its suppression behaviour are unchanged
- [ ] An account with no `cognitoEmail` (dreadnought, still SES sandbox — DRE-2325) is unaffected
- [ ] A WARN and a CRITICAL threshold exist for the new metric

## Out of scope

The dreadnought pool, for the same reason as DRE-2408: still SES sandbox, blocked on DRE-2325.

cards.title: [EPIC] The Claude credential architecture — every gap found in the 2026-08-11/12 three-day outage
cards.description:
**Parked in Backlog deliberately** — this carries a `repo:` label and a card in Todo is auto-dispatched to a build agent. This is a specification to break into children, not a card to build.

## What happened

For **three days**, every QA critic and fix agent across two repos died with:

```
"is_error": true,  "num_turns": 1,  "total_cost_usd": 0
```

Instant, no inference, no cost. It was read as "the AI service is unavailable" and as code rejections. Work stacked at the merge gate. **Four separate wrong diagnoses** were made before the truth, because every link in the chain fails with that same signature and nothing distinguishes them.

The root cause was a credential pointing at an exhausted Claude account, hidden behind a repo secret shadowing an org one, behind a console button that could never write because a GitHub App permission had never been granted. Each fact alone defeats the obvious fix.

Everything below is verified, not inferred. The gaps are ordered by what would have shortened the outage most.

---

## 1. Nothing detects a stale or exhausted credential before it burns a run

**The highest-value fix on this card.**

`model_fallback.py:495-508` — `classify_available` returns True for everything except HTTP 404. **401, 403 and 429 all read as AVAILABLE.** `_probe_real:528-531` treats *no token at all* as available. So the probe says "Fable is fine", the critic selects it, and the action dies at 0.6s / $0.

Make 401/403 a third state that fails the step **loudly and by name** — "the CI credential is rejected" is a different sentence from "the model is unavailable", and the operator needs the first one.

## 2. The health monitor watches the wrong store

`monitors/claude_account_health.py:443-445` probes the console's **vaulted** token. CI authenticates with the **GitHub Actions secret**. They are different stores and they drift.

This is exactly why the operator's dashboard showed 0% used while CI was dead: the console was reporting on an account CI wasn't using. A monitor that cannot see the credential CI actually presents is not monitoring CI.

## 3. Repo secrets silently shadow org secrets

Since 2026-08-10, portico, agent-bureau and bureau-pipeline each carry a **repo-level** `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, written by hand within one second of each other during an earlier outage. A repo secret overrides the org secret of the same name, so `gh secret set --org` **rotates a value nothing reads — and reports success.**

The console's own fan-out writes repo-level, so this is the intended architecture. What is missing is that nothing surfaces which value a given repo actually reads. `DRE-2402` §7 has the measured drift: portico/agent-bureau 08-12, bureau-pipeline 08-10, atlas/deltasolv 07-12, agent-bureau-demo 06-17, vericorr 06-11, org copy (inert) 07-29. **Two months of drift is the normal state, not an anomaly.**

## 4. Reconnect's fan-out had never once worked — and still cannot reach two orgs

Its fan-out writes through `agent-bureau-bot`, which **lacked** `secrets: write` **entirely**. Per-repo failures are recorded and deliberately never abort, so it reported success while writing nothing. The card's own honesty line read *"the pipeline secret has never been rotated from here"* — literally true, for months.

Granted on `dreadnought-foundry` (installation 123249480) on 2026-08-12. **Still NOT GRANTED on EveryBite (139260935) and DeltaSolv (141993364)** — so `atlas` and `deltasolv` remain unreachable by any fan-out.

**The gap to build:** when the fan-out cannot write, that must be a *loud, actionable* failure naming the missing permission and the org — not a silent per-repo skip under a success banner.

## 5. A manual account switch does not re-point CI (`DRE-2400`)

Two engines on one toggle, per `claude_pool.py:45-52`:

| trigger | re-fans the repo secret? |
| -- | -- |
| hard failover — probe verdict of cap/expiry (`DRE-2318`) | **yes** |
| soft threshold, 80% (`DRE-1607`) | no |
| **operator switching account by hand in the UI** | **no** |

A manual switch is the same class as the soft path: it repoints the console only. **This is exactly what caused the outage** — the account was switched to EveryBite at 0% while CI stayed pinned to dreadnoughtfoundry at 99%.

`DRE-2400` is filed and parked pending a decision between warn-only, a second explicit "move CI too" click, or automatic. **The actuator already exists** (`run_failover` writes the secret); it simply is not reachable from a manual switch.

## 6. The two-store split is invisible in the UI (`agent-bureau PR 2035`)

The Subscriptions UI updates the console's billing creds (`CLAUDE_OAUTH_*`). The pipeline's Actions secret is a **different store**, written only by the Reconnect button beside it. Switching accounts and reconnecting are two clicks on one page, and missing the second silently starves CI for days.

PR 2035 makes the drift visible and leads the operator from a switch to the reconnect. **Open, all real checks green.**

## 7. There is now a diagnostic — finish it (`agent-bureau PR 2036`)

`scripts/claude_cred_doctor.py`, seven independently-runnable checks, naming the **first** broken link rather than emitting seven identical failures. Its `token-live` check is the one that would have saved the outage: it distinguishes **invalid credential** from **out of quota**, which produce byte-identical symptoms.

On its first live run it found the EveryBite/DeltaSolv gap in §4, the nine-repo shadowing in §3, and that five repos — not the two expected — had missed the last rotation.

**Open, 3330 tests passing.** Land it, then wire §1 and §2 to reuse its classification rather than growing a second opinion.

## 8. The budget alarm cancels itself on failover (`DRE-2399`, in flight)

The monitor failed the pipeline over to a fresh account and then judged the budget on whichever account was now active — and the replacement has headroom *by definition*, because that is why failover picked it. So the warning raised for the drained account read as "recovered" and cleared itself fifteen minutes later, **while that account sat at 99% with nothing watching it.**

Already has a PR. Listed here because it is the same failure family: a signal that erases itself.

## 9. The OAuth *code* and the OAuth *token* are different artifacts, and nothing says so

The console's Reconnect box takes a `code#state` authorization code. `gh secret set` needs an `sk-ant-oat01-…` token. They look similar, arrive minutes apart, and pasting the first where the second belongs produces — again — the identical instant failure. This cost real time during the incident.

Wherever either value is requested, say which one and what it is for.

---

## Acceptance for the epic

- [ ] A stale or rejected credential fails **loudly, by name**, before an agent burns a run
- [ ] The health monitor watches the store CI actually authenticates with
- [ ] A fan-out that cannot write says so, naming the org and the missing permission
- [ ] The operator can see, for any repo, **which credential CI will actually present** and how old it is
- [ ] A manual account switch either moves CI or says plainly that it did not
- [ ] `claude_cred_doctor` is landed and is the single source of the classification logic

## Related

`DRE-2400`, `DRE-2399`, `DRE-2318`, `DRE-1607`, `DRE-2076`; PRs `agent-bureau#2035`, `#2036`. Portico-side record and operator checklist: `DRE-2402`.

cards.title: OPEN THREADS — everything left unconcluded from the 2026-08-11/12 session
cards.description:
A checklist, not a card to build. **Deliberately parked in Backlog** — it carries a `repo:` label and a card in Todo is auto-dispatched to a build agent by the relay. Nothing here should be built from this description; each item names its own home.

Written 2026-08-12 so re-engaging is a matter of checking things off rather than reconstructing what happened.

---

## 1. Operator actions — nothing else moves without these

- [ ] **Attach the new Lambda@Edge versions** via `_tool/aws/signin-gate.sh`. Deployed but NOT live until attached; CloudFront keeps serving the old version. everybite `…EdgeGateFnE48DA65F-ztXk7zWDJCTn:10`, dreadnought `…-5bOpmmMBDIvA:7`, vericorr TBC.
  - **Check each distribution's current viewer-request association first.** On everybite the old version's delete FAILED (a distribution still referenced it — normal). On dreadnought it deleted CLEANLY, which means no distribution there referenced the previous version. That account serves [share.vericorr.com](<http://share.vericorr.com>), [docs.deltasolv.com](<http://docs.deltasolv.com>) and [share.gridcorr.com](<http://share.gridcorr.com>), so it is worth knowing what they are actually pinned to before attaching.
- [ ] **Grant** `secrets: write` **on TWO more org installations**: EveryBite `139260935` and DeltaSolv `141993364`. dreadnought-foundry `123249480` is done. Until then the console's Reconnect fan-out silently writes nothing to `atlas` and `deltasolv` — both frozen at 2026-07-12.
- [ ] **Replace the OAuth token exposed in the session transcript** (`sk-ant-oat01-…`, one-year validity). Mint fresh, re-set the portico and agent-bureau secrets, revoke the old one if a revoke path exists. Do not paste the value into chat.
- [ ] **Test Reconnect end-to-end.** The cached-token hypothesis is confirmed (`GitHubAppTokenProvider` caches installation tokens until ~5 min before their 1-hour expiry, so the click 4 min after the grant used pre-grant scopes). Click once, then check whether repo secret timestamps move on their own. Expect dreadnought-foundry repos to move and atlas/deltasolv not to — that is the item above.
- [ ] **Review and merge** `dreadnought-foundry/gridcorr` **PR 1** ([DRE-2390](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2390/the-intake-questionnaire-emits-per-field-edits-and-applies-inbound)). That repo has **no CI workflows at all** — zero checks, nothing will ever review it automatically, and agents do not self-merge. It also **rewrote the questionnaire's confidentiality copy**, because "answers stay in this browser… nothing is transmitted" is false inside the viewer. That is a promise to a regulated utility and wants the operator's own eye.
- [ ] **Decide which Claude account backs the fleet's CI token.** The last rotation was for VeriCorr; a successful fan-out writes ONE token to ALL repos, so every company's CI would bill VeriCorr and it would overwrite the token hand-set on portico.

## 2. Decisions made but NOT yet implemented

- [ ] **Access peek is moderators-only** (decided 2026-08-12). Gate `peek` on the moderator group at three call sites — `Grid.tsx`, `ListView.tsx`, `LibraryScreen.tsx`. The pure module and the panel are unaffected. Reason: `GET /library` is not moderator-gated and `accessSummary.people` is raw email addresses; the data was already on the wire, but that UI is what makes a partner's staff list readable by every signed-in project member. On branch `ui/library-details`.

## 3. Unlanded work, analysed and safe — three branches, all pushed

Each branch's HEAD commit carries the full analysis. Nothing is lost; nothing is landed.

- [ ] `ui/viewer-comments` — comments rail: resolve/reopen, delete, shared `/me`, orphan-reply promotion. **Two chrome hunks do not apply to main** (they anchor on `RailFrame`/`RAIL_TITLES` from this branch's own unlanded commit; main solved rail chrome with `RailHost`). ~20 minutes of rework.
- [ ] `ui/library-details` — access peek (see §2), the share-panel group fix, and "Edit details…". The share-panel fix is the smallest, cleanest, zero-conflict change in any of the three: the panel currently calls `moderators` a company and draws a globe beside a Cognito group, with its heading disagreeing with its own footer. `ActionDialog.tsx` needs a five-minute hand-merge against PR 258's `DialogShell` export.
- [ ] `ui/work` — the local dev stack (largest, best-finished, zero conflicts — **belongs on** `infra/*`**, not** `ui/*`), the anchor bridge, and a second comments-rail pass. **Split** `ingest_lib.ts` **before making PRs**: hunk A goes with the dev stack, hunk B (`injectFocusHighlightStyle`) with the anchor bridge, or the two PRs collide on one file. Hunk B changes rendered bytes for EVERY artifact, so the next ingest of any document mints a new revision — state that in the PR.
  - `postMessageProtocol.ts` **+** `FramePane.tsx` **must be RE-TYPED, not merged.** Written against a ViewerShell main has since rebuilt, and the outbound scroll-to post is ungated — it bypasses the two-guard gate [DRE-2389](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2389/the-frame-protocol-gains-a-second-direction-and-the-parent-must-prove) paid for. The design survives; the diff does not.
  - `HANDOFF.md` is committed only so its content survives. Card its §7 decisions and §11 findings, then delete it.
- [ ] **Pick ONE of the two comment-action implementations.** `ui/work` and `ui/viewer-comments` are independent attempts at the same feature from the same base commit — ~900 lines of near-duplicate. Neither is a superset. `ui/viewer-comments` is better factored and gets resolve semantics right; `ui/work` has Edit and click-to-highlight. There is a visual-language choice inside it (icon glyphs vs text buttons). **Do not merge the two** `Thread.tsx` **files.**

## 4. Stale branch pointers — verify then delete

Content confirmed on main by grep; the pointers only *look* unmerged because of squash-merges.

- [ ] `agent/DRE-2355-frame-app` — 9 frame/app markers present on main
- [ ] `feat/drafts-space` — `drafts` present in the everybite config on main
- [ ] `wip/DRE-2355-moderator-gate` — superseded by [DRE-2364](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2364/frameapp-gate-on-the-moderator-role-and-give-the-migration-runner-a), which is on main
- [ ] `agent/om2-run-record` — not investigated

## 4b. Orphaned AWS resources from the 2026-08-12 deploys

CloudFormation warned explicitly: *"Some resources failed to delete but were skipped. These resources may still exist and could incur charges. Clean them up manually."*

- [ ] **everybite** — superseded `EdgeGateFnCurrentVersionDF82D614f41e7b2b9c2f148bbe4cb026f33f570e`, delete failed and skipped (a CloudFront distribution still references it)
- [ ] **vericorr** — superseded `EdgeGateFnCurrentVersionDF82D61482c4e259cd204cc1fd187ffeb6770707`, three retries, all skipped (Summit Midstream's distribution still references version 5)
- dreadnought needs nothing — its old version deleted cleanly, which is itself the anomaly noted in §1

A Lambda@Edge version cannot be deleted while any distribution references it, and CloudFront replicas take hours to drain. So these become deletable only **after** `signin-gate.sh` moves the distributions onto the new versions — do that first, wait, then remove the strays. The charge is negligible; the reason to clean up is that a stray version is indistinguishable from a live one when someone is trying to work out what the edge is actually running.

## 5. Known defects found and NOT fixed

- [ ] **Every Lambda is** `nodejs20.x`, deprecated 2026-04-30. Updates disabled from **2027-03-03**. Seven functions across three accounts — a hard deadline, not a preference.
- [ ] `gridcorr` **has no CI whatsoever** while publishing to a live portal.
- [ ] [DRE-2401](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2401/the-vericorr-aws-profile-cannot-deploy-the-credential-named-deploy-is) — the `vericorr` profile cannot deploy.
- [ ] [DRE-2400](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2400/a-manual-or-soft-threshold-active-account-change-doesnt-re-point-ci) — a manual or soft-threshold account switch does not re-fan `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`; only a hard cap verdict does. Parked pending a decision between warn-only / a second explicit click / automatic.
- [ ] The SPA mints an idempotency key it never sends, and CORS `allowHeaders` could not carry it anyway (found in `HANDOFF.md` §11, uncarded).

## 6. In flight at the time of writing

* portico PR 259 (CLAUDE.md: agents may deploy with per-deploy consent), PR 260 (comment-rail author/date/resolved fix), PR 255 ([DRE-2362](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2362/phase-4s-harness-reports-a-false-fail-clause-49-greps-a-spelling-dre), DIRTY — needs a rebase)
* agent-bureau PRs 2033, 2034, 2035, 2036 (2036 is the credential doctor)
* Epic [DRE-2383](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2383/epic-shared-answers-for-the-oncor-intake-questionnaire-per-field-sync) at 8 of 11: 2390 blocked on the gridcorr merge, 2393 behind it, 2395 last

## 7. Environment, left clean

Worktrees pruned 37 → 10; 139 merged local branches deleted; all three `ui/*` branches pushed to origin (they had never been pushed — 6 commits and 72 files existed on one disk only). Remaining worktrees: the primary (detached at `17ec8aa`, **stale — do not deploy from it**), `portico-infra`, three `ui/*`, `agent-a24d2b3504f2b13dc`, `agent-a6276fa04f58f9e16` (on current main, used for the deploys), `assistant`, `ci-pipeline`, `publish`.

cards.title: The `vericorr` AWS profile cannot deploy — the credential named *-deploy is the one that can't
cards.description:
Found 2026-08-12 while deploying the response routes to all three accounts. Not blocking — `vericorr-admin` works and was used instead — but something is mislabelled or a policy was dropped, and a credential whose *name* promises what it cannot do is exactly what costs an hour during an incident.

## What happens

`npm run diff -- -c account=vericorr --profile vericorr` fails on permissions, not content:

```
User: arn:aws:iam::340646328578:user/vericorr-deploy is not authorized to perform:
cloudformation:DescribeStacks on resource:
arn:aws:cloudformation:us-east-1:340646328578:stack/DocsComments-vericorr/d62285e0-...
```

and

```
sts:AssumeRole on cdk-hnb659fds-deploy-role-340646328578-us-east-1 -> AccessDenied
```

So `vericorr-deploy` can neither read the stack nor assume the CDK deploy role. A `cdk deploy` with that profile fails on its first CloudFormation call.

## What is true about the two profiles

Both `vericorr` and `vericorr-admin` resolve to the **same account, 340646328578**. `vericorr-admin` is simply a higher-privileged user, not a different account. This matches `CLAUDE.md`'s publishing note that summit-midstream *publishes* with `vericorr-admin` and *seeds* with `vericorr` — the split is real and intentional for those two jobs. What is not explained anywhere is why the seed-tier credential is named `-deploy`.

## Why it matters

`infra/README.md` and this repo's docs hand the operator `--profile vericorr` for infra work. Anyone following that hits an `AccessDenied` that looks like a broken stack rather than a wrong credential — which is how it presented today.

## What to decide

One of:

1. **Grant** `vericorr-deploy` **what its name implies** — `cloudformation:*` on the stack plus `sts:AssumeRole` on the CDK deploy role. Right if it was ever meant to deploy.
2. **Rename it to what it is** (`vericorr-seed`, say) and correct every doc that hands out `--profile vericorr` for a deploy. Right if the privilege split is deliberate and should stay.

Either way, `CLAUDE.md`'s command block and `infra/README.md` should name the profile that actually works for each job, per account.

## Not to be confused with

`vericorr`'s repo-level `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, which deliberately shadows the org key so Vericorr's inference bills to Vericorr. Different subject, same word.

cards.title: A manual (or soft-threshold) active-account change doesn't re-point CI — only DRE-2318's hard cap failover does, and the Subscriptions UI implies otherwise
cards.description:
**Parked on purpose.** This is filed for Sid's decision, not for a build agent. It changes which company's Claude subscription pays for every onboarded repo's CI, so it stays in Backlog until he chooses. The *visibility* half is already shipping separately (PR: warn on the Subscriptions page when CI is not on the active account).

## What happens today

Switching the active Claude subscription — by hand on the Subscriptions page, or by the soft 80% auto-advance — repoints **this console** and nothing else. CI keeps authenticating as whichever account the pipeline secret was last written for.

Only the **hard cap failover** re-fans the secret: `claude_pool.run_failover` (`console/backend/claude_pool.py:368`) calls `put_actions_secret` per repo (line 415), gated by the same "Auto-switch when exhausted" toggle (`failover_enabled`, line 359), scheduled from `console/backend/monitors/claude_pool_failover.py:34`. That is [DRE-2318](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2318/claude-accounts-are-an-ordered-pool-with-automatic-failover-a-capped) and it works. But it fires only on a probe verdict of cap or expiry (`_UNUSABLE`, line 100).

The two soft paths do not touch the secret at all:

* `subscriptions.auto_advance_active_account` (`console/backend/subscriptions.py:252`, [DRE-1607](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-1607/epic-production-demo-environment-drop-work-in-watch-agents-fan-out), 80% threshold) — writes `cost_usage.set_active_account` and stops.
* the `setActiveAccount` mutation (`console/backend/schema.py:8582`) behind "Use this" — same.

## What it cost (2026-08-11/12)

The active account was switched to `<redacted-email>`, 5-hour window at 0%. CI carried on authenticating as `<redacted-email>`, which was at **99% of its 5-hour window and "Cooling down"**.

Every CI critic and fix agent then died with `is_error: true, num_turns: 1, total_cost_usd: 0` — instant, zero-cost refusals with no error text. **Ten of them across three days.** They were read as "the AI service is unavailable" and as the critic rejecting the code. The dashboard showed a healthy account the whole time, because the account it was showing was not the one CI was using.

## The decision this card is asking for

Should a manual switch also re-point CI?

The actuator already exists, so the code is small. Roughly: after `persist_active_account` in the `setActiveAccount` mutation, resolve `claude_pool.default_token_for(chosen)` (which reads the per-account vault slot the Reconnect flow writes), fan it to every repo in `sources.REPOS` via `AppActionsSecretsClient.put_actions_secret`, then `claude_pool.clear_assignments(store, rotated)` — the same three steps `claude_reconnect.complete` legs 3-and-clear already perform.

Small is not the same as safe. Three reasons it needs a human decision:

1. **It moves money silently.** One click would move every onboarded repo's inference spend onto the newly-chosen account, across five companies' repos, with no confirmation and nothing in the UI that reads like a billing change.
2. **It fights the per-repo homes.** The pool deliberately keeps per-project home accounts (`repo_accounts` in `console/backend/claude-accounts.json`: atlas → EveryBite, vericorr → VeriCorr, [DRE-1695](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-1695/backfill-existing-projects-subscription-make-subscription-account-not)/2318). A global fan-out overwrites all of them and clears their assignments; the next pool tick has to rebuild the world.
3. **It can only reach accounts the console holds a token for.** `default_token_for` returns None for an account that has never been reconnected, so the fan-out would silently skip — or, worse, half-apply across repos.

Plausible answers, cheapest first:

* **A. Warn only** (what is shipping now): the page names who CI is really on and offers Reconnect. No behaviour change, no billing surprise. Costs the operator one extra deliberate step per switch.
* **B. Offer it, don't do it**: after a manual switch, a "Move CI too" button that runs the fan-out explicitly. Same actuator, but the billing move is a second, named click.
* **C. Do it automatically**: the manual switch fans out. Fastest, and the one that can move a company's spend without anyone noticing.

## Acceptance criteria (only if Sid picks B or C)

- [ ] A manual `setActiveAccount` re-points the pipeline secret through the existing `put_actions_secret` path — never a new secret-writing code path.
- [ ] Accounts with no stored credential are refused up front with a plain-English message, not skipped silently.
- [ ] Per-repo failures are recorded by repo name and never abort the rest (matching `claude_reconnect.complete`).
- [ ] Per-repo pool assignments are cleared for exactly the repos written (`claude_pool.clear_assignments`), so the recorded serving account can't lie.
- [ ] Per-repo home accounts are either honoured or the override is stated in the UI copy — not silently overwritten.
- [ ] No token value is logged, echoed, alerted, or returned in a GraphQL field.
- [ ] A test reproduces the 2026-08-11 shape: active switched to a fresh account, and CI's secret follows (or provably does not, under option B, until the second click).

## Evidence

* `console/backend/claude_pool.py:100,359,368,415` — the hard-failover actuator and its cap-only trigger.
* `console/backend/subscriptions.py:252` — the soft 80% advance; console-only.
* `console/backend/schema.py:8582` — the manual `setActiveAccount` mutation; console-only.
* `console/backend/claude_reconnect.py:468-489` — the fan-out plus assignment-clear this would reuse.

cards.title: A bounced notification email can silently lock someone out of sign-in
cards.description:
**A risk introduced by** [DRE-2394](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2394/send-cognito-email-through-ses-as-no-replyeverybitecom-and-make-the)**, found by the agent that shipped it.** Not a defect in that change — a consequence of it that needs closing.

Moving the pool's email to SES puts **sign-in one-time codes** under the account-level SES **suppression list**. So anyone whose address once bounced or was reported as spam — on a *comment notification*, months ago — can be silently unable to sign in. No error the reader can see, no error we can see without looking, and no way for them to tell us apart from "the code never arrived."

Before [DRE-2394](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2394/send-cognito-email-through-ses-as-no-replyeverybitecom-and-make-the) this could not happen: codes went through `COGNITO_DEFAULT`, where deliverability was AWS's problem and unrelated to our notification traffic.

## Why the obvious fix is wrong

`SesBounceFn` exists and handles bounces — but it is fed by the `docs-comments-<slug>` **configuration set**, which only `notify.ts` names. The [DRE-2394](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2394/send-cognito-email-through-ses-as-no-replyeverybitecom-and-make-the) agent deliberately did **not** attach that set to auth mail, and was right:

* It would put sign-in codes under suppression for bounces **and complaints** — one spam report and that address loses sign-in **permanently and silently**.
* `bounce_lib.attribute()` maps a bounce to a project from the notification's shape; an auth email has no project, so it would mis-attribute to every project.

So auth mail needs its own handling, not the notification path.

## Scope

1. **A dedicated configuration set for auth mail**, with **account-level suppression overridden off** for it. A sign-in code must be attempted even if the address is suppressed — the whole point of the code is that it is how someone regains access.
2. **An event destination for it** so bounces and complaints on auth mail are *visible*. Silence is the current failure mode; do not replace one silence with another.
3. **Attribution that does not lie.** An auth bounce has no project. Either extend `bounce_lib.attribute()` to represent "auth, no project", or keep auth events on a separate path — but do not let them be counted against every project.
4. **An alarm on auth-mail bounce rate.** A rising rate is the only early signal that sign-in is failing for real people, and it is otherwise invisible: the reader assumes the code is slow and gives up.
5. **Check the existing suppression list now.** Any address already on it, from any past notification bounce, is currently unable to sign in to an everybite portal once [DRE-2394](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2394/send-cognito-email-through-ses-as-no-replyeverybitecom-and-make-the) deploys. Enumerate them and say who is affected before the deploy, not after.

## Acceptance

* A sign-in code is delivered to an address on the account suppression list, proven by putting a test address on it and signing in.
* Auth bounces and complaints appear somewhere a human looks, attributed honestly.
* An alarm fires on an auth-mail bounce-rate rise.
* No auth bounce is counted against a project it has nothing to do with.
* The pre-deploy suppression-list check is recorded, with whoever is on it named.
