cards.title: OPERATOR: re-publish the questionnaire and turn shared answering on for d-readiness
cards.description:
Put the rebuilt questionnaire live and switch shared answering on for it. Only you can run this — agents hold no cloud credentials and never deploy, migrate or seed.

**Blocked by:** [DRE-2390](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2390/the-intake-questionnaire-emits-per-field-edits-and-applies-inbound) (the rebuilt document), [DRE-2393](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2393/two-real-browser-sessions-prove-it-and-the-sandbox-and-csp-are-re) (the executed two-session proof). Do not publish before the proof exists; the last time this document went live it looked complete and answered nothing.

## The one door, and why it is the only one

The re-render has to go through **the migration runner**: `infra/scripts/migrate-legacy-docs.ts` with `--as-app`, `portico-publisher=pipeline`, and `portico-actor` set to a real moderator of the `gridcorr` project. Ingest asks Cognito (`AdminListGroupsForUser`) whether that address is in `moderators` **and** in the project, and demotes the `app` claim to `foreign` unless both hold. A static frame with a line in the log is what a wrong address gets you.

**Do not use the Add-document upload flow.** It cannot produce a `frame/app` at all today: `ingest.ts` passes `appGrant: null` while the plan can legitimately be `'app'`, `renderStoredArtifact` throws on that pair, and the throw sits above `recordFailure`. The event is dropped, the document stays `ingestState: ready` **at its previous revision**, and the only trace is three CloudWatch lines. It looks like it worked. That is [DRE-2381](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2381/the-upload-path-cannot-produce-a-frameapp-at-all-it-throws-drops-the); if you want the upload path back, land it first.

Full procedure and the metadata template are in `docs/runbooks/app-frames.md`.

## Two live traps to avoid

* **Library ids are deterministic path slugs** (`d-<slug>`). Re-publishing must not change the document's id, or it appears twice — the published URL never changes, only the library metadata moves.
* **Do not re-run** `scripts/seed-library.ts`**.** The gridcorr library is UI-managed now, so `seed-data/gridcorr.tree.json` is stale, and re-seeding can clobber changes and resurrect moved or deleted items. It is a bootstrap tool only.

## What to run, in order

1. Build the questionnaire in `dreadnought-foundry/gridcorr` and confirm the built `readiness.html` still works at its own URL.
2. Stage the bytes in quarantine with your own credentials and the metadata from the runbook.
3. Re-render `d-readiness` through the migration runner with `--as-app`.
4. Turn on `canRespond` for `d-readiness` as a moderator.
5. Confirm the grants: Hagen and Yannan are viewers, and viewers with the toggle on may answer — they do **not** need to become editors, and promoting them would also hand them rename, move, delete and re-share on the document.
6. `bash infra/scripts/verify-portal.sh gridcorr`.

## Constraints that do not move — restated

1. The frame is `sandbox="allow-scripts"` with **no** same-origin grant. Nothing in this procedure changes it.
2. The artifact CSP is `default-src 'none'; … connect-src 'none'; form-action 'none'`. If a served artifact does not carry `connect-src 'none'`, stop and report it — that is the directive proven to prevent the document sending its whole dataset out in a URL.
3. `localStorage` and downloads are blocked inside the frame. The document's own Share button is hidden there on purpose; the viewer's chrome carries that action.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The served artifact carries the new document code: `aws s3 cp s3://portico-content-<slug>/…/r/<rev>/index.html - | grep -c portico` returns non-zero, the way the [DRE-2338](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2338/migrated-documents-have-no-anchor-bridge-dre-2326-wired-the-upload) runbook check does.
- [ ] The served artifact carries `connect-src 'none'`.
- [ ] `d-readiness` still has exactly one library row, at its original id.
- [ ] `canRespond` is on for `d-readiness` and off everywhere else.
- [ ] Hagen and Yannan are still `viewer`, not `editor`.
- [ ] `verify-portal.sh gridcorr` passes.
- [ ] A follow-on card is open to add the re-publish step to `docs/runbooks/app-frames.md`.

## How this is verified

**By you, in the live portal, with a person watching.** Open the document as Hagen in one browser and as Yannan in another. Hagen answers question 1. Yannan answers question 2. Both see both without reloading. Then both write into the same answer and check that the conflict appears and resolves.

Post the result on this card: the two greps above, the `verify-portal.sh` output, and a screenshot of the two sessions. If any of it does not behave as the executed proof said it would, the difference between the mock and the live account is the finding, and it is worth more than the publish.

The one call I need from you: run this and confirm on the card.

cards.title: [EPIC] Shared answers for the Oncor intake questionnaire — per-field sync in the parent, no CRDT in v1
cards.description:
Hagen and Yannan will fill in the same questionnaire together, each seeing the other's answers within a few seconds, and neither can lose the other's work without being told. We are not using a collaborative-editing engine to do it. This card previously specified Yjs; the review below found that Yjs cannot produce its one real advantage through the seam this card chose, so v1 ships the smaller mechanism that does work. The door to a CRDT stays open and the conditions that would open it are written down.

## Verdict on the previous architecture: reject the mechanism, keep the goal

Three parts of the earlier design were right and are kept:

* **Sync lives in the parent SPA, never in the frame.** The frame is at an opaque origin with `connect-src 'none'`; it cannot open a socket, and that boundary does not move for any feature.
* `postMessage` **is the only channel**, gated by `parseFrameMessage`, one hostile-message test leg per new type.
* **The confidentiality copy is a shipping gate, not a footnote.** It ships with the feature or the feature does not ship.

Two parts were wrong, and they were the load-bearing two.

### Flaw 1 — the storage shim destroys the property Yjs was chosen for

The document writes its whole state as one blob: `setItem(KEY, JSON.stringify(state))`, one key. A shim over `localStorage` therefore hands the parent **a full snapshot, not an edit**. To turn snapshots into CRDT operations you must diff consecutive snapshots, and a diff cannot tell "Hagen added a sentence" from "Hagen replaced the paragraph". It is worse than that: each snapshot the document writes already contains the copy of Yannan's field that the parent pushed in earlier, so every save replays a possibly-stale copy of her text back over the shared state. Feeding that into `Y.Text` re-applies it as a replacement.

The result is whole-blob last-writer-wins, produced by a CRDT. `Y.Text` merges concurrent edits only when it is fed keystroke-level operations from the input element itself. Through a whole-blob storage proxy it cannot be. So the design as drafted paid every cost of Yjs — a new dependency, a binary log, a materialised projection, a compaction scheme, a 400 KB ceiling — and got last-writer-wins anyway.

### Flaw 2 — the 222 textareas argue for per-field sync, not for a text CRDT

222 free-text fields is a real number and it does rule out naive last-writer-wins keyed on client clocks. It does not imply a text CRDT. This is a form with 619 discrete inputs across 132 questions, filled by two people dividing the work by question. It is closer to a spreadsheet than to a prose document, and per-cell is how spreadsheets do it.

For a compliance questionnaire a text CRDT is also the wrong *behaviour*, not just the wrong cost. If Hagen and Yannan write different paragraphs into the same box at the same time, `Y.Text` does not lose either — it interleaves them into text no human wrote, and nothing flags it. That answer goes to a utility's security team. "Both versions, side by side, a person picks" is a better outcome than a silent merge, and it is much less code.

The offline/stale-write case from the old card's table is real and is solved without a CRDT: **a server-assigned per-field version, refused on mismatch**. That is per-field optimistic concurrency, roughly the pattern `routes/access.ts` already uses for its conditional epoch bump. Calling it "reimplementing part of Yjs" overstates it.

### What we rejected, and why — recorded so it is not reopened

| Option | Rejected because |
| -- | -- |
| Yjs through a `localStorage` shim | Flaw 1. Pays for a CRDT, behaves as last-writer-wins. |
| Yjs fed per-field from the document | Works, but the document change it requires is the same change per-field sync needs, and then the CRDT buys only same-textarea interleaving — which we do not want. Deferred, not dismissed. |
| Automerge | Same class as Yjs, larger payload, no advantage here. If we ever want a CRDT, Yjs is the right one. |
| Liveblocks or any hosted realtime vendor | A third party would hold a utility's cyber-readiness answers, which are a map of its own weaknesses. Portico's trust boundary is the AWS account per company (`ADR-0003`); a shared vendor store breaks it, needs a new subprocessor disclosure, and would cost more in review than the feature costs to build. |
| Per-field last-writer-wins on client timestamps | Clock skew means a stale client with a fast clock silently wins. Server-assigned versions instead. |

**What would change our mind about the CRDT:** a workflow where two people genuinely co-author one answer box at the same time and want character-level merging, or a refusal rate on the per-field conflict path high enough to annoy people. Neither is in evidence. Measure the refusal rate before reopening.

## The v1 architecture

```
document (in frame)  ──postMessage {answer, field, value}──▶  Portico SPA
                     ◀──postMessage {apply, field, value}───   │
                                                               │ HTTP (authenticated)
                                                               ▼
                                              GET/POST /d/{docId}/responses
                                                               │
                                                               ▼
                                          pk = resp#<project>#<itemId>
                                          sk = f#<fieldId>   one item per answered field
                                          sk = meta#state    { seq, updatedAt, lastActor }
                                          sk = p#<sub>       presence, short TTL
```

* **One item per answered field**, each carrying `{ value, version, actor, at }`. A write is conditional on the version the client last read. A mismatch is a 409 and the client shows both versions.
* **No projection, no dual write, no compaction, no 400 KB question.** One Query on the partition returns the whole response as readable JSON. That is the operator's report and it is also the state — there is no second copy to disagree.
* **Polling stays**, roughly 3 seconds, `?since=<seq>`, returning changed fields only. WebSockets are not in v1 and are not needed for a form.
* **No new npm dependency. **`client/app/package.json` declares its dependency set frozen for the programme, and this design does not touch it. That is a saving worth naming: adding `yjs` would have been a run-alone lockfile card before any of this could start.
* **The document changes, and it gets a real API rather than a storage shim.** It already had to change — no library can make a document re-render, and this one has no `storage` listener, no `visibilitychange`, no `focus`. Since it changes anyway, it emits per-field edits and applies per-field patches. The `localStorage` proxy was a disguise for that API.

### Why the bridge is not touched

`client/frame/portico-anchor-bridge.js` ships inside **every** frame artifact on five companies' portals. Putting a storage shim in it changes every published document, and it breaks two guards by name: `infra/test/sanitize_lib.test.ts:383` asserts the bridge source contains no `localStorage`, and `:389` caps it at 120 lines. The questionnaire is ours, so the questionnaire carries the code. The bridge stays a one-way bridge and its invariants stay proven.

### The injection-order trap, measured

The old card justified the shim on the bridge running before the document's script (char 804,857 vs 810,114). **The pipeline does not guarantee that. **`injectFrameScript` (`infra/lambda/ingest_lib.ts:1276`) inserts the bridge at `lastIndexOf('</body>')` — structurally last. In the artifact the pipeline actually emits, the document's script is at byte 1351 and the bridge at 3987 (`infra/test/fixtures/frame/app-artifact.html`): the bridge runs **after**. Whatever the live file shows, the ordering is incidental to that document's markup, not an invariant. Nothing in v1 depends on script order, which is the point.

## Constraints that do not move

Every child restates these. They are settled by measurement and are not open for redesign.

1. The frame is `sandbox="allow-scripts"` with **no** same-origin grant, mutation-proven by `client/app/src/features/viewer/sandbox-invariant.test.ts`.
2. `localStorage` in the frame throws — `client/app/e2e/app-frame.spec.ts` asserts `storage: "blocked"`. Downloads are blocked too.
3. The artifact CSP is `default-src 'none'; … connect-src 'none'; form-action 'none'` (`APP_CSP`, `infra/lambda/sanitize_lib.ts`). Widening `connect-src` is proven to exfiltrate. Do not.
4. `postMessage` is the only open channel and `parseFrameMessage` is its gate.
5. Response writes must not land in the `lib#<project>` partition and must not bump `meta#epoch`. Every epoch bump invalidates every warm Lambda container's cached library partition, and `CLAUDE.md` names that as the throughput trigger most likely to fire first.

## Sequencing risks found in the codebase

* **Only the operator's migration runner can re-render this document. **`--as-app` on `scripts/migrate-legacy-docs.ts` is the door; the upload Lambda cannot produce a `frame/app` at all today ([DRE-2381](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2381/the-upload-path-cannot-produce-a-frameapp-at-all-it-throws-drops-the) — it throws above `recordFailure`, drops the event, and leaves a stale `ready` row). So every document change needs an operator re-run, and [DRE-2381](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2381/the-upload-path-cannot-produce-a-frameapp-at-all-it-throws-drops-the) should land before anyone relies on the upload path.
* **The per-subject mutation rate limit is 30 tokens refilling at 1/second** (`MUTATION_RATE_CAPACITY`, `MUTATION_RATE_REFILL_PER_SEC` in `infra/lambda/idempotency_lib.ts`). Any debounce under one second drains the burst in 30 seconds and returns 429 mid-typing.
* **Every mutating route is wrapped by **`guardMutations`, which writes an `idem#<project>` row per write with a 24-hour TTL. Its own header assumes "a handful of rows per active moderator". An editing session at one write every three seconds is thousands.
* **PITR's 35-day window is the floor on deletion** (`docs/data-retention.md` §5.5). A "Clear" button that says the answers are gone is not true for 35 days. That belongs in the copy decision, not in a tooltip.

cards.title: Migration parents every new document to f-unfiled without checking it exists — the document lands invisible
cards.description:
**Hit live on gridcorr, 2026-08-11.** `migrate-legacy-docs.ts` assigns `parentId: UNFILED_FOLDER_ID` (`f-unfiled`) to every `create` target, without checking that folder exists in the project. gridcorr has exactly one folder — `f1786402752937-9pk9jf` ("Oncor Electric Delivery") — and no `f-unfiled`.

Result: the document was written with

```
parentId  f-unfiled
path      root/f-unfiled/d-readiness
```

…a parent pointer to a folder that does not exist. The row is present and `ingestState: ready`, the artifact is correct, the document is **reachable by direct URL** — and it appears on **no screen**. The library showed `1 folder · 0 documents` and the operator's own folder showed `0 docs`.

**The run printed** `✓ readiness.html → /l/d/d-readiness` **and exited 0.** Same failure shape as everything else in this class: a step that cannot fail visibly. The operator found it by looking at the screen, which is the only place it showed.

**This will hit every remaining portal cutover.** everybite has an `f-unfiled` folder, which is the only reason eleven documents landed correctly there. **vericorr, deltasolve, summit-midstream, drafts and board have not been through this** — and a fresh or UI-managed portal has no reason to own a folder named by a seed-era constant.

## Scope

1. **Refuse to write an orphan.** Before a `create` target's row is written, assert its `parentId` resolves to an existing folder row in that project. If it does not, do one of — and decide which, in a comment:
   * **create the Unfiled folder** as part of the run (it is a library-shaped default, and the planner already assumes it), or
   * **refuse the document** with a message naming the missing folder and the project.
     Creating it is probably right, since "Unfiled" is where the planner intends things to go and an operator can then move them. Whichever is chosen, silence is not an option.
2. **Make the dry run say where each document will land.** The plan currently prints the artifact and stub keys but not the parent. An operator reading `create readiness.html → d-readiness` cannot tell it is about to become invisible.
3. **Sweep for existing orphans across all projects.** Any `doc#` row whose `parentId` names a folder with no row. Report them; do not silently re-parent — where a document belongs is an operator decision.
4. **The generalisable guard:** a document that is `ingestState: ready` and reachable by URL but present on no screen is a state the system should not be able to represent. Consider asserting reachability in `verify-portal.md`'s checks, which is where a whole-portal invariant belongs.

## Acceptance

* A `create` into a project with no `f-unfiled` either creates the folder or refuses — never writes an orphan.
* The dry run names the destination folder for every `create`.
* An orphan sweep runs clean across all seven projects, or reports what it found.
* Pinned by a test, mutation-proven: remove the guard and a project without `f-unfiled` produces an orphan again.

Immediate live state: `d-readiness` on gridcorr was re-parented by hand into `f1786402752937-9pk9jf` with its `path` and `depth` corrected, and the epoch bumped. That is a patch, not the fix.

cards.title: Neither the fix-agent nor the critic can read Linear, so "deferred to a card" can never be verified
cards.description:
**Any PR that defers scope to a follow-up card cannot be approved without a human, and the pipeline has no way to notice.** Hit on `dreadnought-foundry/portico` PR #239, which sat blocked for hours with every code-level finding resolved.

**The sequence**

1. The QA critic asked for deferred scope to be carried by a real Linear card rather than PR-body prose — correct, since `linear-sync` moves the card to Done on merge and a prose deferral evaporates.
2. The card ([DRE-2375](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2375/a-content-publish-should-refuse-a-destination-that-holds-a-redirect)) *was* created — by the assistant session driving the work, which has Linear access.
3. The fix-agent then asserted the card existed. The critic checked and found that **the fix-agent step in** `agent-fix.yml` **never receives** `LINEAR_API_KEY` — only the heartbeat/park wrapper steps do. It reasoned that an agent with no Linear access could not have created, read, or learned that identifier, and therefore treated `DRE-2375` as *"unverified and likely invented."*
4. **The critic environment's** `LINEAR_API_KEY` **is also empty**, so it could not check either. It blocked, correctly, on the possibility that a data-loss guard was about to leave the tracker.
5. The fix-agent then looped: three `Fix attempt N blocked` messages, holding for an operator answer. An operator confirmation posted as a **PR comment did not clear it** — the critic requires the confirmation in the **PR body**.

**The critic's inference was sound and its block was right.** The defect is not judgement, it is visibility: **nothing inside the loop can corroborate a card's existence**, so this recurs on every PR that defers anything. And a phantom card is a real risk — the reasoning that produced the suspicion is the reasoning we want.

**Scope**

1. **Give the critic read access to Linear** — the narrowest thing that fixes it. A card-existence check (id resolves, title, state) is enough; it does not need write access. Then "deferred to DRE-nnnn" becomes verifiable instead of a matter of trust.
2. **Decide deliberately whether the fix-agent gets it too.** A fix-agent that can *create* the follow-up card closes the loop without a human — but it can also invent scope and file it, which is worse than the current failure. Read-only for the critic plus human-creates is the conservative split; say which and why in the workflow comment.
3. **Make the park path actually fire.** The fix-agent documented the right escape hatch — write the blocker to `/tmp/fix-blocker.txt` to move the card into the needs-human lane — and never took it, re-attempting instead. After **one** blocked attempt on a human-answerable question, park; do not retry twice more.
4. **Surface "waiting on a human" distinctly from "working".** On the operator dashboard, #239 read as *"Checks failing — fix agent not engaged"*, which is neither true nor actionable. A held PR needs its own state and its own question, or it sits invisibly. This is the highest-value item for the operator even if 1 and 2 are deferred.
5. **State where a confirmation must go.** The critic reads the PR body, not comments. Whatever the human is asked to do, the request should name the exact place — otherwise the answer lands where nothing reads it, which is what happened here.

**Acceptance**

* A PR deferring scope to an existing card can reach APPROVE with no human step.
* A PR deferring to a **non-existent** card still blocks — verify by pointing one at a fabricated id and confirming it fails.
* One blocked attempt on a human-answerable question parks the card rather than retrying.
* The dashboard distinguishes "held, needs an answer" from "checks failing".

Found 2026-08-10. Related: the same PR's critic verdict is a good worked example of the reasoning to preserve — it deduced the missing credential from the workflow file rather than assuming good faith.

cards.title: Render PDFs inline with PDF.js, without weakening the sandbox
cards.description:
Operator, 2026-08-10: *"can you render the PDF document inside the app/frame?"*

Today a PDF gets a download card with **Open** and **Download**, and is never framed. This card is about showing it inline — and the whole difficulty is doing that without touching the isolation boundary.

## Why the obvious approach is closed

**Chrome will not render a PDF inside** `sandbox="allow-scripts"`**.** Proven in real Chrome (`client/app/e2e/pdf-file-pane-chrome.spec.ts`, [DRE-2349](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2349/pdfs-cannot-render-in-the-sandboxed-frame-chrome-blocks-its-viewer)): framed, the navigation fails and commits `chrome-error://chromewebdata` — Chrome's "page has been blocked" document. The **same URL at top level** gets Chrome's PDF viewer and paints. That contrast is the test's point; it runs against real Chrome rather than headless Chromium because headless ships no PDF plugin and cannot distinguish "blocked" from "nothing here can render a PDF at all."

**Adding** `allow-same-origin` **is not an option and must not be proposed by this card.** It would make Chrome's viewer work and simultaneously dissolve the document-isolation boundary — the frame leaves its opaque origin, gains the session, gains same-origin reads. The pair is mutation-proven and guarded by a source check in `sandbox-invariant.test.ts`, whose comment names this exact pressure: it comes back *"just for PDFs."* If this card's implementation ever finds itself wanting that grant, the answer is to stop and re-scope.

## The approach that works

**PDF.js.** It decodes the bytes in JavaScript and paints to a `<canvas>` — no plugin, no navigation, no same-origin. It works inside the sandbox exactly as it stands, which is why every inline PDF preview on the web is built this way.

## What makes this size:L rather than an afternoon

1. **The CSP is the hard part, and it is the part to get right slowly.** The artifact CSP is `default-src 'none'`. PDF.js conventionally wants a worker and `blob:` URLs, so this needs deliberate widening — and widening that CSP is precisely what the [DRE-2364](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2364/frameapp-gate-on-the-moderator-role-and-give-the-migration-runner-a) mutation test proves is dangerous (`connect-src https:` and the document's whole dataset walks out in a URL). Scope any addition to the narrowest directive that works, and **add a mutation test for each new directive** showing what it does and does not permit. If PDF.js can be configured worker-less or same-document, prefer that over widening anything.
2. **Bundle cost.** ~350 KB gzipped against a current bundle of 149 KB. It must load **only when a PDF is opened** — a dynamic import, not a static one. The CI bundle-budget job (250 KB gzipped initial JS) is the gate; do not raise it.
3. **Fidelity is good but not identical** to Chrome's native viewer: text selection, form fields, annotations and print all behave differently. Decide and write down what is in scope — page render and scroll is a reasonable first cut; forms are not.
4. **Open and Download must keep working unchanged.** Inline preview is an addition, never a replacement — a reader on a slow connection, or one who wants the file, still needs both. The `FilePane` source guard forbidding `<iframe`/`sandbox=` stays.

## Acceptance

* A PDF renders inline in the viewer, executed-proven in **real Chrome** (extend the existing chrome spec — note its recorded trap: Chrome's native `<embed>` lives in the extension's shadow DOM, so naive `querySelector` returns null with the PDF plainly on screen).
* `sandbox` is still exactly `allow-scripts`, asserted, and the source guard is untouched.
* Every CSP directive added is justified in a comment and pinned by a mutation test.
* Initial JS is still under the 250 KB gzipped budget; PDF.js loads on demand only.
* Open and Download behave exactly as they do today.

**Not in scope:** annotations, form filling, printing, text search. Name them as follow-ups if wanted.

cards.title: MenuCalc serves soft-deleted ingredients into live recipes
cards.description:
**Repo:** atlas

MenuCalc lets an ingredient be soft-deleted while recipes keep pointing at it — and nothing stops a deleted ingredient being added to a **new** recipe. The allergen flags on a deleted record stop being maintained, but recipes keep consuming them.

## Blast radius, measured against production

|  |  |
| -- | -- |
| soft-deleted ingredients attached to live recipes | **542** |
| live recipes consuming them | **2,656** |
| accounts affected | **95** |

Our three pilot brands: Honeygrow **10 ingredients on 37 live recipes**, Bareburger **1 on 1**, Urbane Cafe none.

## This is the root cause of the Candied Pecans safety finding

Honeygrow, MenuCalc account 73 — there are two records:

| id | name | deleted | Tree Nut | live recipes using it |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `97573` | `Candied Pecans (v)` | **2024-02-29** | **false** | **36** |
| `300724` | `Candied Pecans` | live | **true** | **0** |

The correct record exists, is live, has the right flag — and is attached to nothing. The deleted record has the wrong flag and is on 36 recipes. **EveryBite serves** `97573` (`ids.everybite: OTc1NzM=` in the Honeygrow allergen catalog), which is why the pipeline publishes `Candied Pecans (v)` as `free_from` with an empty allergen list.

So this is not bad data someone entered. It is a right answer nobody was updating, on a record nobody thought was in use.

## What to build

**1. Stop the bleeding.** MenuCalc must not serve a soft-deleted ingredient, and must not accept one into a recipe. A delete that leaves the record consumable is not a delete.

**2. Make the pipeline refuse to inherit from one.** Atlas should not read allergen flags off a deleted ingredient — it should treat it as `unknown` and raise a finding, rather than publishing stale flags as fact.

**3. Remediate per restaurant, as part of onboarding.** For every deleted ingredient still in use, either repoint the recipe at the live replacement or deliberately resurrect the record. This is onboarding work, not a migration — each one needs a person who knows the menu.

## Acceptance

* A soft-deleted ingredient cannot be attached to a recipe, and is not served by the API.
* Atlas raises a finding rather than reading flags from a deleted record, with a revert-red test (repo convention — see `test_exchange_states.py`).
* Honeygrow's `Candied Pecans` resolves to `300724` and publishes `contains: [TREE_NUT]`.
* A per-account report of remaining deleted-but-in-use ingredients exists, so onboarding can work through it.

## Evidence

* `docs/research/ingestion-samples/menucalc-deleted-ingredients-in-live-recipes-2026-08-10.csv` — 254 rows, 62 deleted ingredients, 194 recipes, 22 accounts. The most-reused: `Tortilla (11" white)` 32 recipes, `Candied Pecans (v)` 31, `Crispy Onions (v)` 15, `Freshly Made Egg White Noodles` 15. Deletions span 2020-01-14 to 2026-08-07, so this is not a one-off migration artifact.
* Fleet counts above re-derived live from `service=menucalc` (read-only).
* Tracked on the Honeygrow and Bareburger checklists at `share.everybite.com/allergen-catalog-analysis` as a SAFETY row.

## Related

* [DRE-2348](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2348/extend-name-implies-undeclared-to-the-modifier-catalog) — extend `name_implies_undeclared` to modifiers. That card was written when we believed the pecan record was simply wrong at the source; it is still worth doing as a detector, but this card is the actual cause and should land first.

cards.title: Running Playwright on macOS turns the infra suite red — the platform guard reads the disk, not git
cards.description:
`npx playwright test` on a macOS machine writes the missing darwin snapshots (`specimen-light-chromium-darwin.png`, `specimen-dark-chromium-darwin.png`). `visual_gate_ci.test.ts`'s guard — *"one platform is maintained: linux baselines only, no stale second set"* — then fails, because it reads the **snapshot directory** rather than **git**.

The files are gitignored and can never be committed. The guard is protecting against a stale baseline entering the repo; a local, ignored, regenerable artifact is not that. So the guard fires on the one case it does not care about, and it fires on the machine of whoever is doing the most careful work — the person who just ran the browser suite.

**Observed twice on 2026-08-10**, by two different agents, each losing time to a red suite with no real defect behind it. Both fixed it by deleting the PNGs, which is the right action and an entirely undiscoverable one.

**Scope**

1. Make the guard ask git, not the filesystem: fail on a **tracked** non-linux baseline, ignore an untracked/ignored one. `git ls-files` is the honest source for "is this in the repo".
2. Keep the guard's teeth. It must still fail when a darwin baseline is actually committed — prove that by mutation: `git add -f` one, watch it go red, remove it.
3. If the ignore rule for these artifacts is missing or partial, complete it, so the local file is unambiguously ignored rather than merely untracked.
4. One line in the failure message telling the reader what to do (`rm` the local artifacts) would have saved both agents the detective work. A guard that fires on a benign local condition and does not say so is a papercut that recurs forever.

**Acceptance**

* Running the browser suite locally on macOS leaves `npm test` in `infra` green.
* A committed darwin baseline still fails the guard, demonstrated by mutation.

Found 2026-08-10 by the local-dev-environment agent, and independently hit while verifying the [DRE-2370](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2370/publishts-cannot-ship-the-spa-alone-after-cutover-every-publish-would) publish change.

cards.title: Decide: may a frame/app document open the reader's comments rail?
cards.description:
**An operator decision, not a bug report.** The behaviour is pinned by a test on #234 and is safe to ship either way; this card asks whether to keep it.

**What was found.** A `frame/app` document — one whose own scripts we deliberately keep — can **open the reader's comments rail** with an anchor string of its choosing. Measured in a real browser, not reasoned about: 0 rail hosts mounted before the message, 1 (`data-rail-tier="regular"`) after.

**Why it is possible.** `ViewerShell.tsx:157-163`'s `onAnchorClick` sets the active anchor and calls `setRailOpen(true)` — that *is* the interaction the rail exists for. Nothing can distinguish a bridge-originated `anchor-click` from a document-script-originated one: same window, same `portico: 1` marker, same shape. For `frame/app` the bridge script is embedded in the document's **own artifact**, so the document's scripts can read the marker straight out of it. Assuming an attacker forgets the marker is not a containment argument — the existing fixture omitted it, which is why this went unnoticed.

**Why it was invisible until now.** The assertion covering it read `[data-rail="comments"]`, a selector nothing in the app can render (`RailHost` emits `data-rail={"log"|"viewer"}` and only in the compact tier). It passed unconditionally and would have stayed green while the rail opened on every hostile message.

**What it is bounded by**, asserted in `client/app/e2e/app-frame.spec.ts`:

* the route never moves — a document cannot steer the reader anywhere
* the attacker's string is never rendered, as markup or as text
* no error reaches the shell
* every other containment is unchanged: `connect-src 'none'`, opaque origin, no parent DOM, no storage

So the capability is **UI control, not data access**. The worst case today is a document that pops the reader's own comment rail open on the document they are already reading — a nuisance, and one only a moderator-published document can perform at all, since `frame/app` is moderator-gated.

**The two options**

1. **Accept it.** It is the same channel the anchor bridge legitimately needs, and closing it costs anchoring inside app documents. Record the acceptance in `AMENDMENTS.md` beside A-7 so the next reader finds a decision rather than an oversight. **This is the cheaper option and probably the right one.**
2. **Close it for** `frame/app` **only.** Have `FramePane` ignore `anchor-click` when the document's sub-kind is `app`, keeping it for `frame/portico` and `frame/foreign` where we strip the document's scripts and only our bridge can post. Worth checking first whether paragraph-level anchoring means anything in a document that renders its content dynamically — if it does not, this costs nothing real.

Either way the pinned test on #234 must be updated to match the decision, and it must keep failing if the behaviour changes by accident.

Found while closing the QA critic's finding 2 on #234, 2026-08-10. Related: [DRE-2364](<https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2364>).

cards.title: Measure the app-shell threshold band against the real corpus — the two detectors overlap without nesting
cards.description:
**Corrected 2026-08-11 after** [DRE-2380](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2380/a-moderator-must-be-able-to-declare-a-document-interactive-detection) **measured this properly. The original framing of this card was wrong in two ways, both recorded below so nobody chases them again.**

`renderArtifact` carried two detectors for the same class of document. [DRE-2380](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2380/a-moderator-must-be-able-to-declare-a-document-interactive-detection) folded them into **one call site** (`scriptDrivenVerdict`), behaviour-identical. What remains — and all that remains — is the threshold question, which needs a measurement rather than a judgement.

## What the original card got wrong

1. **"A document between them gets whichever** `if` **was written first" — no behavioural coin flip existed.** Both branches returned identical results (`ok:false`, `fallback:'file'`, `reason:'script-driven'`). The order decided only which *error message* printed.
2. **The worked example ("8 KB of script and 300 characters of text") matches neither detector.** [DRE-2350](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2350/a-javascript-rendered-document-sanitizes-to-a-blank-page-detect-it-and)'s ceiling is 200 **non-whitespace** characters, and 300 characters of prose is ~290 non-whitespace. That document renders as a static frame, and always did.

## The real hole, measured

The two bands **overlap without nesting**, so no single threshold pair covers both purposes:

* Collapse to [DRE-2355](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2355/interactive-documents-need-a-third-frame-kind-that-keeps-their-scripts)'s pair (64 KB / 500 chars) and the `(≥64 KB, 200–499 chars)` corner stops being refused — that is [DRE-2350](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2350/a-javascript-rendered-document-sanitizes-to-a-blank-page-detect-it-and)'s blank page returning, which [DRE-2350](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2350/a-javascript-rendered-document-sanitizes-to-a-blank-page-detect-it-and) explicitly forbids.
* Collapse to [DRE-2350](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2350/a-javascript-rendered-document-sanitizes-to-a-blank-page-detect-it-and)'s pair (1 KB / 200 non-whitespace) and short real documents start being refused.

[DRE-2380](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2380/a-moderator-must-be-able-to-declare-a-document-interactive-detection) pinned this corner with a test rather than guessing at it.

## Scope — a measurement, not a redesign

1. **Measure the real corpus.** The eleven everybite legacy documents, the Allergen Catalog (43 chars of static text), the Oncor intake questionnaire (~204,000 chars by `trim().length`, ~169,000 non-whitespace, 42,518 script bytes), gridcorr's `readiness.html`, and anything on the other portals. Report script bytes and static text for each, both measures.
2. **Pick one pair on that evidence**, or state with evidence that one pair cannot serve both purposes and the two must stay distinct with the reason written down.
3. **Decide the counting rule once** — `trim().length` or non-whitespace — and use it in both places. The two detectors currently disagree on this, which is how the original example came to be wrong.
4. Keep the refusal path intact: no threshold change may let a document that would have been honestly refused render blank instead.

## Now much less urgent

[DRE-2380](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2380/a-moderator-must-be-able-to-declare-a-document-interactive-detection) shipped the explicit `--as-app` declaration, so a moderator no longer depends on the heuristic being right for the document in front of them. The thresholds now only decide the *undeclared* default, which is the conservative direction. Do this when someone has the corpus numbers, not before.

**Do not start this without the measurement.** Guessing a threshold is what produced both errors above.

cards.title: Extend name_implies_undeclared to the modifier catalog
cards.description:
**Repo:** atlas

> **Update 2026-08-10 — read this before starting.** The root cause of the Candied Pecans case has been found and it is **not** a wrong record in EveryBite. MenuCalc holds the correct record (`300724`, Tree Nut = true, attached to no recipes) alongside a **soft-deleted** one (`97573`, Tree Nut = false, deleted 2024-02-29, still attached to 36 live recipes) — and `97573` is the one EveryBite serves. See [DRE-2373](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2373/menucalc-serves-soft-deleted-ingredients-into-live-recipes), which should land first. Correcting the record in EveryBite would paper over the real defect.
>
> This card is still worth doing, but as the **detector**, not the fix. It is the reason all three cases below were found by a person reading data rather than by the pipeline.

The only mechanical detector for "this name suggests an allergen the record does not declare" runs on **dishes only**. Every case we have found so far is a **modifier**.

## What is shipping right now

| brand | record | ships as | the problem |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| Honeygrow | `Candied Pecans (v)` | `free_from`, `allergens: []` | pecans are a tree nut — cause found, [DRE-2373](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2373/menucalc-serves-soft-deleted-ingredients-into-live-recipes) |
| Bareburger | `korean fried chicken wings` | `free_from`, `allergens: []` | battered and sauced — WHEAT, SOY, SESAME all plausible |
| Urbane Cafe | `Garlic Red Pepper Hummus` | `free_from`, `allergens: []` | hummus is made with tahini — SESAME |

`catalog_base.py` sets `free_from` whenever an ingredient record exists and no allergen flag is set, so `free_from` means "the flags were empty" — and the exchange then publishes that to DoorDash as a positive declaration.

## Why it matters beyond the three

The detector is what makes the difference between a page that says **"A diner could be told something wrong today"** and one that says **"Everything still open"**. Honeygrow's Issues page shows the former only because a human happened to spot Candied Pecans. Bareburger's and Urbane Cafe's showed the latter over the identical condition until the same human looked again.

## What to build

Run the existing `name_implies_undeclared` check over `catalog.modifiers` as well as `catalog.dishes`, and raise a SAFETY row per brand when a modifier's name implies an allergen its record does not declare.

Two constraints that are not negotiable:

* **The check flags, it never infers.** It must not add an allergen to any record or change any published state. Deriving a safety claim from a product name is the failure this pipeline exists to prevent — the output is a finding for a human, nothing else.
* **A finding is a SAFETY row on the owning brand's checklist.** Ownership is EveryBite's, but the *fix* may be upstream of us — as [DRE-2373](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2373/menucalc-serves-soft-deleted-ingredients-into-live-recipes) shows, "correct the record" is sometimes the wrong instruction.

## Acceptance

* The three records above are detected on a clean run, on their own brands.
* A test goes red if the check stops covering modifiers — the repo convention is a revert-red probe (see `test_exchange_states.py`, which mutation-tests the free-from rule three ways).
* No published `state` changes as a result of the check firing.

## Context

* Found during the 2026-08-09 review of `share.everybite.com/allergen-catalog-analysis`; three adversarial passes plus the QA critic gate, 35 confirmed defects.
* Tracked as SAFETY rows on each restaurant's checklist: `H-EB-aa87`, `B-EB-b559`, `UC-EB-d943`.
* Detector today: `validate_live.py`, `name_implies_undeclared` (11/12/3 dish rows on the three brands).
* Related shipped work: PR #140 — a free-from claim now needs a clean record AND a sound binding.

cards.title: The pipeline builds cards that are already Done — a slow agent-task run opens a duplicate PR nobody can merge
cards.description:
A dispatched `agent-task` run never re-checks the card before opening its PR. If the card is delivered by any other route while the run is in flight, the agent still finishes and opens a second PR for work that already shipped. The result is an unmergeable orphan that looks exactly like a stuck PR on the board.

Four of these on 2026-08-09/10, all in portico. Each cost the operator a diagnosis.

## The pattern

| Card | Shipped by | Merged | Duplicate | Opened | Gap |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| [DRE-2331](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2331/the-grant-role-dropdown-is-a-full-width-horizontal-strip-not-a-menu) | #206 | 23:43:56 | #207 | 23:35:07 | opened before |
| [DRE-2334](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2334/app-bar-the-portal-name-still-renders-twice-at-root-the-crumb-sits-off) | #212 | 01:33:52 | #219 | 02:03:50 | **30 min after Done** |
| [DRE-2333](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2333/the-library-root-is-called-portico-in-some-surfaces-and-the-portal) | #210 | 01:44:56 | #222 | 02:30:55 | **46 min after Done** |

Every merged PR is authored by `smeed652` — a local agent, which commits as the operator ([DRE-2291](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2291/local-sub-agents-commit-as-the-operator-so-their-prs-leave-the-merge)). Every duplicate is authored by `agent-bureau-bot[bot]` — the pipeline. So the two producers are working the same cards and neither knows about the other.

[DRE-2333](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2333/the-library-root-is-called-portico-in-some-surfaces-and-the-portal) is the clearest case. The card went Todo at 00:55:33, so the relay dispatched immediately. A local agent opened #210 at 01:22 and it merged at 01:44:56; the card went **Done** at 01:45:09. The pipeline's run — slowed by the `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` outage, dying and retrying throughout — finally opened #222 at **02:30:55**, three quarters of an hour after its card was closed.

`agent-task.yml` checked the card once, at dispatch. Nothing looked again.

## Why it is worse than wasted work

The duplicate is **indistinguishable from a genuinely stuck PR**. #219 and #222 both rendered as *"Checks failing — fix agent not engaged"* and #207 as *"Approved — blocked by conflict / failing check"* — badges that send a human looking for a fix agent or a conflict to resolve. There is nothing to fix. The only correct action is to close, and nothing on the board says so.

The fix loop compounds it: #222 burned three `agent-fix` runs against a card that was already delivered.

`#210` and `#222` even share a branch name (`agent/DRE-2333-root-is-the-portal`) — the pipeline recreated a branch the merge had deleted, which is its own signal that nothing checked.

## Approach

1. **Re-check the card immediately before opening the PR.** If its state is Done/Cancelled, or it already carries a merged PR attachment, stop and post why instead of opening one. This is the smallest fix and closes the 30–46 minute window.
2. **Re-check before starting the build too.** A run that sits queued behind an outage should not begin work on a completed card at all. Cheaper than discovering it at the end.
3. **Treat an existing branch as a signal.** If the target branch name already exists or was recently deleted on a merged PR, that is evidence the card was built — refuse rather than force a new one.
4. **Make the orphan self-declaring.** If a duplicate is opened anyway, it must close itself, or label itself so the board can say "duplicate — close it" rather than "checks failing." Pairs with [DRE-2345](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2345/the-board-re-derives-a-prs-status-from-raw-github-state-and-discards).
5. **Look at the dispatch race itself.** Two producers building one card is the root condition. Worth deciding whether a card being worked locally should be marked so the relay skips it — but that is a design question, and items 1–3 stop the damage without answering it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An agent-task run whose card is Done when the build completes does NOT open a PR; it stops and records the reason. A test drives the [DRE-2333](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2333/the-library-root-is-called-portico-in-some-surfaces-and-the-portal) timeline (card Done at 01:45, run finishing 02:30) and asserts no PR is opened.
- [ ] A run whose card is already Done when it starts exits before doing any work.
- [ ] A card that already has a merged PR attachment never gets a second PR.
- [ ] If a duplicate is opened despite the above, it is identifiable as a duplicate without reading the PR — closed automatically or labelled so the console can say "close it".
- [ ] No regression on the ordinary path: a card in Todo/In Progress with no merged PR builds and opens exactly as it does today, pinned by a test.

cards.title: The board re-derives a PR's status from raw GitHub state and discards the reason the pipeline already wrote down
cards.description:
The console's waiting reason is computed from three GitHub facts — the critic verdict, the check counts, and `merge_state_status`. Situations that share those three facts but need opposite responses from the operator collapse onto one badge. Meanwhile the pipeline has usually already written the true reason in plain English on the PR, and the board never reads it.

The board is **not stale** — this was checked live on 2026-08-09, and every open PR it showed matched GitHub at that moment. The failure is vocabulary, not freshness, and the fix is different: carry the reason forward rather than re-derive it.

## The code

`console/backend/enrich.py:352`, `derive_waiting_reason(pr)`:

```python
verdict = str(pr.get("critic_verdict") or "").upper()
dirty   = str(pr.get("merge_state_status") or "").upper() == "DIRTY"
failing = int(pr.get("checks_failed") or 0) > 0
...
if verdict == "APPROVE" and (dirty or failing):
    return APPROVED_BLOCKED
```

`console/backend/inflight.py:290` renders it:

```python
_PR_REASON_OVERRIDES = {
    "FIX_STALLED":      "Checks failing — fix agent not engaged",
    "APPROVED_BLOCKED": "Approved — blocked by conflict / failing check",
    ...
}
```

Both are honest about what they can see. Neither has any input carrying *why*.

## Two live misreads, same night

**PR #207 — read "Approved — blocked by conflict / failing check."** It was a **duplicate build** of [DRE-2331](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2331/the-grant-role-dropdown-is-a-full-width-horizontal-strip-not-a-menu). The card had already shipped via #206 (merged 23:43:56) and gone Done at 23:44. No conflict resolution could ever land it; the only correct action was to close it. The badge sent the operator looking for a merge conflict to fix.

The pipeline already knew. Its own fix agent posted on the PR:

> Fix attempt 1 blocked: PR #207 is not a resolvable merge conflict — it is a duplicate build of the same card.

That sentence is the answer. It sits on the PR and never reaches the board.

**PR #194 — read "Checks failing — fix agent not engaged."** The fix agent had engaged three times, including a fresh-eyes re-derivation, and then deliberately stopped:

> Fix budget exhausted (3 attempts, including a fresh-eyes re-derivation) — holding for a human decision.

"Not engaged" reads as a pipeline failure the operator should chase. The truth is the opposite: the pipeline finished its work and is waiting on a decision. That is the single most important state on the board and it is labelled as neglect.

Both PRs were also indistinguishable from three others on the same board that were healthy and moving — #214, #215 and #217 were minutes old and mid-repair. The operator could not tell "working" from "waiting on you" from "will never merge" without reading every PR by hand.

## Why this is not [DRE-2307](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2307/every-fix-loop-blocker-escalates-to-the-card-as-a-reviewer-dispute)

[DRE-2307](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2307/every-fix-loop-blocker-escalates-to-the-card-as-a-reviewer-dispute) is the same disease in `agent-fix.yml`: the true blocker text goes to the PR and a hardcoded sentence goes to the Linear card. This card is the console re-deriving status from raw state instead of reading what the agent concluded. Fixing [DRE-2307](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2307/every-fix-loop-blocker-escalates-to-the-card-as-a-reviewer-dispute) improves the Linear card comment; the board still computes its own badge from three fields. Both need doing.

## Approach

1. **Read the pipeline's own words.** The fix agent's blocker text, the budget-exhausted notice, and the duplicate finding are already on the PR as worker-bot comments. Ingest the latest one and let it drive the badge instead of the derived triple. Trusted authors only — same identity discipline as `is_worker_bot_comment` ([DRE-1995](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-1995/agent-fix-authenticate-the-bookkeeping-comment-reads-fixconflict)).
2. **Add the states the operator actually acts on.** At minimum: `DUPLICATE_BUILD` (close it), `BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` (decide), and `HELD_AWAITING_ANSWER` (already asked, still waiting). Each must be visually distinct from the healthy repair badges.
3. **Separate "the loop is working" from "the loop stopped."** Today both live in the fix-loop panel. A card the pipeline has given up on must not sit in a group headed "self-healing."
4. **Never say "not engaged" when the agent ran.** If attempts were made, the badge states the count and the outcome. A test asserts that a PR with a fix-attempt history can never render `FIX_STALLED`.
5. **Keep the derivation as the fallback.** When no pipeline reason exists, today's triple is still the right answer. This adds a higher-priority source, it does not replace the cascade.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A PR whose newest worker-bot comment states a blocker renders that reason on the board, not the derived one; a test drives the #207 duplicate text and asserts the badge is the duplicate state.
- [ ] A budget-exhausted PR renders a state meaning "the pipeline is done and is waiting for you," distinct from every in-repair badge. Test with the #194 text.
- [ ] A PR with one or more recorded fix attempts never renders "fix agent not engaged."
- [ ] Cards the pipeline has stopped working on are not counted or grouped as self-healing.
- [ ] Only trusted worker-bot comment authors can drive a badge; a planted comment from any other author is ignored, with a test.
- [ ] With no pipeline reason present, `derive_waiting_reason` behaves exactly as it does today — the existing suite passes unchanged.

cards.title: Branch protection: 3 of 7 repos have none, and the setting that makes author ≠ merger real is off on all 7
cards.description:
Three of the seven repos in the routing map have no branch protection at all, and the one setting that would make "author ≠ merger" enforced by GitHub rather than by our own workflow code is switched off on all seven. Everything here is an operator settings change — no code.

The headline number: on `agent-bureau`, `bureau-pipeline`, `portico` and `deltasolv`, 0 of the last 30 commits on `main` arrived without a pull request. On `atlas` it was 7 of 30, and on `vericorr` it was 30 of 30. Protection is doing real work where it exists.

## What is protected today

Read live 2026-08-09 via `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/branches/main/protection`, `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/rulesets`, and GraphQL `branchProtectionRules`. No repo uses rulesets — every guard is classic protection on the single pattern `main`. Org rulesets are empty on dreadnought-foundry and DeltaSolv.

| Repo | Org plan / visibility | Guard | Direct push to `main` | Force-push | Delete `main` | Required checks | Up-to-date | Approvals | `enforce_admins` | `dismiss_stale_reviews` |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| EveryBite/atlas | Free / private | **none possible** | allowed | allowed | allowed | — | — | — | — | — |
| dreadnought-foundry/vericorr | Team / private | **none** | allowed | allowed | allowed | — | — | — | — | — |
| dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau-demo | Team / private | **none** | allowed | allowed | allowed | — | — | — | — | — |
| DeltaSolv/deltasolv | Team / private | classic | blocked | blocked | blocked | none active | inert flag | **0** | off | false |
| dreadnought-foundry/bureau-pipeline | Team / **public** | classic | blocked | blocked | blocked | none active | inert flag | **0** | off | false |
| dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau | Team / private | classic | blocked | blocked | blocked | active, **zero contexts** | off | **0** | on | true |
| dreadnought-foundry/portico | Team / private | classic | blocked | blocked | blocked | 6 contexts | off | **0** | on | true |

Everywhere: `restrictsPushes` false, `require_last_push_approval` false, `required_linear_history` false, `required_signatures` false, `block_creations` false, `lock_branch` false.

Three readings that need care, because the REST payload misleads:

* `atlas` **returns 403, not 404.** `"Upgrade to GitHub Pro or make this repository public to enable this feature"` on both the protection and the rulesets endpoints. EveryBite is on the Free plan and `atlas` is private, so branch protection is not available at any price we control. This is a plan limit, not neglect.
* `deltasolv` **and** `bureau-pipeline` **look like they require an up-to-date branch, and do not.** REST omits `required_status_checks` entirely when the context list is empty, so absence proves nothing on its own. GraphQL reports `requiresStrictStatusChecks: true` but `requiresStatusChecks: false` — the "require branches to be up to date" flag is stored with its parent rule switched off. It enforces nothing. This is the leftover of [DRE-1924](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-1924/prevent-red-main-require-a-pr-branch-up-to-date-with-main-green-before)'s operator half; the workflow half is what actually runs.
* `agent-bureau` **has required status checks turned on with an empty context list.** That is a no-op too.

So GitHub enforces branch currency on exactly zero repos. `merge_gate.py` condition 0 is the only thing that does, and that is the right place for it.

## Where the direct-push holes actually are

| Repo | Last 30 `main` commits with no associated PR | Who |
| -- | -- | -- |
| agent-bureau, bureau-pipeline, portico, deltasolv | 0 / 30 | — |
| EveryBite/atlas | **7 / 30** | all `smeed652`, 2026-07-30, deck and docs commits |
| dreadnought-foundry/vericorr | **30 / 30** | all `katicm` — last merged PR was 2026-06-12 |

Neither hole has been used by an agent. Both are reachable by one.

## What is load-bearing, and what is decoration

The safety model is: a bureau-bot pool App authors the PR, `agent-bureau-qa-bot` merges it, and `merge_gate.py` refuses to merge without a critic APPROVE bound to the reviewed commit. Branch protection's only job is to stop that being walked around.

**Load-bearing.** Blocking direct pushes, force-pushes and deletion of `main`. Without it the merge gate is advisory — anyone with write access can push past it and rewrite the history the audit trail depends on. Present on four repos, absent on three.

**Load-bearing and currently unclaimed.** `required_approving_review_count: 1`. It is 0 on all seven. `adr-github-app-bot-for-agent-prs.md:123` says the two-bot design exists precisely so that "`required_approving_review_count=1` can stay on" — that intent was never applied. Verified satisfiable: `sync_review_state.py` submits a formal `event=APPROVE` under the `BUREAU_QA_APP_ID` token (`qa-review.yml:108`, `:732`), PR authors are the four-App dispatch pool or `smeed652`, and GitHub refuses self-approval server-side. Every sampled merged PR on portico, agent-bureau, bureau-pipeline, deltasolv and atlas carries an `agent-bureau-qa-bot[bot]` APPROVED review. Turning this on converts author ≠ merger from a convention our own code enforces into a rule GitHub enforces.

**Load-bearing and free.** `enforce_admins`. `grep` over every bureau-pipeline workflow finds exactly one merge call — `gh pr merge "$PR" --merge --delete-branch --match-head-commit "$SHA"` at `merge-gate.yml:265`, as qa-bot, with no `--admin` flag. (`--admin` appears twice in the repo, both times in prose: a comment at `qa-review.yml:726` and a docstring at `sync_review_state.py:13`. Neither is a call.) The console's Merge button is the same shape (`console/backend/pr_merge.py:591`, plain `merge_method: merge`, "never admin/force"). Nothing in the pipeline needs admin bypass, and agent-bureau and portico have run with it on for months.

**Decoration, and in one case harmful.** `dismiss_stale_reviews`. It is on for agent-bureau and portico and it fires: portico PR #205 has a `review_dismissed` event at 2026-08-09T23:47:44Z, two seconds after the fix commit. It duplicates the [DRE-1990](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-1990/qa-review-merge-gate-bind-the-verdict-to-the-reviewed-commit-verdict) verdict-SHA binding at the wrong layer — the gate reads the verdict comment, not the GitHub review — and it does the duplication worse. Harmless today only because the approval count is 0.

## Required status checks are a trap here

The only check names common to all seven repos are `call / review`, `call / card-done` and `call / conflict-sweep`, and the useful-sounding one is a decoy: `call / review` reports that the critic **ran**, not what it decided. Measured on portico commit `8f621a6d` — the head that drew a `REQUEST_CHANGES` verdict — `QA critic review` is `failure` while `call / review` is `success`. Requiring `call / review` would look like a critic gate and be one only by accident.

`QA critic review` (`publish_review_check.py:82`) is the real head-bound, verdict-bearing check — but it landed on 2026-08-07 and appears on only four repos' recent PR heads (atlas, agent-bureau, bureau-pipeline, portico). Every product CI workflow is bespoke: portico's six contexts, `Lint · Typecheck · Unit` on atlas, `Python Tests (GH)` on vericorr, `Lint · Guards` on agent-bureau, `Typecheck · Test · Build` on agent-bureau-demo, `Lint · Type · Test · Build` on deltasolv. There is no fleet-wide check name worth requiring, and a required context that never posts blocks the PR forever with no alert.

Keep portico's six contexts — all six ran and passed on the head of PR #212. Add none anywhere else in this card.

## Interaction check against the live pipeline

* `reconcile.retrigger_dead_heads()` **cannot reach** `main`**.** It is not a force-push. `scripts/reconcile.py:1194-1231` creates an empty commit whose sole parent is the current tip, then `PATCH git/refs/heads/{headRefName}` with no `force` field, so GitHub defaults to `force=false` and the update is a fast-forward regardless. The loop skips any PR whose `headRefName` does not start with `agent/`. `grep` for `--force`, `--force-with-lease`, `push -f` and `force:true` across bureau-pipeline `scripts/` and `.github/` returns zero hits.
* `medic.yml` **writes nothing to git** — zero `git push` occurrences in the file. `agent-fix.yml:474` instructs the fix agent to push to the "SAME branch. Do NOT open a new PR. Do NOT force-push." `red-main-repair.yml:82` fires only when the failing branch *is* the default branch, and it responds by opening a normal PR from `repair/<failing-sha>` — it never writes to the default branch itself.
* `require_last_push_approval: true` **would deadlock the fleet.** The gate's own `PUT .../update-branch` at `merge-gate.yml:236` is authored by qa-bot, the identity that also holds the approval. Never enable it. It is false everywhere today.
* `dismiss_stale_reviews: true` **plus** `required_approving_review_count: 1` **re-creates the** [DRE-2340](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2340/merge-gate-livelock-every-branch-update-destroys-the-approve-it-just) **livelock at the GitHub layer, where content binding cannot reach it.** Each gate `update-branch` dismisses the formal approve; worse, once [DRE-2340](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2340/merge-gate-livelock-every-branch-update-destroys-the-approve-it-just) lands, `should_review_pr` deliberately skips the re-review on unchanged content, so nothing re-submits it. The order in the plan below is not cosmetic: `dismiss_stale_reviews` goes off **before** the approval count goes on.
* `required_linear_history` **and** `required_signatures` **would both break the gate outright** (merge commits by policy; Apps do not sign). Not proposed.
* **Merge queue is out of scope.** [DRE-2340](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2340/merge-gate-livelock-every-branch-update-destroys-the-approve-it-just) already evaluated and rejected it — unavailable for private repos below Enterprise Cloud, and `merge_group:` would need a per-repo trigger in all seven. Do not re-litigate it here.

## Where protection genuinely does not apply

* **EveryBite/atlas — cannot be protected, and it is not ours to fix.** Free plan, private repo, 403 on both APIs. The routes are EveryBite buying Team or the repo moving orgs; both are customer decisions about a customer's billing. The write surface is two admins (`smeed652`, `drmarjanovic`) plus the bureau Apps — six other org members are read-only. Note it, do not chase it.
* **dreadnought-foundry/vericorr — protect the branch, do not require PRs.** Every one of its last 30 `main` commits is a direct push by `katicm`, and its last merged PR was 2026-06-12. Requiring pull requests would stop an external collaborator's work overnight, and the VeriCorr branch arrangement is not ours to change unilaterally. Blocking force-push and deletion does not affect fast-forward pushes, so it costs him nothing.
* **agent-bureau-demo — dormant, but protect it anyway.** One PR ever, untouched since 2026-06-17. It is also the cheapest possible rehearsal of the exact payload.

## The ordered application sequence

Every step is **operator-only** — GitHub settings via `gh api`. There is no code in this card. Do them in this order; the risk climbs as you go, and each step is verified before the next.

**Step 1 — snapshot (no change).** For each of the four protected repos: `gh api repos/{o}/{r}/branches/main/protection > prot-{o}-{r}.json`. *Verify:* four non-empty files. *Rollback:* n/a — this is the rollback for everything else.

**Step 2 — agent-bureau-demo: add the baseline guard.** `gh api -X PUT repos/dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau-demo/branches/main/protection --input baseline.json` where `baseline.json` is:

```json
{
  "required_status_checks": null,
  "enforce_admins": true,
  "required_pull_request_reviews": {"required_approving_review_count": 0, "dismiss_stale_reviews": false},
  "restrictions": null,
  "allow_force_pushes": false,
  "allow_deletions": false
}
```

*Why first:* dormant repo, blast radius zero, and it proves the payload. *Verify:* `GET .../protection` returns the object. *Rollback:* `gh api -X DELETE repos/dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau-demo/branches/main/protection`.

**Step 3 — vericorr: force-push and deletion only.** Same PUT, but with `"required_pull_request_reviews": null` and `"enforce_admins": false`. *Why those two changes:* no PR requirement so Marko's direct pushes keep working; `enforce_admins: false` because `katicm` is a repo admin and binding him to a rule he has not agreed to is the same unilateral change. *Honest limitation:* with `enforce_admins: false` an admin can still force-push. This step stops an agent or a script, not an admin. Raising it to `true` is a conversation with Marko, not an operator action. *Verify:* his next push lands normally. *Rollback:* `gh api -X DELETE repos/dreadnought-foundry/vericorr/branches/main/protection`.

**Step 4 — deltasolv and bureau-pipeline: turn on** `enforce_admins`**.** `gh api -X POST repos/{o}/{r}/branches/main/protection/enforce_admins`, twice. *Why safe:* no merge call uses `--admin`; agent-bureau and portico have had it on for months. *Verify:* watch one agent PR merge to completion on each repo. *Rollback:* `gh api -X DELETE repos/{o}/{r}/branches/main/protection/enforce_admins` — one call, instant.

**Step 5 — portico and agent-bureau:** `dismiss_stale_reviews` **off.** `gh api -X PATCH repos/{o}/{r}/branches/main/protection/required_pull_request_reviews -F dismiss_stale_reviews=false`. Use PATCH on the sub-resource, never a whole-object PUT — a PUT would wipe portico's six required contexts. *Verify:* the next PR shows no `review_dismissed` event in `GET /issues/{n}/events` after a gate `update-branch`. *Rollback:* the same PATCH with `=true`.

**Step 6 — portico only:** `required_approving_review_count` **to 1.** `gh api -X PATCH repos/dreadnought-foundry/portico/branches/main/protection/required_pull_request_reviews -F required_approving_review_count=1`. *Why portico first:* highest PR volume (207 merged in 90 days) and the clearest evidence that qa-bot approves every PR. *Verify within the hour:* watch the next two agent PRs merge unattended. *Rollback:* the same PATCH with `=0`.

**Step 7 — soak 48 hours, then repeat steps 5 and 6 on agent-bureau and bureau-pipeline.** Same commands, same verification.

**Step 8 — deltasolv: check the dependabot path before enabling the approval count.** deltasolv PR #203 merged with **no approving review at all**. Under `required_approving_review_count: 1` that PR would have blocked. Find out why the critic did not approve it before touching this repo. Steps 5 and 6 for deltasolv are conditional on that answer.

**Step 9 — atlas: no change, one decision.** Report to the CEO that the reference production deployment cannot have branch protection while EveryBite is on the Free plan, and that seven of its last thirty `main` commits bypassed the PR flow. The decision is whether to ask EveryBite to upgrade. No operator action until that is answered.

## Break-glass

Applied wrongly, this stalls the fleet **silently**. Agent PRs reach `In Review` and stop; nothing alerts. Check within an hour of every change.

The symptom: `gh pr view {n} -R {o}/{r} --json mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision` returns `BLOCKED` with `REVIEW_REQUIRED`, or the merge-gate run log shows the `gh pr merge` call failing.

| What to undo | One command |
| -- | -- |
| Required approvals | `gh api -X PATCH repos/{o}/{r}/branches/main/protection/required_pull_request_reviews -F required_approving_review_count=0` |
| `enforce_admins` | `gh api -X DELETE repos/{o}/{r}/branches/main/protection/enforce_admins` |
| `dismiss_stale_reviews` | `gh api -X PATCH repos/{o}/{r}/branches/main/protection/required_pull_request_reviews -F dismiss_stale_reviews=true` |
| A newly protected repo (demo, vericorr) | `gh api -X DELETE repos/{o}/{r}/branches/main/protection` |
| Everything, one repo, now | `gh api -X DELETE repos/{o}/{r}/branches/main/protection`, then re-PUT the step-1 snapshot |

The precedent is in `adr-github-app-bot-for-agent-prs.md:17` — an `enforce_admins` disable, push, re-enable recovery. Line 192 marks that dance as emergency-only, which is still right.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every protected repo's current protection JSON is captured before any write
- [ ] `agent-bureau-demo` and `vericorr` block force-push and deletion of `main`
- [ ] `vericorr` does **not** require pull requests, and `katicm` pushes directly to `main` exactly as before
- [ ] `enforce_admins` is on for `deltasolv` and `bureau-pipeline`, and one agent PR has merged unattended on each afterwards
- [ ] `dismiss_stale_reviews` is off on every repo that has a non-zero approval requirement
- [ ] `required_approving_review_count` is 1 on portico, agent-bureau and bureau-pipeline, and two consecutive agent PRs have merged unattended on each
- [ ] No new required status check context is added to any repo; portico's six are unchanged
- [ ] `require_last_push_approval`, `required_linear_history` and `required_signatures` are false everywhere
- [ ] The deltasolv dependabot no-approval case (PR #203) is explained before deltasolv's approval count changes
- [ ] The atlas plan limit is written up for the CEO as a yes/no decision

## Notes

* Found while auditing, worth its own card: `bureau-pipeline/.github/workflows/model-drift.yml:197` runs `git push origin HEAD:main` under `contents: write`, on a `cron: "17 6 * * 1"` schedule. `gh run list --workflow model-drift.yml` is empty — it has never fired. bureau-pipeline requires a pull request before merging, so the push should be rejected and the job should fail every Monday. Branch protection is the only thing standing in front of it, which is the argument for this card in one line.
* `DRE-1924`'s workflow half is live and correct; its operator half ("require branches to be up to date") is not in force anywhere and should stay that way. GitHub's version of that rule is what [DRE-2340](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2340/merge-gate-livelock-every-branch-update-destroys-the-approve-it-just) is removing.
* `DRE-2340` is in progress and relaxes verdict invalidation. Nothing here should be applied in a way that re-tightens it at the GitHub layer.
* Every file, line number and check name in this card was read from `bureau-pipeline@main` and the live GitHub API on 2026-08-09.

cards.title: OPERATOR: request SES production access for the dreadnought account — OM5 cannot close without it
cards.description:
Found during the OM5 pre-flight, 2026-08-09 (`sesv2 get-account`, read-only, all three accounts):

| Account | Production access | 24h quota | Sent 24h |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `everybite` (865022066059) | **true** | 50,000 | 22 (Cognito OTP via SES, [DRE-2265](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2265/cognito-otp-email-rides-cognito-default-flip-all-three-pools-to-ses)) |
| `dreadnought` (442004016891) | **false — sandbox** | 200 | 0 |
| `vericorr` (340646328578) | **true** | 50,000 | 0 |

OM5's final acceptance criterion is *"SES production-access status is confirmed for each account and recorded in* `docs/runbooks/<account>.md` *before this milestone is called done."* The status is now recorded for all three — and one of them fails it.

**Why this matters beyond the checkbox.** The dreadnought account serves `vericorr`, `deltasolve` and `gridcorr`. In sandbox, mail only reaches *verified* addresses, and `notifySafe` swallows every failure by design (a comment write must never 500 because SES did). So a grant notification to a real reader of those three portals is silently dropped — nothing errors, no alarm fires, and the product looks like it notified someone it never reached. That is the worst shape a notification bug can take, and it is invisible without this check.

**Why this is yours and not mine.** A production-access request states the nature of the business, the mail you send and how you handle bounces to AWS — representations only the operator can make. `aws sesv2 put-account-details` would technically execute it; an agent filling in that form is an agent speaking as the company, which the programme's standing boundary forbids regardless of authorization.

**What to submit** (SES console → Account dashboard → Request production access, or `put-account-details`), with the facts already true of this system:

* Mail type: **transactional**. Website: the portal hosts, e.g. `https://share.vericorr.com`.
* Use case: per-recipient notifications to invited readers of private document portals — comment replies, a coalesced grant notification, and nothing else. No marketing, no lists, no purchased addresses; recipients are people a moderator explicitly granted access to.
* Bounce/complaint handling: SES configuration set `docs-comments-<slug>` with a dedicated bounce/complaint handler (P5-B4) writing suppression state; `Portico/SesBounce` metric alarmed (P5-C1).
* Unsubscribe: RFC 8058 one-click, `POST /u/{token}`, deployed, disable-only and idempotent.
* Expected volume: low hundreds per month per account.

**Lead time is the reason this is filed now:** AWS review typically takes ~24 hours and OM4 releases OM5 no earlier than 2026-08-13. Submitting today keeps this off the critical path instead of discovering it on the day.

Close this card when `sesv2 get-account --profile dreadnought` reports `ProductionAccessEnabled: true` and the runbook line is updated.

cards.title: The any-file upload tile ships dark: the server's capability map never declares fileUpload, so the feature stays hidden on every current backend
cards.description:
[DRE-2295](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2295/upload-any-file-type-pdfs-and-images-render-in-the-viewer-everything) gates the new "Upload file" tile behind the [DRE-2279](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2279/the-ui-offers-actions-whose-backend-isnt-deployed-add-document-needs) capability probe, which is correct. But the server never declares the capability, so the gate reads absent and the tile never appears. The feature merges, deploys, and does nothing.

Found while resolving PR #170's merge conflict, not by any test — every suite is green on both sides.

## Why the gate reads absent

`infra/lambda/capabilities_lib.ts` declares only `docUpload`. `infra/test/api_shapes.test.ts` pins `CAPABILITIES` to exactly `{ docUpload: true }`, and the committed `capabilities.json` fixture agrees. The client asks `GET /capabilities` for the whole feature map, finds no `fileUpload` key, and correctly concludes the backend does not support it.

The per-route probe survives only as a **404 fallback** for backends that predate `/capabilities`. So the tile appears on an old backend and vanishes on a current one — the exact inverse of what the gate is for.

This is invisible in CI because the client suite and the infra suite each assert their own side's fixture. Nothing compares the set of capabilities the client asks about against the set the server declares.

## The work

1. Register `fileUpload` in the server's capability map, keyed to `GET /library/docs/upload-formats` in `CAPABILITY_ROUTE_KEYS`.
2. Update `api_shapes.test.ts`'s pinned `CAPABILITIES` assertion and regenerate the `capabilities.json` fixture on both sides.
3. Close the class, not just the instance: add a check that every capability key the client can probe is declared by the server. A client-side key with no server declaration must fail a suite, not ship dark.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `GET /capabilities` returns `fileUpload: true` on a backend that has the any-file upload route; a test asserts it.
- [ ] The client's `useCapability("fileUpload")` gate resolves true against the current server fixture, so the tile renders.
- [ ] A test enumerates the client's probeable capability keys and fails if any is absent from the server's declared map.
- [ ] Both `capabilities.json` fixtures are regenerated from their emitters, not hand-edited.
