cards.title: Every fix-loop blocker escalates to the card as a reviewer dispute — including the hold path, which re-parks the card on each dispatch
cards.description:
`agent-fix.yml` writes the fix agent's real blocker reason to the PR, then posts a **hardcoded** message to the Linear card claiming the agent disagreed with the reviewer. It says that for every blocker, whatever the reason. The card is the surface the CEO reads, so the one place the truth is thrown away is the only place a human looks.

Worse, one of the blocker paths — "a prior blocker is still unanswered, so I am stopping" — can only be reached when the card is *already* parked. It re-applies `needs-human` and re-parks, so every re-dispatch mints another phantom dispute. The card accumulates contradictory reasons for why it is stuck.

## The code

`.github/workflows/agent-fix.yml`, Report step (~line 470):

```bash
if [ -f /tmp/fix-blocker.txt ]; then
  gh pr comment "$PR" --body "🛑 Fix attempt N blocked: $(cat /tmp/fix-blocker.txt)"
  python3 .bureau-pipeline/scripts/linear_ops.py comment "$CARD" \
    "🙋 The fix agent disagrees with the reviewer's blocking finding and stopped
     rather than force a change it believes is wrong. ..."
  park_for_human
fi
```

The true reason is in `$(cat /tmp/fix-blocker.txt)` on the line above. It goes to the PR and is then discarded.

The prompt reaches that file from at least three different states, only one of which is a disagreement:

* **Step 6** — "if a finding is wrong or unfixable in scope, write your reasoning to /tmp/fix-blocker.txt." This is the disagreement the message describes.
* **Step 1b** — an unanswered prior blocker: "write one line to /tmp/fix-blocker.txt saying the prior blocker still awaits the operator's answer, and stop." Structurally this **cannot** be a disagreement — it is a deliberate no-op.
* Any other reason the agent decides it cannot proceed. The file is free text.

The sibling escalations in the same `if/elif/else` — outage-hold and no-progress — each carry their own accurate wording. Only the blocker branch guesses.

## What it did to [DRE-2199](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2199/p5-a3-search-ui-behind-the-existing-pill-k-popover) / portico PR #132

The critic posted **REQUEST_CHANGES** on 08-07 (missing `<1024px` full-screen sheet, `docs/design/addendum-search-surface.md §9`). Two fix runs died on `error_max_turns`, and at **02:05** the card was correctly told: *"The AI service failed several fix runs in a row — that looks like an outage."* Parked, `needs-human`.

Then, on 08-08:

| Time | Card comment | What actually happened |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 18:52 | Fix agent dispatched |  |
| 18:53 | 🙋 **"disagrees with the reviewer's blocking finding"** | Step 1b hold — the 02:05 outage blocker was unanswered |
| 18:55 | Fix agent dispatched | operator answered the design question on the PR and re-armed |
| 19:07 | 🙋 "The AI service failed several fix runs in a row" | true — model errors again |
| 19:08 | Fix agent dispatched |  |
| 19:09 | 🙋 **"disagrees with the reviewer's blocking finding"** | Step 1b hold. The PR comment reads: *"Holding: the prior fix-loop blocker on this PR (2026-08-08T19:07:26Z) still awaits the operator's answer, so this run stops without re-deriving it and without pushing."* |

Two phantom disputes, each ~75 seconds after a dispatch, each re-stamping `needs-human`. Reading the card top-down, the newest and loudest message says the agent is fighting the reviewer. It never was. The blocker was an outage, and before that, an outage.

The cost was real: the operator opened the card to adjudicate a design disagreement that did not exist. The actual state — outage debris on an already-answered question — took reading the PR comment thread in full to recover.

## Why this is not [DRE-2289](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2289/the-fix-agent-is-blind-to-failing-checks-an-approve-verdict-plus-red)

[DRE-2289](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2289/the-fix-agent-is-blind-to-failing-checks-an-approve-verdict-plus-red) is about a missing **work source**: an APPROVE verdict plus red CI gives the fix agent nothing to fix, and it escalates. Its fix is to add failing checks as a trigger.

This card is about the **escalation channel** itself. Even with [DRE-2289](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2289/the-fix-agent-is-blind-to-failing-checks-an-approve-verdict-plus-red) shipped, every blocker still routes through one hardcoded sentence, and the hold path still re-parks on each dispatch. The two overlap on one acceptance criterion; they do not overlap in the fix.

## Approach

1. **Say what the agent said.** The card message must carry the actual blocker text, the same string already posted to the PR. A short plain-English preamble plus the reason, not a preamble that replaces it.
2. **Give the hold path its own branch.** "I am stopping because a previous question is unanswered" is a distinct outcome. It must not claim a dispute, must not re-apply `needs-human` (the card already carries it), and must not re-park a card that is already in Plan Review — one comment, or ideally none, since it adds no information.
3. **Make the hold path idempotent.** Re-dispatching a held card must not multiply escalation comments. The Nth identical hold should be silent on the card.
4. **Keep the honest siblings.** The outage-retry, outage-hold and no-progress messages are accurate and stay as they are.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A blocker escalation to the card includes the contents of `/tmp/fix-blocker.txt`; a test asserts the card comment contains the agent's own reason.
- [ ] No card message asserts a disagreement unless the blocker path taken was the step-6 finding dispute. A test drives the step-1b hold text through the Report logic and proves the output contains no disagreement claim.
- [ ] The step-1b hold does not call `park_for_human` and does not re-add `needs-human`.
- [ ] Two consecutive holds on the same unanswered blocker produce at most one card comment.
- [ ] The outage-retry, outage-hold and no-progress messages are unchanged — a test pins their text.
- [ ] Regression test for the [DRE-2199](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2199/p5-a3-search-ui-behind-the-existing-pill-k-popover) shape: an unanswered outage blocker followed by a dispatch produces no "disagrees with the reviewer" comment on the card.

cards.title: The console never says it failed over — the operator watches a dial to make a decision the dispatcher already made
cards.description:
**Repo:** agent-bureau
**Initiative:** bureau

Sibling of DRE-2281, deliberately scoped to the window BEFORE a cap. DRE-2281 fixes the alert once an account is already dead (HTTP 429 → CRITICAL + runbook). This card is about the hour beforehand: the system already decides to fail over at 80%, and never says so, while the panel the operator watches reads lower than the CLI and explains neither number.

## What the operator hit (2026-08-08)

Side by side, same moment:

* **Claude Code CLI** — "Current session: **94% used**, resets 3:59pm"
* **Console Subscriptions** — "Dreadnought · 5-HOUR **49%**, resets Sat 2:30pm"

Read as "I've got a lot left" — while the interactive session was nearly out. Neither screen is wrong; they measure **different windows on one shared pool**:

* The CLI's own text says it: *"Approximate, based on local sessions on this machine — does not include other devices or [claude.ai](<http://claude.ai>)."*
* The console probes Anthropic and reads `anthropic-ratelimit-unified-5h-utilization` off the response headers — the account's authoritative server-side window — cached for `CACHE_TTL_SECONDS = 300`.

Both draw on `<redacted-email>` (Claude Max 20×), so heavy local Claude Code work consumes the pipeline's headroom and vice versa. Nothing on either screen says that.

## The real problem: the operator is watching a dial to make a decision the system already makes

`subscriptions.py` carries `NEAR_CAP_THRESHOLD = 0.80`, and `agent_dispatch.py` already rides the failover chain — a near-cap account reads `cooling-down` and dispatch borrows the next healthy account down the order. **That is correct and it works.** But:

* Nothing announces the 80% crossing.
* Nothing announces that a failover actually happened, or which account took over.
* So the operator watches the panel to decide "should I switch accounts?" — a decision already taken, silently, by the dispatcher.

This is the escalate-by-exception principle inverted: the system knows something the operator needs, and stays quiet.

## Not in scope (DRE-2281 owns it)

The capped/429 state, its severity, the red tile and the wait-vs-swap runbook. This card must not change `claude_account_health.py`'s 429 classification.

## The work

1. **Label the number.** The tile should say which window it is and when it was measured — "5-HOUR · 49% · as of 1:04pm" — so a 5-minute-old cached figure isn't read as live. Cheapest, highest-value item.
2. **Announce the 80% crossing.** When the ACTIVE account crosses `NEAR_CAP_THRESHOLD`, raise an alert naming the account and the reset estimate. Reuse the DRE-1572 alert model and the existing `cost_usage` probe — no new probe.
3. **Announce the failover itself.** When dispatch borrows a different account, say so: which card/repo, which account took over, why. Today this is invisible; the operator learns by reading a panel.
4. **Say the pool is shared.** The panel should make plain that the account also serves local Claude Code sessions, so 49% is not "the pipeline used half". Wording only — the console cannot see local sessions and must not imply it can.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each Subscriptions window shows its name and an as-of time; a cached value is visibly cached.
- [ ] The active account crossing `NEAR_CAP_THRESHOLD` raises exactly one alert per account per window, naming the account and the reset estimate; it auto-resolves when utilization drops back.
- [ ] A dispatch failover emits one receipt naming the borrowed account and the card that triggered it.
- [ ] `NEAR_CAP_THRESHOLD` is not changed, and `claude_account_health.py`'s 429 handling is untouched (DRE-2281 owns it) — a test asserts both.
- [ ] The panel states that the account is shared with local Claude Code sessions.
- [ ] No new Anthropic probe is added — everything reads the existing `cost_usage` signal.

cards.title: Local sub-agents commit as the operator, so their PRs leave the merge rail and get self-merged — author equals merger
cards.description:
Sub-agents run on this machine with the operator's git and gh credentials, so every PR they open is authored by `smeed652` — a human. The merge gate only ever auto-merges branches named `agent/*`, `repair/*` or `dependabot/*`, so that work falls off the rail entirely and gets merged by hand, by the same person it is attributed to. Author and merger become the same identity, which is the one thing the two-bot design exists to prevent.

This is not a bug. Nothing is broken and nothing errors. A safety property we deliberately built has quietly stopped applying to a large share of the work, and it did so without any change to the pipeline.

## Evidence

Of the last 20 merged PRs in `EveryBite/atlas`, **18 were both authored and merged by** `smeed652`. The two that were not:

* #132 — authored `app/agent-bureau-bot-4` on `agent/DRE-2275-pipeline-main`, merged by `app/agent-bureau-qa-bot`.
* #121 — authored `app/dependabot` on `dependabot/uv/...`, merged by `app/agent-bureau-qa-bot`.

Every other branch was named `docs/...`, `feat/...` or `db/work`. The gate's branch check (`merge-gate.yml`, `case "$BRANCH" in agent/*|repair/*|dependabot/*`) skips all of them, so no critic verdict is required, no auto-merge runs, and the merge is a human action on a human-authored PR.

## Why it matters

Author ≠ merger is enforced by GitHub server-side precisely because it does not depend on anyone remembering. Two separate GitHub Apps exist for this: `agent-bureau-bot` writes, `agent-bureau-qa-bot` merges. When a local agent borrows the operator's identity, the enforcement point is bypassed rather than failed — GitHub sees one human doing normal human things and has nothing to object to.

The second-order cost is that this work also skips the adversarial critic, which is the correctness backstop for unattended automation. Work produced by an agent is being merged with neither of the two gates that exist to check agent output.

## Proposed direction

Local sub-agents should commit and push as `agent-bureau-bot`, on `agent/*` branches, the same as pipeline agents. That single change puts their output back on the normal rail: the critic reviews it, the merge gate auto-merges it on APPROVE plus green CI, and the qa-bot is the merger.

The mechanism already exists — `scripts/github-bot-token.sh` mints an installation token for the bot App, and `config/github-installations.yaml` maps the installation ids. What is missing is making local agents use it by default rather than inheriting the operator's ambient `gh` auth.

Points to settle during the build, not now:

* How an agent gets the token without every agent handling a private key. A helper that mints and exports it, or a git credential helper, are both plausible.
* Commit identity as well as push identity — `user.name` / `user.email` must match the bot, or the commits stay attributed to the operator even when the push does not.
* Where the boundary sits. The operator writing code by hand should still be able to merge by hand; the target is agent-produced work, not all local work.
* Whether the merge gate should also refuse to leave a non-`agent/*` PR unreviewed when its commits are bot-authored, as a backstop for when the identity switch is missed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A sub-agent PR opened locally is authored by `agent-bureau-bot`, on an `agent/*` branch, with commits attributed to the bot.
- [ ] That PR is picked up by the critic and auto-merged by `agent-bureau-qa-bot` on APPROVE plus green CI, with no human merge.
- [ ] Obtaining the identity requires no private key handling by the agent itself.
- [ ] The operator's own hand-authored PRs are unaffected.
- [ ] The runbook or agent charters state which identity local agents use and how it is obtained.

cards.title: The fix agent is blind to failing checks: an APPROVE verdict plus red CI escalates as a phantom dispute and the needs-human hold then skips every later fix run
cards.description:
The fix loop only reads critic findings, so a PR the critic approved but ordinary CI failed has no work source. The fix agent runs, finds nothing to fix, and escalates with a message that describes a dispute that never happened. The escalation applies the `needs-human` hold, and that hold is exactly what `fix_dispatch_blocked()` checks — so every later agent-fix run on that repo skips. Approved work then sits still until a person notices.

This is live right now, not hypothetical.

## What happened tonight

Two Portico PRs hold critic **APPROVE** verdicts and are red on plain type errors:

* **PR #144** (`agent/DRE-2219-draft-status-client`, card DRE-2219) — CI job `client — syntax & no external hosts` fails with two instances of `TS2741` in `src/features/library/status/StatusControl.test.tsx` at lines 303 and 339: `Property 'portalName' is missing in type '{ project: string; folderId: null; }' but required in type 'LibraryScreenProps'`. `portalName` became required in DRE-2277, which merged while #144 was open.
* **PR #141** (`agent/DRE-2217-observability`, card DRE-2217) — CI job `infra — typecheck & test` fails with one `TS2352` in `test/obs_lib.test.ts` at line 549: an `EmfMetadata` cast that needs `as unknown as`.

Both verdicts are APPROVE, authored by `agent-bureau-qa-bot`. #141's verdict says, in its own words, *"No concerns with the delivery. Safe to merge."* and *"No changes required — this section is included for completeness only."*

The fix agent read that verdict, correctly found no requested change, and escalated with: *"the fix agent disagrees with the reviewer's blocking finding."* There was no blocking finding. The message names a dispute that does not exist, so the escalation actively misdirects whoever reads it.

Both cards then got the `needs-human` label. `reconcile.HOLD_LABEL` is `"needs-human"` and `fix_dispatch_blocked()` (`scripts/reconcile.py:548`, reading the hold check at `:527`) returns True on it. Four consecutive `agent-fix.yml` runs in Portico afterwards concluded `skipped`. Nothing was going to move.

## Why the loop cannot see it

`agent-fix.yml` fires only on a `VERDICT: REQUEST_CHANGES` comment from the qa-bot, or on the merge-conflict path. A red check is not a trigger and is not an input. The whole loop is built around one work source — the critic — and CI failure is a second, equally real one that it has no route for.

Net effect: the critic gates *judgement*, CI gates *correctness*, and only the first can start a fix. A two-line type error is enough to strand approved work indefinitely.

## Outcome

An approved PR that is red on CI gets fixed by the same loop that fixes a REQUEST_CHANGES, without a human. When the loop genuinely cannot proceed, the escalation says the real reason.

## Approach

1. **Add failing checks as a work source.** Treat a completed CI run with `conclusion: failure` on an agent branch as a fix trigger alongside the verdict comment. Feed the failing job's log tail into the fix agent's context the way the verdict file is fed today, so the agent has the actual compiler error rather than a check name.
2. **Keep the two sources distinct in the prompt.** A REQUEST_CHANGES fix reworks the diff against a reviewer's finding. A red-CI fix corrects a build or test failure and must not rework approved behaviour. Same separation the merge-conflict mode already uses.
3. **Make the escalation truthful.** The escalation text must be derived from the state the agent actually observed — no finding present, checks red, checks green, model error. Never emit a disagreement message when there is no finding to disagree with.
4. **Bound it.** Cap red-CI fix attempts the same way the verdict loop is capped, so a genuinely unfixable failure escalates once rather than looping.

Consider also whether `needs-human` is the right label for "the loop stopped": it is the hold that disables the repair path, so applying it on a self-inflicted stop guarantees nothing else can recover the PR. That coupling is what turned one bad escalation into four skipped runs. Splitting "a human should look" from "no automation may touch this" is in scope if it falls out cleanly; if not, file it separately.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A PR with an APPROVE verdict and a failing CI check dispatches an agent-fix run. A test asserts the run starts from the check-failure event.
- [ ] The fix agent's context contains the failing job's error output, not just the check name.
- [ ] An escalation message states the observed reason. A test proves that "no critic finding present" produces text that does not claim a disagreement.
- [ ] Red-CI fix attempts are capped, and exhausting the cap escalates once with the real reason.
- [ ] Regression test: the DRE-2219 shape (APPROVE verdict + `TS2741` in a test file) drives a fix attempt rather than an escalation.

cards.title: [EPIC] A new project is set up once, in the console — and is born on the release train with its own Portico share
cards.description:
A new project should be set up in one place, once. You enter it on the console's New Project screen, and everything that makes it a working project follows: the repo and the pipeline, a place on the release train, and a share on Portico. Today that screen saves a name, a colour and some settings, and nothing else. The rest is an operator command plus a handful of pull requests. The train and the share each take their own hand-built cards every time: the website, the relay and portico each needed one to join the train, and the Foundry share is an 11-step operator card ([DRE-3721](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3721/operator-provision-sharedreadnoughtfoundrycom-and-put-ai-readiness-on)).

**CEO, 2026-09-13:** *"Every new project, when we create it, should get put on the train, and it should also spin up a share on Portico. It's just a natural part of setting a project up."*

## Decisions — the record the planner works from (pending CEO approval)

1. **Setup asks three things: the project's name, its company and a colour.** Everything technical is a default in a new **Settings → New projects** page, set once: agents, cards at once, Claude subscription, GitHub org, credentials, AWS account and region, release hours and share rules. An exception for one project is made on that project's own Settings tab after it exists.
   *Why:* CEO, 2026-09-13, on the first draft (six steps, eleven fields): *"when you set up a project, you don't get to make all these different decisions. Some of them are very technical … move that complexity to a configuration underneath settings."*
2. **Every project is born on the release train, and gets a lane when there's something to release.** The scaffold already installs the train with nothing declared ([DRE-3211](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3211/agent-bureau-the-scaffold-ships-the-ninth-stub-release-trainyml-plus)). Setup does not ask what the project ships, because a new repo has nothing to release yet. The card that builds the first releasable thing (a website, a web service or a function) adds its lane from a template, switched off. You can also add a lane on the project's Settings tab. Every lane starts supervised: its first release and one rollback happen by hand, and switching it on stays the CEO's decision.
   *Why:* on 2026-09-13 only agent-bureau's three surfaces release by themselves. bureau-pipeline's and portico's are declared but off, and atlas, deltasolv and agent-bureau-demo do not carry the train at all. Every surface that joined took its own card.
3. **A share belongs to a company, not a repo, and setup works it out without asking.** A new company gets `share.<company domain>`, the naming rule from [DRE-2406](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2406/portal-hostnames-use-three-different-conventions-decide-one-then). A new project for a company that already has a share gets its own shelf there, and our internal projects get a shelf on the Foundry drive ([DRE-3717](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3717/epic-the-dreadnought-foundry-drive-sharedreadnoughtfoundrycom-one-step)).
   *Why:* a share's name is its sign-in group and the key every stored record sits under, so it cannot be renamed later (the `deltasolve` lesson). Two shares for one company would split its people across two sign-ins.
4. **The console does not gain AWS or repo-creation powers.** Pressing Create saves the project. The steps that need those powers run from the operator command that already does them (`scripts/onboard-customer.py`). Pull requests open through the bot and merge themselves through the gates. Anything only a person can do becomes a card in Needs you, carrying the exact command. This answers the credential question this epic left open on 2026-08-07.
   4b. **Credentials are set once per GitHub org, not pasted per repo.** The Settings page shows which of the seven are present. A customer who brings its own Claude key overrides it on the project, keeping the runbook's rule that one token is never shared across customers.
5. **The setup screen shows real state.** After Create, every step shows Done, Merging, Waiting on you or Blocked, read from the live systems: the repo, the route, the pull requests, the first release tag, and the share answering with its sign-in page. It replaces today's tick-it-yourself checklist (`OnboardingTracker`).

## The design

The screens and the full step-by-step walkthrough are the child card's deliverable (see children). The design extends the existing wizard at `/projects/new` ([DRE-1323](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-1323/console-new-project-wizard-steps-2-5-onboarding-tracker), `console/design/screens/web-new-project.html`). It does not start a new one.

## The two outcomes (children), and what the planner should split them into

**Born on the train** (agent-bureau)

* Three surface templates ship in the scaffold: website, web service and function, generalised from `release-website.sh`, `release-console.sh` and `release-relay.sh`. A release-role template for the project's AWS account ships with them.
* The engineer brief and the templates let the card that builds a project's first releasable thing declare its lane at `auto: false`. Declaring the lane files the Needs-you card for the release role, the first supervised release and one rollback.
* The fleet sweep says what each repo actually releases: releasing, declared but off, nothing to ship yet, or no train. Today it only checks that the stub file exists.
* deploy-lag reads every repo's `release.json`. That work is already filed as [DRE-3238](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3238/agent-bureau-the-terminal-deploy-lag-report-reads-its-surfaces-from) (terminal) and [DRE-3214](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3214/agent-bureau-the-consoles-deploylag-reads-the-same-release-data-the) (console).

**Born with a share** (portico first, then agent-bureau)

* A share is created by portico's own deploy (bucket, distribution, certificate, sign-in gate and CDN behaviours) instead of `~/Docs/_tool/aws/setup.sh`, which lives outside every repo.
* The same deploy provisions a new share's grants and its sign-in pages. Today that is `provision-project-grants.ts` and a hand-written `_publish.json`.
* `onboard-customer.py` opens the portico pull request that declares the share, or the shelf on an existing one.
* Portico's own train must be live first ([DRE-3216](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3216/operator-portico-grant-the-portals-release-identity-run-one-supervised)). Until it is, no merge can create a share.

**Both**

* The wizard shrinks from five steps to one screen (name, company, colour) with a read-only "what this project gets" summary drawn from the defaults.
* A new **Settings → New projects** page stores the defaults per tenant. The project's Settings tab gains Release train and Share sections for the exceptions.
* A **company** record gains a web domain. Today nothing stores company → domain in the console (the client derives from the GitHub org, [DRE-1533](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-1533/wire-the-new-project-wizard-submit-registerproject-tenant-scoped)). Portico's `orgDomains` config already holds that mapping for existing shares and is the place to read it from.
* The setup screen reads live state.
* `onboard-customer.py` also declares the channel guard in `config/pipeline-channel.json` (a hand step in the playbook today) and creates the `repo:<slug>` label.
* Retiring a repo also retires its surfaces and its share or shelf (`docs/repo-retirement-runbook.md`).
* One PROOF card: a throwaway project set up from the console, its first release cut by the train, its share sending a signed-out visitor to sign-in, every row on the setup screen Done, and then retired cleanly. Recorded in the repo.

## Order and collisions

* The Foundry share ([DRE-3717](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3717/epic-the-dreadnought-foundry-drive-sharedreadnoughtfoundrycom-one-step)) finishes by hand first. Its run record is the recipe the portico cards encode.
* Both `onboard-customer.py` changes wait for [DRE-3608](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3608/onboard-customerpy-fails-closed-on-an-unreadable-ssm-routing-map-and) (onboarding safety), which edits the same file, and are serialised with each other.
* [DRE-2283](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2283/registering-one-repo-means-editing-11-places-make-project-registration) (one registration record) removes the hand-edited identity files that setup still needs today. It is related, not blocking.

## Background — the card as first filed, 2026-08-07

The end state the project-registry work points at (`adr-project-registry.md`, D4: "roadmap now, build later"). The CEO opens the console's New Project wizard and enters the project once: name, client, repo and colour. The system does the rest: the repo and scaffold, both mirror pull requests, the SSM route, the Linear project and `repo:<slug>` label, and the identity seed. The wizard already saves the presentation row (`registerProject`, [DRE-1533](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-1533/wire-the-new-project-wizard-submit-registerproject-tenant-scoped)). Non-negotiables carried from the ADR: no new slug-keyed literals, colour stays validation-not-generation, and a failure is loud and recoverable, never a silent strand.

Not `agent:planner`-labelled on purpose. Label it and move it when the decisions above are approved.

cards.title: Registering one repo means editing 11 places — make project registration a single canonical record everything derives from
cards.description:
**Repo:** agent-bureau
**Initiative:** bureau
**Plan:** `architecture/project-registry-plan.md` — vetted 2026-08-06, read it before starting. It supersedes the eleven-surface count below with a verified census and an ordered work list.

Onboarding one repo currently means hand-editing about ten separate registrations across two repos, AWS and Linear. Miss one and the failure is silent and specific to whichever surface you forgot.

## Decision on record

**The canonical routing record is the public** `config/repo-map.json` **in** `bureau-pipeline` **at** `main`**.** Operator decision, 2026-08-07 — decision D1 in the plan, §8. `agent-bureau/config/repo-map.json` becomes an explicit tracked mirror; SSM `/bureau/relay/repo-map` remains the relay's live runtime copy.

The reason is that a private canonical makes this card's central deliverable impossible. The cross-repo divergence check is the load-bearing part of this work, and `bureau-pipeline`'s CI runs in product repos with no AWS credentials and no token that can read a private repo — so it could never verify itself against a private source. A public canonical is readable by every consumer with no credentials, which is what `reconcile.live_rail_slugs()` already does. It also ratifies shipped behaviour: `reconcile.py` already calls that file the canonical snapshot, per DRE-2260.

Presentation data — display name, billing client, colour — stays private. Its canonical home at runtime is the console DB `project` table, which is already CEO-editable; a new private `config/project-identities.json` seeds it and feeds the generators.

Decisions D2 (may CI raise drift alerts, or operator make-target only), D3 (must every routing slug have an identity entry) and D4 (console-wizard onboarding epic timing) are still open — see the plan §8.

## The registration surfaces, as of 2026-08-07

The plan's §1.1 has the verified table. Summary: three surfaces previously counted as hand-edits are already generated from the snapshot (`sources.REPOS`, `relay-gh/normalize.py`, `wizard/new-agent/repos.ts`) and cost nothing at onboarding. Six real surfaces were missed by the original count — `flyout/cardMeta.ts`, `demo/demo_library.py` (stale today: missing both `bureau-pipeline` and `portico`), the three colour files, `theme/tokens.css` with its two pinning tests, and `cost_usage._SLUG_ACCOUNT`.

In **bureau-pipeline**: `config/repo-map.json` (now canonical) and `scripts/validate_card.py` → `_FALLBACK_REPO_MAP`, which has no generated-region markers and which the onboarding auto-PR does not update — so that PR cannot pass bureau-pipeline's own `test_inmodule_fallback_matches_the_snapshot`.

Outside git: SSM `/bureau/relay/repo-map` and the Linear `repo:<slug>` label.

## This is not theoretical — it has already cost us

The code comments left behind record the damage:

* `projectColors.ts`: *"Registered 2026-07-29. Unregistered, portico had NO stable colour"*
* `repoLabel.ts`: *"Registered 2026-07-29: portico was live on the dispatch rail but absent from…"*
* `cardMeta.ts`: *"built* `https://github.com/portico/pull/<n>`*, a 404"* — a shipped bug caused purely by a missing registration
* `cardMeta.ts`: *"Worth graduating into…"* — someone already reached this conclusion and moved on

And on 2026-08-06/07, `bureau-pipeline`'s snapshot at tag `v4` did not contain portico, so the atlas and deltasolv reconcile sweeps — which read **every** card in the workspace — declared live portico cards "not on the dispatch rail" and parked nine of them `needs-human`. That hold also disables the conflicted-PR repair path, so DRE-2180 sat about five hours mid-build. Root cause: one stale copy of a list that exists in many places.

## Outcome

Onboarding a repo is **one entry in one place**, plus a generator run. Every other surface derives. A hand-edit that drifts from the canonical record fails CI rather than silently degrading one screen.

## Approach

Extend the machinery that already exists — `scripts/sync_repo_mirrors.py` with its BEGIN/END generated regions, and the snapshot-derived `VALID_SLUGS` pattern in `validate_card.py`. Do not build anything parallel. Ordered work items are in the plan §6; items 1–3 are live bug fixes worth shipping immediately and independently of the rest.

1. **bureau-pipeline — make the gate's fallback literal a generated region.** Markers around `_FALLBACK_REPO_MAP`, regenerated from the canonical snapshot. Fixes the guaranteed-red onboarding PR.
2. **agent-bureau — graduate the escaped copies.** `cardMeta.ts` and `demo_library.py` join `MIRRORS`; `onboard-customer.py`'s bureau-pipeline PR updates both files; `make sync-mirrors CHECK=1` runs in `ci.yml`.
3. **agent-bureau — drift detection across the three stores.** A workflow (on schedule and on push to main) raw-fetches the canonical file at `@main` and diffs it against the mirror, alerting on divergence. A `make check-routing` target does the same plus SSM for the operator.
4. **ADR** — `architecture/decisions/adr-project-registry.md`, recording D1 above and the standing rule that no slug-keyed literal may be added outside a generated region or a derived read.
5. **agent-bureau —** `config/project-identities.json` **+ generated identity mirrors.** Renderers for `PROJECT_IDENTITIES`, `repoLabel.ts`, `projectColors.ts`, `ColorSwatchPicker.tsx`, with validation that every routing slug has an identity entry and every `color_token` exists in `tokens.css`.
6. **agent-bureau — onboarding enters presentation once.** `--display-name/--client/--color-token` flags, the Linear `repo:<slug>` label created proactively, and a failure summary block instead of print-and-scroll-away.
7. **Docs.** `new-project-playbook.md` §2 and the `CLAUDE.md` onboarding paragraph.

## Explicitly out of scope

* Do not change the routing record's flat `slug → "owner/repo"` shape. Five consumers parse it byte-for-byte — the relay, the gate, `deploy.sh`, CDK synth, and `board.py`.
* Do not change the relay's runtime read path (SSM) or its dependency pinning — see the python3.12 constraint in DRE-2272.
* A generator must never invent a colour hex. Validate that the token exists; fail with an instruction to add it.
* No SSM-write or cross-repo-push credentials for CI. The operator-run onboarding CLI already performs those side effects; CI's job is red-on-drift.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An ADR records that the public `bureau-pipeline` snapshot at `main` is the canonical routing record, names agent-bureau's copy a mirror, and states the repair command when they diverge.
- [ ] A credential-free CI check in agent-bureau fails when its mirror diverges from the canonical file — proven by a seeded divergence that turns CI red.
- [ ] `scripts/validate_card.py`'s `_FALLBACK_REPO_MAP` is a generated region, and `onboard-customer.py`'s bureau-pipeline PR passes that repo's own CI.
- [ ] `sources.REPOS`, `sources.PROJECT_IDENTITIES`, `relay-gh/normalize.py`, `cardMeta.ts` and `demo_library.py` contain no hand-written slug literals.
- [ ] The four frontend identity files consume generated regions; no hand-written slug maps remain in `console/web/src`.
- [ ] Adding a repo requires editing one routing entry plus one identity entry and running the generator; the playbook says so and no longer lists mirrors to hand-edit.
- [ ] Registering a fictitious slug end-to-end in a test produces a correct display name, colour and PR URL with no further edits.

cards.title: Edge-region log retention sweep for the sign-in gate (P5-C1 residual)
cards.description:
**Repo:** portico

The follow-on DRE-2217 (P5-C1) names explicitly, so the residual is not left implicit.

## What DRE-2217 closed, and what it could not

DRE-2217 gave the Lambda@Edge sign-in gate a stack-region log group with `logs.RetentionDays.ONE_MONTH`, matching every other log group in the stack. But Lambda@Edge also writes logs to a group named `/aws/lambda/<region>.<function-name>` **in every edge region that serves a request**, created by the Lambda service at runtime, outside any CloudFormation stack. Those groups have no retention: the sign-in gate's logs — the ones carrying sign-in traffic — still accumulate forever, per edge region, in all three AWS accounts.

## The shape of the fix

A CloudFormation stack cannot own these groups (they appear at runtime, in other regions). The realistic close is a small operator-run sweep, in the same family as `_tool/aws/signin-gate.sh` (which already touches every distribution):

* for each account profile, for each active edge region, `aws logs put-retention-policy` (30 days) on `/aws/lambda/<region>.<gate-function-name>` where the group exists
* idempotent, safe to re-run after new edge regions start serving traffic (a new region's group appears only after its first request, so this is a periodic sweep, not a one-shot)

Agents author the script and the exact commands; **the operator runs them** (agents hold no cloud credentials — the Portico security model).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A sweep script (or documented command sequence) sets 30-day retention on every existing `/aws/lambda/<region>.<gate-fn>` group, per account
- [ ] Idempotent and re-runnable; states clearly that new edge regions need a re-run
- [ ] Operator deploy-plan lists the exact per-account commands
- [ ] No CI cloud credentials, no agent-run AWS writes

cards.title: Console's vendored model_fallback.py has drifted — Opus 5 error attribution will silently vanish
cards.description:
`console/backend/model_fallback.py` is a hand-synced **vendored copy** of `bureau-pipeline/scripts/model_fallback.py`. Its own header says "keep in sync". Nothing enforces that, and it has now drifted.

This is the same disease as the hardcoded labels, one layer down: a second copy of the model truth that only a human eye keeps honest.

## The live bug — now armed

The vendored copy still has:

* `OPUS = "claude-opus-4-8"`
* no `RETIRED_MODELS`
* `KNOWN_MODELS = {FABLE, OPUS, SONNET}` — i.e. **without** `claude-opus-5`

`last_error_model()` validates a marker's payload against `KNOWN_MODELS`. So when the pipeline stamps `model-error: claude-opus-5` on a card, the console reads that marker, fails the membership check, and returns `None`.

The failure mode is silence: the console does not report an unknown model, it reports **no model at all**. An is_error death loses its attribution — which is precisely the signal `RETIRED_MODELS` was added upstream to protect.

**This is live now.** The Opus 5 ladder merged 2026-07-28 (bureau-pipeline PR #122), and bureau-pipeline rides `@main` to the whole fleet, so agents are already dispatching Opus 5. The next `is_error` death on Opus 5 loses its attribution.

## Scope change — the `ladder=` delta is gone

The original version of this card asked you to preserve the vendored copy's one intentional delta (`select(ladder=...)`) and write a drift test that tolerated it. **That is no longer the plan.**

That kwarg has been folded upstream (bureau-pipeline PR #123), so upstream and the copy now have **zero** intended differences below the vendored header block. Do not re-introduce a local `ladder=` implementation — upstream's `select()` already accepts it, including the empty/None fallback.

This matters for the test you write: with no allowed exceptions the drift check is a **plain diff**, not a judgement call. An allowed exception is a hole a drift check cannot see through — which is exactly how this copy went from one documented delta to three undocumented ones.

## Fix

1. Re-sync the vendored module to upstream so everything below the vendored header block is byte-identical — including upstream's `select()` docstring, which differs in wording only.
2. Add a test that **fails when the copy drifts**. Fetch upstream `scripts/model_fallback.py` through the transport `agent_roster._gh_fetch` already uses (GitHub contents API over urllib with the App installation token — no `gh` subprocess, the binary is absent in the prod container), strip the vendored header block, and compare. There is precedent for a live-fetch test in this codebase: `scripts/tests/test_sync_standards_skills.py` fetches live standards and `skipTest`s when the fetch fails, so a token-less or offline run degrades rather than red-mains.

## Owns (touch ONLY these files)

`console/backend/model_fallback.py`, `console/backend/tests/` (the new drift test)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `KNOWN_MODELS` in the vendored copy recognises `claude-opus-5`; a test proves `last_error_model()` returns `claude-opus-5` for a `model-error: claude-opus-5` marker instead of `None`
- [ ] Retired ids are still recognised — a test proves a `claude-opus-4-8` marker on an old card still attributes
- [ ] Everything below the vendored header block is byte-identical to upstream; a test asserts this by diff, with NO allowed-exception list
- [ ] The drift test degrades (skip, not fail) when upstream cannot be fetched — offline and token-less runs must not red-main
- [ ] The console's YAML-sourced ladder still drives selection via upstream's `ladder=` kwarg — existing `test_overseer_chat_reply.py` ladder tests pass untouched
- [ ] Full suite green

**Blocked by** bureau-pipeline PR #123 (the fold) — re-syncing before that merges would copy down a `select()` that has no `ladder=` kwarg and break the console's ladder path.

cards.description:
**Repo:** deltasolv

**Design:** design/images/screens/mobile/report-scan-code.png

Scan Code capture step. The capture flow's mode tabs already include a dormant `SCAN` key (`mobile/src/capture/CaptureStep.tsx` currently treats it as a plain photo). This card owns `mobile/src/capture/` edits (scanner stage + parser + tests + the CaptureStep wiring) and its `scan` i18n namespace strings (EN + ES) — no sibling card touches `mobile/src/capture/`.

cards.title: Onboarding flow — language, location, notifications, camera/mic, offline (5 steps)
cards.description:
**Repo:** deltasolv

**Design:** design/images/screens/mobile/onboarding-0-language.png, design/images/screens/mobile/onboarding-1-location.png, design/images/screens/mobile/onboarding-2-notifications.png, design/images/screens/mobile/onboarding-3-camera-mic.png, design/images/screens/mobile/onboarding-4-offline.png

First-run onboarding: a five-step flow (progress dots, "Step N of 5", Back/Continue footer per the exports) shown ONCE after sign-in and before the tab shell. Steps: 1 language (EN/ES radio, applies to i18n immediately), 2 location permission (expo-location request), 3 notifications (add the `expo-notifications` dependency; request permission and record the choice), 4 camera & mic permission (expo-camera), 5 offline mode (enable-offline toggle + Auto-sync-on-Wi-Fi / Sync-on-any-connection radios, "Get Started" finishes). A denied OS permission must never dead-end the flow — Continue always proceeds and the step records what happened. All copy in both `en` and `es` namespace files (`onboarding`) created by DRE-2153; auth itself is untouched (no login/2FA work — out of scope per the epic).

This card OWNS `App.tsx` (the gate wraps between AuthGate and the tab shell — no sibling card may edit `App.tsx`), the new `mobile/src/onboarding/` directory, and the new device-preferences module `mobile/src/prefs/store.ts` (AsyncStorage-backed, generic typed get/set/subscribe) that the Settings card later builds on. Persistence means the flow never reappears after completion, including across app restarts and while offline.

## Contract (shared with the Settings card — exact prefs keys in `mobile/src/prefs/store.ts`)

* `language`: `"en" | "es"`
* `syncPolicy`: `"WIFI_ONLY" | "ANY_NETWORK"`

cards.title: View as User — operator impersonation with audit trail + mobile screen
cards.description:
**Repo:** deltasolv
**Design:** design/images/screens/mobile/superadmin-view-as-user.png

Operator impersonation ("View as User") end-to-end, with an explicit audit trail, in one PR.

**Backend:** honor a new request header `X-View-As-Sub` in `backend/middleware/tenant.py` — ONLY when the REAL caller's membership has `platform_operator = True` (the `request.state.is_platform_operator` context DRE-2145 established). When honored, resolve membership/role/tenant AS the target sub, so the target's role limits what the impersonated session can do — an operator viewing a FIELD user gets FIELD permissions, and the view-only/VENDOR walls apply as the target. Keep the real operator's sub available on `request.state` so nothing attributes actions to the target's identity. A non-operator sending the header gets fail-closed resolution (no tenant, no data) — never silent fallback to their own context.

**Audit:** new model `backend/models/view_as_audit.py` — table `view_as_audit` (id, `operator_sub`, `target_sub`, `tenant_id` nullable, `created_at`) + Alembic migration (renumber against origin/main head right before the PR; single-head guard). An operator-gated mutation `startViewAsUser(targetSub: String!)` writes one audit row per view-as session start and returns ok. The mobile app calls it BEFORE enabling the header — no impersonated reads before the audit row exists.

**Mobile:** replace the placeholder `mobile/src/superadmin/ViewAsUserScreen.tsx` (this card's only screen file) with the PNG build — search field over DRE-2145's `platformUsers(search)`, rows with initials avatar, name-from-email, "role · customer" line, and a "View as" button that calls `startViewAsUser`, stores the target sub, and injects `X-View-As-Sub` alongside the existing header wiring in `mobile/src/graphql/client.ts` (this card may edit `client.ts` — it is serialized after DRE-2157, which owns the base header wiring; reuse `usePlatformViewer` from that card). Provide a clearly visible way to END the impersonation that drops the header and restores the operator's own context.

## Contract

* Header name exactly `X-View-As-Sub`; mutation exactly `startViewAsUser(targetSub: String!)`; table exactly `view_as_audit`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A platform operator can view as a target user: tenant-scoped reads return the target's tenant data under the target's role, with the role walls applied as the target.
- [ ] A non-operator sending `X-View-As-Sub` is failed closed — no impersonation, no data.
- [ ] Every view-as session writes a `view_as_audit` row carrying the REAL operator sub and the target sub before impersonated reads flow.
- [ ] Screen matches design/images/screens/mobile/superadmin-view-as-user.png with live cross-customer search; ending the session restores the operator's own context.
- [ ] Migration + single-head guard green; `ruff`, `mypy`, `pytest`, mobile type-check, and jest green.

**Blocked by:** DRE-2145, DRE-2157

cards.description:
**Repo:** deltasolv

Expose the platform-operator context and the cross-tenant reads the super-admin surfaces need. The identity already exists — `tenant_membership.platform_operator` (boolean) — reuse it; no new identity table, no migration. In `backend/middleware/tenant.py`, set `request.state.is_platform_operator` from the SAME single membership lookup that already sets `membership_role` (True when the resolved row has `platform_operator = True`; False otherwise). Add ONE new resolver file `backend/graphql/resolvers/platform.py` with deliberately cross-tenant reads — they live in the resolver, not `backend/services/` (the tenant-scope guard scans the services tree; `membership.py` documents this pattern):

* `platformViewer` → `{ isPlatformOperator }` — safe for any caller; false when not an operator.
* `platformCustomers` → every tenant with `userCount` (membership rows) and `projectCount` (rows in `project` — needs DRE-2141 merged first).
* `platformUsers(search: String)` → memberships across all tenants matching email/sub, each with its tenant slug + name and role.
* Mutation `createCustomer(name: String!, slug: String!)` → creates a `tenant` row (slug unique — surface a clean error on collision).

Everything except `platformViewer` must fail closed unless `request.state.is_platform_operator` is True — a tenant ADMIN is NOT enough. The VENDOR read wall is deny-by-default, so do not add any of these to `VENDOR_VISIBLE_QUERY_FIELDS`.

## Contract (shared with siblings)

* `request.state.is_platform_operator` — the flag the View-as-User card's impersonation gate reads.
* GraphQL, exactly: `platformViewer { isPlatformOperator }` · `platformCustomers { id slug name userCount projectCount }` · `platformUsers(search) { sub email role tenantId tenantSlug tenantName }` · `createCustomer(name, slug)` — consumed by the mobile super-admin cards.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Middleware sets `request.state.is_platform_operator`; existing role/vendor resolution is unchanged.
- [ ] Non-operator callers (including tenant ADMINs) get nothing from `platformCustomers`/`platformUsers` and cannot `createCustomer`; an operator gets all tenants with correct counts.
- [ ] `platformViewer.isPlatformOperator` is true only for a flagged membership.

cards.title: Console & infra production-readiness hardening (auth expiry, DB recovery, tenant-scoped chat tools, prod image)
cards.description:
**Repo:** agent-bureau
**Initiative:** bureau
**Size:** M (epic — sum of children)
**Source:** `architecture/audits/2026-07-02-live-estate-deep-dive.md` (merged to main, PR #1894) — live-estate deep-dive, epic 7 of 7. These four findings were flagged unverified in the report and then CONFIRMED by a focused adversarial verification pass (run wf_cd9307d6-691, 2026-07-02: 5 confirmed / 2 refuted).

## Problem

Four confirmed production-readiness gaps in the console + infra layer, none touching the pipeline itself:

1. **Unattended board dies silently after 1 hour.** The console session cookie is minted with a fixed `maxAge: 3600` and no renewal in all three mint paths (console/web proxy.ts:142, :170, :285); `refreshToken` exists as an unused type field only. There is no 401 re-auth path (main.tsx:10 builds a bare QueryClient with no error handler; RequireAuth only checks auth at boot). When the cookie expires, useLiveQuery.ts:240-248 classifies the resulting 401 as `connectionState=reconnecting`, keeps the last good data, and polls forever — so an unattended CEO board shows stale data behind a generic "reconnecting" toast indefinitely and never prompts re-auth.
2. **Production DB has a 1-day recovery window with deletion protection off, and the deploy doc lies about it.** infra/lib/data-stack.ts:90-106 sets no `backup` property (RDS default = 1-day PITR) and `deletionProtection: false` (line 105), while infra/DEPLOY.md:194 claims "default retention: 7 days." removalPolicy: RETAIN mitigates accidental stack-delete but not the PITR window. For a customer-facing DB this is a real recovery-risk gap.
3. **The console chat agent's Linear tools are workspace-global — a cross-tenant confidentiality/integrity gap.** agent_tools.py authenticates with one global LINEAR_API_KEY (:62-77), hardwires the DRE team (:212-216), and get_card/comment/set_state (:189) act on any card_id the LLM supplies — with none of the `ensure_tenant_owns_slug` gating that the equivalent direct GraphQL mutations ([schema.py](<http://schema.py>) set_card_state/hold_action) enforce. All tenants share one DRE Linear workspace, so a tenant chatting with their own overseer can steer it to read or mutate another tenant's cards. (Same failure class as the WebSocket leak in [DRE-1981](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-1981/authenticate-the-ingest-websocket-so-live-customer-event-streams).)
4. **The subscription-auth overseer path is dead in production.** console/backend/Dockerfile (python:3.14-slim) installs `claude-agent-sdk` but never installs the `claude` CLI the SDK must spawn — its own requirements.txt comment and MIGRATIONS.md:226-234 flag this as an unfinished infra follow-up. agent_loop.py `_client_for` (:747-753) selects the CLI-spawning ClaudeCodeClient whenever a project has a CLAUDE_OAUTH token (the preferred prod mode per [DRE-1519](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-1519/console-run-overseer-model-calls-through-claude-codeagent-sdk-on-the)), so the overseer turn dies; only the non-preferred raw-API fallback works.

## Outcome

The unattended board re-authenticates or renews instead of dead-ending on stale data; the production DB has a 7-day recovery window with deletion protection on (or the doc tells the truth); chat-agent Linear tools are tenant-scoped through the same gate as the GraphQL resolvers; and the prod image can actually run the subscription-auth overseer.

## Proposed decomposition (from audit + verification — planner to refine)

1. **\[S\] (agent-bureau)** Add a global react-query QueryCache onError in console/web main.tsx that detects 401/ClientError → re-hydrate auth store → RequireAuth redirect to /auth/sign-in; and/or implement the unused refreshToken renewal so the 1-hour cookie renews before expiry. (session-expiry, medium)
2. **\[XS\] (agent-bureau)** Set explicit `backup: { retention: Duration.days(7) }` and `deletionProtection: true` on the production DatabaseCluster (infra/lib/data-stack.ts:90-106); if the stack is genuinely dev-only, correct [DEPLOY.md:194](<http://DEPLOY.md:194>) and document intended prod values separately. (aurora-recovery, high)
3. **\[S\] (agent-bureau)** Bind the chat-agent tool registry to the conversation's tenant_id and route every Linear tool (agent_tools.py linear_get_card/comment/nudge_state/search_cards/file_card) through `ensure_tenant_owns_slug`, mirroring set_card_state/hold_action; reject cross-tenant card IDs. (chat-tool tenant scoping, high — relates to [DRE-1981](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-1981/authenticate-the-ingest-websocket-so-live-customer-event-streams))
4. **\[S\] (agent-bureau)** Install the `claude` CLI in console/backend/Dockerfile's production stage (Node + `npm i -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code`, or the native installer) so the Agent SDK can spawn it, and provide CLAUDE_OAUTH_* as App Runner task secrets. (prod-image, high)

## Verification note

Two related report findings were REFUTED on verification and are NOT included here: RETRY_WITH_GUIDANCE "dropping guidance" (no guidance capability exists to drop — only misleading receipt copy) and linear-sync Done-by-title (branch ref is grepped before title, largely mitigating the [DRE-727](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-727/linear-github-dont-auto-done-epics-when-a-child-pr-merges) class).

cards.title: Fix customer onboarding so one command cannot un-route the fleet or ship a repo that cannot authenticate
cards.description:
**Repo:** agent-bureau
**Initiative:** bureau
**Size:** M (epic — sum of children)
**Source:** `architecture/audits/2026-07-02-live-estate-deep-dive.md` (merged to main, PR #1894) — live-estate deep-dive, epic 5 of 6.

## Problem

The one-command customer onboarding tool has two confirmed traps and the operator toolkit breaks for 2 of the 5 live repos. (1) scripts/onboard-customer.py:387-396 treats ANY failure to read the relay's routing map (a network blip, a throttle, wrong AWS profile) as 'the map is empty', then writes a map containing only the new customer over /bureau/relay/repo-map with --overwrite (lines 399-404) — instantly un-routing every existing customer's cards until a human notices Todo cards not moving. (2) Lines 100-107 print a six-secret setup checklist that omits CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, while lines 350-353 unconditionally set CLAUDE_AUTH_MODE=subscription — a mode in which the pipeline (bureau-pipeline agent-task.yml:101-102, 148-149) relies solely on the omitted token, so an operator who follows the printed checklist onboards a repo whose first agent run fails authentication. (3) scripts/complete-card.py:49,143-145 and scripts/linear-api.py:364-367 hardcode the dreadnought-foundry GitHub org, but atlas lives at EveryBite/atlas and deltasolv at DeltaSolv/deltasolv (config/repo-map.json), so the hand-merge completion tools refuse valid merged PRs for those repos. (4) The GitHub-events relay resolves repos from a baked-in literal list, not the SSM map (cloud/relay-gh/lambda_function.py:396-405), so 'onboarding is one SSM write, no redeploy' is false for real-time console updates.

## Outcome

Onboarding a customer is genuinely one safe command: a transient AWS failure aborts loudly instead of clobbering live routing, the printed checklist is complete so the first agent run authenticates, the completion tools work for every org in the repo-map, and a new repo's real-time console feed works without a relay redeploy.

## Proposed decomposition (from audit — planner to refine)

1. **\[S\] (agent-bureau)** Make [onboard-customer.py](<http://onboard-customer.py>) abort on SSM read failure (distinguish ParameterNotFound from throttle/auth/network at lines 387-396) and refuse shrinking a non-empty live map without --force (lines 399-404); tests.
2. **\[XS\] (agent-bureau)** Add CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN to the printed onboarding secrets (lines 100-107) and reconcile the playbook's six-vs-seven secret counts + test pins.
3. **\[S\] (agent-bureau)** Resolve slug→org via config/repo-map.json in [complete-card.py](<http://complete-card.py>) (:49, 143-145) and [linear-api.py](<http://linear-api.py>) (:364-367) so atlas/deltasolv work; delete the stale '[msg.sh](<http://msg.sh>) complete-card' error text.
4. **\[S\] (agent-bureau)** Make relay-gh resolve repos from the SSM repo-map (lambda_function.py:396-405), not the baked normalize.REPOS literal, so onboarding needs no relay redeploy for console updates.
